nodes.title: How to Turn Your Knowledge Graph Embeddings into Generative Models
nodes.tldr: Reinterprets knowledge graph embedding scores as probabilistic circuits, enabling exact likelihood training, efficient sampling and built-in logical constraints with little loss in link prediction.
nodes.problem: Popular KG embedding models are energy-based, so they lack exact likelihood, sampling and logical constraints.
nodes.approach: Restrict circuit activations to be non-negative or square the outputs to obtain tractable generative circuits.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Knowledge Graphs & Relational Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment between knowledge graphs and generative probabilistic models
nodes.niche_reason: Generative view of KG embeddings via circuits is an unusual cross-over.

nodes.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Threshold-based Auto-labeling
nodes.tldr: Derives sample complexity bounds for human-labeled validation data needed to guarantee quality of threshold-based auto-labeled data, and shows validation usage can be prohibitively large.
nodes.problem: Auto-labeling via confidence thresholds lacks guarantees on the quality of machine-labeled data.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of threshold-based auto-labeling with finite-sample bounds, validated on synthetic and real datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Labeling pipeline straddles data curation and statistical learning theory.
nodes.niche_reason: Threshold auto-labeling theory is a specialized niche.

nodes.title: SwiftSage: A Generative Agent with Fast and Slow Thinking for Complex Interactive Tasks
nodes.tldr: Combines a fine-tuned small encoder-decoder for fast actions with LLM subgoal planning for deliberate reasoning, outperforming SayCan, ReAct, and Reflexion on ScienceWorld.
nodes.problem: Interactive complex tasks need both fast intuition and deliberate planning.
nodes.approach: Dual-process agent: behavior-cloned Swift module with GPT-4 Sage module via heuristic integration.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: LLM agents with fast/slow thinking are common

nodes.title: The Clock and the Pizza: Two Stories in Mechanistic Explanation of Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Shows networks trained on modular addition can learn qualitatively different algorithms, including a new Pizza procedure alongside the known Clock algorithm, depending on hyperparameters.
nodes.problem: It is unclear whether networks reliably rediscover a single known algorithm on simple tasks.
nodes.approach: Controlled hyperparameter and initialization sweeps with mechanistic analysis of learned solutions.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Mechanistic study of small algorithmic tasks; topic is between interpretability and training dynamics.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic study of algorithm discovery is specialised.

nodes.title: Plug-and-Play Stability for Intracortical Brain-Computer Interfaces: A One-Year Demonstration of Seamless Brain-to-Text Communication
nodes.tldr: Enables a brain-computer interface to self-recalibrate online using language-model-corrected pseudo-labels, stable over 403 days with a clinical participant.
nodes.problem: Intracortical BCI decoders degrade over days and need disruptive supervised recalibration.
nodes.approach: Language models correct decoded outputs, and these pseudo-labels update the decoder online.
nodes.confidence_reason: BCI application straddles neuroscience and continual learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Long-term clinical BCI recalibration with LLM pseudo-labels is rare.

nodes.title: Sampling from Gaussian Process Posteriors using Stochastic Gradient Descent
nodes.tldr: Shows stochastic gradient descent can sample from Gaussian process posteriors cheaply, using low-variance objectives and inducing points, giving accurate predictions even without convergence.
nodes.problem: Gaussian process posterior sampling requires costly cubic linear-system solves sensitive to conditioning.
nodes.approach: Stochastic gradient algorithms with low-variance objectives to approximately solve GP linear systems.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Scalable GP inference is an established specialised area.

nodes.title: ARTree: A Deep Autoregressive Model for Phylogenetic Inference
nodes.tldr: ARTree models phylogenetic tree topologies autoregressively with GNNs, adding leaves one at a time, for variational inference over trees.
nodes.problem: Flexible probabilistic models over tree topologies without hand-engineered features.
nodes.approach: GNN-based autoregressive leaf-addition model used as a variational distribution.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Phylogenetic inference with deep learning is very rare.

nodes.title: Topological Parallax: A Geometric Specification for Deep Perception Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces topological parallax, a persistent-homology-based tool comparing a trained model's multiscale geometry to a reference dataset to assess trustworthy interpolation and perturbation.
nodes.problem: Determining whether a trained model shares the geometric structure of its dataset for safety and robustness.
nodes.approach: Bi-filtered persistence module on Rips complexes with geodesic distortion, proven stable under dataset perturbation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory-heavy topological tool; fits several topics, no clear single home.
nodes.niche_reason: Topological data analysis of deep models is very rare.

nodes.title: Implicit Variational Inference for High-Dimensional Posteriors
nodes.tldr: Approximates Bayesian posteriors with neural implicit samplers, using linearised bounds and a new architecture scaling to tens of millions of latent variables.
nodes.problem: Capturing complex correlated posteriors in high-dimensional Bayesian networks is hard for existing methods.
nodes.approach: Implicit neural sampler with locally linearised variational bounds, avoiding discriminators and adversarial objectives.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit variational inference for very large Bayesian nets is specialised.

nodes.title: Neural Injective Functions for Multisets, Measures and Graphs via a Finite Witness Theorem
nodes.tldr: Proves neural-network moments with analytic non-polynomial activations define injective multiset functions via a finite witness theorem, with consequences for GNN separation and approximation.
nodes.problem: Injectivity of practical neural multiset functions was unstudied compared with polynomial moments.
nodes.approach: Finite witness theorem showing neural moments are injective; derive approximation and GNN separation results.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Injectivity theory for multiset functions is a rare theoretical direction.

nodes.title: Improved Algorithms for Stochastic Linear Bandits Using Tail Bounds for Martingale Mixtures
nodes.tldr: Builds tighter confidence sequences for stochastic linear bandits using a tail bound for adaptive martingale mixtures, with worst-case regret guarantees and gains on hyperparameter tuning.
nodes.problem: Large confidence sets give weak regret and performance in stochastic linear bandits.
nodes.approach: Novel tail bound for martingale mixtures yields tighter confidence sequences, with convex-program action selection.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Bandit confidence sequence theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: L-CAD: Language-based Colorization with Any-level Descriptions using Diffusion Priors
nodes.tldr: Language-guided image colorization handling descriptions of any detail level by using pretrained diffusion priors, alignment modules and a new sampling strategy for instance-aware colors.
nodes.problem: Language-based colorization assumes comprehensive descriptions and underperforms on partial ones.
nodes.approach: Pretrained text-to-image diffusion priors with condition alignment modules and instance-aware sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: Language-guided colorization is an established but specialised task.

nodes.title: The Rashomon Importance Distribution: Getting RID of Unstable, Single Model-based Variable Importance
nodes.tldr: Defines variable importance over all near-optimal Rashomon models, stable across distributions, with consistency guarantees and an HIV gene case study.
nodes.problem: Single-model variable importance is unstable and reflects one of many equally good explanations of the same data.
nodes.approach: Aggregate variable importance across all good models, stabilized over the data distribution, applicable to most model classes.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Rashomon-set variable importance is a rare, cross-disciplinary statistics angle.

nodes.title: 4M: Massively Multimodal Masked Modeling
nodes.tldr: Trains one Transformer encoder-decoder with masked modeling over many discrete modalities, yielding a versatile vision foundation model usable for editing and generation.
nodes.problem: Vision models are specialised to one modality and task, unlike versatile large language models.
nodes.approach: Maps all modalities to discrete tokens and performs masked modeling on random token subsets.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal masked foundation models are a common direction

nodes.title: Bayesian target optimisation for high-precision holographic optogenetics
nodes.tldr: Uses nonparametric Bayesian models of neural responses to optimise laser powers and target locations, reducing off-target stimulation in holographic optogenetics.
nodes.problem: Off-target stimulation of nearby non-target neurons limits precise optogenetic control.
nodes.approach: Nonparametric Bayesian response model, then optimisation of laser powers and target locations.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Very few ML papers address holographic optogenetic control

nodes.title: A Unified Generalization Analysis of Re-Weighting and Logit-Adjustment for Imbalanced Learning
nodes.tldr: Derives a fine-grained generalization bound for re-weighting and logit adjustment on imbalanced data, unifying both methods and yielding a new algorithm.
nodes.problem: Existing generalization analyses of re-weighting and logit adjustment are coarse and fail to explain empirical results.
nodes.approach: Data-dependent contraction technique applied to class-modified losses to bound generalization error.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised generalization analysis of imbalanced learning losses

nodes.title: Can Language Models Solve Graph Problems in Natural Language?
nodes.tldr: NLGraph is a 29k-problem benchmark of graph reasoning tasks in natural language for LLMs, with Build-a-Graph and Algorithmic prompting improving results by up to 17%.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether LLMs can process textual graph descriptions and perform structured graph operations.
nodes.approach: Benchmark of eight graph tasks plus two instruction-based prompting methods, Build-a-Graph and Algorithmic prompting.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised LLM reasoning evaluation on graph algorithm problems.

nodes.title: Expressive Sign Equivariant Networks for Spectral Geometric Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows sign invariance is limiting for eigenvector-based learning and develops provably expressive sign-equivariant networks based on equivariant polynomial characterizations.
nodes.problem: Eigenvector sign ambiguity limits models for orthogonal equivariance and graph positional encodings.
nodes.approach: Sign equivariant architectures derived from analytic characterization of sign equivariant polynomials.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Eigenvector symmetry-aware architectures are a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: Double Gumbel Q-Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows networks add two heteroscedastic Gumbel noise sources to Q-learning; Double Gumbel Q-Learning with a pessimism hyperparameter beats DDPG, TD3 and SAC across 33 tasks.
nodes.problem: Overestimation and noise in deep Q-learning from function approximation errors.
nodes.approach: Model Q-errors as Gumbel noise and derive a maximum-likelihood loss with a tunable pessimism parameter.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another deep RL algorithm, though extreme value theory angle is mildly unusual.

nodes.title: Approximate Heavy Tails in Offline (Multi-Pass) Stochastic Gradient Descent
nodes.tldr: Shows offline (multi-pass) SGD's stationary distribution has approximate power-law tails, with approximation controlled by how well empirical data matches the true distribution.
nodes.problem: Heavy tails are known for online SGD, but their origin with finite training data is unexplained.
nodes.approach: Wasserstein convergence bounds from offline SGD to online SGD as the number of data points grows.
nodes.niche_reason: Finite-data heavy-tail origin is a rare theoretical angle

nodes.title: Effective Human-AI Teams via Learned Natural Language Rules and Onboarding
nodes.tldr: Learns natural-language rules from LLM-described data regions that teach humans when to rely on an AI via onboarding, improving human-AI team accuracy.
nodes.problem: Humans need to know when to trust, collaborate with, or ignore an AI agent.
nodes.approach: Embedding-space region discovery, contrastive LLM-based region description, and an onboarding stage teaching the rules.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Human-AI teaming with learned natural-language rules is unusual; no HCI area in vocab.

nodes.title: Auditing for Human Expertise
nodes.tldr: Proposes a hypothesis test checking whether expert predictions are conditionally independent of outcomes, showing physicians use information beyond a screening algorithm.
nodes.problem: Whether human experts add value beyond what an algorithm trained on available data can capture.
nodes.approach: Conditional independence test of expert predictions against outcomes given features, applied to emergency department data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Statistical test fits no exact topic; healthcare is the application
nodes.niche_reason: Testing human expertise for complementarity is an unusual framing

nodes.title: Delegated Classification
nodes.tldr: Models outsourced machine learning as a principal-agent game, proving budget-optimal performance contracts are thresholds and linking them to Neyman-Pearson testing.
nodes.problem: Conflicts of interest arise when ML tasks are delegated to rational agents.
nodes.approach: Contract-design theory with threshold-form optimal contracts, estimated using learning curves and scaling laws.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Economics contract theory applied to ML delegation is rare.

nodes.title: Mesogeos: A multi-purpose dataset for data-driven wildfire modeling in the Mediterranean
nodes.tldr: Mesogeos is a 17-year Mediterranean wildfire datacube combining weather, vegetation, human activity and fire records, with tracks for danger forecasting and burned-area estimation.
nodes.problem: Data-driven wildfire modeling lacks a large, harmonized, ML-ready dataset for the Mediterranean.
nodes.approach: Harmonize drivers and fire records on a 1km daily grid datacube and define two ML tracks with baselines.
nodes.niche_reason: Regional wildfire ML datasets are a rare niche.

nodes.title: OpenAssistant Conversations - Democratizing Large Language Model Alignment
nodes.tldr: Releases OpenAssistant Conversations, a crowd-sourced, human-annotated corpus of 161k messages in 35 languages with quality ratings, improving models fine-tuned for alignment.
nodes.problem: High-quality human feedback data for LLM alignment is expensive and mostly proprietary.
nodes.approach: Volunteer crowd-sourced conversation trees with 461k quality ratings, released openly and used for fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Alignment datasets are common mainstream work.

nodes.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
nodes.tldr: Adapts zeroth-order SGD to run in place so language models fine-tune with inference-level memory, matching backprop on many tasks.
nodes.problem: Backpropagation needs prohibitive memory to fine-tune large language models.
nodes.approach: In-place zeroth-order gradient estimation from two forward passes, compatible with LoRA and prefix tuning.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning is a specialised memory-saving niche

nodes.title: Exposing Attention Glitches with Flip-Flop Language Modeling
nodes.tldr: Introduces flip-flop language modeling, a synthetic task revealing sporadic long-range copying errors in Transformers called attention glitches.
nodes.problem: Transformers intermittently fail at long-range reasoning, possibly causing LLM hallucinations.
nodes.approach: Parametric synthetic binary copy benchmark with regularization and mechanistic analyses of errors.
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment call between architecture analysis and LLM reasoning benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic probes of attention failure are specialised but not rare

nodes.title: ClimSim: A large multi-scale dataset for hybrid physics-ML climate emulation
nodes.tldr: Presents ClimSim, a 5.7-billion-sample multi-scale dataset for training ML emulators that replace high-resolution physics in hybrid climate simulators, with baselines.
nodes.problem: Hybrid physics-ML climate simulation lacks accessible large training data and workflows.
nodes.approach: Release a massive multi-scale climate simulation dataset with deterministic and stochastic regression baselines.
nodes.niche_reason: Climate emulation datasets are a rare application area.

nodes.title: Rank-N-Contrast: Learning Continuous Representations for Regression
nodes.tldr: Rank-N-Contrast learns regression representations by contrasting samples according to their target rankings, guaranteeing representations ordered like targets and improving robustness.
nodes.problem: End-to-end regression networks learn fragmented representations that ignore the continuous order of targets.
nodes.approach: Contrastive learning where samples are ranked by target-space distance and contrasted against each other.
nodes.niche_reason: Contrastive regression is specialised but growing.

nodes.title: Full-Atom Protein Pocket Design via Iterative Refinement
nodes.tldr: FAIR co-designs protein pocket sequence and full-atom 3D structure by iterative coarse-to-fine refinement conditioned on the ligand, improving AAR and RMSD over 10%.
nodes.problem: Designing ligand-binding protein pockets with sidechains, efficiently and with ligand context.
nodes.approach: Full-shot iterative refinement from backbone to full atoms with hierarchical context encoder and ligand updates.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised protein design problem within a busy AI-for-science area.

nodes.title: Max-Margin Token Selection in Attention Mechanism
nodes.tldr: Proves gradient descent on softmax attention converges in direction to a max-margin solution that selects locally optimal tokens.
nodes.problem: Nonconvex optimization dynamics of attention are poorly understood theoretically.
nodes.approach: Analyzes the implicit bias of gradient descent on the attention parameters, linking it to SVM margin maximization.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit-bias theory of attention is specialised but established.

nodes.title: DeWave: Discrete Encoding of EEG Waves for EEG to Text Translation
nodes.tldr: DeWave uses a quantized variational encoder to turn EEG into discrete codes aligned with pretrained language models for open-vocabulary EEG-to-text translation without eye-fixation markers.
nodes.problem: EEG-to-text translation depends on word-level event markers or eye fixations that are hard to obtain at inference.
nodes.approach: Vector-quantized discrete codex of EEG waves with text-EEG contrastive alignment to pretrained language models.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: EEG-to-text decoding is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Differentiable Registration of Images and LiDAR Point Clouds with VoxelPoint-to-Pixel Matching
nodes.tldr: Learns cross-modal image-LiDAR features with a differentiable probabilistic PnP solver, so pose supervision flows end-to-end.
nodes.problem: Image-LiDAR registration struggles to align cross-modal features and cannot supervise non-differentiable PnP.
nodes.approach: Triplet network matching voxel, point, and pixel branches, trained through a differentiable probabilistic PnP.
nodes.niche_reason: Image-LiDAR registration is established; differentiable PnP end-to-end is specialised.

nodes.title: On the Planning Abilities of Large Language Models - A Critical Investigation
nodes.tldr: Systematically evaluates LLMs on IPC-style planning tasks, finding poor autonomous plan success (~12% for GPT-4) but useful heuristic guidance for sound planners and verifier back-prompting.
nodes.problem: Whether LLMs can actually plan autonomously or guide classical planners.
nodes.approach: Benchmark suite of planning-competition domains evaluated in autonomous and heuristic modes with external verifiers.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM planning evaluation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Aleatoric and Epistemic Discrimination: Fundamental Limits of Fairness Interventions
nodes.tldr: Separates discrimination into aleatoric (inherent in data) and epistemic (model choices), using Blackwell's comparison of experiments to quantify fairness limits and benchmark fairness interventions.
nodes.problem: Unclear how much accuracy-fairness limits come from data versus model development choices.
nodes.approach: Characterize fairness-constrained performance limits via Blackwell's statistical experiment comparison; measure gap to existing interventions.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory-driven fairness limits are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Provable Training for Graph Contrastive Learning
nodes.tldr: POT regularizes graph contrastive learning using a node compactness metric, a provable lower bound derived by bound propagation, to address imbalanced node training.
nodes.problem: Some nodes are consistently undertrained and violate the contrastive principle across augmentations.
nodes.approach: Derive node compactness via bound propagation and add it as a regularizer to contrastive loss.
nodes.niche_reason: Established graph contrastive learning with provable twist.

nodes.title: Hierarchical Integration Diffusion Model for Realistic Image Deblurring
nodes.tldr: HI-Diff runs diffusion in a compact latent space to produce a prior feature for a regression-based deblurring network, improving distortion metrics with fewer inference steps.
nodes.problem: Diffusion-based deblurring is computationally heavy and its outputs misalign with distortion-based metrics.
nodes.approach: Latent-space diffusion generates priors fed hierarchically into a regression-based transformer deblurring process.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-for-restoration is a common direction.

nodes.title: On the Minimax Regret for Online Learning with Feedback Graphs
nodes.tldr: Tightens minimax regret bounds for online learning with feedback graphs, interpolating between bandits and experts via a q-Tsallis FTRL algorithm.
nodes.problem: Closing gaps between known upper and lower regret bounds for strongly observable feedback graphs.
nodes.approach: FTRL with q-Tsallis entropy, q tuned to the independence number, plus an improved lower bound via multitask reduction.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Tight regret bounds for feedback graphs is a specialised theory niche

nodes.title: Structure-free Graph Condensation: From Large-scale Graphs to Condensed Graph-free Data
nodes.tldr: Graph condensation with no explicit structure, encoding topology into node features aligned with GNN training trajectories.
nodes.problem: Existing graph condensation jointly optimizes nodes and edges, hurting effectiveness and generalization.
nodes.approach: Training-trajectory meta-matching synthesizes graph-free data; a GNN feature score dynamically evaluates condensed data quality.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised graph dataset distillation

nodes.title: Regularized Behavior Cloning for Blocking the Leakage of Past Action Information
nodes.tldr: Regularizes behavior cloning with a conditional-independence penalty to stop imitation from copying leaked past actions in observation histories, evaluated with a kernel-based estimator.
nodes.problem: Behavior cloning with observation histories imitates its own past actions when action information leaks into histories.
nodes.approach: Past Action Leakage Regularization using a kernel-based conditional independence metric estimator.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Past action leakage in imitation is a rare, specific problem.

nodes.title: Posterior Contraction Rates for Matérn Gaussian Processes on Riemannian Manifolds
nodes.tldr: Proves optimal posterior contraction rates for intrinsic Matérn Gaussian processes on Riemannian manifolds, and shows extrinsic processes attain matching rates with matched smoothness.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether intrinsic manifold Gaussian processes provably beat extrinsic Euclidean restrictions in data efficiency.
nodes.approach: Posterior contraction analysis using Sobolev trace and extension theorems between manifold and ambient space.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Highly specialised geometric GP theory with few comparable papers.

nodes.title: Which Models have Perceptually-Aligned Gradients? An Explanation via Off-Manifold Robustness
nodes.tldr: Explains perceptually-aligned gradients via off-manifold robustness, showing input gradients align with the data manifold and correlate with perceptual alignment.
nodes.problem: Why robust classifiers have perceptually aligned input gradients and generative-like abilities.
nodes.approach: Off-manifold robustness theory, validated across gradient-norm, smoothing, and adversarial training.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised explanation of a known robustness phenomenon

nodes.title: 3D-LLM: Injecting the 3D World into Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: 3D-LLMs take 3D point clouds as input, trained on 300k collected 3D-language samples using 2D VLM backbones and localization, for captioning, QA, grounding and navigation.
nodes.problem: LLMs lack grounding in the 3D physical world
nodes.approach: Render multi-view features into 3D features, train on 3D-language data with localization mechanism
nodes.niche_reason: 3D language models are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
nodes.tldr: Trains a language model to decide when and how to call external tools such as calculators and search, using self-supervised data.
nodes.problem: LMs struggle with arithmetic and factual lookup despite strong few-shot ability.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised API-call insertion from a handful of demonstrations per tool.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Tool-use LMs are a crowded agent direction

nodes.title: STEVE-1: A Generative Model for Text-to-Behavior in Minecraft
nodes.tldr: Instruction-tunes a Minecraft video-pretrained policy to follow text and visual commands via a MineCLIP latent prior, using self-supervised relabeling for about $60.
nodes.problem: Instruction-following behavior models need costly instruction-labeled trajectory datasets.
nodes.approach: Adapt the policy to MineCLIP latent commands and train a text-to-latent prior with behavioral cloning.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Minecraft text-to-behavior models are a specialised niche

nodes.title: Pareto Frontiers in Deep Feature Learning: Data, Compute, Width, and Luck
nodes.tldr: Shows sparse parity learning exposes a data, compute, width and luck tradeoff; wide sparse-init MLPs improve tabular sample efficiency.
nodes.problem: Gradient-based training of MLPs on sparse parity faces a statistical query lower bound and poor sample efficiency.
nodes.approach: Sparse initialization and increased width to find lottery-ticket neurons, validated on tabular benchmarks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory on feature learning with a tabular application; primary area is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised sparse-parity feature learning analysis

nodes.title: Deep Fractional Fourier Transform
nodes.tldr: Introduces a fast 2D fractional Fourier transform and an MFRFC operator that jointly processes spatial and frequency views, improving many vision tasks.
nodes.problem: Vision networks treat spatial and frequency domains separately, missing unified representations for non-stationary images.
nodes.approach: Multi-order fractional Fourier convolution operator that can be inserted into existing backbones, with a fast 2D FRFT implementation.
nodes.confidence_reason: Fractional Fourier transform is a signal tool; primary area is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Fractional Fourier operators for vision are a rare transform

nodes.title: Puzzlefusion: Unleashing the Power of Diffusion Models for Spatial Puzzle Solving
nodes.tldr: Uses a conditional diffusion model to solve spatial puzzles, estimating 2D translations and rotations that align jigsaw pieces and room layouts, with new datasets.
nodes.problem: Aligning irregular puzzle pieces, such as jigsaw tiles and room layouts, needs an end-to-end model and training data.
nodes.approach: Diffusion as conditional generation of piece poses, trained on new synthetic Voronoi and real MagicPlan datasets.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based jigsaw and room-layout assembly is a rare application niche.

nodes.title: A Graph-Theoretic Framework for Understanding Open-World Semi-Supervised Learning
nodes.tldr: Graph-theoretic framework for open-world semi-supervised learning showing spectral open-world representation learning equals spectral decomposition, with provable clustering error bounds for known and novel classes.
nodes.problem: Open-world semi-supervised learning lacks theoretical foundations.
nodes.approach: Graph factorization formulation and SORL spectral loss with derived error bounds.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of open-world SSL is specialised.

nodes.title: ResShift: Efficient Diffusion Model for Image Super-resolution by Residual Shifting
nodes.tldr: Speeds up diffusion super-resolution by shifting residuals between LR and HR images, matching state-of-the-art quality in 20 sampling steps.
nodes.problem: Diffusion super-resolution needs hundreds of sampling steps, and acceleration blurs results.
nodes.approach: Residual-shifting Markov chain between image pairs with a tailored noise schedule controlling shift and noise.
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient diffusion super-resolution is a crowded direction

nodes.title: Normalizing flow neural networks by JKO scheme
nodes.tldr: Neural ODE normalizing flow trained block-wise via the JKO scheme for Wasserstein gradient flows, avoiding SDE sampling and score matching.
nodes.problem: End-to-end normalizing flow training is memory-heavy and hard to optimize.
nodes.approach: Stacked residual blocks trained block-wise with JKO-inspired steps and adaptive time reparameterization.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Wasserstein-flow-inspired flows are less common.

nodes.title: SimFBO: Towards Simple, Flexible and Communication-efficient Federated Bilevel Learning
nodes.tldr: SimFBO is a sub-loop-free federated bilevel optimization framework with generalized server aggregation, plus ShroFBO for system heterogeneity, with linear speedup and improved complexities.
nodes.problem: Existing federated bilevel optimization is complicated, needing sub-loops with many communication rounds.
nodes.approach: Simple single-loop FBO with generalized server-side aggregation and a heterogeneity-robust variant.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated bilevel optimization is a rare theory-heavy niche.

nodes.title: Differentially Private Approximate Near Neighbor Counting in High Dimensions
nodes.tldr: Presents a differentially private near-neighbor counting algorithm whose noise is dimension-free, using a locality-sensitive hashing variant and fuzzy range boundaries.
nodes.problem: Private range counting either has error polynomial in n or grows exponentially with dimension.
nodes.approach: Novel use of a locality-sensitive hashing variant, accepting fuzzy ball boundaries for dimension-free noise.
nodes.niche_reason: Dimension-free private near-neighbor counting is very rare

nodes.title: Thought Cloning: Learning to Think while Acting by Imitating Human Thinking
nodes.tldr: Thought Cloning trains agents to imitate human actions and the language thoughts behind them, generalizing better out of distribution and aiding interpretability and safety.
nodes.problem: RL agents lack human-like thinking in language, hurting generalization, planning and adaptation.
nodes.approach: Imitation learning of paired thoughts and actions with a hierarchical agent that generates thoughts before acting.
nodes.niche_reason: Imitating human inner-speech thoughts for agents is an unusual direction.

nodes.title: Students Parrot Their Teachers: Membership Inference on Model Distillation
nodes.tldr: Designs membership inference attacks showing knowledge distillation gives limited privacy to both teacher and student training sets, even without querying real training points.
nodes.problem: Whether model distillation actually protects the privacy of teacher and student training data.
nodes.approach: New membership inference attacks on distillation, including attacks querying only highly influenced inputs and teacher poisoning.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Privacy attacks on distillation are an established but specialised topic.

nodes.title: CS4ML: A general framework for active learning with arbitrary data based on Christoffel functions
nodes.tldr: Generalizes active regression sampling to arbitrary data types using generalized Christoffel functions, with near-optimal sample complexity guarantees.
nodes.problem: Active learning assumes pointwise samples, but scientific data often comes in transforms or gradients
nodes.approach: Optimize random sampling measures via generalized Christoffel functions over arbitrary nonlinear approximation spaces.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Active learning sits between sample-complexity theory and experimental design
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised active-learning theory for scientific computing

nodes.title: Feature Adaptation for Sparse Linear Regression
nodes.tldr: Gives a polynomial-time method that adapts the Lasso to ill-conditioned correlated designs, achieving near-optimal sample complexity for constant sparsity and few outlier eigenvalues.
nodes.problem: Lasso needs far more samples than necessary when covariates are correlated and ill-conditioned.
nodes.approach: Feature adaptation that automatically reshapes the design to tolerate a few approximate dependencies.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse regression theory is established; feature-adaptation framing is specialised

nodes.title: Inference-Time Intervention: Eliciting Truthful Answers from a Language Model
nodes.tldr: Inference-Time Intervention shifts activations along learned truthful directions in a few attention heads, roughly doubling Alpaca's TruthfulQA truthfulness.
nodes.problem: Language models produce falsehoods, and it is unclear how to steer them toward truthful answers cheaply.
nodes.approach: Learns truthful directions from a few hundred examples and adds them to selected attention-head activations at inference, tuning strength.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Activation steering for truthfulness is specialised but increasingly studied.

nodes.title: A Dynamical System View of Langevin-Based Non-Convex Sampling
nodes.tldr: Shows last-iterate Wasserstein convergence for many Langevin-type sampling schemes by reducing discrete-time analysis to their better-understood continuous-time counterparts.
nodes.problem: Existing non-convex sampling guarantees lack last-iterate bounds and cover few Langevin schemes.
nodes.approach: Reduce discrete sampler last-iterate analysis to continuous-time dynamics via dynamical-systems tools.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Sampling theory is established but specialised

nodes.title: Tree Variational Autoencoders
nodes.tldr: Tree-structured VAE that learns a hierarchical clustering of data with a tree-based latent posterior and specialized leaf decoders for generation.
nodes.problem: Existing generative models do not expose hierarchical cluster structure among latent variables.
nodes.approach: Learns the optimal tree over latent variables, with leaf decoders and per-cluster sampling.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Hierarchical VAE clustering is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Stable Nonconvex-Nonconcave Training via Linear Interpolation
nodes.tldr: Analyzes linear interpolation to stabilize nonconvex-nonconcave training, proposing RAPP with last-iterate convergence for comonotone problems and rediscovering Lookahead with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Training instabilities from nonmonotone loss landscapes in minimax problems like GANs.
nodes.approach: Relaxed approximate proximal point method using nonexpansive operator theory and linear interpolation.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Nonmonotone minimax operator theory is a specialised optimization niche.

nodes.title: Convergence of Alternating Gradient Descent for Matrix Factorization
nodes.tldr: Proves alternating gradient descent with fixed step size converges linearly on asymmetric matrix factorization from a random initialization, using uniform PL and smoothness arguments.
nodes.problem: Convergence rates of alternating gradient descent for nonconvex low-rank matrix factorization.
nodes.approach: Atypical random initialization plus uniform Polyak-Lojasiewicz and Lipschitz smoothness arguments with mild overparameterization.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Nonconvex factorization convergence theory is specialised but well-studied.

nodes.title: Uncovering the Hidden Dynamics of Video Self-supervised Learning under Distribution Shifts
nodes.tldr: Studies six video self-supervised methods under context, viewpoint, actor, source shifts, zero-shot and open-set settings using a 17-pair test bed, revealing method-specific robustness patterns.
nodes.problem: How video self-supervised models behave under different natural distribution shifts.
nodes.approach: Systematic benchmark of v-SimCLR, v-MoCo, v-BYOL, v-SimSiam, v-DINO, v-MAE across shift protocols.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Empirical robustness study of video SSL is specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Layer-wise Equivariances Automatically using Gradients
nodes.tldr: Learns the degree of equivariance per layer from data by optimizing a Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood over soft-equivariance parameterisations, discovering symmetries automatically.
nodes.problem: Symmetry constraints must be specified in advance and cannot adapt to the data.
nodes.approach: Flexible soft equivariance parameterisation with marginal likelihood optimization via differentiable Laplace approximations.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian automatic symmetry discovery is a rare direction.

nodes.title: Online Control for Meta-optimization
nodes.tldr: Formulates hyperparameter meta-optimization as an optimal control problem and uses convex relaxation from nonstochastic control to learn optimizers with regret guarantees.
nodes.problem: Choosing optimizer hyperparameters per instance is nonconvex, lacking global optimality guarantees.
nodes.approach: Optimal control formulation with convex relaxation for online learning of optimization methods.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Control-theoretic meta-optimization is a rare angle

nodes.title: Anonymous and Copy-Robust Delegations for Liquid Democracy
nodes.tldr: Studies fractional delegation rules for liquid democracy, proving Mixed Borda branching and random walk rule are equivalent and satisfy anonymity and copy-robustness, with polynomial-time computation.
nodes.problem: Trade-off between anonymity and copy-robustness in ranked delegation rules for liquid democracy.
nodes.approach: Markov chain tree theorem and Fulkerson's algorithm to analyze and compute fractional delegation rules.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Computational social choice and voting theory is very rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: Contrastive Lift: 3D Object Instance Segmentation by Slow-Fast Contrastive Fusion
nodes.tldr: Lifts 2D instance segments into 3D with a neural field, fusing them via a scalable slow-fast contrastive clustering objective.
nodes.problem: 3D instance segmentation lacks large annotated datasets and struggles with scenes containing many objects.
nodes.approach: Lifts pretrained 2D segmentations via neural fields with multi-view consistency, requiring no tracking or object-count bound.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: 2D-to-3D lifting for segmentation is a fairly common approach

nodes.title: Kiki or Bouba? Sound Symbolism in Vision-and-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Probes CLIP and Stable Diffusion with zero-shot tests and finds they exhibit sound symbolism, such as the kiki-bouba effect, linking pseudowords to shapes.
nodes.problem: Whether vision-language models reflect human sound-symbolic associations between speech sounds and visual meaning.
nodes.approach: Zero-shot knowledge probing of CLIP and Stable Diffusion using pseudowords and shape/visual associations.
nodes.niche_reason: Cognitive-science-inspired probing of sound symbolism is very rare.

nodes.title: Paxion: Patching Action Knowledge in Video-Language Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces ActionBench showing video-language models lack action knowledge, and Paxion, which patches frozen models with a Knowledge Patcher trained by a discriminative video dynamics objective.
nodes.problem: Video-language models lack understanding of actions and temporal order, relying on object shortcuts.
nodes.approach: Knowledge Patcher and Fuser added to frozen VidLMs, trained with discriminative video dynamics modeling loss.
nodes.niche_reason: Probing and patching action knowledge in VidLMs is specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video Generation
nodes.tldr: Casts sequential decision making as text-conditioned video generation: a planner synthesizes future frames for a goal, then actions are extracted, generalizing across tasks and robots.
nodes.problem: Building general-purpose agents that generalize to novel goals across environments with different state and action spaces.
nodes.approach: Text-conditioned video diffusion as planner with inverse dynamics to extract control actions.
nodes.confidence_reason: Could be video generation, planning or robot policy learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Video-generation-as-policy is an established but specialised direction.

nodes.title: Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Speeds up pretrained diffusion sampling by denoising multiple steps in parallel via Picard iterations, trading compute for speed without measurable quality loss.
nodes.problem: Diffusion sampling needs many sequential denoising steps, making generation slow.
nodes.approach: Guess future denoising steps and refine them with Picard iterations until convergence.
nodes.niche_reason: Common: diffusion sampler acceleration is crowded.

nodes.title: Tight Risk Bounds for Gradient Descent on Separable Data
nodes.tldr: Establishes tight upper and lower population risk bounds for gradient descent on separable linear classification for any smooth loss, depending on its tail decay rate.
nodes.problem: Tight generalization risk of unregularized gradient methods on separable data.
nodes.approach: Matching upper and lower bounds with a simpler proof technique, extended to SGD.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Established theory topic with specialised audience.

nodes.title: Monarch Mixer: A Simple Sub-Quadratic GEMM-Based Architecture
nodes.tldr: Monarch Mixer is a sub-quadratic architecture using Monarch matrices along both sequence and model dimensions, matching Transformers on language and vision with hardware-efficient GEMM operations.
nodes.problem: Transformers scale quadratically in sequence length and model dimension.
nodes.approach: Replace attention and MLPs with Monarch structured matrices as a single sub-quadratic primitive.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Structured-matrix architectures are an established but specialised alternative.

nodes.title: HIQL: Offline Goal-Conditioned RL with Latent States as Actions
nodes.tldr: HIQL learns goal-conditioned policies from offline data hierarchically with one action-free value function, a high-level policy predicting latent subgoals and a low-level policy reaching them.
nodes.problem: Estimating accurate values for far goals from offline data is hard in goal-conditioned RL.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical policies sharing an action-free value function, with latent states as high-level actions.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline goal-conditioned RL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: A Scalable Neural Network for DSIC Affine Maximizer Auction Design
nodes.tldr: Neural network that builds affine maximizer auction parameters and candidate allocations, guaranteeing DSIC and scaling to larger multi-item auctions.
nodes.problem: Regret-based auction networks lack DSIC, while affine maximizer auctions do not scale to many candidates
nodes.approach: Permutation-equivariant network generating AMA parameters and an allocation menu from bidder and item embeddings
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Neural DSIC auction design is a rare intersection

nodes.title: Precise asymptotic generalization for multiclass classification with overparameterized linear models
nodes.tldr: Resolves when overparameterized linear multiclass classifiers generalize, with misclassification rates tending to 0 or 1 asymptotically.
nodes.problem: The generalization regimes of overparameterized multiclass linear models were conjectured but not fully characterized.
nodes.approach: Tight lower and upper bounds under a Gaussian bi-level model, with a new Hanson-Wright variant.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Sharp multiclass asymptotics are a rare theory niche.

nodes.title: Bayesian Extensive-Rank Matrix Factorization with Rotational Invariant Priors
nodes.tldr: Derives rotation invariant estimators for noisy Bayesian extensive-rank matrix factorization, conjectured optimal in the large-dimension limit, using random matrix theory, spherical integrals and replica methods.
nodes.problem: Statistical and algorithmic limits of extensive-rank matrix factorization with noise are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Rotation invariant estimators derived with random matrix theory, spherical integrals, and replica method.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical-physics matrix factorization theory is very rare in ML.

nodes.title: Semi-Supervised Domain Generalization with Known and Unknown Classes
nodes.tldr: CWAEE handles semi-supervised domain generalization with mixed known and unknown classes, using one-vs-rest classifiers, adaptive thresholds and Fourier-based consistency regularization.
nodes.problem: Semi-supervised domain generalization when unlabeled data contains unknown classes alongside known ones.
nodes.approach: One-vs-rest class-wise adaptive thresholds to detect unknowns, plus Fourier-augmentation consistency regularization.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Open-set semi-supervised domain generalization is a specialised setting.

nodes.title: Context-PIPs: Persistent Independent Particles Demands Spatial Context Features
nodes.tldr: Improves tracking of query points in videos by aggregating spatial context features, reducing occluded-point trajectory error.
nodes.problem: Independent point trajectory estimation ignores spatial context, hurting accuracy for occluded points.
nodes.approach: Two modules, SOFE and TAFA, aggregate spatial context into source and target point features.
nodes.niche_reason: Common point-tracking area with incremental feature-aggregation gains.

nodes.title: Group Fairness in Peer Review
nodes.tldr: Assigns reviewers to papers so that no research community gains by withdrawing from a large conference, via a core-based group fairness notion.
nodes.problem: Large conferences give some communities poorly matched reviewers, while splitting them isolates fields.
nodes.approach: Simple peer-review model with an efficient algorithm that always finds a core-stable assignment.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: fairness framing versus game-theoretic mechanism design
nodes.niche_reason: core-based fairness for reviewer assignment is a rare angle

nodes.title: Demystifying Softmax Gating Function in Gaussian Mixture of Experts
nodes.tldr: Proves convergence rates for maximum likelihood parameter estimation in softmax-gated Gaussian mixture of experts, using novel Voronoi loss functions to handle identifiability.
nodes.problem: Parameter estimation for softmax-gated mixture of experts lacks theory, due to gating-expert interactions and identifiability issues.
nodes.approach: Voronoi loss functions among parameters, then MLE convergence analysis including over-specified expert counts.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: theory of MoE sits between architecture and statistical learning
nodes.niche_reason: Estimation theory for softmax-gated MoE is a rare theoretical niche

nodes.title: On the Learnability of Multilabel Ranking
nodes.tldr: Characterizes learnability of multilabel ranking under relevance-score feedback in batch and online settings, grouping ranking losses into two learnability classes.
nodes.problem: Whether multilabel ranking with relevance-score feedback is learnable has been unresolved.
nodes.approach: Learnability analysis of a broad family of ranking losses, yielding two equivalence classes of losses.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Learnability of multilabel ranking losses is rare

nodes.title: Privacy Assessment on Reconstructed Images: Are Existing Evaluation Metrics Faithful to Human Perception?
nodes.tldr: Shows PSNR and SSIM correlate weakly with human judgments of privacy leakage in reconstructed images, and proposes SemSim, a learned semantic metric.
nodes.problem: Whether hand-crafted image metrics faithfully reflect human perception of privacy leakage in reconstruction attacks.
nodes.approach: Human study across datasets and attacks; train SemSim with triplet loss on recognizability annotations.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Evaluating privacy metrics against human perception is uncommon.

nodes.title: On the Role of Randomization in Adversarially Robust Classification
nodes.tldr: Clarifies when randomized ensembles beat deterministic classifiers under adversarial risk, and proves any probabilistic binary classifier is outperformed by some deterministic one.
nodes.problem: Conflicting findings on whether randomization improves adversarial robustness of classifiers.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of adversarial risk for randomized ensembles and noise injection versus deterministic hypothesis sets.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial robustness theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: On the Gini-impurity Preservation For Privacy Random Forests
nodes.tldr: Proposes an encryption scheme for random forests that preserves Gini impurity in ciphertexts, with proofs of minimum-Gini preservation and security guarantees.
nodes.problem: Privacy-preserving random forests that keep the Gini impurity needed for tree construction.
nodes.approach: Modified binary search tree storing several examples per node, with encryption using label and order information.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: Encryption-based privacy for random forests fits no topic cleanly.
nodes.niche_reason: Encryption-based privacy for tree ensembles is very rare.

nodes.title: Supervised Pretraining Can Learn In-Context Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Decision-Pretrained Transformer is supervised-pretrained to predict optimal actions from in-context interaction data, yielding in-context RL linked to Bayesian posterior sampling with regret guarantees.
nodes.problem: Understanding and instilling in-context decision-making ability in transformers for bandits and MDPs.
nodes.approach: Supervised pretraining to predict optimal actions given query state and in-context dataset; theory via posterior sampling.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: In-context RL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: SPINN processes multi-dimensional PDE inputs per axis with forward-mode autodiff, cutting cost while scaling collocation points.
nodes.problem: Training PINNs on multi-dimensional PDEs needs huge numbers of collocation points at prohibitive cost.
nodes.approach: Per-axis separable network architecture combined with forward-mode autodiff for PDE residuals.
nodes.niche_reason: Separable architecture for scalable PINN training is specialised

nodes.title: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
nodes.tldr: BIRD is a text-to-SQL benchmark over 95 large, dirty databases, showing that database values and SQL efficiency remain hard even for GPT-4.
nodes.problem: Text-to-SQL benchmarks use small database contents, leaving a gap between academic evaluation and real-world databases.
nodes.approach: 12,751 question-SQL pairs over 37 professional domains, with external knowledge and an execution-efficiency analysis.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Text-to-SQL is a well-populated benchmark area

nodes.title: Slow and Weak Attractor Computation Embedded in Fast and Strong E-I Balanced Neural Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Shows continuous attractor networks and excitation-inhibition balanced networks can coexist by using two synapse sets, one strong-fast and one weak-slow.
nodes.problem: Attractor networks and E-I balanced networks need conflicting connectivity, so they are usually studied separately.
nodes.approach: Dual-synapse neural circuit model with simulations and theory, applied to fast object tracking.
nodes.niche_reason: Computational neuroscience of attractors and E-I balance; very few ML-adjacent peers

nodes.title: DataComp: In search of the next generation of multimodal datasets
nodes.tldr: DataComp is a benchmark for dataset design with a 12.8B image-text candidate pool and standardized CLIP training, producing DataComp-1B that beats OpenAI's CLIP ViT-L/14.
nodes.problem: Dataset design for multimodal models gets little systematic research attention compared with architectures.
nodes.approach: Fixed CLIP training pipeline across compute scales where participants submit filtering strategies, evaluated on 38 downstream sets.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Data curation for CLIP is a popular area.

nodes.title: Human-like Few-Shot Learning via Bayesian Reasoning over Natural Language
nodes.tldr: Models human-like concept induction as Bayesian reasoning where a language model proposes natural-language hypotheses reweighted by a human-estimated prior and likelihood.
nodes.problem: Concept learning must balance tractable inference against expressive hypothesis classes, as humans do.
nodes.approach: Language model proposes hypotheses in natural language; Bayesian reweighting with a human-estimated prior.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Cognitive-science concept learning sits between meta-learning and Bayesian inference.
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian induction over LM-proposed hypotheses is an unusual cognitive angle.

nodes.title: Epistemic Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Introduces the epinet, a small add-on network giving joint predictive uncertainty that beats huge ensembles at far lower compute.
nodes.problem: Getting good joint predictions and uncertainty from neural networks without prohibitively large ensembles.
nodes.approach: Epinet architecture supplementing pretrained networks, formalized as epistemic neural networks evaluated on joint predictions.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Uncertainty estimation is established; the joint-prediction framing is specialised.

nodes.title: Sample Complexity of Forecast Aggregation
nodes.tldr: Proves forecast aggregation from report samples needs sample complexity exponential in expert count in general, but not when signals are conditionally independent.
nodes.problem: Sample complexity of learning an optimal aggregator of experts' probabilistic forecasts.
nodes.approach: Reduction from distribution learning for lower bounds, plus upper bound under conditional independence.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Information aggregation theory is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Hypernetwork-based Meta-Learning for Low-Rank Physics-Informed Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proposes lightweight low-rank PINNs and a hypernetwork-based meta-learning algorithm to rapidly approximate PDE solutions across varying input parameters, mitigating PINN failure modes.
nodes.problem: PINNs need repeated costly training for many-query PDE scenarios with varying parameters.
nodes.approach: Low-rank PINN with hundreds of parameters whose weights are generated by a meta-learned hypernetwork.
nodes.niche_reason: PINN variants are established; hypernetwork meta-learning angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Private (Stochastic) Non-Convex Optimization Revisited: Second-Order Stationary Points and Excess Risks
nodes.tldr: Proposes a variance-reduced DP framework with two gradient oracles for private second-order stationary points, and analyzes the exponential mechanism for global minima.
nodes.problem: Differentially private non-convex optimization: stationary points and excess risk.
nodes.approach: SpiderBoost-based dual-oracle algorithm and exponential mechanism analysis with lower bounds.
nodes.niche_reason: Private non-convex optimization theory is a narrow niche.

nodes.title: Evaluating Post-hoc Explanations for Graph Neural Networks via Robustness Analysis
nodes.tldr: Proposes OAR, an OOD-resistant adversarial-robustness metric for evaluating post-hoc GNN explanation subgraphs, plus a faster SimOAR variant.
nodes.problem: Evaluating GNN explanations by feeding explanatory subgraphs suffers from out-of-distribution artifacts.
nodes.approach: Measure explanation subgraph robustness under attack with an OOD reweighting block, plus a simplified efficient version.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised evaluation of explanations for graph models.

nodes.title: What Planning Problems Can A Relational Neural Network Solve?
nodes.tldr: Circuit complexity analysis of graph and transformer policies for planning, showing three classes of planning problems by how circuit width and depth scale.
nodes.problem: When relational networks can represent goal-conditioned planning policies, and how efficient they are.
nodes.approach: Constructive circuit complexity proofs drawing on serialized goal regression search.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Planning topic and complexity-theory topic both plausible
nodes.niche_reason: Circuit complexity of learned planning policies is rare

nodes.title: A Rigorous Link between Deep Ensembles and (Variational) Bayesian Methods
nodes.tldr: Gives a rigorous link between deep ensembles, Bayesian and variational Bayesian methods through Wasserstein gradient flows, deriving interacting ensembles with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Lack of a unified theory connecting deep ensembles with Bayesian and variational inference.
nodes.approach: Reformulate training as convex optimization over probability measures using generalised variational inference and Wasserstein gradient flows.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Wasserstein-flow theory unifying ensembles and Bayes is uncommon.

nodes.title: Inferring the Future by Imagining the Past
nodes.tldr: Monte Carlo sampler that infers past and future events from a static scene, matching human intuitions via path-tracing ideas.
nodes.problem: Humans infer event sequences from a single static snapshot; models of this are missing.
nodes.approach: Monte Carlo inverse-planning algorithm using few samples, borrowing path-tracing techniques.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: cognitive-science inverse planning vs Bayesian inference is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: cognitive-science inference linked to graphics path tracing

nodes.title: Model Spider: Learning to Rank Pre-Trained Models Efficiently
nodes.tldr: Learns to rank pre-trained models for a target task by embedding models and tasks, avoiding costly passes over the whole zoo.
nodes.problem: Choosing the best pre-trained model for a task is costly when every model must be run.
nodes.approach: Tokenize models and tasks into vectors, learn a fitness score on training tasks, then re-rank top candidates.
nodes.confidence_reason: Ranking pre-trained models; transfer vs meta-learning is close.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned pre-trained model ranking is established but specialised

nodes.title: Continual Learning for Instruction Following from Realtime Feedback
nodes.tldr: Continually trains an instruction-following agent from users' binary realtime feedback, treating feedback as reward in a contextual bandit, improving accuracy over time.
nodes.problem: Improving an instruction-following agent continually from live binary user feedback during collaboration.
nodes.approach: Contextual bandit learning that converts realtime binary user feedback into immediate reward.

nodes.niche_reason: Learning from live user feedback in instruction following is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Privacy Auditing with One (1) Training Run
nodes.tldr: A privacy auditing scheme gets empirical DP lower bounds for DP-SGD from one training run by adding or removing many examples in parallel.
nodes.problem: Auditing differentially private training usually requires training hundreds of models.
nodes.approach: Parallel independent insertion and removal of training examples, analyzed via DP-to-generalization connection.
