nodes.title: Reinforcement Learning Gradients as Vitamin for Online Finetuning Decision Transformers
nodes.tldr: Shows that adding TD3 gradients to online fine-tuning of Decision Transformers fixes poor return-to-go estimates, improving performance after low-reward offline pretraining.
nodes.problem: Online fine-tuning of the Online Decision Transformer struggles when pretrained on low-reward data.

secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Decision transformers are common; RL-gradient hybrids are a familiar variant.

nodes.title: Scalable and Effective Arithmetic Tree Generation for Adder and Multiplier Designs
nodes.tldr: ArithTreeRL casts adder and multiplier design as tree-generation games solved with reinforcement learning, improving delay and size over prior arithmetic design methods.
nodes.problem: Adder and multiplier units limit speed and area, and prior design methods optimize them poorly.

nodes.title: VASA-1: Lifelike Audio-Driven Talking Faces Generated in Real Time

nodes.title: LightGaussian: Unbounded 3D Gaussian Compression with 15x Reduction and 200+ FPS

nodes.title: The Sample-Communication Complexity Trade-off in Federated Q-Learning

nodes.title: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation of Large Language Models

nodes.title: Memorize What Matters: Emergent Scene Decomposition from Multitraverse

nodes.title: Ensemble Learning for Heterogeneous Large Language Models with Deep Parallel Collaboration

nodes.niche_reason: LLM ensembling at the distribution level across vocabularies is specialised.

nodes.title: The Power of Resets in Online Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows that online RL with local simulator access (resets to visited states) enables sample-efficient learning under Q*-realizability for low-coverability MDPs, including Exogenous Block MDPs.
nodes.problem: Online RL needs strong representation assumptions even when simulators are available.
nodes.approach: Local planning with resets, plus RVFS, a recursive value-function search algorithm for computational efficiency.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Simulator-reset RL theory is established but specialised

nodes.title: QTIP: Quantization with Trellises and Incoherence Processing
nodes.tldr: QTIP uses trellis coded quantization with incoherence processing for ultra-high-dimensional LLM weight quantization, achieving state-of-the-art quality and fast, hardware-efficient inference.
nodes.problem: Vector quantization for LLMs is limited to low dimensions by exponentially large codebooks.
nodes.approach: Trellis coded quantization with bitshift trellis and lookup-free computed codes plus incoherence processing.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning

nodes.title: Not All Diffusion Model Activations Have Been Evaluated as Discriminative Features
nodes.tldr: Studies which diffusion model activations serve as dense discriminative features, identifying universal properties that let inferior activations be filtered qualitatively.
nodes.problem: Selecting effective discriminative activations from many diffusion backbone signals is unresolved, and full-scale comparison is infeasible.
nodes.approach: Three universal properties identified via qualitative analysis, then feature selection for several popular diffusion models.
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion activations as features: representation or diffusion topic is ambiguous.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion features for dense tasks is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Benign overfitting in leaky ReLU networks with moderate input dimension
nodes.tldr: Characterizes benign versus harmful overfitting in two-layer leaky ReLU networks trained with hinge loss by signal-to-noise ratio, requiring only input dimension linear in sample size.
nodes.problem: When interpolating leaky ReLU networks generalize, without requiring near-orthogonal training data.
nodes.approach: Approximate margin maximization analysis of gradient descent under signal-plus-noise data decomposition.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Benign overfitting theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Scale Equivariant Graph Metanetworks
nodes.tldr: Message-passing metanetwork that is equivariant to scaling symmetries of weights and biases, used to process neural network parameters.
nodes.problem: Weight-space networks ignore scaling symmetries introduced by common activation functions.
nodes.approach: Graph metanetwork with scale-equivariant neuron and edge representations; can simulate feedforward passes.
nodes.confidence_reason: Weight-space GNN; ambiguous between GNN and representation learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: scaling-symmetry equivariant processing of network weights.

nodes.title: Is Behavior Cloning All You Need? Understanding Horizon in Imitation Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves that behavior cloning with log loss can achieve horizon-independent sample complexity offline, showing the offline-online imitation learning gap is not fundamental.
nodes.problem: Whether offline behavior cloning inherently suffers quadratic horizon dependence compared with online imitation learning.
nodes.approach: New learning-theoretic analysis of BC with logarithmic loss for general policy classes, with supporting experiments.
nodes.niche_reason: Imitation learning theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Saliency-driven Experience Replay for Continual Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses predicted visual saliency as a modulation signal in experience replay, improving continual learning classifiers and their robustness to spurious features and attacks.
nodes.problem: Catastrophic forgetting in continual classification when tasks arrive as non-i.i.d. sequences.
nodes.approach: Auxiliary saliency prediction features modulate and stabilize replay-based learning across task sequences.
nodes.niche_reason: Replay is crowded; saliency-modulated replay is specialised.

nodes.title: Extensive-Form Game Solving via Blackwell Approachability on Treeplexes
nodes.tldr: Provides a Blackwell approachability framework on the sequence-form polytope, yielding stepsize-invariant regret minimizers and an O(1/T) Nash convergence rate in self-play.
nodes.problem: Extensive-form game solving lacks stepsize-invariant regret minimizers on sequence-form strategy spaces.
nodes.approach: Blackwell approachability over treeplexes, combined with predictive online mirror descent in self-play.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Treeplex approachability for extensive-form games is a niche algorithmic area

nodes.title: BricksRL: A Platform for Democratizing Robotics and Reinforcement Learning Research and Education with LEGO
nodes.tldr: A platform linking LEGO hubs to TorchRL so cheap robots can be trained end-to-end in the real world for RL research and education.
nodes.problem: Real-world robot RL is inaccessible and costly for research and education
nodes.approach: Bluetooth bridge from LEGO hubs to the TorchRL library
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Platform paper; closest topics are hardware and RL.
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual educational LEGO-based RL platform, few close analogues

nodes.title: Efficient Adversarial Training in LLMs with Continuous Attacks
nodes.tldr: Proposes C-AdvUL and C-AdvIPO, which run adversarial training in continuous embedding space to make LLMs robust to discrete jailbreak attacks at far lower cost.
nodes.problem: Discrete adversarial attacks used in LLM adversarial training are too computationally expensive per iteration.
nodes.approach: Continuous embedding-space attacks trained with a utility-preserving fine-tuning loss, plus an adversarial IPO variant.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks

nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial training for LLM robustness is an active mainstream area

nodes.title: Finding Transformer Circuits With Edge Pruning
nodes.tldr: Discovers transformer circuits by gradient-based pruning of edges between components, yielding sparser, faithful circuits that scale to CodeLlama-13B.
nodes.problem: Existing circuit discovery relies on inefficient search or inaccurate approximations.
nodes.approach: Gradient-based pruning applied to edges rather than neurons, framed as an optimization problem.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning

nodes.title: Provable Benefit of Cutout and CutMix for Feature Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves CutMix learns rarer features than Cutout and vanilla training in two-layer networks, explaining its higher test accuracy.
nodes.problem: Theoretical understanding of why patch-level augmentations like Cutout and CutMix help is missing.
nodes.approach: Analyze two-layer networks on a feature-noise data model under vanilla, Cutout, and CutMix training.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of augmentation is specialised; Cutout and CutMix are well studied.

nodes.title: NeuroClips: Towards High-fidelity and Smooth fMRI-to-Video Reconstruction
nodes.tldr: NeuroClips reconstructs smooth, high-fidelity video from fMRI by combining a semantics reconstructor for keyframes and a perception reconstructor for low-level flow with a text-to-video diffusion model.
nodes.problem: Decoding continuous visual experience from fMRI into smooth, faithful video is hard.
nodes.approach: Semantic keyframe and perception-flow reconstructors guiding a pre-trained text-to-video diffusion model.
nodes.niche_reason: Brain-to-video decoding is a rare cross-disciplinary topic.

nodes.title: SpikeReveal: Unlocking Temporal Sequences from Real Blurry Inputs with Spike Streams
nodes.tldr: First self-supervised framework for spike-guided motion deblurring, recovering sharp image sequences from blurry inputs using spike camera streams.
nodes.problem: Supervised spike-based deblurring degrades on real scenes that differ from the synthetic training data.
nodes.approach: Cascaded self-supervised model with knowledge distillation and a re-blurring loss in a lightweight deblur network.
nodes.niche_reason: Spike-camera guided deblurring is a rare sensor-specific niche

nodes.title: Optimization Algorithm Design via Electric Circuits
nodes.tldr: Designs convex optimisation algorithms by first building an RLC circuit whose dynamics solve the problem, then automatically discretising it into provably convergent methods.
nodes.problem: Designing convergent optimisation algorithms, especially distributed ones, is laborious and ad hoc.
nodes.approach: Map problems to RLC circuit continuous-time dynamics, then computer-assisted discretisation with convergence guarantees.
nodes.niche_reason: Circuit-analogy algorithm design is a rare cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Weisfeiler and Leman Go Loopy: A New Hierarchy for Graph Representational Learning
nodes.tldr: Introduces r-loopy Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy and r-loopy MPNN that count cycles up to length r+2 and homomorphisms of cactus graphs, incomparable to k-WL.
nodes.problem: Increasing the expressive and counting power of GNNs beyond 1-WL.

nodes.niche_reason: GNN expressivity theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Context and Geometry Aware Voxel Transformer for Semantic Scene Completion
nodes.tldr: Introduces a voxel transformer with context-aware queries and 3D deformable attention to resolve depth ambiguity in vision-based semantic scene completion.
nodes.problem: Shared queries and missing depth cues cause undirected aggregation and depth ambiguity in SSC.
nodes.approach: Image-specific query generation plus cross-attention extended to 3D space, combined with voxel and TPV representations.
nodes.niche_reason: Semantic scene completion is a specialised 3D perception topic

nodes.title: Disentangling the Roles of Distinct Cell Classes with Cell-Type Dynamical Systems
nodes.tldr: Cell-type dynamical systems give each neuron class its own latent with sign-constrained dynamics, predicting cell-specific perturbation effects on behavior.
nodes.problem: Latent dynamical models of neural population activity ignore multiple cell types, limiting interpretation of perturbations.
nodes.approach: Latent linear dynamical system with separate excitatory and inhibitory latents and biologically constrained emissions.

nodes.niche_reason: Cell-class latent dynamics for perturbation modelling is rare

nodes.title: MultiOOD: Scaling Out-of-Distribution Detection for Multiple Modalities
nodes.tldr: Introduces MultiOOD, a benchmark for multimodal out-of-distribution detection, plus the Agree-to-Disagree training algorithm and NP-Mix outlier synthesis that improve detection.
nodes.problem: OOD detection research focuses on unimodal image data, ignoring multimodal real-world settings.
nodes.approach: Benchmark across modality combinations, A2D encouraging modality prediction discrepancy, NP-Mix nearest-class outlier synthesis.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal OOD detection is established but specialised.

nodes.title: DiffLight: A Partial Rewards Conditioned Diffusion Model for Traffic Signal Control with Missing Data
nodes.tldr: Uses a conditional diffusion model to jointly impute missing traffic data and choose signal timings in offline traffic signal control.
nodes.problem: Traffic signal control fails when sensor data from neighbouring intersections is missing or lost.
nodes.approach: Partial-reward conditioned diffusion with a spatial-temporal transformer and a diffusion communication mechanism.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion-based control with missing data spans offline RL and generative modelling.
nodes.niche_reason: Traffic control with missing sensor data is specialised but established.

nodes.title: MassSpecGym: A benchmark for the discovery and identification of molecules
nodes.tldr: MassSpecGym is a large public benchmark for MS/MS molecule identification, with de novo structure generation, molecule retrieval and spectrum simulation tasks and a generalization-demanding split.
nodes.problem: Predicting molecular structures from tandem mass spectra lacks standard datasets and evaluation protocols.
nodes.approach: Curate largest public MS/MS spectra collection, define three annotation tasks, metrics, and a structure-based data split.
nodes.niche_reason: Mass spectrometry ML is a rare scientific niche.

nodes.title: Many-Shot In-Context Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows hundreds of in-context examples boost LLM performance, and that model-generated or no rationales can work nearly as well.
nodes.problem: Few-shot ICL is limited; many-shot prompts need scarce human-written rationales.
nodes.approach: Many-shot prompting with reinforced (model-generated) and unsupervised rationale-free examples.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Many-shot ICL studies are increasingly common

nodes.title: Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Presents Buffer of Thoughts, which stores reusable high-level thought templates, retrieves and instantiates one per problem, and updates the buffer as tasks are solved.
nodes.problem: Multi-query reasoning methods are costly, and single-query prompting lacks reusable problem-solving structure.
nodes.approach: A meta-buffer of distilled thought templates, adaptively instantiated per problem and managed by a buffer manager.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Prompting-based reasoning augmentation is a common LLM direction

nodes.title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
nodes.tldr: xLSTM scales LSTMs for language modeling with exponential gating and new scalar (sLSTM) and parallelizable matrix-memory (mLSTM) cells, competing with Transformers and state-space models.
nodes.problem: Whether scaled-up LSTMs can compete with Transformers and SSMs in language modeling.
nodes.approach: Exponential gating, sLSTM and mLSTM memory structures stacked in residual xLSTM blocks.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention

nodes.title: QKFormer: Hierarchical Spiking Transformer using Q-K Attention
nodes.tldr: QKFormer is a hierarchical spiking transformer with linear-complexity binary Q-K attention and deformed-shortcut patch embedding, reaching over 85% ImageNet-1K accuracy for directly trained SNNs.
nodes.problem: Spiking neural networks lag behind ANNs in accuracy while spiking transformers need efficient attention.
nodes.approach: Spike-form Q-K attention, hierarchical multi-scale tokens, and Spiking Patch Embedding with Deformed Shortcut.
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking transformers are a rare neuromorphic niche.

nodes.title: Flexible task abstractions emerge in linear networks with fast and bounded units
nodes.tldr: Analyzes linear gated networks with fast, non-negative, bounded gates, showing weights specialize into task modules and gates form task abstractions, mirroring cognitive neuroscience findings on flexibility.
nodes.problem: How flexible task abstractions emerge in neural systems under changing data distributions.
nodes.approach: Analytical reduction of gradient-descent learning dynamics in a linear gated network to an effective eigenspace.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of cognitive flexibility via gated linear networks is rare.

nodes.title: Auditing Privacy Mechanisms via Label Inference Attacks
nodes.tldr: Proposes reconstruction-advantage measures to audit label privatization schemes, theoretically and empirically showing differentially private schemes dominate or match heuristic schemes on privacy-utility tradeoffs.
nodes.problem: Labels released through privatization schemes need auditing for how much they leak about true labels.
nodes.approach: Additive and multiplicative reconstruction-advantage measures, analyzed under a distributional model and tested empirically.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Privacy auditing of label release is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Semi-supervised Multi-label Learning with Balanced Binary Angular Margin Loss
nodes.tldr: A semi-supervised multi-label method using a balanced binary angular margin loss to fix variance bias between positive and negative feature angle distributions during self-training.
nodes.problem: Self-training in semi-supervised multi-label learning suffers variance bias between positive and negative sample feature distributions.
nodes.approach: Balanced angular margin loss with Gaussian feature-angle distribution transformation and prototype-based negative sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: Semi-supervised multi-label learning is a rare niche.

nodes.title: A Phase Transition between Positional and Semantic Learning in a Solvable Model of Dot-Product Attention
nodes.tldr: Closed-form analysis of a solvable dot-product attention model shows a phase transition from positional to semantic attention as sample complexity grows.
nodes.problem: How algorithmic mechanisms such as semantic attention emerge during language model training is theoretically unclear.
nodes.approach: Replica-method analysis of a non-linear self-attention layer with tied, low-rank query and key matrices.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical-physics analysis of attention emergence is a rare theoretical niche

nodes.title: GAIA: Rethinking Action Quality Assessment for AI-Generated Videos

nodes.title: Reverse Transition Kernel: A Flexible Framework to Accelerate Diffusion Inference

nodes.title: Flipped Classroom: Aligning Teacher Attention with Student in Generalized Category Discovery
nodes.tldr: Makes the teacher in a teacher-student semi-supervised setup update its attention to match the student, improving generalized category discovery.

nodes.title: DeSparsify: Adversarial Attack Against Token Sparsification Mechanisms
nodes.tldr: Presents DeSparsify, an adversarial attack that forces token-sparsified vision transformers into worst-case compute, degrading availability while staying stealthy.
nodes.problem: Input-dependent token sparsification in vision transformers can be exploited to exhaust resources.

nodes.niche_reason: Attacks on efficiency mechanisms in vision transformers are a rare direction

nodes.title: Variational Delayed Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: Reformulates RL with delayed observations as variational inference, alternating TD learning in a delay-free environment with behavior cloning for better sample efficiency.

nodes.title: BioTrove: A Large Curated Image Dataset Enabling AI for Biodiversity

nodes.title: Are Language Models Actually Useful for Time Series Forecasting?

nodes.title: Instruction Tuning Large Language Models to Understand Electronic Health Records
nodes.tldr: Releases MIMIC-Instr, 400K instruction-following examples from MIMIC-IV, and Llemr, a framework letting LLMs process complex EHR data for question answering and clinical prediction.

nodes.title: CVQA: Culturally-diverse Multilingual Visual Question Answering Benchmark

nodes.title: FuseFL: One-Shot Federated Learning through the Lens of Causality with Progressive Model Fusion

nodes.title: Approximating mutual information of high-dimensional variables using learned representations

nodes.title: No-regret Learning in Harmonic Games: Extrapolation in the Face of Conflicting Interests

nodes.title: Towards Understanding Evolving Patterns in Sequential Data

nodes.title: Real-world Image Dehazing with Coherence-based Pseudo Labeling and Cooperative Unfolding Network

nodes.title: Principled Bayesian Optimization in Collaboration with Human Experts
nodes.tldr: A principled Bayesian optimization method that uses binary accept/reject advice from possibly unreliable human experts, with handover and no-harm guarantees.

nodes.title: Probablistic Emulation of a Global Climate Model with Spherical DYffusion

nodes.title: $\texttt{dattri}$: A Library for Efficient Data Attribution

nodes.title: Stochastic Taylor Derivative Estimator: Efficient amortization for arbitrary differential operators

nodes.title: Non-convolutional graph neural networks.

nodes.title: Energy-Guided Continuous Entropic Barycenter Estimation for General Costs

nodes.title: Connecting Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Contrastive Self-supervised Learning

nodes.title: Fine Tuning Out-of-Vocabulary Item Recommendation with User Sequence Imagination

nodes.problem: Causal effects may be unidentifiable, and graphs require many observed variables.
nodes.approach: Elimination procedure removing functional variables while preserving identifiability.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Functional-dependency causal identification is specialised

nodes.title: Enhancing Zero-Shot Vision Models by Label-Free Prompt Distribution Learning and Bias Correcting
nodes.tldr: Label-free CLIP zero-shot method that learns prompt prototype distributions, fuses them with CLIP by confidence matching, and corrects label bias without hyperparameter tuning.
nodes.problem: CLIP zero-shot performance suffers from Web-data label bias, and prompt tuning needs labels.
nodes.approach: Learned prompt prototype distributions fused with CLIP, plus label-free logit adjustment.
nodes.niche_reason: Common: CLIP prompt adaptation is crowded.

nodes.title: Parallel Backpropagation for Shared-Feature Visualization
nodes.tldr: Visualizes shared visual features driving macaque IT neurons' responses to out-of-category images by backpropagating matched activations of a reference image to pixels.
nodes.problem: Explaining why out-of-category images excite neurons selective for faces or bodies.
nodes.approach: Pick a similarly activating reference image, backpropagate both to pixels, enhancing shared dimensions.
nodes.confidence_reason: neuroscience versus interpretability is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: macaque IT shared-feature visualization is a very rare niche

nodes.title: AuctionNet: A Novel Benchmark for Decision-Making in Large-Scale Games
nodes.tldr: AuctionNet is a benchmark of a realistic large-scale ad auction environment, a 500M-record dataset, and baseline auto-bidding algorithms, used in the NeurIPS 2024 competition.
nodes.problem: Lack of realistic large-scale game environments hinders research on bid decision-making.
nodes.approach: Simulated GSP ad auction with generative opportunity module, diverse bidding agents, pre-generated data, and baseline evaluations.
nodes.niche_reason: Ad auction bidding benchmark is a rare application setting.

nodes.title: Observational Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Langauge Model Performance
nodes.tldr: Builds scaling laws from about 100 public models without training, showing emergent abilities and agent performance are predictable from simpler benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Scaling laws require training many models across scales, which is costly and limits their use.
nodes.approach: Fits a low-dimensional capability space across model families that differ only in compute efficiency.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Observational scaling analysis is established but specialised

nodes.title: Mean-Field Langevin Dynamics for Signed Measures via a Bilevel Approach
nodes.tldr: Extends mean-field Langevin dynamics to signed measures via a bilevel reduction, with convergence guarantees for infinite-width two-layer networks and sparse deconvolution.
nodes.problem: MFLD only handles probability measures, not signed-measure problems like two-layer networks.
nodes.approach: Bilevel reformulation from signed to probability measures with log-Sobolev-based guarantees.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field Langevin for signed measures is very specialized theory.

nodes.title: Questioning the Survey Responses of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Evaluates 43 LLMs on American Community Survey questions, finding ordering and label biases and, once debiased, near-uniform random answers that mislead demographic alignment conclusions.
nodes.problem: Using LLM survey responses to infer represented demographics or values may be unreliable.
nodes.approach: Large-scale evaluation on census survey questions with randomized answer ordering.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Survey-based LLM opinion evaluation is a specialised social-science angle.

nodes.title: Diffusion Priors for Variational Likelihood Estimation and Image Denoising
nodes.tldr: Uses diffusion priors with adaptive likelihood estimation and MAP inference in the reverse process to denoise real-world structured, signal-dependent noise.
nodes.problem: Diffusion-prior denoisers handle only simple noise or use approximate posteriors.
nodes.approach: Adaptive variational likelihood estimation combined with MAP inference during reverse diffusion.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based restoration is common.

nodes.title: DenoiseRep: Denoising Model for Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: Treats each embedding layer of a backbone as a denoising step, then fuses denoising into the weights so the result is computation-free and label-free.
nodes.problem: Denoising models are powerful generators but underused for discriminative representation learning.
nodes.approach: Cascaded embedding layers act as recursive denoisers, fused into backbone parameters without extra compute.
nodes.confidence_reason: Denoising reframed as representation learning; could fit vision or generative areas.
nodes.niche_reason: Denoising for discriminative features is established but specialised.

nodes.title: 3DGS-Enhancer: Enhancing Unbounded 3D Gaussian Splatting with View-consistent 2D Diffusion Priors
nodes.tldr: Enhances 3D Gaussian splatting reconstructions of unbounded scenes by restoring novel views with a video diffusion prior, then fine-tuning the 3DGS model on them.
nodes.problem: Sparse-view novel view synthesis with 3DGS leaves under-sampled regions with artefacts.
nodes.approach: Treat view consistency as temporal consistency in video diffusion; spatial-temporal decoder fuses restored and input views.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: 3DGS with diffusion priors is a crowded, popular direction.

nodes.title: Thompson Sampling For Combinatorial Bandits: Polynomial Regret and Mismatched Sampling Paradox
nodes.tldr: Proposes a Thompson Sampling variant for combinatorial bandits with polynomial regret, and shows a mismatched-sampling paradox where knowing true rewards hurts.
nodes.problem: Thompson Sampling regret in combinatorial semi-bandits scales exponentially with problem dimension.
nodes.approach: Thompson Sampling with a well-chosen Gaussian posterior, plus finite-time regret analysis.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised bandit theory, not mainstream ML.

nodes.title: Recursive PAC-Bayes: A Frequentist Approach to Sequential Prior Updates with No Information Loss
nodes.tldr: A PAC-Bayes procedure enabling sequential prior updates without losing confidence information, so final bounds reflect all sequentially used data.
nodes.problem: PAC-Bayes final bounds lose confidence from data-dependent priors, limiting sequential prior updates
nodes.approach: Decompose posterior loss into excess loss relative to a downscaled prior loss, bounded recursively.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised PAC-Bayes bound theory

nodes.title: DreamCatcher: A Wearer-aware Multi-modal Sleep Event Dataset Based on Earables in Non-restrictive Environments
nodes.tldr: DreamCatcher is the first public wearer-aware sleep event dataset on earables with dual-channel audio and motion from 12 pairs of sleepers, with benchmarks.
nodes.problem: No dataset for wearer-aware sleep event detection on earables
nodes.approach: Collect 210 hours of synchronous audio and motion with fine labels; benchmark models
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Earable sleep sensing dataset is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: DapperFL: Domain Adaptive Federated Learning with Model Fusion Pruning for Edge Devices
nodes.tldr: A heterogeneous federated learning framework that prunes personalized compact local models using fused cross-domain knowledge, with domain-adaptive regularization, for edge devices.
nodes.problem: Federated learning on edge devices suffers from system heterogeneity and domain shift.
nodes.approach: Model fusion pruning for compact local models plus domain-adaptive regularization and heterogeneous aggregation.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Heterogeneous federated learning with domain shift and pruning; established but specialised.

nodes.title: Scaling Proprioceptive-Visual Learning with Heterogeneous Pre-trained Transformers
nodes.tldr: Heterogeneous Pre-trained Transformers align proprioception and vision from different embodiments into token sequences feeding a shared trunk, scaling robot policy pretraining across 52 datasets.
nodes.problem: Heterogeneity across robot embodiments and tasks blocks generalist robot policy training.
nodes.approach: Embodiment-specific stems map proprioception and vision to tokens for a shared pre-trained transformer trunk.
nodes.niche_reason: Robot foundation models and cross-embodiment pretraining are very active.

nodes.title: Algebraic Positional Encodings
nodes.tldr: Proposes positional encodings derived from the algebraic specification of a domain, treating positions as orthogonal operators, covering sequences, grids, trees and their compositions.
nodes.problem: Positional encodings for Transformers are ad hoc and do not preserve domain structure.
nodes.approach: Map algebraic domain specification to positional encodings where positions act as orthogonal operators.
nodes.niche_reason: Positional encoding research is established; algebraic framing is more specialised.

nodes.title: Second-order forward-mode optimization of recurrent neural networks for neuroscience
nodes.tldr: Introduces SOFO, a backpropagation-free second-order optimizer using batched forward-mode differentiation, enabling constant-memory RNN training for brain-dynamics models.
nodes.problem: RNN brain models have ill-conditioned loss surfaces and backprop cannot handle long horizons.
nodes.approach: Second-order updates from parallel batched forward-mode directional derivatives, avoiding backpropagation through time.
nodes.niche_reason: Backprop-free second-order training for brain models is rare.

nodes.title: ConvBench: A Multi-Turn Conversation Evaluation Benchmark with Hierarchical Ablation Capability for Large Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: ConvBench is a benchmark of 577 multi-turn visual conversations with hierarchical perception, reasoning and creativity ablation and an automatic evaluator for large vision-language models.
nodes.problem: No benchmark evaluates multi-turn visual conversation with decoupled capability attribution.
nodes.approach: Curated conversations with progressive capability examination and an automatic evaluation framework.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal LLM benchmarks are very common.

nodes.title: Learning rigid-body simulators over implicit shapes for large-scale scenes and vision
nodes.tldr: SDF-Sim is a graph-network learned rigid-body simulator using learned signed distance functions, scaling to hundreds of objects and over a million nodes.
nodes.problem: Mesh-based learned simulators scale poorly to scenes with many objects and detailed shapes.
nodes.approach: Represent shapes with learned SDFs to speed distance and collision computation within a GNN simulator.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned rigid-body simulators are a rare direction.

nodes.title: Towards an Information Theoretic Framework of Context-Based Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Unifies context-based offline meta-RL methods as optimizing one mutual information objective between tasks and latent representations, yielding new supervised and self-supervised algorithms.
nodes.problem: Existing context-based methods seem disconnected, lacking a unifying information-theoretic account.
nodes.approach: Maximizes I(Z;M) between task and latent representation, via supervised and self-supervised bound implementations.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Context-based offline meta-RL theory is specialized.

nodes.title: Tetrahedron Splatting for 3D Generation
nodes.tldr: TeT-Splatting is a tetrahedral-grid 3D representation with a differentiable tetrahedron rasterizer, combining easy optimization, precise mesh extraction, and real-time rendering for text-to-3D.
nodes.problem: Existing 3D representations for diffusion-prior text-to-3D trade off optimization ease, mesh extraction quality, and rendering speed.
nodes.approach: Surface-based volumetric rendering in a tetrahedral grid with tile-based rasterizer and SDF eikonal and normal regularization.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Representation design for text-to-3D is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Archaeoscape: Bringing Aerial Laser Scanning Archaeology to the Deep Learning Era
nodes.tldr: Archaeoscape is a large open-access aerial laser scanning dataset of 888 km2 in Cambodia, with 31k annotated Angkorian features and benchmarked segmentation models.
nodes.problem: Expert-annotated, open-access laser scanning data for archaeology is scarce, blocking deep learning on it.
nodes.approach: Curates a large annotated ALS dataset and benchmarks recent segmentation models for hidden archaeological structures.
nodes.niche_reason: Deep learning on aerial laser scanning archaeology is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Rethinking Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Effective Metric-Based Exploration Bonus
nodes.tldr: Proposes a theoretically grounded metric-based state-discrepancy exploration bonus with an ensemble-variance diversity scaling factor, improving hard-exploration tasks.
nodes.problem: Metric-based intrinsic rewards rely on count-based scaling or have inaccurate bisimulation approximations, hurting hard exploration.
nodes.approach: A robust state discrepancy metric plus diversity-enhanced bonus scaling from reward-model ensemble variance.
nodes.niche_reason: Intrinsic-motivation exploration is a common RL topic.

nodes.title: Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?
nodes.tldr: Spider2-V benchmarks multimodal agents on 494 real data science and engineering tasks across 20 enterprise applications; the best agents succeed only 14%.
nodes.problem: Assessing whether multimodal agents can automate professional data science and engineering workflows.
nodes.approach: Executable benchmark with automatic task setup, evaluation metrics, and documentation across enterprise software GUIs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Agent benchmarks are common, though professional data workflows are narrower.

nodes.title: Exploitation of a Latent Mechanism in Graph Contrastive Learning: Representation Scattering
nodes.tldr: Identifies representation scattering as a common mechanism behind graph contrastive learning methods and proposes SGRL, which adds center-away scattering with a topology constraint.
nodes.problem: The mechanisms behind the effectiveness of diverse graph contrastive learning frameworks are not well understood.
nodes.approach: Unify GCL via representation scattering; add center-away scattering plus topology-based constraint (SGRL).
nodes.niche_reason: Graph contrastive learning is a common subfield.

nodes.title: Trading Place for Space: Increasing Location Resolution Reduces Contextual Capacity in Hippocampal Codes
nodes.tldr: Shows hippocampal place cells can store exponentially many contexts, trading position resolution against contextual capacity via field width.
nodes.problem: How many distinct environments the hippocampal place code can represent, and at what cost, is unclear.
nodes.approach: Geometric analysis of place-field firing statistics, measuring distances between context representations.
nodes.niche_reason: Place-cell capacity theory is very rare in ML venues.

nodes.title: A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic
nodes.tldr: Creates GSM1k, a fresh GSM8k-style benchmark, finding accuracy drops up to 8% for some LLM families, indicating contamination, while frontier models generalize.
nodes.problem: Whether LLM math benchmark scores reflect memorization from contamination rather than reasoning.
nodes.approach: Commission a fresh GSM8k-style benchmark and compare model performance and memorization likelihood.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM benchmark contamination studies are common.

nodes.title: Gradients of Functions of Large Matrices
nodes.tldr: Derives adjoint systems for Lanczos and Arnoldi iterations, enabling efficient differentiation of matrix functions in PDE, Gaussian process and Bayesian NN tuning.
nodes.problem: Tuning models that evaluate matrix functions requires differentiating Lanczos and Arnoldi, which was unexplored.
nodes.approach: Previously unknown adjoint systems implemented in JAX, competitive with specialized differentiation libraries.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Adjoints for Krylov iterations are a rare niche

nodes.title: Non-Asymptotic Uncertainty Quantification in High-Dimensional Learning
nodes.tldr: Corrects confidence intervals for regression predictors, including LASSO and neural networks, by estimating bias means and variances from training data.
nodes.problem: Asymptotic confidence intervals such as debiased LASSO are overly narrow for finite-dimensional real data.
nodes.approach: Data-driven non-asymptotic adjustment exploiting high-dimensional concentration of bias terms.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Non-asymptotic UQ for LASSO and networks is specialised

nodes.title: Sample Complexity Reduction via Policy Difference Estimation in Tabular Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows estimating policy differences relative to a single reference policy nearly suffices for pure exploration in tabular RL, giving the tightest known sample complexity bound.
nodes.problem: Sample complexity of identifying an epsilon-optimal policy from a policy set in contextual bandits and tabular RL.
nodes.approach: Estimate one reference policy then only deviations of others; separation result between bandits and RL.
nodes.niche_reason: Instance-dependent RL sample complexity theory is a narrow subfield.

nodes.title: Identification and Estimation of the Bi-Directional MR with Some Invalid Instruments
nodes.tldr: Gives necessary and sufficient identifiability conditions for bi-directional Mendelian randomization with invalid instruments, and a cluster-fusion method to estimate causal effects.
nodes.problem: Estimating causal effects in bi-directional Mendelian randomization when invalid instruments and confounding exist.
nodes.approach: Identify valid instrument sets theoretically, then discover them with a cluster-fusion-like algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Bi-directional Mendelian randomization identifiability is a rare niche

nodes.title: Who Evaluates the Evaluations? Objectively Scoring Text-to-Image Prompt Coherence Metrics with T2IScoreScore (TS2)
nodes.tldr: TS2 is a benchmark of semantic error graphs that rigorously checks whether text-to-image prompt faithfulness metrics order images by objective error count.
nodes.problem: Text-to-image faithfulness metrics are validated weakly, against easy images and weak baselines.
nodes.approach: Curated prompts with increasingly erroneous images, scored by meta-metric statistical tests.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: meta-evaluation of T2I metrics is specialised but growing

nodes.title: Automatically Learning Hybrid Digital Twins of Dynamical Systems
nodes.tldr: Uses an LLM-driven evolutionary search to automatically propose and optimize hybrid digital twins that combine mechanistic and neural components for better generalization.
nodes.problem: Hybrid digital twins are hard to specify automatically and generalize poorly in data-scarce settings.
nodes.approach: LLM-guided evolutionary search over hybrid model specs with offline parameter optimization.
nodes.primary_topic: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Model discovery vs dynamical-systems modeling are close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-driven evolutionary digital-twin discovery is unusual.

nodes.title: TextCtrl: Diffusion-based Scene Text Editing with Prior Guidance Control
nodes.tldr: TextCtrl edits scene text in images with a diffusion model guided by explicit style and glyph-structure priors and a glyph-adaptive self-attention mechanism.
nodes.problem: Scene text editing struggles with GAN generalization and diffusion style deviations, lacking real evaluation data.
nodes.approach: Style-structure guidance in training plus glyph-adaptive mutual self-attention at inference; new ScenePair dataset.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based scene text editing is a specialised image editing niche.

nodes.title: GIC: Gaussian-Informed Continuum for Physical Property Identification and Simulation
nodes.tldr: Estimates physical properties of objects from video by combining 3D Gaussian reconstruction with a simulated continuum that renders masks as guidance.
nodes.problem: Physical property identification from visual observations lacks geometry-aware guidance.
nodes.approach: Hybrid dynamic 3D Gaussians and continuum simulation with motion factorization and coarse-to-fine density filling.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Visual system identification combining Gaussians and continuum physics is rare

nodes.title: A Textbook Remedy for Domain Shifts: Knowledge Priors for Medical Image Analysis
nodes.tldr: KnoBo injects medical textbook knowledge as concept bottlenecks, making chest X-ray and skin models far more robust to hospital and demographic domain shifts.
nodes.problem: Medical vision models fail under hospital and demographic domain shifts, lacking clinically grounded priors.
nodes.approach: Concept bottleneck models whose concept space is built by retrieval-augmented LLMs from PubMed.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: domain-shift robustness vs medical interpretability overlap
nodes.niche_reason: established concept-bottleneck line with a medical twist

nodes.title: Doob's Lagrangian: A Sample-Efficient Variational Approach to Transition Path Sampling
nodes.tldr: Casts Doob's h-transform as a simulation-free variational objective over trajectories, with boundary conditions built into the model.
nodes.problem: Conditioning diffusive dynamics on rare endpoints needs infeasible forward simulation.
nodes.approach: Variational optimization over trajectories with a parameterization enforcing endpoints, no simulation.
nodes.confidence_reason: Transition path sampling sits between sampling methods and molecular physics.
nodes.niche_reason: Variational Doob transform for rare-event path sampling is rare.

nodes.title: Unveiling Encoder-Free Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: EVE is an encoder-free vision-language model with a unified decoder and extra visual supervision, rivaling encoder-based VLMs using only 35M public training samples.
nodes.problem: Vision encoders impose inductive biases; training pure encoder-free VLMs is slow and underperforms.
nodes.approach: Unified decoder bridging vision-language representations plus auxiliary visual recognition supervision.
nodes.niche_reason: Encoder-free VLMs are an uncommon alternative to mainstream VLM design.

nodes.title: Diffusion Model with Cross Attention as an Inductive Bias for Disentanglement
nodes.tldr: Shows a diffusion model with cross-attention over concept tokens learns disentangled representations without extra regularization, via time-varying information bottlenecks.
nodes.problem: Learning disentangled representations unsupervised usually needs tailored losses or structures.
nodes.approach: Encode images into concept tokens conditioning a latent diffusion U-Net via cross-attention.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised disentanglement via diffusion architecture

nodes.title: Are Graph Neural Networks Optimal Approximation Algorithms?
nodes.tldr: Designs GNN architectures that capture optimal semidefinite-programming approximation algorithms for Max-CSPs under the Unique Games Conjecture, achieving strong results on Max-Cut and related problems.
nodes.problem: Combinatorial optimization GNNs lack principled links to optimal approximation algorithms.
nodes.approach: Message-passing networks that represent SDP-based relaxations, with a bound-producing decoder from embeddings.
nodes.niche_reason: GNNs mirroring optimal SDP approximation is unusual.

nodes.title: The ALCHEmist: Automated Labeling 500x CHEaper than LLM Data Annotators
nodes.tldr: Alchemist has LLMs write labeling programs instead of labeling directly, matching or beating LLM annotation at roughly 500 times lower cost with reusable, auditable programs.
nodes.problem: Using top LLMs as annotators is expensive and yields static, hard-to-audit datasets.
nodes.approach: Prompt models to generate programs that produce labels, stored and applied locally, in a weak-supervision style.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-based labeling is common; program-based weak supervision is specialised.

nodes.title: Heavy-Tailed Class Imbalance and Why Adam Outperforms Gradient Descent on Language Models
nodes.tldr: Shows Adam beats gradient descent on language models because heavy-tailed token imbalance slows rare-word learning, while sign-based methods are robust to it.
nodes.problem: Why Adam outperforms gradient descent on language models by a larger margin than on other tasks.
nodes.approach: Cross-architecture experiments plus linear-model and continuous-time analysis of class-imbalanced gradients.
nodes.niche_reason: Heavy-tailed class imbalance explaining Adam is specialised

nodes.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search based Space Transfer for Black Box Optimization
nodes.tldr: Uses Monte Carlo tree search to iteratively partition and select promising subspaces, transferring knowledge from similar source tasks in Bayesian optimization.
nodes.problem: Bayesian optimization restarts from scratch on each problem, and existing search-space transfer lacks adaptivity.
nodes.approach: MCTS-guided adaptive subspace division and reconstruction during optimization, warm-starting from source tasks.
nodes.confidence_reason: Bayesian optimization with transfer; Optimization vs Transfer topics
nodes.niche_reason: Search-space transfer for black-box optimization is specialised

nodes.title: Generated and Pseudo Content guided Prototype Refinement for Few-shot Point Cloud Segmentation
nodes.tldr: Refines few-shot point cloud segmentation prototypes with LLM-generated class descriptions and pseudo-query context, beating prior methods on S3DIS and ScanNet.
nodes.problem: Support sets are small, and class information bias between support and query yields low-quality prototypes.
nodes.approach: Enrich prototypes with LLM class descriptions and reliable pseudo-query context, plus dual distillation regularization.
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot 3D segmentation is established but specialized

nodes.title: CAT3D: Create Anything in 3D with Multi-View Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: CAT3D generates consistent novel views from any number of input images with a multi-view diffusion model, feeding 3D reconstruction to create scenes within a minute.
nodes.problem: 3D scene capture normally requires hundreds to thousands of input images.
nodes.approach: Multi-view diffusion model synthesizes consistent novel views, then robust 3D reconstruction.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based 3D generation is a crowded area.

nodes.title: On the Identifiability of Poisson Branching Structural Causal Model Using Probability Generating Function
nodes.tldr: Establishes identifiability of Poisson branching structural causal models via probability generating functions and gives an algorithm to learn causal skeletons and directions from count data.
nodes.problem: Causal discovery for count data with branching structure has identifiable directions missed by existing methods.
nodes.approach: Closed-form PGF of PB-SCM whose components encode local structures, used for a discovery algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal discovery for branching count data is a narrow niche.

nodes.title: What type of inference is planning?
nodes.tldr: Shows planning-as-inference corresponds to different entropy weights in the variational objective, and derives a loopy belief propagation planner for factored MDPs.
nodes.problem: It is unclear which inference type planning-as-inference means; prior types suit only low-stochasticity MDPs.
nodes.approach: Variational framework with entropy weightings, plus a loopy belief propagation analogue for approximate planning in factored MDPs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Planning-as-inference links probabilistic inference and RL theory.
nodes.niche_reason: Planning-as-inference theory is specialised but a long-standing topic.

nodes.title: Optimal Algorithms for Online Convex Optimization with Adversarial Constraints
nodes.tldr: A simple first-order policy achieves O(sqrt T) regret and near O(sqrt T) cumulative constraint violation in constrained online convex optimization, using Lyapunov optimization.
nodes.problem: Whether COCO can simultaneously achieve sqrt(T) regret and sqrt(T) constraint violation without restrictive assumptions was open.
nodes.approach: Combine adaptive OCO policies as black box with Lyapunov optimization drift analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Online convex optimization theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Do causal predictors generalize better to new domains?
nodes.tldr: Tests whether causal-feature predictors generalize better across domains on 16 tabular tasks, finding all-feature predictors consistently beat causal-feature ones in-domain and out-of-domain.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether causal features yield predictors that generalize better across domains.
nodes.approach: Benchmarks causal versus all-feature predictors on 16 tabular tasks across multiple domains, plus causal DG methods.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Causal feature selection for domain generalization is a specialised question.

nodes.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting as Markov Chain Monte Carlo
nodes.tldr: Recasts 3D Gaussian Splatting as MCMC sampling with SGLD updates, replacing densification heuristics with state transitions for better quality and robustness to initialization.
nodes.problem: Heuristic Gaussian cloning and splitting generalize poorly and depend on initialization.
nodes.approach: Treat Gaussians as MCMC samples, add SGLD noise, relocalize instead of clone, and apply L1 regularization.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Gaussian splatting is very active; MCMC view is a modest twist.

nodes.title: The Value of Reward Lookahead in Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Quantifies the value of advance reward information in RL using competitive analysis, deriving exact worst-case ratios across the full spectrum of lookahead.
nodes.problem: It is unclear how much value agents gain from knowing future rewards before acting.
nodes.approach: Competitive ratio analysis comparing standard RL agents against partial-lookahead agents under worst-case rewards.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Competitive analysis of reward lookahead is rare in RL theory.

nodes.title: Scribbles for All: Benchmarking Scribble Supervised Segmentation Across Datasets
nodes.tldr: Scribbles for All provides scribble-labeled versions of popular segmentation datasets and an algorithm that generates synthetic scribbles from any dense labels.
nodes.problem: Weakly supervised segmentation with scribbles lacks challenging benchmark datasets for fair evaluation.
nodes.approach: Automatic scribble generation from dense annotations, then benchmarking segmentation models trained on synthetic scribbles.
nodes.niche_reason: Scribble-supervised segmentation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Improving Environment Novelty Quantification for Effective Unsupervised Environment Design
nodes.tldr: CENIE measures environment novelty via the student's state-action coverage modeled with Gaussian mixtures, complementing regret in unsupervised environment design for better generalization.
nodes.problem: Regret-based unsupervised environment design ignores environment novelty, limiting generalization.
nodes.approach: Quantify novelty from agent state-action coverage with GMMs and combine it with regret for curriculum generation.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Unsupervised environment design is a rare RL subfield.

nodes.title: GenArtist: Multimodal LLM as an Agent for Unified Image Generation and Editing
nodes.tldr: An MLLM agent decomposes image generation and editing tasks into sub-problems, plans a tool-call tree, and verifies each step.
nodes.problem: Single image models fail on complex prompts and lack verification and self-correction
nodes.approach: Tool library orchestrated by an MLLM agent with tree planning, position-aware inputs, and step-wise self-correction
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Agentic image generation is an active, crowded area

nodes.title: Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning of Diffusion Models with Energy-Based Models
nodes.tldr: DxMI fine-tunes diffusion models with maximum entropy inverse RL jointly with an energy-based model, enabling high-quality few-step sampling and MCMC-free EBM training.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models produce poor samples with few steps, and EBM training is unstable and needs MCMC.
nodes.approach: Minimax joint training of diffusion model and EBM via maximum entropy IRL, with dynamic programming RL updates (DxDP).
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual IRL and EBM view of diffusion training.

nodes.title: Slight Corruption in Pre-training Data Makes Better Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Shows that slight synthetic corruption of conditions in diffusion pre-training data improves image quality and diversity, and proposes condition embedding perturbation.
nodes.problem: Web-scale diffusion pre-training data contains corrupted image-condition pairs; effects unknown
nodes.approach: Synthetic corruption of ImageNet and CC3M plus condition embedding perturbation (CEP)
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Pre-training corruption angle on diffusion is unusual

nodes.title: StoryDiffusion: Consistent Self-Attention for Long-Range Image and Video Generation
nodes.tldr: StoryDiffusion adds zero-shot Consistent Self-Attention to diffusion models for subject-consistent image sequences, then a semantic motion predictor turns them into long consistent videos.
nodes.problem: Keeping subjects and details consistent across a series of generated images and long videos.
nodes.approach: Consistent Self-Attention sharing across images plus semantic-space motion predictor for transitions.
nodes.niche_reason: Consistent subject generation is a popular, active topic.

nodes.title: BPQP: A Differentiable Convex Optimization Framework for Efficient End-to-End Learning
nodes.tldr: BPQP differentiates convex optimization layers by solving the backward pass as another QP, avoiding costly Jacobians and scaling to large problems.
nodes.problem: Differentiating large-scale constrained convex optimization layers via implicit differentiation is expensive.
nodes.approach: Reformulate the backward pass as a simplified QP solved efficiently, decoupled from the forward solver.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Differentiable convex optimization layers are a rare niche.

nodes.title: Learning Better Representations From Less Data For Propositional Satisfiability
nodes.tldr: Trains an attention model to generate resolution proofs for SAT, using expert iteration to beat teacher proofs with far less training data.
nodes.problem: Neural SAT solvers need huge datasets and symbolic verifiers to ensure output correctness.
nodes.approach: Attention-based autoregressive clause selection with certificate-driven training and expert iteration.
nodes.confidence_reason: neuro-symbolic SAT fits no single area cleanly
nodes.niche_reason: neural resolution proof generation for SAT is unusual

nodes.title: Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization
nodes.tldr: Models autoregressive image tokens in continuous space with a per-token diffusion loss, removing the need for vector-quantized tokenizers.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive image generators are conventionally tied to discrete vector-quantized tokens.
nodes.approach: Diffusion loss models each token's continuous distribution inside masked and standard autoregressive models.
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive image generation is active; continuous-token variants are less common.

nodes.title: MedCalc-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models for Medical Calculations
nodes.tldr: Releases MedCalc-Bench, over 1000 manually reviewed instances across 55 clinical calculation tasks, showing LLMs remain unreliable for medical calculators.
nodes.problem: Medical LLM benchmarks focus on QA, not the quantitative equation-based calculations clinicians use.
nodes.approach: Patient-note instances with ground-truth answers and step-by-step explanations for 55 calculator tasks.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Clinical calculator benchmark for LLMs is an uncommon angle

nodes.title: Reproducibility of predictive networks for mouse visual cortex
nodes.tldr: Shows neuronal embeddings from predictive visual cortex models are unstable across fits, and that adaptive L1 regularization and pruning improve consistency.
nodes.problem: Overparameterized neuron models may lack unique solutions, so embeddings may not support cell-type taxonomies.
nodes.approach: Per-neuron adaptive L1 regularization plus iterative feature pruning, evaluated for cross-fit clustering consistency.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Reproducibility of neural predictive models for cell types is rare

nodes.title: UniTox: Leveraging LLMs to Curate a Unified Dataset of Drug-Induced Toxicity from FDA Labels
nodes.tldr: Builds UniTox, a dataset of drug-induced toxicity ratings across eight organ systems for 2,418 FDA drugs, curated with GPT-4o and clinician-validated.
nodes.problem: Toxicity datasets are small, single-organ and costly to curate from lengthy drug labels.
nodes.approach: LLM extraction of toxicity summaries and ratings from FDA labels, validated by clinicians and benchmarked with ML models.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-curated drug-toxicity dataset from labels is an unusual application.

nodes.title: Cambrian-1: A Fully Open, Vision-Centric Exploration of Multimodal LLMs
nodes.tldr: Open, vision-centric study of multimodal LLMs comparing over 15 vision encoders, proposing a spatial vision aggregator, and releasing data, models and recipes.
nodes.problem: Vision design choices in MLLMs are underexplored and disconnected from visual representation learning.
nodes.approach: Evaluate visual representations through visual instruction tuning, plus a spatially aware token-reducing connector.
nodes.niche_reason: Vision encoders for MLLMs is a crowded area

nodes.title: PrivAuditor: Benchmarking Data Protection Vulnerabilities in LLM Adaptation Techniques
nodes.tldr: PrivAuditor benchmarks privacy leakage and membership inference vulnerabilities across parameter-efficient and other fine-tuning adaptation techniques for LLMs.
nodes.problem: Privacy risks of adapting pretrained LLMs with sensitive domain data are poorly characterized.
nodes.approach: Benchmark membership inference and related attacks across multiple adaptation techniques, models and datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM privacy auditing is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Generalized Linear Programming Value Functions
nodes.tldr: Learns the generalized LP value function with an input-convex neural network that under-approximates it without solving LPs, enabling fast heuristics for two-stage MILPs.
nodes.problem: Modeling the LP optimal value as constraint bounds vary is costly for large-scale decomposition.
nodes.approach: Structural characterization yields an unsupervised input-convex network giving a true under-approximation.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Learning LP value functions for MILP is a rare operations research niche.

nodes.title: MambaTree: Tree Topology is All You Need in State Space Model
nodes.tldr: Builds a dynamic tree topology from spatial relations and features so state space model propagation captures long-range dependencies in vision and text.
nodes.problem: Sequence-based state space models struggle to model long-range dependencies due to geometric sequence constraints.
nodes.approach: Tree-structured feature propagation with a linear-complexity dynamic programming algorithm for long-range interactions.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.confidence_reason: Vision and text claims span SSM architecture and graph propagation.
nodes.niche_reason: SSM variants are crowded; tree topology adds a specialised twist.

nodes.title: A benchmark for prediction of transcriptomic responses to chemical perturbations across cell types
nodes.tldr: OP3 benchmark and new single-cell dataset of 146 compounds on human blood cells for predicting chemical perturbation effects on cell-type-specific gene expression, with competition winners.
nodes.problem: Lack of well-designed benchmarks for predicting transcriptomic responses to chemical perturbations in unseen cell types.
nodes.approach: New single-cell perturbation dataset, evaluation metrics, data representations, and NeurIPS 2023 competition methods.
nodes.niche_reason: Single-cell perturbation modeling is a rare ML niche.

nodes.title: Statistical Estimation in the Spiked Tensor Model via the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
nodes.tldr: Analyzes QAOA on the spiked tensor model, proving its 1-step weak recovery threshold matches tensor power iteration and discovering a sine-Gaussian overlap law.
nodes.problem: Whether quantum approximate optimization can beat classical thresholds for planted tensor estimation.
nodes.approach: Fourier-transform-based analysis of combinatorial sums to compute QAOA recovery thresholds and overlap distributions.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum algorithms for statistical estimation is a very rare direction.

nodes.title: Dataset and Lessons Learned from the 2024 SaTML LLM Capture-the-Flag Competition
nodes.tldr: Report on a capture-the-flag competition for LLM prompt-injection defenses, releasing a dataset of over 137k multi-turn attack chats and an open platform.
nodes.problem: LLM systems are vulnerable to crafted messages that overwrite instructions or leak secret system prompts.
nodes.approach: Two-phase competition where teams build system-prompt defenses, then attack each other's defenses.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt injection and LLM security are heavily studied mainstream topics.

nodes.title: Interpret Your Decision: Logical Reasoning Regularization for Generalization in Visual Classification
nodes.tldr: L-Reg is a logical-reasoning-derived regularizer that reduces model complexity, improves interpretability and generalization in visual classification across multi-domain generalization and generalized category discovery.
nodes.problem: Vision models generalize poorly to unseen domains and novel categories.
nodes.approach: Derive a logical regularization term reducing feature distribution and classifier weight complexity.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Logic-based regularization for generalization is a less common angle.

nodes.title: Breaking Long-Tailed Learning Bottlenecks: A Controllable Paradigm with Hypernetwork-Generated Diverse Experts
nodes.tldr: A long-tailed learning paradigm that generates diverse experts with hypernetworks to cover test distributions and outputs a model matching user head-tail trade-off preferences.
nodes.problem: Long-tailed learning fails under test distribution shift and cannot adapt to head-tail trade-off preferences.
nodes.approach: Hypernetwork-generated diverse expert ensemble optimized to adapt to any test distribution and preference.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles long-tail recognition, distribution shift and multi-objective optimization.
nodes.niche_reason: Long-tail learning is established; preference control is a twist.

nodes.title: Stabilized Proximal-Point Methods for Federated Optimization
nodes.tldr: S-DANE is a distributed proximal-point method with auxiliary prox-centers, plus accelerated and adaptive variants achieving best-known communication complexity for federated optimization.
nodes.problem: DANE needs accurate local subproblem solves, costing local computation in federated optimization.
nodes.approach: Hybrid-projection-inspired proximal-point method with auxiliary prox-centers, plus acceleration and line-search adaptivity.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated convex optimization is established; the second-order similarity angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Generalized Protein Pocket Generation with Prior-Informed Flow Matching
nodes.tldr: Flow-matching generator for protein binding pockets that learns protein-ligand interaction priors and uses affinity and geometry guidance at sampling time.
nodes.problem: Pocket generation is slow with physics computations or hurts quality without domain knowledge.
nodes.approach: Flow matching with interaction priors and multi-granularity guidance during sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: Pocket generation with flow matching is specialised.

nodes.title: FuseAnyPart: Diffusion-Driven Facial Parts Swapping via Multiple Reference Images
nodes.tldr: Diffusion-based method that swaps individual facial parts from multiple reference faces by fusing them in latent space before injecting into a UNet.
nodes.problem: Swapping selected facial parts from several people while keeping the rest of the target unchanged.
nodes.approach: Mask-based fusion module in latent space plus addition-based injection into a diffusion UNet.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Facial part-level swapping is a specialised editing niche

nodes.title: MmCows: A Multimodal Dataset for Dairy Cattle Monitoring
nodes.tldr: MmCows is a multimodal dairy cattle monitoring dataset combining wearable and implantable sensors, UWB localization, environmental data, and 4.8M annotated camera frames.
nodes.problem: Few datasets combine multiple sensing modalities for precision livestock monitoring.
nodes.approach: Collect and annotate synchronized sensor, image, milk-yield, and weather data from ten dairy cows with benchmarks.
nodes.niche_reason: Livestock monitoring dataset is a very rare application domain.

nodes.title: ChronoMagic-Bench: A Benchmark for Metamorphic Evaluation of Text-to-Time-lapse Video Generation
nodes.tldr: ChronoMagic-Bench evaluates text-to-video models on metamorphic time-lapse generation with 1,649 prompts, new MTScore and CHScore metrics, and a 460k-pair ChronoMagic-Pro dataset.
nodes.problem: Existing T2V benchmarks ignore temporal coherence and metamorphic amplitude in time-lapse video generation.
nodes.approach: Categorized prompts with reference videos, two automatic metrics aligned to human preference, and a large time-lapse dataset.
nodes.niche_reason: Video generation benchmarks are common; time-lapse metamorphosis focus is specialised.

nodes.title: Non-asymptotic Approximation Error Bounds of Parameterized Quantum Circuits
nodes.tldr: Constructs data re-uploading quantum circuits for multivariate polynomials and smooth functions, giving first non-asymptotic approximation bounds, possibly smaller than deep ReLU networks.
nodes.problem: Expressivity of parameterized quantum circuits lacks constructive non-asymptotic approximation results.
nodes.approach: Construct data re-uploading PQCs and bound error by qubits, depth, and trainable parameters.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum ML approximation theory has few comparable papers.

nodes.title: Online Bayesian Persuasion Without a Clue
nodes.tldr: Online Bayesian persuasion algorithm needing no knowledge of prior or receiver utilities achieves sublinear regret, with matching lower bounds and PAC sample complexity.
nodes.problem: Online Bayesian persuasion assumes the sender knows the prior or receiver utilities, which is unrealistic.
nodes.approach: Search a representation of signaling schemes to learn receiver best responses without prior knowledge.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian persuasion is a very rare topic in ML venues.

nodes.title: PhoCoLens: Photorealistic and Consistent Reconstruction in Lensless Imaging
nodes.tldr: Recovers photorealistic lensless images by first reconstructing low-frequency content with PSF-aware deconvolution, then adding high-frequency detail from a pretrained diffusion prior.
nodes.problem: Lensless cameras need reconstruction that is both data-consistent and photorealistic, but current algorithms fall short.
nodes.approach: Spatially varying deconvolution for low frequencies, conditioned diffusion model for high-frequency details.
nodes.niche_reason: Lensless imaging is a niche computational imaging area

nodes.title: The Collusion of Memory and Nonlinearity in Stochastic Approximation With Constant Stepsize
nodes.tldr: Analyzes stochastic approximation with Markovian data and nonlinear updates at constant stepsize, establishing weak convergence and a precise asymptotic bias with an interaction term.
nodes.problem: Prior stochastic approximation theory treats either i.i.d. data or linear updates, not both together.
nodes.approach: Exploit smoothness and recurrence of SA updates to analyze correlation between iterates and Markovian data.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialized stochastic approximation theory

nodes.title: Goal Reduction with Loop-Removal Accelerates RL and Models Human Brain Activity in Goal-Directed Learning
nodes.tldr: Goal-reducer derives subgoals from distant goals via loop removal on replay data, speeds up goal-conditioned RL, and matches human vmPFC and basal ganglia fMRI patterns.
nodes.problem: Goal-directed RL struggles with vast goal spaces while humans use intermediate subgoals for long-horizon tasks.
nodes.approach: Loop-removal technique distills subgoals from replay buffer, integrated with DQN and SAC, compared against human fMRI.
nodes.niche_reason: Combines goal-conditioned RL with human fMRI evidence, unusual angle.

nodes.title: Scaling Laws and Compute-Optimal Training Beyond Fixed Training Durations
nodes.tldr: Shows constant learning rate with cooldown, plus weight averaging, scales as predictably as cosine schedules, enabling cheaper scaling-law experiments across training durations.
nodes.problem: Cosine schedules tie runs to fixed duration, making scaling-law and compute-optimal studies costly.
nodes.approach: Empirically study constant LR with cooldown and stochastic weight averaging for scaling experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Topic is a judgment call between close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Scaling-law and LR schedule studies are common in LLM training.

nodes.title: MetaLA: Unified Optimal Linear Approximation to Softmax Attention Map
nodes.tldr: Identifies three conditions for an optimal linear approximation to softmax attention and proposes MetaLA, which satisfies all three.
nodes.problem: Linear-complexity replacements for softmax attention are suboptimal and no current design meets all conditions.
nodes.approach: Unify linear models as linear attention and derive a design for dynamic memory, static approximation, and few parameters.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Linear attention approximation is a crowded research direction

nodes.title: Acoustic Volume Rendering for Neural Impulse Response Fields
nodes.tldr: Acoustic Volume Rendering adapts volume rendering with frequency-domain integration to learn neural impulse response fields for novel poses, plus an AcoustiX simulation platform.
nodes.problem: Synthesizing sound at arbitrary positions requires modeling room impulse responses, which are time-series unlike radiance fields.
nodes.approach: Frequency-domain volume rendering with spherical integration to fit impulse response measurements.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Neural acoustic fields via volume rendering have very few similar papers.

nodes.title: Can Learned Optimization Make Reinforcement Learning Less Difficult?
nodes.tldr: Meta-learns a parameterised update rule for RL that targets plasticity loss, non-stationarity and exploration, outperforming standard optimizers on single and small environment sets.
nodes.problem: RL optimisation suffers non-stationarity, plasticity loss and the need for exploration.
nodes.approach: Learned optimizer whose input features and update structure encode known RL difficulty remedies.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Learned optimizers targeting RL-specific difficulties are a rare combination.
