nodes.title: Graph-based Uncertainty Metrics for Long-form Language Model Generations
nodes.tldr: Represents LLM generations and claims as a bipartite graph, using centrality metrics to estimate claim-level uncertainty and improve factuality through decoding.
nodes.problem: Estimating claim-level uncertainty for hallucination-prone long-form LLM generations.
nodes.approach: Bipartite generation-claim graph scored with centrality measures, plus uncertainty-aware decoding.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Claim-level uncertainty for LLM hallucination is a common topic

nodes.title: Minimum Entropy Coupling with Bottleneck
nodes.tldr: Extends minimum entropy coupling with a bottleneck for lossy compression under log loss, with a greedy algorithm and tradeoffs in Markov coding games.
nodes.problem: Lossy compression where the reconstruction distribution differs from the source distribution.
nodes.approach: Decompose into entropy-bounded information maximization for the encoder and minimum entropy coupling for the decoder.
nodes.niche_reason: Minimum entropy coupling with a bottleneck is a very rare niche

nodes.title: PV-Tuning: Beyond Straight-Through Estimation for Extreme LLM Compression
nodes.tldr: PV-Tuning is a representation-agnostic quantization-aware fine-tuning framework beyond straight-through estimation, enabling Pareto-optimal 2-bit Llama-2 compression with convergence guarantees in restricted cases.
nodes.problem: Straight-through estimator fine-tuning is suboptimal for extreme 1-2 bit LLM compression.
nodes.approach: Alternating updates of discrete and continuous compressed-weight parameters, generalizing prior fine-tuning strategies.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM quantization is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Curvature Clues: Decoding Deep Learning Privacy with Input Loss Curvature
nodes.tldr: Shows input loss curvature (Hessian trace w.r.t. input) distinguishes train from test data, bounds distinguishability via privacy, and yields a stronger black-box membership inference attack.
nodes.problem: Understanding train-test distinguishability and improving membership inference attacks.
nodes.approach: Theoretical bound linking curvature to privacy and training set size, plus curvature-based membership inference attack.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Membership inference is established; curvature angle is somewhat distinctive.

nodes.title: A Pairwise Pseudo-likelihood Approach for Matrix Completion with Informative Missingness
nodes.tldr: A regularized pairwise pseudo-likelihood estimator for low-rank matrix completion when missingness depends on the unobserved values, with asymptotic recovery guarantees up to shift and scaling.
nodes.problem: Matrix completion when observation probability depends on the unobserved matrix entries (informative missingness).
nodes.approach: Regularized pairwise pseudo-likelihood under a separable observation probability assumption, with asymptotic consistency proofs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Statistical estimation theory; closest seed topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Informative-missingness matrix completion is a rare statistical niche.

nodes.title: NeoRL: Efficient Exploration for Nonepisodic RL
nodes.tldr: Optimistic model-based RL that learns from one trajectory without resets, with a regret bound for nonlinear systems with Gaussian process dynamics.
nodes.problem: Nonepisodic RL must learn unknown nonlinear dynamics from one trajectory, with no resets.
nodes.approach: Optimism under epistemic uncertainty with calibrated probabilistic models, planning optimistically over the unknown dynamics.
nodes.niche_reason: Nonepisodic RL with regret bounds is a rare, theory-focused direction.

nodes.title: Latent Diffusion for Neural Spiking Data
nodes.tldr: LDNS uses an S4 autoencoder to map spike trains to continuous latents and trains conditional diffusion models to generate realistic, behavior-dependent neural spiking data.
nodes.problem: Generating realistic, behavior-conditioned neural population spiking data from recordings.
nodes.approach: Structured state-space autoencoder to latents, then conditional latent diffusion with an expressive observation model.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion generation of spike trains is a rare neuroscience-ML niche.

nodes.title: Voila-A: Aligning Vision-Language Models with User's Gaze Attention
nodes.tldr: Aligns vision-language models with human gaze from wearable devices, using a GPT-4 annotated dataset to integrate gaze into VLM attention.
nodes.problem: VLMs struggle with complex multi-object scenes and do not focus on where human users look.
nodes.approach: Gaze-conditioned VLM trained on GPT-4 generated VOILA-COCO data, evaluated on a gaze-tracked test set.
nodes.niche_reason: Gaze-conditioned VLMs are a specialised human-AI interaction niche

nodes.title: Recurrent neural network dynamical systems for biological vision
nodes.tldr: A hybrid architecture combining continuous-time recurrent dynamics with convolutional processing, matching CNN accuracy on ImageNet while modeling monkey visual cortex activity and offering analysis tools.
nodes.problem: CNNs lack biological recurrent dynamics while RNNs lack efficient spatial processing for vision neuroscience.
nodes.approach: Continuous-time convolutional recurrent dynamical systems with iterative analysis toolkit and multi-area RNN back-ends.
nodes.niche_reason: Neuroscience-inspired dynamical vision models are an uncommon cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: VMamba: Visual State Space Model
nodes.tldr: VMamba adapts Mamba into a linear-complexity vision backbone using visual state-space blocks with a four-route 2D selective scan, performing well on diverse vision tasks.
nodes.problem: Vision backbones need computational efficiency beyond CNNs and quadratic-cost Transformers.
nodes.approach: Visual State-Space blocks with SS2D four-direction selective scan, plus architectural and implementation optimizations.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Vision Mamba backbones became a common research direction.

nodes.title: Constrained Adaptive Attack: Effective Adversarial Attack Against Deep Neural Networks for Tabular Data
nodes.tldr: Proposes CAPGD, an adaptive gradient attack, and CAA, combining it with search-based MOEVA, to effectively attack deep tabular models under feature constraints.
nodes.problem: No effective adversarial attacks exist for deep tabular models with categorical features and constraints.
nodes.approach: Parameter-free constrained adaptive gradient attack combined with a search-based attack.
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial attacks on tabular data are less studied than on images.

nodes.title: Croissant: A Metadata Format for ML-Ready Datasets
nodes.tldr: Proposes Croissant, a shared metadata format that makes ML datasets discoverable, portable, and loadable across tools and platforms.
nodes.problem: ML datasets are hard to discover, port, and load across tools.
nodes.approach: A shared metadata schema for describing datasets, supported by major repositories.
nodes.niche_reason: Dataset metadata standards are a niche area

nodes.title: Enhancing Preference-based Linear Bandits via Human Response Time
nodes.tldr: Combines binary choices with human response times, grounded in the EZ diffusion model, to estimate utilities and speed up preference-based best-arm identification.
nodes.problem: Binary preference queries reveal little about preference strength.
nodes.approach: Joint choice and response-time utility estimator plugged into fixed-budget preference linear bandits.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual: psychology-grounded response-time signal in preference bandits.

nodes.title: Mechanism design augmented with output advice
nodes.tldr: Revisits mechanism design with learning-augmented output recommendations, proposing a quality-of-recommendation measure and new mechanisms with worst-case guarantees.
nodes.problem: Mechanisms with imperfect output recommendations need graceful performance guarantees.
nodes.approach: Quality-of-recommendation metric plus analysis of facility location, scheduling, and auctions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Output-recommendation advice for mechanism design is a very narrow sub-area.

nodes.title: In-and-Out: Algorithmic Diffusion for Sampling Convex Bodies
nodes.tldr: Presents a random walk for uniform sampling of convex bodies with state-of-the-art runtime and Renyi-divergence guarantees, proven via a stochastic diffusion view.
nodes.problem: Uniform sampling from high-dimensional convex bodies needs stronger output guarantees.
nodes.approach: Stochastic-diffusion random walk analysed through functional isoperimetric constants.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Rare theoretical sampling problem with a diffusion-based proof

nodes.title: Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
nodes.tldr: Proposes Myhill-Nerode-inspired metrics testing whether generative models recover a deterministic automaton world model; their implicit world models prove far less coherent than standard diagnostics suggest.
nodes.problem: How to assess whether generative models implicitly learn coherent world models of underlying reality.
nodes.approach: Evaluation metrics from the Myhill-Nerode theorem applied to DFA-governed domains like games, logic, navigation.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Formal-language-theory based world model evaluation is unusual.

nodes.title: 4+3 Phases of Compute-Optimal Neural Scaling Laws
nodes.tldr: Uses a solvable neural scaling model to derive compute-optimal model size phases and scaling-law exponents across data and target complexity.
nodes.problem: Predicting compute-optimal model size and scaling-law behavior in the infinite-data regime.
nodes.approach: One-pass SGD on a mean-squared solvable model, analyzing loss curves and phase boundaries in the data and target complexity plane.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Scaling-law theory sits between deep learning theory and pretraining.
nodes.niche_reason: Solvable scaling model phase analysis is a rare theory angle.

nodes.title: Learning to grok: Emergence of in-context learning and skill composition in modular arithmetic tasks
nodes.tldr: Studies how in-context learning and skill composition emerge in transformers trained on modular arithmetic tasks, finding transitions with the number of pretraining tasks.
nodes.problem: Understanding how in-context learning and skill composition emerge in language-model-like transformers.
nodes.approach: Train GPT-style transformers on linear modular functions and analyze generalization transitions and internal mechanisms.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Controlled-task emergence studies are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Visual CoT: Advancing Multi-Modal Language Models with a Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Visual CoT: 438k-sample dataset with key-region boxes and reasoning steps, plus a multi-turn pipeline and benchmark for focusing MLLMs on relevant image regions.
nodes.problem: MLLMs struggle with high-resolution images and small key regions, and lack interpretability.
nodes.approach: Dataset annotated with intermediate bounding boxes and reasoning; multi-turn pipeline that dynamically focuses on visual regions.
nodes.confidence_reason: Dataset, benchmark and method; topic between multimodal LLMs and VLMs.
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal CoT datasets are common.

nodes.title: WikiDBs: A Large-Scale Corpus Of Relational Databases From Wikidata
nodes.tldr: Releases WikiDBs, a corpus of 100,000 multi-table relational databases built from Wikidata with foreign keys, plus code to generate custom variants.
nodes.problem: Representation learning for multi-table relational databases lacks openly available training resources.
nodes.approach: Generate Wikidata-based databases with realistic characteristics, then test imputation and column-type tasks.
nodes.niche_reason: Relational database corpora are a specialized resource

nodes.title: SARDet-100K: Towards Open-Source Benchmark and ToolKit for Large-Scale SAR Object Detection
nodes.tldr: Releases SARDet-100K, a large multi-class SAR object detection benchmark standardized from 10 datasets, plus MSFA pretraining and an open-source toolkit.
nodes.problem: SAR object detection lacks large, diverse public datasets and open-source code.
nodes.approach: Standardizes 10 datasets and proposes multi-stage pretraining with filter augmentation bridging RGB to SAR.
nodes.niche_reason: SAR detection is specialised, with few large public datasets

nodes.title: Cell ontology guided transcriptome foundation model
nodes.tldr: Pretrains a transcriptome foundation model using cell ontology graph relationships between cell types to learn biologically meaningful gene co-expression.
nodes.problem: Transcriptome foundation models ignore taxonomic relationships among cell types.
nodes.approach: Inject cell ontology graph into self-supervised pretraining on single-cell expression data.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Knowledge Graphs & Relational Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Single-cell foundation models with ontology guidance are uncommon.

nodes.title: Zipper: Addressing Degeneracy in Algorithm-Agnostic Inference
nodes.tldr: Zipper fixes degeneracy in algorithm-agnostic inference by overlapping test splits with a slider parameter, yielding asymptotically normal statistics and higher power in model comparison tests.
nodes.problem: Predictiveness-difference test statistics degenerate under the null of equal goodness-of-fit.
nodes.approach: Overlapping data splits bound by a slider parameter for cross-fitting, producing a non-degenerate normal statistic.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical inference for black-box model comparison is rare in ML venues.

nodes.title: Don't Look Twice: Faster Video Transformers with Run-Length Tokenization
nodes.tldr: Removes temporally repeated video patches before inference by merging runs into single tokens with positional encoding, speeding up video transformer training 30%.
nodes.problem: Video transformers train slowly because they process huge numbers of mostly redundant temporal tokens.
nodes.approach: Content-aware run-length encoding of repeated patches, requiring no dataset-specific tuning and negligible overhead.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Run-length tokenization for video transformers is specialised

nodes.title: Cracking the Code of Juxtaposition: Can AI Models Understand the Humorous Contradictions
nodes.tldr: Introduces YesBut, a benchmark of two-panel comics with contradictory narratives, showing current vision-language models still struggle with humor.
nodes.problem: Vision-language models may not grasp humor from juxtaposed panels with nonlinear narratives.
nodes.approach: Tiered benchmark tasks from literal comprehension to deep narrative reasoning, evaluated on commercial and open VLMs.
nodes.niche_reason: Humor and comic narrative understanding is a rare evaluation niche

nodes.title: Towards training digitally-tied analog blocks via hybrid gradient computation
nodes.tldr: Introduces feedforward-tied energy-based models, a hybrid analog-digital framework trained with Equilibrium Propagation and hybrid gradient computation for energy-efficient training.
nodes.problem: Lack of theory for training hybrid networks mixing analog energy-based blocks with digital components.
nodes.approach: ff-EBMs with implicit differentiation and Equilibrium Propagation to compute gradients across analog and digital blocks.
nodes.niche_reason: Analog hardware training with equilibrium propagation is very rare.

nodes.title: Identifying Equivalent Training Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Uses Koopman operator theory and topological conjugacy to test whether two neural training runs have equivalent dynamics, including grokking versus non-grokking Transformers.
nodes.problem: No practical way to tell when two DNN training trajectories have equivalent dynamics
nodes.approach: Comparing Koopman eigenvalues to identify conjugate training dynamics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual dynamical-systems lens on training; few similar papers

nodes.title: DeTikZify: Synthesizing Graphics Programs for Scientific Figures and Sketches with TikZ
nodes.tldr: DeTikZify is a multimodal LM that synthesizes TikZ graphics programs from sketches or figures, refining outputs with MCTS at inference.
nodes.problem: Scientific figures are slow to create by hand, and existing figures lack semantic, editable code representations.
nodes.approach: Train a multimodal LM on new TikZ, sketch, and figure datasets, plus MCTS-based iterative refinement at inference.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment between code generation and vision-language topics
nodes.niche_reason: Sketch-to-TikZ program synthesis is a rare, cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Guiding a Diffusion Model with a Bad Version of Itself
nodes.tldr: Guides a diffusion model with a smaller, less-trained version of itself instead of an unconditional model, improving quality without losing variation.
nodes.problem: Classifier-free guidance improves quality at the cost of reduced sample variation.
nodes.approach: Guide sampling with a smaller, less-trained copy of the same diffusion network.
nodes.niche_reason: Classifier-free guidance variants are a crowded diffusion sub-area.

nodes.title: Multistable Shape from Shading Emerges from Patch Diffusion
nodes.tldr: Trains a small patch-based diffusion model on synthetic shading patches that yields multiple plausible 3D shapes for ambiguous images, matching human multistable perception.
nodes.problem: Shape-from-shading models output single shapes, missing the multiple interpretations humans perceive.
nodes.approach: Small denoising diffusion model over 16x16 normal-field patches, deployed multi-scale with inter-patch consistency guidance.
nodes.niche_reason: Modeling multistable human shape perception with diffusion is rare.

nodes.title: DiscoveryWorld: A Virtual Environment for Developing and Evaluating Automated Scientific Discovery Agents
nodes.tldr: Introduces DiscoveryWorld, a simulated multi-modal environment with 24 scientific tasks that benchmarks agents' full discovery cycles, finding strong baselines struggle.
nodes.problem: Evaluating end-to-end scientific reasoning is hard because real experiments are costly or infeasible.
nodes.approach: Parametric simulated tasks requiring hypotheses, experiments and conclusions, with three automatic metrics.
secondary_topics: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Simulated scientific-discovery environments for agents are a rare niche.

nodes.title: Divide-and-Conquer Meets Consensus: Unleashing the Power of Functions in Code Generation
nodes.tldr: Generates code by recursively decomposing requirements into sub-functions and selecting functions by behavioural consensus, beating prior methods on HumanEval, MBPP and MATH.
nodes.problem: LLMs struggle with complex code requirements, and plan-and-test self-refinement is error-prone.
nodes.approach: Divide-and-conquer function tree with functional consensus based on program behaviour similarity.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM code generation is a crowded area; consensus-based decomposition is a variant.

nodes.title: LINGOLY: A Benchmark of Olympiad-Level Linguistic Reasoning Puzzles in Low Resource and Extinct Languages
nodes.tldr: LingOly benchmark of 1,133 olympiad linguistics puzzles in low-resource and extinct languages, testing LLM in-context multi-step reasoning.
nodes.problem: LLM reasoning is hard to measure without memorisation, since common benchmarks leak into training data.
nodes.approach: Linguistics olympiad puzzles over 90 low-resource languages, scored against a no-context baseline.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: specialised benchmark, but LLM evaluation is crowded

nodes.title: PACE: Marrying generalization in PArameter-efficient fine-tuning with Consistency rEgularization
nodes.tldr: PACE improves PEFT generalization by enforcing consistency under multiplicative noise on adapter features, which implicitly reduces gradient norms and aligns the model with the pre-trained one.
nodes.problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning often sacrifices generalization of the adapted model.
nodes.approach: Consistency regularization across multiplicatively perturbed adapter features, backed by gradient-norm generalization theory.
nodes.niche_reason: PEFT variants are very common.

nodes.title: Graph Diffusion Transformers for Multi-Conditional Molecular Generation
nodes.tldr: Graph DiT is a transformer-based graph diffusion model that generates molecules conditioned on multiple numerical and categorical properties.
nodes.problem: Diffusion molecule generators cannot easily condition on multiple properties such as synthetic score and gas permeability.
nodes.approach: Condition encoder plus transformer graph denoiser, with a graph-dependent noise model for atoms and bonds.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-property graph diffusion for molecules is specialised but established.

nodes.title: CycleNet: Enhancing Time Series Forecasting through Modeling Periodic Patterns
nodes.tldr: CycleNet models periodic patterns with learnable recurrent cycles and forecasts residuals using a linear layer or shallow MLP, with over 90% fewer parameters.
nodes.problem: Long-term time series forecasting does not explicitly exploit stable periodic patterns.
nodes.approach: Residual Cycle Forecasting with learnable recurrent cycles plus a simple linear or MLP predictor.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Time series forecasting is a crowded benchmark-driven area.

nodes.title: Return of Unconditional Generation: A Self-supervised Representation Generation Method
nodes.tldr: Closes the gap between unconditional and class-conditional image generation by generating self-supervised encoder representations and using them to condition the generator.
nodes.problem: Unconditional generation lags far behind label-conditioned generation because labels supply semantics.
nodes.approach: Generate semantic representations in a self-supervised encoder space, then condition the image generator on them.
nodes.niche_reason: Unconditional image generation is established but less crowded.

nodes.title: Axioms for AI Alignment from Human Feedback
nodes.tldr: Analyzes RLHF reward learning through social choice axioms, showing Bradley-Terry-Luce models fail basic axioms and proposing linear social choice rules with axiomatic guarantees.
nodes.problem: RLHF reward learning aggregates human preferences but lacks axiomatic justification.
nodes.approach: Apply social choice axioms to reward learning and design rules within a linear social choice framework.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Social choice axioms applied to RLHF is a very rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Neural Krylov Iteration for Accelerating Linear System Solving
nodes.tldr: Neural operator predicts the invariant subspace of a sparse linear system to guide Krylov iteration, cutting iterations up to 16x and time up to 5.5x.
nodes.problem: Krylov subspace solvers for large sparse linear systems need many iterations and are slow.
nodes.approach: Neural operator predicts invariant subspace with QR and projection loss, which then accelerates Krylov iteration.
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-augmented numerical linear algebra solvers are a rare niche.

nodes.title: A Taxonomy of Challenges to Curating Fair Datasets
nodes.tldr: Interview study with 30 dataset curators producing a taxonomy of challenges and trade-offs across the fair dataset curation lifecycle, with recommendations.
nodes.problem: Practical challenges of curating fairer ML datasets are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Qualitative interviews with 30 curators and taxonomy construction.
nodes.niche_reason: Interview-based study of fair dataset curation is rare.

nodes.title: Self-Consuming Generative Models with Curated Data Provably Optimize Human Preferences
nodes.tldr: Shows curating self-generated data with a reward model implicitly optimizes preferences in iterative retraining; real-data mixing ensures stability.
nodes.problem: Self-consuming generative model retraining collapses or drifts, and curation effects are unclear.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of reward-based curation in retraining loops, with CIFAR10 experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment call between generative model theory and synthetic data curation.
nodes.niche_reason: Curation-driven retraining theory is a specialised, less crowded topic.

nodes.title: One-Shot Safety Alignment for Large Language Models via Optimal Dualization
nodes.tldr: Reduces constrained RLHF safety alignment to an unconstrained problem by pre-optimizing a closed-form convex dual, avoiding costly primal-dual iterations.
nodes.problem: Lagrangian primal-dual RLHF for safety constraints is expensive and unstable.
nodes.approach: Pre-optimize a smooth, convex, closed-form dual function to reduce constrained alignment to unconstrained training.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Constrained RLHF is a common alignment direction; dualization is a variant.

nodes.title: Learning Linear Causal Representations from General Environments: Identifiability and Intrinsic Ambiguity
nodes.tldr: Shows linear causal representations from general environments are identifiable up to an unavoidable surrounded-node ambiguity, with the LiNGCReL algorithm.
nodes.problem: Causal representation identifiability usually needs single-node interventions, which are unrealistic when latents are unknown.
nodes.approach: LiNGCReL algorithm for linear causal models and mixing functions, learning from data across general environments.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Identifiability under general environments is a rare theory niche

nodes.title: Dissecting Query-Key Interaction in Vision Transformers
nodes.tldr: Decomposes ViT query-key interactions with SVD, showing early layers attend to similar tokens for grouping and late layers to dissimilar ones for context.
nodes.problem: It is unclear whether vision transformer self-attention does perceptual grouping or uses context from dissimilar tokens.
nodes.approach: Singular value decomposition of the interaction matrix W_q^T W_k reveals interpretable semantic feature interactions across layers.
nodes.niche_reason: Weight-level SVD analysis of ViT attention is a specialised interpretability niche.

nodes.title: IMDL-BenCo: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Codebase for Image Manipulation Detection & Localization
nodes.tldr: Introduces IMDL-BenCo, a benchmark and modular codebase that reimplements eight image manipulation detection models with standard protocols and robustness tests.
nodes.problem: Image manipulation detection lacks a comprehensive benchmark, so model comparisons are unreliable
nodes.approach: Modular codebase with standardized components, training protocols and GPU-accelerated metrics
nodes.confidence_reason: Forgery detection benchmark; no dedicated forensics topic in vocab.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised forensics benchmark; detection is a smaller research niche

nodes.title: Molecule Design by Latent Prompt Transformer
nodes.tldr: Latent Prompt Transformer does property-conditioned molecule generation by inferring a latent prompt from target properties and refining it online.
nodes.problem: Designing molecules that meet target biological properties and chemical constraints is a hard conditional generation problem.
nodes.approach: Latent prompt with a learned prior guides causal-Transformer generation, using posterior sampling and online learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-prompt generative models for molecule design; specialised

nodes.title: Unified Gradient-Based Machine Unlearning with Remain Geometry Enhancement
nodes.tldr: Reframes approximate machine unlearning as a manifold-constrained update using remaining-data Hessian geometry, with a cheap fast-slow approximation.
nodes.problem: Gradient-based unlearning in Euclidean space can interfere with retained performance and needs costly Hessians.
nodes.approach: Fast-slow parameter updates that implicitly approximate a Hessian-modulated salient unlearning direction.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Gradient-based approximate unlearning is a crowded, active area.

nodes.title: Hardness of Learning Neural Networks under the Manifold Hypothesis
nodes.tldr: Proves neural network learning is hard under bounded-curvature data manifolds, but becomes efficiently learnable with added volume assumptions.
nodes.problem: Whether the manifold hypothesis makes learning neural networks computationally tractable.
nodes.approach: SQ and cryptographic hardness reductions extended to geometric inputs, plus an interpolation-based learnability argument.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Established learning-hardness theory; manifold-geometry angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Semi-Supervised Sparse Gaussian Classification: Provable Benefits of Unlabeled Data
nodes.tldr: Identifies a regime of sparse high-dimensional Gaussian classification where efficient semi-supervised learning succeeds but purely supervised or unsupervised methods fail.
nodes.problem: Whether unlabeled data provably helps semi-supervised sparse classification and feature selection.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic and low-degree computational lower bounds for feature selection under semi-supervised data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical-computational gaps for SSL are specialised theory.

nodes.title: Generalization Analysis for Label-Specific Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: Derives generalization bounds for label-specific representation learning in multi-label settings, with weaker label-count dependence via a new vector-contraction inequality.
nodes.problem: Generalization theory for label-specific representations in multi-label learning is missing.
nodes.approach: Novel vector-contraction inequality applied to general function classes and typical LSRL methods.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Generalization bounds for label-specific multi-label representations are specialised.

nodes.title: Neural Assets: 3D-Aware Multi-Object Scene Synthesis with Image Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Neural Assets are per-object representations that replace text tokens in image diffusion models, enabling 3D pose control and recomposition of multiple objects in a scene.
nodes.problem: Controlling the 3D pose of multiple individual objects in image diffusion models.
nodes.approach: Pool object visuals from a reference frame conditioned on target poses, fine-tune a text-to-image diffusion model with them.
nodes.niche_reason: Object-level 3D-aware diffusion control is specialised.

nodes.title: TrackIME: Enhanced Video Point Tracking via Instance Motion Estimation
nodes.tldr: Joint point tracking and segmentation that prunes search regions to the target instance and compensates for occluded points, avoiding down-sampling.
nodes.problem: Dense point tracking across video frames is computationally heavy, so models down-sample and lose trajectory accuracy.
nodes.approach: Instance trajectory estimated from aggregated point tracks prunes frame regions; tracking and segmentation run jointly.
nodes.niche_reason: Point tracking with segmentation is an established video vision line

nodes.title: Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning
nodes.tldr: Derives exact solutions showing unbalanced layer-wise initializations and learning rates drive rich feature learning, which can shorten time to grokking.
nodes.problem: The mechanisms behind rich feature learning in neural networks, versus lazy training, remain poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Exact solutions to a minimal lazy-to-rich model, with conserved quantities, extended to linear and piecewise-linear nets.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Rich-regime theory is specialised; initialization and grokking links are less common.

nodes.title: Who's asking? User personas and the mechanics of latent misalignment
nodes.tldr: Shows user persona strongly affects whether safety-tuned LLMs reveal harmful content, with activation steering bypassing filters and harm persisting in hidden layers.
nodes.problem: Safety-tuned models may still divulge harmful information depending on who they believe they are talking to.
nodes.approach: Persona manipulation via prompting and activation steering, plus analysis of harmful content in hidden layers.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Persona-driven misalignment is a specialised safety angle.

nodes.title: Statistical Efficiency of Distributional Temporal Difference Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves finite-sample bounds for distributional temporal difference learning, with a minimax-optimal rate for the 1-Wasserstein case and matching bounds for categorical TD.
nodes.problem: Sample complexity of distributional policy evaluation was not known non-asymptotically.
nodes.approach: Non-parametric distributional TD analysed with a novel Freedman inequality in Hilbert spaces.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Non-asymptotic distributional RL theory is rare.

nodes.title: Adversarial Environment Design via Regret-Guided Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Trains a diffusion environment generator guided by the agent's regret, producing challenging but learnable curricula that improve zero-shot robustness in RL.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised environment design is limited by generator capability, hurting robust RL policies.
nodes.approach: Regret-guided diffusion model that directly generates adversarial yet diverse training environments.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.confidence_reason: Environment generation sits between RL curricula and generative modeling.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-generated RL training environments are an unusual cross-over.

nodes.title: Poisson Variational Autoencoder
nodes.tldr: VAE with discrete Poisson spike-count latents combined with predictive coding, adding a metabolic cost that yields sparse, more separable representations.
nodes.problem: Standard VAEs use continuous latents, unlike discrete spiking neurons in biological vision.
nodes.approach: Poisson-distributed latent VAE with predictive coding and a metabolic cost term.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Poisson spike-count VAE with predictive coding is unusual.

nodes.title: Functional Bilevel Optimization for Machine Learning
nodes.tldr: Formulates bilevel optimization with the inner problem over a function space, allowing over-parameterized neural networks as inner predictors.
nodes.problem: Parametric bilevel methods need strong convexity in parameters, excluding over-parameterized neural networks.
nodes.approach: Scalable functional bilevel algorithms using an adjoint method, tested on instrumental regression and RL.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Functional bilevel optimization is a specialised optimization direction

nodes.title: MKGL: Mastery of a Three-Word Language
nodes.tldr: Teaches an LLM a three-word knowledge-graph language with real-time KG context retrieval, cutting completion errors versus KG embedding methods.
nodes.problem: LLM use on knowledge graphs is underexplored, though triplet facts allow minimal hallucination.
nodes.approach: Defines a KG language with a tailored dictionary, KG context retrieval, and KG token embedding augmentation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Knowledge Graphs & Relational Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: LLM-KG integration sits between knowledge graphs and LLM retrieval.
nodes.niche_reason: Teaching an LLM a constrained three-word knowledge-graph language is unusual.

nodes.title: Trajectory Flow Matching with Applications to Clinical Time Series Modelling
nodes.tldr: Trajectory Flow Matching trains neural SDEs for irregular clinical time series without backpropagating through dynamics, with better stability and uncertainty prediction.
nodes.problem: Neural SDE training is unstable and unscalable due to backpropagation through dynamics.
nodes.approach: Simulation-free flow-matching training of neural SDEs with a reparameterization trick, adapted to clinical data.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Neural SDEs for clinical time series are specialised.

nodes.title: Compositional Generalization Across Distributional Shifts with Sparse Tree Operations
nodes.tldr: Extends the Differentiable Tree Machine with sparse vector representations and seq2seq support, keeping compositional generalization in a unified neurosymbolic model with a fully neural path.
nodes.problem: Neural networks struggle with compositional generalization, and hybrid neurosymbolic systems lack scalability and flexibility.
nodes.approach: Sparse vector-symbolic tree representations in a unified Differentiable Tree Machine extended to seq2seq tasks.
nodes.niche_reason: Neurosymbolic tree-based compositionality is a niche line of work.

nodes.title: MInference 1.0: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context LLMs via Dynamic Sparse Attention
nodes.tldr: MInference identifies three sparse attention patterns per head offline and builds dynamic sparse indices with GPU kernels to cut long-context pre-filling latency up to 10x.
nodes.problem: Quadratic attention makes pre-filling of million-token prompts extremely slow.
nodes.approach: Assign per-head sparse patterns (A-shape, Vertical-Slash, Block-Sparse) offline, build sparse indices dynamically, use optimized kernels.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient long-context inference is a heavily studied area.

nodes.title: Reconstruct and Match: Out-of-Distribution Robustness via Topological Homogeneity
nodes.tldr: Reconstructs object components into slots and reasons over them with a hypergraph, improving out-of-distribution generalization and test-time adaptation.
nodes.problem: Deep models break under distribution shift; pairwise invariances ignore object part topology.
nodes.approach: Unsupervised slot reconstruction plus hypergraph relational reasoning over slots with structural constraints.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Primary OOD topic chosen; slot and hypergraph parts are secondary.
nodes.niche_reason: Slot-hypergraph invariance for OOD is specialised

nodes.title: Value Imprint: A Technique for Auditing the Human Values Embedded in RLHF Datasets
nodes.tldr: Value Imprint audits human values in RLHF datasets using a values taxonomy, 6,501 annotated preferences, and a classifier; information-utility values dominate.
nodes.problem: Which human values are embedded in RLHF preference datasets is poorly understood
nodes.approach: Build values taxonomy, annotate preferences, train classifier to audit three RLHF datasets
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Values audit of RLHF data draws on philosophy; unusual angle

nodes.title: Deep Learning for Computing Convergence Rates of Markov Chains
nodes.tldr: DCDC is a sample-based algorithm that uses a neural-network solver for a Contractive Drift Equation to produce explicit Wasserstein convergence bounds for general Markov chains.
nodes.problem: Deriving practically useful convergence bounds for general state-space Markov chains is analytically hard.
nodes.approach: Solve the Contractive Drift Equation with a neural network from samples, then convert the solution into a Wasserstein convergence bound.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-based convergence-bound computation for Markov chains is very rare.

nodes.title: Bigger, Regularized, Optimistic: scaling for compute and sample efficient continuous control
nodes.tldr: BRO shows strong regularization lets critics scale up in size, and with optimistic exploration yields state-of-the-art sample-efficient model-free continuous control across 40 tasks.
nodes.problem: Improving sample efficiency in continuous-control RL via scaling rather than algorithmic tricks.
nodes.approach: Large regularized critic networks combined with optimistic exploration.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Deep RL algorithm improvements are a common topic.

nodes.title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
nodes.tldr: ReFT learns task-specific interventions on hidden representations of a frozen model; LoReFT is 15-65x more parameter-efficient than LoRA while matching or beating PEFTs.
nodes.problem: Weight-based parameter-efficient finetuning may be less powerful or efficient than editing representations.
nodes.approach: Learn low-rank linear subspace interventions on frozen model hidden representations.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: PEFT is crowded, but representation-level intervention is a distinct direction.

nodes.title: Voxel Mamba: Group-Free State Space Models for Point Cloud based 3D Object Detection
nodes.tldr: Voxel Mamba serializes all voxels into a single sequence using state space models with dual-scale blocks for efficient, accurate point cloud 3D detection.
nodes.problem: Serialization-based 3D detectors lose voxel spatial proximity
nodes.approach: Group-free single-sequence SSM with dual-scale blocks and positional encoding
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: SSMs for 3D detection are a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Approximating the Top Eigenvector in Random Order Streams
nodes.tldr: A streaming algorithm approximates the top eigenvector of A^T A with space parameterized by heavy rows when rows arrive in random order, with a matching lower bound.
nodes.problem: Approximating the top singular vector of a matrix in a random order row stream with small space.
nodes.approach: Streaming power-iteration-style algorithm analyzed with heavy-row parameter; improved gap analysis of Price's method.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Streaming linear algebra theory is very rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: Personalizing Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with Variational Preference Learning
nodes.tldr: Variational Preference Learning infers a latent user variable and conditions reward models and policies on it, enabling personalized RLHF for diverse, pluralistic preferences.
nodes.problem: Standard RLHF averages over diverse human preferences, producing inaccurate rewards for subgroups.
nodes.approach: Latent-variable reward modeling with user-specific latent inferred from preference data, plus uncertainty and active learning.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Pluralistic preference learning is growing but still specialised.

nodes.title: Achieving Optimal Clustering in Gaussian Mixture Models with Anisotropic Covariance Structures
nodes.tldr: Derives minimax lower bounds for clustering under anisotropic Gaussian mixtures and an adapted Lloyd's algorithm that is optimal and converges in logarithmic iterations.
nodes.problem: Clustering accuracy under unknown, non-identity covariances lacks tight minimax theory and efficient algorithms.
nodes.approach: Lloyd-style iteration that estimates and uses covariance information at each step.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Minimax clustering theory with an algorithm; could be optimization or probabilistic.
nodes.niche_reason: Minimax clustering theory under anisotropic GMMs is specialised.

nodes.title: Improving the Worst-Case Bidirectional Communication Complexity for Nonconvex Distributed Optimization under Function Similarity
nodes.tldr: MARINA-P compresses server-to-worker downlink messages with correlated permutation compressors, and M3 extends it to bidirectional compression with momentum.
nodes.problem: Prevalent downlink compression approaches are inefficient for distributed nonconvex optimization.
nodes.approach: Correlated permutation compressors whose server-to-worker complexity improves with worker count, plus momentum uplink compression.
nodes.niche_reason: Correlated compressors for downlink communication are a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Selective Generation for Controllable Language Models
nodes.tldr: Proposes selective generation algorithms that control the false discovery rate with respect to textual entailment, using supervised and semi-supervised conformal approaches to curb LLM hallucination.
nodes.problem: Applying certified risk control to language generation lacks an appropriate correctness metric.
nodes.approach: Use textual entailment as correctness and calibrate selection with supervised or pseudo-labeled conformal prediction.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Certified risk control for generation is specialised.

nodes.title: Boosting Vision-Language Models with Transduction
nodes.tldr: Introduces TransCLIP, a plug-and-play transductive method that uses unlabeled data with a KL constraint to boost zero- and few-shot vision-language models.
nodes.problem: Zero- and few-shot vision-language models are inductive and do not exploit unlabeled test data structure.
nodes.approach: Regularized maximum-likelihood transduction with a KL penalty to text-encoder knowledge, solved by block majorize-minimize.
nodes.niche_reason: Transductive adaptation of CLIP-style models is fairly common

nodes.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
nodes.tldr: Replaces raster-scan next-token prediction with coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction, letting GPT-style image models beat diffusion transformers and follow power-law scaling.
nodes.problem: Raster-scan autoregressive image models are slow and underperform diffusion transformers
nodes.approach: Next-resolution autoregressive prediction over multi-scale token maps, with scaling and zero-shot editing evaluation
nodes.niche_reason: Visual autoregressive variants are fairly common now

nodes.title: Brain-JEPA: Brain Dynamics Foundation Model with Gradient Positioning and Spatiotemporal Masking
nodes.tldr: Brain-JEPA is an fMRI brain-dynamics foundation model using joint-embedding prediction, with gradient-based positional encoding and spatiotemporal masking.
nodes.problem: Brain activity models need strong fMRI representations that generalize across populations.
nodes.approach: JEPA pretraining with brain gradient positioning and spatiotemporal masking of fMRI patches.
nodes.niche_reason: Brain foundation models with JEPA are a rare, cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: A-FedPD: Aligning Dual-Drift is All Federated Primal-Dual Learning Needs
nodes.tldr: Fixes dual drift in federated primal-dual learning caused by inactive clients under partial participation, using virtual dual updates to align local and global variables.
nodes.problem: Stale dual variables of long-inactive clients degrade federated primal-dual methods in non-convex settings.
nodes.approach: Virtual dual updates aligning global consensus with local dual variables for unparticipated clients, with convergence analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated primal-dual methods are a specialised but established niche

nodes.title: SynRS3D: A Synthetic Dataset for Global 3D Semantic Understanding from Monocular Remote Sensing Imagery
nodes.tldr: Releases SynRS3D, a 69,667-image synthetic remote sensing dataset with height and land-cover labels, plus RS3DAda, a domain adaptation method for synthetic-to-real transfer.
nodes.problem: Global 3D semantic understanding from remote sensing lacks costly, geographically diverse annotations.
nodes.approach: Automated synthetic data pipeline plus multi-task unsupervised domain adaptation.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic monocular remote sensing 3D data is a rare niche

nodes.title: Localized Zeroth-Order Prompt Optimization
nodes.tldr: Argues that local prompt optima are more useful than global ones, and proposes ZOPO, a zeroth-order prompt search guided by an NTK-based Gaussian process.
nodes.problem: Global prompt optimization is inefficient for black-box LLMs, since global optima are rare and hard to find.
nodes.approach: Zeroth-order search with a Neural Tangent Kernel-derived Gaussian process to find well-performing local optima efficiently.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt optimization is common, but local-optima and zeroth-order framing is specialised

nodes.title: Assouad, Fano, and Le Cam with Interaction: A Unifying Lower Bound Framework and Characterization for Bandit Learnability
nodes.tldr: Introduces the interactive Fano method and fractional covering number, unifying estimation and interactive decision-making lower bounds and characterizing learnability of any stochastic bandit problem.
nodes.problem: Classical lower-bound tools fail for interactive decision making, while DEC-based bounds miss tight passive estimation bounds.
nodes.approach: Interactive Fano method plus the fractional covering number complexity measure extending the Decision-Estimation Coefficient.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Highly theoretical lower-bound machinery for interactive learning.

nodes.title: Optimizing Automatic Differentiation with Deep Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses deep RL to pick cross-country elimination orders that minimize multiplications for exact Jacobian computation, giving up to 33% gains and a JAX interpreter.
nodes.problem: Jacobian accumulation by automatic differentiation costs many multiplications, and optimal elimination order is hard to find.
nodes.approach: Model elimination ordering as a single-player game played by an RL agent, validated with a JAX interpreter.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: RL applied to an automatic-differentiation systems problem; primary topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned elimination ordering for autodiff is an unusual application

nodes.title: BetterBench: Assessing AI Benchmarks, Uncovering Issues, and Establishing Best Practices
nodes.tldr: Proposes a 40-practice framework for assessing AI benchmark quality, audits 25 benchmarks, and offers a checklist and living repository.
nodes.problem: Many AI benchmarks have quality issues and poor statistical reporting.
nodes.approach: Life-cycle best-practice checklist applied to audit 25 existing benchmarks.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.confidence_reason: Evaluation methodology vs benchmark datasets is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Meta-evaluation of benchmarks is specialised but growing.

nodes.title: PCP-MAE: Learning to Predict Centers for Point Masked Autoencoders
nodes.tldr: Improves point-cloud masked autoencoders by learning to predict patch centers instead of using given centers, forcing the encoder to learn semantic features.
nodes.problem: Point MAE decoders reconstruct from given patch centers, so the encoder learns weak semantic representations.
nodes.approach: Predicting Center Module sharing encoder parameters with cross-attention to predict masked centers.
nodes.niche_reason: Masked point cloud autoencoders are a common direction

nodes.title: CTIBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Cyber Threat Intelligence
nodes.tldr: CTIBench is a benchmark of datasets evaluating LLMs on practical cyber threat intelligence tasks.
nodes.problem: No benchmark for applied cyber threat intelligence tasks for LLMs
nodes.approach: Curated CTI datasets and evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Cybersecurity-specific LLM evaluation is a rare domain.

nodes.title: Learn To be Efficient: Build Structured Sparsity in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Trains LLMs to activate fewer neurons via an efficiency-aware objective, yielding structured sparsity that reduces LLaMA2-7B latency by 25% at 50% sparsity.
nodes.problem: Post-training activation sparsity in LLMs leaves inference efficiency gains untapped.
nodes.approach: Efficiency-aware training with a hardware-aware custom kernel for non-ReLU LLMs like LLaMA.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Training LLMs for structured activation sparsity is a specialised efficiency niche.

nodes.title: Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making
nodes.tldr: Embodied Agent Interface unifies embodied decision-making tasks and LLM modules (goal interpretation, subgoal decomposition, action sequencing, transition modeling) with fine-grained error-type metrics to benchmark LLMs.
nodes.problem: LLMs for embodied decision making lack systematic evaluation beyond final success rate.
nodes.approach: A unified interface formalizing tasks and LLM modules with fine-grained error metrics.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: LLM embodied evaluation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Induced Model Matching: Restricted Models Help Train Full-Featured Models
nodes.tldr: Induced Model Matching aligns the context-restricted version of a large model with an accurate restricted-feature model, generalizing noising and reverse distillation, shown on language modeling and RL.
nodes.problem: Using an accurate restricted-feature model as side information when training a full-featured model.
nodes.approach: Match the induced restricted version of the full model to the restricted model.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Training with restricted-model side information is an unusual framing.

nodes.title: CooHOI: Learning Cooperative Human-Object Interaction with Manipulated Object Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Teaches multiple humanoids to carry heavy objects together by first learning single-agent interaction from motion priors, then multi-agent cooperation through shared object dynamics.
nodes.problem: Multi-humanoid transport lacks mocap data and cannot be solved by single-agent training paradigms.
nodes.approach: Single-agent imitation of motion priors, then CTDE multi-agent RL where teammates respond to shared object-dynamics changes.
nodes.confidence_reason: Physics-based animation and robotics both fit; multi-agent RL is primary.
nodes.niche_reason: Cooperative humanoid-object transport is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Flex-MoE: Modeling Arbitrary Modality Combination via the Flexible Mixture-of-Experts
nodes.tldr: Flex-MoE handles arbitrary missing-modality combinations using a missing modality bank and sparse mixture-of-experts routers, evaluated on ADNI and MIMIC-IV.
nodes.problem: Multimodal models struggle with arbitrary missing modality combinations, common in medical data.
nodes.approach: Missing modality bank plus generalized and specialized routers assigning experts per observed modality combination.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Missing-modality MoE for medical data is specialised.

nodes.title: Kermut: Composite kernel regression for protein variant effects
nodes.tldr: Kermut is a Gaussian process with a composite kernel for protein mutation similarity, achieving state-of-the-art variant effect prediction with uncertainty estimates.
nodes.problem: Reliable protein variant effect prediction with calibrated uncertainty for protein engineering.
nodes.approach: Gaussian process regression with composite kernel combining sequence and structure-based mutation similarity.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: GP-based protein fitness prediction is a rare combination.

nodes.title: VideoGUI: A Benchmark for GUI Automation from Instructional Videos
nodes.tldr: VideoGUI is a benchmark that tests GUI assistants on visual-centric tasks drawn from instructional videos, at planning and atomic action levels.
nodes.problem: Existing GUI automation evaluations use simple language-only instructions, missing visual-centric, professional software tasks.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical evaluation across high-level planning, middle-level action narration, and atomic action execution metrics.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: GUI automation from instructional video is a specialised evaluation niche.

nodes.title: Robust Prompt Optimization for Defending Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
nodes.tldr: Defends LLMs against jailbreaks by optimizing a transferable defensive suffix that accounts for worst-case adaptive attacks, cutting GPT-4 attack success to 6%.
nodes.problem: LLM jailbreak defenses fail against new and adaptive attacks.
nodes.approach: Robust Prompt Optimization: adversary-aware objective optimizing a lightweight system-level suffix.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Jailbreak defenses are a crowded safety area; optimization-based defense is common.

nodes.title: Statistical Multicriteria Benchmarking via the GSD-Front
nodes.tldr: Proposes the GSD-front, a generalized stochastic dominance alternative to the Pareto front, with a consistent estimator and robust statistical test for multicriteria classifier benchmarking.
nodes.problem: Comparing classifiers over multiple metrics needs to account for benchmark-suite uncertainty and robustness to assumptions.
nodes.approach: Generalized stochastic dominance ordering, consistent front estimation, a statistical test relaxed via imprecise probabilities.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Stochastic-dominance and imprecise-probability benchmarking is very rare.

nodes.title: Bridge the Points: Graph-based Few-shot Segment Anything Semantically
nodes.tldr: Prompts Segment Anything for few-shot semantic segmentation by selecting point prompts with a directed-graph clustering of masks and points, avoiding extra hyperparameters.
nodes.problem: SAM-based few-shot segmentation struggles with prompt selection, tuning, and slow inference.
nodes.approach: Positive-negative point alignment plus graph-based point-mask clustering and gating.
nodes.niche_reason: SAM-based prompting for segmentation is a common, active direction

nodes.title: Small coresets via negative dependence: DPPs, linear statistics, and concentration
nodes.tldr: Proves determinantal point process coresets can be smaller than independent-sampling coresets, with new concentration inequalities for linear statistics of DPPs including non-symmetric kernels.
nodes.problem: Whether DPP-based coresets are fundamentally smaller than independently sampled ones was open.
nodes.approach: Coreset loss viewed as a linear statistic, with concentration bounds for DPPs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory paper on coresets; topic sits between probability theory and data curation.
nodes.niche_reason: DPP coresets with concentration theory is rare.

nodes.title: Physically Compatible 3D Object Modeling from a Single Image
nodes.tldr: Single-image 3D reconstruction that enforces static equilibrium as a hard constraint, producing shapes that stay physically stable under forces.
nodes.problem: Single-view reconstructions assume rigidity or ignore forces, so objects can be unstable when built.
nodes.approach: Decomposes mechanical properties, external forces and rest-shape geometry, linked by static equilibrium in optimisation.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.confidence_reason: Reconstruction vs. physics-simulation framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-constrained single-image 3D modeling is an unusual combination

nodes.title: Metric Transforms and Low Rank Representations of Kernels for Fast Attention
nodes.tldr: Uses group representation theory to classify which functions keep attention matrices low-rank, showing low-degree polynomials are the only piecewise continuous option.
nodes.problem: Which functions can make attention fast by keeping QK^T low-rank, and which kernels are classifiable?
nodes.approach: Group representation theory of hyperrectangles classifies low-rank-preserving functions and l1 kernels.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.confidence_reason: Mixed math results spanning kernels and efficient attention; primary is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Representation theory of hyperrectangles for attention is very rare

nodes.title: Distributed-Order Fractional Graph Operating Network
nodes.tldr: DRAGON is a continuous graph neural network with distributed-order fractional calculus, learning a distribution over derivative orders, interpreted as non-Markovian anomalous-diffusion random walk.
nodes.problem: Continuous GNNs use integer or single fractional order dynamics, limiting feature updating expressiveness.
nodes.approach: Learnable probability distribution over fractional derivative orders in graph differential equation dynamics.
nodes.niche_reason: Fractional-calculus continuous GNNs are a rare niche.

nodes.title: Rethinking 3D Convolution in $\ell_p$-norm Space
nodes.tldr: Introduces lp-norm based 3D convolution, showing l1-norm convolution is an effective, energy-efficient point cloud feature extractor with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Standard 3D convolution can lose features under some conditions, weakening point-cloud backbones.
nodes.approach: Lp-norm convolution with universal approximation proof, plus l1-specific optimization to speed up training.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.confidence_reason: Operator redesign with approximation theory; could fit efficiency or architecture topics
nodes.niche_reason: Lp-norm convolution operators are an unusual, energy-focused departure from standard CNNs

nodes.title: CryoBench: Diverse and challenging datasets for the heterogeneity problem in cryo-EM
nodes.tldr: Introduces CryoBench, five datasets, metrics, and benchmarks for heterogeneous cryo-EM reconstruction with ground truth, then evaluates existing neural and non-neural tools.
nodes.problem: Heterogeneous cryo-EM reconstruction lacks standardized benchmarks with ground truth.
nodes.approach: Datasets with conformational and compositional heterogeneity, plus noise sensitivity and new quantitative metrics.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: few ML benchmarks exist for cryo-EM heterogeneity.

nodes.title: Advancing Spiking Neural Networks for Sequential Modeling with Central Pattern Generators
nodes.tldr: Proposes CPG-PE, a spike-form positional encoding for spiking networks inspired by brain central pattern generators, showing sinusoidal PE is a special case.
nodes.problem: Spiking networks lack an effective, hardware-friendly positional encoding for sequential tasks.
nodes.approach: Encode positions via membrane-potential dynamics of a central pattern generator.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spiking positional encoding fits neuroscience and sequence modeling
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking sequence models with CPG-based encodings are a rare niche

nodes.title: Input-to-State Stable Coupled Oscillator Networks for Closed-form Model-based Control in Latent Space
nodes.tldr: Coupled Oscillator Networks give input-to-state stable latent dynamics with invertible input mapping, enabling closed-form potential-energy-shaping control in a learned low-dimensional space.
nodes.problem: Latent-space models lack physical structure, stability guarantees, and invertible input-to-latent forcing for model-based control.
nodes.approach: Coupled oscillator network dynamics model with provable stability enabling closed-form control strategies in latent space.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Control-theoretic structured latent dynamics is a rare, specialised combination.

nodes.title: Towards Unified Multimodal Editing with Enhanced Knowledge Collaboration
nodes.tldr: UniKE unifies intrinsic knowledge editing and external knowledge resorting in multimodal LLMs as key-value memories, disentangling semantic and truthfulness spaces for reliable, general, local edits.
nodes.problem: Existing MLLM knowledge editing methods can't balance reliability, generality and locality.
nodes.approach: Treat both knowledge types as vectorized key-value memories edited at the same semantic level, with disentangled knowledge spaces.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal model editing is established but specialised.

nodes.title: A generalized neural tangent kernel for surrogate gradient learning
nodes.tldr: Generalizes the neural tangent kernel to surrogate-gradient learning, giving theory for training binary and spiking networks whose activations have no useful derivatives.
nodes.problem: Surrogate gradient learning works in practice but lacks theory for activations with jumps.
nodes.approach: Surrogate gradient NTK analyzed in the infinite-width limit with kernel regression comparison.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Surrogate-gradient theory for spiking networks is rare.

nodes.title: Aligner: Efficient Alignment by Learning to Correct
nodes.tldr: Aligner trains a small plug-and-play model to learn correctional residuals between preferred and dispreferred answers, improving many LLMs without fine-tuning them.
nodes.problem: Alignment methods are too complex for rapid iteration across many deployed LLMs.
nodes.approach: Small residual-correction model applied to upstream answers, then bootstrapped as synthetic preference data.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Alignment via post-hoc correction is a crowded direction.

nodes.title: BMRS: Bayesian Model Reduction for Structured Pruning
nodes.tldr: BMRS prunes whole neurons or filters using Bayesian model reduction with truncated log-normal or log-uniform priors, giving threshold-free compression.
nodes.problem: Structured pruning of overparameterized networks with principled, tuning-free compression.
nodes.approach: Bayesian model reduction on structured-pruning posteriors under truncated log-normal/log-uniform priors.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Pruning is established; Bayesian model reduction angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Unitary Convolutions for Learning on Graphs and Groups
nodes.tldr: Proposes unitary group convolutions, especially unitary graph convolutions, that provably avoid over-smoothing and enable deeper, more stable networks competitive with state-of-the-art GNNs.
nodes.problem: Deep group-convolutional networks and GNNs suffer instability and over-smoothing, limiting long-range learning.
nodes.approach: Unitary parameterized convolutions on graphs and groups preserving norm and feature distinctness.
nodes.niche_reason: Unitary architectures for GNNs are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Model Fusion through Bayesian Optimization in Language Model Fine-Tuning
nodes.tldr: Model fusion for language model fine-tuning using multi-objective Bayesian optimization over metric and loss, with two-stage hyperparameter selection.
nodes.problem: Choosing hyperparameters and checkpoints in fine-tuning is hard, and loss and metric landscapes disagree.
nodes.approach: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization that fuses models in parameter space while optimizing both metric and loss.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian optimization over fused model parameters is a specialised fine-tuning method

nodes.title: EMR-Merging: Tuning-Free High-Performance Model Merging
nodes.tldr: Merges separately finetuned models into one multi-task model without tuning by electing a unified model and adding lightweight task-specific masks and rescalers.
nodes.problem: Merged models usually degrade in performance or need extra data and training to tune.
nodes.approach: Elect a unified weight set, then per-task masks and rescalers align direction and magnitude.
nodes.niche_reason: Model merging is a crowded, active area

nodes.title: Towards Universal Mesh Movement Networks
nodes.tldr: Learns a zero-shot graph-network mesh mover that repositions meshes for different PDEs and boundary geometries, far faster than Monge-Ampere solvers.
nodes.problem: Learned mesh movement needs retraining per PDE and boundary geometry and often inverts elements.
nodes.approach: Graph Transformer encoder with a Graph Attention Network decoder moves mesh nodes non-intrusively.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned zero-shot mesh movement is a specialised scientific ML niche.

nodes.title: In-Context Learning with Transformers: Softmax Attention Adapts to Function Lipschitzness
nodes.tldr: Shows softmax attention in-context learns a nearest-neighbor-like window whose width adapts to task Lipschitzness and label noise, an adaptivity linear attention cannot replicate.
nodes.problem: The role of softmax attention in in-context learning of regression tasks is theoretically unclear.
nodes.approach: Analyze attention units pretrained on regression tasks, characterizing the learned window and low-rank subspace projection.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: ICL theory is active but specialised.

nodes.title: RedPajama: an Open Dataset for Training Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Releases RedPajama-V1, an open reproduction of the LLaMA training data, and RedPajama-V2, a massive web corpus with quality signals for filtering.
nodes.problem: Open language models lack transparent, high-quality, large-scale pretraining data with curation metadata.
nodes.approach: Open LLaMA data reproduction plus raw web text with quality signals, validated by 1.6B-parameter ablations.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Open pretraining corpora are a well-populated resource area

nodes.title: MMLONGBENCH-DOC: Benchmarking Long-context Document Understanding with Visualizations
nodes.tldr: MMLONGBENCH-DOC is a benchmark of 1,082 expert-annotated questions over long multimodal PDF documents, where the best model scores only 44.9% F1.
nodes.problem: Long-context document understanding by vision-language models remains an open problem.
nodes.approach: Benchmark of 135 long PDFs with cross-page, multi-source, and unanswerable questions.
nodes.niche_reason: Document VQA benchmarks are a common, crowded evaluation genre

nodes.title: Diffusion Models With Learned Adaptive Noise
nodes.tldr: MuLAN learns a multivariate, input-conditional diffusion noise process as a variational posterior, tightening the ELBO and setting state-of-the-art density estimation with fewer steps.
nodes.problem: The fixed diffusion process limits likelihood estimation; ELBO is assumed invariant to noise schedule.
nodes.approach: Learned multivariate noise schedule, adaptive input-conditioned diffusion, and auxiliary variables within a Bayesian variational framework.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion theory variant; common area, somewhat specialised angle.

nodes.title: Latent Intrinsics Emerge from Training to Relight
nodes.tldr: Learns image relighting purely from data using latent intrinsics and latent lighting variables, achieving SOTA relighting and recovering albedo without any albedo supervision.
nodes.problem: Inverse-graphics relighting is hard to error-control and limited to chosen intrinsics.
nodes.approach: Data-driven relighting with latent intrinsic and lighting representations, from which albedo emerges.
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-intrinsic relighting without explicit inverse graphics is unusual.

nodes.title: Generalization Error Bounds for Two-stage Recommender Systems with Tree Structure
nodes.tldr: Derives Rademacher-based generalisation bounds for two-stage tree-structured recommenders, showing more branches and harmonised stage distributions help.
nodes.problem: Generalisation guarantees for two-stage recommenders with tree-based retrieval and a separate ranker.
nodes.approach: Error decomposition with Rademacher complexity bounds for beam-search tree retrievers and shifted-distribution rankers.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: No recommender topic exists; generalisation theory is the closest fit.
nodes.niche_reason: Generalisation theory for tree-structured recommender pipelines is rare.

nodes.title: Neglected Hessian component explains mysteries in sharpness regularization
nodes.tldr: Argues the indefinite nonlinear modeling error part of the Hessian explains why SAM-style sharpness regularization helps while gradient penalties and weight noise often do not.
nodes.problem: Why similar sharpness regularizers (SAM, gradient penalty, weight noise) differ in generalization benefit.
nodes.approach: Decompose Hessian into Gauss-Newton and nonlinear modeling error matrices; analyze empirically and theoretically.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Sharpness literature is established; Hessian decomposition angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Adaptive Image Quality Assessment via Teaching Large Multimodal Model to Compare
nodes.tldr: Trains a large multimodal model to compare image quality pairs and converts soft comparisons against anchor images into continuous quality scores via MAP estimation.
nodes.problem: Turning relative quality comparisons from LMMs into reliable continuous perceptual quality scores is unexplored.
nodes.approach: Scaled comparative instruction tuning across IQA datasets and soft-comparison inference against anchors with maximum a posteriori score estimation.
nodes.niche_reason: LMM-based quality assessment is established but specialised.

nodes.title: SeeA*: Efficient Exploration-Enhanced A* Search by Selective Sampling
nodes.tldr: Speeds up A* search by expanding the best node from a sampled subset of the open list, enabling exploration of promising branches.
nodes.problem: A* search trusts an imperfect heuristic and always expands the single best open node, limiting exploration.
nodes.approach: Selective sampling builds a dynamic subset of OPEN and expands its best-heuristic node, with three sampling techniques compared.
nodes.confidence_reason: Classical heuristic search, filed under exploration; could be planning
nodes.niche_reason: Revisits classical heuristic search, an unusual direction for ML venues

nodes.title: Polynomial-Time Computation of Exact $\Phi$-Equilibria in Polyhedral Games
nodes.tldr: Gives the first polynomial-time algorithm for exact linear-deviation correlated equilibria in extensive-form games, via a generalized Ellipsoid Against Hope framework.
