nodes.niche_reason: Open VLM releases are a crowded mainstream area.

nodes.title: The Generative Leap: Tight Sample Complexity for Efficiently Learning Gaussian Multi-Index Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces generative leap exponent and proves sample complexity d^{max(1,k*/2)} is necessary for low-degree algorithms and achieved by spectral U-statistics for Gaussian multi-index models.
nodes.problem: Tight sample complexity for efficiently recovering the hidden subspace in Gaussian multi-index models.
nodes.approach: Low-degree polynomial lower bound plus sequential spectral U-statistic estimator on Hermite tensors.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Highly technical high-dimensional statistics theory with few similar papers.

nodes.title: Diversity-Aware Policy Optimization for Large Language Model Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Studies solution diversity in RL for LLM reasoning, introduces potential@k, and proposes a token-level diversity objective applied to positive samples in R1-zero style training.
nodes.problem: The role of solution diversity in RL-based LLM reasoning training is underexplored.
nodes.approach: Token-level diversity objective selectively applied to positive samples within R1-zero style policy optimization.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Very crowded RL-for-reasoning space following DeepSeek-R1.

nodes.title: Self-Assembling Graph Perceptrons
nodes.tldr: Graph Perceptrons self-assemble during training, adapting neurons and synapses to match MLP performance at about 5% of the size, aiding interpretability.
nodes.problem: Artificial networks need hand-crafted architectures and overparameterization, unlike plastic biological brains.
nodes.approach: Graph Perceptron with a self-assembly mechanism that adapts neuron count and connectivity during training.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans architecture design, neuroscience inspiration, and network compression.
nodes.niche_reason: Brain-inspired self-growing networks are unusual versus mainstream architectures.

nodes.title: Generalizable Reasoning through Compositional Energy Minimization
nodes.tldr: Composes learned energy landscapes over subproblems at test time to solve harder reasoning instances, with parallel energy minimization for sampling.
nodes.problem: End-to-end reasoning models fail to generalize to problems larger than their training distribution.
nodes.approach: Compositional energy functions over subproblems plus Parallel Energy Minimization sampling.
nodes.confidence_reason: Reasoning-as-energy fits neither LLM reasoning nor sampling cleanly
nodes.niche_reason: Energy-based compositional reasoning is an unusual direction

nodes.title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
nodes.tldr: Vgent builds graph-structured video representations and uses retrieval plus structured reasoning to improve long video question answering in video LLMs.
nodes.problem: Long videos exceed LVLM context windows and lose temporal dependencies in standard retrieval.
nodes.approach: Graph-based video retrieval with an intermediate structured verification and reasoning step.
nodes.niche_reason: Video RAG is an active, fairly crowded research direction.

nodes.title: Solving Neural Min-Max Games: The Role of Architecture, Initialization & Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Proves global convergence of gradient descent-ascent for non-convex min-max games with two-layer networks, via hidden convexity and overparameterization.
nodes.problem: Why simple gradient methods converge in non-convex neural min-max games.
nodes.approach: Hidden convex-concave geometry plus path-length bound for alternating gradient descent-ascent.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Optimization vs deep learning theory boundary.
nodes.niche_reason: Hidden-convexity min-max analysis for two-layer networks is rare.

nodes.title: Open-Insect: Benchmarking Open-Set Recognition of Novel Species in Biodiversity Monitoring
nodes.tldr: Introduces Open-Insect, a fine-grained insect image dataset benchmarking 38 open-set recognition methods for detecting unseen species in biodiversity monitoring.
nodes.problem: Image classifiers cannot flag unseen species in poorly studied, highly diverse insect taxa.
nodes.approach: Benchmark of 38 open-set recognition methods across post-hoc, regularization, and auxiliary-data training.
nodes.niche_reason: Insect open-set recognition for biodiversity is a rare application niche

nodes.title: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents
nodes.tldr: SWE-smith synthesizes 50k bug-fixing tasks with auto-built environments from Python repos, training a state-of-the-art open software engineering agent model.
nodes.problem: Training data for software engineering agents is scarce, small, and expensive to build and store.
nodes.approach: Pipeline that creates repo environments and synthesizes task instances that break existing tests, then trains agents on trajectories.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: SWE agents and coding data are a very crowded topic.

nodes.title: Efficient Fairness-Performance Pareto Front Computation
nodes.tldr: Computes the optimal fairness-performance Pareto front without training fair representation models, by reducing it to a compact discrete problem solved with concave-convex programming.
nodes.problem: Computing the optimal fairness-accuracy trade-off typically requires training complex fair representation models.
nodes.approach: Derive structural properties of optimal fair representations, reduce to a compact discrete problem, solve via concave-convex programming.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical fairness trade-off computation is specialised.

nodes.title: InfMasking: Unleashing Synergistic Information by Contrastive Multimodal Interactions
nodes.tldr: Enhances synergistic cross-modal information by aligning fused representations with masked-feature versions, using a mutual-information-based InfMasking loss.
nodes.problem: Multimodal fusion misses synergistic information that only emerges from specific cross-modal interactions.
nodes.approach: Contrastive alignment of fused representations with heavily masked modality features via a mutual-information InfMasking loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Contrastive fusion objective could also fit self-supervised representation topics
nodes.niche_reason: Synergy-focused multimodal contrastive learning is a specialised angle

nodes.title: Advanced Sign Language Video Generation with Compressed and Quantized Multi-Condition Tokenization
nodes.tldr: SignViP generates identity-preserving sign language videos from text by translating it into discrete fine-grained pose and hand tokens that guide a diffusion model.
nodes.problem: Single coarse skeleton conditions limit naturalness and expressiveness of generated sign language videos.
nodes.approach: FSQ autoencoder compresses multi-condition embeddings into discrete tokens; a token translator maps text to them.
nodes.niche_reason: sign language video generation is a specialised application

nodes.title: On Agnostic PAC Learning in the Small Error Regime
nodes.tldr: Constructs an efficient agnostic PAC learner that is constant-factor optimal when the best hypothesis error is small.
nodes.problem: Open whether agnostic learners can match lower bounds when the best achievable error is small.
nodes.approach: Aggregates ERM classifiers into a computationally efficient learner analyzed with tau-dependent error bounds.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-grained agnostic PAC optimality is a narrow theory question

nodes.title: Trust Region Constrained Measure Transport in Path Space for Stochastic Optimal Control and Inference
nodes.tldr: Solves stochastic optimal control by iteratively solving trust-region constrained problems that anneal from the prior to the target path measure.
nodes.problem: Optimizing controls toward a target path measure is hard when it differs greatly from the prior.
nodes.approach: Trust-region constrained subproblems that yield geometric annealing with principled time-step choice.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Stochastic control vs sampling; topic straddles two areas
nodes.niche_reason: Path-space measure transport for control is an unusual angle

nodes.title: Towards Interpretable and Efficient Attention: Compressing All by Contracting a Few
nodes.tldr: Derives Contract-and-Broadcast Self-Attention from a unified optimization objective via algorithm unrolling, yielding attention that is interpretable and linear-time through a few representative tokens.
nodes.problem: Attention lacks a clear optimization objective and has quadratic cost; interpretability and efficiency are studied separately.
nodes.approach: Unroll a gradient step of a compression objective into CBSA, contracting few representatives and broadcasting to tokens.
nodes.niche_reason: White-box attention from unrolling is established but specialised.

nodes.title: LaViDa: A Large Diffusion Model for Vision-Language Understanding
nodes.tldr: Builds a vision-language model on a discrete diffusion language model, enabling faster parallel decoding and controllable, bidirectional generation.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive VLMs are slow at inference and hard to control, such as format-constrained outputs.
nodes.approach: Equip a diffusion LM with a vision encoder, using complementary masking, prefix KV cache, and timestep shifting.
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment between multimodal LLMs and diffusion language models.
nodes.niche_reason: Established multimodal area; diffusion-based VLMs are uncommon.

nodes.title: OpenCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents
nodes.tldr: OpenCUA releases annotation tools, a large multi-OS computer-use dataset, and open agent models that lead open systems on OSWorld-Verified.
nodes.problem: Capable computer-use agents are closed, leaving research on their capabilities and risks blocked.
nodes.approach: Human demonstration annotation infrastructure, AgentNet dataset, and reflective long chain-of-thought state-action pipeline.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Computer-use agents are a fast-growing, crowded area.

nodes.title: From Counterfactuals to Trees: Competitive Analysis of Model Extraction Attacks
nodes.tldr: Formalises model extraction through competitive analysis and gives reconstruction algorithms that perfectly recover additive tree models, with query complexity bounds.
nodes.problem: Counterfactual explanations raise model-extraction risk, and the oracle queries needed are not formally characterised.
nodes.approach: Anytime reconstruction algorithms for decision trees, gradient boosting and random forests, analysed via competitive analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Extraction via counterfactual oracles with competitive analysis is rare.

nodes.title: A Closer Look at Model Collapse: From a Generalization-to-Memorization Perspective
nodes.tldr: Shows diffusion models shift from generalization to memorization when trained recursively on synthetic data, and proposes entropy-based data selection to mitigate collapse.
nodes.problem: Recursive training on synthetic diffusion outputs causes collapse, with models increasingly memorizing data.
nodes.approach: Entropy-based selection of synthetic training samples in each recursive cycle to keep generation diverse.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Collapse from synthetic data straddles data curation and diffusion memorization
nodes.niche_reason: Model collapse is an active but common theme in generative research

nodes.title: Hierarchical Shortest-Path Graph Kernel Network
nodes.tldr: Integrates a hierarchical shortest-path graph kernel with learnable hidden graph features, so graph similarity is trained end-to-end for graph classification.
nodes.problem: Graph kernels use fixed similarity measures that cannot be optimized for the downstream task.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical shortest-path kernel features matched against learnable hidden graph features, trained end-to-end.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Learnable graph kernels are specialised but established.

nodes.title: Deep Continuous-Time State-Space Models for Marked Event Sequences
nodes.tldr: State-space point process model for marked event sequences that uses jump SDEs and a parallel scan for linear-time, expressive intensities.
nodes.problem: Existing marked temporal point process models are limited in expressivity and inductive bias for irregular event times.
nodes.approach: Interleaves stochastic jump differential equations with nonlinearities in a deep SSM, trained with a parallel scan.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Deep SSMs applied to marked temporal point processes; specialised

nodes.title: The Complexity of Symmetric Equilibria in Min-Max Optimization and Team Zero-Sum Games
nodes.tldr: Proves computing Nash equilibria in 3-player adversarial team games is CLS-complete and symmetric equilibria in symmetric min-max and team zero-sum games are PPAD-complete.
nodes.problem: Computational complexity of symmetric equilibria in min-max optimization and team zero-sum games.
nodes.approach: Reductions from symmetric identical-payoff two-player games using polymatrix constructions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Pure computational complexity of equilibria; few ML papers resemble it.

nodes.title: CoLT: The conditional localization test for assessing the accuracy of neural posterior estimates
nodes.tldr: CoLT is a conditional localization test that learns where a neural posterior estimate deviates most from the true posterior, validating simulation-based inference with single true-posterior draws per input.
nodes.problem: Validating whether a neural posterior estimate accurately approximates the true posterior across all inputs.
nodes.approach: Learn a localization function selecting points of maximal discrepancy for a conditional hypothesis test.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical testing of neural posterior estimators is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Understanding Parametric and Contextual Knowledge Reconciliation within Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Traces how LLMs reconcile parametric and retrieved contextual knowledge through entity flows, finding each knowledge type is routed via separate attention heads.
nodes.problem: Unclear how LLMs internally resolve conflicts between retrieved and parametric knowledge.
nodes.approach: Entity-aware linear probes with special marker tokens and a rank-8 LoRA, tracing entity flows across layers.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Entity-flow tracing of parametric vs contextual knowledge conflicts; specialised.

nodes.title: DAPO : Improving Multi-Step Reasoning Abilities of Large Language Models with Direct Advantage-Based Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: Step-level offline RL with an independently trained critic giving dense per-step advantages, improving multi-step math and code reasoning in LLMs.
nodes.problem: Sparse outcome rewards create high-variance policy optimization and poor value estimates for LLM reasoning.
nodes.approach: Direct advantage-based policy optimization with a critic trained separately from the actor.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL for LLM reasoning is very crowded; step-level variants are common.

nodes.title: Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Adversarial Attacks
nodes.tldr: Dynamical low-rank training with a spectral regularizer controlling core condition number compresses networks over 94 percent while retaining or improving adversarial robustness.
nodes.problem: Compressing networks for constrained devices usually degrades adversarial robustness.
nodes.approach: Rank-adaptive dynamical low-rank training plus a regularizer on the condition number of each layer's low-rank core.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Low-rank compression combined with robustness is specialised.

nodes.title: A Closer Look at Graph Transformers: Cross-Aggregation and Beyond
nodes.tldr: Identifies cross-aggregation as the shared mechanism behind graph transformer topology strategies and proposes UGCFormer, a linear-complexity dual cross-attention transformer with consistency constraint.
nodes.problem: The mechanism behind how graph transformers exploit topology information is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Linearized dual cross-attention between topology and node attributes plus representational consistency constraint.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph transformers are a common research direction.

nodes.title: Learning Robust Vision-Language Models from Natural Latent Spaces
nodes.tldr: CoAPT tunes prompts for robust VLMs by denoising images with total variation and restoring features from pretrained latent space, balancing clean and adversarial accuracy.
nodes.problem: Adversarial prompt tuning for VLMs hurts either clean generalisation or adversarial robustness.
nodes.approach: Total-variation smoothing of images to disrupt perturbations, then guided feature restoration in VLM latent space.
nodes.niche_reason: adversarial prompt tuning for VLMs is a crowded line

nodes.title: MigGPT: Harnessing Large Language Models for Automated Migration of Out-of-Tree Linux Kernel Patches Across Versions
nodes.tldr: MigGPT uses a code fingerprint structure and three modules to let LLMs migrate out-of-tree Linux kernel patches across versions, reaching 72.59% completion on a new benchmark.
nodes.problem: Manual maintenance of out-of-tree kernel patches across versions, with LLMs struggling on context and migration points.
nodes.approach: Code fingerprint structure preserving snippet information, plus modules for accurate migration point identification and patching.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Linux kernel patch migration with LLMs is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: d1: Scaling Reasoning in Diffusion Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Adapts pretrained masked diffusion LLMs into reasoning models using masked SFT followed by diffu-GRPO, a critic-free policy-gradient RL method.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether non-autoregressive diffusion LLMs can benefit from RL-based reasoning advances.
nodes.approach: Masked SFT distills reasoning data; diffu-GRPO applies critic-free policy gradients to masked dLLMs.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL for diffusion LLMs is an emerging but specialised direction

nodes.title: Composite Flow Matching for Reinforcement Learning with Shifted-Dynamics Data
nodes.tldr: CompFlow models target dynamics as a conditional flow on the source-domain flow, estimating the dynamics gap via Wasserstein distance to exploit shifted-dynamics offline RL data.
nodes.problem: Source-domain offline data with dynamics shift is hard to exploit; KL-based gap estimates are ill-defined for disjoint support.
nodes.approach: Composite flow matching linking source and target dynamics, with Wasserstein-based dynamics gap estimation.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Off-dynamics RL with flow matching is a specialised combination.

nodes.title: OpenBox: Annotate Any Bounding Boxes in 3D
nodes.tldr: OpenBox auto-annotates 3D bounding boxes by linking 2D foundation-model instances to point clouds and sizing boxes by rigidity and motion state, avoiding self-training.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised open-vocabulary 3D box annotation is low-quality and requires costly iterative self-training.
nodes.approach: Two-stage pipeline: 2D-to-3D cue association with refinement, then rigidity/motion-aware class-specific box generation.
nodes.niche_reason: Auto-labeling for driving 3D detection is established but specialised.

nodes.title: MDReID: Modality-Decoupled Learning for Any-to-Any Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification
nodes.tldr: Decouples modality-shared and modality-specific features so object re-identification works across mismatched image modalities.
nodes.problem: Re-identification assumes matched modalities, failing when query and gallery modalities differ.
nodes.approach: Modality Decoupling Module plus modality-aware metric learning exploiting shared and specific feature distributions.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: No re-ID topic in vocab; cross-modal representation is the closest fit.
nodes.niche_reason: Any-to-any multi-modal re-ID is a specialised, less-crowded direction.

nodes.title: What Makes a Reward Model a Good Teacher? An Optimization Perspective
nodes.tldr: Shows reward models with low reward variance cause flat RLHF objectives and slow optimization, so accuracy alone is an insufficient reward-model criterion.
nodes.problem: Reward models are judged by accuracy, which may not reflect their usefulness for RLHF optimization.
nodes.approach: Proves flat-landscape bounds tied to reward variance, validated with experiments on language models up to 8B.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: RLHF reward-model quality is a crowded mainstream area.

nodes.title: Escaping saddle points without Lipschitz smoothness: the power of nonlinear preconditioning
nodes.tldr: Shows nonlinearly preconditioned gradient methods, including clipping, still avoid saddle points under generalized smoothness, with near-dimension-free second-order guarantees.
nodes.problem: Saddle-point escape analysis of gradient methods assumes Lipschitz smoothness that practical problems violate.
nodes.approach: Dynamical systems tools applied to a unified generalized-smoothness condition for nonlinear preconditioning and clipping.
nodes.niche_reason: Established nonconvex optimization theory, specialised angle

nodes.title: Understanding LLM Behaviors via Compression: Data Generation, Knowledge Acquisition and Scaling Laws
nodes.tldr: Explains LLM scaling laws, knowledge acquisition, and hallucinations by viewing LLM training as Kolmogorov-style compression within a Syntax-Knowledge data model.
nodes.problem: Principled explanations of LLM scaling laws, hallucinations, and knowledge acquisition are lacking.
nodes.approach: Two-part coding via Kolmogorov Structure Function, analyzed in a Bayesian hierarchical data-generation model.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.confidence_reason: theory spans information theory and LLM scaling topics
nodes.niche_reason: theoretical compression view of LLMs is specialised

nodes.title: MedSG-Bench: A Benchmark for Medical Image Sequences Grounding
nodes.tldr: A benchmark and instruction-tuning dataset for grounding in medical image sequences, covering change and consistency grounding across modalities, plus a baseline MLLM.
nodes.problem: Medical visual grounding benchmarks ignore sequential images needing cross-image alignment and temporal comparison.
nodes.approach: Eight VQA-style tasks over 76 datasets, a 188K instruction dataset, and the MedSeq-Grounder MLLM.
nodes.niche_reason: Sequential medical image grounding for MLLMs is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Differentiable Sparsity via $D$-Gating: Simple and Versatile Structured Penalization
nodes.tldr: Differentiable structured overparameterization splitting weight groups into a primary vector and scalar gates, equivalent to group sparsity penalties, needing no special optimizer.
nodes.problem: Structured sparsity penalties are non-differentiable and break standard SGD.
nodes.approach: Gated overparameterization whose local minima match L2,2/D group penalties, with gradient-flow convergence.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Gating reparameterization for group sparsity is specialized but not rare.

nodes.title: A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Proposes a taxonomy and evaluation protocol quantifying online tuning budgets for offline RL, provides clean single-file implementations, and the Unifloral algorithm yielding TD3-AWR and MoBRAC.
nodes.problem: Offline RL suffers from ambiguous problem definitions, entangled designs, and unfair evaluation hidden by online hyperparameter tuning.
nodes.approach: Taxonomy, budget-aware evaluation, minimal implementations, and a unified algorithm with shared hyperparameter space.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL algorithms are a common, active area.

nodes.title: VITA-1.5: Towards GPT-4o Level Real-Time Vision and Speech Interaction
nodes.tldr: Multi-stage training teaches an LLM to understand vision and speech, enabling end-to-end real-time speech-to-speech dialogue without separate ASR and TTS modules.
nodes.problem: Achieving strong vision and speech performance together in a multimodal LLM for real-time interaction.
nodes.approach: Progressive multi-stage training integrating visual and speech modalities with end-to-end speech generation.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal LLMs are crowded; speech integration is somewhat less so.

nodes.title: Cue3D: Quantifying the Role of Image Cues in Single-Image 3D Generation
nodes.tldr: Model-agnostic framework that perturbs shading, texture, silhouette and other cues to measure how seven single-image 3D generators use each cue.
nodes.problem: Unclear which image cues single-image 3D generators actually rely on
nodes.approach: Systematic perturbation of monocular cues across seven state-of-the-art 3D generators
nodes.confidence_reason: Analysis paper; topic split between generative 3D and monocular geometry.
nodes.niche_reason: Cue-level analysis of 3D generators is a small, emerging area

nodes.title: UFO: A Unified Approach to Fine-grained Visual Perception via Open-ended Language Interface
nodes.tldr: Unifies object detection, segmentation and vision-language tasks by casting all perception targets into language, using embedding retrieval for pixel-level segmentation.
nodes.problem: Integrating fine-grained perception into generalist models needs task-specific architectures that complicate training.
nodes.approach: Language-space target representation with a retrieval-based segmentation head, trained multi-task on five datasets.
nodes.confidence_reason: Generalist perception straddles segmentation and multimodal LLM topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Generalist perception with language interfaces is a common, crowded direction.

nodes.title: Gaze Beyond the Frame: Forecasting Egocentric 3D Visual Span
nodes.tldr: Forecasts future 3D visual span from egocentric views by lifting SLAM keypoints into gaze-compatible volumes and predicting with 3D U-Net and transformers.
nodes.problem: Forecasting where a person's visual attention goes next in 3D is under-explored compared with motion forecasting.
nodes.approach: Lifts SLAM keypoints into gaze-compatible volumes, then predicts future visual-span regions with 3D U-Net and transformers.
nodes.confidence_reason: Egocentric gaze forecasting; video vs 3D-scene topics both plausible.
nodes.niche_reason: 3D egocentric visual-span forecasting is a rare direction.

nodes.title: GraLoRA: Granular Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
nodes.tldr: GraLoRA partitions weight matrices into sub-blocks each with its own low-rank adapter, fixing LoRA's gradient entanglement and rank-scaling limits at negligible extra cost.
nodes.problem: LoRA overfits and stagnates at higher ranks due to structural bottleneck and gradient entanglement.
nodes.approach: Granular low-rank adaptation using per-sub-block adapters of the weight matrix.
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another LoRA variant in a very crowded area.

nodes.title: Embodied Web Agents: Bridging Physical-Digital Realms for Integrated Agent Intelligence
nodes.tldr: Embodied Web Agents bridges embodied 3D environments with web interfaces, releasing a benchmark of cooking, navigation, shopping and geolocation tasks revealing large gaps to humans.
nodes.problem: Agents are siloed between physical embodiment and web knowledge
nodes.approach: Unified simulation platform integrating 3D environments with web interfaces and benchmark
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Combining embodied and web agents is unusual.

nodes.title: Differentiable Cyclic Causal Discovery Under Unmeasured Confounders
nodes.tldr: DCCD-CONF learns nonlinear cyclic causal graphs with unmeasured confounders from interventional data by alternating graph optimization and confounder-distribution estimation via log-likelihood, with consistency guarantees.
nodes.problem: Causal discovery with feedback loops and hidden confounders in nonlinear systems.
nodes.approach: Differentiable likelihood-based alternating optimization of cyclic graph structure and confounder distribution.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Cyclic, confounded differentiable causal discovery is rare.

nodes.title: Clustering via Hedonic Games: New Concepts and Algorithms
nodes.tldr: Connects graphical hedonic games to clustering, designing efficient algorithms for locally stable and locally popular partitions with friend and enemy graphs, applied to clustering and community detection.
nodes.problem: Linking coalition formation game stability to data clustering and community detection.
nodes.approach: Define local popularity and local stability on friend/enemy graphs and design polynomial-time algorithms.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Hedonic games for clustering is very rare in ML.

nodes.title: Asymmetric Duos: Sidekicks Improve Uncertainty
nodes.tldr: Proposes Asymmetric Duos, pairing a large model with a smaller sidekick via learned weighted averaging, improving accuracy and uncertainty at about 10-20% extra compute.
nodes.problem: Ensembling full-size networks for uncertainty is too costly for today's large models and fine-tuning.
nodes.approach: Learned weighted averaging of a large model's predictions with a cheap, less accurate sidekick model.
nodes.niche_reason: Ensembling for uncertainty is a common, well-explored direction

nodes.title: Guarantees for Alternating Least Squares in Overparameterized Tensor Decompositions
nodes.tldr: Proves that overparameterizing the rank in alternating least squares provably makes tensor decomposition converge globally with high probability under random initialization.
nodes.problem: Global convergence of iterative tensor decomposition methods, which lack guarantees in non-convex settings.
nodes.approach: Overparameterized ALS with rank k=O(r^2) and new matrix anticoncentration arguments.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Rare theory of overparameterized ALS for tensor decomposition

nodes.title: OmniSync: Towards Universal Lip Synchronization via Diffusion Transformers
nodes.tldr: Mask-free diffusion-transformer lip-sync framework that edits video frames directly, with spatiotemporal classifier-free guidance to strengthen weak audio conditioning.
nodes.problem: Lip sync methods rely on reference frames and masks, limiting robustness to pose, occlusion, and stylized content.
nodes.approach: Diffusion transformer trained mask-free with flow-matching noise initialization and dynamic guidance.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Audio-driven lip sync is a specialised generative video task

nodes.title: Memo: Training Memory-Efficient Embodied Agents with Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Memo trains transformer RL policies by interleaving periodic summarization tokens, enabling memory-efficient long-horizon embodied decision-making.
nodes.problem: Visual inputs overflow transformer context limits in long-horizon embodied RL.
nodes.approach: Interleaved summarization tokens create and retrieve compressed memory during training.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Memory architecture for RL; could fit LLM memory or embodied RL
nodes.niche_reason: Memory-compressed transformer RL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Multitask Learning with Stochastic Interpolants
nodes.tldr: Operator-based stochastic interpolants generalize flow and diffusion time dynamics to vectors, matrices and operators, enabling zero-shot conditional generation and inpainting.
nodes.problem: Flow and diffusion models need task-specific training and cannot bridge distributions across dimensions.
nodes.approach: Replace scalar time in stochastic interpolants with vectors, matrices or linear operators for multitask generation.
nodes.niche_reason: Generalized interpolant frameworks are specialised but established.

nodes.title: StreamForest: Efficient Online Video Understanding with Persistent Event Memory
nodes.tldr: Streaming video MLLM that stores past frames in a persistent event-level memory forest and uses fine-grained short-term windows for real-time perception.
nodes.problem: Online video MLLMs struggle with storage of history and real-time spatiotemporal reasoning.
nodes.approach: Persistent event memory forest with penalty-guided merging plus a fine-grained spatiotemporal window.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Streaming video MLLMs with memory structures are specialised.

nodes.title: Precise Asymptotics and Refined Regret of Variance-Aware UCB
nodes.tldr: Characterizes asymptotic arm-pulling rates of UCB-V, reveals possible instability, and proves a refined regret bound with matching lower bound.
nodes.problem: Behavior and sharp regret of variance-aware UCB in multi-armed bandits are not understood.
nodes.approach: Asymptotic and high-probability analysis of arm-pulling rates, yielding refined regret upper bound and matching lower bound.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Bandit theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Depth-Width Tradeoffs for Transformers on Graph Tasks
nodes.tldr: Shows linearly wide transformers solve many graph tasks at constant depth, while some tasks need quadratic width; wider models train and infer faster.
nodes.problem: Minimal transformer size needed for graph algorithmic tasks is not well understood as width grows.
nodes.approach: Shows linear width lets constant-depth transformers solve many graph tasks; some need quadratic width.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Expressivity theory of graph transformers is specialised

nodes.title: Establishing Linear Surrogate Regret Bounds for Convex Smooth Losses via Convolutional Fenchel–Young Losses
nodes.tldr: Constructs a convex smooth surrogate loss with linear surrogate regret bound for discrete targets, via Fenchel-Young losses from a convolutional negentropy.
nodes.problem: Believed trade-off: smooth convex surrogates lose linear surrogate regret bounds.
nodes.approach: Infimal convolution of a generalized negentropy with the target Bayes risk yields smooth Fenchel-Young losses plus a tailored link.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Surrogate regret theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: FAPEX: Fractional Amplitude-Phase Expressor for Robust Cross-Subject Seizure Prediction
nodes.tldr: FAPEX uses a learnable fractional neural frame operator for time-frequency decomposition plus state-space and channel attention to predict seizures across subjects and recording modalities.
nodes.problem: Subject-agnostic seizure prediction under high spectral variability across individuals and recordings.
nodes.approach: Fractional-order learnable time-frequency operator extracting phase/amplitude, with state-space modeling and channelwise attention.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: EEG seizure prediction with fractional operators is niche.

nodes.title: TREND: Unsupervised 3D Representation Learning via Temporal Forecasting for LiDAR Perception
nodes.tldr: Pre-trains LiDAR 3D representations unsupervised by forecasting future observations with a recurrent embedding and a temporal LiDAR neural field rendered differentiably.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised LiDAR pre-training ignores temporal sequences capturing object motion and semantics.
nodes.approach: Recurrent embeddings across time plus a temporal LiDAR neural field with differentiable rendering loss for forecasting.
nodes.niche_reason: LiDAR self-supervised pre-training is established but specialised.

nodes.title: UniSite: The First Cross-Structure Dataset and Learning Framework for End-to-End Ligand Binding Site Detection
nodes.tldr: UniSite introduces the first cross-structure dataset and end-to-end set-prediction framework for protein ligand binding site detection, with new evaluation metrics.
nodes.problem: Binding site detection datasets are complex-centric, pipelines are discontinuous, and metrics are inadequate.
nodes.approach: Cross-structure dataset, end-to-end detection framework, and improved evaluation metrics.
nodes.niche_reason: Ligand binding-site detection is a niche structural biology task.

nodes.title: What Expressivity Theory Misses: Message Passing Complexity for GNNs
nodes.tldr: Proposes Message Passing Complexity, a continuous measure of how hard a task is for a GNN via message passing, capturing over-squashing beyond expressivity theory.
nodes.problem: Expressivity theory is binary and idealized, and higher expressivity is unnecessary for most real tasks.
nodes.approach: Continuous complexity measure for message-passing architectures, validated against empirical GNN performance.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: GNN theory beyond expressivity is a specialised but active niche.

nodes.title: Sketched Gaussian Mechanism for Private Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: Combines sketching and the Gaussian mechanism into one private federated learning scheme, with privacy improving as sketch dimension grows and competitive utility.
nodes.problem: Communication compression and client differential privacy are analysed separately, leaving privacy loose.
nodes.approach: Joint Renyi-DP analysis of sketched Gaussian mechanism with gradient descent or adaptive server optimizers.
nodes.niche_reason: Joint sketching and DP analysis is specialised but established

nodes.title: STITCH-OPE: Trajectory Stitching with Guided Diffusion for Off-Policy Evaluation
nodes.tldr: STITCH-OPE uses a behavior-pretrained diffusion model guided by target-policy score minus behavior score, and stitches partial trajectories for long-horizon off-policy evaluation with reduced variance.
nodes.problem: Off-policy evaluation suffers variance blow-up or compounding model errors in long-horizon high-dimensional problems.
nodes.approach: Guided denoising diffusion with behavior-score subtraction and trajectory stitching to generate target-policy rollouts.
nodes.niche_reason: Off-policy evaluation with diffusion models is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Improving Perturbation-based Explanations by Understanding the Role of Uncertainty Calibration
nodes.tldr: Shows models are miscalibrated under explanation perturbations, proves this hurts explanation quality, and introduces ReCalX to recalibrate models while preserving predictions.
nodes.problem: Perturbation-based explanations are unreliable because model behavior under perturbations is miscalibrated.
nodes.approach: ReCalX recalibration targeted at perturbation-specific miscalibration, with theory on explanation quality.
nodes.niche_reason: Linking calibration and explanation reliability is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: Inner Speech as Behavior Guides: Steerable Imitation of Diverse Behaviors for Human-AI coordination
nodes.tldr: Generates language inner speech from observations with a VLM-guided CVAE, then conditions a diffusion behavior-cloning policy on it to steer diverse behavior.
nodes.problem: Imitation learning misses the diversity and non-Markovian nature of human behavior and cannot steer it at inference.
nodes.approach: VLM-scaffolded CVAE produces inner speech as behavioral intent; diffusion policy conditions on it.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Inner speech as steering intent for imitation is a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: EvoLM: In Search of Lost Language Model Training Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Trains over 100 small LMs from scratch to analyze how pre-training, continued pre-training, SFT, and RL each affect reasoning, releasing all models and data.
nodes.problem: Downstream developers cannot easily tell how each LM training stage's design choices affect results.
nodes.approach: Trains over 100 LMs from scratch across pre-training, continued pre-training, SFT, and RL, releasing all artifacts.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: LM training-stage analysis is a common research theme

nodes.title: Rethinking Entropy in Test-Time Adaptation: The Missing Piece from Energy Duality
nodes.tldr: Argues entropy minimization alone fails to reduce energy, and proposes ReTTA, which jointly optimizes likelihood and entropy at test time.
nodes.problem: Entropy-minimizing test-time adaptation ignores energy and gives unreliable likelihood estimates.
nodes.approach: Energy-based likelihood objective trained with sliced score matching, plus a cross-entropy term.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Test-time adaptation and energy-based likelihood modelling are close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Energy-based test-time adaptation is a less common TTA angle.

nodes.title: UniteFormer: Unifying Node and Edge Modalities in Transformers for Vehicle Routing Problems
nodes.tldr: UniteFormer is a single neural vehicle-routing solver handling node-only, edge-only or hybrid inputs via a mixed GCN-attention encoder, trained with REINFORCE and strong on TSP/CVRP.
nodes.problem: Neural VRP solvers rely on either node or edge inputs, limiting flexibility and generalization.
nodes.approach: Mixed GCN-attention encoder with parallel decoder, trained by REINFORCE on randomly sampled input types.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural combinatorial optimization is a relatively small subfield.

nodes.title: Why Diffusion Models Don’t Memorize: The Role of Implicit Dynamical Regularization in Training
nodes.tldr: Shows diffusion models generalize early and memorize later, with memorization onset scaling linearly in training set size, creating a window where generalization persists.
nodes.problem: Why diffusion models generalize rather than memorize training data remains unexplained.
nodes.approach: Analysis of two training timescales, plus a random features model in the high-dimensional limit.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Memorization dynamics in diffusion models is a growing theory topic

nodes.title: Sampling-Efficient Test-Time Scaling: Self-Estimating the Best-of-N Sampling in Early Decoding
nodes.tldr: Best-of-N decoding that truncates unpromising samples early using internal-state consistency, so no reward model is needed.
nodes.problem: Best-of-N sampling is memory-hungry and needs costly reward models for selection.
nodes.approach: Early sampling consistency in internal states identifies the most promising path, truncating the rest.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Test-time scaling and best-of-N are active, common topics

nodes.title: Q-Insight: Understanding Image Quality via Visual Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Q-Insight trains an MLLM with GRPO to reason about image quality, giving interpretable assessments and scores from limited rating data without heavy supervised fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: MLLM-based image quality methods give uninterpretable scores or need large annotated supervised datasets.
nodes.approach: GRPO reinforcement learning on a multimodal LLM with score and degradation reasoning rewards.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: IQA with MLLM RL is specialised, though RL-for-MLLM is trending.

nodes.title: Selective Omniprediction and Fair Abstention
nodes.tldr: Gives algorithms for selective classifiers that abstain optimally for an entire class of losses, extends to group-wise fair abstention, and connects to group-conditional conformal prediction.
nodes.problem: Building a single abstaining classifier that is optimal across many losses and subgroups.
nodes.approach: Omniprediction and multigroup fairness via calibrated multiaccurate predictors with post-processed abstention.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Omniprediction with abstention is a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: DMWM: Dual-Mind World Model with Long-Term Imagination
nodes.tldr: DMWM pairs an RSSM intuitive system with a logic-integrated neural network reasoning system to keep long-horizon imagination logically consistent and reduce accumulated prediction error.
nodes.problem: RSSM world models accumulate prediction errors, limiting long-term imagination for policy learning.
nodes.approach: Dual-process world model: RSSM System 1 plus logic-integrated neural System 2 with inter-system feedback.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Logic-integrated network details are thin in the abstract.
nodes.niche_reason: Neuro-symbolic dual-process world models are unusual.

nodes.title: An Analysis of Causal Effect Estimation using Outcome Invariant Data Augmentation
nodes.tldr: Argues outcome-invariant data augmentation acts as an intervention on treatment, and introduces IV-like regression to reduce hidden-confounding bias in causal estimation.
nodes.problem: Hidden confounding biases causal effect estimates when instruments are unavailable.
nodes.approach: Regularized IV-like regression and parameterized augmentation composed to simulate worst-case shifts.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Causal inference vs augmentation-for-generalization framing.
nodes.niche_reason: Outcome-invariant augmentation as intervention is unusual.

nodes.title: Dual Data Alignment Makes AI-Generated Image Detector Easier Generalizable
nodes.tldr: Detects AI-generated images by aligning real and synthetic training pairs in pixel and frequency domains, removing spurious frequency cues; adds two test sets.
nodes.problem: AI-generated image detectors overfit to spurious biases and generalize poorly.
nodes.approach: Dual Data Alignment fusing real and reconstructed images in pixel and frequency domains.
nodes.niche_reason: Active but specialised forensic detection area.

nodes.title: Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to find interpretable concepts in a text-to-image diffusion model and shows how interventions control composition early and style or texture later.
nodes.problem: Understanding the inner workings and time evolution of concepts in diffusion model generation.
nodes.approach: Sparse autoencoder probing of diffusion activations plus interventions across diffusion timesteps.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic interpretability of diffusion models is emerging but specialised.

nodes.title: LABridge: Text–Image Latent Alignment Framework via Mean-Conditioned OU Process
nodes.tldr: LABridge aligns text and image latents with a mean-conditioned Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, improving text-image alignment with fewer denoising steps.
nodes.problem: Diffusion text-to-image models suffer semantic instability and slow iterative denoising.
nodes.approach: Text-conditioned priors from a learned alignment encoder, joined to image latents by an OU bridge.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion bridges between text priors and image latents are less common

nodes.title: In Search of Adam’s Secret Sauce
nodes.tldr: Trains over 1,500 language models to compare Adam with signed variants, finding beta1 equal to beta2 keeps near-optimal performance and offers an interpretation.
nodes.problem: Why Adam works so well for transformer language model training, beyond signed-gradient simplifications.
nodes.approach: Large-scale comparison of Adam to signed momentum variants, and analysis of constraining beta1 equal beta2.
nodes.niche_reason: Adam variant analysis is a mainstream optimization topic

nodes.title: Scalable Fingerprinting of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Perinucleus sampling embeds up to 24,576 persistent, harmless fingerprints in an LLM, two orders of magnitude more than prior schemes, to identify model ownership via API access.
nodes.problem: Existing LLM fingerprinting schemes embed too few fingerprints, risking false discovery, leakage and coalition attacks.
nodes.approach: Perinucleus sampling to generate scalable, persistent fingerprints, with security analysis.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Model fingerprinting at scale is an uncommon topic.

nodes.title: Mean-Field Sampling for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: SUBSAMPLE-MFQ learns cooperative multi-agent policies in time polynomial in a subsample size k, converging to optimal at O(1/sqrt(k)) via mean-field sampling.
nodes.problem: Joint state-action space grows exponentially with the number of agents in cooperative MARL.
nodes.approach: Mean-field Q-learning on subsampled agents with a decentralized randomized policy and convergence proof.
nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field MARL theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: The ML.ENERGY Benchmark: Toward Automated Inference Energy Measurement and Optimization
nodes.tldr: A benchmark suite and leaderboard measuring inference energy of 40 model architectures across six tasks, showing some optimizations saving over 40% energy.
nodes.problem: Energy is overlooked when benchmarking and optimizing generative AI inference services.
nodes.approach: Realistic service-environment measurement with design principles, plus automated optimization recommendations.
nodes.confidence_reason: Benchmark for energy; could fit systems area instead.
nodes.niche_reason: Energy-focused inference benchmarking is rare relative to accuracy benchmarks.

nodes.title: Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting
nodes.tldr: Grafting edits pretrained diffusion transformers into hybrid architectures (conv, local, linear attention) using under 2% pretraining compute, enabling cheap architecture exploration.
nodes.problem: Studying new architecture designs without costly pretraining from scratch.
nodes.approach: Replace operators and restructure blocks in pretrained DiTs, then briefly fine-tune.
nodes.niche_reason: Architecture exploration via editing pretrained models is somewhat unusual.

nodes.title: IA-GGAD: Zero-shot Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection via Invariant and Affinity Learning
nodes.tldr: Detects anomalies on unseen graphs zero-shot by learning domain-invariant node features and structure-insensitive affinity features.
nodes.problem: Graph anomaly detectors fail across graphs due to feature and structure shifts.
nodes.approach: Anomaly-driven invariant learning for feature shift plus affinity learning for structure shift.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: No anomaly-detection topic; domain generalization vs GNN placement
nodes.niche_reason: Generalist graph anomaly detection is specialised but active

nodes.title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Introduces WebPuzzle benchmark and DeepDiver, an RL framework that teaches LLMs to scale web-search intensity adaptively, matching much larger models on real-web information seeking.
nodes.problem: LLMs under-search and settle on under-evidenced answers in open-web information seeking.
nodes.approach: Cold-start SFT then RL curriculum on synthesized WebPuzzle data to cultivate search intensity scaling.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Search agents trained with RL are a crowded current topic.

nodes.title: QFFT, Question-Free Fine-Tuning for Adaptive Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Question-Free Fine-Tuning trains on long chain-of-thought responses without the question, so models reason briefly on easy problems and at length when needed.
nodes.problem: Long CoT reasoning models overthink, producing redundant steps on simple questions.
nodes.approach: Fine-tune on Long CoT responses with the input question removed to elicit adaptive reasoning patterns.
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient LLM reasoning is a crowded recent topic.

nodes.title: Multi-Agent Learning under Uncertainty: Recurrence vs. Concentration
nodes.tldr: Shows stochastic regularized learning in continuous games need not converge, but under strong monotonicity its long-run play concentrates near equilibrium.
nodes.problem: Characterizing long-run behavior of learning dynamics in games under persistent randomness.
nodes.approach: Analyzes stochastic regularized learning in continuous and discrete time, bounding return times and concentration.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: stochastic regularized learning in games is specialised

nodes.title: Searching Latent Program Spaces
nodes.tldr: Latent Program Network learns a latent space of implicit programs and does gradient-based search in it at test time, doubling out-of-distribution performance on ARC-AGI.
nodes.problem: Neural models lack structured test-time adaptation; program synthesis needs hand-built DSLs and has combinatorial search.
nodes.approach: Architecture with learned latent program space searched by gradient ascent at test time.
nodes.niche_reason: Latent program search for abstract reasoning is an uncommon direction.

nodes.title: Any-stepsize Gradient Descent for Separable Data under Fenchel–Young Losses
nodes.tldr: Shows gradient descent converges with arbitrary stepsize on separable data for many Fenchel-Young losses, attributing rates to separation margin rather than self-bounding.
nodes.problem: Understanding which loss properties allow GD to converge with arbitrarily large stepsizes.
nodes.approach: Perceptron-style convergence analysis for Fenchel-Young losses including Tsallis and Rényi entropies.
nodes.niche_reason: Large-stepsize GD on separable data is a narrow theory niche.

nodes.title: Data-Juicer 2.0: Cloud-Scale Adaptive Data Processing for and with Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Data-Juicer 2.0 is a scalable system with 100+ operators for processing multimodal foundation-model data, with adaptive execution on Ray over TB-scale data.
nodes.problem: Scalable processing of multimodal data for foundation models
nodes.approach: Operator-based system with adaptive runtime layer, Hugging Face and Ray integration
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised data-infrastructure topic, moderately common.

nodes.title: SegMASt3R: Geometry Grounded Segment Matching
nodes.tldr: SegMASt3R uses 3D foundation model priors to match segments across wide-baseline image pairs, beating SAM2 and local feature matching, and aiding mapping and navigation.
nodes.problem: Matching coherent segments across images with extreme viewpoint changes is hard for existing methods.
nodes.approach: Architecture exploiting a 3D foundation model's inductive bias for segment matching up to 180 degree rotations.
nodes.niche_reason: Segment-level wide-baseline matching is rarer than keypoint matching.

nodes.title: Position: Machine Learning Conferences Should Establish a "Refutations and Critiques" Track
nodes.tldr: Argues ML conferences should create a dedicated Refutations and Critiques track so flawed published work can be systematically challenged and corrected.
nodes.problem: Peer review lets flawed ML papers get accepted, with no robust channel for systematic correction.
nodes.approach: Position paper proposing an R&C track, covering track design, review principles, and pitfalls.
nodes.niche_reason: meta-research on conference governance is rare in ML venues

nodes.title: Reinforcement Learning with Imperfect Transition Predictions: A Bellman-Jensen Approach
nodes.tldr: Handles RL with imperfect multi-step transition predictions by introducing a Bayesian value function and Bellman-Jensen gap analysis, giving sample complexity guarantees without exponential state blow-up.
nodes.problem: Multi-step predictions blow up MDP state space and existing RL theory cannot analyze erroneous predictions.
nodes.approach: Bayesian value function and Bellman-Jensen gap analysis for prediction-augmented MDPs.
nodes.niche_reason: RL with imperfect lookahead predictions is a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: MME: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Manually annotated evaluation benchmark covering 14 perception and cognition subtasks, comparing 30 multimodal LLMs with concise instructions to avoid data leakage.
nodes.problem: Anecdotal case studies cannot fully measure multimodal LLM perception and cognition, and public datasets risk leakage.
nodes.approach: Hand-designed instruction-answer pairs with concise, uniform prompts enabling fair quantitative comparison across models.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal LLM benchmarks are a crowded, mainstream direction.

nodes.title: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
nodes.tldr: Introduces OS-Harm, 150 tasks across misuse, prompt injection, and misbehaviour to measure safety of computer-use agents, with an automated judge.
nodes.problem: The safety of LLM computer-use agents that operate GUIs has been largely unmeasured.
nodes.approach: Tasks built on OSWorld, plus an automated judge scoring accuracy and safety of frontier agents.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Agent safety benchmarking for GUI computer-use is uncommon

nodes.title: Convergence Rates of Constrained Expected Improvement
nodes.tldr: Proves constrained expected improvement converges at explicit rates for RKHS and Gaussian process objectives, with Matérn and squared-exponential kernels.
nodes.problem: The convergence rate of constrained expected improvement for constrained Bayesian optimisation was unknown.
nodes.approach: Upper-bound simple regret using RKHS and GP assumptions with standard kernels.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: convergence theory for constrained BO is specialised

nodes.title: Think or Not? Exploring Thinking Efficiency in Large Reasoning Models via an Information-Theoretic Lens
nodes.tldr: Introduces information-theoretic metrics and an entropy-based Adaptive Think strategy that halts reasoning once confident, cutting token use with competitive accuracy.
nodes.problem: Large reasoning models produce excessively long reasoning chains with diminishing information gain.
nodes.approach: InfoBias and InfoGain metrics motivate an entropy-based early-stopping reasoning strategy.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Reasoning-length efficiency is a crowded, fast-moving area.

nodes.title: The Fragile Truth of Saliency: Improving LLM Input Attribution via Attention Bias Optimization
nodes.tldr: Stress-tests LLM input saliency methods with needle-in-a-haystack settings, finds they misattribute irrelevant context, and proposes attention bias optimization for more accurate token attribution.
nodes.problem: Input saliency methods for LLMs lack rigorous evaluation and misassign importance to irrelevant context.
nodes.approach: NIAH-inspired stress tests and a saliency method optimizing per-token attention bias to measure causal impact.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: LLM attribution methods are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Decomposing stimulus-specific sensory neural information via diffusion models
nodes.tldr: Axiomatic decomposition of mutual information into per-stimulus and per-pixel contributions, generalizing Fisher information and made tractable for neural populations via diffusion models.
nodes.problem: Per-stimulus information decompositions are ill-posed and intractable for high-dimensional neural populations.
nodes.approach: Axioms for stimulus-specific decomposition, plus diffusion-model estimators that scale to naturalistic images.
nodes.niche_reason: Axiomatic stimulus-level information decomposition is a very rare topic

nodes.title: NOVA: A Benchmark for Rare Anomaly Localization and Clinical Reasoning in Brain MRI
nodes.tldr: NOVA is an evaluation-only benchmark of about 900 brain MRI scans with 281 rare pathologies, testing anomaly localisation, captioning, and diagnostic reasoning of vision-language models.
nodes.problem: Medical benchmarks with few common outliers fail to test open-world generalization on rare conditions.
nodes.approach: Expert-annotated brain MRI set with clinical narratives and bounding boxes for stress-testing VLMs.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare-disease brain MRI anomaly benchmark is a narrow niche.

nodes.title: Bits Leaked per Query: Information-Theoretic Bounds for Adversarial Attacks on LLMs
nodes.tldr: Bounds attack query counts on LLMs via mutual information, showing that leaking answer tokens, logits, or reasoning traces sharply cuts the queries needed.
nodes.problem: No principled limit exists on how much LLM output leakage enables adversarial attacks on hidden properties.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic bound: queries needed scale with inverse mutual information between observation and target property.

nodes.niche_reason: Information-leakage bounds for LLM attacks are a rare theoretical angle

nodes.title: Zero-shot Denoising via Neural Compression: Theoretical and algorithmic framework
nodes.tldr: ZS-NCD denoises one noisy image by training an untrained neural compression network on its patches, using entropy constraints against overfitting, with error bounds.
nodes.problem: Denoising without training data or clean references while avoiding overfitting to noise.
nodes.approach: Optimize a neural compression network on patches of one noisy image and aggregate overlapping patch outputs.
nodes.niche_reason: Compression-based zero-shot denoising with theory is a rare angle.

nodes.title: Deciphering the Extremes: A Novel Approach for Pathological Long-tailed Recognition in Scientific Discovery
nodes.tldr: Proposes balanced contrastive learning plus smooth regularization to recognize rare classes in extremely imbalanced scientific datasets.
nodes.problem: Existing long-tailed methods fail on scientific data with extreme imbalance and few samples.
nodes.approach: Balanced supervised contrastive learning with smooth objective regularization.

nodes.title: GSRF: Complex-Valued 3D Gaussian Splatting for Efficient Radio-Frequency Data Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to radio-frequency data, using complex-valued Gaussians to synthesize RSSI faster than NeRF methods.
nodes.problem: NeRF-based RF synthesis is accurate but slow to train and slow at inference.

nodes.title: The Power of Iterative Filtering for Supervised Learning with (Heavy) Contamination
nodes.tldr: Introduces iterative polynomial filtering, an outlier-removal method that yields efficient supervised learning under nasty and heavy additive contamination, and tolerant testable learning.
nodes.problem: Supervised learning with adversarially contaminated training data lacks efficient algorithms with strong guarantees.
nodes.approach: Outlier removal via iterative polynomial filtering; low-degree and sandwiching approximators yield learning guarantees.

nodes.niche_reason: Nasty-noise learning via polynomial filtering is a rare theory niche.

nodes.title: Tensor Product Attention Is All You Need
nodes.tldr: Tensor Product Attention factorizes queries, keys, and values into low-rank tensor components, shrinking the KV cache while matching or beating standard Transformers.
nodes.problem: Long-sequence inference needs large key-value caches, which dominate memory overhead.
nodes.approach: Contextual low-rank tensor-decomposed Q, K, V compatible with RoPE.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Tensor-factorized attention is a less common attention variant.

nodes.title: The Graphon Limit Hypothesis: Understanding Neural Network Pruning via Infinite Width Analysis
nodes.tldr: Shows pruned network connectivity converges to graphons at infinite width and derives a Graphon NTK to explain trainability differences between pruning methods.
nodes.problem: Why some sparse structures train better than others at equal sparsity is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Graph-limit (graphon) characterization of sparse connectivity and a derived Graphon neural tangent kernel.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Graph limit theory applied to pruning is rare.

nodes.title: MMLongBench: Benchmarking Long-Context Vision-Language Models Effectively and Thoroughly
nodes.tldr: Introduces a 13k-example benchmark of five long-context vision-language task types, tested at 8K–128K tokens across 46 closed and open models.
nodes.problem: Long-context vision-language models lack thorough benchmarks covering diverse tasks and input lengths.
nodes.approach: Standardized 8K–128K benchmark with 13,331 examples across five task categories and diverse image types.

nodes.title: Enhancing Training Data Attribution with Representational Optimization
nodes.tldr: Representation-based training data attribution using a trainable encoder and attention pooling, learned via a ranking objective to match gradient-based accuracy at far lower cost.
nodes.problem: Gradient-based attribution is costly, while representation-based methods use heuristic embeddings.

nodes.niche_reason: Attribution-optimized representations are a specialized corner of data attribution.

nodes.title: Controlling Thinking Speed in Reasoning Models
nodes.tldr: Finds a steering vector controlling slow versus fast thinking in reasoning models, paired with difficulty estimation, cutting tokens 8.6% with +1.3% accuracy, training-free.
nodes.problem: Large reasoning models cannot adjust thinking speed, causing high latency and compute on easy steps.
nodes.approach: Representation-editing steering vector for slow-fast transitions plus real-time difficulty estimation to adapt per reasoning segment.

nodes.niche_reason: Efficient reasoning in LRMs is a hot, crowded topic.

nodes.title: Abstract Rendering: Certified Rendering Under 3D Semantic Uncertainty
nodes.tldr: Computes provable bounds on all images rendered under varying camera poses and 3D scenes, enabling certification of downstream vision models.
nodes.problem: Continuous camera and scene variations make rendered inputs to vision models unverifiable
nodes.approach: Piecewise linear bound propagation through rendering, with custom abstractions for matrix inversion and sorting

nodes.title: Temperature is All You Need for Generalization in Langevin Dynamics and other Markov Processes
nodes.tldr: Proves a time-independent generalization bound for Langevin dynamics that depends on temperature and initial loss, not dimension or training time.
nodes.problem: Generalization bounds for noisy Markov training usually depend on training time, mixing or dimension.

nodes.title: Polyline Path Masked Attention for Vision Transformer
nodes.tldr: Merges Mamba2's structured spatial mask with ViT self-attention through a polyline path scanning mask, improving dense prediction over SSM and Transformer baselines.
nodes.problem: Self-attention in ViTs lacks explicit spatial adjacency priors among image tokens.

nodes.niche_reason: Hybrid SSM-attention vision backbones are specialised

nodes.title: Optimal Mistake Bounds for Transductive Online Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves transductive online mistake bounds of order sqrt(d) for Littlestone dimension d, tight and a quadratic gap from standard online learning.
nodes.problem: How much unlabeled instance access helps online learning has been an open problem for 30 years.
nodes.approach: Matching lower and upper mistake bounds for concept classes with Littlestone dimension d.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity

nodes.title: Predictive Preference Learning from Human Interventions
nodes.tldr: PPL propagates each human intervention into predicted future steps as preference signals, improving interactive imitation efficiency in driving and manipulation.
nodes.problem: Interactive imitation corrects only current-state actions, ignoring potentially hazardous future states.
nodes.approach: Extend each human intervention over a preference horizon and apply preference optimization on predicted future states.

nodes.niche_reason: Human-in-the-loop imitation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: GeoSVR: Taming Sparse Voxels for Geometrically Accurate Surface Reconstruction
nodes.tldr: GeoSVR reconstructs accurate, complete surfaces with sparse voxels, using a voxel-uncertainty monocular depth constraint and surface regularization.
nodes.problem: Splatting-based surface reconstruction is bottlenecked, and sparse voxels lack scene constraints for convergence.
nodes.approach: Voxel-uncertainty monocular depth constraint plus sparse-voxel surface regularization for geometric consistency.

nodes.niche_reason: Surface reconstruction is mainstream; sparse-voxel variant is less common

nodes.title: Stop the Nonconsensual Use of Nude Images in Research
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing researchers should stop collecting and distributing nonconsensual nude images for nudity detection, supported by a systematic review and a call to action.
nodes.problem: Nudity detection research uses and distributes nonconsensually collected nude images, perpetuating image-based sexual abuse.

nodes.title: TGA: True-to-Geometry Avatar Dynamic Reconstruction
nodes.tldr: A perspective-aware 4D Gaussian avatar framework with Jacobian-guided deformation and incremental BVH pivoting for accurate facial geometry and fast per-frame mesh extraction.

nodes.title: Spectral Perturbation Bounds for Low-Rank Approximation with Applications to Privacy
nodes.tldr: Gives sharper high-probability spectral-norm bounds for low-rank approximation under symmetric perturbations, improving private PCA utility by up to sqrt(n).

nodes.approach: Contour bootstrapping from complex analysis gives sharp spectral bounds, extended to polynomial and matrix-exponential functionals.

nodes.title: Differentiable Decision Tree via "ReLU+Argmin" Reformulation
nodes.tldr: An exact ReLU+Argmin reformulation makes hard-split oblique decision trees trainable by gradient descent, scaling to depth 12 on million-sample datasets.

nodes.niche_reason: Differentiable hard decision trees are uncommon in the deep learning mainstream.

nodes.title: Conditional Representation Learning for Customized Tasks
nodes.tldr: Conditional Representation Learning uses an LLM to generate descriptive words forming a semantic basis for a user criterion, then projects VLM image features into it.
nodes.problem: Universal embeddings capture dominant semantics that may not match customized downstream criteria.
nodes.approach: LLM-generated descriptive texts define a conditional basis; project CLIP-style image features onto it.
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles representation learning and vision-language retrieval.
nodes.niche_reason: Criterion-conditioned embeddings without fine-tuning are fairly specialised.

nodes.title: MoESD: Unveil Speculative Decoding's Potential for Accelerating Sparse MoE
nodes.tldr: Speculative decoding accelerates sparse MoE models more than dense ones at medium batch sizes; a theoretical model and 'target efficiency' metric explain it.

nodes.title: BayeSQP: Bayesian Optimization through Sequential Quadratic Programming

nodes.title: AGENTIF: Benchmarking Large Language Models Instruction Following Ability in Agentic Scenarios

nodes.tldr: Keeps visuomotor policies in-distribution by treating expert latent embeddings as a barrier, with a dynamics model steering rollouts back toward expert states.

nodes.title: Win Fast or Lose Slow: Balancing Speed and Accuracy in Latency-Sensitive Decisions of LLMs

nodes.title: ElliCE: Efficient and Provably Robust Algorithmic Recourse via the Rashomon Sets

authors: Jacobus G. M. van der Linden

nodes.title: Hybrid-Balance GFlowNet for Solving Vehicle Routing Problems

nodes.title: Characterizing control between interacting subsystems with deep Jacobian estimation
