nodes.title: AlphaZero Neural Scaling and Zipf's Law: a Tale of Board Games and Power Laws
nodes.tldr: Finds AlphaZero's scaling follows Zipf's law over game states, with inverse scaling linked to end-game states larger models over-focus on.
nodes.problem: Why neural scaling laws arise is unclear, and whether Zipf-based theories explain RL agents.
nodes.approach: Empirical analysis of AlphaZero state frequencies and loss curves against a quanta-based scaling model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Scaling-law framing of a game-playing RL agent is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Zipf-based scaling analysis of game-playing RL is rare

nodes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of the network
nodes.tldr: Perception Encoder shows contrastive vision-language training yields strong embeddings in intermediate layers, extracted via language and spatial alignment for state-of-the-art vision tasks.
nodes.problem: Building a single vision encoder that excels at classification, retrieval, VQA and dense prediction.
nodes.approach: Scaled contrastive recipe with video data engine plus language alignment and spatial alignment of intermediate features.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Vision-language encoder pretraining is a mainstream topic.

nodes.title: Two‑Stage Learning of Stabilizing Neural Controllers via Zubov Sampling and Iterative Domain Expansion
nodes.tldr: A two-stage framework jointly trains a neural controller and Lyapunov function, using Zubov-inspired sampling to enlarge provable stability regions and faster verification.
nodes.problem: Learned neural controllers lack stability guarantees and estimates of their region of attraction.
nodes.approach: Zubov-based training-data sampling and domain expansion, with CROWN-style verification via Jacobian bound propagation.
nodes.confidence_reason: Control synthesis versus neural verification is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Verified neural Lyapunov control is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Error Broadcast and Decorrelation as a Potential Artificial and Natural Learning Mechanism
nodes.tldr: Trains networks without weight transport by broadcasting output errors to layers and penalizing error-activation correlations, a biologically plausible backprop alternative.
nodes.problem: Backpropagation requires weight transport, which is biologically implausible.
nodes.approach: Layerwise losses penalizing correlation between layer activations and output errors, grounded in MMSE orthogonality.
nodes.confidence_reason: Learning-rule topic is a judgment call between training dynamics and neuroscience.
nodes.niche_reason: Biologically plausible credit assignment is a rare niche

nodes.title: Simultaneous Swap Regret Minimization via KL-Calibration
nodes.tldr: Introduces KL-calibration, equivalent to swap regret under log loss, with an algorithm achieving sublinear T^1/3 rates for calibration and swap regret.
nodes.problem: Classical l1-calibration is hard to optimize, and easier calibration measures need stronger guarantees.
nodes.approach: Randomized rounding and non-uniform discretization to minimize swap regret for log loss and smooth proper losses.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: swap-regret calibration theory is a rare, specialised direction

nodes.title: Memory Mosaics at scale
nodes.tldr: Scales memory mosaics, associative-memory networks, to 10B parameters on 1T tokens; v2 matches transformers on training knowledge and beats them on new tasks.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether associative-memory networks can match transformers at LLM scale on knowledge and in-context learning.
nodes.approach: Scale memory mosaics v2 with architectural modifications to 10B parameters on one trillion tokens.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Architecture-vs-scaling study; several LLM topics plausible.
nodes.niche_reason: Associative-memory networks at LLM scale are a rare direction.

nodes.title: BevSplat: Resolving Height Ambiguity via Feature-Based Gaussian Primitives for Weakly-Supervised Cross-View Localization
nodes.tldr: Estimates ground camera pose against satellite images by lifting ground pixels to 3D Gaussians whose features form a BEV map, resolving height ambiguity.
nodes.problem: Cross-view localization suffers height ambiguity from missing depth in ground and satellite views.
nodes.approach: Feature-based per-pixel 3D Gaussians synthesized into a BEV feature map for pose estimation.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Weakly supervised cross-view localization is specialised.

nodes.title: On Transferring Transferability: Towards a Theory for Size Generalization
nodes.tldr: Frames size generalization as continuity in a limit space identifying small and large problem instances, with design principles for transferable graph, set, and point-cloud models.
nodes.problem: When a model trained on small inputs transfers to larger-dimensional inputs lacks general theory.
nodes.approach: Limit-space framework where transferability equals continuity; instantiated on existing architectures with modifications.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Any-dimensional learning theory across sizes is a rare topic.

nodes.title: Quantum speedup of non-linear Monte Carlo problems
nodes.tldr: Proposes a quantum-inside-quantum algorithm achieving quadratic speedup for estimating nested expectations, extending quantum Monte Carlo advantage to non-linear functionals of distributions.
nodes.problem: Quantum quadratic speedup is known for mean estimation but not for non-linear functionals like nested expectations.
nodes.approach: Quantum-inside-quantum algorithm improving on quantum-accelerated multilevel Monte Carlo.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Quantum algorithm theory fits poorly into any listed topic.
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum algorithms for nested expectations are very rare in ML venues.

nodes.title: Dynamical Decoupling of Generalization and Overfitting in Large Two-Layer Networks
nodes.tldr: Dynamical mean field theory shows large two-layer networks have separated timescales that decouple feature learning from overfitting, with non-monotone test error.
nodes.problem: Characterizing training dynamics that determine inductive bias and generalization in overparametrized networks.
nodes.approach: Dynamical mean field theory analysis of two-layer network training in the proportional high-dimensional regime.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical-physics DMFT analysis is a rare theory technique.

nodes.title: LODGE: Level-of-Detail Large-Scale Gaussian Splatting with Efficient Rendering
nodes.tldr: Hierarchical level-of-detail method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that renders large scenes in real time under tight memory budgets.
nodes.problem: Rendering large 3DGS scenes is slow and memory-hungry on constrained devices.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical LOD subsets selected by camera distance, with chunked dynamic loading.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Established 3DGS line; LOD with chunked loading is specialised.

nodes.title: On the sample complexity of semi-supervised multi-objective learning
nodes.tldr: Shows that with Bregman losses, unlabeled data can alleviate labeled-data needs in multi-objective learning via simple pseudo-labeling.
nodes.problem: Multi-objective learning sample complexity grows with model class size, even with semi-supervision.
nodes.approach: Lower-bound constructions for some losses, upper bounds for Bregman losses, and pseudo-labeling.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Established learning-theory area; multi-objective angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Multi-agent Markov Entanglement
nodes.tldr: Shows an MDP admits value decomposition if and only if its transition matrix is not entangled, introduces a measure bounding decomposition error.
nodes.problem: Why value decomposition works in multi-agent RL is theoretically unexplained.
nodes.approach: Defines Markov entanglement, a quantum-inspired measure of decomposability, and bounds decomposition error for N-agent MDPs.
nodes.niche_reason: Markov entanglement analysis of value decomposition is an unusual theory angle.

nodes.title: Frame Context Packing and Drift Prevention in Next-Frame-Prediction Video Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: FramePack compresses frame contexts by importance for next-frame video diffusion, enabling thousands-of-frame inference, and adds drift prevention methods against error accumulation.
nodes.problem: Next-frame video models face context length limits and drifting error accumulation.
nodes.approach: Importance-based frame context packing with early endpoints, adjusted sampling order, and discrete history.
nodes.niche_reason: Video diffusion improvements are common.

nodes.title: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction
nodes.tldr: KVzip evicts KV cache entries by scoring importance through LLM context reconstruction, giving query-agnostic compression with 3-4x smaller cache and about 2x faster decoding.
nodes.problem: KV cache memory and latency growth with context length, and query-aware eviction failing across multiple queries.
nodes.approach: Score KV pair importance by having the LLM reconstruct the context from cache; evict low-importance pairs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: KV cache compression is a crowded, active area.

nodes.title: Transstratal Adversarial Attack: Compromising Multi-Layered Defenses in Text-to-Image Models
nodes.tldr: Transstratal Adversarial Attack uses LLM-generated candidates and genetic optimization to craft prompts that bypass prompt filters, concept erasers, and image filters together in text-to-image systems.
nodes.problem: Adversarial attacks on isolated defenses fail against multi-layered safety stacks in text-to-image models.
nodes.approach: Black-box LLM candidate generation plus adversarial genetic search to bypass all layers at once.
nodes.niche_reason: T2I safety attacks are an active, fairly common area.

nodes.title: Fast Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion: 100× Speedup via Parallel and Sparse Planning
nodes.tldr: Speeds up Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion up to 100x via parallel rollouts with delayed tree updates and trajectory coarsening, keeping planning quality.
nodes.problem: Diffusion planning with tree search is too slow at test time due to sequential tree search and iterative denoising.
nodes.approach: Parallel rollouts with redundancy-aware selection, and sparse planning over coarsened, shorter trajectories.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion planning sits between RL planning and generative sampling
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-plus-tree-search planning is an established niche

nodes.title: SageAttention3: Microscaling FP4 Attention for Inference and An Exploration of 8-Bit Training
nodes.tldr: SageAttention3 uses Blackwell FP4 tensor cores for 5x faster attention inference and explores accurate 8-bit attention for training, lossless in fine-tuning but slower in pretraining.
nodes.problem: Attention's quadratic cost limits inference and training efficiency, and low-bit attention is unexplored for training.
nodes.approach: Microscaling FP4 attention GPU kernels and 8-bit forward/backward attention design.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient attention kernels are established but hardware-specialised.

nodes.title: InfinityStar: Uniﬁed Spacetime AutoRegressive Modeling for Visual Generation
nodes.tldr: Unified discrete spacetime autoregressive model that generates high-resolution images and long 720p videos, supporting text-to-image, text-to-video, and image-to-video tasks.
nodes.problem: Diffusion dominates video generation, while autoregressive models lag in quality and speed.
nodes.approach: Purely discrete autoregressive modeling that jointly captures spatial and temporal dependencies in one architecture.
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive video generation is a growing but mainstream direction.

nodes.title: HM3: Hierarchical Multi-Objective Model Merging for Pretrained Models
nodes.tldr: HM3 merges pretrained models across both parameter and architecture spaces using hierarchical multi-objective search and actor-critic policies to produce Pareto-optimal merged models.
nodes.problem: Model merging ignores architecture space, where layer compatibility and huge search spaces make merging hard.
nodes.approach: Bilevel multi-objective search: existing parameter merging plus actor-critic layer-path exploration.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.confidence_reason: model merging placement across parameter and architecture search is uncertain
nodes.niche_reason: architecture-level merging is early-stage but model merging is common

nodes.title: Ctrl-DNA: Controllable Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory DNA Design via Constrained RL
nodes.tldr: Fine-tunes autoregressive genomic language models with constrained RL to design promoters and enhancers with cell-type-specific activity and fewer off-target effects.
nodes.problem: Generated regulatory DNA often lacks novelty and reliable cell-type-specific activity.
nodes.approach: Constrained RL that maximizes target-cell activity while penalizing off-target effects in autoregressive genomic LMs.
nodes.confidence_reason: Biology application versus constrained-RL method contribution
nodes.niche_reason: Constrained RL for regulatory DNA design is a cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Diffusion Generative Modeling on Lie Group Representations
nodes.tldr: Score-based diffusion operates directly in Lie group representation spaces, letting it model distributions on non-Abelian groups such as SO(3) and SE(3) for molecular tasks.
nodes.problem: Diffusion on Lie groups is limited; standard score matching assumes translation geometry.
nodes.approach: Generalized score matching with Langevin dynamics as direct sums of Lie algebra representations, plus paired SDEs.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion over general Lie group representations is an unusual direction.

nodes.title: DNAEdit: Direct Noise Alignment for Text-Guided Rectified Flow Editing
nodes.tldr: DNAEdit improves training-free rectified-flow image editing by directly refining the Gaussian noise via velocity-field alignment, plus Mobile Velocity Guidance and a long-prompt benchmark.
nodes.problem: Rectified-flow inversion accumulates drift, degrading reconstruction and text-guided editing quality.
nodes.approach: Direct Noise Alignment adjusts noise using predicted versus expected velocity, with Mobile Velocity Guidance for editing.
nodes.niche_reason: Training-free diffusion/flow editing is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Flow Density Control: Generative Optimization Beyond Entropy-Regularized Fine-Tuning
nodes.tldr: Fine-tunes flow and diffusion models for general utilities beyond expected reward, via a sequence of simpler fine-tuning tasks with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Fine-tuning generative models optimizes only expected reward while preserving prior via KL.
nodes.approach: Reduce general-utility fine-tuning to a sequence of standard fine-tunings, using mirror flows.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.confidence_reason: Blends generative fine-tuning, RL and optimal transport; primary is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: General utilities beyond average reward are less common.

nodes.title: Instance-Optimality for Private KL Distribution Estimation
nodes.tldr: Gives minimax-optimal and instance-optimal estimators for discrete distributions under KL divergence, with and without differential privacy, using Good-Turing variants.
nodes.problem: Minimax-optimal private estimators can perform poorly on real, non-worst-case distributions
nodes.approach: Private Good-Turing estimators analyzed against local-neighborhood instance-optimality
nodes.niche_reason: Instance-optimal private estimation under KL is a rare topic

nodes.title: Agnostic Learning under Targeted Poisoning: Optimal Rates and the Role of Randomness
nodes.tldr: Proves optimal excess error of order sqrt(d*eta) for agnostic learning under instance-targeted poisoning, showing randomized learners are necessary even when random bits are visible.
nodes.problem: Optimal error rates for learning under instance-targeted data poisoning in the agnostic setting.
nodes.approach: Matching upper and lower bounds using randomized learners and a single fixed hard distribution.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-theoretic targeted poisoning rates are a rare theory niche.

nodes.title: Angles Don’t Lie: Unlocking Training‑Efficient RL Through the Model’s Own Signals
nodes.tldr: Speeds RL fine-tuning of LLMs by selecting each epoch's training data using angle concentration of token hidden states, a signal correlated with gradient impact.
nodes.problem: Uniform data sampling in LLM RL fine-tuning wastes samples on redundant or low-signal queries
nodes.approach: Gradient-driven, angle-informed per-epoch data navigation using the model's own hidden-state angular distribution
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another RL fine-tuning data selection method

nodes.title: Augmenting Biological Fitness Prediction Benchmarks with Landscapes Features from GraphFLA
nodes.tldr: GraphFLA builds and analyzes biological fitness landscapes, computing topographic features to interpret fitness-prediction model performance, and releases 155 combinatorially complete landscapes.
nodes.problem: Fitness prediction benchmarks lack landscape topography information needed to interpret and compare models.
nodes.approach: Python framework computing 20 landscape features over thousands of ProteinGym/RNAGym landscapes, plus new landscape datasets.
nodes.niche_reason: Fitness landscape analysis for benchmark interpretation is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Proxy-SPEX: Sample-Efficient Interpretability via Sparse Feature Interactions in LLMs
nodes.tldr: Attributes influential feature interactions in LLM outputs with gradient-boosted trees fit on masked outputs, using 10x fewer inferences than SPEX.
nodes.problem: Finding feature interactions requires enumerating combinations, which scales poorly and needs many model inferences.
nodes.approach: Exploit hierarchical interaction structure: fit gradient-boosted trees to masked outputs, then extract important interactions.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Interaction attribution for LLMs is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense
nodes.tldr: Parameterizes dense linear RNNs as fixed points of diagonal RNNs, trading expressivity for efficiency and reaching state of the art on state-tracking benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Diagonal state-space models lack the full state-tracking expressivity of dense RNNs.
nodes.approach: Dense linear recurrences expressed as fixed points of parallelizable diagonal recurrences.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Established linear-RNN line with a specialised fixed-point twist

nodes.title: Flattening Hierarchies with Policy Bootstrapping
nodes.tldr: Trains a flat goal-conditioned policy by bootstrapping on subgoal-conditioned policies with advantage-weighted importance sampling, avoiding subgoal generative models and scaling to long-horizon offline GCRL.
nodes.problem: Scaling offline goal-conditioned RL to long horizons without complex hierarchical subgoal generation.
nodes.approach: Policy bootstrapping from subgoal-conditioned policies using advantage-weighted importance sampling in a flat policy.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline GCRL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Towards Multi-Table Learning: A Novel Paradigm for Complementarity Quantification and Integration
nodes.tldr: Proposes a complementarity-strength metric and ATCA-Net, a cross-table attention network, to learn from multiple related tables jointly.
nodes.problem: Tabular learning methods cannot quantify or exploit complementary information spread across multiple distinct tables.
nodes.approach: Define complementarity strength metric and a network with adaptive table encoders plus cross-table attention.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-table learning is a rare formulation within tabular ML.

nodes.title: Large Language Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Trains LLaDA, a masked diffusion language model from scratch, competitive with autoregressive LLMs on in-context learning and instruction following, and addressing the reversal curse.
nodes.problem: Core LLM capabilities are assumed to require autoregressive models; this assumption is untested.
nodes.approach: Masked diffusion with forward masking and reverse generation, trained by likelihood bound, then SFT.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based LLMs are an emerging, still-uncommon alternative to autoregression.

nodes.title: Amortized Variational Transdimensional Inference
nodes.tldr: CoSMIC normalizing flows enable a single amortized variational density over transdimensional multi-model spaces, trained with a variational transdimensional inference approach.
nodes.problem: Flow-based variational inference is limited to fixed-dimensional parameter spaces, not multi-model Bayesian inference.
nodes.approach: Contextually specified masking in autoregressive conditional flows plus stochastic VTI training with Bayesian optimization and gradient estimation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Transdimensional amortized variational inference is very rare.

nodes.title: Abstain Mask Retain Core: Time Series Prediction by Adaptive Masking Loss with Representation Consistency
nodes.tldr: AMRC finds truncating history can improve forecasts, then uses information-bottleneck-inspired adaptive masking loss and representation consistency to suppress redundant features in time-series forecasting.
nodes.problem: Forecasting models learn redundant noisy features from long histories, hurting signal extraction.
nodes.approach: Dynamic masking loss on discriminative temporal segments plus representation consistency constraint.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Time series forecasting methods are common.

nodes.title: Generalized Linear Mode Connectivity for Transformers
nodes.tldr: Generalizes linear mode connectivity to four symmetry classes, finding low-barrier linear paths between independently trained Vision Transformers and GPT-2 models.
nodes.problem: Permutation-only symmetry handling misses the richer symmetries of Transformers, hiding linear mode connectivity.
nodes.approach: Unified alignment framework with permutations, semi-permutations, orthogonal and invertible maps, extended to multi-model settings.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Model-merging symmetry theory is specialised but active

nodes.title: Accelerating Optimization via Differentiable Stopping Time
nodes.tldr: Makes the time to reach a target loss differentiable via a discrete stopping time, enabling gradient-based tuning of optimizers' hyperparameters.
nodes.problem: Minimizing time-to-target-loss is traditionally treated as non-differentiable, blocking gradient-based acceleration.
nodes.approach: Differentiable discrete stopping time with an efficient sensitivity algorithm, grounded in continuous ODE theory.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Differentiating through time-to-convergence is an unusual optimization angle

nodes.title: GaussianFusion: Gaussian-Based Multi-Sensor Fusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
nodes.tldr: GaussianFusion fuses multi-sensor features through compact 2D Gaussians with explicit and implicit features, with a cascade planning head for end-to-end driving on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive.
nodes.problem: Sensor fusion for end-to-end driving is either hard to interpret or computationally dense.
nodes.approach: Scene-wide 2D Gaussians progressively refined with multi-modal features, feeding an iterative cascade trajectory planner.
nodes.niche_reason: Common end-to-end driving fusion direction.

nodes.title: VPO: Reasoning Preferences Optimization Based on $\mathcal{V}$-Usable Information
nodes.tldr: Constrains negative gradients in DPO using V-usable information to mitigate squeezing effects, improving mathematical reasoning alignment.
nodes.problem: DPO's negative gradients squeeze output confidence, hurting reasoning alignment.
nodes.approach: Negative-gradient constraint on non-preference samples selected by V-usable information similarity.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: DPO variants are crowded

nodes.title: NormFit: A Lightweight Solution for Few-Shot Federated Learning with Non-IID Data
nodes.tldr: NormFit federated few-shot adaptation fine-tunes only the vision encoder's Pre-LayerNorm parameters of CLIP-like VLMs, cutting communication and computation while handling non-IID data.
nodes.problem: Few-shot federated VLM adaptation suffers communication overhead, compute cost and non-IID degradation.
nodes.approach: Tune only Pre-LayerNorm parameters of the vision encoder, with a generalization gap argument.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated VLM few-shot adaptation is specialised.

nodes.title: GeoLLaVA-8K: Scaling Remote-Sensing Multimodal Large Language Models to 8K Resolution
nodes.tldr: Multimodal LLM for 8K remote-sensing imagery, pruning redundant background tokens and selecting anchored object tokens, plus new ultra-high-resolution VQA datasets.
nodes.problem: Ultra-high-resolution remote-sensing MLLMs face scarce training data and token explosion from huge images.
nodes.approach: Background Token Pruning and Anchored Token Selection to cut memory while keeping key object semantics.
nodes.niche_reason: Ultra-high-resolution remote-sensing MLLMs are rare in the literature.

nodes.title: A Token is Worth over 1,000 Tokens: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Low-Rank Clone
nodes.tldr: Pre-training method that distills a strong teacher into a small LM via low-rank soft pruning and activation cloning, using only 20B tokens.
nodes.problem: Small language models are costly to train, and hard pruning and alignment lose information.
nodes.approach: Trainable low-rank projections compress teacher weights and align student activations, including FFN.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Small-LM distillation is a crowded area.

nodes.title: EAG3R: Event-Augmented 3D Geometry Estimation for Dynamic and Extreme-Lighting Scenes
nodes.tldr: EAG3R adds asynchronous event-camera streams to a MonST3R pointmap backbone with SNR-aware fusion and event photometric loss for robust geometry in dynamic, low-light scenes.
nodes.problem: RGB-only pointmap reconstruction fails with dynamic objects and extreme illumination.
nodes.approach: Retinex enhancement, event adapter with SNR-aware fusion, and event-based photometric consistency loss.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Event cameras combined with feed-forward pointmap reconstruction is rare.

nodes.title: Vanish into Thin Air: Cross-prompt Universal Adversarial Attacks for SAM2
nodes.tldr: UAP-SAM2 is the first cross-prompt universal adversarial attack on SAM2, using target scanning and dual semantic deviation across frames to disrupt video segmentation.
nodes.problem: Robustness of SAM2 to adversarial perturbations is unexplored and SAM attacks transfer poorly.
nodes.approach: Prompt-randomized target scanning and a dual semantic deviation objective within and across frames.
nodes.niche_reason: Attacks on segmentation foundation models are specialised.

nodes.title: On Traceability in $\ell_p$ Stochastic Convex Optimization
nodes.tldr: Shows accurate stochastic convex optimization under lp geometry requires traceability of training samples, linking to differential privacy lower bounds via a sparse fingerprinting lemma.
nodes.problem: Whether accurate learners in lp stochastic convex optimization must leak identifiable training samples.
nodes.approach: Prove traceability versus excess risk thresholds using a sparse variant of the fingerprinting lemma.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Highly technical privacy lower-bound theory with few comparable papers.

nodes.title: A Implies B: Circuit Analysis in LLMs for Propositional Logical Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Uses causal mediation analysis to find a sparse, modular circuit that solves propositional logic in Mistral and Gemma models.
nodes.problem: Unclear which components LLMs use to combine facts in multi-step logical reasoning.
nodes.approach: Causal mediation analysis of attention heads and layers, decomposing the circuit into four sub-circuits.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Circuit-level logic reasoning analysis is specialised

nodes.title: Cycle-Sync: Robust Global Camera Pose Estimation through Enhanced Cycle-Consistent Synchronization
nodes.tldr: Cycle-Sync is a global camera pose estimation framework using cycle-consistent message-passing least squares with exact-recovery guarantees and outlier rejection, avoiding bundle adjustment.
nodes.problem: Global camera pose estimation is fragile to outliers and lacks strong recovery guarantees.
nodes.approach: Adapt message-passing least squares with cycle consistency, robust loss, and subspace-inspired outlier rejection.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Synchronization-based SfM with theory is relatively rare.

nodes.title: Vector Quantization in the Brain: Grid-like Codes in World Models
nodes.tldr: Proposes GCQ, a brain-inspired method that compresses observation-action sequences into discrete codes from grid-like attractor patterns, serving as a world model.
nodes.problem: Conventional vector quantization handles static inputs and cannot jointly compress space and time for planning.
nodes.approach: Action-conditioned codebook whose codewords come from continuous attractor networks, selected by action.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Brain-inspired codes; topic placement is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Attractor-based grid codes for world models are very rare

nodes.title: TRIDENT: Tri-Modal Molecular Representation Learning with Taxonomic Annotations and Local Correspondence
nodes.tldr: TRIDENT jointly aligns SMILES, text, and taxonomic annotations of molecules using volume-based global alignment and local substructure-text matching, achieving state-of-the-art on 18 tasks.
nodes.problem: Molecular representation learning overlooks textual and taxonomic functional information about molecules.
nodes.approach: Volume-based tri-modal alignment replaces contrastive loss, with a momentum-balanced local objective linking substructures to sub-text.
nodes.niche_reason: Tri-modal molecular alignment with taxonomy is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Breaking the Batch Barrier (B3) of Contrastive Learning via Smart Batch Mining
nodes.tldr: Builds contrastive training batches by clustering a teacher-model similarity graph so each batch holds strong in-batch negatives, reaching SOTA with batches 4-16x smaller.
nodes.problem: Contrastive embedding quality depends on batch size and negative quality, which random batches limit.
nodes.approach: Rank examples with a teacher embedding model, build a sparse similarity graph, and group communities into batches.
nodes.niche_reason: Batch construction for contrastive learning is a common direction.

nodes.title: Toward Relative Positional Encoding in Spiking Transformers
nodes.tldr: Introduces Gray-PE and Log-PE, relative positional encodings for spiking Transformers that preserve binary spikes, with gains on forecasting, text, and image classification.
nodes.problem: Spiking Transformers only have absolute positional encodings; relative positions are hard to encode with binary spikes.
nodes.approach: Gray-code encoding of relative distances and logarithmic distance matrix added to spiking attention maps.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Spiking networks lack a vocab topic; placed under transformer attention
nodes.niche_reason: Relative positional encoding for spiking transformers is a rare direction

nodes.title: CLiFT: Compressive Light-Field Tokens for Compute Efficient and Adaptive Neural Rendering
nodes.tldr: Neural rendering representing scenes as compressed light-field tokens selected by latent K-means, allowing a compute-adaptive renderer to trade token count against quality and speed.
nodes.problem: Compute-efficient and adaptive novel view synthesis with compact scene representations.
nodes.approach: Multi-view encoder tokens, K-means centroid selection, condenser compression, and a renderer handling variable token counts.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Token-based compressed light-field rendering is somewhat specialised.

nodes.title: Fast-Slow Thinking GRPO for Large Vision-Language Model Reasoning
nodes.tldr: FAST-GRPO adapts reasoning depth in vision-language models using question-difficulty metrics, length rewards and difficulty-aware KL, cutting tokens 32-67% while improving accuracy.
nodes.problem: GRPO for vision-language reasoning yields verbose outputs with marginal accuracy gains.
nodes.approach: Difficulty-estimating metrics with adaptive length-based rewards and difficulty-aware KL in GRPO.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: GRPO reasoning variants are very crowded.

nodes.title: Transformer Copilot: Learning from The Mistake Log in LLM Fine-tuning
nodes.tldr: Adds a Copilot model that learns from a log of the Pilot LLM's fine-tuning mistakes and rectifies its logits at inference, improving 12 benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Standard supervised fine-tuning discards the model's own error signals during training.
nodes.approach: Record a Mistake Log during fine-tuning; jointly train a Copilot that corrects Pilot logits at inference.
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-tuning variants are common, though the copilot idea is somewhat novel.

nodes.title: Ambient Diffusion Omni: Training Good Models with Bad Data
nodes.tldr: Ambient Diffusion Omni trains diffusion models on low-quality, synthetic, and OOD images by exploiting spectral power law decay and locality, improving ImageNet FID and text-to-image quality.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models discard lower-quality images that could still carry useful training signal.
nodes.approach: Train using noise-time dependent use of corrupted data, since noise dampens skew between observed and desired distributions.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Learning from corrupted data for diffusion is established but specialised.

nodes.title: JavisGPT: A Unified Multi-modal LLM for Sounding-Video Comprehension and Generation
nodes.tldr: JavisGPT is a unified multimodal LLM for joint audio-video comprehension and generation, with a SyncFusion module, a pretrained JAV-DiT generator, and a 200K instruction dataset.
nodes.problem: Unified understanding and generation of temporally synchronized sounding video from multimodal instructions.
nodes.approach: Encoder-LLM-decoder with SyncFusion and synchrony-aware queries; three-stage training on JavisInst-Omni.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Unified audio-video understanding and generation is specialised.

nodes.title: Lost in Transmission: When and Why LLMs Fail to Reason Globally
nodes.tldr: Models attention as bounded communication, showing graph-reachability-style tasks need high bandwidth, and that chain-of-thought can turn such hard problems easy.
nodes.problem: LLMs fail at complex reasoning over large parts of their input; the cause is unclear.
nodes.approach: Bounded attention prefix oracle model formalizing per-head bandwidth limits, plus experiments on frontier LLMs.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory of LLM reasoning limits straddles reasoning and complexity theory.
nodes.niche_reason: Communication-complexity view of LLM reasoning is unusual.

nodes.title: Uncertain Knowledge Graph Completion via Semi-Supervised Confidence Distribution Learning
nodes.tldr: Completes uncertain knowledge graphs by turning triple confidences into distributions and self-training with meta-learned pseudo labels to fix imbalance.
nodes.problem: Imbalanced confidence distributions hurt uncertain knowledge graph completion.
nodes.approach: Confidence distribution learning with semi-supervised pseudo-labeling predicted by meta-learning.
nodes.confidence_reason: Knowledge graph completion has no exact topic; GNN/embeddings closest.
nodes.niche_reason: Uncertain knowledge graphs are a rare subfield.

nodes.title: Regret Bounds for Adversarial Contextual Bandits with General Function Approximation and Delayed Feedback
nodes.tldr: Gives regret bounds for adversarial contextual bandits with delayed feedback, including a general function approximation bound via an online regression oracle and a matching-style lower bound.
nodes.problem: Regret minimization in contextual bandits when adversarially chosen delays postpone loss observations.
nodes.approach: Algorithms with finite policy class and online least-squares oracle, plus stability analysis of Vovk's aggregating forecaster.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial delayed contextual bandit theory is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Diffusion-Based Hierarchical Graph Neural Networks for Simulating Nonlinear Solid Mechanics
nodes.tldr: Learned simulator pairing parallel rolling diffusion inference with a multiscale algebraic-multigrid GNN for solid mechanics; faster than diffusion simulators.
nodes.problem: Learned mesh simulators miss global bending effects and accumulate error over long rollouts.
nodes.approach: Parallel diffusion refinement across a temporal window plus hierarchical message passing on AMG-coarsened meshes.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned simulators with diffusion refinement are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Privacy amplification by random allocation
nodes.tldr: Shows random k-out-of-t allocation's privacy is upper bounded by Poisson subsampling, with efficient numerical accounting for Gaussian noise.
nodes.problem: Existing analyses of random allocation rely on loose shuffling bounds or costly Monte Carlo simulation.
nodes.approach: Theoretical guarantees linking random allocation to Poisson subsampling, plus numerical estimation algorithms.
nodes.niche_reason: DP-SGD accounting is established; random allocation analysis is specialised.

nodes.title: Protein Design with Dynamic Protein Vocabulary
nodes.tldr: ProDVa designs proteins from text descriptions by dynamically retrieving natural protein fragments with a fragment encoder, improving foldability with far less training data.
nodes.problem: Text-conditioned protein design yields functionally aligned sequences with poor structural plausibility.
nodes.approach: Text encoder, protein language model and fragment encoder retrieving natural protein fragments from functional descriptions.
nodes.niche_reason: Text-guided protein design is specialised but active.

nodes.title: Identifiability of Deep Polynomial Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Characterises when deep polynomial networks are identifiable from their function, linking layer widths and activation degrees to low-rank tensor uniqueness theorems.
nodes.problem: Identifiability of polynomial neural networks, needed for interpretability, is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Constructive proofs linking deep polynomial networks to low-rank tensor decompositions and Kruskal-type uniqueness, plus neurovariety dimension results.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Algebraic identifiability of polynomial networks is very rare

nodes.title: ZeroS: Zero‑Sum Linear Attention for Efficient Transformers
nodes.tldr: Zero-sum linear attention removes the constant zero-order term and reweights softmax residuals, allowing negative weights and contrastive operations at O(N) cost.
nodes.problem: Linear attention underperforms softmax because of convex-only combinations and uniform accumulated weight bias in long contexts.
nodes.approach: Remove the 1/t zero-order term and reweight the remaining zero-sum softmax residuals to get signed, stable attention weights.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Linear attention variants are a common, active topic.

nodes.title: Transformers for Mixed-type Event Sequences
nodes.tldr: Presents a single autoregressive transformer with discrete and continuous heads, using a normalizing flow for continuous attributes to model mixed-type event sequences.
nodes.problem: Mixed-type event sequences, such as records mixing discrete events with continuous measurements, are hard to model with one structure.
nodes.approach: Marked temporal point process transformer with a normalizing-flow head for continuous times and attributes, avoiding integration.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Mixed-type temporal point processes are a specialised modeling niche.

nodes.title: Flow Equivariant Recurrent Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Makes recurrent networks equivariant to continuous time-parameterized symmetries (flows), improving training speed and length and velocity generalization.
nodes.problem: Sequence models such as RNNs do not respect continuous time-parameterized symmetries like visual motion.
nodes.approach: Introduce flow equivariance into recurrent architectures via one-parameter Lie subgroup constraints.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: No equivariance topic in vocab; sequence-model fit is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare symmetry-based angle on recurrent sequence models

nodes.title: Learning (Approximately) Equivariant Networks via Constrained Optimization
nodes.tldr: ACE starts with a flexible non-equivariant network and constrains it toward approximate equivariance via homotopy-style constrained optimization, balancing symmetry against flexibility.
nodes.problem: Strict equivariance can hurt fitting on imperfectly symmetric data, while unconstrained models ignore partial symmetry.
nodes.approach: Constrained optimization that gradually tightens deviation from equivariance, reaching a data-driven equilibrium.
nodes.confidence_reason: Equivariance architecture versus constrained optimization is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Approximate equivariance via constraints is a specialised but active direction.

nodes.title: HyperET: Efficient Training in Hyperbolic Space for Multi-modal Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: HyperET aligns visual and textual representations at arbitrary granularity in hyperbolic space with Möbius-based learnable matrices, boosting MLLMs with under 1% extra parameters.
nodes.problem: Vision encoders in MLLMs lack multi-granularity language alignment, making training computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Dynamic hyperbolic radius adjustment using Möbius multiplication with diagonal, block-diagonal, or banded matrices.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.confidence_reason: Hyperbolic alignment is a method for MLLM efficiency; topic choice is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Hyperbolic geometry for MLLMs is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: An Evidence-Based Post-Hoc Adjustment Framework for Anomaly Detection Under Data Contamination
nodes.tldr: EPHAD is a test-time method that adjusts outputs of anomaly detectors trained on contaminated data using evidence from CLIP, classical detectors or domain knowledge.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised anomaly detectors degrade when training data contains undetected anomalies.
nodes.approach: Post-hoc test-time adjustment combining the contaminated model's prior with external evidence such as CLIP.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Anomaly detection under contamination is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Robo2VLM: Improving Visual Question Answering using Large-Scale Robot Manipulation Data
nodes.tldr: Generates a visual question answering dataset from robot demonstrations by segmenting trajectories into phases and using force and pose ground truth.
nodes.problem: VLMs lack spatial and interaction reasoning grounded in physical robot manipulation.
nodes.approach: Uses non-visual sensor signals like pose and gripper aperture to derive VQA ground truth.
nodes.niche_reason: Robot trajectories used to generate VQA data for VLMs is unusual

nodes.title: On the necessity of adaptive regularisation: Optimal anytime online learning on $\boldsymbol{\ell_p}$-balls
nodes.tldr: Shows fixed regularisers cannot be anytime optimal for online convex optimization over lp-balls across dimension regimes, and proves matching lower bounds.
nodes.problem: Anytime-optimal regret for online convex optimization on lp-balls across dimension regimes.
nodes.approach: Adaptive-regularisation FTRL analysis plus lower bounds for separable regularisers.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised question on regulariser adaptivity for online learning

nodes.title: Do-PFN: In-Context Learning for Causal Effect Estimation
nodes.tldr: Pre-trains prior-data fitted networks on synthetic causal structures so they predict interventional outcomes from observational data in-context, without knowing the causal graph.
nodes.problem: Estimating causal effects without interventional data or known causal graphs.
nodes.approach: Amortized in-context learning with PFNs pre-trained on synthetic causal data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: PFN-based amortized causal effect estimation.

nodes.title: What are you sinking? A geometric approach on attention sink
nodes.tldr: Argues attention sinks reflect geometric reference frames that anchor transformer representations, with three frame types tied to position encoding choices.
nodes.problem: Why attention sinks arise in transformers, whether they are an architectural artifact.
nodes.approach: Analyzes several architectures to classify centralized, distributed and bidirectional reference frames during training.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Geometric account of attention sinks is an unusual angle

nodes.title: CoT Information: Improved Sample Complexity under Chain-of-Thought Supervision
nodes.tldr: Develops a statistical learning theory for chain-of-thought supervision, defining CoT information and proving faster sample-complexity rates than end-to-end supervision with matching lower bounds.
nodes.problem: How much chain-of-thought supervision improves sample complexity of learning multi-step functions.
nodes.approach: Define CoT information; derive upper bounds and information-theoretic lower bounds in a PAC-style framework.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of CoT is growing but still specialised.

nodes.title: Online Strategic Classification With Noise and Partial Feedback
nodes.tldr: Learns a linear classifier online against strategic agents who manipulate features, with partial labels and Massart noise, achieving O(sqrt(T)) regret.
nodes.problem: Strategic agents manipulate features while the principal sees only positive labels and noisy data
nodes.approach: A novel online learning algorithm that converges to the clairvoyant optimal halfspace classifier under Massart noise.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Combines strategic manipulation, partial labels and noise; primary topic is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Strategic classification with noise and partial feedback is a rare combination

nodes.title: Fire360: A Benchmark for Robust Perception and Episodic Memory in Degraded 360° Firefighting Video
nodes.tldr: Fire360 is a benchmark of 228 degraded 360-degree firefighting videos testing VQA, captioning, localization, safety reasoning and retrieval of fire-damaged objects.
nodes.problem: Evaluating perception and episodic memory in smoke-filled, degraded safety-critical video.
nodes.approach: Annotated 360-degree video dataset with five tasks including transformed object retrieval.
nodes.niche_reason: Firefighting 360-degree video benchmark is a very rare domain.

nodes.title: Pan-LUT: Efficient Pan-sharpening via Learnable Look-Up Tables
nodes.tldr: Fuses panchromatic and multispectral remote sensing images with learnable lookup tables, under 700K parameters and very fast inference.
nodes.problem: Deep pan-sharpening is too computationally heavy for large remote sensing images on modest hardware.
nodes.approach: PAN-guided, spatial-detail and adaptive output lookup tables for channel-wise spectral mapping and fusion.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised remote-sensing fusion with an efficiency angle

nodes.title: ARECHO: Autoregressive Evaluation via Chain-Based Hypothesis Optimization for Speech Multi-Metric Estimation
nodes.tldr: ARECHO predicts multiple speech quality metrics jointly using autoregressive classifier-chain dependency modeling with tokenization and confidence-oriented decoding, reference-free.
nodes.problem: Joint estimation of speech metrics with differing scales and dependencies
nodes.approach: Dynamic classifier chain over tokenized speech with two-step confidence-oriented decoding
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.confidence_reason: Speech quality metric estimation sits between synthesis and audio understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-metric speech assessment is a rare niche

nodes.title: Jacobian-Based Interpretation of Nonlinear Neural Encoding Model
nodes.tldr: Proposes JNE, a Jacobian-based metric measuring nonlinearity of fMRI encoding models, revealing a hierarchy across visual cortex.
nodes.problem: Encoding models of fMRI lack any metric for the brain's nonlinear responses.
nodes.approach: Statistical dispersion of local Jacobians mapping model representations to predicted BOLD responses.
nodes.niche_reason: Nonlinearity metric for brain encoding models is rare

nodes.title: Position: If Innovation in AI systematically Violates Fundamental Rights, Is It Innovation at All?
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing regulation like the EU AI Act, with sandboxes and rights impact assessments, enables rather than blocks responsible AI innovation.
nodes.problem: Whether AI regulation and innovation are opposed, given harms to fundamental rights.
nodes.approach: Policy argument using analogies and the EU AI Act's adaptive mechanisms as a model.
nodes.confidence_reason: Policy position paper; ethics versus position topic is a close call.
nodes.niche_reason: AI policy position papers are established at venues but specialised.

nodes.title: SoTA with Less: MCTS-Guided Sample Selection for Data-Efficient Visual Reasoning Self-Improvement
nodes.tldr: ThinkLite-VL reaches strong visual reasoning with far fewer samples by using MCTS iteration counts to pick hard examples for reinforcement fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Selecting appropriately difficult samples for data-efficient reinforcement fine-tuning of vision-language reasoning models.
nodes.approach: Repurpose MCTS to measure sample difficulty via reasoning iterations, then select challenging samples for RFT self-improvement.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: RL fine-tuning of VLMs for reasoning is crowded.

nodes.title: Seeing Sound, Hearing Sight: Uncovering Modality Bias and Conflict of AI models in Sound Localization
nodes.tldr: Shows AI audio-visual models over-rely on vision unlike humans, then builds EchoPin, a neuroscience-inspired localizer trained on HRTF-rendered audio.
nodes.problem: Multimodal AI models for sound localization may be biased toward vision and fail under audiovisual conflict.
nodes.approach: Human psychophysics comparison, then training on HRTF-filtered, cochleagram-transformed simulated stereo audio.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual: neuroscience-inspired audio-visual localization and modality-conflict analysis.

nodes.title: 3D Interaction Geometric Pre-training for Molecular Relational Learning
nodes.tldr: Pre-trains a 2D molecular relational model to learn 3D interaction geometry from a virtual environment, avoiding costly quantum mechanical calculations.
nodes.problem: Molecular relational learning uses only 2D topology because 3D interaction geometry is too expensive to compute.
nodes.approach: Geometric pre-training on a constructed 3D virtual interaction environment, transferred to 2D models.
nodes.niche_reason: molecular interaction pre-training is specialised

nodes.title: Can We Infer Confidential Properties of Training Data from LLMs?
nodes.tldr: Introduces PropInfer benchmark and two attacks showing LLMs fine-tuned on sensitive data leak dataset-level properties such as demographics or disease prevalence.
nodes.problem: Fine-tuned LLMs may leak confidential dataset-level properties of their sensitive training data.
nodes.approach: Prompt-based generation attack and a shadow-model attack using word-frequency signals, evaluated on ChatDoctor.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Property inference on LLM fine-tuning data is a specialised niche

nodes.title: Boundary-Value PDEs Meet Higher-Order Differential Topology-aware GNNs
nodes.tldr: Higher-order graph neural operator built on exterior calculus that solves electromagnetic boundary value problems, outperforming prior neural operators.
nodes.problem: GNN neural operators ignore the physical meaning of higher-order mesh elements tied to differential forms.
nodes.approach: Higher-order message passing based on discrete and finite element exterior calculus, with physics-informed losses.
nodes.niche_reason: Higher-order GNN neural operators with exterior calculus are rare.

nodes.title: L2DGCN: Learnable Enhancement and Label Selection Dynamic Graph Convolutional Networks for Mitigating Degree Bias
nodes.tldr: Addresses degree bias in GNN node classification with a teacher-student model that propagates labels globally and learns edge perturbations to help low-degree nodes.
nodes.problem: Message passing struggles to propagate information to low-degree nodes under sparse labels.
nodes.approach: Teacher with improved label propagation, student with learnable edge perturbation, and a selector filtering unreliable pseudo-labels.
nodes.confidence_reason: Degree bias framing fits both GNN and fairness topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Degree bias in GNNs and label-efficient learning are common topics.

nodes.title: Taccel: Scaling Up Vision-based Tactile Robotics via High-performance GPU Simulation
nodes.tldr: Taccel is a GPU simulator for vision-based tactile sensors using IPC and affine body dynamics, reaching 915 FPS with 4096 environments and enabling sim-to-real transfer.
nodes.problem: No fast, accurate simulator exists for vision-based tactile sensors, limiting tactile robotics scale.
nodes.approach: GPU simulation combining Incremental Potential Contact and Affine Body Dynamics with tactile image rendering.
nodes.niche_reason: Tactile sensor simulation is a niche within robotics.

nodes.title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference
nodes.tldr: Shows LLM outputs vary with GPU count, type, and batch size due to floating-point non-associativity, and proposes LayerCast, storing 16-bit weights with FP32 computation.
nodes.problem: LLM inference results, especially for reasoning models, are not reproducible across hardware and system configurations.
nodes.approach: Controlled experiments tracing nondeterminism to numerical precision, plus LayerCast inference with 16-bit weights and FP32 compute.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Numerical reproducibility of LLM inference is a specialised but growing topic.

nodes.title: Rethinking Multimodal Learning from the Perspective of Mitigating Classification Ability Disproportion
nodes.tldr: Boosts weak modalities in multimodal learning by jointly optimizing classification and residual errors with adaptive classifier assignment.
nodes.problem: Modality imbalance arises from disproportionate classification ability across modalities.
nodes.approach: Sustained boosting with adaptive classifier assignment and convergence analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Modality imbalance fits multimodal and optimization areas
nodes.niche_reason: Modality imbalance is a common multimodal topic

nodes.title: Set Smoothness Unlocks Clarke Hyper-stationarity in Bilevel Optimization
nodes.tldr: Introduces set smoothness of lower-level solution sets to show Clarke hyper-stationarity is computable in nonsmooth bilevel optimization, with a zeroth-order algorithm and non-asymptotic guarantees.
nodes.problem: Bilevel optimization lacks strong stationarity guarantees without restrictive smoothness assumptions on the hyper-objective.
nodes.approach: Set smoothness yields weak convexity of hyper-objectives; a zeroth-order method finds approximate Clarke stationary points.
nodes.niche_reason: Nonsmooth variational analysis of bilevel problems is rare.

nodes.title: Reasoning Planning for Language Models
nodes.tldr: EPIC learns a shared representation of model reasoning ability and query-method fit, selecting reasoning methods that trade accuracy against compute cost.
nodes.problem: Choosing a reasoning method per query, given that more candidate answers don't always help.
nodes.approach: Contrastive two-tower planner regularized by theoretical aggregation accuracy bounds.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.confidence_reason: Reasoning method selection straddles inference efficiency and reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Per-query reasoning method selection is active but specialised.

nodes.title: ROOT: Rethinking Offline Optimization as Distributional Translation via Probabilistic Bridge
nodes.tldr: Recasts offline black-box optimization as distributional translation, learning a probabilistic bridge from low-value to high-value inputs using synthetic GP-based functions.
nodes.problem: Offline black-box optimization is limited by scarce observed input-output data.
nodes.approach: Learn a probabilistic bridge trained on synthetic functions built from mean posteriors of multiple Gaussian processes.
nodes.confidence_reason: Offline optimization spans optimization and generative bridge modeling
nodes.niche_reason: Offline optimization via distributional bridges is an unusual framing

nodes.title: LeMiCa: Lexicographic Minimax Path Caching for Efficient Diffusion-Based Video Generation
nodes.tldr: LeMiCa accelerates diffusion video generation without training by scheduling caching as a minimax graph path that bounds accumulated error.
nodes.problem: Caching speeds diffusion video inference, but local error heuristics let global errors accumulate visibly.
nodes.approach: Cache scheduling as an error-weighted directed graph, solved by lexicographic minimax path optimisation.
nodes.confidence_reason: caching acceleration vs video-generation application placement
nodes.niche_reason: diffusion caching for acceleration is a common direction

nodes.title: Learning Linear Attention in Polynomial Time
nodes.tldr: Proves polynomial-time agnostic PAC learnability of single-layer multi-head linear attention transformers by recasting it as optimal kernel prediction in an RKHS.
nodes.problem: Efficient learnability of Transformers from data is an open question beyond expressivity results.
nodes.approach: Reduce learning multi-head linear attention to kernel predictor in RKHS; polynomial-time check for identical best-fit computations.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Provable polynomial-time learning of transformers is rare.

nodes.title: Virus Infection Attack on LLMs: Your Poisoning Can Spread "VIA" Synthetic Data
nodes.tldr: Shows poisoned content can propagate through LLM-generated synthetic training data, and proposes a virus-inspired attack that spreads poisoning even from clean queries.
nodes.problem: Synthetic-data training may propagate poisoning and backdoor attacks, a risk left uninvestigated.
nodes.approach: Virus-inspired attack hides payloads in a shell and hijacks benign samples to propagate via synthetic data.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Poisoning propagation through synthetic data is a specialised security topic

nodes.title: Trajectory Graph Learning: Aligning with Long Trajectories in Reinforcement Learning Without Reward Design
nodes.tldr: Aligns a policy with expert-labelled long trajectories without rewards, showing the general problem is NP-complete and solving tractable structured cases with graph-based planning.
nodes.problem: Reward design is hard, and imitation methods align actions per state, losing long-horizon coherence.
nodes.approach: Graph-based planning under structural assumptions for known dynamics; UCB-style exploration for unknown dynamics.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.confidence_reason: Imitation vs. reward-free RL vs. theory is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Trajectory-level alignment with NP-completeness results is uncommon

nodes.title: Minimax-Optimal Univariate Function Selection in Sparse Additive Models: Rates, Adaptation, and the Estimation-Selection Gap
nodes.tldr: Establishes minimax separation rates for univariate function selection in sparse additive models, with adaptive selection, and shows optimal estimation need not give optimal selection.
nodes.problem: Characterize fundamental limits of variable selection in high-dimensional sparse additive models.
nodes.approach: Minimax analysis via multiple testing and support recovery, with an adaptive selection procedure.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Minimax nonparametric variable selection theory is a very rare niche in ML venues.

nodes.title: Fine-grained List-wise Alignment for Generative Medication Recommendation
nodes.tldr: An LLM medication recommender that builds drug lists one drug at a time with step-wise GRPO and potential-based reward shaping that models drug-drug interactions.
nodes.problem: Point-wise medication recommenders ignore synergistic drug effects and adverse drug-drug interactions.
nodes.approach: Sequential add/remove drug decisions optimised with GRPO, plus patient modelling from clinical knowledge and collaborative signals.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-based medication recommendation is specialised but growing

nodes.title: Stochastic Process Learning via Operator Flow Matching
nodes.tldr: Operator flow matching learns stochastic process priors on function spaces, giving tractable densities and functional regression with mean and density estimates at new points.
nodes.problem: Learning stochastic process priors over functions across arbitrary domains with tractable densities.
nodes.approach: Flow matching on function spaces built on neural operators.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual function-space generative modeling of stochastic processes.

nodes.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
nodes.tldr: Shows affine maps between language model residual streams transfer sparse autoencoder weights, probes and steering vectors across model sizes, cutting SAE training cost.
nodes.problem: Comparing and reusing learned features across language models of different sizes is costly.
nodes.approach: Cheap affine residual-stream mapping, used to initialize SAEs trained on a smaller model.

secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised cross-model SAE transfer for interpretability

nodes.title: RepLDM: Reprogramming Pretrained Latent Diffusion Models for High-Quality, High-Efficiency, High-Resolution Image Generation
nodes.tldr: Reprograms pretrained latent diffusion models for high-resolution generation via parameter-free attention guidance and progressive pixel-space upsampling, improving quality and speed.
nodes.problem: Pretrained LDMs produce structural distortions at resolutions above their training one.
nodes.approach: Attention guidance stage for structure, then progressive pixel-space upsampling with fewer denoising steps.
nodes.niche_reason: Training-free high-resolution diffusion variants are common.

nodes.title: Measuring and Controlling Solution Degeneracy across Task-Trained Recurrent Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Quantifies and controls solution degeneracy across behavior, neural dynamics and weights in task-trained RNNs, validating the Contravariance Principle.
nodes.problem: Different RNNs solving the same task can learn strikingly different internal solutions.
nodes.approach: Systematic measurement across 3,400 RNNs varying task complexity, size, and regularization.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic study of RNN solution variability is an unusual cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Prismatic Synthesis: Gradient-based Data Diversification Boosts Generalization in LLM Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Defines data diversity via entropy of model loss gradients, then generates synthetic data targeting underrepresented gradient regions for better LLM reasoning.
nodes.problem: Heuristic diversity metrics do not predict how well LLMs generalize.
nodes.approach: G-Vendi gradient-entropy metric guides targeted synthetic data generation.

nodes.niche_reason: Gradient-based data diversity is specialised but growing

nodes.title: Less is More: Improving LLM Alignment via Preference Data Selection
nodes.tldr: Curates DPO preference data via margin maximization and Bayesian aggregation of reward sources, using 10% of UltraFeedback for gains on AlpacaEval2.
nodes.problem: Noisy preference data causes parameter shrinkage in DPO; data selection is overlooked.
nodes.approach: Margin-maximization dataset curation plus Bayesian aggregation of external and implicit reward margins.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: DPO variants are a crowded alignment direction

nodes.title: CausalVerse: Benchmarking Causal Representation Learning with Configurable High-Fidelity Simulations
nodes.tldr: CausalVerse is a benchmark of high-fidelity simulated images and videos with configurable ground-truth causal structure for evaluating causal representation learning methods.
nodes.problem: Causal representation learning evaluation lacks datasets combining visual realism with known ground-truth causal variables.
nodes.approach: Simulated image and video data in four domains with configurable causal structures, used to evaluate CRL methods.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Benchmarking causal representation learning is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Stop DDoS Attacking the Research Community with AI-Generated Survey Papers
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing AI-generated surveys flood preprint servers, and calling for norms, expert oversight, and live community-maintained surveys.
nodes.problem: Low-effort, LLM-written survey papers are flooding research venues and degrading the scientific record.
nodes.approach: Argument supported by trend analysis and quality audits, proposing Dynamic Live Surveys as infrastructure.
nodes.niche_reason: Position on AI-generated survey floods is an unusual angle

nodes.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
nodes.tldr: Shows sparse autoencoders suffer feature absorption on hierarchical features, where monosemantic latents fail to fire and get absorbed into child features.
nodes.problem: Sparse autoencoders for LLM interpretability may not decompose hierarchical features robustly.
nodes.approach: Metric to detect absorption, validated across hundreds of LLM sparse autoencoders.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: SAE failure analysis is active but a specialised interpretability niche.

nodes.title: Beyond Expectations: Quantile-Guided Alignment for Risk-Calibrated Language Models
nodes.tldr: Quantile-Guided Alignment extends RLHF with quantile constraints on reward so users can improve specific tails of the output distribution, reducing rare catastrophic outputs.
nodes.problem: Standard RLHF maximizes average reward and leaves high-risk tail outputs poorly controlled.
nodes.approach: Augmented reward formulation enforcing quantile constraints across one or multiple reward dimensions during RLHF.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RLHF variant, though tail-risk framing is somewhat distinctive.

nodes.title: Structured Sparse Transition Matrices to Enable State Tracking in State-Space Models
nodes.tldr: Parametrizes SSM transition matrices as a column one-hot matrix times a complex diagonal, enabling FSA state tracking at near-diagonal-SSM cost.
nodes.problem: Structured SSM transitions limit expressivity for FSA state tracking, while dense ones are too costly.
nodes.approach: Structured sparse transition matrix from one-hot and complex-diagonal factors, with parallel scans.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: FSA state-tracking expressivity for SSMs is an unusual theory-driven angle

nodes.title: Personalized Decision Modeling: Utility Optimization or Textualized-Symbolic Reasoning
nodes.tldr: ATHENA models individual decisions by discovering group-level symbolic utility functions with LLMs, then adapting semantic templates per person, improving F1 on travel and vaccine choice.
nodes.problem: Individual decision models in high-stakes settings diverge from population-optimal predictions, mixing numerical and linguistic factors.
nodes.approach: Two stages: LLM-augmented symbolic utility discovery at group level, then individual semantic template adaptation guided by the utility.
secondary_topics: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles human decision modeling, symbolic discovery, and LLM reasoning.
nodes.niche_reason: Behavioral choice modeling with LLM symbolic discovery is uncommon.

nodes.title: Benchmarking Egocentric Multimodal Goal Inference for Assistive Wearable Agents
nodes.tldr: Benchmark and 30-hour egocentric dataset for inferring a wearable user's goal from multimodal context, showing VLMs lag humans on goal generation.
nodes.problem: Wearable agents need users to state goals explicitly, and proactive goal inference lacks benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Collects multimodal egocentric recordings with reference goals; evaluates MCQ and open-ended VLM goal generation.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: proactive goal inference for wearable assistants.

nodes.title: Measuring and Guiding Monosemanticity
nodes.tldr: Introduces a monosemanticity score for LLM features and Guided Sparse Autoencoders that condition latents on labelled concepts, improving steering and detection.
nodes.problem: Sparse autoencoder features in LLMs are often poorly isolated and not reliably monosemantic.
nodes.approach: Quantify monosemanticity with FMS, then train SAEs with labelled-concept conditioning in the latent space.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: SAE interpretability is a crowded, active area

nodes.title: Brain-Inspired fMRI-to-Text Decoding via Incremental and Wrap-Up Language Modeling
nodes.tldr: Decodes long fMRI sequences to text by decoding segments incrementally with summary wrap-ups, plus text-guided masked autoencoding of semantically salient time points.
nodes.problem: Single-pass fMRI-to-text decoding degrades on long sequences from memory overload and semantic drift.
nodes.approach: Segment-wise incremental decoding with wrap-up summaries, and attention-guided masking of fMRI time points.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: fMRI-to-text decoding is a specialised brain-computer interface topic.

nodes.title: On Linear Mode Connectivity of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures
nodes.tldr: Characterizes permutation symmetries of mixture-of-experts models and proposes a matching algorithm that reveals linear mode connectivity between independently trained dense, sparse and shared-expert MoEs.
nodes.problem: Whether linear mode connectivity holds for mixture-of-experts architectures.
nodes.approach: Symmetry analysis of experts and gating, plus a matching algorithm to align independently trained MoEs.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Mode connectivity for MoEs is a rare intersection.

nodes.title: Generalizable Insights for Graph Transformers in Theory and Practice
nodes.tldr: Proposes the Generalized-Distance Transformer and studies its expressivity and design choices across millions of graphs, distilling generalizable insights for graph transformer attention and positional encodings.
nodes.problem: Gap between graph transformer expressivity theory and large-scale empirical design guidance.
nodes.approach: Unified GT architecture analyzed theoretically and evaluated across diverse domains, scales, and few-shot transfer.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Mixes architecture design, expressivity theory, and large empirical study.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised graph learning subfield.

nodes.title: Checklists Are Better Than Reward Models For Aligning Language Models
nodes.tldr: RLCF extracts instruction-specific checklists and scores responses with AI judges and verifiers as RL rewards, improving instruction following on every benchmark tested.
nodes.problem: Fixed criteria like helpfulness give weak, generic reward signals for instruction-following alignment.
nodes.approach: Reinforcement Learning from Checklist Feedback with checklist items scored by judges and verifier programs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: LLM alignment via RL is common; checklists are a modest variation.

nodes.title: Online Functional Tensor Decomposition via Continual Learning for Streaming Data Completion
nodes.tldr: OFTD represents streaming spatio-temporal data as a CP tensor decomposition parameterized by implicit neural representations, updated continually with long-tail memory replay for completion.
nodes.problem: Completing streaming tensor data while updating without forgetting prior knowledge.
nodes.approach: CP decomposition with coordinate-based INRs trained continually, using long-tail memory replay.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Combines tensor decomposition, INRs, and continual learning; no single close topic.
nodes.niche_reason: Online functional tensor decomposition is a rare topic.

nodes.title: FUDOKI: Discrete Flow-based Unified Understanding and Generation via Kinetic-Optimal Velocities
nodes.tldr: A unified multimodal model for understanding and image generation built purely on discrete flow matching with kinetic-optimal velocities, initialized from autoregressive MLLMs.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive unified MLLMs are limited by raster-scan generation order and causal context.
