nodes.approach: Discrete flow matching with metric-induced probability paths and kinetic-optimal velocities, adapted from pretrained AR MLLMs.
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles unified multimodal LLMs and discrete flow generation.
nodes.niche_reason: Non-autoregressive unified multimodal models are an emerging but specialised direction.

nodes.title: Enhancing LLM Watermark Resilience Against Both Scrubbing and Spoofing Attacks
nodes.tldr: SEEK is an LLM watermark using equivalent texture keys within a window, improving resistance to scrubbing without losing robustness to spoofing attacks.
nodes.problem: LLM watermarks face a trade-off between scrubbing resistance and spoofing resistance set by window size.
nodes.approach: Sub-vocabulary decomposed equivalent texture keys so multiple tokens in a window independently support detection.
nodes.niche_reason: Text watermarking is an established but specialised area.

nodes.title: CausalPFN: Amortized Causal Effect Estimation via In-Context Learning
nodes.tldr: A single transformer, trained on simulated causal datasets, that estimates treatment effects on new observational data in context, with calibrated uncertainty and no tuning.
nodes.problem: Choosing a causal effect estimator from dozens of methods needs substantial expert effort
nodes.approach: Prior-fitted network trained on ignorable simulated data-generating processes, used in context
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Amortized causal inference via PFNs is a rare combination

nodes.title: Private Set Union with Multiple Contributions
nodes.tldr: Studies differentially private set union when users hold multiple items, introduces a utility ratio, proves no instance-optimal algorithm exists for k>1, and gives prediction-aware algorithms.
nodes.problem: Computing the union of users' item sets privately while maximizing the number of reported items.
nodes.approach: Algorithms with utility-ratio guarantees, lower bounds, and prediction-augmented mechanisms degrading with L-infinity error.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical DP set-union with predictions is a narrow specialty.

nodes.title: Learning Interestingness in Automated Mathematical Theory Formation
nodes.tldr: Introduces Fermat, an RL environment for mathematical theory discovery, and an LLM-based evolutionary algorithm with function abstraction to synthesize interestingness measures.
nodes.problem: Automating open-ended mathematical theory formation and scoring interestingness of mathematical objects.
nodes.approach: Symbolic RL environment plus LLM-driven evolutionary synthesis of interestingness functions with abstraction.
nodes.primary_topic: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.niche_reason: Learning interestingness for theory discovery is very rare.

nodes.title: MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs
nodes.tldr: Mixture of Block Attention routes each query to a learned subset of key-value blocks, enabling switching between full and sparse attention for long-context LLMs.
nodes.problem: Quadratic attention cost limits long-context LLMs, and fixed sparse patterns impose task-specific biases.
nodes.approach: Applies Mixture-of-Experts gating to attention blocks so the model chooses where to attend.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse attention for long context is a crowded direction.

nodes.title: Spatial-MLLM: Boosting MLLM Capabilities in Visual-based Spatial Intelligence
nodes.tldr: Spatial-MLLM adds a 3D spatial encoder from a visual geometry model to a video MLLM for spatial reasoning from 2D inputs, via SFT and GRPO.
nodes.problem: MLLMs lack spatial intelligence from purely 2D images or video without 3D data.
nodes.approach: Dual encoder combining semantic 2D and geometry-model 3D features, space-aware frame sampling, SFT and GRPO.
nodes.niche_reason: Spatial reasoning for MLLMs is active but specialised.

nodes.title: GeoRemover: Removing Objects and Their Causal Visual Artifacts
nodes.tldr: Removes objects with their shadows and reflections by editing depth geometry first, then rendering photorealistic RGB conditioned on it.
nodes.problem: Mask-aligned inpainting misses causal artifacts like shadows and reflections, or over-erases other objects.
nodes.approach: Two-stage geometry removal then appearance rendering, with a preference-driven objective on depth.
nodes.niche_reason: Object removal with causal effects is specialised editing work

nodes.title: Orochi: Versatile Biomedical Image Processor
nodes.tldr: Orochi is a pretrained Mamba-based all-in-one biomedical image processor for registration, fusion, restoration and super-resolution, using task-related joint-embedding pretraining and three fine-tuning tiers.
nodes.problem: Biomedical image processing models are task- and dataset-specific, burdening biologists.
nodes.approach: Pretrain multi-head hierarchy Mamba on 100+ studies with task-related joint-embedding degradations; full/normal/light fine-tuning.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Biomedical foundation model for low-level tasks; specialised.

nodes.title: AI Research Agents for Machine Learning: Search, Exploration, and Generalization in MLE-bench
nodes.tldr: Formalizes ML research agents as search policies over candidate solutions and shows that pairing search strategy with operator design lifts MLE-bench Kaggle medal rates.
nodes.problem: Agent performance on MLE-bench is unclear across search strategies and operator sets.
nodes.approach: Frames agents as search policies (Greedy, MCTS, Evolutionary) over operator sets, systematically varied.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM coding agents for ML engineering are a crowded area.

nodes.title: Breaking the Performance Ceiling in Reinforcement Learning requires Inference Strategies
nodes.tldr: Shows test-time inference strategies with extra seconds of compute break the performance ceiling of trained multi-agent RL systems, up to 126% gain.
nodes.problem: Complex multi-agent RL systems plateau at a performance ceiling under zero-shot inference.
nodes.approach: Execution-time inference phase with a chosen strategy and compute budget, evaluated over 60k experiments.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Inference-time strategies for complex RL; specialised

nodes.title: ELECTRA: A Cartesian Network for 3D Charge Density Prediction with Floating Orbitals
nodes.tldr: ELECTRA is an equivariant Cartesian tensor network that predicts electronic charge density as floating Gaussian orbitals, cutting DFT SCF iterations by about half.
nodes.problem: Predicting 3D electronic charge densities accurately and efficiently without hand-placed atom-centered orbitals.
nodes.approach: Equivariant network predicts orbital positions, weights, and covariances with a symmetry-breaking mechanism, inspired by Gaussian splatting.
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum-chemistry density prediction with floating orbitals is rare.

nodes.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
nodes.tldr: Language model that scales test-time compute by iterating a recurrent block in latent space instead of generating more reasoning tokens.
nodes.problem: Test-time compute scaling usually requires producing more chain-of-thought tokens.
nodes.approach: Recurrent-depth transformer unrolling a shared block to arbitrary depth at inference.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.confidence_reason: Reasoning vs architecture: a judgment call between two topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Latent recurrent depth is a distinctive alternative to CoT.

nodes.title: RoFt-Mol: Benchmarking Robust Fine-tuning with Molecular Graph Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks eight fine-tuning methods for molecular graph foundation models and proposes ROFT-MOL, combining post-hoc weight interpolation with weight ensembles.
nodes.problem: Fine-tuning molecular graph foundation models overfits under scarce labels and mixed regression and classification.
nodes.approach: Classifies eight methods into weight-based, representation-based, and partial fine-tuning; hybrid interpolation and ensembling.
nodes.niche_reason: Molecular fine-tuning benchmark is specialized, not mainstream.

nodes.title: X-Field: A Physically Informed Representation for 3D X-ray Reconstruction
nodes.tldr: Represents X-ray scenes with 3D ellipsoids of distinct attenuation coefficients and path-partitioning for cumulative attenuation, improving X-ray novel view synthesis and CT reconstruction.
nodes.problem: Visible-light 3D representations ignore X-ray penetration and attenuation physics in sparse-view reconstruction.
nodes.approach: Attenuation-coefficient ellipsoids, path-partitioning intersection algorithm, progressive initialization, material-based optimization.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: X-ray physics-based splatting-like representation is an unusual niche.

nodes.title: MoCha: Towards Movie-Grade Talking Character Generation
nodes.tldr: MoCha generates full talking-character video from speech and text using localized audio attention and joint speech/text-labelled training, supporting multi-character turn-based dialogue.
nodes.problem: Video generation lacks speech-driven full-character animation beyond talking heads for cinematic storytelling.
nodes.approach: Diffusion video model with localized audio attention, joint speech and text data training, and character-tag prompts.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Speech-driven character video is a specialised video generation niche.

nodes.title: MLIP Arena: Advancing Fairness and Transparency in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials via an Open, Accessible Benchmark Platform
nodes.tldr: Introduces MLIP Arena, a benchmark platform that scores machine-learning interatomic potentials on physics awareness, reactivity, extreme stability and thermodynamics.
nodes.problem: Existing interatomic potential benchmarks suffer from data leakage and rely on error metrics tied to DFT references.
nodes.approach: Physics-based evaluation beyond static DFT references, with a reproducible Python package and online leaderboard.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised benchmarking of atomistic ML potentials

nodes.title: Curl Descent : Non-Gradient Learning Dynamics with Sign-Diverse Plasticity
nodes.tldr: Analyzes learning dynamics with non-gradient curl terms from sign-diverse plasticity in student-teacher networks, showing they can destabilize learning or surprisingly speed up escape from saddles.
nodes.problem: Whether learning rules not following gradient descent can still optimize, relevant to biological plasticity.
nodes.approach: Analytic student-teacher analysis adding rule-flipped neurons that introduce curl components into weight dynamics.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Very rare non-gradient learning dynamics angle.

nodes.title: Spatial Understanding from Videos: Structured Prompts Meet Simulation Data
nodes.tldr: Improves VLM 3D spatial reasoning with SpatialMind, a structured prompting strategy, and ScanForgeQA, a fine-tuning QA dataset generated automatically from 3D simulation scenes.
nodes.problem: Pretrained VLMs have spatial uncertainty and too little 3D spatial training data.
nodes.approach: Decomposed structured prompting plus simulation-built QA data for fine-tuning, without architecture changes.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: VLM vs multimodal LLM area overlap makes the primary topic a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: VLM 3D spatial reasoning via simulation data is specialised

nodes.title: An Analytical Theory of Spectral Bias in the Learning Dynamics of Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Derives exact gradient-flow solutions for linear and convolutional diffusion denoisers, exposing a power-law spectral bias where mode convergence time scales inversely with variance.
nodes.problem: How the learned distribution of diffusion models evolves during training.
nodes.approach: Gaussian-equivalence-based analytical solutions for linear and convolutional denoiser weight dynamics and generated KL divergence.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Exact training-dynamics theory for diffusion is rare.

nodes.title: PLMTrajRec: A Scalable and Generalizable Trajectory Recovery Method with Pre-trained Language Models
nodes.tldr: Presents PLMTrajRec, which fine-tunes a pretrained language model to recover missing points in sparse vehicle trajectories across different sampling intervals.
nodes.problem: Sparse trajectories lack detail, and dense trajectory data for training recovery models is scarce.
nodes.approach: Converts sampling intervals into prompts, unifies intervals via a trajectory encoder, and adds road-condition prompts.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Trajectory recovery with PLMs is a specialised spatiotemporal task

nodes.title: LLM Meeting Decision Trees on Tabular Data
nodes.tldr: Uses an LLM to rewrite decision-tree rules and corrects tree predictions with an LLM-derived error vector, avoiding tabular text serialization.
nodes.problem: Serializing tabular data into text for LLMs is not universal, raises privacy risks, and limits context.
nodes.approach: LLM-redesigned decision-tree rules, plus a calibration step that adds an LLM-derived error-correction vector to tree outputs.
nodes.confidence_reason: Tabular learning and LLM topics both fit; primary is judgment.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-guided decision-tree rule refinement for tabular data is unusual.

nodes.title: Multidimensional Bayesian Utility Maximization: Tight Approximations to Welfare
nodes.tldr: Studies multidimensional Bayesian utility maximization with unit-demand buyers, giving simple prior-independent mechanisms with tight (1-1/e) and log(n/m) welfare approximations.
nodes.problem: Approximating optimal welfare with simple mechanisms for multi-item unit-demand buyers under i.i.d. values.
nodes.approach: Prior-independent approximately optimal mechanisms with matching lower bounds in n and m.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Algorithmic mechanism design theory, far from ML mainstream.

nodes.title: Word-Level Emotional Expression Control in Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Self-trains a pretrained zero-shot TTS model to control emotion and speaking rate per word, using transition smoothing and dynamic speed control without intra-sentence data.
nodes.problem: Existing emotional TTS works at utterance level and lacks word-level expressive control, with scarce annotated data.
nodes.approach: Multi-round inference with transition smoothing and dynamic speed control, then self-training with emotional attention bias.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: Word-level emotional TTS control is a specialised speech niche

nodes.title: SATURN: SAT-based Reinforcement Learning to Unleash LLMs Reasoning
nodes.tldr: SATURN trains LLM reasoning with RL on scalable, rule-verifiable SAT problems with controllable difficulty and curriculum, improving math and coding benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Existing RL tasks for LLM reasoning lack scalability, verifiability and difficulty control.
nodes.approach: SAT-based task generation with rule verification and easy-to-hard curriculum RL on distilled Qwen models.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL for LLM reasoning is crowded; SAT tasks add some novelty.

nodes.title: Corporate Needs You to Find the Difference: Revisiting Submodular and Supermodular Ratio Optimization Problems
nodes.tldr: Shows submodular and supermodular ratio problems including densest subgraph are equivalent, and that SuperGreedy++ and Fujishige-Wolfe min-norm point are universal solvers outperforming specialised baselines.
nodes.problem: Minimizing or maximizing average value f(S)/|S| of submodular or supermodular functions lacks unified efficient solvers.
nodes.approach: Strongly polynomial reductions among problems via min-norm point; apply SuperGreedy++ and Wolfe algorithms with large-scale experiments.
nodes.niche_reason: Submodular ratio optimization and densest subgraph are very rare in ML.

nodes.title: Optimal and Provable Calibration in High-Dimensional Binary Classification: Angular Calibration and Platt Scaling
nodes.tldr: Proposes angular calibration for high-dimensional linear binary classifiers, provably calibrated and Bregman-optimal, and shows Platt scaling converges to the same solution.
nodes.problem: Provably calibrating linear classifiers in high-dimensional regimes with comparable samples and features.
nodes.approach: Interpolate with a chance classifier using the estimated angle between estimator and true weights.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised high-dimensional statistics treatment of calibration.

nodes.title: UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms
nodes.tldr: UMA is a family of universal interatomic models trained on 500M atomic structures across molecules, materials and catalysts, using mixture of linear experts.
nodes.problem: Fast, accurate, generalizable atomic property prediction across chemical domains.
nodes.approach: Large-scale multi-domain training with scaling laws and a mixture-of-linear-experts architecture.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Interatomic potentials are a specialised but active science-ML area.

nodes.title: ReSim: Reliable World Simulation for Autonomous Driving
nodes.tldr: A controllable driving world model trained on real expert data plus simulator non-expert data, simulating hazardous behaviors and adding a Video2Reward module for policy selection.
nodes.problem: Driving world models trained on safe expert data fail to follow hazardous or non-expert ego actions.
nodes.approach: Diffusion transformer video generator trained on mixed real and CARLA data, with action conditioning and a reward estimator.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Driving world models are a popular current direction.

nodes.title: Dynamic Algorithm for Explainable $k$-medians Clustering under $\ell_p$ Norm
nodes.tldr: First algorithm for explainable k-medians clustering with threshold decision trees under every finite lp norm, with near-logarithmic approximation guarantees and dynamic updates.
nodes.problem: Explainable k-medians clustering approximation beyond l1 and l2 norms.
nodes.approach: Threshold decision-tree construction with lp-dependent approximation analysis, supporting dynamic updates.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Explainable clustering approximation theory is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Envisioning Beyond the Pixels: Benchmarking Reasoning-Informed Visual Editing
nodes.tldr: RISEBench is a benchmark testing whether visual editing models can apply temporal, causal, spatial, and logical reasoning to instructions.
nodes.problem: Visual editing models lack evaluation on instructions that require reasoning, not just appearance changes.
nodes.approach: Curated reasoning-category test cases scored on instruction reasoning, consistency, and plausibility with human and LMM judges.
nodes.niche_reason: Reasoning-focused image editing benchmark is a specialised angle

nodes.title: FPSAttention: Training-Aware FP8 and Sparsity Co-Design for Fast Video Diffusion
nodes.tldr: FPSAttention co-designs FP8 quantization and sparsity for video diffusion attention with 3D tile granularity and step-aware strategy, giving 4.96x end-to-end speedup.
nodes.problem: Slow video diffusion inference; naive combination of quantization and sparsity degrades quality
nodes.approach: Training-aware joint FP8 and sparse attention with unified 3D tiles and Hopper kernel
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient video diffusion is active but hardware co-design is specialised

nodes.title: Partition-Then-Adapt: Combating Prediction Bias for Reliable Multi-Modal Test-Time Adaptation
nodes.tldr: Partition-Then-Adapt splits test batches by prediction bias into reliable and unreliable samples, reweights them, and aligns modalities with attention for multi-modal test-time adaptation.
nodes.problem: Test-time adaptation fails when multiple modalities shift simultaneously, with severe prediction bias.
nodes.approach: Debiased reweighting via label-frequency partitioning plus attention-guided multi-modal alignment.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-modal TTA is specialised.

nodes.title: DeltaFlow: An Efficient Multi-frame Scene Flow Estimation Method
nodes.tldr: DeltaFlow is a lightweight 3D multi-frame scene flow estimator using a delta scheme for temporal features at constant cost, plus category-balanced and instance consistency losses.
nodes.problem: Multi-frame scene flow costs grow with frame count, and class imbalance and motion inconsistency persist.
nodes.approach: Delta scheme temporal feature extraction with Category-Balanced and Instance Consistency losses.
nodes.niche_reason: Scene flow on LiDAR is established but specialised.

nodes.title: MGUP: A Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy for Stochastic Optimization
nodes.tldr: Adds a plug-in selective update to momentum optimizers like AdamW and Lion, taking larger steps on a fixed fraction of parameters, with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Large-model training lacks a general mechanism for fine-grained selective updates with convergence guarantees.
nodes.approach: Per-iteration selection of a fixed proportion of parameters receiving larger step sizes, with smaller nonzero steps elsewhere.
nodes.niche_reason: Optimizer variants are a crowded area

nodes.title: Universal Causal Inference in a Topos
nodes.tldr: Formulates causal inference in a topos, introducing topos causal models that generalize SCMs with intuitionistic internal logic and a universal property.
nodes.problem: Causal inference lacks a universal categorical foundation generalizing structural causal models.
nodes.approach: Topos causal models using sheaves, subobject classifier for interventions and Heyting algebra semantics.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Topos-theoretic causality is extremely rare in ML.

nodes.title: Achieving $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/N)$ Optimality Gap in Restless Bandits through Gaussian Approximation
nodes.tldr: Proposes a stochastic-programming policy for finite-horizon restless bandits achieving O(1/N) optimality gap on degenerate instances via Gaussian approximation.
nodes.problem: Fluid-based LP policies lose Theta(1/sqrt N) per-arm optimality on degenerate restless bandits.
nodes.approach: Gaussian stochastic system capturing mean and variance of arm dynamics, solved as a stochastic program.
nodes.niche_reason: Gaussian-approximation policies for degenerate restless bandits are rare

nodes.title: Computational Efficiency under Covariate Shift in Kernel Ridge Regression
nodes.tldr: Shows random projection kernel ridge regression retains statistical accuracy under covariate shift while giving significant computational and memory savings.
nodes.problem: Trade-off between computational efficiency and statistical accuracy of kernel regression under covariate shift.
nodes.approach: Learning-rate analysis of random-subspace RKHS hypothesis spaces under covariate shift.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Kernel theory under covariate shift is a rare combination.

nodes.title: Shortcut Features as Top Eigenfunctions of NTK: A Linear Neural Network Case and More
nodes.tldr: NTK analysis shows shortcut features are top NTK eigenfunctions under cluster imbalance, and max-margin bias alone does not explain shortcut learning.
nodes.problem: Why neural networks prefer shortcut features that do not generalize beyond the training set.
nodes.approach: NTK eigenfunction analysis of linear networks, extended empirically to ReLU and ResNet models.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: NTK analysis of shortcut learning is specialised.

nodes.title: HYPERION: Fine-Grained Hypersphere Alignment for Robust Federated Graph Learning
nodes.tldr: Robust federated graph learning under noisy labels, aligning client embeddings on a hypersphere and purifying noisy samples at the server.
nodes.problem: Label noise propagates through edges and is hard to detect in federated graph learning.
nodes.approach: Client-side hypersphere alignment plus server-side geometric hyperspherical purification.
nodes.niche_reason: Hyperspherical federated graph learning under noise is unusual.

nodes.title: TransMLA: Migrating GQA Models to MLA with Full DeepSeek Compatibility and Speedup
nodes.tldr: Converts any GQA-based pretrained LLM into a DeepSeek-compatible MLA model, compressing the KV cache and enabling up to 10x speedup after 6B fine-tuning tokens.
nodes.problem: Model providers lack incentive to retrain GQA models as MLA from scratch.
nodes.approach: Low-rank KV compression converting GQA weights into DeepSeek-compatible MLA format, then fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: KV-cache compression is a crowded inference topic; GQA-to-MLA conversion is less common.

nodes.title: Tackling Biased Evaluators in Dueling Bandits
nodes.tldr: Proposes bias-sensitive dueling bandit algorithms that minimise regret when human evaluators give systematically biased preference feedback, with known or unknown bias.
nodes.problem: Dueling bandit regret when pairwise preference feedback from evaluators is systematically biased.
nodes.approach: Unbiased arm performance estimator plus bias-sensitive algorithm; block coordinate descent when bias is unknown.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Dueling bandits are specialised; the biased-evaluator variant is less common.

nodes.title: Regularized least squares learning with heavy-tailed noise is minimax optimal
nodes.tldr: Shows kernel ridge regression with only finitely many noise moments attains minimax-optimal rates, via subgaussian plus polynomial excess-risk bounds.
nodes.problem: Kernel ridge regression theory usually assumes subexponential noise, which excludes heavy-tailed noise.
nodes.approach: Integral-operator analysis with a Fuk-Nagaev inequality for Hilbert-space valued random variables.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Heavy-tailed noise in kernel regression is a specialised theory area

nodes.title: Is Grokking a Computational Glass Relaxation?
nodes.tldr: Interprets grokking as glass relaxation, finding no entropy barrier between memorisation and generalisation, and proposes a toy optimizer that removes grokking.
nodes.problem: Explaining why neural networks abruptly generalise long after memorising the training data (grokking).
nodes.approach: Samples Boltzmann entropy over training loss and test accuracy, and uses a Wang-Landau molecular-dynamics optimizer.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Physics glass-relaxation framing of grokking is a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Hyperbolic Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Finds LLM token embeddings are hyperbolic, then fine-tunes them with HypLoRA, a low-rank adaptation performed directly on the hyperbolic manifold, improving reasoning.
nodes.problem: Euclidean embeddings may poorly fit the power-law, tree-like structure of LLM token embeddings.
nodes.approach: Low-rank adaptation directly on the hyperbolic manifold, avoiding cancellation from repeated exp and log maps.
nodes.niche_reason: Hyperbolic fine-tuning of LLMs is a rare geometric angle

nodes.title: On the Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing In Practice
nodes.tldr: Analyses why kernel conditional independence tests fail in practice, finding conditional-mean-embedding errors inflate Type I error and kernel choice matters for power.
nodes.problem: Popular conditional independence tests frequently fail in practice despite known theoretical impossibility results.
nodes.approach: Analyses the Kernel-based CI test and Generalized Covariance Measure, identifying error sources in conditional mean embeddings.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Practical failure analysis of CI tests; specialised statistical topic.

nodes.title: Training-Free Constrained Generation With Stable Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Integrates stable diffusion with constrained optimization so generated samples strictly satisfy physical or functional constraints, without training.
nodes.problem: Latent diffusion models cannot easily enforce strict physical or domain constraints on outputs.
nodes.approach: Training-free constrained optimization over the diffusion generation process, tested on materials and copyright constraints.
nodes.niche_reason: Hard constraint enforcement in latent diffusion is less common

nodes.title: Transformer brain encoders explain human high-level visual responses
nodes.tldr: Uses transformer attention to dynamically route retinotopic visual features to category-selective brain areas, predicting fMRI responses better than static-receptive-field encoding models.
nodes.problem: Linear encoding models ignore feature-map structure and static receptive fields miss high-level visual areas.
nodes.approach: Attention-based routing of DNN feature maps with attention signals visualisable per category area.
nodes.niche_reason: Transformer-based brain encoding is a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Towards Building Model/Prompt-Transferable Attackers against Large Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Crafts adversarial images that transfer across black-box LVLMs and prompts by steering mutual information between outputs and disentangled input patterns.
nodes.problem: Adversarial attacks on LVLMs overfit one model and prompt and fail to transfer.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic constraints estimating mutual information gain, incorporated into adversarial learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Transferable attacks on LVLMs are a common adversarial direction

nodes.title: RobustMerge: Parameter-Efficient Model Merging for MLLMs with Direction Robustness
nodes.tldr: Presents RobustMerge, a training-free method that merges parameter-efficient multimodal LLM adapters while preserving direction robustness via singular-value compensation.
nodes.problem: Full fine-tuning merging methods fail when merging low-rank parameter-efficient modules.
nodes.approach: Prunes parameters using inter-parameter relations and applies cross-task normalization for unseen-task generalization.
nodes.confidence_reason: Model merging has no explicit topic; PEFT is closest
nodes.niche_reason: Model merging is a popular, growing direction

nodes.title: Unlocking hidden biomolecular conformational landscapes in diffusion models at inference time
nodes.tldr: Enhances diffusion-model sampling of protein conformational ensembles at inference time using classifier guidance, filtering, and free energy estimation.
nodes.problem: Predicting the full distribution of biomolecular conformations is far harder than predicting a static structure.
nodes.approach: Inference-time classifier guidance and filtering over diffusion sampling with free energy estimation.
nodes.niche_reason: Conformational ensemble sampling for proteins is a rare niche

nodes.title: MesaTask: Towards Task-Driven Tabletop Scene Generation via 3D Spatial Reasoning
nodes.tldr: MesaTask offers a 10k-scene tabletop dataset and an LLM framework with spatial reasoning chains and DPO to generate task-conforming 3D tabletop scenes for robots.
nodes.problem: Robots need task-relevant tabletop scenes, but manual or random layouts lack plausibility and task alignment.
nodes.approach: LLM with spatial reasoning chain (objects, relations, scene graph) plus DPO, trained on MesaTask-10K.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans 3D scene generation, LLM reasoning and robot data; primary is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Task-driven tabletop layout generation for robotics is a rare niche.

nodes.title: An Optimized Franz-Parisi Criterion and its Equivalence with SQ Lower Bounds
nodes.tldr: Proves an optimized Franz-Parisi criterion is equivalent to statistical query lower bounds for statistical detection problems, unifying several known hardness results.
nodes.problem: Characterizing computational hardness phases in statistical detection problems.
nodes.approach: Refined annealed Franz-Parisi overlap criterion linked to SQ lower bounds under a mild assumption.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Computational hardness via statistical-physics potentials is rare

nodes.title: Distributional Training Data Attribution: What do Influence Functions Sample?
nodes.tldr: Introduces distributional training data attribution, predicting how output distributions over training runs depend on data, and shows influence functions arise from unrolled differentiation.
nodes.problem: Data attribution ignores training randomness from initialization and batching.
nodes.approach: Distributional attribution framework linking influence functions to unrolled differentiation without convexity assumptions.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Data attribution is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Long-Tailed Recognition via Information-Preservable Two-Stage Learning
nodes.tldr: Two-stage long-tailed recognition: an information-theoretic representation learning stage minimizing intra-class distance, then a sampling strategy selecting informative instances to fix majority-biased decision boundaries.
nodes.problem: Deep classifiers are biased toward frequent classes on long-tailed data.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic representation learning followed by informative-instance sampling to rectify decision boundaries.
nodes.niche_reason: Long-tailed recognition is a common benchmark topic.

nodes.title: Joint‑Embedding vs Reconstruction: Provable Benefits of Latent Space Prediction for Self‑Supervised Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows joint-embedding SSL beats reconstruction when irrelevant features have large magnitude, using closed-form solutions to compare alignment requirements.
nodes.problem: Practitioners lack guidance on choosing between reconstruction and joint-embedding self-supervised learning.
nodes.approach: Closed-form analysis of both paradigms characterizing how augmentation alignment with irrelevant features affects asymptotic optimality.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory comparing SSL paradigms is specialised but active

nodes.title: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning
nodes.tldr: Shows LLM unlearning is reversible by finetuning, and proposes UNDO, distilling an unlearned model into a noised copy to make removal robust.
nodes.problem: Current LLM unlearning is fragile: a few finetuning steps restore the removed capabilities.
nodes.approach: Distill unlearned model into a noised randomly initialised student, trading compute for robustness.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Unlearning robustness is an active, crowded direction

nodes.title: High-Dimensional Calibration from Swap Regret
nodes.tldr: Shows multi-dimensional online calibration reduces to swap-regret minimization, giving efficient epsilon-calibrated forecasts over arbitrary convex sets and norms.
nodes.problem: Online calibration of multi-dimensional forecasts over arbitrary convex sets and norms.
nodes.approach: Reduce calibration to swap regret minimized with TreeSwap and Follow-The-Leader.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-dimensional calibration via swap regret is a rare theoretical angle.

nodes.title: MetaGS: A Meta-Learned Gaussian-Phong Model for Out-of-Distribution 3D Scene Relighting
nodes.tldr: Meta-learns 3D Gaussian splatting and embeds Blinn-Phong shading priors to relight scenes under unseen lighting conditions.
nodes.problem: Relighting fails when test lighting differs from training lighting distributions
nodes.approach: Meta-learning across lighting conditions plus physically based Blinn-Phong priors inside Gaussian splatting.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Established 3DGS area with a relighting twist

nodes.title: DiCo: Revitalizing ConvNets for Scalable and Efficient Diffusion Modeling
nodes.tldr: DiCo builds diffusion models from pure ConvNet blocks with compact channel attention, matching DiT quality on ImageNet with roughly 3x faster inference.
nodes.problem: Diffusion Transformers are computationally heavy while their global attention is often redundant.
nodes.approach: Replace self-attention with convolutions plus compact channel attention to raise channel diversity.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion architecture variants are common.

nodes.title: Non-Asymptotic Analysis Of Data Augmentation For Precision Matrix Estimation
nodes.tldr: Derives concentration bounds for precision matrix estimators, shrinkage and data augmentation, using a new deterministic equivalent for generalized resolvents with dependent samples.
nodes.problem: Understanding how artificial samples affect high-dimensional inverse covariance estimation and tuning their proportion.
nodes.approach: Random matrix theory with a novel deterministic equivalent for generalized resolvents under structured dependence.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Random matrix analysis of augmentation for covariance estimation is rare.

nodes.title: On Universality Classes of Equivariant Networks
nodes.tldr: Shows separation power does not determine approximation ability of equivariant networks, characterizing universality classes of shallow invariant networks and conditions for non-universality.
nodes.problem: Understanding the universality (approximation power) of equivariant networks beyond separation power.
nodes.approach: Characterize universality classes of shallow invariant networks and derive implications for equivariant ones via projection.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Approximation theory of equivariant nets is a specialised theory niche.

nodes.title: On the Universal Near Optimality of Hedge in Combinatorial Settings
nodes.tldr: Proves Hedge is near-optimal for combinatorial online learning, and that OMD with dilated entropy inherits its regret on DAG shortest paths.
nodes.problem: Whether the classical Hedge algorithm is optimal for all combinatorial online learning settings
nodes.approach: Matching lower bound for any algorithm, tightness analysis on m-sets, and an OMD iterate-equivalence.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Optimality of Hedge in combinatorial online learning is specialised theory

nodes.title: Blameless Users in a Clean Room: Defining Copyright Protection for Generative Models
nodes.tldr: Argues near access-freeness does not prevent copying and proposes clean-room copy protection, a risk-based copyright guarantee for generative models.
nodes.problem: Existing provable copyright protection for generative models is technically and legally insufficient.
nodes.approach: Defines a blameless copy-protection framework, instantiates it as clean-room protection, and links differential privacy to it.
nodes.confidence_reason: Legal-technical theory spanning ethics and privacy; primary topic is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Formal copyright definitions for generative models are rare

nodes.title: Unveiling the Power of Multiple Gossip Steps: A Stability-Based Generalization Analysis in Decentralized Training
nodes.tldr: Gives stability-based generalization and excess error bounds for decentralized training with multiple gossip steps, showing a gap to centralized SGD remains even with infinite gossip.
nodes.problem: Why multi-gossip steps help decentralized training and whether they close the gap to centralized training.
nodes.approach: Stability analysis yielding generalization bounds under non-convex settings across topology, heterogeneity, and node count.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Generalization theory for decentralized SGD is a rare topic.

nodes.title: LLM-Explorer: A Plug-in Reinforcement Learning Policy Exploration Enhancement Driven by Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: LLM-Explorer prompts an LLM with the agent's learning trajectory to generate task-specific, adaptive exploration distributions, plugging into DQN, DDPG and TD3.
nodes.problem: Preset, rigid exploration processes ignore task features and the agent's learning status.
nodes.approach: Periodically have an LLM analyze trajectories and output a probability distribution for exploration noise.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-guided exploration is specialised but growing.

nodes.title: Generative Trajectory Stitching through Diffusion Composition
nodes.tldr: Solves new long-horizon planning tasks by stitching overlapping trajectory chunks sampled from one bidirectional diffusion model that conditions neighboring segments.
nodes.problem: Diffusion planners only solve tasks resembling their training data, limiting trajectory stitching.
nodes.approach: Overlapping trajectory chunks modeled jointly by a bidirectional diffusion model, so information propagates across segments.
nodes.confidence_reason: Planning and offline RL overlap; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: compositional diffusion planning.

nodes.title: Improved Representation Steering for Language Models
nodes.tldr: Improves LLM representation steering with a bidirectional preference objective that promotes and suppresses concepts, narrowing the gap with prompting.
nodes.problem: Representation steering is less effective than prompting for introducing or suppressing concepts.
nodes.approach: Bidirectional reference-free preference optimization that jointly steers concepts toward and away from targets.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.confidence_reason: Steering method sits between interpretability and preference optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Representation steering is established but specialised next to fine-tuning

nodes.title: OCTDiff: Bridged Diffusion Model for Portable OCT Super-Resolution and Enhancement
nodes.tldr: OCTDiff is a bridged diffusion model with adaptive noise aggregation and multi-scale cross-attention that super-resolves portable OCT retinal images, using a clinical-score-guided loss.
nodes.problem: Low-cost portable OCT images have poor resolution, limiting diagnostic utility.
nodes.approach: Image-to-image diffusion with adaptive noise aggregation, multi-scale cross-attention U-Net, and clinical quality-guided loss.
nodes.niche_reason: Portable OCT super-resolution is a niche medical imaging task.

nodes.title: Blackbox Model Provenance via Palimpsestic Membership Inference
nodes.tldr: Tests whether a black-box derivative LLM or its text is derived from an open-weight model by correlating memorization with the model's training-example order.
nodes.problem: Proving a black-box model or its generated text was derived from a specific training run.
nodes.approach: Independence tests correlating likelihoods of training examples with shuffled training order, via queries or observed text.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Provenance via training-order correlation is a rare approach

nodes.title: ROGR: Relightable 3D Objects using Generative Relighting
nodes.tldr: Reconstructs relightable 3D objects by training a lighting-conditioned NeRF on images generated under many illuminations by a generative relighting model.
nodes.problem: Creating relightable 3D object models from multi-view captures.
nodes.approach: Generative relighting for training data, then dual-branch lighting-conditioned NeRF.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Relightable NeRF via generative relighting is specialised.

nodes.title: Tighter CMI-Based Generalization Bounds via Stochastic Projection and Quantization
nodes.tldr: Tighter conditional mutual information generalization bounds via stochastic projection and quantization, fixing vacuous prior cases and showing memorization is unnecessary for generalization.
nodes.problem: Existing MI and CMI generalization bounds are vacuous or wrong for some learning problems.
nodes.approach: Stochastic projection and lossy compression applied to conditional mutual information bounds.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Information-theoretic generalization bounds are rare theory.

nodes.title: Towards Reliable Code-as-Policies: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Embodied Task Planning
nodes.tldr: Adds symbolic verification and interactive validation to LLM code-as-policies, so generated robot code explores the environment to fill in missing observations.
nodes.problem: LLM code-as-policies lack environmental grounding in dynamic, partially observable settings.
nodes.approach: Neuro-symbolic verification plus exploratory code that interacts with the environment during validation.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM code-as-policies is active; neuro-symbolic exploratory validation is specialised

nodes.title: Joint Hierarchical Representation Learning of Samples and Features via Informed Tree-Wasserstein Distance
nodes.tldr: Jointly learns hierarchical trees for samples and features by alternating Tree-Wasserstein Distance computations, with convergence guarantees and gains in hyperbolic GCNs and scRNA-seq.
nodes.problem: Existing hierarchical representation learning handles only one data mode, samples or features, at a time.
nodes.approach: Alternately build a tree for one mode and compute TWD for the other, iteratively refining both.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Joint sample-feature tree-Wasserstein learning is very rare.

nodes.title: HawkBench: Investigating Resilience of RAG Methods on Stratified Information-Seeking Tasks
nodes.tldr: HawkBench is a human-labeled, multi-domain RAG benchmark stratified by information-seeking task type, measuring how resilient methods are across query types.
nodes.problem: Existing RAG benchmarks mostly test factoid queries on varying knowledge bases, missing diverse needs.
nodes.approach: Human-labeled multi-domain benchmark stratified by information-seeking task type, evaluating RAG methods on quality and latency.
nodes.niche_reason: RAG benchmarks are common; stratified information-seeking evaluation is a variant

nodes.title: OrthoLoC: UAV 6-DoF Localization and Calibration Using Orthographic Geodata
nodes.tldr: Introduces a UAV localization dataset matching aerial images to free orthographic geodata, plus AdHoP refinement that improves any feature matcher.
nodes.problem: Aerial localization without GNSS needs large databases or heavy 3D models.
nodes.approach: Paired benchmark decoupling retrieval from matching, and an AdHoP refinement module.
nodes.niche_reason: UAV localization against orthographic geodata is an unusual setup

nodes.title: Twilight: Adaptive Attention Sparsity with Hierarchical Top-$p$ Pruning
nodes.tldr: Twilight adds adaptive token budgets to sparse attention via top-p pruning, removing up to 98% of tokens with little accuracy loss and 1.4x speedup.
nodes.problem: Fixed-budget sparse attention cannot adapt to varying accuracy-efficiency needs in long-context LLMs.
nodes.approach: Apply nucleus (top-p) selection hierarchically to attention weights to decide per-query budgets.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse attention and KV cache efficiency is a very active area.

nodes.title: Shallow Diffuse: Robust and Invisible Watermarking through Low-Dim Subspaces in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Shallow Diffuse embeds robust invisible watermarks into diffusion outputs by placing them in the null space of a low-dimensional subspace, decoupling watermarking from sampling.
nodes.problem: Watermarking diffusion-generated images robustly and invisibly to counter misinformation and copyright misuse.
nodes.approach: Exploit a low-dimensional subspace in generation so the watermark lies in its null space, separate from sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: Watermarking is specialised but active for generative models.

nodes.title: AdaReasoner: Adaptive Reasoning Enables More Flexible Thinking
nodes.tldr: AdaReasoner is an LLM-agnostic plugin trained with RL to select task-specific reasoning configurations (temperature, steps), with convergence guarantees and gains across six LLMs.
nodes.problem: Fixed reasoning configurations are seldom task-optimal for LLMs across diverse reasoning tasks.
nodes.approach: RL-trained plugin with factorized action space, targeted exploration and pretrained reward model to choose configurations.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.confidence_reason: Between RL-for-LLM reasoning and prompting/configuration selection topics.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM reasoning plus RL is mainstream, though configuration selection is slightly distinct.

nodes.title: Distilling LLM Agent into Small Models with Retrieval and Code Tools
nodes.tldr: Distills full LLM agent behavior, including retrieval and code tool use, into small language models using teacher trajectories and self-consistent actions.
nodes.problem: Small language models hallucinate on rare facts and precise computation where CoT distillation fails.
nodes.approach: First-thought prefix for teacher trajectories plus self-consistent action generation at test time.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Distilling LLM agents is a common and growing direction.

nodes.title: LoRAShop: Training-Free Multi-Concept Image Generation and Editing with Rectified Flow Transformers
nodes.tldr: LoRAShop is training-free: it derives concept masks from early diffusion transformer features and blends multiple LoRAs regionally for multi-concept generation and editing.
nodes.problem: Combining multiple personalized LoRA concepts in one image while preserving identity and scene context.
nodes.approach: Derive disentangled latent masks from a prior forward pass and blend LoRA weights within masked regions in Flux.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion personalization and LoRA editing are crowded topics.

nodes.title: Stable Gradients for Stable Learning at Scale in Deep Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Finds that non-stationarity combined with gradient pathologies from architectural choices limits deep RL scaling, and proposes simple interventions that stabilize gradient flow.
nodes.problem: Deep RL networks degrade when scaled in depth and width, and the root causes are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Empirical gradient analysis followed by architectural interventions that keep gradient flow stable, compatible with existing agents.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Established scaling problem with a gradient-focused angle

nodes.title: Language Modeling by Language Models
nodes.tldr: Genesys is a multi-agent LLM system that proposes, implements, and verifies new language model architectures using genetic programming and a ladder of scales, finding 1,162 designs competitive with known ones.
nodes.problem: Automating discovery of novel language model architectures with LLM agents is inefficient and bottlenecked by invalid designs.
nodes.approach: Genetic programming backbone with multi-agent proposal, review, code generation, and selective verification at increasing scales.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans agents, architecture discovery, and scientific discovery.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-driven architecture research automation is an unusual direction.

nodes.title: Vision Transformers with Self-Distilled Registers
nodes.tldr: PH-Reg adds register tokens to a pretrained ViT via self-distillation with test-time augmentation, reducing artifact tokens without full retraining, improving dense prediction.
nodes.problem: Pretrained ViTs have artifact tokens that hurt dense localization, but retraining them with registers is infeasible.
nodes.approach: Self-distillation from a frozen teacher with denoised test-time augmented features, updating a small subset of student weights.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Post hoc register insertion for ViTs is a specialised fix.

nodes.title: Graph–Smoothed Bayesian Black-Box Shift Estimator and Its Information Geometry
nodes.tldr: GS-B3SE is a Bayesian black-box shift estimator with Laplacian-Gaussian priors tied by a label-similarity graph, with identifiability, contraction proofs and information-geometry analysis.
nodes.problem: Estimating target label priors under label shift with brittle confusion-matrix inversion that ignores noise.
nodes.approach: Probabilistic estimator with graph-smoothed priors, solved by HMC or block Newton-CG.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Label-shift estimation with information geometry is specialised.

nodes.title: An Efficient Orlicz-Sobolev Approach for Transporting Unbalanced Measures on a Graph
nodes.tldr: Introduces Orlicz-Sobolev transport, an efficiently computable distance for unbalanced measures on graphs built from an Orlicz-geometry entropy partial transport variant.
nodes.problem: Optimal transport on graphs for measures with different total mass is computationally heavy.
nodes.approach: Orlicz-EPT with dual-based regularization yielding a univariate optimization for fast computation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Orlicz geometry unbalanced transport on graphs is very rare.

nodes.title: HyPINO: Multi-Physics Neural Operators via HyperPINNs and the Method of Manufactured Solutions
nodes.tldr: A hypernetwork maps PDE parameterizations to PINN weights, enabling zero-shot solving of many 2D linear PDEs, with iterative residual refinement and faster PINN fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Zero-shot generalization of neural operators across diverse parametric PDEs without task-specific fine-tuning.
nodes.approach: Swin-transformer hypernetwork generating PINNs, trained on manufactured-solution data plus physics-informed losses, with iterative delta-PDE refinement.
nodes.niche_reason: Hypernetwork-generated PINNs for multi-physics zero-shot PDE solving is uncommon.

nodes.title: Language Models can Self-Improve at State-Value Estimation for Better Search
nodes.tldr: Self-Taught Lookahead trains an LLM value function to simulate one lookahead step in language, improving state-value estimates and web agent search without rewards or labels.
nodes.problem: Estimating state values for LLM agent search without costly ground-truth rewards or demonstrations.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised training of a value LLM to verbalize next action, state and rationale, like chain-of-thought value iteration.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles agents and reasoning/value learning; topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM agent search and self-improvement is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Pass@K Policy Optimization: Solving Harder Reinforcement Learning Problems
nodes.tldr: Pass@k Policy Optimization derives low-variance unbiased pass@k estimators, jointly transforming batched rewards to optimize pass@k and improve exploration on hard problems.
nodes.problem: Independent sample rewards optimize pass@1 and under-utilize sampling capacity, stalling on hard problems.
nodes.approach: Joint reward transformation with unbiased low-variance pass@k gradient estimators for any k ≤ n, with k annealing.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL for LLM reasoning is crowded, though pass@k estimator is distinct.

nodes.title: Strategic Costs of Perceived Bias in Fair Selection
nodes.tldr: Game-theoretic model showing that group differences in perceived post-selection value lead candidates to rational effort gaps that propagate disparities through fair selection.
nodes.problem: Explaining persistent group disparities in meritocratic selection when perceived value differs across groups.
nodes.approach: Nash equilibrium characterization in the large-agent limit plus a cost-sensitive selectivity optimization.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Strategic effort under perceived bias is an unusual angle

nodes.title: A multiscale analysis of mean-field transformers in the moderate interaction regime
nodes.tldr: Models token evolution in encoder transformers as mean-field interacting particles and characterizes multiscale collapse and clustering dynamics with convergence proofs.
nodes.problem: Understanding how tokens evolve through transformer depth at inference time.
nodes.approach: Mean-field particle system in the moderate interaction regime with rigorous limit characterization.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field multiscale analysis of attention dynamics is rare

nodes.title: CoRe: Benchmarking LLMs’ Code Reasoning Capabilities through Static Analysis Tasks
nodes.tldr: CoRe is a human-verified benchmark of 12,553 static-analysis tasks testing whether LLMs reason about data dependency, control dependency and information flow in code.
nodes.problem: LLM code evaluations measure end-to-end outcomes, not semantic program reasoning.
nodes.approach: Semantics-aware diverse sampling of program dependency tasks across C/C++, Java, Python.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Code-reasoning benchmarks are common; static analysis focus adds some distinction.

nodes.title: FuXi-Ocean: A Global Ocean Forecasting System with Sub-Daily Resolution
nodes.tldr: FuXi-Ocean is a data-driven global ocean forecaster producing six-hourly, eddy-resolving 1/12-degree predictions down to 1500 m, using a Mixture-of-Time module to limit error accumulation.
nodes.problem: Data-driven ocean models run daily and accumulate errors when forecasting sub-daily at eddy-resolving scales.
nodes.approach: Context-aware feature extraction with stacked attention and a Mixture-of-Time module weighting multiple temporal contexts.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Data-driven ocean forecasting is an emerging but specialised area

nodes.title: Sparse VideoGen2: Accelerate Video Generation with Sparse Attention via Semantic-Aware Permutation
nodes.tldr: Training-free sparse attention for video diffusion transformers that clusters tokens by semantics and densifies critical tokens for GPU-efficient speedups.
nodes.problem: Quadratic attention makes video diffusion transformers slow, and existing sparse methods misidentify critical tokens.
nodes.approach: K-means semantic-aware token permutation with top-p budget control and custom kernels.
nodes.confidence_reason: Attention acceleration fits efficiency and generation; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse attention acceleration is a crowded direction.

nodes.title: Head Pursuit: Probing Attention Specialization in Multimodal Transformers
nodes.tldr: Head Pursuit ranks attention heads by relevance to concepts via a signal-processing view of logit-lens probing, and editing ~1% of heads suppresses or enhances concepts.
nodes.problem: Understanding how attention heads specialize in semantic or visual attributes in multimodal models.
nodes.approach: Matching-pursuit-style probing of head activations through the decoder, then targeted head editing.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Interpretability of attention heads is a crowded topic.

nodes.title: Unbiased Prototype Consistency Learning for Multi-Modal and Multi-Task Object Re-Identification
nodes.tldr: Proposes a unified model for multi-modal and multi-task object re-identification across modalities and categories, using unbiased prototypes and cluster prototype consistency regularization.
nodes.problem: Re-ID models are specific to one modality and category, wasting resources and lacking generality.
nodes.approach: Unbiased prototype-guided modality enhancement plus cluster prototype consistency regularization for a unified model.
nodes.confidence_reason: Re-identification fits recognition or retrieval; no exact topic.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-modal re-identification is an established specialised area.

nodes.title: Bridging Theory and Practice in Link Representation with Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: First comprehensive study of GNN expressiveness for link representation, with a unifying framework giving a hierarchy of link models and theory-guided practical insights.
nodes.problem: Expressive power of GNNs has been studied for graphs, not for link (node-pair) representations.
nodes.approach: Unifying k_phi-k_rho-m framework subsuming message-passing link models, enabling formal expressiveness hierarchy and analysis.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: GNN expressiveness theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Puppeteer: Rig and Animate Your 3D Models
nodes.tldr: Puppeteer automates 3D rigging and animation: autoregressive transformer predicts skeletons, attention predicts skinning weights, and differentiable optimization produces stable animations.
nodes.problem: Rigging and animating static 3D models relies on expert intervention.
nodes.approach: Autoregressive skeleton prediction with joint tokenization, topology-aware skinning attention, differentiable animation optimization.
nodes.niche_reason: Automatic rigging is a rare 3D content creation niche.

nodes.title: Compositional Neural Network Verification via Assume-Guarantee Reasoning
nodes.tldr: CoVeNN decomposes neural network verification into sub-problems via assume-guarantee reasoning, using any underlying verifier to scale verification to larger networks with less memory.
nodes.problem: Neural network verifiers do not scale to large networks due to memory demands.
nodes.approach: Iterative assume-guarantee compositional framework generating verification sub-problems for an underlying verifier.
nodes.confidence_reason: Formal NN verification has no exact topic; Adversarial Robustness is closest.
nodes.niche_reason: Formal compositional verification of networks is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of Long Reasoning Models
nodes.tldr: Identifies underthinking in long reasoning models, which switch thoughts prematurely, defines a token-efficiency metric, and proposes a thought-switching penalty decoding strategy that boosts accuracy without fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Long reasoning models frequently abandon promising reasoning paths, hurting accuracy on hard math problems.
nodes.approach: Thought switching penalty (Tip) decoding that discourages premature transitions between thoughts.
nodes.niche_reason: Reasoning model analysis is a crowded, hot topic.

nodes.title: Analog In-memory Training on General Non-ideal Resistive Elements: The Impact of Response Functions
nodes.tldr: Analyzes gradient-based training on analog in-memory hardware with asymmetric non-linear response functions and proposes residual learning that converges to a critical point.
nodes.problem: Non-ideal, asymmetric resistive device responses impose an implicit penalty that distorts analog SGD.
nodes.approach: Residual learning formulated as a bilevel optimization that provably converges exactly to a critical point.
nodes.niche_reason: Analog in-memory training dynamics are rare in mainstream ML.

nodes.title: InstructHOI: Context-Aware Instruction for Multi-Modal Reasoning in Human-Object Interaction Detection
nodes.tldr: Guides a multimodal foundation model with context-aware instructions mined at the human-object level, plus a token selector, for human-object interaction detection.
nodes.problem: HOI detectors underuse the reasoning ability of large foundation models for ambiguous interactions.
nodes.approach: Context-aware instruction generator fused with language, plus interest-token filtering.
nodes.confidence_reason: HOI detection has no exact topic; VLM reasoning is the core.
nodes.niche_reason: HOI detection with reasoning-driven instructions is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Towards Understanding Camera Motions in Any Video
nodes.tldr: CameraBench provides an expert-annotated dataset and taxonomy of camera motion primitives, evaluating SfM and VLMs and fine-tuning a VLM for camera motion understanding.
nodes.problem: Understanding camera motion in videos, requiring both geometric and semantic scene understanding.
nodes.approach: Cinematographer-designed taxonomy, annotated benchmark, human study, and VLM fine-tuning for motion tasks.
nodes.niche_reason: Camera motion semantics benchmarking is a rare topic.

nodes.title: Broken Tokens? Your Language Model can Secretly Handle Non-Canonical Tokenizations
nodes.tldr: Shows LLMs stay robust to non-canonical tokenizations, and character-level splits can even improve string and arithmetic tasks.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether LMs depend on the canonical tokenizer or handle alternative tokenizations.
nodes.approach: Evaluate across 20 benchmarks with random and character-level tokenizations, then trace robustness to instruction tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.confidence_reason: Tokenization robustness straddles evaluation and interpretability; no tokenization topic exists.
nodes.niche_reason: Tokenization robustness is a niche angle on LM evaluation.

nodes.title: Is the acquisition worth the cost? Surrogate losses for Consistent Two-stage Classifiers
nodes.tldr: Derives a hinge-based surrogate loss for two-stage classifiers that defer to a costly second stage, and proves its consistency with the true loss.
nodes.problem: The natural cost-sensitive loss for two-stage consultation is hard to optimize directly.
nodes.approach: Joint training of both classifiers with a hinge surrogate that is consistent with the l01c loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Surrogate-loss consistency theory; no dedicated topic, judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-to-defer surrogate theory, specialised setting

nodes.title: 🎧MOSPA: Human Motion Generation Driven by Spatial Audio
nodes.tldr: Introduces a spatial-audio motion dataset and a diffusion model that generates realistic human motion conditioned on the spatial features of sound.
nodes.problem: Virtual humans rarely respond realistically to spatial audio, which prior motion models ignore.
nodes.approach: Introduces a spatial audio-driven motion dataset and a diffusion model fusing spatial audio features.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Spatial-audio-driven motion generation is very rare

nodes.title: Communication-Efficient Language Model Training Scales Reliably and Robustly: Scaling Laws for DiLoCo
nodes.tldr: Studies scaling laws for DiLoCo, a communication-efficient distributed LLM training method, showing it scales predictably and can beat data-parallel training under fixed compute.
nodes.problem: How communication-efficient DiLoCo behaves as model size grows is not well characterized.
nodes.approach: Empirical scaling-law fits over replicas, hyperparameters and token budgets under fixed compute.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Scaling-law analysis of a distributed training algorithm; fits several topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Distributed low-communication training scaling is specialised.

nodes.title: CTRL-ALT-DECEIT Sabotage Evaluations for Automated AI R&D
nodes.tldr: Extends MLE-Bench with sabotage and sandbagging tasks to test whether AI agents can undermine ML R&D, and evaluates LM monitors at detecting such behavior.
nodes.problem: Measuring whether frontier AI agents can sabotage, sandbag, or subvert oversight when automating ML engineering.
nodes.approach: Sabotage and sandbagging task suite built on MLE-Bench with LM monitor detection evaluation in Inspect.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: AI control evaluations are an established but specialised safety area.

nodes.title: Activation Control for Efficiently Eliciting Long Chain-of-thought Ability of Language Models
nodes.tldr: Finds a few late-layer activations control long chain-of-thought behavior and proposes training-free activation control to elicit it.
nodes.problem: Eliciting long chain-of-thought reasoning normally needs costly RL or distilled supervised data.
nodes.approach: Amplify contrastively identified activations with analytic functions and wait tokens at inference.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Activation steering for long reasoning is specialised, though increasingly studied.

nodes.title: Depth-Bounds for Neural Networks via the Braid Arrangement
nodes.tldr: Proves a non-constant lower bound on hidden layers for computing the maximum of d numbers with braid-compatible ReLU networks.
nodes.problem: The minimal hidden-layer depth for exactly representing all piecewise linear functions with ReLU networks is an open question.
nodes.approach: Polyhedral combinatorics using the braid fan, with combinatorial proofs for the maximum of 5 numbers.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Braid-fan depth bounds for ReLU networks are a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Among Us: A Sandbox for Measuring and Detecting Agentic Deception
nodes.tldr: Introduces Among Us as a sandbox to measure open-ended LLM agent deception, evaluating 18 models and showing probes and SAE features can detect deception.
nodes.problem: Existing evaluations miss open-ended, long-term deceptive behavior in language agents.
nodes.approach: Social deception game sandbox, evaluate LLMs, train linear probes and SAEs on activations to detect lying.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Deception evaluation in games is established but specialised safety work.

nodes.title: Agnostic Active Learning Is Always Better Than Passive Learning
nodes.tldr: The paper gives optimal query complexity for agnostic active learning across all concept classes, with a leading term always below passive learning's sample complexity.
nodes.problem: Whether agnostic active learning can always beat passive learning was a long-standing open question.
nodes.approach: New general active learning algorithm achieving the minimax first-order query complexity, removing disagreement-coefficient factors.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Agnostic active learning theory is a rare, specialised theory topic.

nodes.title: TransferTraj: A Vehicle Trajectory Learning Model for Region and Task Transferability
nodes.tldr: Learns vehicle GPS trajectories that transfer across regions and tasks without retraining, using a unified masking-and-recovery input-output scheme.
nodes.problem: Trajectory models fail to transfer across regions with different spatial contexts and across tasks with different input-output structures.
nodes.approach: Region-transferable encoder fusing spatial, temporal, POI and road modalities, with a spatial-context mixture of experts.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment call between time-series and spatio-temporal application topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Vehicle trajectory transfer learning is a specialized niche.

nodes.title: Critical Batch Size Revisited: A Simple Empirical Approach to Large-Batch Language Model Training
nodes.tldr: Measures the critical batch size directly during LLM training, showing it grows over training and motivating batch size warmup for large-batch pretraining.
nodes.problem: Critical batch size estimates rely on strong gradient-noise assumptions, limiting trust.
nodes.approach: Empirically measure the critical batch size on OLMo models, then apply batch size warmup.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Common: LLM training efficiency is a mainstream concern.

nodes.title: FFN Fusion: Rethinking Sequential Computation in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: FFN Fusion parallelizes consecutive FFN layers, especially after attention removal, cutting LLM inference latency; applied to Llama-3.1-405B to produce a 253B model.
nodes.problem: Sequential layer computation limits LLM inference latency.
nodes.approach: Identify and fuse sequences of FFN layers into parallel operations with minimal accuracy loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: LLM inference efficiency is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Two Heads are Better than One: Simulating Large Transformers with Small Ones
nodes.tldr: Proves long-input transformers can be simulated by short-input ones, needing only linearly many copies under sliding-window masks and attention sinks.
nodes.problem: Quadratic self-attention cost limits long sequences, while short-sequence hardware is well optimized.
nodes.approach: Theoretical simulation constructions with worst-case and average-case bounds on the number of small transformers.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Simulation-based theory of long-input transformers is rare

nodes.title: MonarchAttention: Zero-Shot Conversion to Fast, Hardware-Aware Structured Attention
nodes.tldr: Approximates softmax attention with Monarch matrices in sub-quadratic time, converting pretrained transformers zero-shot with large GPU speed-ups over FlashAttention-2.
nodes.problem: Attention's quadratic cost in sequence length limits long inputs, and prior fast approximations need retraining.
nodes.approach: Variational optimization projects softmax attention onto Monarch matrices, with hardware-efficient tensor-core kernels.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Structured-matrix attention approximation is specialised

nodes.title: Ambient Proteins - Training Diffusion Models on Noisy Structures
nodes.tldr: Ambient Protein Diffusion treats low-confidence AlphaFold structures as corrupted data, adjusting the diffusion objective per corruption level, improving diversity and designability for long proteins.
nodes.problem: Protein diffusion models are limited by quality of synthetic AlphaFold structures, especially for long proteins.
nodes.approach: Ambient diffusion training with noise-level-dependent objective based on structure confidence.
nodes.niche_reason: Training diffusion on corrupted data for protein design is an uncommon angle.

nodes.title: EvoBrain: Dynamic Multi-Channel EEG Graph Modeling for Time-Evolving Brain Networks
nodes.tldr: Presents EvoBrain, a seizure detector pairing a two-stream Mamba with a Laplacian-encoded GCN over explicitly time-evolving EEG graphs.
