nodes.problem: Detecting and estimating sparse rank-one signals with directional prior information better than plain spectral methods.
nodes.approach: Spectral methods on Y plus diag of nonlinear degree profile; rigorous threshold analysis and designed nonlinearity.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Rare random-matrix and spectral algorithm theory for planted structures.

nodes.title: DICEPTION: A Generalist Diffusion Model for Visual Perceptual Tasks
nodes.tldr: Repurposes a text-to-image diffusion model into a generalist visual perception model that approaches specialist performance with far less data.
nodes.problem: Generalist perception models need robust multi-task capability under limited compute and data.
nodes.approach: Pixel-aligned training that preserves pre-trained diffusion priors, with efficient adaptation to new tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.confidence_reason: generalist perception model built on a diffusion backbone
nodes.niche_reason: diffusion as a generalist perception backbone is less common

nodes.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Characterizes reward hacking under best-of-n inference-time alignment, introduces Best-of-Poisson and HedgeTune to pick optimal parameters that hedge against proxy reward overoptimization.
nodes.problem: Overoptimizing imperfect reward models at inference time degrades true reward.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of BoN, SBoN, and BoP with an algorithm tuning inference-time parameters.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Inference-time alignment theory is specialised.

nodes.title: On the Surprising Effectiveness of Large Learning Rates under Standard Width Scaling
nodes.tldr: Shows that large learning rates under standard parameterization train stably via a controlled divergence regime with a well-defined infinite-width limit.
nodes.problem: Why standard-parameterized networks train stably at large learning rates, contradicting infinite-width theory.
nodes.approach: Finer-grained analysis of the unstable regime under cross-entropy loss, splitting it into two sub-regimes.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Established theory direction, but large-LR standard-parameterization regime is specialised

nodes.title: Scaling can lead to compositional generalization
nodes.tldr: Scaling data and model size alone yields compositional generalization in standard networks, proven for MLPs, with task constituents linearly decodable from hidden activations.
nodes.problem: Whether standard neural networks can systematically generalize over compositional task structure.
nodes.approach: Scaling experiments, approximation proof for MLPs, and linear decoding of task constituents from activations.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Compositionality research is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Reverse Engineering Human Preferences with Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses LLM-judge scores as RL reward to train a preamble generator that boosts downstream judged scores undetectably, exposing LLM-as-a-judge vulnerabilities.
nodes.problem: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation is exploitable by tuning outputs to the judge's preferences.
nodes.approach: RL-train a preamble generator with judge-LLM reward, pipelined with frozen candidate LLMs, transferring across judges.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.confidence_reason: Fits LLM evaluation, alignment, and adversarial attack topics about equally.
nodes.niche_reason: Attacking LLM judges via upstream preambles is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: Horizon Reduction Makes RL Scalable
nodes.tldr: Studies offline RL scalability with datasets 1000x larger, finds poor scaling due to horizon, and shows horizon reduction techniques greatly improve results.
nodes.problem: Offline RL algorithms saturate well below ideal performance as data scales.
nodes.approach: Apply horizon-reduction (n-step, hierarchical) methods and evaluate on huge datasets.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL is common; scaling angle is moderately fresh.

nodes.title: Mitigating Instability in High Residual Adaptive Sampling for PINNs via Langevin Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Shows high-residual adaptive sampling for PINNs needs stricter learning rate bounds and proposes Langevin dynamics-based adaptive sampling that is stable across learning rates and model complexity.
nodes.problem: Residual-based adaptive collocation sampling for PINNs is unstable and neglects medium and low residual points.
nodes.approach: Langevin dynamics-based adaptive sampling (LAS) of collocation points.
nodes.niche_reason: PINN sampling strategies are an established specialised subarea.

nodes.title: Optimal Nuisance Function Tuning for Estimating a Doubly Robust Functional under Proportional Asymptotics
nodes.tldr: Derives asymptotically optimal ridge tuning for nuisance-function estimation of the expected conditional covariance under proportional asymptotics, and compares estimators and sample splitting.
nodes.problem: Choosing nuisance regression tuning parameters when estimating the expected conditional covariance in high dimensions.
nodes.approach: Proportional-asymptotic analysis of ridge-based ECC estimators and sample-splitting strategies.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Highly technical semiparametric statistics rarely seen in ML.

nodes.title: SViMo: Synchronized Diffusion for Video and Motion Generation in Hand-object Interaction Scenarios
nodes.tldr: Jointly generates hand-object interaction video and 3D motion with a synchronized diffusion process that feeds motion back to video, without predefined object models.
nodes.problem: Video generators sacrifice physics, and 3D HOI motion generators rely on predefined objects and lab-captured data.
nodes.approach: Synchronized diffusion with tri-modal adaptive modulation, 3D full attention, and a vision-aware 3D interaction diffusion feedback loop.
nodes.niche_reason: Joint HOI video-motion generation is a specialised cross-modal niche

nodes.title: Uni-LoRA: One Vector is All You Need
nodes.tldr: Unifies LoRA variants as projections from one trainable vector, using an isometric global projection to fine-tune an entire LLM with a single vector.
nodes.problem: Existing LoRA variants limit cross-layer parameter sharing, wasting parameter efficiency.
nodes.approach: Isometric global projection from a d-dimensional subspace to the full LoRA parameter space.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Parameter-efficient LoRA variants are a crowded direction

nodes.title: Boosting Generative Image Modeling via Joint Image-Feature Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Jointly models VAE image latents and DINO semantic features with one diffusion transformer, improving generation quality and training speed, and enabling representation guidance.
nodes.problem: Latent diffusion models do not integrate representation learning with generative modeling in a unified way.
nodes.approach: Diffusion over joint image-latent and self-supervised feature pairs, with a Representation Guidance inference strategy.
nodes.niche_reason: Joint generative and semantic-feature diffusion is a specialised direction.

nodes.title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature reliance through controlled suppression
nodes.tldr: Revisits the texture-bias claim for CNNs with controlled suppression of shape, texture and color cues, finding CNNs rely mainly on local shape, with domain-specific differences.
nodes.problem: The claim that ImageNet CNNs are texture-biased rests on a confounded cue-conflict experiment.
nodes.approach: Domain-agnostic framework suppressing shape, texture, and color cues, evaluated on humans and models across vision domains.
nodes.niche_reason: Shape-texture bias analysis is established but specialised.

nodes.title: To Distill or Decide? Understanding the Algorithmic Trade-off in Partially Observable RL
nodes.tldr: Theoretical and empirical study of when privileged expert distillation beats standard RL in partially observable settings, showing latent stochasticity decides the trade-off.
nodes.problem: When to use privileged expert distillation versus standard RL under partial observability.
nodes.approach: Analyze a perturbed Block MDP contrasting approximate decodability with belief contraction, plus locomotion experiments.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised theory of privileged-information learning in POMDPs.

nodes.title: High-order Equivariant Flow Matching for Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Prediction
nodes.tldr: Generates DFT Hamiltonian matrices from molecular geometry with SE(3)-equivariant flow matching, cutting Hamiltonian error and accelerating SCF convergence.
nodes.problem: Costly iterative SCF in DFT; deterministic regression ignores the structured nature of Hamiltonians.
nodes.approach: Equivariant flow matching learns distributions over Hamiltonians, plus orbital-energy fine-tuning for physical fidelity.
nodes.confidence_reason: Flow-matching method on DFT; primary physics-vs-generative choice is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Flow matching for DFT Hamiltonians is a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Measuring Fingerprints of Web-filtered Text Datasets and Fingerprint Propagation Through Training
nodes.tldr: Shows neural classifiers can identify which web-filtered pretraining corpus a text came from, and that these dataset fingerprints persist into model-generated text.
nodes.problem: Web-filtered LLM pretraining datasets may carry hidden fingerprints that affect generalization.
nodes.approach: Dataset classification experiments on pretraining corpora and on text sampled from models trained on them.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles data attribution and pretraining-data analysis; topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialized analysis of pretraining data artifacts

nodes.title: CoralVQA: A Large-Scale Visual Question Answering Dataset for Coral Reef Image Understanding
nodes.tldr: Introduces CoralVQA, a dataset of 12,805 coral reef images with 277,653 question-answer pairs for benchmarking vision-language models on reef ecology and health.
nodes.problem: No domain-specific VQA dataset exists for coral reef image understanding and conservation.
nodes.approach: Semi-automatic annotation pipeline with marine biologists; benchmark of several LVLMs.
nodes.niche_reason: Coral reef VQA is a very rare application domain.

nodes.title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
nodes.tldr: Finds majority voting, not debate, explains most multi-agent LLM gains; a martingale argument shows debate alone adds no expected correctness.
nodes.problem: Unclear which components of multi-agent debate actually drive LLM performance gains.
nodes.approach: Disentangle voting from debate, model debate as a stochastic martingale process, and test belief-correcting interventions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Debate analysis straddles reasoning and multi-agent LLM topics
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-agent debate analyses are a growing but common topic

nodes.title: Product Distribution Learning with Imperfect Advice
nodes.tldr: Shows product distributions on the Boolean hypercube can be learned with fewer than d/eps^2 samples when given imperfect advice parameters, without knowing advice quality.
nodes.problem: Learning product distributions needs Omega(d/eps^2) samples; can advice about the distribution reduce this?
nodes.approach: Efficient algorithm exploiting advice distribution Q when its mean is close in L1, achieving sublinear dimension dependence.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-augmented distribution learning is a rare theoretical subarea.

nodes.title: CAR-Flow: Condition-Aware Reparameterization Aligns Source and Target for Better Flow Matching
nodes.tldr: CAR-Flow learns a lightweight condition-dependent shift of source and/or target distributions in flow matching, shortening transport paths and improving SiT-XL/2 FID from 2.07 to 1.68.
nodes.problem: Flow models must learn both mass transport and conditional injection
nodes.approach: Learned condition-aware shift reparameterizing source and target distributions
nodes.niche_reason: Flow matching variants for image generation are crowded

nodes.title: EraseFlow: Learning Concept Erasure Policies via GFlowNet-Driven Alignment
nodes.tldr: Frames concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion as GFlowNet trajectory sampling, steering denoising away from target concepts without hand-crafted rewards.
nodes.problem: Concept erasure in text-to-image models degrades quality or relies on brittle losses.
nodes.approach: Trajectory-balance GFlowNet policy over denoising paths that preserves the model prior.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: Concept erasure straddles unlearning/safety and diffusion sampling; GFlowNet angle.
nodes.niche_reason: Concept erasure is active; GFlowNet-based erasure is less common.

nodes.title: BEDLAM2.0: Synthetic humans and cameras in motion
nodes.tldr: BEDLAM2.0 is a synthetic video dataset with diverse humans, clothing, hair, shoes, environments and camera motions, improving world-coordinate 3D human motion estimation.
nodes.problem: Lack of video data with ground truth human and camera motion for world-coordinate human estimation.
nodes.approach: Render richer synthetic humans and moving cameras with ground-truth body parameters and camera paths.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic human datasets are a specialised vision subfield.

nodes.title: Repurposing Marigold for Zero-Shot Metric Depth Estimation via Defocus Blur Cues
nodes.tldr: Turns the pretrained Marigold diffusion depth model into a metric depth predictor at inference time, using defocus blur from two apertures without training.
nodes.problem: Metric depth estimators generalize poorly to out-of-distribution datasets.
nodes.approach: Optimizes metric scaling and diffusion noise latents using a defocus-blur image formation loss.
nodes.niche_reason: Defocus-based metric depth from a diffusion prior is unusual.

nodes.title: Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE
nodes.tldr: Adds orthogonality and variance losses to the MoE auxiliary balancing loss to improve expert specialization and routing discriminativeness without architectural changes.
nodes.problem: Auxiliary load-balancing loss causes expert overlap and uniform routing, hindering specialization.
nodes.approach: Orthogonality loss on experts plus variance loss on routing, combined with the existing auxiliary loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: MoE routing and balancing variants are a common topic.

nodes.title: Gaussian Herding across Pens: An Optimal Transport Perspective on Global Gaussian Reduction for 3DGS
nodes.tldr: Casts 3D Gaussian splatting compaction as global Gaussian mixture reduction via optimal transport, retaining quality with only 10% of Gaussians and beating prior compaction methods.
nodes.problem: 3DGS needs millions of redundant Gaussians; heuristic pruning lacks global fidelity guarantees.
nodes.approach: Minimize composite transport divergence over a KD-tree partition, then fine-tune color and opacity.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Optimal-transport view of 3DGS compaction is somewhat distinctive.

nodes.title: Wider or Deeper? Scaling LLM Inference-Time Compute with Adaptive Branching Tree Search
nodes.tldr: Proposes AB-MCTS, a tree search that decides adaptively whether to sample new LLM responses or refine existing ones using external feedback, beating repeated sampling.
nodes.problem: Repeated sampling for LLM reasoning ignores external feedback that could refine candidate solutions.
nodes.approach: Adaptive branching Monte Carlo tree search that chooses between wider expansion and deeper revisiting.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Inference-time search for LLMs is a crowded direction

nodes.title: The emergence of sparse attention: impact of data distribution and benefits of repetition
nodes.tldr: Explains when sparse attention emerges in training: timing follows power laws in task, architecture and optimizer, and repetition speeds it up.
nodes.problem: Sparse attention emergence during training lacks a principled explanation.
nodes.approach: Toy-model theory plus small-Transformer experiments on linear regression and associative recall.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Power-law emergence timing of sparse attention is an uncommon theory-plus-experiment angle.

nodes.title: Robust Neural Rendering in the Wild with Asymmetric Dual 3D Gaussian Splatting
nodes.tldr: Trains two Gaussian Splatting models in parallel with a consistency constraint and asymmetric masks, suppressing run-specific artifacts when reconstructing scenes from in-the-wild photos.
nodes.problem: In-the-wild photos have lighting changes and transient distractors that cause unstable 3D reconstructions.
nodes.approach: Two 3DGS models with divergent complementary masks and a dynamic EMA proxy variant for efficiency.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: In-the-wild 3DGS reconstruction is an active, common direction.

nodes.title: SAGE: A Unified Framework for Generalizable Object State Recognition with State-Action Graph Embedding
nodes.tldr: SAGE builds an LLM-generated state-action graph refined with vision-language models to recognize object states and transitions in video, generalizing to unseen objects and actions.
nodes.problem: Recognizing object physical states and transformations in video generalizes poorly to unseen actions and objects.
nodes.approach: LLM-built State-Action Graph embeddings multimodally refined with VLMs, decomposing states into shareable language-described concepts.
nodes.niche_reason: Object state recognition in video is a rare subtask.

nodes.title: AceSearcher: Bootstrapping Reasoning and Search for LLMs via Reinforced Self-Play
nodes.tldr: AceSearcher trains one LLM via cooperative self-play to alternate between decomposing queries and solving with retrieved context, using SFT then reinforcement fine-tuning on final-answer accuracy.
nodes.problem: Search-augmented LLMs struggle with multi-hop retrieval and complex reasoning without intermediate annotations.
nodes.approach: Self-play with decomposer and solver roles, SFT on mixed tasks plus reinforcement fine-tuning on answer correctness.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Search-augmented reasoning with RL is a currently crowded direction.

nodes.title: Generalized Top-k Mallows Model for Ranked Choices
nodes.tldr: Provides sampling, efficient choice probability computation, and active parameter learning for the generalized top-k Mallows ranking model, with analysis and comparison to multinomial logit.
nodes.problem: Classic Mallows model poorly captures users who only rank a few preferred items.
nodes.approach: Novel sampling scheme, efficient choice probability algorithm, and active learning estimator for generalized top-k Mallows.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Ranking distribution models for choice modelling are very rare.

nodes.title: TabArena: A Living Benchmark for Machine Learning on Tabular Data
nodes.tldr: Launches a continuously maintained tabular ML benchmark with curated datasets, models, a public leaderboard, and maintenance protocols.
nodes.problem: Static tabular benchmarks go stale as flaws are found and new models appear.
nodes.approach: Large-scale benchmarking with hyperparameter ensembling and validation-method analysis, plus a public living leaderboard.
nodes.niche_reason: tabular benchmark infrastructure, specialised

nodes.title: Improving Bilinear RNN with Closed-loop Control
nodes.tldr: Proposes Comba, a bilinear RNN with scalar-plus-low-rank state transitions and closed-loop state and output feedback, with a hardware-efficient Triton kernel.
nodes.problem: Delta-rule bilinear RNNs lack a principled analysis of their advantages and limitations.
nodes.approach: Closed-loop control theory applied to recurrent state transitions, with feedback corrections.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Closed-loop control view of bilinear RNNs is specialised

nodes.title: DisMo: Disentangled Motion Representations for Open-World Motion Transfer
nodes.tldr: DisMo learns appearance-independent motion representations from raw video, enabling open-world motion transfer between unrelated entities, pluggable into video generators and strong in zero-shot action classification.
nodes.problem: Video generators lack explicit motion representations separate from content, limiting motion transfer.
nodes.approach: Image-space reconstruction objective learning abstract motion embeddings, attached to video models via lightweight adapters.
nodes.niche_reason: Content-independent motion representations for open-world transfer are rare.

nodes.title: T-REGS: Minimum Spanning Tree Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
nodes.tldr: T-REGS regularizes self-supervised representations with minimum spanning tree length, provably reducing dimensional collapse and promoting uniformity on Riemannian manifolds.
nodes.problem: Dimensional collapse and non-uniform distributions in self-supervised representations
nodes.approach: Regularizer based on minimum spanning tree length of the embeddings
nodes.niche_reason: Topological/geometric regularizer is a specialised take on SSL

nodes.title: Deep Compositional Phase Diffusion for Long Motion Sequence Generation
nodes.tldr: Compositional Phase Diffusion uses semantic and transitional phase modules in a motion phase autoencoder latent space to generate long, smoothly transitioning motion sequences and enable inbetweening.
nodes.problem: Abrupt transitions when composing multiple semantically generated motion clips into long sequences.
nodes.approach: Diffusion modules operating in a phase-based latent frequency space of a pretrained motion phase autoencoder.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Text-to-motion is established; phase-space composition is specialised.

nodes.title: KARMA: Leveraging Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Knowledge Graph Enrichment
nodes.tldr: Nine collaborative LLM agents extract entities and relations from literature, align them to a schema, and resolve conflicts to enrich knowledge graphs.
nodes.problem: Manual knowledge graph curation cannot keep pace with the growth of scientific literature.
nodes.approach: Multi-agent LLM pipeline that iteratively parses documents, verifies extracted facts, and integrates them under domain schema.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Knowledge Graphs & Relational Learning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-based KG construction is an active, growing area.

nodes.title: Integration Matters for Learning PDEs with Backwards SDEs
nodes.tldr: Shows Euler-Maruyama discretization bias hurts BSDE-based PDE solvers and fixes it with a Stratonovich formulation integrated by stochastic Heun, matching PINN performance.
nodes.problem: BSDE-based deep PDE solvers underperform PINNs due to discretization bias.
nodes.approach: Stratonovich BSDE formulation with stochastic Heun integration removes the Euler-Maruyama bias.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Method for PDE solvers with SDE/stochastic control flavor; topic fits several areas.
nodes.niche_reason: BSDE-based PDE solvers are a rare numerical niche.

nodes.title: Right Question is Already Half the Answer: Fully Unsupervised LLM Reasoning Incentivization
nodes.tldr: Improves LLM reasoning without any labels by minimizing semantic entropy on unlabeled questions, reaching competitive accuracy gains on math and MMLU-Pro.
nodes.problem: Reasoning RL for LLMs usually needs supervised traces, verified answers, or reward models.
nodes.approach: Entropy Minimized Policy Optimization: minimize semantic entropy of model answers on unlabeled questions.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Label-free RL for LLM reasoning is a crowded area

nodes.title: ConTextTab: A Semantics-Aware Tabular In-Context Learner
nodes.tldr: ConTextTab is a table-native in-context learner using modality-specific embeddings and real-world tabular training data to add semantic awareness, setting a new standard on CARTE.
nodes.problem: Table-native ICL models trained on synthetic data lack semantics, while LLM-based tabular models handle little context.
nodes.approach: Table-native ICL architecture with specialized data-modality embeddings trained on large real-world tables.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Tabular foundation models are specialised but increasingly established.

nodes.title: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
nodes.tldr: AI-Researcher is an autonomous LLM agent system covering literature review, hypothesis, implementation and paper writing, evaluated on the new Scientist-Bench benchmark.
nodes.problem: Automating the full scientific research pipeline with LLM agents and evaluating autonomous research quality.
nodes.approach: Multi-stage agent framework plus Scientist-Bench of paper-derived guided and open-ended innovation tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.confidence_reason: System plus benchmark; agents versus scientific discovery is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: AI-scientist systems are active but still specialised.

nodes.title: Not All Data are Good Labels: On the Self-supervised Labeling for Time Series Forecasting
nodes.tldr: SCAM re-labels time series training data with pseudo labels from a reconstruction network using adaptive masking and spectral norm regularization, improving forecasting generalization.
nodes.problem: Forecasting models underuse available data and overfit noisy labels.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised pseudo-label replacement via adaptive-mask self-correction plus spectral norm regularization.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Label refinement for forecasting is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Target Stochasticity
nodes.tldr: Shows the closed-form and stochastic flow matching losses give nearly equal results in high dimensions, ruling out target stochasticity as the source of generalization.
nodes.problem: Understanding why flow matching and diffusion models generalize, specifically whether loss stochasticity matters.
nodes.approach: Empirical comparison of closed-form versus stochastic conditional flow matching loss on standard image datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Generalization theory of flow matching is specialised but active.

nodes.title: 3D Equivariant Visuomotor Policy Learning via Spherical Projection
nodes.tldr: Image-to-Sphere Policy lifts RGB camera features onto a sphere to get SO(3)-equivariant diffusion policies without point clouds, improving data efficiency.
nodes.problem: Equivariant diffusion policies need multi-camera point clouds, incompatible with eye-in-hand RGB cameras.
nodes.approach: Project 2D RGB features onto a sphere so SO(3) symmetries are modelled without reconstruction.
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariant monocular-RGB policies are a specialised extension of diffusion policy

nodes.title: Improving LLM General Preference Alignment via Optimistic Online Mirror Descent
nodes.tldr: Casts LLM alignment under general preferences as a two-player game and uses optimistic online mirror descent to reach Nash policies with improved convergence rates.
nodes.problem: Aligning LLMs without assuming the Bradley-Terry reward model, under general preferences.
nodes.approach: Optimistic online mirror descent in a two-player preference game, with O(1/T) duality gap and last-iterate linear convergence.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Preference alignment is crowded, though game-theoretic angle is less so.

nodes.title: Purifying Shampoo: Investigating Shampoo's Heuristics by Decomposing its Preconditioner
nodes.tldr: Analyzes Shampoo's heuristics by decomposing its preconditioner into eigenvalues and eigenbasis, removing learning-rate grafting and proposing an adaptive eigenbasis update frequency criterion.
nodes.problem: Shampoo relies on unjustified heuristics such as grafting and stale preconditioning.
nodes.approach: Frobenius-norm view versus full-matrix Adam, decouple eigenvalue and eigenbasis updates, adaptive QR-based criterion.
nodes.niche_reason: Second-order neural optimizers are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Generating Informative Samples for Risk-Averse Fine-Tuning of Downstream Tasks
nodes.tldr: Uses a diffusion model guided toward high-loss inputs to synthesize samples that make CVaR risk-averse training more stable.
nodes.problem: Estimating CVaR tail risk needs rare high-loss samples that are hard to observe.
nodes.approach: Score-based diffusion sampling from a loss-reweighted distribution with importance-weighted training.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Could fit synthetic data, risk optimization, or diffusion; chose data synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: Risk-averse fine-tuning with generated tail samples is specialised

nodes.title: SoFar: Language-Grounded Orientation Bridges Spatial Reasoning and Object Manipulation
nodes.tldr: Defines language-based semantic object orientation and uses it in VLM agents for zero-shot 6-DoF spatial reasoning and robot manipulation.
nodes.problem: Spatial reasoning ignores object orientation, which matters for fine-grained 6-DoF manipulation.
nodes.approach: Reference-frame-free orientation described in language, a 300K-object dataset, and a point-cloud orientation predictor.
nodes.niche_reason: Language-defined object orientation is a rare framing

nodes.title: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
nodes.tldr: Argues representation superposition drives neural scaling: under strong superposition loss scales inversely with model dimension, consistent with open LLMs and Chinchilla scaling laws.
nodes.problem: The origin of power-law neural scaling of loss with model size is unclear.
nodes.approach: Toy model with weight decay controlling superposition, comparing weak and strong regimes against real LLMs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.confidence_reason: Could also fit interpretability or deep learning theory.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic explanations of scaling laws are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Representation Entanglement for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers Is Much Easier Than You Think
nodes.tldr: Entangles image latents with one class token from a pretrained foundation model during diffusion-transformer denoising, speeding training and improving generation at negligible cost.
nodes.problem: External representation alignment is absent at inference, underusing discriminative features in diffusion training.
nodes.approach: Denoise a single extra class token jointly with image latents, reconstructing both at inference.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion transformer training is crowded; representation-alignment variant.

nodes.title: Object-centric 3D Motion Field for Robot Learning from Human Videos
nodes.tldr: Represents actions as an object-centric 3D motion field extracted from human videos with a denoising estimator, enabling zero-shot robot control with cross-embodiment transfer.
nodes.problem: Learning robot policies from human videos needs an action representation that is both informative and tractable.
nodes.approach: Denoising 3D motion-field estimator trained on noisy depth, and dense object-centric motion-field prediction for policies.
nodes.confidence_reason: Perception representation vs. robot policy learning is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Learning from human videos is growing but still specialised

nodes.title: FP4 All the Way: Fully Quantized Training of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: First fully quantized LLM training in mostly FP4, using NVFP4 and stochastic rounding; a 7B model trained on 200B tokens matches BF16.
nodes.problem: Training large language models fully in 4-bit precision without losing quality.
nodes.approach: NVFP4 block-scaled format, stochastic rounding in backward/update, round-to-nearest forward, plus a gradient-to-noise threshold analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Quantization is common, though FP4 training is somewhat new.

nodes.title: Discrete Spatial Diffusion: Intensity-Preserving Diffusion Modeling
nodes.tldr: Diffusion via a discrete-state jump process that conserves particle counts exactly, applied to images, porous rock and battery electrode microstructures.
nodes.problem: Standard continuous diffusion cannot preserve discrete quantities and conservation laws like mass in scientific data.
nodes.approach: Continuous-time discrete-state spatial jump process with exact intensity conservation in forward and reverse processes.
nodes.niche_reason: Conservation-preserving discrete diffusion for scientific images is rare.

nodes.title: ModHiFi: Identifying High Fidelity predictive components for Model Modification
nodes.tldr: Selects components by a subset-fidelity score so pruning and class unlearning need no training data or loss, with speedups on ImageNet models.
nodes.problem: Modifying trained models for pruning or unlearning without data or the loss function
nodes.approach: Subset Fidelity score on locally reconstructive component subsets, optimal for uncorrelated features
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Data-free pruning and unlearning is specialised

nodes.title: VoxDet: Rethinking 3D Semantic Scene Completion as Dense Object Detection
nodes.tldr: Reframes 3D semantic scene completion as dense object detection by converting voxel class labels into instance-level offset labels, reaching top SemanticKITTI results.
nodes.problem: Voxel-wise segmentation formulations of scene completion neglect instance-level discriminability.
nodes.approach: Training-free voxel-to-instance offset labels, decoupled offset regression and semantic prediction in a dense detection framework.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised 3D scene completion task.

nodes.title: Estimating cognitive biases with attention-aware inverse planning
nodes.tldr: Formalizes attention-aware inverse planning to infer people's attentional biases from behavior, combining deep RL with cognitive modeling on driving scenarios.
nodes.problem: Autonomous systems that interact with people need to estimate human cognitive biases, which standard inverse RL ignores.
nodes.approach: Combine deep RL agents with computational cognitive models to infer attention strategies from Waymo driving scenarios.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Inferring attentional biases via inverse planning is a rare cognitive-modeling angle.

nodes.title: Shift Before You Learn: Enabling Low-Rank Representations in Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows the shifted successor measure, not the raw one, is approximately low-rank, giving finite-sample guarantees and improved goal-conditioned RL.
nodes.problem: Low-rank assumptions about the successor measure in RL are often unjustified.
nodes.approach: Shifted successor measure low-rank estimation with Type II Poincaré inequalities for spectral recoverability.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory-heavy; topic straddles RL theory and representation learning
nodes.niche_reason: Low-rank structure of shifted successor measures is a rare niche

nodes.title: E2Former: An Efficient and Equivariant Transformer with Linear-Scaling Tensor Products
nodes.tldr: An equivariant transformer using Wigner 6j convolution moves tensor-product cost from edges to nodes, giving linear scaling and 7x-30x speedups over SO(3) convolutions.
nodes.problem: High cost of spherical tensor products in equivariant networks for large molecular systems.
nodes.approach: Wigner 6j convolution shifts computation from edges to nodes while preserving rotational equivariance.
nodes.confidence_reason: Between graph neural networks and molecular science application.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised equivariant tensor-product efficiency for molecular systems.

nodes.title: Approximate Domain Unlearning for Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces Approximate Domain Unlearning, which lowers VLM recognition for specified image domains such as illustrations while keeping accuracy on other domains like real photos.
nodes.problem: Pretrained VLMs generalize across domains too well, so domain-specific knowledge cannot be removed by class unlearning.
nodes.approach: Explicitly disentangles domain distributions in feature space and adaptively captures instance-specific domain information.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: VLM unlearning is active; domain-level forgetting is specialised

nodes.title: Mulberry: Empowering MLLM with o1-like Reasoning and Reflection via Collective Monte Carlo Tree Search
nodes.tldr: Mulberry trains multimodal LLMs for o1-like reasoning and reflection using Collective Monte Carlo Tree Search across multiple models to build the Mulberry-260k reasoning-tree dataset.
nodes.problem: Teaching MLLMs to generate step-by-step reasoning with reflection.
nodes.approach: Collective MCTS with multiple models for reasoning-path search, then collective SFT on resulting trees.
nodes.niche_reason: Reasoning MLLMs via search and SFT are very crowded.

nodes.title: Towards Comprehensive Scene Understanding: Integrating First and Third-Person Views for LVLMs
nodes.tldr: Adds exocentric views to egocentric inputs for LVLMs, with a new 4K-QA multi-view benchmark and M3CoT, a training-free prompting method fusing scene graphs.
nodes.problem: Narrow egocentric views lack global context, causing LVLM failures on spatial queries.
nodes.approach: Training-free prompting that builds a unified scene representation from three perspectives' scene graphs.
nodes.niche_reason: Ego-exo multi-view VLM reasoning is an emerging niche

nodes.title: Caption This, Reason That: VLMs Caught in the Middle
nodes.tldr: Analyzes VLMs along perception, attention and memory axes, finding that reasoning over self-generated captions improves weak visual reasoning, and tests targeted fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Why VLMs fail at counting and relational visual reasoning
nodes.approach: Cognitive-science task suite, vision-text decoupling analysis and targeted fine-tuning
nodes.niche_reason: VLM evaluation and reasoning analyses are very common

nodes.title: Task-Optimized Convolutional Recurrent Networks Align with Tactile Processing in the Rodent Brain
nodes.tldr: Task-optimized convolutional recurrent networks in an Encoder-Attender-Decoder framework match rodent somatosensory cortex responses to whisker tactile input, with self-supervised models fitting as well as supervised.
nodes.problem: Tactile processing is poorly understood in neuroscience and weak in artificial systems.
nodes.approach: Compare temporal architectures trained on simulated whisker-array inputs against neural data; test contrastive self-supervision.
nodes.niche_reason: Rodent whisker tactile neural modeling is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: DeCaFlow: A deconfounding causal generative model
nodes.tldr: DeCaFlow is a causal generative model trained once on observational data and a causal graph, answering any identifiable interventional or counterfactual query despite hidden confounders.
nodes.problem: Accurate causal inference on continuous variables under hidden confounding from only observational data and a causal graph.
nodes.approach: Deconfounding causal normalizing-flow-style generative model using proxy variables, with identifiability proofs for interventional and counterfactual queries.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised causal inference with latent confounders; established subfield.

nodes.title: Self Forcing: Bridging the Train-Test Gap in Autoregressive Video Diffusion
nodes.tldr: Trains autoregressive video diffusion by rolling out self-generated frames during training with a video-level loss, enabling real-time streaming generation.
nodes.problem: Exposure bias: video models trained on ground-truth context fail on their own imperfect outputs.
nodes.approach: Autoregressive rollout with KV caching during training, video-level loss, rolling KV cache for extrapolation.
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive video diffusion is a busy area but exposure-bias rollout is specific.

nodes.title: Ridge Boosting is Both Robust and Efficient
nodes.tldr: A single kernel ridge boosting step on any initial predictor is both multiaccurate under RKHS-bounded distribution shifts and semiparametrically efficient per target.
nodes.problem: Estimators typically trade off statistical efficiency against robustness to distribution shift.
nodes.approach: One boosting step with kernel ridge regression, analyzed for bias and semiparametric efficiency.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Bridges semiparametric statistics and multiaccuracy, which is rare.

nodes.title: Machine Unlearning Doesn't Do What You Think: Lessons for Generative AI Policy and Research
nodes.tldr: Argues machine unlearning cannot serve as a general-purpose fix for removing or suppressing information in generative models, identifying mismatches between unlearning goals and feasible implementations.
nodes.problem: Unlearning is proposed for privacy, copyright and safety but its goals and feasible methods mismatch.
nodes.approach: Conceptual framework analyzing targeted information removal versus output suppression for researchers and policymakers.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Policy-oriented critique of an established subarea.

nodes.title: Gradient-Variation Online Adaptivity for Accelerated Optimization with Hölder Smoothness
nodes.tldr: Gradient-variation online learning for Holder-smooth functions that adapts without knowing smoothness, yielding universal accelerated offline optimization.
nodes.problem: Acceleration and universality under unknown Holder smoothness in online and offline convex optimization.
nodes.approach: Parameter-free gradient-variation regret algorithm plus online-to-batch conversion and guess-and-check detection.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Holder-smooth universal acceleration is rare

nodes.title: AgentBreeder: Mitigating the AI Safety Risks of Multi-Agent Scaffolds via Self-Improvement
nodes.tldr: AgentBreeder uses multi-objective evolutionary search over multi-agent scaffolds, raising safety benchmark scores 79.4% while keeping capability, and exposing weak scaffolds that emerge alongside capability gains.
nodes.problem: Multi-agent LLM scaffolds boost capability, but their safety impact is largely unexplored.
nodes.approach: Self-improving evolutionary search over scaffolds under multi-objective safety and capability scoring.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Scaffold safety via evolutionary search is specialised but active

nodes.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.tldr: Hierarchical three-tier graph memory for LLM multi-agent systems that retrieves cross-trial insights and collaboration trajectories, letting agent teams evolve without modifying their frameworks.
nodes.problem: Multi-agent LLM systems have simplistic memory that ignores inter-agent collaboration trajectories.
nodes.approach: Three-tier insight, query, and interaction graph memory with bi-directional traversal for retrieval.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Hierarchical memory for multi-agent LLM teams is specialised

nodes.title: ShapeLLM-Omni: A Native Multimodal LLM for 3D Generation and Understanding
nodes.tldr: A native 3D-aware multimodal LLM that understands and generates 3D shapes and text, built on discrete 3D tokens and a new instruction dataset.
nodes.problem: Multimodal LLMs handle images and text but lack native 3D understanding and generation.
nodes.approach: 3D VQ-VAE discrete tokens, then instruction fine-tuning of Qwen-2.5-VL on 3D-Alpaca.
nodes.niche_reason: Native 3D-generative MLLMs are a rare direction.

nodes.title: From Shortcut to Induction Head: How Data Diversity Shapes Algorithm Selection in Transformers
nodes.tldr: Proves that data diversity decides whether a one-layer transformer learns an induction head that generalizes or a positional shortcut that fails out of distribution.
nodes.problem: Pretraining data choice determines whether transformers learn generalizable algorithms or positional shortcuts.
nodes.approach: Gradient-training analysis of a single-layer transformer on trigger-copy tasks, using a max-sum distance ratio.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of induction head emergence from data diversity is rare

nodes.title: Orient Anything V2: Unifying Orientation and Rotation Understanding
nodes.tldr: Foundation model estimating 3D object orientation and relative rotation from one or two images, handling rotational symmetries.
nodes.problem: Orientation estimators assume a single front face and cannot handle symmetric objects or relative rotation.
nodes.approach: Synthetic 3D assets from generative models, model-in-the-loop front-face annotation, periodic distribution loss, multi-frame rotation head.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: orientation estimation is a common vision task

nodes.title: Principled Data Augmentation for Learning to Solve Quadratic Programming Problems
nodes.tldr: Augments quadratic programs with optimality-preserving transformations and pretrains MPNNs contrastively, improving learning-to-optimize in data-scarce settings.
nodes.problem: Robust MPNN learning-to-optimize for quadratic programs struggles with scarce training data.
nodes.approach: Optimality-preserving data augmentation for QPs, plus contrastive pretraining of MPNNs with augmented instances.
nodes.confidence_reason: Learning-to-optimize for QPs; GNN and contrastive aspects also apply
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-to-optimize for quadratic programs is a niche combinatorial angle

nodes.title: GenColor: Generative and Expressive Color Enhancement with Pixel-Perfect Texture Preservation
nodes.tldr: GenColor combines ControlNet-based diffusion with a color-transfer network for expressive color enhancement with pixel-perfect texture preservation, trained on a new 1.2M photo dataset.
nodes.problem: Photo color enhancement needs expressiveness, adaptability, and texture preservation simultaneously.
nodes.approach: Conditional diffusion generates color reference, then a color-transfer network with texture-aware degradation transfers it.
nodes.niche_reason: Photo color enhancement is a specialised image-editing niche.

nodes.title: Bipolar Self-attention for Spiking Transformers
nodes.tldr: Replaces spiking self-attention with a bipolar, spike-driven formulation using ternary matrix products and a shift-based softmax, narrowing the gap to ANN transformers.
nodes.problem: Spiking transformers lag ANN transformers because binary spikes limit attention expressivity.
nodes.approach: Ternary matrix multiplication captures bipolar membrane interactions; shift-based Softmax keeps attention normalized.
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking transformers with bipolar attention are a rare direction

nodes.title: Variational Learning Finds Flatter Solutions at the Edge of Stability
nodes.tldr: Shows variational learning finds flatter solutions than gradient descent at the edge of stability, controlled by posterior shape and sample count.
nodes.problem: Implicit regularization of variational learning is unexplained for deep networks.
nodes.approach: Edge-of-stability analysis on a quadratic model, extended to deep networks; empirical checks on ResNet and ViT.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Edge-of-stability analysis of variational learning is specialised

nodes.title: Minimax Adaptive Online Nonparametric Regression over Besov spaces
nodes.tldr: Adaptive wavelet-based algorithm for online adversarial regression over Besov spaces, achieving minimax-optimal regret without knowing smoothness parameters, with a locally adaptive extension.
nodes.problem: Online regression against irregular comparator functions without knowing their smoothness in Besov classes.
nodes.approach: Adaptive wavelet predictor with minimax regret bounds and locally adaptive resolution over time and space.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Wavelet-based online regression over Besov spaces is highly specialised theory.

nodes.title: Hamiltonian Descent Algorithms for Optimization: Accelerated Rates via Randomized Integration Time
nodes.tldr: Randomizing the integration time of Hamiltonian flow for optimization yields accelerated convergence rates matching Nesterov's method in continuous and discrete time.
nodes.problem: Whether Hamiltonian dynamics with velocity resets can achieve accelerated optimization rates.
nodes.approach: Randomized Hamiltonian flow and discrete randomized Hamiltonian gradient descent with accelerated-rate proofs.
nodes.niche_reason: Hamiltonian dynamics for optimization is a rare theory direction.

nodes.title: What One Cannot, Two Can: Two-Layer Transformers Provably Represent Induction Heads on Any-Order Markov Chains
nodes.tldr: Proves a two-layer, single-head-per-layer transformer can represent induction heads for any k-th order Markov chain, and analyzes learning dynamics in the first-order case.
nodes.problem: Whether two-layer transformers can represent conditional k-grams for higher-order Markov sources.
nodes.approach: Explicit two-layer construction plus learning dynamics analysis of a simplified first-order variant.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Transformer ICL theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
nodes.tldr: Absolute Zero trains one model to propose and solve its own code-reasoning tasks, verified by a code executor, matching strong baselines without human data.
nodes.problem: RLVR for reasoning still relies on human-curated question-answer data, which is scarce and may limit scaling.
nodes.approach: Self-play where the model proposes verifiable code tasks maximizing learning progress, validated and answered via code execution.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RLVR for reasoning is crowded; the zero-data self-play angle is moderately novel.

nodes.title: Adaptive Prediction-Powered AutoEval with Reliability and Efficiency Guarantees
nodes.tldr: R-AutoEval+ adaptively tunes reliance on LLM-judge synthetic data in prediction-powered inference, giving finite-sample reliability and never-worse sample efficiency for model evaluation.
nodes.problem: Autoevaluators bias model evaluation and can lose sample efficiency versus real data
nodes.approach: Adaptive evaluation variable in prediction-powered inference with game-theoretic statistical guarantees
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical guarantees for LLM-judge evaluation are rare

nodes.title: A Unified Solution to Video Fusion: From Multi-Frame Learning to Benchmarking
nodes.tldr: Unified multi-frame video fusion framework with optical-flow feature warping for temporally consistent results, plus a benchmark covering four fusion tasks.
nodes.problem: Per-frame image fusion causes flicker and temporal inconsistency in videos, with no unified video fusion benchmark.
nodes.approach: Multi-frame learning with optical-flow-based feature warping across frames, evaluated with joint spatial and temporal consistency metrics.
nodes.niche_reason: Video fusion is a specialised low-level vision niche.

nodes.title: Geometry Meets Incentives: Sample-Efficient Incentivized Exploration with Linear Contexts
nodes.tldr: Shows incentivized exploration with linear bandits in Euclidean balls needs only polynomial initial samples, so incentive compatibility and regret-optimality can coexist.
nodes.problem: High-dimensional incentivized exploration needs exponential initial samples for incentive compatibility.
nodes.approach: Incentive-compatible exploration algorithm exploiting geometry of Euclidean unit-ball action sets.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Narrow intersection of mechanism design and bandit exploration

nodes.title: Unifying Proportional Fairness in Centroid and Non-Centroid Clustering
nodes.tldr: Semi-centroid clustering combines centroid and non-centroid losses, and a polynomial-time algorithm achieves a constant approximation to the core fairness criterion.
nodes.problem: Proportional fairness in clustering has been studied only in separate centroid and non-centroid settings.
nodes.approach: Unified loss paradigm and a polynomial-time algorithm for approximate core, plus improved FJR bounds.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Fair clustering versus social choice placement is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Proportional fairness in clustering is a rare, cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: When Worse is Better: Navigating the Compression Generation Trade-off In Visual Tokenization
nodes.tldr: Scaling laws show more compressed visual tokenizer latents can help small autoregressive generators; Causally Regularized Tokenization makes tokens easier to model.
nodes.problem: Trade-off between tokenizer compression and reconstruction versus ease of learning for the stage-2 generative model.
nodes.approach: Scaling-law study of tokenizer rate-distortion plus causal regularization of stage-1 latents.
nodes.niche_reason: Tokenizer design for AR image generation is active but specialised.

nodes.title: SANSA: Unleashing the Hidden Semantics in SAM2 for Few-Shot Segmentation
nodes.tldr: Repurposes SAM2 for few-shot segmentation by exposing its latent semantic structure, with minimal modifications, achieving state-of-the-art on generalization benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Few-shot segmentation needs semantic matching, but SAM2 features are entangled with tracking cues.
nodes.approach: Expose SAM2's latent semantic structure with minimal task-specific modifications for few-shot segmentation.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Segment Anything adaptation is a crowded direction

nodes.title: Learning the Wrong Lessons: Syntactic-Domain Spurious Correlations in Language Models
nodes.tldr: Shows LLMs learn spurious syntax-domain correlations that can degrade knowledge tasks and bypass refusals, and provides a detection framework.
nodes.problem: Models may learn spurious syntax-domain associations that override semantics and enable jailbreaks.
nodes.approach: Synthetic training data plus an evaluation framework that detects syntax-domain correlations in trained models.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Analysis paper; fits interpretability and safety topics about equally.
nodes.niche_reason: Syntax-domain spurious correlations in LLMs are a specialised analysis niche.

nodes.title: Adaptive Surrogate Gradients for Sequential Reinforcement Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Shows surrogate gradient slope choice matters for spiking-network RL and trains a drone position controller using a privileged guiding policy.
nodes.problem: Spiking networks need surrogate gradients and long sequences, which hinder RL control training.
nodes.approach: Adaptive surrogate slope schedule plus bootstrapping from a privileged guiding policy during online RL.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking-network RL for real robot control is very rare

nodes.title: Uni-MuMER: Unified Multi-Task Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Model for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
nodes.tldr: Uni-MuMER fully fine-tunes a vision-language model for handwritten math expression recognition with tree-aware chain-of-thought, error-driven learning and symbol counting, surpassing specialized models and Gemini.
nodes.problem: Handwritten math expression recognition suffers from isolated architectural tweaks and free symbol layouts.
nodes.approach: Multi-task fine-tuning of a VLM with Tree-CoT, Error-Driven Learning, and Symbol Counting data tasks.
nodes.niche_reason: Handwritten math expression recognition is a rare vision-language niche.

nodes.title: Neptune-X: Active X-to-Maritime Generation for Universal Maritime Object Detection
nodes.tldr: Neptune-X generates diverse maritime scenes with a multi-modality-conditioned model and actively selects synthetic samples by task relevance to improve maritime object detection.
nodes.problem: Scarce annotated maritime data and poor generalization across maritime attributes in detection.
nodes.approach: X-to-Maritime generative model with bidirectional object-water attention and attribute-correlated active sampling, plus a new dataset.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Combines synthetic data generation, selection, and detection; primary topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Maritime imagery is a rare application domain.

nodes.title: MokA: Multimodal Low-Rank Adaptation for MLLMs
nodes.tldr: MokA is a multimodal-aware LoRA variant using modality-specific unimodal parameters plus explicit cross-modal interaction for fine-tuning multimodal LLMs.
nodes.problem: LLM-derived parameter-efficient fine-tuning ignores multimodal characteristics and underuses all modalities in MLLMs.
nodes.approach: Low-rank adaptation with modality-specific compression matrices and cross-modal adaptation component.
nodes.niche_reason: LoRA variants for MLLMs are a crowded area.

nodes.title: Return of ChebNet: Understanding and Improving an Overlooked GNN on Long Range Tasks
nodes.tldr: Stable-ChebNet revisits the spectral ChebNet GNN, stabilizes its training as a non-dissipative dynamical system, and gains strong long-range graph performance.
nodes.problem: Message passing GNNs struggle to capture long-range node dependencies.
nodes.approach: Cast ChebNet polynomial filtering as a stable dynamical system, avoiding eigendecomposition and rewiring.
nodes.niche_reason: Long-range GNN work is common; a ChebNet revisit is less so.

nodes.title: Enhancing Contrastive Learning with Variable Similarity
nodes.tldr: Contrastive learning with variable similarity targets that decrease as augmentation strength increases, fixing misguided invariance assumptions for strongly augmented positives; gains on ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1k.
nodes.problem: Strong augmentations can distort semantics, making fixed-positive-pair invariance misleading in contrastive learning.
nodes.approach: Adjust positive-pair similarity by augmentation extent, with theoretical generalization justification.
nodes.niche_reason: Contrastive learning variants are common.

nodes.title: Torch-Uncertainty: Deep Learning Uncertainty Quantification
nodes.tldr: Introduces Torch-Uncertainty, a PyTorch and Lightning framework for training and benchmarking deep networks with uncertainty quantification methods across classification, segmentation and regression.
nodes.problem: No unified tool exists to train and evaluate deep networks with diverse uncertainty quantification methods.
nodes.approach: Modular library that wraps UQ methods around standard training loops, with benchmarks across tasks.
nodes.niche_reason: UQ is established; unified libraries are a common contribution type.

nodes.title: Injecting Frame-Event Complementary Fusion into Diffusion for Optical Flow in Challenging Scenes
nodes.tldr: Estimates optical flow in low-light and high-speed scenes by fusing frame and event camera features and denoising flow with a diffusion model.
nodes.problem: Optical flow fails in high-speed and low-light scenes due to motion blur and noise in frame cameras.
nodes.approach: Attention-guided frame-event fusion feeding a diffusion decoder that denoises noisy flow into clear flow.
nodes.niche_reason: Event-frame optical flow is established but specialised.

nodes.title: PoE-World: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts
nodes.tldr: PoE-World models environments as weighted products of LLM-synthesized programmatic experts, learning stochastic world models from few observations and enabling planning on Atari games.
nodes.problem: Deep world models need lots of data; program-based world models were limited to grid-worlds.
nodes.approach: LLM program synthesis of programmatic experts combined as an exponentially-weighted product, used in model-based planning.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Program-synthesis world models are an unusual direction.

nodes.title: AutoToM: Scaling Model-based Mental Inference via Automated Agent Modeling
nodes.tldr: Uses an LLM to propose and iteratively refine agent models, performing Bayesian inverse planning to infer mental states and beating existing theory-of-mind methods.
nodes.problem: Prompted LLMs make systematic errors on theory-of-mind, while handcrafted agent models do not generalize.
nodes.approach: Automated agent-model proposal, Bayesian inverse planning with an LLM backend, and uncertainty-guided refinement.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory-of-mind sits between cognitive science and LLM agents
nodes.niche_reason: Automated Bayesian ToM inference with LLM backends is specialised

nodes.title: FlashMD: long-stride, universal prediction of molecular dynamics
nodes.tldr: Predicts atomic positions and momenta over strides 10-100x longer than MD timesteps, respecting Hamiltonian structure and supporting any thermodynamic ensemble.
nodes.problem: Machine-learned MD remains stuck at tiny integration steps, blocking long-timescale simulations.
nodes.approach: Architecture embedding Hamiltonian dynamics properties, generalized to arbitrary ensembles and validated on equilibrium properties.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Long-stride learned MD integration is a rare, cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Compositional Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion for Extendable Planning
nodes.tldr: Extends diffusion-based tree search planning to reason over complete plan compositions, using online, distributed, and cached composers for longer plans.
nodes.problem: Diffusion planners are limited to training trajectory lengths and search only within single trajectories.
nodes.approach: Tree search over diffusion plan compositions with online, distributed, and preplan composer components.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion planning sits between offline RL and generative planning
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based tree search planning is a specialised direction

nodes.title: Near-Optimal Experiment Design in Linear non-Gaussian Cyclic Models
nodes.tldr: Characterizes equivalence classes of cyclic linear non-Gaussian causal models as bipartite perfect matchings and gives near-optimal adaptive intervention design via adaptive submodularity.
nodes.problem: Efficiently choosing interventions to identify cyclic linear non-Gaussian causal graphs.
nodes.approach: Bipartite matching characterization with greedy adaptive stochastic optimization over equivalence classes.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Cyclic non-Gaussian causal experiment design is a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: Scalable Cross-View Sample Alignment for Multi-View Clustering with View Structure Similarity
nodes.tldr: Aligns unsynchronized samples across views using similarity graphs to a benchmark view, enabling multi-view clustering without aligned samples.
nodes.problem: Multi-view clustering assumes sample correspondence across views, which is often missing in real data.
nodes.approach: Cluster-label matching picks a benchmark view, then similarity-graph alignment feeds a late-fusion clustering.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.confidence_reason: Multi-view clustering has no clean vocabulary topic match
nodes.niche_reason: Unaligned-view clustering is specialised, not rare

nodes.title: Streaming Attention Approximation via Discrepancy Theory
nodes.tldr: BalanceKV is a streaming algorithm that approximates attention by selecting balanced key/value tokens via discrepancy theory, with space lower bounds and improved long-context performance.
nodes.problem: Memory cost of attention during long-context token generation, and its streaming complexity.
nodes.approach: Vector balancing (Banaszczyk, self-balancing walk) to select key-value subsets, plus lower bounds on streaming attention space.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Discrepancy theory applied to KV caches is a rare theoretical angle.

nodes.title: Memory-Enhanced Neural Solvers for Routing Problems
nodes.tldr: Uses memory to dynamically update neural routing solvers' action distributions from past decision outcomes, improving TSP and CVRP search at inference.
nodes.problem: Neural routing solvers cannot adapt to instances or exploit leftover compute budget at inference.

nodes.niche_reason: Evolutionary multi-view classification is a rare niche

nodes.title: Policy Compatible Skill Incremental Learning via Lazy Learning Interface
nodes.tldr: SIL-C keeps evolving skill libraries compatible with existing hierarchical policies by lazily mapping subtasks to skills, avoiding policy retraining.
nodes.problem: Improving skills incrementally breaks compatibility with downstream skill-based policies that rely on them.
nodes.approach: Bilateral lazy-learning mapping aligns policy subtask space with skill space via trajectory similarity.
nodes.confidence_reason: skill-based RL vs continual learning placement is ambiguous
nodes.niche_reason: skill-policy compatibility under skill evolution is rarely studied

nodes.title: Accelerating Diffusion LLMs via Adaptive Parallel Decoding
nodes.tldr: Speeds up diffusion LLMs by adaptively sampling more tokens in parallel, guided by a small autoregressive model's joint probability.
nodes.problem: Diffusion LLMs promise parallel decoding but lose quality or speed relative to autoregressive models.
nodes.approach: Multiplicative mixture of dLLM marginals and a small AR model's joint probability sets the parallel token count.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion LLM decoding speedups are a current but fairly active area.

nodes.title: Continuous Thought Machines
nodes.tldr: Introduces a model whose neurons each have private temporal weights and whose synchronization serves as the latent representation, enabling adaptive compute.
nodes.problem: Standard neural networks ignore neuron-level timing and the dynamics that biological brains use.
nodes.approach: Neuron-level temporal processing with per-neuron weights, plus neural synchronization as representation.
nodes.confidence_reason: Brain-inspired architecture; could also be architecture design
nodes.niche_reason: Brain-inspired neuron dynamics architectures are rare

nodes.title: ORIGAMISPACE: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs in Multi-Step Spatial Reasoning with Mathematical Constraints
nodes.tldr: Benchmark of 350 origami instances testing MLLMs on multi-step spatial reasoning with mathematical constraints, plus an RL environment for code generation.
nodes.problem: Evaluating multimodal LLMs on multi-step spatial reasoning under precise mathematical constraints is hard.
nodes.approach: Origami crease-pattern dataset with four tasks, including interactive CP code generation for RL training.
nodes.niche_reason: Origami folding is a rare task domain for MLLM evaluation

nodes.title: Differentiable Hierarchical Visual Tokenization
nodes.tldr: End-to-end differentiable image tokenizer that adapts patch granularity to content via hierarchical model selection with information criteria, usable as a drop-in for pretrained ViTs.
nodes.problem: Vision Transformers use fixed patch tokens that ignore image spatial and semantic structure.
nodes.approach: Differentiable hierarchical tokenization chosen by information-criterion model selection, at pixel-level granularity.
nodes.confidence_reason: Tokenizer is architectural; overlaps with segmentation and vectorization topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Content-adaptive differentiable tokenization for ViTs is unusual

nodes.title: SceneDesigner: Controllable Multi-Object Image Generation with 9-DoF Pose Manipulation
nodes.tldr: SceneDesigner controls the 9-DoF poses of multiple objects in text-to-image generation via a branched network with a CNOCS map representation, RL rebalancing, and disentangled sampling.
nodes.problem: Simultaneous control over 9D pose (location, size, orientation) of multiple objects in image generation is unsolved.
nodes.approach: Branched network with CNOCS pose maps, new dataset, RL fine-tuning on rebalanced data, disentangled object sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: Pose-controlled multi-object generation is a specialised controllable generation niche.

nodes.title: Fisher meets Feynman: score-based variational inference with a product of experts
nodes.tldr: Proposes a product-of-experts family of t-distributions for black-box variational inference, sampled via a Feynman identity latent variable model.
nodes.problem: Variational families for black-box inference struggle to capture skew, heavy tails, and multiple modes.
nodes.approach: Fits expert exponents by minimizing regularized Fisher divergence, reduced to a convex quadratic program.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Feynman-identity product-of-experts variational families are very rare.

nodes.title: Alligat0R: Pre-Training through Covisibility Segmentation for Relative Camera Pose Regression
nodes.tldr: Pre-trains vision models by segmenting pixel covisibility between image pairs instead of cross-view completion, improving relative pose regression over CroCo.
nodes.problem: Cross-view completion is ill-posed in non-covisible regions, limiting pre-training effectiveness.
nodes.approach: Covisibility segmentation pre-training labeling pixels as covisible, occluded, or out-of-view, on the new Cub3 dataset.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Covisibility pre-training for pose regression is specialized.

nodes.title: Efficient Prompt Compression with Evaluator Heads for Long-Context Transformer Inference
nodes.tldr: EHPC identifies evaluator attention heads in early layers to select important tokens, enabling training-free prompt compression and long-context inference acceleration.
nodes.problem: Long prompts raise LLM cost and hurt performance.
nodes.approach: Use early-layer evaluator heads to skim and keep key tokens during prefill, then pass them on.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt compression is established; head-based selection is specialised.

nodes.title: BioCLIP 2: Emergent Properties from Scaling Hierarchical Contrastive Learning
nodes.tldr: Trains BioCLIP 2 on 214M organism images with hierarchical contrastive learning, showing emergent embedding structure that tracks ecology and traits as scale grows.
nodes.problem: Whether large-scale biological contrastive training yields meaningful emergent structure is unknown.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical contrastive vision-language training on TreeOfLife-200M, a 214M-image organism dataset.
nodes.niche_reason: Biology vision-language foundation models are specialised but growing.

nodes.title: Decomposing Interventional Causality into Synergistic, Redundant, and Unique Components
nodes.tldr: Decomposes interventional causal effects into synergistic, redundant, and unique parts via partial information decomposition and Mobius inversion, illustrated on logic gates and networks.
nodes.problem: Existing decompositions are observational, not capturing how interventions share causal power among variables.
nodes.approach: Closed-form Mobius function of the redundancy lattice applied to interventional causal measures.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual angle: interventional PID for causal power decomposition.

nodes.title: Fair Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games via Conflict-Aware Gradient Adjustment
nodes.tldr: Adjusts policy gradients from individual and collective objectives when they conflict, improving social welfare in social dilemmas while keeping rewards fair across agents.
nodes.problem: Mixed-motive multi-agent RL balances individual and collective returns without addressing fairness of individual rewards.
nodes.approach: Conflict-aware gradient adjustment that balances individual and collective policy gradients when they disagree.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Fair cooperation via gradient conflicts is a specialised MARL angle.

nodes.title: DNA-DetectLLM: Unveiling AI-Generated Text via a DNA-Inspired Mutation-Repair Paradigm
nodes.tldr: Zero-shot AI-text detector that repairs each input toward an ideal AI-generated sequence and scores the cumulative repair effort.
nodes.problem: Human and AI text feature distributions overlap, blurring detection boundaries.
nodes.approach: Iterative token repair toward an ideal sequence, with cumulative repair effort as the detection signal.
nodes.confidence_reason: No dedicated detection topic; provenance vs adversarial robustness
nodes.niche_reason: AI-text detection is a crowded topic; repair-based signal is a twist

nodes.title: Transferable Black-Box One-Shot Forging of Watermarks via Image Preference Models
nodes.tldr: Forges and removes post-hoc image watermarks in a black-box, one-shot setting by backpropagating through a watermark preference model trained on procedural images.
nodes.problem: Watermark forging, stealing a watermark from genuine content and applying it to malicious content, is underexplored.
nodes.approach: Preference model trained with ranking loss; input optimized by backpropagation from a single watermarked image.
nodes.niche_reason: Watermark security is a growing but specialised area

nodes.title: Probing Neural Combinatorial Optimization Models
nodes.tldr: Probes representations of neural combinatorial optimization models, finding low-level construction information and inductive biases, and using insights to improve generalization.
nodes.problem: Neural combinatorial optimization models are black boxes, hindering research and deployment.
nodes.approach: Probing tasks plus CS-Probing, which tests probe coefficients for statistical significance.
nodes.niche_reason: Interpretability of neural combinatorial optimization is rare.

nodes.title: Towards a Golden Classifier-Free Guidance Path via Foresight Fixed Point Iterations
