nodes.tldr: Reframes classifier-free guidance as fixed-point iterations and proposes Foresight Guidance, which solves longer-interval subproblems early in diffusion for better quality and efficiency.
nodes.problem: Classifier-free guidance rests on divergent interpretations and single-step iterations that are inefficient.
nodes.approach: Fixed-point iteration view of guidance with longer-interval solves in early diffusion stages.
nodes.niche_reason: CFG variants are a crowded diffusion sub-area.

nodes.title: PARTONOMY: Large Multimodal Models with Part-Level Visual Understanding
nodes.tldr: Benchmark showing large multimodal models fail at pixel-level part grounding, plus PLUM, a segmenting LMM using span tagging and feedback on prior predictions.
nodes.problem: Large multimodal models struggle to ground object parts at pixel level, limiting fine-grained compositional reasoning.
nodes.approach: Span tagging replaces unseen [SEG] tokens, and predictions feed back into future segmentations in a loop.
nodes.confidence_reason: Benchmark and new segmenting-LMM method both central.
nodes.niche_reason: Segmenting LMMs are an emerging but specialised direction.

nodes.title: Scaling Unlocks Broader Generation and Deeper Functional Understanding of Proteins
nodes.tldr: ProGen3 is a sparse generative protein language model family up to 46B parameters; scaling and wet-lab results show larger models make viable proteins.
nodes.problem: Little systematic study of how model scale and data distribution affect generated proteins.
nodes.approach: Compute-optimal scaling of sparse MoE protein LMs on curated 3.4B-protein data, with wet-lab and alignment evaluation.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Protein language models are an established specialised area.

nodes.title: SGCD: Stain-Guided CycleDiffusion for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation of Histopathology Image Classification
nodes.tldr: Adapts histopathology classifiers across stain domains without paired data by translating images with a bidirectional dual-diffusion model and a stain-guided consistency loss.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised domain adaptation needs high-quality translation, but that usually requires paired data.
nodes.approach: Dual diffusion models with bidirectional generative constraints synthesize target data for fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based domain adaptation for pathology is specialised

nodes.title: GeRaF: Neural Geometry Reconstruction from Radio Frequency Signals
nodes.tldr: First neural implicit reconstruction of near-range 3D geometry from radio frequency signals, using filter-based, physics-based volumetric rendering toward millimeter-level geometry.
nodes.problem: RF sensing sees through occlusion but has low resolution and noise, so RGB and LiDAR methods do not transfer.
nodes.approach: Lens-less full-space sampling and alpha blending, with learned signed distance, reflectiveness, and signal power.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: RF-signal neural geometry reconstruction is a very rare direction

nodes.title: LogicTree: Improving Complex Reasoning of LLMs via Instantiated Multi-step Synthetic Logical Data
nodes.tldr: Synthesizes multi-step logical reasoning data by backward deduction over logic rules and instantiates real-world scenarios with LLMs, improving complex logical reasoning accuracy by 9.4%.
nodes.problem: Template-based synthetic logical reasoning data lacks complexity and real-world instantiation, limiting LLM reasoning.
nodes.approach: Build multi-step logic trees via rule pattern matching, then instantiate scenarios with a two-stage LLM process.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic reasoning data for LLMs is common.

nodes.title: ARM: Adaptive Reasoning Model
nodes.tldr: Trains a model to pick a direct answer, short CoT, code, or long CoT per task via Ada-GRPO, cutting tokens ~30% with similar performance.
nodes.problem: Reasoning models overthink easy tasks, wasting tokens with fixed long chains of thought.
nodes.approach: Adaptive format selection trained with Ada-GRPO, a GRPO variant that avoids format collapse.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient reasoning with RL is a crowded, fast-moving area.

nodes.title: PhySense: Sensor Placement Optimization for Accurate Physics Sensing
nodes.tldr: Reconstructs dense physical fields from sparse sensors with a flow-based model, then optimizes sensor placement by projected gradient descent.
nodes.problem: Sparse-data reconstruction methods ignore optimizing where the sensors are placed.
nodes.approach: Cross-attention flow model for reconstruction, then placement optimization under spatial constraints with variance-minimization guarantees.
nodes.confidence_reason: Physics-field reconstruction and placement straddles physics and PDE-operator topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Joint sensor placement and field reconstruction is rare.

nodes.title: Discovering Opinion Intervals from Conflicts in Signed Graphs
nodes.tldr: Infers small sets of opinion intervals consistent with signed interaction graphs, with hardness results, approximation schemes and a German parliament case study.
nodes.problem: Whether signed-graph conflicts reveal a small set of interpretable opinion ranges.
nodes.approach: Polynomial-time approximation via interval graphs and correlation clustering, plus scalable heuristics.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Hardness results on social signed-graph data; theory or social science
nodes.niche_reason: Opinion intervals from signed graphs is a very rare angle.

nodes.title: Learnable Burst-Encodable Time-of-Flight Imaging for High-Fidelity Long-Distance Depth Sensing
nodes.tldr: Introduces burst-encodable time-of-flight imaging that avoids phase wrapping, with jointly learned coding functions and a depth network for long-distance depth sensing.
nodes.problem: Long-distance depth sensing where indirect ToF suffers phase wrapping and low signal-to-noise ratio.
nodes.approach: Burst-mode pulse emission with end-to-end learned coding functions and depth network, hardware-constrained.
nodes.confidence_reason: Hardware sensing design with learned coding; could fit depth or low-level
nodes.niche_reason: Learned burst-mode time-of-flight coding is a rare sensing paradigm

nodes.title: AdaSPEC: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Speculative Decoders
nodes.tldr: Distills a draft model for speculative decoding while filtering out hard-to-fit tokens, raising token acceptance rate without hurting generation quality.
nodes.problem: Standard KL distillation minimizes divergence on all tokens, misaligned with maximizing draft token acceptance rate.
nodes.approach: Reference-model-based selective token filtering during knowledge distillation of the draft model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Speculative decoding is a fast-growing, crowded inference topic.

nodes.title: On the Expressive Power of Mixture-of-Experts for Structured Complex Tasks
nodes.tldr: Proves shallow and deep mixture-of-experts networks approximate low-dimensional and compositionally sparse functions efficiently, showing exponential expressivity with depth.
nodes.problem: Theoretical reasons for mixture-of-experts efficiency on complex tasks remain poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Approximation-theory analysis under low-dimensionality and compositional sparsity priors.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: MoE expressivity theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Mozart: Modularized and Efficient MoE Training on 3.5D Wafer-Scale Chiplet Architectures
nodes.tldr: Algorithm-hardware co-design for training MoE LLMs on wafer-scale chiplets, with expert allocation, streaming scheduling, and an NoP-Tree topology to cut communication costs.
nodes.problem: MoE sparsity causes memory locality, communication overhead, and poor utilization on hardware.
nodes.approach: Chiplet-aware expert allocation, fine-grained overlapped scheduling, and heterogeneous chiplet co-location with hierarchical memory.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Wafer-scale chiplet hardware co-design for MoE is rare.

nodes.title: Private Hyperparameter Tuning with Ex-Post Guarantee
nodes.tldr: Extends ex-post differential privacy so any sequence of private estimators can be released at a utility-first privacy cost, with free hyperparameter tuning.
nodes.problem: Utility-first privacy analysis has been limited to simple Laplace and Gaussian noise mechanisms.
nodes.approach: Generalizes correlated-noise ex-post DP to arbitrary private estimators, at most doubling the privacy budget.
nodes.niche_reason: Established DP theory with a specialised utility-first variant

nodes.title: CURE: Concept Unlearning via Orthogonal Representation Editing in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: CURE is a training-free closed-form weight edit using SVD-based orthogonal projections (Spectral Eraser) to unlearn concepts from diffusion models in seconds with little collateral damage.
nodes.problem: Safety interventions for text-to-image models suffer from incomplete removal, jailbreaks, inefficiency, or collateral capability loss.
nodes.approach: Closed-form orthogonal projection onto discriminative subspaces from token embedding SVD, with spectral expansion to control forgetting strength.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Concept erasure in diffusion is active but specialised.

nodes.title: SAVVY: Spatial Awareness via Audio-Visual LLMs through Seeing and Hearing
nodes.tldr: Introduces SAVVY-Bench for 3D spatial reasoning with spatial audio and SAVVY, a training-free pipeline tracking objects via audio-visual cues into a global dynamic map.
nodes.problem: Audio-visual LLMs lack 3D spatial reasoning in dynamic scenes with spatial audio.
nodes.approach: Training-free pipeline: egocentric audio-visual track estimation, then global dynamic map construction and coordinate transformation.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Spatial-audio 3D reasoning for AV-LLMs is rare.

nodes.title: Which Features are Learnt by Contrastive Learning? On the Role of Simplicity Bias in Class Collapse and Feature Suppression
nodes.tldr: Gives a theoretical framework showing that gradient descent's simplicity bias causes class collapse and feature suppression in contrastive learning, and proposes remedies.
nodes.problem: No theory explains which features contrastive learning learns or why class collapse and feature suppression occur at test time.
nodes.approach: Unified theoretical analysis of SGD simplicity bias in contrastive learning, suggesting larger embedding dimension and better augmentations.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of contrastive learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: A Study of Global and Episodic Bonuses for Exploration in Contextual MDPs
nodes.tldr: Studies when global versus episodic novelty bonuses help exploration in contextual MDPs, explains it via cross-context value variance, and combines both for state-of-the-art results.
nodes.problem: Ad-hoc, poorly understood use of global and episodic exploration bonuses in contextual MDPs.
nodes.approach: Controlled experiments, a shared-structure framework, and combined bonus algorithms with function approximation.
nodes.niche_reason: Exploration in contextual MDPs is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Structure-informed Language Models Are Protein Designers
nodes.tldr: LM-Design adds a lightweight structural adapter to protein language models and iteratively refines outputs, achieving state-of-the-art inverse-folding sequence recovery.
nodes.problem: Designing protein sequences that fold into a given structure.
nodes.approach: Structural adapter implanted in a pretrained protein LM with iterative refinement at inference.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised protein ML topic.

nodes.title: Random Classification Noise does not defeat All Convex Potential Boosters Irrespective of Model Choice
nodes.tldr: Shows random classification noise does not defeat all convex boosters: the negative result stems from linear separators as the model class, not losses or algorithms.
nodes.problem: Revisiting Long and Servedio's claim that noise defeats all convex potential boosters.
nodes.approach: Use class-probability-estimation loss theory and a new general convex booster to localize failure to the model class.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Boosting noise-robustness theory is now a very rare topic.

nodes.title: Direct Parameterization of Lipschitz-Bounded Deep Networks
nodes.tldr: A complete direct parameterization of deep networks satisfying tightest SDP-based Lipschitz bounds, enabling unconstrained gradient training via sandwich layers and improving certified robustness.
nodes.problem: Training networks with guaranteed Lipschitz bounds without projections or costly SDP constraints.
nodes.approach: Smooth surjective map from free parameters onto weights satisfying the SDP bound, as sandwich layers.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Lipschitz-constrained architectures are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models
nodes.tldr: Hyena replaces attention with a subquadratic operator of implicit long convolutions and data-controlled gating, matching Transformer quality with less compute and faster at long sequences.
nodes.problem: Attention's quadratic cost limits context length and subquadratic alternatives lag in capability.
nodes.approach: Interleave implicitly parametrized long convolutions with multiplicative gating as drop-in attention replacement.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Subquadratic attention alternatives are a common, active area.

nodes.title: Pre-training for Speech Translation: CTC Meets Optimal Transport
nodes.tldr: Pre-trains speech translation encoders with CTC combined with optimal transport in a Siamese acoustic-text setup, shrinking the speech-text modality gap without architectural changes.
nodes.problem: Closing the modality gap between speech and text in speech-to-text translation.
nodes.approach: CTC pre-training plus Wasserstein-distance alignment of acoustic and textual encoder representations.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised speech translation with optimal transport angle.

nodes.title: Graphically Structured Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Builds diffusion model architectures from a problem's graphical model, learning algorithm-like tasks such as sorting and Sudoku with better scaling.
nodes.problem: Generative models for algorithm-like problems ignore their explicit graphical structure.
nodes.approach: Diffusion models with architectures tailored to the problem's graphical structure, subcomputations and permutation invariances.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Structured diffusion design spans generative modeling and probabilistic structure.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion for algorithmic structured problems is rare.

nodes.title: Cross-Modal Fine-Tuning: Align then Refine
nodes.tldr: Extends one large pretrained model to many modalities by learning an embedding network that aligns target data with the pretraining modality before fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Gains from large pretrained models do not reach modalities lacking suitable pretrained models.
nodes.approach: Align-then-refine: a learned embedding aligns inputs to the pretrained feature distribution, then the model is fine-tuned.
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-modal transfer of pretrained models is established but specialised

nodes.title: Learning Signed Distance Functions from Noisy 3D Point Clouds via Noise to Noise Mapping
nodes.tldr: Learns accurate signed distance functions from noisy point clouds by noise-to-noise mapping, needing no clean or ground-truth supervision.
nodes.problem: Learning SDFs from noisy point clouds usually requires clean data, normals, or ground-truth distances.
nodes.approach: Loss over multiple noisy observations enforcing statistical and geometric consistency without correspondences.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Noise-to-noise SDF learning is a specialised 3D niche

nodes.title: Cones: Concept Neurons in Diffusion Models for Customized Generation
nodes.tldr: Finds small clusters of concept neurons in diffusion models that control specific subjects; shutting or combining them enables customized generation.
nodes.problem: Customizing diffusion models for subjects is costly, and their internal mechanisms are opaque.
nodes.approach: Identify neurons via gradient statistics, then store a sparse index set instead of weights.
nodes.niche_reason: Concept neurons in diffusion are niche interpretability work.

nodes.title: AdaptDiffuser: Diffusion Models as Adaptive Self-evolving Planners
nodes.tldr: AdaptDiffuser self-evolves a diffusion planner by generating reward-guided synthetic expert data, filtering it with a discriminator, and fine-tuning to improve seen and unseen tasks.
nodes.problem: Diffusion planners are limited by training data diversity and generalize poorly to new tasks.
nodes.approach: Reward-gradient-guided synthetic data generation, discriminator selection, and iterative fine-tuning of the diffusion model.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion planning for offline RL is fairly common.

nodes.title: Tighter Lower Bounds for Shuffling SGD: Random Permutations and Beyond
nodes.tldr: Proves tighter convergence lower bounds for without-replacement SGD with random reshuffling and arbitrary permutations, closing gaps with upper bounds and matching GraB.
nodes.problem: Existing lower bounds for shuffling SGD are loose in condition number and component count dependencies.
nodes.approach: Construct hard instances for weighted average iterates under random reshuffling and arbitrary permutation-based SGD.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Lower bounds for shuffling SGD are a narrow theoretical niche.

nodes.title: Generalization on the Unseen, Logic Reasoning and Degree Curriculum
nodes.tldr: Studies generalization on the unseen for Boolean functions, showing GD-trained models learn min-degree interpolators, explaining length generalization and motivating a Degree-Curriculum algorithm.
nodes.problem: Out-of-distribution generalization when part of the combinatorial input domain is unseen in logic and arithmetic tasks.
nodes.approach: Theory and experiments on Boolean function learning across architectures plus incremental-support curriculum.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Boolean-function OOD generalization theory is a rare angle.

nodes.title: Sharper Bounds for $\ell_p$ Sensitivity Sampling
nodes.tldr: Proves sharper sample complexity for sensitivity sampling in l_p subspace embeddings, beating the general S*d bound and tight for p below 2.
nodes.problem: Known sensitivity-sampling guarantees beyond the general S*d bound exist only for l_2 embeddings.
nodes.approach: Refined analysis of sensitivity and leverage score sampling for p not equal 2, with matching lower-bound constructions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Coreset theory sits between learning-theory lower bounds and data curation.
nodes.niche_reason: Sensitivity sampling for l_p embeddings is a narrow theory niche.

nodes.title: Self-Repellent Random Walks on General Graphs - Achieving Minimal Sampling Variance via Nonlinear Markov Chains
nodes.tldr: Designs self-repellent random walks, nonlinear Markov chains that avoid highly visited nodes, proving convergence and a CLT showing asymptotic sampling variance decreases at rate 1/alpha.
nodes.problem: Reducing sampling variance of MCMC random walks on graphs beyond standard Markov chain samplers.
nodes.approach: Nonlinear Markov chain with repulsion from visit history; stochastic approximation analysis and asymptotic covariance derivation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Nonlinear Markov chain samplers with asymptotic variance analysis are rare.

nodes.title: Calibrating Multimodal Learning
nodes.tldr: CML is a regularizer that keeps multimodal prediction confidence from rising when a modality is removed, improving calibration and robustness.
nodes.problem: Multimodal classifiers give unreliable confidence and lean on partial modalities, even when corrupted.
nodes.approach: Regularization that penalizes confidence increases when any modality is removed, plugged into existing models.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal calibration is a moderately common topic.

nodes.title: Flipping Coins to Estimate Pseudocounts for Exploration in Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Derives state visitation counts by training a supervised objective on Rademacher coin-flip targets, used as an exploration bonus in RL.
nodes.problem: Count-based exploration in high-dimensional states relies on density models.
nodes.approach: Averages Rademacher samples in a supervised regression objective that estimates visit counts.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Coin-flip pseudocount derivation is an unusual exploration idea

nodes.title: Subequivariant Graph Reinforcement Learning in 3D Environments
nodes.tldr: Introduces 3D morphology-agnostic RL benchmarks and a subequivariant transformer policy, so one controller generalizes to arbitrary directions and start configurations.
nodes.problem: Morphology-agnostic RL benchmarks restrict agents to 2D movement and fixed start points
nodes.approach: Subequivariant graph transformer injecting geometric symmetry into policy and Q-function
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.confidence_reason: Morphology-agnostic RL; equivariant policy spans RL and GNN topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare 3D morphology-agnostic setup with symmetry-based policies

nodes.title: GibbsDDRM: A Partially Collapsed Gibbs Sampler for Solving Blind Inverse Problems with Denoising Diffusion Restoration
nodes.tldr: GibbsDDRM solves blind inverse problems with unknown linear operators by posterior sampling with a pre-trained diffusion prior inside a partially collapsed Gibbs sampler.
nodes.problem: Diffusion-prior restoration needs the measurement operator, which is unknown in blind settings.
nodes.approach: Joint posterior sampling over data, measurements and operator using a partially collapsed Gibbs sampler.
nodes.niche_reason: Blind inverse problems with diffusion priors are specialised but active.

nodes.title: Quantile Credit Assignment
nodes.tldr: Uses return-quantile predictions to build a luck-dependent baseline for policy gradients, separating environment randomness from agent skill with unbiased, lower-variance gradients.
nodes.problem: Credit assignment must separate environmental luck from the agent's controllable effects.
nodes.approach: Quantile-regression return distribution estimation used as a baseline, with a hindsight variant.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Quantile-based luck baselines are a specialised credit-assignment niche

nodes.title: Reparameterized Policy Learning for Multimodal Trajectory Optimization
nodes.tldr: Models the RL policy as a latent-variable generative model of trajectories, enabling multimodal exploration and data-efficient model-based learning on sparse-reward tasks.
nodes.problem: Gaussian policies are unimodal and get stuck in local optima in high-dimensional continuous control.
nodes.approach: Latent-conditioned multimodal policy with a variational objective, trained on a learned world model.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Mixes policy parameterization, model-based RL and exploration
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal latent-variable policies are established but specialised

nodes.title: Robust Budget Pacing with a Single Sample
nodes.tldr: Shows that one historical sample per distribution suffices for near-optimal budget pacing regret in repeated second-price auctions, improving the prior T log T requirement.
nodes.problem: How many historical samples an advertiser needs to learn a good budget expenditure plan under nonstationary values.
nodes.approach: Learn a target spend plan from one sample per distribution and track it with a controller; analyze regret.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Sits between online learning and auction mechanism theory.
nodes.niche_reason: Sample-efficient budget pacing for ad auctions is an unusual niche.

nodes.title: Gaussian Process Priors for Systems of Linear Partial Differential Equations with Constant Coefficients
nodes.tldr: EPGP constructs Gaussian process priors whose samples exactly solve any linear constant-coefficient PDE system, using the Ehrenpreis-Palamodov principle for spectral kernels.
nodes.problem: Embedding exact linear PDE constraints into Gaussian process priors for physical systems.
nodes.approach: Ehrenpreis-Palamodov nonlinear Fourier transform to build spectral GP kernels.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Algebraic analysis for PDE-constrained GPs is very rare.

nodes.title: Weighted Flow Diffusion for Local Graph Clustering with Node Attributes: an Algorithm and Statistical Guarantees
nodes.tldr: Local graph clustering algorithm using attribute-aware mass diffusion from a seed node, with statistical recovery guarantees under a contextual graph model.
nodes.problem: Recovering small target clusters in large attributed graphs from a single seed node.
nodes.approach: Weighted flow diffusion combining structural and node-attribute proximity, analysed with high-dimensional concentration.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: No graph-clustering topic in vocab; placed under Other.
nodes.niche_reason: Attributed local graph clustering is established but specialised.

nodes.title: When Personalization Harms Performance: Reconsidering the Use of Group Attributes in Prediction
nodes.tldr: Shows personalizing models with group attributes can hurt group-level accuracy, gives fair-use conditions checkable with one extra model, and finds violations in clinical prediction.
nodes.problem: Personalization with group attributes can unintentionally reduce accuracy for the groups providing those attributes.
nodes.approach: Formal fair-use conditions for group attributes, verified by training one additional model, with a clinical prevalence study.
nodes.niche_reason: Fairness angle on personalization is specialised but established in clinical ML.

nodes.title: Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?
nodes.tldr: Measures how LM opinions align with 60 US demographic groups using public opinion polls, finding substantial misalignment that persists after steering.
nodes.problem: Opinions that language models reflect on subjective topics may misalign with society.
nodes.approach: Builds OpinionQA from public opinion polls and compares model answers against demographic groups.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM opinion bias is a well-studied topic

nodes.title: Data Feedback Loops: Model-driven Amplification of Dataset Biases
nodes.tldr: Shows bias amplifies in feedback loops where model outputs become future training data, depending on whether outputs faithfully sample the training distribution.
nodes.problem: Model outputs replacing human annotations in scraped data may amplify biases over time.
nodes.approach: Formalise recorded interaction feedback systems, track a bias statistic over time, propose a stabilising intervention.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Bias amplification vs. synthetic-data framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Data feedback loops are a specialised but recognised problem

nodes.title: Inflow, Outflow, and Reciprocity in Machine Learning
nodes.tldr: Proposes a framework to measure contributions (outflow) and benefits (inflow) of entities pooling data for ML models, and reciprocity between them, with theory for some model classes.
nodes.problem: Quantifying value exchange between data contributors and beneficiaries in pooled machine learning.
nodes.approach: Define outflow, inflow and reciprocity measures; prove approximate reciprocity under distributional assumptions and test empirically.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Framework spans data pooling, fairness-like reciprocity and theory; no clean topic.
nodes.niche_reason: Reciprocity of data contribution and benefit is very rare.

nodes.title: Do Perceptually Aligned Gradients Imply Robustness?
nodes.tldr: Shows perceptually aligned input gradients promote adversarial robustness, proposes an objective that directly induces them, and uses this to boost adversarial training.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether perceptually aligned gradients are merely a byproduct of robust training or matter on their own.
nodes.approach: Training objective that directly promotes input-gradient alignment, tested for adversarial robustness.
nodes.niche_reason: Perceptually aligned gradients are a niche but active robustness topic

nodes.title: Same Pre-training Loss, Better Downstream: Implicit Bias Matters for Language Models
nodes.tldr: Shows models with equal pre-training loss differ in downstream performance, and that SGD's implicit bias toward flatter minima explains transferability in language models.
nodes.problem: Pre-training loss does not fully explain downstream performance of language models.
nodes.approach: Empirical flatness (Hessian trace) analysis and theory that SGD noise prefers flat minima, with a synthetic proof.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit bias of pre-training is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Pretraining Language Models with Human Preferences
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks five objectives for pretraining LMs with human feedback and finds conditional training on preference scores cuts undesirable content by an order of magnitude without hurting capabilities.
nodes.problem: Standard LM pretraining imitates text containing content that violates human preferences.
nodes.approach: Compare pretraining objectives; conditional training conditions token distribution on human preference scores.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Alignment is crowded, though pretraining-stage angle is less common.

nodes.title: Diffusion Models as Artists: Are we Closing the Gap between Humans and Machines?
nodes.tldr: Evaluates how human-like one-shot diffusion model drawings are using diversity-recognizability and originality measures plus human psychophysics, finding a remaining gap in visual strategies.
nodes.problem: Whether diffusion models can produce drawings indistinguishable from human drawings.
nodes.approach: Adapted diversity-recognizability scoring, originality metrics, and psychophysics-derived diagnostic features compared against diffusion-derived ones.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Cognitive-science comparison of diffusion drawings with human psychophysics is unusual.

nodes.title: Sketch-Flip-Merge: Mergeable Sketches for Private Distinct Counting
nodes.tldr: First cardinality sketches that are mergeable, differentially private, and accurate, using a randomized algorithm for logical operations on noisy bits with tight privacy analysis.
nodes.problem: Private distinct counting with sketches that remain private when merged.
nodes.approach: Randomized logical operations on noisy bits, tight DP analysis, provably optimal cardinality estimation.
nodes.niche_reason: Data-sketching algorithms with DP are rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: Continuation Path Learning for Homotopy Optimization
nodes.tldr: Learns the entire continuation path of homotopy optimization with a single model, jointly optimizing all surrogate subproblems and enabling real-time generation of intermediate solutions.
nodes.problem: Homotopy optimization is sensitive to continuation schedules and discards useful intermediate solutions.
nodes.approach: Model-based learning of the full continuation path with simultaneous optimization of all surrogate subproblems.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned homotopy continuation is a rare optimization niche.

nodes.title: OCD: Learning to Overfit with Conditional Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Generates input-specific network weights with a conditional diffusion model, imitating per-sample finetuning, and ensembles multiple samples for accuracy.
nodes.problem: Adapting a model to each individual input without costly per-sample finetuning.
nodes.approach: Conditional diffusion model predicts weights of one layer, conditioned on input, activations, and output.
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion generates per-input weights; topic split between generative and meta-learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-generated per-input weights for overfitting is an unusual framing.

nodes.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
nodes.tldr: Speculative decoding runs a small draft model to propose tokens and verifies them in parallel with the large model, yielding exact samples 2-3x faster without retraining.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive transformer decoding is slow because K tokens require K serial model runs.
nodes.approach: Draft-then-verify speculative sampling that preserves the output distribution while generating several tokens per large-model pass.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Inference acceleration is a crowded, mainstream area.

nodes.title: Bayes-optimal Learning of Deep Random Networks of Extensive-width
nodes.tldr: Derives closed-form Bayes-optimal test error for learning deep random networks of extensive width, and for ridge and kernel regression.
nodes.problem: Optimal test error of learning deep random networks in the proportional regime is unknown.
nodes.approach: Asymptotic high-dimensional analysis with closed-form error expressions for several learners.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Proportional-regime Bayes-optimal analysis is a specialised theory niche

nodes.title: Instant Soup: Cheap Pruning Ensembles in A Single Pass Can Draw Lottery Tickets from Large Models
nodes.tldr: Merges weak masks from a few cheap iterations into one denoised subnetwork, giving lottery-ticket-quality pruning of large pretrained models at a fraction of IMP cost.
nodes.problem: Iterative magnitude pruning for lottery tickets requires repeated full training, which grows with model size.
nodes.approach: Aggregate superposed weak subnetworks from varied training protocols and data subsets to average out noise.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Lottery-ticket pruning is established; soup-based mask aggregation is specialised.

nodes.title: Facial Expression Recognition with Adaptive Frame Rate based on Multiple Testing Correction
nodes.tldr: Speeds up video facial expression recognition by adaptively choosing frame rate per clip, using Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery control for reliable decisions.
nodes.problem: Processing every frame of video for facial expression recognition is computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Sequential frame-rate selection with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control, requiring no network retraining.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.confidence_reason: Facial analysis versus video processing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Adaptive frame rate for facial expression video is specialised

nodes.title: Buying Information for Stochastic Optimization
nodes.tldr: Formulates buying information for stochastic optimization as online learning, giving a 2-competitive deterministic and e/(e-1)-competitive randomized algorithm for tight ski-rental-style trade-offs.
nodes.problem: How should a learner pay for extra information to improve stochastic optimization decisions under a known distribution?
nodes.approach: Competitive-ratio analysis of an online buying rule, plus an 8-competitive polynomial-time adaptive algorithm for Min-Sum Set Cover.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.confidence_reason: Competitive online-learning analysis; could also fit bandits or sequential decisions.
nodes.niche_reason: Buying information via ski-rental-style competitive analysis is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Tractable Control for Autoregressive Language Generation
nodes.tldr: Imposes lexical constraints on GPT-2 generation by guiding it with distilled hidden Markov models whose constraint probabilities are tractable to compute.
nodes.problem: Sampling autoregressive text that satisfies lexical constraints is intractable.
nodes.approach: Tractable probabilistic models, distilled HMMs, guide autoregressive decoding.
nodes.niche_reason: Tractable-model constraint decoding is specialised.

nodes.title: Arithmetic Sampling: Parallel Diverse Decoding for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Arithmetic sampling draws diverse LLM samples from an implicit arithmetic code book: embarrassingly parallel, provably diverse beams, unbiased, closing much of the beam-search BLEU gap.
nodes.problem: LLM decoding trades off output diversity against parallelism, with duplicates in parallel sampling.
nodes.approach: Sample according to an arithmetic code book implicitly defined by the LM, compatible with top-k and nucleus variants.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Decoding methods are established; arithmetic-coding view is specialised.

nodes.title: A Fully First-Order Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
nodes.tldr: F2SA is a fully first-order stochastic bilevel optimization method with finite-time convergence guarantees, avoiding Hessian computations and improved by momentum.
nodes.problem: Stochastic bilevel optimization methods need costly Hessians or lack finite-time guarantees.
nodes.approach: Penalty-style fully first-order stochastic approximation with non-asymptotic complexity analysis and momentum variant.
nodes.niche_reason: Bilevel optimization theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: BEATs: Audio Pre-Training with Acoustic Tokenizers
nodes.tldr: BEATs iteratively trains an acoustic tokenizer and audio SSL model with discrete label prediction, achieving state-of-the-art audio classification on AudioSet and ESC-50.
nodes.problem: Audio self-supervised pretraining with reconstruction loss captures redundant detail over semantics.
nodes.approach: Iterative joint optimization of semantic acoustic tokenizer and masked discrete-label prediction model.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Audio SSL is established but a smaller area than vision or text.

nodes.title: Denoising MCMC for Accelerating Diffusion-Based Generative Models
nodes.tldr: Speeds diffusion sampling by using MCMC to produce near-manifold initializations that a reverse SDE/ODE integrator then denoises.
nodes.problem: Diffusion samplers often need thousands of reverse-SDE/ODE steps per image.
nodes.approach: Denoising MCMC: Langevin Gibbs samples in data-time product space, then a reverse S/ODE integrator denoises them.
nodes.niche_reason: Faster diffusion sampling is a crowded direction; MCMC initialization is distinctive.

nodes.title: Neural Continuous-Discrete State Space Models for Irregularly-Sampled Time Series
nodes.tldr: NCDSSM models irregularly sampled time series with continuous-time latent dynamics and discrete observations, using auxiliary variables for amortized inference and filtering-based Bayesian inference.
nodes.problem: Irregularly sampled, partially missing time series are hard to model and forecast accurately.
nodes.approach: Continuous-discrete state space model with auxiliary-variable recognition and filtering-theory inference over dynamic states.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Continuous-time latent dynamics is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning-Rate-Free Learning by D-Adaptation
nodes.tldr: D-Adaptation is a parameter-free learning-rate method for SGD and Adam variants that matches tuned rates without knowing the distance to the solution.
nodes.problem: Gradient descent speed depends on a learning rate that needs the unknown distance to the solution.
nodes.approach: Single-loop adaptive step size estimating distance on the fly, with no line search or extra gradient calls.
nodes.niche_reason: Adaptive learning-rate methods are a crowded area.

nodes.title: Settling the Reward Hypothesis
nodes.tldr: Characterizes exactly which goals and purposes can be captured by maximizing expected cumulative scalar reward, settling the reward hypothesis.
nodes.problem: Whether all goals and purposes can be expressed as reward maximization remains an open hypothesis.
nodes.approach: Formal analysis specifying the implicit requirements on goals under which reward maximization holds.
nodes.confidence_reason: Abstract is short; no methods or experiments to confirm specifics.
nodes.niche_reason: Foundational question on whether goals reduce to reward maximization is rare.

nodes.title: Taming graph kernels with random features
nodes.tldr: Introduces graph random features, unbiased randomized estimators of graph node kernels like regularized Laplacian, scaling kernel methods below cubic time with distributed and quasi Monte Carlo variants.
nodes.problem: Graph kernel algorithms have cubic time complexity in the number of nodes.
nodes.approach: Random-walk-based unbiased estimators of graph kernels, with reinforced-walk quasi Monte Carlo variance reduction.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Random-feature approximations of graph kernels are a rare topic.

nodes.title: BPipe: Memory-Balanced Pipeline Parallelism for Training Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: BPipe balances activation memory across GPUs in pipeline parallelism by transferring activations, speeding up GPT-3 96B/134B training 1.25x-2.17x over Megatron-LM.
nodes.problem: Pipeline parallelism leaves some GPUs memory-starved while others are underused, hurting LLM training efficiency.
nodes.approach: Activation balancing that transfers intermediate activations between GPUs to equalize memory use.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Distributed training systems work is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Second-Order Optimization with Lazy Hessians
nodes.tldr: Shows Newton's method can reuse a Hessian for many iterations, reaching second-order stationarity globally and improving total arithmetic complexity by a factor of sqrt(d).
nodes.problem: Second-order methods are expensive because Hessians are recomputed every iteration.
nodes.approach: Lazy Hessian updates with cubic or quadratic regularisation, updating the Hessian about once every d iterations.
nodes.niche_reason: Lazy second-order updates are specialised but established

nodes.title: Mimetic Initialization of Self-Attention Layers
nodes.tldr: Initializes self-attention query, key, value and projection weights to mimic pretrained Transformers, training small-data vanilla ViTs faster and more accurately.
nodes.problem: Transformers train poorly on small datasets, where pretrained models are the usual workaround.
nodes.approach: Closed-form, learning-free initialization making query-key product identity and value-projection product negative identity.
nodes.niche_reason: Closed-form attention initialization is specialised but established

nodes.title: Inferring Relational Potentials in Interacting Systems
nodes.tldr: Discovers relational energy potentials that reconstruct interacting-agent trajectories, enabling test-time manipulation, forecasting, and out-of-distribution detection.
nodes.problem: Inferring the precise interactions governing multi-agent systems, while keeping flexibility in trajectory modeling.
nodes.approach: Represents interactions as energy functions whose minimisation reconstructs trajectories; low energy marks constraint-respecting motion.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Relational inference straddles graph learning and trajectory dynamics
nodes.niche_reason: Relational inference is established; energy-potential framing is specialised

nodes.title: Self-Interpretable Time Series Prediction with Counterfactual Explanations
nodes.tldr: CounTS is a self-interpretable variational Bayesian model that generates counterfactual, actionable explanations alongside time series predictions.
nodes.problem: Post-hoc time series explanations score segments but do not say what change would alter the prediction.
nodes.approach: Counterfactual inference via time-series abduction, action and prediction in a variational model.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Self-interpretable counterfactual time series models are a specialised niche

nodes.title: SparseProp: Efficient Sparse Backpropagation for Faster Training of Neural Networks at the Edge
nodes.tldr: SparseProp is a fast vectorized CPU implementation of backpropagation for unstructured sparse networks, enabling real speedups when training sparse models or transfer learning on edge hardware.
nodes.problem: Sparse training lacks efficient implementations on commodity hardware.
nodes.approach: Vectorized sparse backpropagation algorithm for linear and convolutional layers on CPUs.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse training kernels on CPUs are specialised.

nodes.title: Efficient Self-supervised Learning with Contextualized Target Representations for Vision, Speech and Language
nodes.tldr: data2vec 2.0 speeds multimodal self-supervised pretraining by skipping masked tokens, using a convolutional decoder and reusing teacher targets, matching baselines with far less compute.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised learners across vision, speech and text are computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Efficient data2vec: encode only visible tokens, convolutional decoder, amortized contextualized teacher targets.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Masked self-supervised pretraining is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Refining Generative Process with Discriminator Guidance in Score-based Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Discriminator Guidance adds a post-hoc discriminator gradient to the pretrained diffusion score, correcting sampling toward the data score and reaching ImageNet FID 1.83.
nodes.problem: Pretrained diffusion models produce imperfect samples due to score estimation errors.
nodes.approach: Post-hoc discriminator on denoising paths supplies an auxiliary score correction term during sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: Guidance for diffusion sampling is a common topic.

nodes.title: Exponential Smoothing for Off-Policy Learning
nodes.tldr: Exponential smoothing regularization for IPS-based off-policy learning, with a two-sided PAC-Bayes bound that needs no bounded weights.
nodes.problem: Off-policy learning via IPS has high variance, and clipped IPS is used without theory for when regularization helps.
nodes.approach: Smooth regularization of the IPS risk with learning certificates; identifies cases where regularization is unnecessary.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: PAC-Bayes certificates for off-policy learning are a specialised niche

nodes.title: Adversarial Policies Beat Superhuman Go AIs
nodes.tldr: Adversarial policies beat superhuman KataGo over 97% of the time by exploiting blind spots, transferring zero-shot to other Go AIs.
nodes.problem: Superhuman game AIs may have hidden failure modes that standard play metrics miss.
nodes.approach: Train adversarial policies that trick the victim into blunders rather than playing strong Go.
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial attacks on game AIs are specialised but established

nodes.title: Unifying Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Methods for Convex and Strongly Convex Objective Functions
nodes.tldr: Unifies Nesterov's accelerated gradient for convex and strongly convex functions with one momentum algorithm, improving convergence on ill-conditioned problems.
nodes.problem: Nesterov acceleration is handled separately for convex and strongly convex objectives
nodes.approach: Unified Lagrangian and ODE framework yielding one momentum algorithm, extended to non-Euclidean settings
nodes.niche_reason: Unified Nesterov momentum theory is specialised

nodes.title: Scaling Vision Transformers to 22 Billion Parameters
nodes.tldr: Recipe for stable training of a 22-billion-parameter Vision Transformer, showing downstream performance, fairness, and robustness improve with scale.
nodes.problem: Vision Transformers had not been scaled to the size of large language models.
nodes.approach: Efficient, stable training recipe for a 22B dense ViT, evaluated with frozen-feature probes.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Large-scale vision transformers are a mainstream direction

nodes.title: Resurrecting Recurrent Neural Networks for Long Sequences
nodes.tldr: Shows careful RNN design with signal propagation, linearized diagonal recurrence and normalization matches deep state-space models on long-range tasks, with the LRU block.
nodes.problem: Unclear why deep state-space models outperform RNNs on long sequence tasks.
nodes.approach: Linearized, diagonalized recurrence with better parameterization, initialization and normalization.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Established linear-recurrence line with a revisiting angle

nodes.title: Specializing Smaller Language Models towards Multi-Step Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Distills multi-step chain-of-thought math reasoning from GPT-3.5 into small T5 models by specializing their capacity toward a target task, trading off general ability.
nodes.problem: Small language models lack emergent multi-step reasoning ability present in very large models.
nodes.approach: Distill chain-of-thought from a large model into small T5 variants, specializing capacity to math reasoning.
nodes.niche_reason: Reasoning distillation was a common direction.

nodes.title: H-Likelihood Approach to Deep Neural Networks with Temporal-Spatial Random Effects for High-Cardinality Categorical Features
nodes.tldr: Proposes a hierarchical-likelihood training of neural networks with correlated random effects for clustered high-cardinality categorical data, giving exact MLEs and online learning.
nodes.problem: DNNs ignore temporal-spatial correlation and high-cardinality categorical features in clustered data.
nodes.approach: Joint optimization of negative h-likelihood with random effects and a two-step algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Statistical methodology paper with unclear topic fit.
nodes.niche_reason: Classical hierarchical likelihood statistics fused with DNNs is unusual.

nodes.title: Marginalization is not Marginal: No Bad VAE Local Minima when Learning Optimal Sparse Representations
nodes.tldr: Proves VAE energy minima, local or global, recover optimally sparse latent representations for a single-layer decoder, because marginalization smooths away bad local minima.
nodes.problem: The VAE loss surface is poorly understood beyond the simplified affine decoder case.
nodes.approach: Analyzes a single-layer decoder on NP-hard sparse regression and compares to deterministic autoencoders.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: VAE loss-surface theory for sparse coding is rare

nodes.title: Adapting to game trees in zero-sum imperfect information games
nodes.tldr: Proves a sample lower bound for learning epsilon-optimal strategies in zero-sum imperfect-information games, and two FTRL algorithms matching or adapting to it.
nodes.problem: Learning equilibrium strategies in imperfect-information games from trajectory feedback is sample-hungry.
nodes.approach: Follow-the-regularized-leader self-play with regularization balanced or adapted to information sets.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Imperfect-information game learning theory is specialised

nodes.title: JAWS-X: Addressing Efficiency Bottlenecks of Conformal Prediction Under Standard and Feedback Covariate Shift
nodes.tldr: Proposes jackknife+-based conformal prediction methods that retain finite-sample coverage under standard and feedback covariate shift while balancing computational and statistical efficiency.
nodes.problem: Conformal prediction under covariate shift with feedback is either very expensive or wastes labeled data.
nodes.approach: JAW-FCS extends jackknife+ coverage guarantees, with K-leave-one-out and K-fold relaxations preserving finite-sample guarantees.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Conformal prediction under feedback shift is a rare, specialised statistical setting.

nodes.title: Diffusion Models are Minimax Optimal Distribution Estimators
nodes.tldr: Proves diffusion models trained with score matching reach nearly minimax optimal rates for densities in Besov spaces and adapt to low-dimensional data.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models lack rigorous approximation and generalization guarantees for distribution estimation.
nodes.approach: Analyze approximation and generalization error of empirical score matching over Besov-class densities.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Minimax theory of diffusion estimators is established but specialised

nodes.title: Reinforcement Learning from Passive Data via Latent Intentions
nodes.tldr: Learns state, policy and outcome representations from passive action- and reward-free video via a temporal-difference objective over latent intentions, accelerating downstream RL.
nodes.problem: Using passive observational data without reward or action labels to accelerate RL.
nodes.approach: TD-style learning of intention-conditioned outcome likelihoods to build value-predictive features.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Pretraining RL from action-free video is established but specialised.

nodes.title: TRAK: Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
nodes.tldr: TRAK is a data attribution method using randomly projected kernel approximations that matches costly retraining-based attribution with only a handful of trained models.
nodes.problem: Data attribution methods trade off computational tractability and effectiveness for large non-convex models.
nodes.approach: Linearize model via random projection of gradients and use the after-kernel with few model ensembles.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Data attribution is an established but specialised subfield.

nodes.title: StyleGAN-T: Unlocking the Power of GANs for Fast Large-Scale Text-to-Image Synthesis
nodes.tldr: StyleGAN-T adapts StyleGAN to large-scale text-to-image synthesis, redesigning generator, discriminator and training for competitive one-step generation versus diffusion.
nodes.problem: GANs lag behind diffusion and autoregressive models in large-scale text-to-image generation.
nodes.approach: Redesigned StyleGAN architecture with strong text conditioning, CLIP-based discriminator and stable training for scale.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: GAN-based text-to-image is now uncommon next to diffusion.

nodes.title: ODS: Test-Time Adaptation in the Presence of Open-World Data Shift
nodes.tldr: ODS handles test-time adaptation under simultaneous covariate and label distribution shift by decoupling the mixed shifts and addressing each separately.
nodes.problem: Test-time adaptation when both input and label distributions shift in open-world settings.
nodes.approach: Analyze error versus shifts, then decouple covariate and label shift and adapt each accordingly.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Test-time adaptation is a common research area.

nodes.title: Returning The Favour: When Regression Benefits From Probabilistic Causal Knowledge
nodes.tldr: Shows that collider independences in a causal DAG act as inductive biases, and gives a regression framework with provable generalization gains in RKHS.
nodes.problem: Regression ignores probabilistic causal knowledge encoded in DAGs, wasting useful inductive bias.
nodes.approach: Collider-based constraints on RKHS hypotheses with closed-form empirical risk minimizers.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Collider-based regression priors are an unusual angle

nodes.title: Delayed Feedback in Kernel Bandits
nodes.tldr: Kernel bandit algorithm for stochastically delayed feedback, with a regret bound that improves on prior work and is additive in expected delay.
nodes.problem: Kernel bandits assume immediate feedback, which fails in recommendation, clinical trials and hyperparameter tuning.
nodes.approach: Regret bound of sqrt(max information gain times T) plus expected delay, analyzed via kernel information gain.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Delayed-feedback kernel bandits are a specialised sub-area of bandit theory

nodes.title: FlexGen: High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
nodes.tldr: FlexGen runs high-throughput LLM generation on one GPU by offloading and compressing weights and cache across GPU, CPU and disk.
nodes.problem: Large LLMs need multiple high-end accelerators, which is too costly for latency-insensitive batch inference.
nodes.approach: Linear programming picks tensor placement across memory tiers, and 4-bit compression of weights and attention cache enlarges batch size.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM inference efficiency is a crowded, mainstream systems topic.

nodes.title: Multicalibration as Boosting for Regression
nodes.tldr: Shows multicalibration is equivalent to boosting for squared-error regression, giving a simple agnostic boosting algorithm and tight weak-learning conditions for Bayes optimality.
nodes.problem: Relationship between multicalibration and boosting for regression is not well characterized.
nodes.approach: Swap-regret-like characterization of multicalibration yielding a simple oracle-based boosting algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Multicalibration-boosting theory is a niche theory area.

nodes.title: Semi Bandit dynamics in Congestion Games: Convergence to Nash Equilibrium and No-Regret Guarantees.
nodes.tldr: Shows a variant of online stochastic gradient descent converges to Nash equilibria in congestion games with semi-bandit feedback, while also achieving sublinear regret.
nodes.problem: Learning Nash equilibria in congestion games with exponentially large action sets under semi-bandit feedback.
nodes.approach: Online SGD analyzed with Caratheodory's theorem and non-convex stochastic optimization; polynomial dependence on players.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Game-theoretic learning dynamics in congestion games is rare

nodes.title: Equivariant Architectures for Learning in Deep Weight Spaces
nodes.tldr: Designs neural architectures that take MLP weights as input and are equivariant to neuron permutation symmetries, fully characterizing equivariant affine layers.
nodes.problem: Processing neural network weights directly requires respecting the permutation symmetry of hidden neurons.
nodes.approach: Characterize all permutation-equivariant affine layers on weight spaces and implement them via pooling, broadcasting and linear layers.
nodes.niche_reason: Learning on neural weight spaces is a very rare direction.

nodes.title: Learning GFlowNets From Partial Episodes For Improved Convergence And Stability
nodes.tldr: Introduces subtrajectory balance, a GFlowNet objective inspired by TD(lambda) that learns from partial action subsequences, speeding convergence and handling longer, sparser environments.
nodes.problem: GFlowNet objectives trade off gradient bias and variance between local and whole-trajectory signals.
nodes.approach: Trajectory-balance-style loss over partial subtrajectories of varying lengths, with a TD(lambda)-like weighting.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: GFlowNet sampler could fit generative or RL topics
nodes.niche_reason: GFlowNet training objectives are a relatively rare, specialised direction.

nodes.title: Spherical Fourier Neural Operators: Learning Stable Dynamics on the Sphere
nodes.tldr: Generalizes Fourier neural operators to spherical geometry, enabling stable year-long autoregressive atmospheric forecasts without flat-geometry artifacts.
nodes.problem: Standard FNOs assume flat geometry, causing artifacts and dissipation when learning dynamics on the sphere.
nodes.approach: Spherical generalization of the Fourier neural operator for global convolutions on spherical grids.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural operators on spherical geometry for climate are uncommon.

nodes.title: DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature
nodes.tldr: DetectGPT detects LLM-generated text zero-shot by noting such text lies in negative-curvature regions of the model's log-probability, using perturbations from another language model.
nodes.problem: Detecting machine-generated text without training classifiers, datasets or watermarking.
nodes.approach: Compare log-probability of a passage with perturbed rewrites to measure probability curvature.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.confidence_reason: Detection of LLM text fits provenance or safety areas.
nodes.niche_reason: Popular topic though curvature criterion is distinctive.

nodes.title: Memory-Based Dual Gaussian Processes for Sequential Learning
nodes.tldr: Keeps sequential Gaussian process learning accurate by actively building and updating a memory of past data within a dual sparse variational GP.
nodes.problem: Sequential GP learning accumulates errors in posterior, hyperparameters and inducing points.
nodes.approach: Dual sparse variational GP with an actively maintained memory of past data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Memory-based sparse GPs for sequential learning is specialised.

nodes.title: Practical and Matching Gradient Variance Bounds for Black-Box Variational Bayesian Inference
nodes.tldr: Proves matching gradient variance bounds for black-box variational inference satisfying the ABC condition, and shows mean-field parameterization has better dimension dependence.
nodes.problem: Gradient variance of black-box VI was not shown to satisfy conditions needed for SGD convergence analysis.
nodes.approach: Derive tight variance bounds for smooth, quadratically growing log-likelihoods and nonlinear covariance parameterizations.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised theory of BBVI gradient variance; few papers.

nodes.title: Adversarial Example Does Good: Preventing Painting Imitation from Diffusion Models via Adversarial Examples
nodes.tldr: Uses adversarial perturbations on artworks (AdvDM) so diffusion models cannot extract style features, protecting paintings from imitation.
nodes.problem: Protecting artists' paintings from unauthorized style imitation by diffusion models.
nodes.approach: Monte-Carlo adversarial example optimization over latents sampled from the diffusion reverse process.
nodes.niche_reason: Protective adversarial perturbations against generative models is specialised but growing.

nodes.title: Over-parametrization via Lifting for Low-rank Matrix Sensing: Conversion of Spurious Solutions to Strict Saddle Points
nodes.tldr: Shows that lifting low-rank matrix sensing into an over-parametrized hierarchy turns spurious stationary points into escapable strict saddles.
nodes.problem: Spurious stationary points make non-convex low-rank matrix recovery hard to solve.
nodes.approach: Lifting with Burer-Monteiro factorization yields an infinite hierarchy of over-parametrized non-convex problems.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised non-convex landscape theory; lifting hierarchy is uncommon

nodes.title: How Bad is Top-$K$ Recommendation under Competing Content Creators?
nodes.tldr: Proves creator competition under top-K recommendation loses only a small, tight constant fraction of user welfare, given random user choices.
nodes.problem: Whether competing creators with no-regret learning harm user welfare in relevance-driven recommendation.
nodes.approach: Price of Anarchy analysis of a Random Utility user model with creators running no-regret learning.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Game-theoretic creator competition is a rare angle on recommenders

nodes.title: Fourmer: An Efficient Global Modeling Paradigm for Image Restoration
nodes.tldr: Fourier-domain image restoration architecture with global pixel interactions and channel evolution, using fewer resources than prior global-modeling restorers.
nodes.problem: Global-modeling restoration models have high memory cost and ignore task-specific degradation.
nodes.approach: Fourier spatial interaction and Fourier channel evolution, exploiting Fourier degradation priors.
nodes.niche_reason: Fourier restoration is a moderately common low-level vision topic.

nodes.title: Hiera: A Hierarchical Vision Transformer without the Bells-and-Whistles
nodes.tldr: Hiera removes vision-specific components from hierarchical vision transformers, using MAE pretraining to be more accurate and faster than prior models.
nodes.problem: Hierarchical vision transformers add complexity that makes them slower than plain ViTs without accuracy gains.
nodes.approach: Strip vision-specific components and rely on MAE pretraining to train a simple hierarchical ViT.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Mainstream vision transformer architecture work

nodes.title: Interventional Causal Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows interventional data lets causal latent factors be identified up to permutation and scaling, and block-affine identification under imperfect interventions, without distributional assumptions.
nodes.problem: Identifying latent causal factors from low-level sensory data without strong structural assumptions.
nodes.approach: Exploit support-geometry signatures in interventional data to prove identifiability results.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Specialized causal representation theory; a well-studied niche

nodes.title: Tilted Sparse Additive Models
nodes.tldr: Proposes sparse additive models trained with tilted empirical risk minimization, giving robust, imbalanced and variable-selection learning with generalization and approximation bounds.
nodes.problem: Standard ERM-based additive models fail under complex non-Gaussian noise and label imbalance.
nodes.approach: Tilted risk weighting of individual losses, optimized with an accelerated Prox-SVRG plus random Fourier acceleration.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Tilted-risk additive models are a specialised robust-learning niche

nodes.title: ProtST: Multi-Modality Learning of Protein Sequences and Biomedical Texts
nodes.tldr: ProtST pretrains protein language models with biomedical text descriptions via unimodal and multimodal alignment and mask-prediction tasks, enabling zero-shot protein classification and retrieval.
nodes.problem: Protein language models learn from sequences only and do not explicitly acquire protein function information.
nodes.approach: Build ProtDescribe sequence-text dataset; pretrain with unimodal masking, multimodal alignment, and multimodal masking.
nodes.niche_reason: Protein-text multimodal learning is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Multi-Epoch Matrix Factorization Mechanisms for Private Machine Learning
nodes.tldr: New differentially private mechanisms for multi-epoch gradient training using extended matrix factorization, with an efficient Fourier-based variant for long training runs.
nodes.problem: Matrix factorization DP mechanisms handle single participation; multi-epoch training with repeated participation lacks good privacy-utility tradeoffs.
nodes.approach: Extend online matrix factorization mechanisms to multiple participations with sensitivity theory and a Fourier-transform-based efficient mechanism.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised DP mechanism design with strong theory component.

nodes.title: On the Power of Pre-training for Generalization in RL: Provable Benefits and Hardness
nodes.tldr: Proves pre-training over training environments gives at most constant-factor asymptotic gains in RL, but can help non-asymptotically via a policy elimination algorithm.
nodes.problem: How much pre-training in RL environments helps efficient fine-tuning on a target environment is unclear.
nodes.approach: Policy collection-elimination algorithm with distribution-dependent regret bounds independent of state-action space size.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Provable RL pretraining benefits are specialised theory

nodes.title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Embeds a detectable watermark in LLM text by softly promoting a pseudorandom green token list during sampling, detected via a statistical test without model access.
nodes.problem: Machine-generated text needs to be reliably detectable without degrading quality or requiring API access.
nodes.approach: Randomized green token sets promote green tokens during sampling; detection uses a z-test with interpretable p-values.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Widely studied LLM watermarking topic.

nodes.title: Differentially Private Hierarchical Clustering with Provable Approximation Guarantees
nodes.tldr: First differentially private approximation algorithms for hierarchical clustering, with lower bounds and an exact-recovery result on stochastic block models.
nodes.problem: Hierarchical clustering must protect individual data under differential privacy, which costs additive error.
nodes.approach: Private approximation algorithms with provable additive error, plus a 1+o(1) method under block separation.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Private hierarchical clustering with guarantees is rare

nodes.title: Why does Throwing Away Data Improve Worst-Group Error?
nodes.tldr: Uses extreme value theory to show that discarding data from heavy-tailed distributions restores classifier symmetry, improving worst-group generalization of linear classifiers.
nodes.problem: Why throwing away data to balance groups improves worst-group error contradicts standard learning theory.
nodes.approach: Extreme value theory analysis of tail behavior and geometric symmetry of linear classifiers.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: extreme value theory for worst-group error is unusual

nodes.title: Pix2Struct: Screenshot Parsing as Pretraining for Visual Language Understanding
nodes.tldr: Pix2Struct pretrains an image-to-text model by parsing masked web screenshots into HTML, then fine-tunes for visually-situated language understanding tasks.
nodes.problem: Visually-situated language tasks rely on domain-specific recipes that share little data or models.
nodes.approach: Screenshot-to-HTML masked pretraining with variable-resolution inputs and prompts rendered onto images.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Document and screenshot VLM pretraining is a common direction.

nodes.title: Best of Both Worlds Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: First best-of-both-worlds policy optimization for tabular MDPs, achieving polylog(T) regret for stochastic losses while keeping sqrt(T) worst-case adversarial regret.
nodes.problem: Policy optimization regret bounds are worst-case pessimistic and do not adapt to stochastic losses.
nodes.approach: Carefully designed Tsallis or Shannon entropy regularizers, bonuses, and learning rates; log-barrier for first-order bound.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Best-of-both-worlds regret for MDPs is rare theoretical work.

nodes.title: Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling
nodes.tldr: Releases Pythia, 16 LLMs from 70M to 12B parameters trained on identical data order, with 154 checkpoints each for analyzing training dynamics.
nodes.problem: Understanding how LLMs develop over training and change with scale needs controlled, reproducible setups.
nodes.approach: Train a model family on the same public data order with public checkpoints and dataloader reconstruction tools.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Open LLM training-suite analysis is a common research pattern

nodes.title: Robustly Learning a Single Neuron via Sharpness
nodes.tldr: Gives an efficient algorithm for learning a single neuron under adversarial label noise, approximating optimal L2 error within a constant factor.
nodes.problem: Learning a neuron under adversarial label noise typically needs strong distributional assumptions.
nodes.approach: Uses a novel connection to local error bounds from optimization theory to succeed under milder assumptions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: agnostic single-neuron learning via optimization-theory tools.

nodes.title: Evaluating Self-Supervised Learning via Risk Decomposition
nodes.tldr: Decomposes SSL risk into approximation, representation usability, probe generalization, and encoder generalization terms, and analyzes 169 vision models to guide design.
nodes.problem: Single-metric SSL evaluation hides tradeoffs and does not show how to improve representations.
nodes.approach: Four-term risk decomposition with efficient estimators across 30 design choices.
nodes.niche_reason: SSL evaluation is mainstream, though this decomposition is novel

nodes.title: Sequential Underspecified Instrument Selection for Cause-Effect Estimation
nodes.tldr: Estimates causal effects of high-dimensional treatments with fewer instruments, combining partial estimates and adaptively choosing the most informative instruments.
nodes.problem: Causal effects of high-dimensional treatments are unidentifiable with fewer instruments than treatments
nodes.approach: Recover treatment-effect projections onto instrumented subspaces, combine them, and greedily pick informative instruments.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Instrument selection for high-dimensional treatments is specialised causal work

nodes.title: Bidirectional Adaptation for Robust Semi-Supervised Learning with Inconsistent Data Distributions
