nodes.tldr: Theoretical analysis of semi-supervised learning under mismatched labeled/unlabeled distributions, with a Bidirectional Adaptation framework to debias pseudo-labels and sample weights.
nodes.problem: Semi-supervised learning degrades when labeled and unlabeled data come from inconsistent distributions.
nodes.approach: Generalization-error theory identifying failure causes, then bidirectional adaptation to decouple pseudo-label and target predictors with debiased weights.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Split between SSL, domain shift, and generalization theory.
nodes.niche_reason: Robust SSL under distribution shift is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Towards Theoretical Understanding of Inverse Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Establishes a minimax sample complexity lower bound and a matching uniform sampling upper bound for estimating the feasible reward set in inverse RL.
nodes.problem: Inverse RL reward ambiguity; sample complexity of estimating the feasible reward set is not well understood.
nodes.approach: PAC analysis under a generative model with finite-horizon MDPs; uniform sampling strategy US-IRL analyzed.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: IRL sample complexity theory is specialized but established.

nodes.title: Difference of submodular minimization via DC programming
nodes.tldr: Applies DC programming algorithms to difference-of-submodular minimization, with convergence and local-minimality guarantees and gains on corpus and feature selection.
nodes.problem: Existing difference-of-submodular minimization algorithms underexploit the connection to DC programming.
nodes.approach: Introduce DCA variants for the DC reformulation and analyze convergence and local minimality.
nodes.niche_reason: Submodular and DC optimization is a rare niche in ML.

nodes.title: Mu$^2$SLAM: Multitask, Multilingual Speech and Language Models
nodes.tldr: Mu2SLAM is a multilingual sequence-to-sequence model pre-trained jointly on unlabeled speech, text and supervised ASR, speech translation and MT data across over 100 languages.
nodes.problem: Building a single model for multilingual speech and text understanding with aligned cross-modal representations.
nodes.approach: T5-style denoising with quantized speech targets plus encoder MLM, mixing unlabeled and supervised speech-text tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: Joint multilingual speech-text pretraining is specialised.

nodes.title: Mastering the Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning Benchmark from Pixels
nodes.tldr: Unsupervised model-based RL pre-trains a visual agent, then fine-tunes with a hybrid Dyna-MPC planner, beating baselines on URLB from pixels.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised RL pretraining from pixels has unclear benefit for generalising to downstream visual tasks.
nodes.approach: Unsupervised model-based pretraining, task-aware fine-tuning, and a hybrid Dyna-MPC planner.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Unsupervised pretraining for visual RL is specialised but active

nodes.title: Fundamental Limits of Two-layer Autoencoders, and Achieving Them with Gradient Methods
nodes.tldr: Characterizes the fundamental limits of non-linear two-layer autoencoders and shows gradient methods reach them, revealing the learned features.
nodes.problem: Gradient-trained autoencoders' limits and learned features were poorly understood, even for two layers.
nodes.approach: Analysis in the proportional regime of population risk minimizers for Gaussian data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised theory of shallow autoencoders.

nodes.title: Using Large Language Models to Simulate Multiple Humans and Replicate Human Subject Studies
nodes.tldr: Introduces Turing Experiments, which test whether language models can simulate representative human participants, replicating classic economic, psycholinguistic and social-psychology studies and revealing hyper-accuracy distortion.
nodes.problem: Evaluating whether LLMs can simulate human behavior across a population of participants.
nodes.approach: Simulate human-subject studies (Ultimatum Game, Garden Path, Milgram, Wisdom of Crowds) with prompted language models.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM simulation of human-subject studies is an unusual cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Generalized Teacher Forcing for Learning Chaotic Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Generalized teacher forcing gives provably bounded gradients when training RNNs on chaotic systems, and with piecewise-linear RNNs reconstructs dynamical systems in low dimensions.
nodes.problem: Exploding gradients when training RNNs to reconstruct chaotic dynamical systems from time series.
nodes.approach: Modified teacher forcing with bounded gradients combined with a rearranged piecewise-linear RNN architecture.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamical systems reconstruction with PLRNNs is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Beyond the Universal Law of Robustness: Sharper Laws for Random Features and Neural Tangent Kernels
nodes.tldr: Proves random-features models are not robust at any degree of overparameterization, while NTK models meet the universal robustness lower bound.
nodes.problem: Whether over-parameterization alone explains adversarial robustness of random feature and NTK models.
nodes.approach: Analyze empirical risk minimization for random features and NTK, decoupling kernel and interaction matrix effects.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Robustness theory of random features and NTK is specialised

nodes.title: Active Ranking of Experts Based on their Performances in Many Tasks
nodes.tldr: Actively ranks n experts across d tasks under a monotonicity assumption, with instance-dependent query bounds matched by lower bounds.
nodes.problem: Recovering the correct expert ranking from noisy, costly pairwise task evaluations.
nodes.approach: Adaptive sequential querying of expert-task pairs with high-probability guarantees.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Active ranking under monotonicity across tasks is a niche setting.

nodes.title: Nonparametric Extensions of Randomized Response for Private Confidence Sets
nodes.tldr: Introduces a nonparametric sequential randomized response giving private confidence intervals and time-uniform confidence sequences for means under local differential privacy.
nodes.problem: Inferring population means from locally differentially private data, without parametric assumptions.
nodes.approach: Generalize Warner's randomized response to bounded variables, then derive private Hoeffding-type intervals and sequences.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Private nonparametric confidence sequences are a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: Fast Private Kernel Density Estimation via Locality Sensitive Quantization
nodes.tldr: Gives a differentially private kernel density estimator whose runtime is linear in dimension by privatizing fast non-private KDE methods as a black box.
nodes.problem: Differentially private kernel density estimation is exponential in dimension for prior Gaussian-kernel methods.
nodes.approach: Locality Sensitive Quantization wraps RFF, FGT, and LSH KDE methods into private mechanisms.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Private KDE is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Towards Reliable Neural Specifications
nodes.tldr: Proposes neural activation patterns as specifications for verifying neural network properties, enabling larger verifiable input regions than data-neighborhood specifications on MNIST and CIFAR10.
nodes.problem: Existing data-based specifications give tight verified regions that fail to cover test inputs.
nodes.approach: Mine neural activation patterns statistically and use them as specifications for formal verification.
nodes.niche_reason: Specification design for neural network verification is a rare niche.

nodes.title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
nodes.tldr: Prunes large GPT-family models to 50-60% sparsity in one shot without retraining, with negligible perplexity increase, running in hours on 175B-scale models.
nodes.problem: Massive GPT-family models are costly to deploy; pruning usually requires expensive retraining.
nodes.approach: Efficient one-shot weight pruning with layerwise weight reconstruction, no retraining.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM pruning and compression is a crowded mainstream area

nodes.title: HETAL: Efficient Privacy-preserving Transfer Learning with Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.tldr: HETAL enables practical encrypted transfer learning using CKKS homomorphic encryption, with fast encrypted matrix multiplication and accurate softmax approximation, training in under an hour.
nodes.problem: Prior homomorphic-encryption work focused on encrypted inference, not private training for transfer learning.
nodes.approach: CKKS-based encrypted training with efficient matrix multiplication, softmax approximation, and validation-based early stopping.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Homomorphic-encryption training is a rare cryptography-ML crossover.

nodes.title: Task-specific experimental design for treatment effect estimation
nodes.tldr: Derives task-specific experimental design strategies for treatment effect estimation tailored to downstream goals, needing an order of magnitude less data than RCTs in targeted marketing.
nodes.problem: Generic sample-efficient causal experiments ignore the downstream task the causal effect is needed for.
nodes.approach: Sampling strategy optimised for a specific downstream application's objective, evaluated on real datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Task-aware causal experimental design is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Information-Theoretic State Space Model for Multi-View Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Fuses multi-view observations, including missing views, into a latent state space model for control, scaling linearly with the number of views.
nodes.problem: Multi-view control is hard when observations are temporally dependent and views are intermittently missing.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic objective capturing the underlying state space model from sequences of multi-view observations.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Multi-view RL overlaps representation learning and model-based control.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-view state-space control is a fairly unusual angle.

nodes.title: Patch-level Routing in Mixture-of-Experts is Provably Sample-efficient for Convolutional Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proves patch-level routing in mixture-of-experts reduces CNN sample complexity by a factor of about n/l through discriminative routing.
nodes.problem: Why patch-level routing in mixture-of-experts works well and how many samples it needs was unexplained.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of a mixture of two-layer CNN experts with prioritized patch routing, plus MNIST/CIFAR-10/CelebA experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of MoE routing for CNNs is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Efficient RL via Disentangled Environment and Agent Representations
nodes.tldr: SEAR learns structured visual RL representations by separating agent from environment using agent masks in an auxiliary loss, beating model-free baselines on 18 environments.
nodes.problem: Inefficient visual RL representations that ignore agent-environment separation
nodes.approach: Auxiliary loss using agent shape/mask knowledge to disentangle representations
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Visual RL representation learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Transformer-based Stagewise Decomposition for Large-Scale Multistage Stochastic Optimization
nodes.tldr: TranSDDP uses a Transformer to sequentially generate subgradient cutting planes approximating value functions, speeding up large-scale multistage stochastic programming versus SDDP.
nodes.problem: Stagewise decomposition methods like SDDP scale poorly for large multistage stochastic programs.
nodes.approach: Transformer generates piecewise-linear value function cuts sequentially, replacing incremental cut accumulation.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned stochastic programming decomposition is very rare.

nodes.title: Provably Learning Object-Centric Representations
nodes.tldr: Proves that under compositionality and irreducibility assumptions, object-centric representations are identifiable by invertible compositional inference models, without supervision.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised object-centric representation learning lacks a theory of when object identification is possible.
nodes.approach: Formalizes compositionality and irreducibility of scene generation, proves identifiability, and validates on synthetic data.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Identifiability theory for object-centric models is rare

nodes.title: Raising the Cost of Malicious AI-Powered Image Editing
nodes.tldr: Immunizes images with imperceptible adversarial perturbations that make diffusion-based editing produce unrealistic outputs, plus policy for model developers to enforce it.
nodes.problem: Large diffusion models enable malicious, realistic manipulation of others' images.
nodes.approach: Crafts imperceptible perturbations that disrupt targeted diffusion models' editing, with two perturbation methods.
nodes.confidence_reason: Misuse prevention straddles image editing and adversarial robustness.
nodes.niche_reason: Protective adversarial perturbations against editing are specialised.

nodes.title: On the Statistical Benefits of Temporal Difference Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves temporal difference learning gives asymptotic mean-squared error gains over direct estimation, characterized by inverse trajectory pooling and trajectory crossing time.
nodes.problem: When and by how much TD learning beats direct value estimation on Markov chains is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Asymptotic analysis with an inverse trajectory pooling coefficient and a trajectory crossing time bound on TD errors.
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical theory of TD versus direct estimation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Are labels informative in semi-supervised learning? Estimating and leveraging the missing-data mechanism.
nodes.tldr: Estimates how labelling depends on class, then reweights labelled examples with inverse propensity weighting to debias semi-supervised learning.

nodes.title: InfoNet: Neural Estimation of Mutual Information without Test-Time Optimization
nodes.tldr: InfoNet is a neural network that directly outputs mutual information estimates for data streams, avoiding costly test-time optimization.
nodes.problem: Existing mutual information estimators are too slow for real-time use or not differentiable.
nodes.approach: Attention-based network trained on a dual formulation of mutual information with large-scale simulated data.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Learned MI estimation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Perturb-and-Project: Differentially Private Similarities and Marginals
nodes.tldr: Differentially private algorithms using input perturbation followed by projection to release pairwise cosine similarities and k-way marginals, with sum-of-squares based Gaussian complexity bounds.
nodes.problem: Efficiently releasing private pairwise similarities and k-way marginals with strong accuracy guarantees.
nodes.approach: Add noise to input then project to admissible datasets; analyze with sum-of-squares certificates bounding Gaussian complexity.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical DP with sum-of-squares certificates is quite rare.

nodes.title: Size-invariance Matters: Rethinking Metrics and Losses for Imbalanced Multi-object Salient Object Detection
nodes.tldr: Argues salient object detection metrics are size-sensitive and proposes per-object evaluation with an optimization framework that treats objects of all sizes equally.
nodes.problem: Current saliency metrics favour large objects and ignore small salient objects in multi-object images.
nodes.approach: Evaluates each salient object separately, combines results, and trains with a size-balanced optimization objective.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised SOD evaluation problem with generalization analysis

nodes.title: Position: Beyond Personhood: Agency, Accountability, and the Limits of Anthropomorphic Ethical Analysis
nodes.tldr: Argues AI should be seen as the outcome of political processes, not an ethical agent, contrasting mechanistic and volitional agency views.
nodes.problem: AI research implicitly assumes a mechanistic view of agency, which limits ethical analysis of AI.
nodes.approach: Draws on political science and philosophy to contrast two views of agency and their accountability implications.
nodes.niche_reason: Political-philosophy framing of AI agency is an unusual cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: SAPG: Split and Aggregate Policy Gradients
nodes.tldr: On-policy RL algorithm that splits massively parallel environments into chunks and fuses them with importance sampling, overcoming PPO performance saturation at large scale.
nodes.problem: PPO and on-policy methods fail to benefit from very many parallel simulated environments.
nodes.approach: Split environments into groups with separate policies and aggregate data via importance sampling.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: On-policy deep RL algorithms are a common topic.

nodes.title: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Task-Specific Exam Generation
nodes.tldr: Scores retrieval-augmented LLMs on a synthetic multiple-choice exam generated from the task corpus, using item response theory to refine it.
nodes.problem: Choosing RAG components for a task needs a cheap, reliable task-specific accuracy measure.
nodes.approach: Auto-generated exam questions, with IRT used to estimate exam quality and drop uninformative items.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Evaluation method for RAG is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Sample-specific Masks for Visual Reprogramming-based Prompting
nodes.tldr: Sample-specific multi-channel masks generated by a lightweight ConvNet improve visual reprogramming of pre-trained classifiers, with theory showing reduced approximation error versus shared masks.
nodes.problem: Shared masks across all samples in visual reprogramming limit generalization and increase approximation error.
nodes.approach: Generate per-sample three-channel masks with a lightweight ConvNet and patch-wise interpolation to place the learned pattern.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Visual reprogramming is a rare prompting-style niche.

nodes.title: Pricing with Contextual Elasticity and Heteroscedastic Valuation
nodes.tldr: Online contextual pricing algorithm that models feature-based price elasticity as heteroscedastic valuations, achieving near-optimal regret even under adversarial contexts.
nodes.problem: Dynamic pricing needs to account for customer price elasticity that depends on product features.
nodes.approach: Pricing with Perturbation, an efficient algorithm with matching regret lower bound.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Contextual elasticity pricing is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Fine-tuning Reinforcement Learning Models is Secretly a Forgetting Mitigation Problem
nodes.tldr: Shows RL fine-tuning fails largely because pretrained capabilities are forgotten on unvisited states, and knowledge-retention techniques fix it, setting a NetHack state of the art.
nodes.problem: Fine-tuning pretrained RL models transfers poorly because of forgetting on states not visited early in fine-tuning.
nodes.approach: Diagnose forgetting of pretrained capabilities and apply standard knowledge retention methods during fine-tuning on NetHack and Montezuma's Revenge.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-tuning pretrained RL agents is established but specialised, with few comparable studies.

nodes.title: SparseTSF: Modeling Long-term Time Series Forecasting with *1k* Parameters
nodes.tldr: SparseTSF forecasts long-term time series with under 1k parameters by downsampling to decouple periodicity and trend, using cross-period sparse forecasting.
nodes.problem: Long-term time series forecasting with extremely low parameter counts and compute.
nodes.approach: Cross-period sparse forecasting that downsamples sequences to predict cross-period trends.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised forecasting direction.

nodes.title: Regression with Multi-Expert Deferral
nodes.tldr: Extends learning to defer to regression with multiple experts, proving H-consistency guarantees for new surrogate losses in single- and two-stage settings.
nodes.problem: Learning to defer is studied for classification, but regression's continuous labels complicate it.
nodes.approach: Surrogate losses for single- and two-stage multi-expert regression deferral with H-consistency bounds.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-expert deferral for regression is a rare theory niche

nodes.title: Robust and Conjugate Gaussian Process Regression
nodes.tldr: Robust conjugate Gaussian process regression uses generalised Bayesian inference to handle non-Gaussian noise while keeping exact closed-form conditioning at negligible extra cost.
nodes.problem: Standard GPs assume Gaussian noise; existing robust GPs lose closed-form conjugate updates.
nodes.approach: Generalised Bayesian inference yielding provably robust yet conjugate GP posterior updates.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Robust conjugate GP inference is a rare, specialised topic.

nodes.title: Doubly Robust Causal Effect Estimation under Networked Interference via Targeted Learning
nodes.tldr: Proposes a doubly robust causal effect estimator for networked interference by training neural networks with a targeted loss that tolerates misspecification.
nodes.problem: Causal effect estimation under networked interference is biased when nuisance models are misspecified.
nodes.approach: Targeted learning adapted to neural networks, yielding an end-to-end estimator with faster convergence.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Networked-interference causal estimation is specialised

nodes.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.1, Knowledge Storage and Extraction
nodes.tldr: Controlled biography experiments show LLMs extract knowledge only if pretraining data is augmented, with linear probing revealing how knowledge is encoded; recommends rewriting pretraining data.
nodes.problem: Whether LLMs genuinely extract stored knowledge or rely on seen question formats, and how data diversity matters.
nodes.approach: Controlled synthetic biography pretraining with diversity augmentation and linear probing of hidden representations.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Controlled synthetic study of LLM knowledge storage is specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Causal Relations from Subsampled Time Series with Two Time-Slices
nodes.tldr: Learns causal relations from coarsely subsampled time series using only two time-slices, via a descendant-identifying conditional independence test (DHT-CIT) instead of costly interventions.
nodes.problem: Causal discovery from time series sampled at coarser timescale than the true causal timescale, without interventions.
nodes.approach: Iterative conditional independence criterion on two time-slices to identify descendants and build a causal ordering.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Causal discovery under temporal subsampling is a specialised, rarely studied setting.

nodes.title: How do Large Language Models Navigate Conflicts between Honesty and Helpfulness?
nodes.tldr: Uses human psychology models to show RLHF improves both honesty and helpfulness, while chain-of-thought prompting shifts LLMs toward helpfulness over honesty.
nodes.problem: How LLMs trade off honesty against helpfulness, such as rounding truths, is not well characterized.
nodes.approach: Psychologically grounded behavioral experiments on many LLMs, comparing RLHF, reasoning prompts, and conversational framing.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Psychology-grounded honesty analysis of LLMs is unusual

nodes.title: How Free is Parameter-Free Stochastic Optimization?
nodes.tldr: Shows a simple hyperparameter search makes non-convex stochastic optimization fully parameter-free, and proves fully parameter-free convex SGD is infeasible under stochastic gradients.
nodes.problem: Parameter-free methods still need knowledge of problem constants, so they are only partially parameter-free.
nodes.approach: Hyperparameter search for the non-convex setting; lower bound analysis for the convex stochastic gradient setting.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised optimization theory niche

nodes.title: Code as Reward: Empowering Reinforcement Learning with VLMs
nodes.tldr: VLM-CaR uses VLM-generated code to create dense reward functions, avoiding costly per-step VLM queries during RL.
nodes.problem: Querying VLMs for rewards during RL training is too computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Generate dense reward code from VLM feedback, then train RL policies on that code.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: VLM-based reward design is a growing but fairly common direction.

nodes.title: Is DPO Superior to PPO for LLM Alignment? A Comprehensive Study
nodes.tldr: Compares DPO and PPO for LLM alignment, finding theoretical limits for DPO and that tuned PPO outperforms it across RLHF testbeds.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether reward-free DPO truly beats reward-based PPO for aligning LLMs with human preferences.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of DPO plus an empirical study of PPO's key factors across dialogue and code testbeds.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Core mainstream LLM alignment comparison

nodes.title: ViP: A Differentially Private Foundation Model for Computer Vision
nodes.tldr: Trains a differentially private masked-autoencoder vision transformer on LAION-400M under epsilon=8, achieving 55.7% linear probing on ImageNet.
nodes.problem: Internet-scale vision foundation models risk privacy and copyright violations from uncurated training data.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised masked autoencoders trained with DP-SGD under a strict privacy budget.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Private foundation model pretraining at scale is a specialised direction.

nodes.title: Locally Estimated Global Perturbations are Better than Local Perturbations for Federated Sharpness-aware Minimization
nodes.tldr: Estimates the global SAM perturbation locally from the difference between successive global models, improving federated generalization with one backprop per step.
nodes.problem: Local sharpness estimates fail to match global flatness under heterogeneous federated client data.
nodes.approach: Global perturbation direction estimated as the difference of consecutive global models, one backprop per step.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated SAM variants are a common, crowded direction

nodes.title: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Debate
nodes.tldr: Designs debate protocols where an honest strategy needs only polynomially many simulation steps to verify stochastic AI systems against exponentially resourced dishonest debaters.
nodes.problem: Original AI safety debate assumed honest strategies simulate deterministic systems for exponentially many steps.
nodes.approach: Doubly-efficient debate protocols with polynomial-step honest strategy, proven via complexity-theoretic analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Complexity-theoretic debate protocols for oversight are rare.

nodes.title: Improved Operator Learning by Orthogonal Attention
nodes.tldr: Builds neural operators for PDE surrogates from orthogonal attention, parameterizing eigenfunctions of the kernel integral operator with neural networks.
nodes.problem: Neural operator surrogates for PDE solution families need to generalize well with limited data.
nodes.approach: Orthonormal eigenfunction parameterization with an orthogonalization step that regularizes and mitigates overfitting.
nodes.niche_reason: neural operators are specialised; the orthogonal attention variant is distinctive

nodes.title: Agnostic Sample Compression Schemes for Regression
nodes.tldr: Gives the first bounded sample-compression schemes for agnostic regression under l_p losses, including linear-size schemes for linear regression and impossibility results for other p.
nodes.problem: Bounded sample compression was unknown for agnostic regression under l_p losses.
nodes.approach: Generic approximate compression scheme exponential in fat-shattering dimension, plus efficient exact schemes for l1 and l-infinity.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Sample compression for agnostic regression is a rare theory niche.

nodes.title: A Geometric Decomposition of Finite Games: Convergence vs. Recurrence under Exponential Weights
nodes.tldr: Decomposes finite games via a Shahshahani-metric Riemannian framework, showing incompressible (harmonic) games make exponential weights dynamics volume-preserving and Poincare recurrent.
nodes.problem: Understanding learning dynamics in games by decomposing them into simpler components with known long-run behavior.
nodes.approach: Riemannian Helmholtz-type decomposition under the Shahshahani metric defining incompressible games and linking them to harmonic games.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Geometric game-dynamics decomposition is a very rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: Learning to Model the World With Language
nodes.tldr: Agent learns a multimodal world model that predicts future text and images, using diverse language as a predictive signal and acting via imagined rollouts.
nodes.problem: Language-conditioned agents fail to use diverse language such as game rules and state descriptions.
nodes.approach: Multimodal world model trained to predict future language and images, with policy learning from imagined rollouts.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Language-grounded world-model agents are specialised.

nodes.title: Neural Collapse meets Differential Privacy: Curious behaviors of NoisyGD with Near-Perfect Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses neural collapse to explain why pre-training helps differentially private fine-tuning, and shows PCA and feature normalization improve robustness.
nodes.problem: Why pre-trained representations help DP fine-tuning, and why DP fine-tuning is less robust.
nodes.approach: Layer-peeled model analysis of NoisyGD with feature normalization and PCA on last-layer features.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: DP learning and neural-collapse theory both central; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural collapse meets DP fine-tuning is a rare combination.

nodes.title: On Stronger Computational Separations Between Multimodal and Unimodal Machine Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves a stronger average-case computational separation where typical tasks are hard for unimodal learning but easy for multimodal learning, and discusses its naturalness.
nodes.problem: Whether multimodal learning is provably computationally easier than unimodal learning on typical instances.
nodes.approach: Average-case computational separation proofs under cryptographic-style assumptions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of multimodal vs unimodal learning separations is very rare.

nodes.title: Individual Fairness in Graph Decomposition
nodes.tldr: Gives low-diameter decomposition algorithms for planar graphs that add individual fairness, separating comparably distant node pairs with comparable probability, tested on redistricting networks.
nodes.problem: Classic randomized low-diameter decompositions treat nearby node pairs unfairly in cluster separation.
nodes.approach: Novel decomposition algorithms trading off individual fairness, cluster connectivity, and number of clusters, with lower-bound ties to metric embeddings.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Fair graph decomposition for redistricting is a very rare theory topic.

nodes.title: SAMformer: Unlocking the Potential of Transformers in Time Series Forecasting with Sharpness-Aware Minimization and Channel-Wise Attention
nodes.tldr: A shallow lightweight transformer trained with sharpness-aware minimization and channel-wise attention, matching large foundation forecasters with far fewer parameters.
nodes.problem: Transformers underperform simple linear baselines in long-term multivariate time series forecasting.
nodes.approach: Sharpness-aware optimization of a shallow transformer with channel-wise attention to escape bad minima.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Transformer forecasting is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Position: Near to Mid-term Risks and Opportunities of Open-Source Generative AI
nodes.tldr: Argues for responsible open-sourcing of generative AI in the near term, with an openness taxonomy applied to 40 LLMs and mitigation options.
nodes.problem: Regulation of generative AI could hurt open-source development, while near-term risks are debated.
nodes.approach: Introduces an AI openness taxonomy and weighs differential benefits and risks of open versus closed models.
nodes.niche_reason: Policy analysis of open-source generative AI is specialised

nodes.title: Sequential Neural Score Estimation: Likelihood-Free Inference with Conditional Score Based Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Performs Bayesian posterior inference for simulator models by training a conditional score-based diffusion model in a sequential simulation scheme.
nodes.problem: Costly simulations for likelihood-free Bayesian inference in simulator-based models.
nodes.approach: Learns the posterior score directly with a conditional diffusion model, guiding simulations with the current posterior estimate.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Score-based simulation inference is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Do Models Explain Themselves? Counterfactual Simulatability of Natural Language Explanations
nodes.tldr: Proposes counterfactual simulatability metrics showing LLM natural-language explanations have low precision, which does not track plausibility.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether LLM explanations let humans predict how the model behaves on new inputs.
nodes.approach: LLM-generated counterfactual inputs score explanations for precision and generality.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Explanation evaluation for LLMs is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Flextron: Many-in-One Flexible Large Language Model
nodes.tldr: Converts a pretrained LLM into a nested elastic model with input-adaptive token routing, serving multiple latency targets with ~7.6% of pretraining tokens.
nodes.problem: Deploying LLMs under varied compute and latency budgets requires costly separate training runs
nodes.approach: Nested elastic sub-network structure with a sample-efficient post-training method and routing algorithms.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Elastic, deployment-flexible LLMs are specialised but established

nodes.title: Tuning-Free Stochastic Optimization
nodes.tldr: Formalizes tuning-free stochastic optimization and proves algorithms can match optimally tuned SGD up to polylog factors given only loose hints on problem parameters.
nodes.problem: Hyperparameter tuning is prohibitively costly; can algorithms self-tune to match optimally tuned SGD?
nodes.approach: Formal definition of tuning-free algorithms with upper bounds and impossibility results for convex smooth and Lipschitz settings.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Parameter-free optimization theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Optimal Deterministic Policies with Stochastic Policy Gradients
nodes.tldr: Theory of learning stochastic policies via policy gradients to deploy deterministic versions, proving global convergence to the best deterministic policy and tuning exploration.
nodes.problem: Stochastic policies are trained but deterministic ones deployed, with little theory for this practice.
nodes.approach: New framework for (hyper)policies with global convergence under gradient domination and exploration-level tradeoff analysis.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Policy gradient theory is established but a specialised subtopic.

nodes.title: Learning Exceptional Subgroups by End-to-End Maximizing KL-Divergence
nodes.tldr: SYFLOW finds exceptional subgroups end-to-end by maximizing KL divergence with normalizing flows for target distributions and a neural layer yielding interpretable subgroup descriptions.
nodes.problem: Subgroup discovery needs pre-discretized features, simple targets, and scales poorly with limited diversity.
nodes.approach: Normalizing flow models target distribution; differentiable rule layer maximizes KL divergence for interpretable subgroups.
nodes.confidence_reason: Subgroup discovery fits no seed topic well; Tabular is closest judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Differentiable subgroup discovery is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Environment Design for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Adaptive environment design for inverse RL: the learner picks environments to query the expert in, identifying the reward function faster and more robustly.
nodes.problem: Inverse RL is sample-inefficient and brittle to changes in environment dynamics.
nodes.approach: Learner repeatedly selects informative environments in which to observe expert demonstrations.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual active environment selection angle for IRL.

nodes.title: DISCRET: Synthesizing Faithful Explanations For Treatment Effect Estimation
nodes.tldr: DISCRET is a self-interpretable treatment effect estimator that synthesizes faithful rule-based explanations per sample, using them as database queries and an RL search algorithm.
nodes.problem: Individual treatment effect models lack either accuracy, explanations, or faithfulness of explanations.
nodes.approach: RL-based synthesis of rule explanations that double as database queries identifying similar subgroups.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Rule-synthesis explanations for treatment effects is an unusual combination.

nodes.title: Position: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing that AI representations across vision and language models are converging toward a shared model of reality.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether independently trained AI models represent data in increasingly similar ways.
nodes.approach: Survey of representation alignment evidence across domains, plus cross-modal distance-similarity analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: cross-domain representation convergence hypothesis, unusual framing

nodes.title: Position: Open-Endedness is Essential for Artificial Superhuman Intelligence
nodes.tldr: Argues open-endedness, defined via novelty and learnability, is essential for artificial superhuman intelligence and achievable with open-ended foundation models, noting safety implications.
nodes.problem: Creating open-ended, self-improving AI toward superhuman intelligence remains elusive.
nodes.approach: Position argument with a formal novelty-and-learnability definition and a path via foundation models.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Open-endedness as a research agenda is a rare perspective.

nodes.title: Private Truly-Everlasting Robust-Prediction
nodes.tldr: Strengthens private everlasting prediction with poisoning robustness, a relaxed privacy definition decoupling delta from time horizon, and improved constructions.
nodes.problem: Private everlasting prediction needs robustness to poisoning and privacy not degrading over endless query streams.
nodes.approach: Modified PEP definitions plus new constructions with improved sample complexity and a relaxed privacy notion.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Very narrow theoretical private-learning model with few close relatives.

nodes.title: Position: Technical Research and Talent is Needed for Effective AI Governance
nodes.tldr: Position paper surveying EU, US, and Chinese AI policies, finding technical tools lag regulatory demands, and calls for ML researcher involvement.
nodes.problem: Governance aspirations outpace the technical tooling needed to implement them.
nodes.approach: Survey public-sector policy documents and map their technical requirements against current state of the art.
nodes.niche_reason: Technical gaps in AI governance are an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model
nodes.tldr: Evolves natural-language heuristic ideas and their LLM-generated code together, producing high-performance heuristics with few LLM queries.
nodes.problem: Manually designing heuristics for combinatorial optimization is labour-intensive and expertise-dependent.
nodes.approach: Evolutionary search jointly over LLM-written thoughts and translated code for automatic heuristic design.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.confidence_reason: heuristic design via LLM evolution spans code generation and optimization
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-driven program search is a growing but specialised combinatorial niche.

nodes.title: RIME: Robust Preference-based Reinforcement Learning with Noisy Preferences
nodes.tldr: Learns rewards from noisy human preferences by filtering noisy labels with sample selection and warm-starting the reward model.
nodes.problem: Preference-based RL needs high-quality expert feedback and is not robust to noise.
nodes.approach: Sample-selection discriminator filters noisy preferences; warm-started reward model limits cumulative selection error.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Common preference-based RL variant; robustness to noisy labels.

nodes.title: Replicable Learning of Large-Margin Halfspaces
nodes.tldr: Gives efficient replicable algorithms for learning large-margin halfspaces with dimension-independent polynomial time and improved sample complexity, plus variants trading runtime for sample complexity.
nodes.problem: Learning large-margin halfspaces replicably with better sample complexity and efficiency.
nodes.approach: New replicable algorithms, including one via the DP-to-replicability reduction, with sample and time tradeoffs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Replicability in learning theory is a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Discrete Diffusion Modeling by Estimating the Ratios of the Data Distribution
nodes.tldr: Introduces score entropy, a loss extending score matching to discrete spaces, yielding SEDD discrete diffusion language models that beat prior diffusion LMs and rival GPT-2.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models underperform on discrete data like text because score matching does not extend naturally.
nodes.approach: Score entropy loss estimating ratios of the data distribution to build discrete diffusion models.
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete diffusion for text is a specialised but growing direction.

nodes.title: Convergence of Some Convex Message Passing Algorithms to a Fixed Point
nodes.tldr: Proves convex message passing methods such as TRW-S and max-sum diffusion converge to a fixed point in O(1/epsilon) iterations, via coordinate descent on piecewise-affine convex objectives.
nodes.problem: Convergence of convex message passing for MAP inference to any point was unproven.
nodes.approach: Prove convergence for coordinate descent on piecewise-affine convex objectives and show message passing methods are special cases.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Inference in graphical models theory; no exact topic, optimization closest.
nodes.niche_reason: Classical graphical-model inference convergence theory is now uncommon.

nodes.title: Interpreting and Improving Large Language Models in Arithmetic Calculation
nodes.tldr: Finds that a small set of attention heads and MLPs drive LLM arithmetic, and that selectively fine-tuning them improves math without hurting other tasks.
nodes.problem: The mechanisms LLMs use for simple arithmetic remain unclear, limiting reliability.
nodes.approach: Identifies pivotal attention heads and MLPs for operands, then selectively fine-tunes them.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic arithmetic circuits in LLMs are specialised but active

nodes.title: How Deep Networks Learn Sparse and Hierarchical Data: the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model
nodes.tldr: Introduces the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model showing sparsity yields invariance to discrete spatial transformations, linking hierarchical representation learning to performance and CNN sample complexity.
nodes.problem: Why deep networks learn high-dimensional data: link between hierarchical representations and invariance to transformations.
nodes.approach: Generative hierarchical data model with sparsity; analyze CNN sample complexity and learned representations.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-style hierarchical data models are a specialised theory direction.

nodes.title: Information Complexity of Stochastic Convex Optimization: Applications to Generalization, Memorization, and Tracing
nodes.tldr: Characterizes the tradeoff between accuracy and conditional mutual information in stochastic convex optimization, showing memorization is necessary and enabling training-sample tracing adversaries.
nodes.problem: Quantifying how much memorization is required to learn in stochastic convex optimization.
nodes.approach: CMI lower bounds for Lipschitz and strongly convex settings and an adversary identifying training samples.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Information-theoretic memorization lower bounds for SCO are rare.

nodes.title: High-Probability Convergence for Composite and Distributed Stochastic Minimization and Variational Inequalities with Heavy-Tailed Noise
nodes.tldr: New clipped stochastic methods for composite and distributed optimization and variational inequalities with tight high-probability convergence under heavy-tailed noise.
nodes.problem: High-probability convergence for composite and distributed stochastic optimization with heavy-tailed noise.
nodes.approach: Clip stochastic gradient differences in Prox-SGD and parallel methods; prove tight high-probability bounds.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised stochastic optimization theory.

nodes.title: Sharp Rates in Dependent Learning Theory: Avoiding Sample Size Deflation for the Square Loss
nodes.tldr: Proves near mixing-free learning rates for empirical risk minimization with square loss on dependent data, so mixing time only appears in an additive higher-order term.
nodes.problem: Learning rates with dependent data are deflated multiplicatively by mixing time, giving loose variance proxies.
nodes.approach: Mixed-tail generic chaining analysis in Orlicz spaces yielding instance-optimal ERM rates under beta-mixing.
