nodes.title: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
nodes.tldr: Frames LLM alignment losses like DPO as human-aware losses reflecting prospect theory, and proposes KTO, which optimizes a Kahneman-Tversky utility using only binary good/bad feedback.
nodes.problem: Alignment objectives implicitly encode human biases but differ from prospect-theoretic utilities and need paired preferences.
nodes.approach: Define HALOs and optimize a Kahneman-Tversky value function (KTO) on binary signals.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Preference-optimization variants are crowded, though the framing is distinct.

nodes.title: Tight Partial Identification of Causal Effects with Marginal Distribution of Unmeasured Confounders
nodes.tldr: Derives closed-form tight partial identification bounds for causal effects given a discrete confounder marginal, showing such information helps little as confounder cardinality grows.
nodes.problem: Partial identification of causal effects with latent confounders lacks tight bounds using confounder marginal information.
nodes.approach: Closed-form tight bounds for any confounder marginal P(U) in the discrete case, with an iff criterion.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Narrow theoretical causal inference topic.

nodes.title: ERQ: Error Reduction for Post-Training Quantization of Vision Transformers
nodes.tldr: Reduces post-training quantization error for vision transformers by sequentially fixing activation and then weight quantization error with ridge regression.
nodes.problem: PTQ for ViTs ignores the interdependence of quantized weights and activations, causing large error.
nodes.approach: Two-step: ridge-regression weight updates for activations, then iterative rounding refinement for weights.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Post-training quantization of ViTs is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Evaluation of LLMs on Syntax-Aware Code Fill-in-the-Middle Tasks
nodes.tldr: SAFIM benchmarks LLMs on syntax-aware code fill-in-the-middle with 17,720 post-cutoff examples, finding FIM pretraining and data quality matter more than model size.
nodes.problem: Existing evaluation of code fill-in-the-middle ignores syntax-aware program structures and risks contamination.
nodes.approach: Benchmark of block and conditional completions with prompt designs and syntax-aware post-processing, evaluating 15 LLMs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Code infilling evaluation is specialised within code LLMs.

nodes.title: Fast Timing-Conditioned Latent Audio Diffusion
nodes.tldr: Latent diffusion model with timing embeddings that generates variable-length 44.1kHz stereo music and sound from text prompts, fast on one GPU.
nodes.problem: Long-form stereo audio generation from text is compute-heavy and ignores variable clip duration.
nodes.approach: Latent diffusion over a fully-convolutional VAE latent, conditioned on text and timing embeddings.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Audio, Speech & Music Generation
nodes.niche_reason: Common topic: text-to-audio latent diffusion

nodes.title: Accurate LoRA-Finetuning Quantization of LLMs via Information Retention
nodes.tldr: IR-QLoRA improves accuracy of quantized LoRA-finetuned LLMs at 2-4 bits using information-calibrated quantization and an elastic connection, with tiny extra time cost.
nodes.problem: Quantized LLMs degrade and fail to benefit from LoRA finetuning.
nodes.approach: Statistics-based information calibration quantization plus finetuning-based information elastic connection for LoRA.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Quantized LoRA variants are a common, crowded direction.

nodes.title: The Perception-Robustness Tradeoff in Deterministic Image Restoration
nodes.tldr: Proves perceptual quality and measurement consistency trade off via unbounded Lipschitz constants, making deterministic restorers adversarially fragile.
nodes.problem: Deterministic inverse-problem solvers struggle to balance perceptual quality and measurement consistency.
nodes.approach: Lipschitz-constant lower-bound proof, validated on single-image super-resolution.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of perception-consistency tradeoff in restoration is specialised

nodes.title: Position: On the Societal Impact of Open Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing open-weight foundation models have distinct benefits and risks, and proposes a marginal-risk framework for assessing misuse.
nodes.problem: Public release of foundation model weights raises contested questions about societal benefits and misuse risk.
nodes.approach: Identifies five properties mediating benefits and risks, plus a framework measuring marginal risk relative to existing technology.
nodes.niche_reason: Open-weight release policy and marginal-risk analysis is specialised

nodes.title: No Dimensional Sampling Coresets for Classification
nodes.tldr: Gives the first dimension-free coreset bounds for classification via sensitivity sampling, valid for distributional inputs, iid samples and many loss functions.
nodes.problem: Coreset size for classification usually grows with data dimension, limiting optimization on small subsets.
nodes.approach: Rademacher-complexity version of sensitivity sampling yielding sample complexity bounds independent of dimension.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: theory paper; data-reduction framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Dimension-free classification coresets are a rare result

nodes.title: Sparse Inducing Points in Deep Gaussian Processes: Enhancing Modeling with Denoising Diffusion Variational Inference
nodes.tldr: Denoising Diffusion Variational Inference uses a diffusion SDE to sample posteriors over inducing points in deep Gaussian processes, with an explicit variational lower bound.
nodes.problem: Standard variational inference for inducing points in deep GPs is biased.
nodes.approach: Generate inducing-variable posterior samples with a score-matched denoising diffusion SDE and derive a new ELBO.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Combining deep GPs with diffusion-based inference is unusual.

nodes.title: FiT: Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion Model
nodes.tldr: Diffusion transformer that treats images as dynamically sized token sequences, enabling generation at arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios with training-free extrapolation.
nodes.problem: Diffusion transformers fail on image resolutions and aspect ratios outside their trained domain.
nodes.approach: Dynamic-size token sequences with a flexible training strategy and training-free extrapolation.
nodes.niche_reason: diffusion transformers are a mainstream area

nodes.title: BBox-Adapter: Lightweight Adapting for Black-Box Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: BBox-Adapter adapts black-box LLMs via a lightweight adapter trained with ranking-based NCE, treating target data as positive and source as negative, with online adaptation.
nodes.problem: Black-box API-only LLMs cannot be fine-tuned with parameters, embeddings, or output probabilities.
nodes.approach: Ranking-based noise contrastive estimation adapter with online positive and negative sampling from feedback.
nodes.niche_reason: Adapting API-only black-box models is a specialised setting.

nodes.title: Efficient Precision and Recall Metrics for Assessing Generative Models using Hubness-aware Sampling
nodes.tldr: Efficient precision and recall metrics for generative models using hubness-aware sampling and approximate nearest neighbors, matching original P&R at far lower cost.
nodes.problem: Precision and recall metrics for generative models become computationally infeasible as dataset size grows.
nodes.approach: Hubness-aware sampling removes redundancy in ratio computation and manifold membership, combined with approximate k-NN.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Generative-model metrics are a specialised evaluation niche.

nodes.title: FedMBridge: Bridgeable Multimodal Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: FedMBridge uses a topology-aware hypernetwork to bridge statistical and architecture heterogeneity in multimodal federated learning with personalized client architectures.
nodes.problem: Multimodal federated learning with heterogeneous data and unrestricted client model architectures.
nodes.approach: Topology-aware hypernetwork generating client models and sharing information communication-efficiently.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised multimodal federated learning setting.

nodes.title: Position: Measure Dataset Diversity, Don't Just Claim It
nodes.tldr: Argues dataset diversity claims lack definitions; analyzes 135 image and text datasets and applies measurement theory to recommend how to conceptualize and evaluate diversity.
nodes.problem: Dataset curators claim diversity, bias and quality without clear definitions or validation.
nodes.approach: Survey of 135 datasets plus measurement-theory recommendations for operationalizing and evaluating diversity.
nodes.confidence_reason: Position paper spanning dataset curation, evaluation and fairness.
nodes.niche_reason: Applies social-science measurement theory to dataset practice, an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Listenable Maps for Audio Classifiers
nodes.tldr: Trains a decoder on a frozen audio classifier to output binary masks that highlight the input regions driving the decision, yielding faithful, listenable explanations.
nodes.problem: Deep audio classifiers are hard to interpret, and gradient or masking explanations are often unfaithful.
nodes.approach: Trained decoder masks the audio, maximizing classifier confidence on the kept part and minimizing it on the removed part.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Audio-specific explainability is less explored than image explainability

nodes.title: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
nodes.tldr: TravelPlanner is a benchmark with a sandbox and millions of records where language agents plan trips under constraints, and even GPT-4 succeeds only 0.6%.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether LLM language agents can handle complex, real-world multi-constraint planning beyond prior constrained agents.
nodes.approach: Travel-planning sandbox with tools over about four million records and 1,225 curated planning intents with reference plans.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: LLM agent benchmarks are common; travel planning is a specific scenario

nodes.title: Self-Alignment of Large Language Models via Monopolylogue-based Social Scene Simulation
nodes.tldr: LLMs align themselves by simulating social scenes around a query and fine-tuning on the resulting consequence-aware data, outperforming baselines.
nodes.problem: Aligning LLMs with human values while accounting for all affected parties' concerns.
nodes.approach: Monopolylogue-style social scene simulator generates data for LLM self-alignment fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Social-simulation-based self-alignment is a distinctive angle on alignment.

nodes.title: Inferring the Long-Term Causal Effects of Long-Term Treatments from Short-Term Experiments
nodes.tldr: Estimates long-term causal effects of continual treatments from short-term experiments by linking the problem to offline RL with doubly-robust estimators and confidence intervals.
nodes.problem: Surrogate methods fail when a continual treatment directly affects long-term outcomes, yet only short-term data exist.
nodes.approach: Cast as offline RL and use doubly-robust estimators for estimation and inference.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Long-term treatment effect inference via offline RL is rare.

nodes.title: Predictive Linear Online Tracking for Unknown Targets
nodes.tldr: PLOT learns a time-varying model of an unknown moving target by recursive least squares, then uses receding-horizon control, with dynamic regret bounds and quadrotor demo.
nodes.problem: Online tracking of an unknown, non-stationary target in linear control systems.
nodes.approach: Recursive least squares with exponential forgetting feeding a receding-horizon optimal controller.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Online non-stochastic control theory with hardware is uncommon.

nodes.title: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Smooth Optimization under the Polyak–Łojasiewicz Condition
nodes.tldr: Proves lower bounds on incremental first-order oracle calls for finite-sum PL optimization and proposes a decentralized method nearly matching them.
nodes.problem: Complexity of optimizing finite sums under the PL condition, centralized and distributed, is unclear.
nodes.approach: Oracle-complexity lower-bound constructions plus a decentralized first-order method on mixing networks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised optimization complexity theory, established but narrow

nodes.title: Mean-field Chaos Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Applies mean-field propagation-of-chaos theory to score-based diffusion, treating high-cardinality data as interacting particles to make training scale to large point clouds.
nodes.problem: Score-based models suffer the curse of dimensionality on high-cardinality data distributions.
nodes.approach: Score matching for infinite-dimensional chaotic particle systems with a subdivision strategy for efficient training.
nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field diffusion for point clouds is very unusual.

nodes.title: Jetfire: Efficient and Accurate Transformer Pretraining with INT8 Data Flow and Per-Block Quantization
nodes.tldr: Proposes Jetfire, an INT8 transformer pretraining method with an INT8 data flow and per-block quantization for faster, accurate training.
nodes.problem: Fully quantized transformer pretraining gives poor speedup and accuracy loss due to memory overhead.
nodes.approach: INT8 data flow across the transformer block with per-block quantization.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient low-precision training is a crowded mainstream area.

nodes.title: Challenges in Training PINNs: A Loss Landscape Perspective
nodes.tldr: Shows PINN training is hard because differential operators make the loss ill-conditioned, and proposes the second-order NysNewton-CG optimizer plus Adam+L-BFGS.
nodes.problem: Physics-informed neural networks are hard to train due to ill-conditioned loss landscapes.
nodes.approach: Loss-landscape analysis, Adam+L-BFGS comparison, and a Nystrom-preconditioned Newton-CG optimizer.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised scientific ML optimization focus.

nodes.title: Rethinking Data Shapley for Data Selection Tasks: Misleads and Merits
nodes.tldr: Shows Data Shapley can perform no better than random selection without utility constraints, and identifies monotone-transformed modular utilities where it is optimal.
nodes.problem: Data Shapley's data selection performance is inconsistent across settings.
nodes.approach: Hypothesis testing framework and analysis of utility function classes for data valuation.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Focused analysis of a specific valuation method

nodes.title: WebLINX: Real-World Website Navigation with Multi-Turn Dialogue
nodes.tldr: Benchmark of 100K multi-turn interactions for conversational web navigation, plus a retrieval-style HTML pruning model for LLM web agents.
nodes.problem: LLMs cannot process full web pages in real time, and finetuned agents fail to generalize to unseen websites.
nodes.approach: Retrieval-inspired model ranks and prunes HTML elements, then evaluates text and multimodal models on expert demonstrations.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Conversational web navigation benchmarking is a less crowded agent direction

nodes.title: Repoformer: Selective Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Completion
nodes.tldr: Trains a code LM to decide when retrieval helps and when to skip it, cutting inference cost up to 70% without hurting completion quality.
nodes.problem: Always-on retrieval in repo-level code completion often wastes compute and can hurt generation with unhelpful contexts.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised selective RAG where the same code LM self-evaluates whether to retrieve and uses noisy contexts.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Retrieval for code completion is an active, fairly crowded direction

nodes.title: Gambling-Based Confidence Sequences for Bounded Random Vectors
nodes.tldr: Builds confidence sequences for bounded multivariate means via a gambling framework with mixture-portfolio strategies, tighter than prior methods.
nodes.problem: Constructing anytime-valid confidence sequences for bounded multivariate stochastic processes.
nodes.approach: Gambling-based betting framework using mixture (universal) portfolio strategies.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.confidence_reason: Statistical vs online-learning topic is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised statistical inference; few ML papers resemble it

nodes.title: Rejuvenating image-GPT as Strong Visual Representation Learners
nodes.tldr: D-iGPT improves autoregressive image pretraining by predicting semantic tokens from CLIP-like models plus visible tokens, reaching 90% ImageNet top-1.
nodes.problem: Pixel-level autoregressive pretraining learns weak visual representations.
nodes.approach: Autoregressive prediction of semantic tokens plus visible-token prediction with ViT.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive visual pretraining is established, with many variants.

nodes.title: Parameterized Physics-informed Neural Networks for Parameterized PDEs
nodes.tldr: P2INNs extend physics-informed neural networks by encoding PDE parameters in a latent representation, giving accurate, parameter-efficient surrogates for parameterized PDEs.
nodes.problem: PINNs need repeated retraining to solve PDEs across many parameter values.
nodes.approach: Parameterized PINN with explicit latent encoding of PDE parameters.
nodes.niche_reason: PINN variants are established; parameterized setting is specialised.

nodes.title: Decoding-time Realignment of Language Models
nodes.tldr: Decoding-time Realignment interpolates between aligned and reference models at inference to tune KL regularization strength without retraining multiple models.
nodes.problem: Choosing RLHF regularization strength requires costly retraining across values.
nodes.approach: Linearly interpolate logits of reference and aligned models at decoding time.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Alignment tuning variant in a crowded RLHF space.

nodes.title: Adaptive Online Experimental Design for Causal Discovery
nodes.tldr: Formalizes causal discovery as online pure exploration and proposes a track-and-stop algorithm choosing interventions from a graph separating system, with problem-dependent sample complexity bounds.
nodes.problem: Existing causal discovery assumes infinite interventional data and ignores intervention sample efficiency.
nodes.approach: Adaptive track-and-stop intervention selection via allocation matching with a confidence-based stopping rule.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Bandit-style adaptive experimental design for causal graphs is uncommon.

nodes.title: Position: Considerations for Differentially Private Learning with Large-Scale Public Pretraining
nodes.tldr: Position paper questioning whether pretraining on large web-scraped public data should count as privacy-preserving in differentially private learning, and whether benchmarks suit sensitive-domain evaluation.
nodes.problem: Differentially private learning with public pretraining may overstate privacy and rely on inappropriate benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Critical review and argumentation about public pretraining assumptions, benchmark suitability, and outsourcing of data.
nodes.niche_reason: Differential privacy is established; public-pretraining critique is specialised.

nodes.title: LLM Maybe LongLM: SelfExtend LLM Context Window Without Tuning
nodes.tldr: SelfExtend extends LLM context windows without fine-tuning by combining grouped attention for distant tokens with neighbor attention for nearby tokens at inference.
nodes.problem: LLMs fail to generalize to inputs longer than the training length.
nodes.approach: Bi-level attention using the model's own self-attention with grouped and neighbor positions, needing minimal code changes.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Context extension is a common direction.

nodes.title: Position: Amazing Things Come From Having Many Good Models
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing the Rashomon effect, many equally good models, should reshape tabular ML around fairness, uncertainty and variable importance.
nodes.problem: Model multiplicity is usually treated as a nuisance rather than a resource in predictive ML.
nodes.approach: Conceptual position arguing consequences of many near-optimal models for practice and policy.
nodes.niche_reason: Rashomon-effect perspective is rare in mainstream ML.

nodes.title: Preference Optimization for Molecule Synthesis with Conditional Residual Energy-based Models
nodes.tldr: Adds a conditional residual energy-based model to reweight retrosynthetic routes by criteria like cost, yield, and step count, improving top-1 accuracy by 2.5%.
nodes.problem: Greedy retrosynthetic route search lacks lookahead and cannot control routes by cost, yield, or steps.
nodes.approach: Plug-and-play conditional residual energy-based model scoring entire synthetic routes under chosen criteria.
nodes.confidence_reason: energy-based route reweighting spans chemistry application and generative modelling
nodes.niche_reason: Retrosynthesis is established; energy-based route-level reweighting is specialised.

nodes.title: DRCT: Diffusion Reconstruction Contrastive Training towards Universal Detection of Diffusion Generated Images
nodes.tldr: Improves generated-image detectors by contrastively training on hard diffusion-reconstruction samples, with a million-scale dataset.
nodes.problem: Detectors of diffusion-generated images lose accuracy badly on images from unseen diffusion models.
nodes.approach: Diffusion reconstruction creates hard negatives, trained with contrastive learning to capture diffusion artifacts.
nodes.confidence_reason: detection could sit under provenance or image classification
nodes.niche_reason: AI-generated image detection, a specialised safety niche

nodes.title: A Theory of Fault-Tolerant Learning
nodes.tldr: Introduces fault-tolerant PAC learning: random faults match standard PAC, but adversarial faults can cost linear sample complexity in perturbation functions, improvable for deletion faults.
nodes.problem: Formalizing and bounding learnability of models robust to hardware or environmental faults.
nodes.approach: PAC-style framework with sample complexity upper and lower bounds under adversarial perturbation functions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Rare learning-theory framing of fault tolerance.

nodes.title: Theoretical Analysis of Learned Database Operations under Distribution Shift through Distribution Learnability
nodes.tldr: Gives the first theoretical characterization of learned database operations (indexing, cardinality estimation, sorting) under distribution shift, via a distribution learnability framework with performance bounds.
nodes.problem: Learned database operations degrade under data distribution shift with no theoretical guarantees.
nodes.approach: Develop the distribution learnability framework and new tools to bound learned model performance on dynamic datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of learned database components is very rare.

nodes.title: InterpreTabNet: Distilling Predictive Signals from Tabular Data by Salient Feature Interpretation
nodes.tldr: Models TabNet attention as a Gumbel-Softmax latent variable with a KL regularizer for sparse feature masks, and uses GPT-4 to describe them in text.
nodes.problem: TabNet attention masks are dense, making predictive rationales hard to read.
nodes.approach: Gumbel-Softmax latent attention with KL sparsity regularizer, then LLM-based mask explanation.
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse-attention interpretable tabular models are specialised.

nodes.title: PRISE: LLM-Style Sequence Compression for Learning Temporal Action Abstractions in Control
nodes.tldr: PRISE treats skill discovery as sequence compression: quantizes continuous actions and applies byte pair encoding to learn temporal action abstractions that boost behavior cloning.
nodes.problem: Learning variable-length temporal action abstractions from multitask demonstrations
nodes.approach: Continuous action quantization combined with byte pair encoding to induce skill tokens
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual borrowing of LLM tokenization for control skills

nodes.title: Prospective Side Information for Latent MDPs
nodes.tldr: Studies latent MDPs where agents receive weakly revealing context each episode, proving an Omega(K^{2/3}) regret lower bound and a matching algorithm.
nodes.problem: Latent-context decision problems lack a framework between fully observed and fully hidden contexts.
nodes.approach: Regret lower bound and matching algorithm for the prospective side-information setting.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Latent MDPs with prospective side information interpolate a rarely studied setting.

nodes.title: Position: Understanding LLMs Requires More Than Statistical Generalization
nodes.tldr: Argues LLM capabilities like in-context learning and rule extrapolation need separate theory, because autoregressive models are non-identifiable and equal-loss models can differ.
nodes.problem: Some desirable LLM qualities may not follow from statistical generalization, yet theory mostly explains generalization alone.
nodes.approach: Argues autoregressive models are non-identifiable and illustrates it with three case studies.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Non-identifiability as an LLM theory lens is an unusual perspective.

nodes.title: Towards Optimal Adversarial Robust Q-learning with Bellman Infinity-error
nodes.tldr: Proves an optimal robust policy exists under state perturbations and shows Bellman infinity-norm error is needed; trains CAR-DQN minimizing a surrogate of it.
nodes.problem: Existence and training of optimal state-adversarially robust policies in deep RL.
nodes.approach: Consistency assumption for policy, proof of deterministic robust policy, and L-infinity Bellman error surrogate in DQN.
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial robust RL theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Emergent Equivariance in Deep Ensembles
nodes.tldr: Proves via neural tangent kernel theory that data-augmented deep ensembles become equivariant at infinite width, though individual members are not.
nodes.problem: Can equivariance arise without architectural constraints, only from data augmentation?
nodes.approach: NTK analysis of infinite-width ensembles under data augmentation, supported by numerical experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariance emerging in ensembles via NTK is unusual.

nodes.title: ACM-MILP: Adaptive Constraint Modification via Grouping and Selection for Hardness-Preserving MILP Instance Generation
nodes.tldr: Generates hardness-preserving MILP instances by grouping strongly related constraints via community detection and modifying them collectively.
nodes.problem: Scarce real MILP data limits learning methods, and random single-constraint edits break problem structure.
nodes.approach: Latent-space adaptive constraint selection plus community-detected constraint groups for collective modifications.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic MILP instance generation is a rare niche

nodes.title: Estimating Unknown Population Sizes Using the Hypergeometric Distribution
nodes.tldr: Estimates unknown population and category sizes from sampling without replacement, using a hypergeometric likelihood inside a VAE, even under sparse data.
nodes.problem: Estimating discrete distributions when population and category sizes are unknown.
nodes.approach: Hypergeometric likelihood within a VAE that models latent mixtures.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles probabilistic estimation and VAE generative modeling.
nodes.niche_reason: Hypergeometric likelihood for unknown population sizes is rare.

nodes.title: Defining Neural Network Architecture through Polytope Structures of Datasets
nodes.tldr: Derives upper and lower bounds on neural network width from a dataset's polytope structure, and an algorithm that infers that structure from trained networks.
nodes.problem: How wide a neural network must be to classify a dataset is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Polytope-geometry width bounds for simplicial complexes and manifolds, plus an inverse algorithm from trained networks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory result about architecture width; topic boundary is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Polytope-geometry view of width bounds is an unusual angle

nodes.title: Pausing Policy Learning in Non-stationary Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows that deliberately pausing policy updates in non-stationary online RL can reduce dynamic regret and improve reward over continuous updating.
nodes.problem: Real-time RL in time-varying environments suffers a temporal gap between data collection, updates, and deployment.
nodes.approach: Forecasting-based online RL with a computed optimal ratio of update to hold duration.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Non-stationary policy scheduling could be RL theory or algorithms.
nodes.niche_reason: Deliberate policy hold in non-stationary RL is an unusual direction

nodes.title: PriorBoost: An Adaptive Algorithm for Learning from Aggregate Responses
nodes.tldr: PriorBoost adaptively forms aggregation bags of increasingly homogeneous samples for learning from aggregate responses, with theory for linear models and GLMs and label-DP analysis.
nodes.problem: How to construct aggregation bags for event-level loss when only aggregate labels are observed.
nodes.approach: Reduce optimal bagging to 1D size-constrained k-means and adaptively form homogeneous bags.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Aggregate-response learning is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Memory Consolidation Enables Long-Context Video Understanding
nodes.tldr: Extends pretrained video transformers to long temporal context by fine-tuning them to attend to compressed memories of past activations.
nodes.problem: Video transformers have quadratic cost and short temporal context, limiting long-video understanding.
nodes.approach: Non-parametric memory from past activations, redundancy-reduced and consolidated into a fine-tuned ViT.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Long-context video transformers are increasingly common

nodes.title: Test-Time Model Adaptation with Only Forward Passes
nodes.tldr: Adapts quantized, hard-coded vision models at test time by learning only an input prompt with evolution strategies, avoiding backpropagation.
nodes.problem: Test-time adaptation needs backpropagation, which quantized edge models cannot support.
nodes.approach: Learn an added input prompt via CMA-ES, with fitness from feature-statistics discrepancy and entropy.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Gradient-free test-time adaptation is specialised.

nodes.title: Closing the Gap: Achieving Global Convergence (Last Iterate) of Actor-Critic under Markovian Sampling with Neural Network Parametrization
nodes.tldr: Provides global last-iterate convergence for actor-critic with multi-layer networks, Markovian sampling and continuous spaces, with O(eps^-3) sample complexity.
nodes.problem: Actor-critic theory ignores practical settings like neural parametrisation, Markovian sampling and continuous spaces.
nodes.approach: Weak gradient domination of MDPs with a careful analysis of critic estimation error.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Actor-critic convergence theory is established but specialised

nodes.title: Transport of Algebraic Structure to Latent Embeddings
nodes.tldr: Learns latent-space set operations like union that provably respect algebraic laws such as associativity, via a bijection to a mirrored algebra.
nodes.problem: Latent embeddings of sets do not respect the algebraic laws of their input space.
nodes.approach: Learned bijection from latent space to a mirrored algebra with the desired laws.
nodes.confidence_reason: Thin abstract; representation vs. algebra topic is ambiguous.
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual angle: enforcing algebraic laws on latent embedding operations.

nodes.title: Expressivity and Generalization: Fragment-Biases for Molecular GNNs
nodes.tldr: Fragment-WL extends the Weisfeiler-Leman test to analyze fragment-biased molecular GNNs and yields a more expressive architecture.
nodes.problem: Fragment-biased molecular GNNs perform well but lack any expressivity theory.
nodes.approach: Fragment-WL extends Weisfeiler-Leman; new GNN uses infinite-vocabulary fragmentation for expressiveness.
nodes.niche_reason: Expressivity theory for fragment-biased molecular GNNs is specialised

nodes.title: Position: Intent-aligned AI Systems Must Optimize for Agency Preservation
nodes.tldr: Argues that aligning AI only to human intent is insufficient and that long-term human agency should be explicitly optimized, with a formal definition.
nodes.problem: Intent-aligned AI may erode long-term human agency and enable manipulation.
nodes.approach: Formal agency-preserving definition with forward-looking explicit agency evaluations.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Agency preservation as a distinct alignment target is unusual

nodes.title: Designing Decision Support Systems using Counterfactual Prediction Sets
nodes.tldr: Designs decision support via conformal prediction sets using online learning with counterfactual monotonicity, achieving exponentially better regret than bandits, validated by a 2,751-person human study.
nodes.problem: Decision support systems need design methods without stylized expert models.
nodes.approach: Online learning over nested conformal prediction sets using counterfactual monotonicity, evaluated with a human subject study.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans bandits, conformal prediction, and human-AI decision support.
nodes.niche_reason: Human-AI decision support with conformal sets is unusual.

nodes.title: AlphaFold Meets Flow Matching for Generating Protein Ensembles
nodes.tldr: AlphaFlow and ESMFlow fine-tune AlphaFold/ESMFold under flow matching to generate sequence-conditioned protein conformational ensembles, rivaling MD at faster convergence.
nodes.problem: Single-state structure predictors cannot sample dynamic protein conformational ensembles.
nodes.approach: Fine-tune AlphaFold/ESMFold within a flow matching framework, optionally trained on MD ensembles.
nodes.niche_reason: Protein ensemble generation is specialised but active.

nodes.title: Dynamic Facility Location in High Dimensional Euclidean Spaces
nodes.tldr: Gives the first fully dynamic facility location algorithm for high-dimensional Euclidean space, with O(c) approximation and sublinear amortized update time.
nodes.problem: Maintaining a stable, high-quality facility location solution under point insertions and deletions in high dimensions.
nodes.approach: Dynamic nearest-neighbour oracles give sublinear update time with O(1) amortized recourse.
nodes.confidence_reason: Theoretical algorithms paper; no clear ML topic fits well
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamic high-dimensional clustering is a rare ML-adjacent niche

nodes.title: LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima
nodes.tldr: Proves that LoRA fine-tuning in the NTK regime has no spurious local minima when rank exceeds about the square root of N.
nodes.problem: Theory of LoRA fine-tuning is limited; gradient descent may get stuck in spurious local minima.
nodes.approach: NTK-regime analysis over N data points, comparing full fine-tuning against LoRA of varying rank.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: theory of LoRA training dynamics, specialised

nodes.title: High-Performance Temporal Reversible Spiking Neural Networks with $\mathcal{O}(L)$ Training Memory and $\mathcal{O}(1)$ Inference Cost
nodes.tldr: Makes spiking neural networks temporally reversible so training memory is O(L) and inference energy O(1), keeping ImageNet accuracy.
nodes.problem: Multi-timestep SNN simulation inflates training memory and inference energy.
nodes.approach: Turns off temporal dynamics in most neurons and adds reversible temporal interactions at the remaining neurons.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: SNNs are a specialised neuromorphic area; memory-reversible design is distinctive.

nodes.title: Fundamental Benefit of Alternating Updates in Minimax Optimization
nodes.tldr: Proves alternating gradient descent-ascent converges faster than simultaneous updates and introduces Alex-GDA, which matches extragradient rates with fewer gradients.
nodes.problem: Why alternating gradient descent-ascent is faster than simultaneous updates is not understood.
nodes.approach: Fine-grained convergence analysis for strongly-convex-strongly-concave objectives, plus extrapolated alternating updates.
nodes.niche_reason: Minimax convergence analysis is established but specialised

nodes.title: Candidate Pseudolabel Learning: Enhancing Vision-Language Models by Prompt Tuning with Unlabeled Data
nodes.tldr: Fine-tunes vision-language models on unlabeled data by generating refined candidate pseudolabels instead of hard ones, improving label inclusion and class balance.
nodes.problem: Pseudolabeling fails when zero-shot VLMs are weak, producing many incorrect hard pseudolabels.
nodes.approach: Progressively generate refined candidate pseudolabels via intra- and inter-instance label selection from a confidence matrix.
nodes.niche_reason: Pseudolabeling and prompt tuning of CLIP-style models is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Low-Cost High-Power Membership Inference Attacks
nodes.tldr: RMIA is a membership inference attack using a refined likelihood-ratio null with reference models and population samples, powerful even at low FPR.
nodes.problem: Membership inference attacks are either costly or low-powered at low false-positive rates.
nodes.approach: Fine-grained null-hypothesis likelihood ratio test leveraging reference models and population data.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Membership inference is established; specialised privacy subfield.

nodes.title: Pruned Pivot: Correlation Clustering Algorithm for Dynamic, Parallel, and Local Computation Models
nodes.tldr: Gives correlation clustering algorithms that run dynamically, in parallel (MPC) and locally (LCA), with constant amortized update time and Pivot-level approximation.
nodes.problem: Correlation clustering on large, constantly changing graphs
nodes.approach: Dynamic and local variant of the Pivot algorithm
nodes.confidence_reason: Combinatorial graph algorithm; closest vocab topics are approximate fits.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare algorithmic niche with few ML-mainstream analogues

nodes.title: APT: Adaptive Pruning and Tuning Pretrained Language Models for Efficient Training and Inference
nodes.tldr: Jointly prunes and tunes pretrained language models, adding salient tuning parameters early and discarding unimportant ones for faster training and inference.
nodes.problem: Fine-tuning LMs is memory-costly, and structured pruning speeds inference but often increases training cost.
nodes.approach: Adaptive pruning and tuning: dynamically add salient tuning parameters while removing unimportant ones during fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Pruning and PEFT for LM fine-tuning is a crowded direction.

nodes.title: ULAREF: A Unified Label Refinement Framework for Learning with Inaccurate Supervision
nodes.tldr: Proposes a unified label-refinement framework that handles many forms of inaccurate supervision by detecting unreliable labels and enhancing them with a consistency-trained model.
nodes.problem: Weakly supervised learning uses separate specialized algorithms for each type of inaccurate label annotation.
nodes.approach: Global reliability detection, then local enhancement via a model fine-tuned with a proposed consistency loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Weak-supervision topic fits no single area cleanly
nodes.niche_reason: Noisy and weak label learning is a well-trodden area

nodes.title: A Touch, Vision, and Language Dataset for Multimodal Alignment
nodes.tldr: Releases a 44K vision-touch dataset with language labels and trains a tactile encoder and touch-vision-language model that outperforms GPT-4V on a touch-vision benchmark.
nodes.problem: Touch is absent from multimodal language models, partly because tactile data lacks natural language labels.
nodes.approach: Human and GPT-4V pseudo-labeled vision-touch pairs train an aligned tactile encoder and a TVL text-generation model.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Touch-vision-language modelling is a rare cross-modal angle

nodes.title: Fast Sampling-Based Sketches for Tensors
nodes.tldr: Fast sampling-based sketches for two- and three-mode tensors, enabling l0 sampling and l1 embeddings on rank-one tensors in time scaling with d instead of d^q.
nodes.problem: Applying sampling-based sketches to tensors is too slow for rank-one inputs.
nodes.approach: Sampling construction based on fast convolution to compute sums over random subsets of tensor entries.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical sketching algorithms for tensors are very rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: Offline Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning Scales to Large Models
nodes.tldr: Shows offline actor-critic RL with Perceiver-based transformers scales like supervised learning and beats behavior cloning on 132 multi-task continuous control tasks, including real robots.
nodes.problem: Whether offline RL can scale to large models and outperform behavioral cloning on large mixed-quality multi-task datasets.
nodes.approach: Perceiver-based actor-critic with self- and cross-attention, trained with simple offline actor-critic algorithms on large datasets.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL is a common topic; scaling angle is fairly mainstream.

nodes.title: Pairwise Alignment Improves Graph Domain Adaptation
nodes.tldr: Pair-Align addresses graph domain adaptation by reweighting edges for conditional structure shift and label weights for label shift, with theoretical justification.
nodes.problem: Graph models generalize poorly when train and test graphs differ in connection patterns and labels.
nodes.approach: Edge-weight recalibration for conditional structure shift plus label-weighted loss for label shift.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Graph-specific distribution shift is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Faithfulness Measurable Masked Language Models
nodes.tldr: Fine-tunes masked language models so masked tokens stay in-distribution, making token-importance explanations cheap to measure for faithfulness.
nodes.problem: Measuring faithfulness of token-importance explanations via masking is out-of-distribution and expensive.
nodes.approach: Fine-tuning with masking so masked inputs are in-distribution, enabling cheap faithfulness measurement.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Faithfulness of NLP explanations is an established but specialised subfield.

nodes.title: Masked Face Recognition with Generative-to-Discriminative Representations
nodes.tldr: Learns occlusion-robust masked face representations by pretraining a generative inpainting encoder, then a discriminative reformer distilled from a face recognition model.
nodes.problem: Recognizing faces under diverse mask occlusions with insufficient or inaccurate representations.
nodes.approach: Greedy module-wise training: generative encoder, discriminative reformer with relation distillation, then classifier.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Masked face recognition is a specialised application.

nodes.title: Any-Precision LLM: Low-Cost Deployment of Multiple, Different-Sized LLMs
nodes.tldr: Any-precision quantization of LLMs overlays models of different bit-widths into one memory footprint, with a custom serving engine, cutting cost of deploying multiple model sizes.
nodes.problem: High cost of deploying multiple differently sized LLMs simultaneously.
nodes.approach: Post-training any-precision quantization overlaying 3..n-bit models in one n-bit footprint plus specialised inference engine.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Quantization is crowded but multi-model overlay deployment is specialised.

nodes.title: Compressible Dynamics in Deep Overparameterized Low-Rank Learning & Adaptation
nodes.tldr: Shows overparameterized low-rank weight dynamics stay in low-dimensional subspaces, enabling compact factorizations that match overparameterized training and inspiring Deep LoRA.
nodes.problem: Overparameterization helps optimization and generalization but raises compute costs as models grow.
nodes.approach: Train compact deep factorizations confined to invariant subspaces, applied to matrix completion and LLM fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.confidence_reason: Low-rank training dynamics theory plus fine-tuning method; two topics
nodes.niche_reason: Deep low-rank factorization dynamics is a specialised theory niche

nodes.title: Less is More: on the Over-Globalizing Problem in Graph Transformers
nodes.tldr: Shows global attention in graph transformers over-weights distant nodes, and proposes CoBFormer, a bi-level inter/intra-cluster transformer with collaborative training.
nodes.problem: Global attention in graph transformers overly focuses on distant nodes, hurting useful local information.
nodes.approach: Bi-level transformer with inter-cluster and intra-cluster modules trained collaboratively.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph transformers are a common research line.

nodes.title: Conformal prediction for multi-dimensional time series by ellipsoidal sets
nodes.tldr: MultiDimSPCI is a sequential conformal prediction method building ellipsoidal prediction regions for multivariate non-exchangeable time series with finite-sample coverage-gap bounds.
nodes.problem: Valid conformal prediction regions for multivariate time series responses, which are non-exchangeable.
nodes.approach: Sequential conformal prediction with ellipsoidal sets using multivariate residual scoring.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Conformal prediction for time series is established but specialised.

nodes.title: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
nodes.tldr: Models LLM agents as computational graphs and automatically optimizes node prompts and graph connectivity to improve agent orchestration.
nodes.problem: Prompt-engineering agent designs are disparate code bases with no unified, optimizable structure.
nodes.approach: Graph optimizers refining node prompts and rewiring edges between agent operations.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: LLM agent design is an active, crowded area.

nodes.title: A Dynamic Algorithm for Weighted Submodular Cover Problem
nodes.tldr: Gives a randomized dynamic algorithm for weighted submodular cover under insertions and deletions, with polylogarithmic query cost per update.
nodes.problem: Maintaining near-optimal submodular cover solutions as ground-set elements are inserted and deleted.
nodes.approach: Randomized algorithm giving a bicriteria approximation with polylogarithmic query complexity per update.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.confidence_reason: Dynamic submodular optimization sits between optimization and online learning
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamic weighted submodular cover is a rare algorithmic niche

nodes.title: Tabular Insights, Visual Impacts: Transferring Expertise from Tables to Images
nodes.tldr: Charms aligns image channels with tabular attributes via optimal transport, transferring expert tabular knowledge to improve image classifiers without tabular inputs at test time.
nodes.problem: Expert tabular data is unavailable at inference, yet could help image-based predictions.
nodes.approach: Optimal-transport channel-attribute alignment maximising mutual information for numeric and categorical features.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.confidence_reason: cross-modal transfer straddles representation learning and optimal transport
nodes.niche_reason: unusual tabular-to-vision knowledge transfer

nodes.title: Locality-Sensitive Hashing-Based Efficient Point Transformer with Applications in High-Energy Physics
nodes.tldr: HEPT is a locality-sensitive-hashing-based efficient point transformer with near-linear complexity for large-scale point clouds, outperforming GNNs and transformers on high-energy physics tasks.
nodes.problem: Efficient, accurate transformers for large scientific point clouds in high-energy physics.
nodes.approach: E2LSH with OR and AND constructions for kernel approximation, using regular hardware-friendly operations.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare high-energy physics point cloud transformer application.

nodes.title: Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator
nodes.tldr: Has language models write pseudocode that an interpreter runs, with the LM simulating undefined semantic steps, improving reasoning over chain-of-thought.
nodes.problem: Chain-of-thought struggles with reasoning tasks that mix logic and semantic judgments.
nodes.approach: Generate code, have an interpreter flag undefined calls, and emulate them with the LM as an LMulator.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Code-based LLM reasoning is a common prompting direction

nodes.title: Stereographic Spherical Sliced Wasserstein Distances
nodes.tldr: Introduces Stereographic Spherical Sliced Wasserstein distance using stereographic projection and generalized Radon transform for fast comparison of spherical distributions.
nodes.problem: Efficiently comparing probability measures on the sphere
nodes.approach: Stereographic projection with generalized Radon transform for sliced Wasserstein
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Spherical sliced OT is a rare mathematical niche.

nodes.title: Local vs. Global Interpretability: A Computational Complexity Perspective
nodes.tldr: Uses computational complexity theory to show local and global explanations are duality-linked, and which is harder to compute depends on the model class.
nodes.problem: Many known local versus global interpretability results are informal or lack rigorous proofs.
nodes.approach: Proves a local-global duality and computes explanation complexity for linear models, decision trees and neural networks.

nodes.niche_reason: Complexity-theoretic analysis of explanations is a rare angle

nodes.title: CompeteAI: Understanding the Competition Dynamics of Large Language Model-based Agents
nodes.tldr: Proposes a framework and GPT-4 simulated virtual town where restaurant agents compete for customers, revealing competition dynamics that align with market and sociological theory.
nodes.problem: Little is known about competition, as opposed to cooperation, among LLM-based agents.

nodes.niche_reason: Competition among LLM agents is less studied than cooperation.

nodes.title: Minimax Optimality of Score-based Diffusion Models: Beyond the Density Lower Bound Assumptions
nodes.tldr: Shows a kernel-based score estimator achieves optimal error and proves near minimax optimality of diffusion models under only sub-Gaussian assumptions, removing density lower bound requirements.

nodes.title: How Private are DP-SGD Implementations?
nodes.tldr: Shows shuffling-based DP-SGD has a substantial privacy gap versus the Poisson subsampling accounting usually applied, so reported guarantees may be overstated.

nodes.title: Transformers Learn Nonlinear Features In Context: Nonconvex Mean-field Dynamics on the Attention Landscape
nodes.tldr: Proves that mean-field gradient flow for an MLP-plus-linear-attention transformer has a benign nonconvex landscape and avoids saddle points for in-context learning.
nodes.problem: Existing in-context learning theory covers only single-layer attention on linear regression, not nonlinear feature-augmented transformers.
nodes.approach: Mean-field and two-timescale analysis of Wasserstein gradient flow, with second-order stability of the dynamics.

nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field analysis of in-context transformers is rare

nodes.title: Position: Reinforcement Learning in Dynamic Treatment Regimes Needs Critical Reexamination
nodes.tldr: Critically examines offline RL for dynamic treatment regimes, showing evaluation choices can make RL lose to random baselines on a sepsis dataset.

nodes.title: Domain Generalisation via Imprecise Learning
nodes.tldr: Imprecise Domain Generalisation lets learners optimize over a spectrum of generalization strategies during training, with operators choosing their preference only at deployment.

nodes.title: Memoria: Resolving Fateful Forgetting Problem through Human-Inspired Memory Architecture
nodes.tldr: Memoria is a human-inspired external memory system for neural networks that counters long-term forgetting by reproducing primacy, recency, and contiguity effects.
nodes.problem: Information in neural networks is fatefully forgotten over time, so long-term retention fails.

nodes.title: CLIF: Complementary Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron for Spiking Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Complementary LIF neuron for spiking neural networks adds extra backpropagation paths to fix temporal gradient vanishing while keeping binary outputs, rivaling same-structure ANNs.

nodes.title: Refined Coreset Selection: Towards Minimal Coreset Size under Model Performance Constraints

nodes.title: By Tying Embeddings You Are Assuming the Distributional Hypothesis

nodes.title: Triple Changes Estimator for Targeted Policies
nodes.tldr: Extends the triple difference estimator to changes-in-changes, giving a triple changes estimator that recovers counterfactual distributions, applied to Medicaid expansion and preventive care.
nodes.problem: Difference-in-differences needs parallel trends and estimates only average effects; triple difference shares this limit.

nodes.title: DITTO: Diffusion Inference-Time T-Optimization for Music Generation
nodes.tldr: DITTO controls pre-trained text-to-music diffusion models at inference time by optimizing initial noise latents through differentiable feature-matching losses, enabling inpainting, looping and melody control.

nodes.title: On a Neural Implementation of Brenier's Polar Factorization

nodes.tldr: Studies bandit LQR control with heterogeneous cost curvatures, reducing it to bandit convex optimization with memory and interpolating regret guarantees.

nodes.title: Upweighting Easy Samples in Fine-Tuning Mitigates Forgetting

nodes.title: Position: Current Model Licensing Practices are Dragging Us into a Quagmire of Legal Noncompliance
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing current model licensing practices create legal noncompliance risks, and proposing ModelGo Licenses as a standardized draft.
nodes.problem: Inconsistent ML model licenses on public hubs create legal noncompliance risks.
nodes.approach: Clause review of popular licenses, Hugging Face examples, and a new draft license.
nodes.niche_reason: ML model licensing law is a rare research direction

nodes.title: Generalized Random Forests Using Fixed-Point Trees
nodes.tldr: Replaces gradient-based splitting in generalized random forests with a gradient-free fixed-point approximation, keeping consistency guarantees while greatly speeding up effect estimation.
nodes.problem: Gradient-based GRF splitting is expensive and unstable in high dimensions.
nodes.approach: Fixed-point approximation that avoids Jacobian estimation in tree splitting.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal forest variants are specialised but established.

nodes.title: The Value of Prediction in Identifying the Worst-Off
nodes.tldr: Models welfare effects of prediction for targeting the worst-off in government programs, comparing it with bureaucratic capacity expansion using a German unemployment case study.
nodes.problem: Whether prediction identifies the worst-off better than expanding bureaucratic capacity.
nodes.approach: Mathematical welfare models plus a real-world long-term unemployment case study.
nodes.confidence_reason: Topic straddles fairness and public-policy areas
nodes.niche_reason: Welfare analysis of prediction for targeting the worst-off is rare

nodes.title: Implicit Regularization for Tubal Tensor Factorizations via Gradient Descent
nodes.tldr: Proves that gradient descent on an overparameterized tubal tensor factorization with small random initialization implicitly favours low tubal rank.
nodes.problem: Implicit regularization in tensor factorization was only shown for gradient flow or lazy training.
nodes.approach: Analysis of discrete gradient descent beyond lazy training, with numerical simulations of the tubal rank dynamics.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Tubal tensor implicit bias under gradient descent is an unusual theory niche.

nodes.title: Training Deep Learning Models with Norm-Constrained LMOs
nodes.tldr: Optimizers that use a linear minimization oracle over norm balls, with a spectral norm for deep nets that transfers hyperparameters across model sizes.
nodes.problem: Optimizers should adapt to problem geometry, and hyperparameters should transfer across model sizes.
nodes.approach: Stochastic LMO-based update family with a chosen norm for deep architectures; memory-efficient, no Adam reliance.
nodes.niche_reason: Non-Euclidean LMO optimizers are specialised but established.

nodes.title: Doubly Robust Conformalized Survival Analysis with Right-Censored Data
nodes.tldr: Conformal method for lower survival-time bounds from right-censored data, imputing censoring times and using weighted conformal calibration with a doubly robust guarantee.
nodes.problem: Lower prediction bounds for survival times are hard with right-censored data beyond restrictive type-I censoring.
nodes.approach: Impute unobserved censoring times with a machine learning model, then calibrate a survival model via weighted conformal inference.
nodes.niche_reason: Conformal survival prediction is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Going Deeper into Locally Differentially Private Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proposes UPGNET, a local-DP graph learning pipeline with high-order aggregation and feature regularization layers that preserve node-classification utility under privacy.
nodes.problem: Local differential privacy on node features distorts graph data and severely degrades GNN node-classification accuracy.
nodes.approach: Three-stage LDP protocol for node features, plus High-Order Aggregator and Node Feature Regularization layers.
nodes.niche_reason: Private GNN learning under LDP is specialised within privacy-preserving ML

nodes.title: Overcoming Multi-step Complexity in Multimodal Theory-of-Mind Reasoning: A Scalable Bayesian Planner
nodes.tldr: Scalable Bayesian theory-of-mind planner decomposes multi-step mental-state inference into Bayesian updates, transferring small-LM ToM likelihood estimation to larger LMs for multimodal benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Computational theory-of-mind methods scale poorly in multimodal environments with multi-step planning.
nodes.approach: Stepwise Bayesian updates with weak-to-strong control transferring ToM likelihood estimation from small to large LMs.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory-of-mind with Bayesian planning is relatively rare.

nodes.title: Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models
nodes.tldr: Presents TarFlow, a transformer-based autoregressive normalizing flow with noise augmentation, denoising, and guidance that reaches diffusion-comparable image samples and state-of-the-art likelihoods.
nodes.problem: Normalizing flows were thought to be weak generative models and have received little attention recently.
nodes.approach: Stack autoregressive transformer blocks on image patches with alternating directions, plus noise augmentation, post-training denoising, and guidance.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Normalizing flows are now a less common direction than diffusion.

nodes.title: Emergence in non-neural models: grokking modular arithmetic via average gradient outer product
nodes.tldr: Grokking on modular arithmetic also occurs in Recursive Feature Machines, driven by block-circulant features from the average gradient outer product, not neural networks.
nodes.problem: Whether grokking and emergence are specific to neural networks and gradient descent.
nodes.approach: Iterate kernel machines with AGOP feature learning; analyze learned block-circulant features and Fourier multiplication.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Non-neural grokking via kernel feature learning is uncommon.

nodes.title: Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight
nodes.tldr: Introduces CAPA, a chance-adjusted model similarity metric based on shared mistakes, showing LLM judges favor similar models and that model errors grow more correlated with capability.
nodes.problem: How model similarity affects AI oversight through LLM-as-judge and weak-to-strong training.
nodes.approach: Define CAPA similarity and analyze judge scoring bias and weak-to-strong generalization gains.

secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans LLM evaluation, judge bias, and weak-to-strong safety.
nodes.niche_reason: Model-similarity view of oversight is a distinctive angle.

nodes.title: Algorithm Development in Neural Networks: Insights from the Streaming Parity Task
nodes.tldr: Case study of RNNs on streaming parity showing a phase transition to infinite generalization, explained by representational merging that builds a finite automaton.
nodes.problem: How networks can generalize infinitely beyond training lengths by learning algorithms.
nodes.approach: Effective theory of representational dynamics of RNNs trained on the streaming parity task.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Rare focus on algorithm emergence in RNN dynamics.

nodes.title: CVE-Bench: A Benchmark for AI Agents’ Ability to Exploit Real-World Web Application Vulnerabilities
nodes.tldr: CVE-Bench is a sandboxed benchmark of critical real-world CVE web vulnerabilities for evaluating LLM agents' exploitation ability; top agents exploit up to 13%.
nodes.problem: Lack of realistic benchmarks for LLM agents exploiting real-world web application vulnerabilities.

nodes.title: RE-Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI R&D Capabilities of Language Model Agents against Human Experts
nodes.tldr: RE-Bench compares frontier AI agents with 61 human experts on seven open-ended ML research engineering tasks; agents win at short budgets, humans at long ones.
nodes.problem: AI R&D capabilities of agents lack realistic evaluations with direct comparison to human experts.
nodes.approach: Seven 8-hour research engineering environments with 71 expert attempts, compared against best-of-k public frontier agents.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Human-versus-agent AI R&D benchmarks are a specialised evaluation niche.

nodes.title: Position: A Critical Perspective on The Value in Studying Deep Learning Phenomena
authors: Alan Jeffares, M van der Schaar

nodes.title: Position: Deep Learning is Not So Mysterious or Different

nodes.niche_reason: Argument within the mainstream generalization debate

nodes.title: Statistical Collusion by Collectives on Learning Platforms
nodes.tldr: Develops a framework for how collectives can coordinate altered data submissions to steer learning platforms, including algorithms for estimating impact from observed data.
nodes.problem: Collectives lack ways to predict the effect of coordinated data changes on learning platforms.

nodes.title: Long-Form Speech Generation with Spoken Language Models
nodes.tldr: Trains a state-space spoken language model that generates coherent multi-minute speech directly from audio tokens, outperforming Transformers in coherence and efficiency.
nodes.problem: Textless spoken language models lose coherence and memory efficiency beyond tens of seconds of speech.

nodes.title: Statistical Test for Feature Selection Pipelines by Selective Inference
nodes.tldr: Proposes a statistical test for the significance of whole feature selection pipelines, with valid false-positive control through selective inference.

nodes.title: An Analysis for Reasoning Bias of Language Models with Small Initialization
nodes.tldr: Shows smaller parameter initialization makes LLMs favor reasoning over memorization, with theory showing embeddings and self-attention drive the bias.

nodes.title: Prices, Bids, Values: One ML-Powered Combinatorial Auction to Rule Them All
nodes.tldr: Combines value and demand queries in ML-based preference elicitation, yielding MLHCA, a combinatorial auction with lower efficiency loss and fewer queries.

nodes.niche_reason: Auction design with ML elicitation is a rare cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Linearization Turns Neural Operators into Function-Valued Gaussian Processes
nodes.tldr: Adds post-hoc Bayesian uncertainty to trained neural operators by linearizing the network, giving function-valued Gaussian process predictions without retraining.
nodes.problem: Quantifying predictive error of neural operators used as PDE surrogates in high-stakes simulation
nodes.approach: Linearized Laplace approximation pushing weight-space Gaussian uncertainty through the operator post-hoc
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian UQ for neural operators is specialised but established

nodes.title: Soft Reasoning: Navigating Solution Spaces in Large Language Models through Controlled Embedding Exploration
nodes.tldr: Soft Reasoning perturbs the first-token embedding and uses Bayesian optimisation with a verifier-guided objective to explore diverse reasoning paths in LLMs efficiently.
nodes.problem: LLMs reason poorly due to limited diversity and inefficient search over solutions.

nodes.niche_reason: Embedding-space search with Bayesian optimisation is an uncommon test-time approach.

nodes.title: ResQ: Mixed-Precision Quantization of Large Language Models with Low-Rank Residuals
nodes.tldr: Post-training quantization for LLMs that keeps a low-rank principal subspace in 8-bit and quantizes the rest to 4-bit with random rotations to suppress outliers.

nodes.approach: PCA-identified high-precision subspace plus invariant random rotation within subspaces.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM quantization is a crowded area; mixed-precision low-rank is a variant.

nodes.title: What Limits Virtual Agent Application? OmniBench: A Scalable Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Essential Virtual Agent Capabilities
nodes.tldr: Self-generating graph-based benchmark that synthesizes controllable-complexity virtual agent tasks by subtask composition, with a multidimensional evaluation framework.
nodes.problem: Existing virtual-agent benchmarks have uncontrollable complexity, heavy manual annotation, and narrow evaluation.
nodes.approach: Automated graph-structured task synthesis via subtask composition, plus OmniEval across 10 capabilities.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Virtual-agent benchmarks are established but specialised.

nodes.title: CoPINN: Cognitive Physics-Informed Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proposes CoPINN, a physics-informed network that trains from easy to hard sample points, scheduled by PDE residual gradients, to reduce boundary errors.
nodes.problem: PINNs treat easy and hard sample points alike, causing poor minima near physical boundaries.

nodes.niche_reason: Physics-informed learning is established; curriculum variant specialised

nodes.title: Raptor: Scalable Train-Free Embeddings for 3D Medical Volumes Leveraging Pretrained 2D Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Raptor makes train-free volume embeddings by running a frozen 2D foundation model on slices and compressing tokens with random projections.
nodes.problem: Training volumetric foundation models is too costly, and large volumetric datasets are scarce.
nodes.approach: Frozen 2D model applied to cross-sections, then random planar tensor reduction of visual tokens.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Train-free medical volume embeddings are specialised but emerging.

nodes.title: Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity
nodes.tldr: Proposes implicit state-space models that iterate to a fixed point, implementing RNN nonlinear state transitions while keeping parallel training and improved state tracking.
nodes.problem: SSMs and transformers are less expressive than RNNs, which lack parallel training.
nodes.approach: Iterate a transformation to approximate fixed points, with a curriculum requiring full convergence on few tokens.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit state-space RNN hybrids are specialised.

nodes.title: Catoni Contextual Bandits are Robust to Heavy-tailed Rewards
nodes.tldr: Uses Catoni's robust estimator in contextual bandits so regret depends on reward variance and only logarithmically on reward range.

nodes.approach: Variance-weighted regression with Catoni estimation and peeling-based handling of unknown variance.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Heavy-tailed contextual bandit regret is specialised

nodes.title: Hide & Seek: Transformer Symmetries Obscure Sharpness & Riemannian Geometry Finds It
nodes.tldr: Redefines transformer sharpness on a symmetry-quotiented manifold via Riemannian geometry, with higher-order terms restoring correlation with generalization.
nodes.problem: Existing sharpness measures fail for transformers because attention symmetries make flatness ambiguous.
nodes.approach: Geodesic sharpness on the quotient manifold, approximated to higher order along geodesics.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Quotient-manifold sharpness for transformers is an unusual geometric angle

nodes.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once: LLMs can In-Context Learn Multiple Tasks in Superposition
nodes.tldr: Shows LLMs can run several distinct in-context learning tasks at once in one inference call, a phenomenon called task superposition.
nodes.problem: Whether LLMs can perform multiple computationally distinct ICL tasks simultaneously.
nodes.approach: Empirical study across LLM families plus transformer expressivity theory and task-vector analysis.

secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability

nodes.title: The Synergy of LLMs & RL Unlocks Offline Learning of Generalizable Language-Conditioned Policies with Low-fidelity Data
nodes.tldr: TEDUO learns language-conditioned policies from unlabeled offline datasets by using LLMs both to annotate data and as generalizable instruction-following agents in symbolic environments.
nodes.problem: Offline learning of language-conditioned policies that generalize to unseen goals from scarce, unlabeled data.
nodes.approach: LLMs augment offline datasets with annotations, then serve as generalizable agents trained via offline RL.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: LLM plus offline RL is a fairly common combination.

nodes.title: SDP-CROWN: Efficient Bound Propagation for Neural Network Verification with Tightness of Semidefinite Programming
nodes.tldr: Hybrid neural network verifier adding an SDP-derived l2 inter-neuron coupling bound to linear bound propagation, achieving near-SDP tightness at scale on large models.
nodes.problem: Linear bound-propagation verifiers are loose with neuron coupling; SDP verifiers do not scale.
nodes.approach: New SDP-derived linear bound with one extra parameter per layer, plugged into alpha-CROWN.
nodes.niche_reason: Formal neural network verification is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: rStar-Math: Small LLMs Can Master Math Reasoning with Self-Evolved Deep Thinking
nodes.tldr: Shows small language models reach state-of-the-art math reasoning via MCTS search guided by a small process reward model, trained by self-evolution without distillation.
nodes.problem: Small language models lack strong multi-step math reasoning without distillation from larger teachers.
nodes.approach: MCTS-generated verified trajectories train a policy SLM and process preference model via self-evolution.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Math reasoning with LLMs and reward models is a crowded mainstream topic

nodes.title: Partition First, Embed Later: Laplacian-Based Feature Partitioning for Refined Embedding and Visualization of High-Dimensional Data
nodes.tldr: Partitions high-dimensional features into subsets with smooth graph-Laplacian structure, then learns a separate embedding per subset for visualization, with recovery guarantees.
nodes.problem: Single embeddings distort data driven by several latent processes living in different feature subsets.
nodes.approach: Laplacian-smoothness optimization over mutually exclusive feature partitions, generalizing embedding methods to multiple embeddings.

nodes.title: Self-supervised Masked Graph Autoencoder via Structure-aware Curriculum
nodes.tldr: Masks graph edges in an easy-to-hard curriculum, with a difficulty measurer and self-paced scheduler, to improve masked graph autoencoder node representations.
nodes.problem: Masked graph autoencoders treat all masked edges equally despite differing reconstruction difficulty.
nodes.approach: Structure-aware difficulty measurement plus a self-paced scheduler that gradually adds harder masked edges.
nodes.niche_reason: Masked graph autoencoders are a common SSL direction

nodes.title: Polynomial-Delay MAG Listing with Novel Locally Complete Orientation Rules
nodes.tldr: First polynomial-delay algorithm for listing all maximal ancestral graphs in a Markov equivalence class, using new locally complete orientation rules with singleton background knowledge.
nodes.problem: Enumerating all MAGs in a Markov equivalence class efficiently under latent confounding.
nodes.approach: Recursively add singleton background knowledge and apply sound, locally complete orientation rules.
