nodes.niche_reason: Graphical causal discovery enumeration theory is a rare specialised topic.

nodes.title: $K^2$VAE: A Koopman-Kalman Enhanced Variational AutoEncoder for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
nodes.tldr: A VAE for long-horizon probabilistic time series forecasting that uses Koopman linearization and a Kalman-style refinement to limit error accumulation.
nodes.problem: Nonlinear dynamics and iteration cost hurt long-term probabilistic time series forecasting.
nodes.approach: KoopmanNet linearizes dynamics; KalmanNet refines predictions and uncertainty in the linear system.

secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows

nodes.title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
nodes.tldr: Speeds long-context LLM inference with a retrieval-augmented draft model for speculative decoding, improving quality and running over 2x faster.
nodes.problem: Speculative decoding gains vanish for long contexts because KV cache operations are memory-bound.
nodes.approach: RAG drafter on shortened retrieval contexts speculates for the long-context target, with inference-time knowledge transfer.

nodes.niche_reason: Speculative decoding and RAG are both crowded directions

nodes.title: Geometric Representation Condition Improves Equivariant Molecule Generation
nodes.tldr: Two-stage molecular generation that first samples a geometric representation, then conditions the molecule on it, improving quality and conditional generation.
nodes.problem: Molecular generators struggle with quality, especially under property conditions.
nodes.approach: Generate an informative geometric representation first, then condition equivariant molecule generation on it.

nodes.title: Neural Discovery in Mathematics: Do Machines Dream of Colored Planes?
nodes.tldr: Uses neural networks as differentiable approximators to reformulate the Hadwiger-Nelson plane-coloring problem, yielding two new six-colorings via gradient-based search.

nodes.title: Robust Noise Attenuation via Adaptive Pooling of Transformer Outputs
nodes.tldr: Shows standard transformer pooling collapses at low signal-to-noise, and proposes attention-based adaptive pooling that approximates the optimal vector quantizer for any SNR.
nodes.problem: AvgPool, MaxPool and ClsToken collapse when input signal-to-noise ratio fluctuates.

nodes.niche_reason: Noise-robust transformer pooling is specialised

nodes.title: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
nodes.tldr: Localizing unlearning and edits to components of the factual-recall lookup-table mechanism yields more robust, relearning-resistant knowledge removal with fewer side effects than output-based localization.
nodes.problem: Knowledge editing and unlearning in LLMs are fragile and cause side effects.
nodes.approach: Use mechanistic interpretability to localize circuits for factual recall and train only those components.

nodes.title: FedSSI: Rehearsal-Free Continual Federated Learning with Synergistic Synaptic Intelligence
nodes.tldr: Rehearsal-free regularization for continual federated learning that adapts synaptic intelligence to heterogeneous client data, avoiding stored samples.

nodes.approach: Synaptic intelligence regularization tailored to heterogeneous federated data
nodes.niche_reason: Continual federated learning is specialised but active

nodes.title: MODA: MOdular Duplex Attention for Multimodal Perception, Cognition, and Emotion Understanding
nodes.tldr: Introduces MODA, a duplex attention mechanism that refines within modalities and interacts across them to address attention deficits in multimodal LLMs.
nodes.problem: Multimodal LLMs suffer inconsistent cross-modal attention and decaying attention across layers.

nodes.title: Position: AI Agents Need Authenticated Delegation

nodes.title: LotteryCodec: Searching the Implicit Representation in a Random Network for Low-Complexity Image Compression
nodes.tldr: LotteryCodec compresses images by overfitting a binary mask over a random shared network, validating a lottery codec hypothesis with state-of-the-art single-image compression.

nodes.title: Adjusting Model Size in Continual Gaussian Processes: How Big is Big Enough?

nodes.title: Position: In-House Evaluation Is Not Enough. Towards Robust Third-Party Evaluation and Flaw Disclosure for General-Purpose AI
nodes.tldr: Argues in-house evaluation is insufficient; proposes standardized AI flaw reports, disclosure programs with legal safe harbors, and coordination infrastructure for third-party evaluation.

nodes.title: Robust ML Auditing using Prior Knowledge

nodes.tldr: Introduces exogenous isomorphism to simplify complete counterfactual identifiability, with guarantees for bijective and triangular monotonic SCMs and neural estimation.

nodes.title: Learning Soft Sparse Shapes for Efficient Time-Series Classification
nodes.tldr: SoftShape merges low-contribution shapelets into soft representations and uses router-activated expert networks for efficient, interpretable time-series classification.
nodes.problem: Hard shapelet selection discards useful subsequences and is inefficient for time-series classification.
nodes.approach: Soft shape sparsification plus mixture-of-experts shape learning blocks with a shared expert.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Shapelet-based classification is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Distribution-aware Fairness Learning in Medical Image Segmentation From A Control-Theoretic Perspective
nodes.tldr: Proposes distribution-aware mixture of experts, inspired by optimal control, to reduce demographic bias in medical image segmentation across architectures.
nodes.problem: Demographic and clinical imbalance in medical data causes biased segmentation performance.
nodes.approach: Mixture-of-experts gating conditioned on demographic and clinical factors, plugged into existing networks.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.confidence_reason: Fairness versus MoE architecture is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Control-theory framing of fairness in segmentation is somewhat unusual

nodes.title: TLLC: Transfer Learning-based Label Completion for Crowdsourcing
nodes.tldr: Completes sparse crowdsourced labels by pretraining a Siamese network on high-confidence instances, then transferring it to model each worker's annotations.
nodes.problem: Workers label too few instances to model each worker reliably in crowdsourced label completion
nodes.approach: Transfer learning from high-confidence source domain to per-worker target domains
nodes.confidence_reason: Crowdsourced label completion; no weak-supervision topic in vocab.
nodes.niche_reason: Crowdsourcing label completion is a specialised, smaller research area

nodes.title: Not All Wrong is Bad: Using Adversarial Examples for Unlearning
nodes.tldr: Uses adversarial examples to drive approximate machine unlearning, making forget-set behavior match unseen data and approaching exact unlearning performance.
nodes.problem: Approximate unlearning methods fail to match accuracy and confidence of exact unlearning.
nodes.approach: Fine-tune using adversarial examples of forget data as unlearning targets.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Approximate unlearning is a common active topic.

nodes.title: Diffusion-based Adversarial Purification from the Perspective of the Frequency Domain
nodes.tldr: Purifies adversarial images with diffusion by restoring low-frequency amplitude and phase from the input, removing perturbations while preserving structure.
nodes.problem: Diffusion purification indiscriminately damages image frequencies, harming content and structure.
nodes.approach: Frequency-aware reverse-process updates on amplitude and phase spectra at each diffusion step.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion purification is a crowded adversarial defense topic.

nodes.title: Position: AI Safety should prioritize the Future of Work
nodes.tldr: Argues AI safety should address the future of work, proposing copyright collective licensing and pro-worker global governance against labor inequality.
nodes.problem: AI safety agendas overlook labor displacement, income inequality, and training-data compensation.
nodes.approach: Economic-theory argument for collective licensing and pro-worker AI governance.
nodes.niche_reason: Labor-economics framing of AI safety is unusual for ML

nodes.title: Theoretical Limitations of Ensembles in the Age of Overparameterization
nodes.tldr: Proves infinite overparameterized random-feature ensembles become pointwise equivalent to single infinite-width regressors, so modern ensembles offer no inherent generalization advantage.
nodes.problem: Whether classic ensemble gains carry over to overparameterized and deep ensembles is unclear.
nodes.approach: Analyze ensembles of random feature regressors, deriving exact ridgeless and approximate ridge equivalences.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Established theory line; ensemble equivalence is specialised.

nodes.title: Robust Automatic Modulation Classification with Fuzzy Regularization
nodes.tldr: Adds a fuzzy regularisation term to automatic modulation classification that models prediction ambiguity, reweights samples and widens margins between confusable modulation types.
nodes.problem: Confusable modulation schemes produce near-identical predicted distributions, especially at low SNR.
nodes.approach: Backpropagated ambiguity modelling, adaptive loss scaling for sample reweighting, and margin maximisation between clusters.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Radio-signal domain plus uncertainty framing; topic is a judgement call
nodes.niche_reason: Fuzzy regularisation for radio modulation is rare

nodes.title: Re-ranking Reasoning Context with Tree Search Makes Large Vision-Language Models Stronger
nodes.tldr: Multimodal RAG for VQA that enriches the knowledge base with self-consistent reasoning contexts and re-ranks them with Monte Carlo tree search using heuristic rewards.
nodes.problem: Retrieved knowledge lacks reasoning examples, and LVLM responses built on it are erratic.
nodes.approach: Reasoning-context knowledge base plus MCTS with heuristic rewards to re-rank retrieved examples.
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal RAG for VQA is a common direction.

nodes.title: Monte-Carlo Tree Search with Uncertainty Propagation via Optimal Transport
nodes.tldr: Wasserstein MCTS models node values as Gaussians and backs up via Wasserstein barycenters with alpha-divergence, propagating uncertainty for stochastic, partially observable planning with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: MCTS backups handle uncertainty poorly in highly stochastic, partially observable MDPs.
nodes.approach: Gaussian value nodes with Wasserstein barycenter backup plus optimistic and Thompson sampling selection.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Optimal transport applied to MCTS backups is unusual.

nodes.title: EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks 24 multimodal LLMs as vision-driven embodied agents across 1,128 tasks in four environments, finding weak low-level manipulation.
nodes.problem: No comprehensive evaluation framework exists for MLLM-based embodied agents acting from visual input.
nodes.approach: Six capability subsets spanning high-level semantic tasks to atomic navigation and manipulation actions.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: MLLM embodied-agent benchmarking is active but specialised

nodes.title: Train for the Worst, Plan for the Best: Understanding Token Ordering in Masked Diffusions
nodes.tldr: Masked diffusion models train on harder subproblems than autoregressive ones, but adaptive decoding order at inference lifts Sudoku accuracy from under 7% to about 90%.
nodes.problem: Understanding trade-off between training difficulty and inference flexibility in masked diffusion models.
nodes.approach: Theory and experiments on infilling hardness, plus adaptive token-ordering inference strategies.
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete diffusion theory is rising but still specialised.

nodes.title: CollabLLM: From Passive Responders to Active Collaborators
nodes.tldr: CollabLLM trains LLMs with multiturn-aware rewards from simulated collaboration so they proactively uncover user intent, improving task performance, interactivity and user satisfaction.
nodes.problem: LLMs trained on next-turn rewards respond passively and are inefficient in long multiturn interactions.
nodes.approach: Reinforcement fine-tuning with rewards estimated by simulating future conversation turns with a user simulator.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Preference/RL fine-tuning for LLMs is common; multiturn collaboration slightly distinct.

nodes.title: Enforcing Latent Euclidean Geometry in Single-Cell VAEs for Manifold Interpolation
nodes.tldr: FlatVI regularises single-cell VAE latent spaces toward Euclidean geometry so linear interpolation approximates geodesics for trajectory inference.
nodes.problem: Linear latent interpolation in single-cell VAEs need not follow geodesics on the data manifold.
nodes.approach: Regularise discrete-likelihood VAE latent manifold toward flat Euclidean geometry using statistical manifold structure.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Riemannian geometry applied to single-cell VAEs is rare.

nodes.title: Flopping for FLOPs: Leveraging Equivariance for Computational Efficiency
nodes.tldr: Builds mirror-equivariant networks with block-diagonal linear layers that halve FLOPs while keeping cost per parameter comparable.
nodes.problem: Equivariance improves parameter efficiency but usually raises computational cost per parameter.
nodes.approach: Parametrize features as mirror-symmetric and mirror-antisymmetric irreps, making linear layers block-diagonal.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.confidence_reason: Efficiency versus equivariant architecture; judgment call between two topics
nodes.niche_reason: Flopping-equivariant efficient layers; specialised architecture direction

nodes.title: Generative Social Choice: The Next Generation
nodes.tldr: Extends generative social choice with approximate LLM queries and a slate-length budget, giving theoretical guarantees for representative statement slates.
nodes.problem: Producing a proportional, concise slate of statements from user opinions with imperfect LLM queries.
nodes.approach: Proportional committee-style selection over LLM-generated candidate statements, with approximately optimal queries and bounded slate length.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Social choice combined with LLM candidate generation is an unusual cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Hierarchical Refinement: Optimal Transport to Infinity and Beyond
nodes.tldr: Computes bijective optimal transport couplings in log-linear time and linear space by recursively refining low-rank OT partitions.
nodes.problem: Full-rank OT via Sinkhorn needs quadratic space, while low-rank OT cannot produce one-to-one correspondences.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical multiscale partitioning via low-rank OT subproblems that converges to a Monge-map bijection.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Scalable exact optimal transport for assignment; established but specialised.

nodes.title: am-ELO: A Stable Framework for Arena-based LLM Evaluation
nodes.tldr: Replaces iterative ELO updates with maximum likelihood estimation and models annotator reliability, giving a stable ranking for arena-based LLM evaluation.
nodes.problem: ELO-based arena rankings are unstable and ignore differences in annotator ability.
nodes.approach: Replaces iterative ELO updates with MLE and modifies the Elo probability function to estimate annotator reliability jointly.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Arena-style LLM ranking is a common, active evaluation topic.

nodes.title: SK-VQA: Synthetic Knowledge Generation at Scale for Training Context-Augmented Multimodal LLMs
nodes.tldr: SK-VQA releases a 2M-pair synthetic multimodal dataset with external knowledge sources for training and benchmarking context-augmented VQA.
nodes.problem: Knowledge-based VQA and context-augmented generation lack large training data and benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Large-scale synthetic generation of visual question-answer pairs grounded in external knowledge.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic knowledge VQA data for multimodal RAG is specialised

nodes.title: Understanding and Mitigating Memorization in Generative Models via Sharpness of Probability Landscapes
nodes.tldr: Analyzes diffusion memorization via sharpness of log-density, proposes an early memorization metric, and mitigates it by optimizing initial noise with sharpness regularization.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models memorize training data, and detecting memorization early in generation is hard.
nodes.approach: Geometric sharpness analysis of log density, with sharpness-aware regularization of the initial noise.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: Memorization straddles diffusion evaluation and privacy attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Sharpness-based diffusion memorization analysis is a specialised angle

nodes.title: Statistical Query Hardness of Multiclass Linear Classification with Random Classification Noise
nodes.tldr: Proves super-polynomial statistical query lower bounds for multiclass linear classification under random classification noise once there are three or more labels.
nodes.problem: The complexity of multiclass linear classification with random classification noise was unknown beyond two labels.
nodes.approach: Statistical query lower bound constructions for three or more labels and constant or small separation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: SQ hardness under structured label noise is specialised

nodes.title: In-Context Denoising with One-Layer Transformers: Connections between Attention and Associative Memory Retrieval
nodes.tldr: Shows a one-layer transformer solves restricted in-context denoising optimally, with attention performing one gradient step on a dense associative memory energy.
nodes.problem: Unclear how attention relates to dense associative memory retrieval in in-context denoising settings.
nodes.approach: Bayesian framework analyzing in-context denoising, comparing a trained attention layer to DAM energy updates.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Established attention-Hopfield link, with a specialised denoising analysis

nodes.title: Identifying Causal Direction via Variational Bayesian Compression
nodes.tldr: Infers causal direction between two variables by approximating codelengths with variational Bayesian neural networks under the algorithmic Markov condition.
nodes.problem: Determining cause versus effect from observational data with codelength methods limited by simple functions or costly GPs.
nodes.approach: Use variational Bayesian neural network learning as the codelength interpretation for each causal direction.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bivariate causal direction via MDL is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Layer-wise Alignment: Examining Safety Alignment Across Image Encoder Layers in Vision Language Models
nodes.tldr: Shows early exits from a VLM's image encoder raise harmful outputs, and fixes this with Layer-Wise PPO, a multimodal RLHF variant.
nodes.problem: Vision-language models' harmful information is unevenly spread across image-encoder layers, enabling early-exit vulnerabilities.
nodes.approach: Modifies Clipped-PPO to perform layer-wise multimodal RLHF, reducing harmfulness caused by early exits.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.confidence_reason: VLM safety spans multimodal and LLM safety topics
nodes.niche_reason: Layer-level safety of VLM image encoders is a specialised safety niche

nodes.title: Is Complex Query Answering Really Complex?
nodes.tldr: Shows most complex query answering benchmarks reduce to simple link prediction, and proposes harder benchmarks requiring genuine multi-hop reasoning where models perform poorly.
nodes.problem: Complex query answering benchmarks on knowledge graphs overstate progress because most queries are easily reducible.
nodes.approach: Analyze query reducibility in existing benchmarks and construct new benchmarks of queries that require multi-hop reasoning.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Knowledge Graphs & Relational Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Knowledge graph query answering is a rare, specialised subfield.

nodes.title: AutoAdvExBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Exploitation of Adversarial Example Defenses
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks whether LLM agents can autonomously break adversarial-example defenses, finding agents break 87% of CTF-style defenses but only 37% of real ones.
nodes.problem: Security benchmarks proxy real tasks, so it is unclear whether LLMs can exploit real adversarial defenses.
nodes.approach: Benchmark where agents must autonomously write attacks against CTF-style and real-world defenses.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM agents breaking adversarial defenses is an emerging, specialised benchmark area.

nodes.title: LOCATE 3D: Real-World Object Localization via Self-Supervised Learning in 3D
nodes.tldr: Localizes objects in 3D scenes from referring expressions, using a self-supervised 3D-JEPA encoder on featurized point clouds plus a new grounding dataset.
nodes.problem: Localizing objects in 3D scenes from natural language on real sensor streams.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised masked latent prediction on point clouds, then language-conditioned mask and box decoder.
nodes.confidence_reason: Primary topic is a judgment call between 3D and VLM areas.
nodes.niche_reason: Grounding on real RGB-D streams is less common than static 3D.

nodes.title: Penalizing Infeasible Actions and Reward Scaling in Reinforcement Learning with Offline Data
nodes.tldr: Offline RL algorithm PARS curbs Q-value extrapolation errors via reward scaling with layer norm and penalizing infeasible actions, excelling in offline-to-online D4RL.
nodes.problem: Q-value extrapolation errors in offline RL and offline-to-online fine-tuning
nodes.approach: Reward scaling with layer normalization plus penalty on infeasible actions so Q-values decay outside data range
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Crowded offline RL topic, though extrapolation angle is somewhat specific

nodes.title: Learning Safety Constraints for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Learns a polytope of safety constraints in LLM representation space, detecting unsafe inputs and steering outputs geometrically without changing model weights.
nodes.problem: LLMs produce harmful outputs and are vulnerable to adversarial attacks despite alignment.
nodes.approach: Learns polytope facets that separate safe and unsafe regions, enabling post-hoc geometric steering.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: geometric safety polytopes in representation space are specialised

nodes.title: Ad-Hoc Human-AI Coordination Challenge
nodes.tldr: Launches a Hanabi challenge for ad-hoc human-AI coordination, with cheap human proxy agents trained on a 3,079-game dataset and a controlled evaluation system.
nodes.problem: Human-AI coordination evaluation is costly and hard to reproduce.
nodes.approach: Human proxy agents learned from a deliberately limited human Hanabi dataset, hosted in a controlled evaluation system.
nodes.niche_reason: Hanabi human-AI coordination with proxy agents is a rare benchmark niche.

nodes.title: Scaling Collapse Reveals Universal Dynamics in Compute-Optimally Trained Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Finds loss curves of compute-optimal models collapse onto one universal curve with learning-rate decay, explained by a simple SGD-noise model linked to scaling laws.
nodes.problem: Training dynamics at scale are hard to predict from theory, despite regularities across model sizes.
nodes.approach: Normalizes loss curves by compute and loss, plus an SGD-noise dynamics model with learning-rate schedules.

Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Universal loss-curve collapse is a rare empirical regularity

nodes.title: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
nodes.tldr: Detects AI-generated images by freezing principal SVD components of a vision foundation model and adapting only the remaining subspace, improving generalization.
nodes.problem: Detectors of AI-generated images overfit to limited fake patterns and fail to generalize.
nodes.approach: SVD splits feature space into orthogonal subspaces; the principal part is frozen and the rest is tuned.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.confidence_reason: AI-image forensics straddles classification and provenance
nodes.niche_reason: AI-generated image detection is active but a specialised topic

nodes.title: Benign Samples Matter! Fine-tuning On Outlier Benign Samples Severely Breaks Safety
nodes.tldr: Finds outlier samples in benign data via Self-Inf-N; fine-tuning LLMs on just 100 of them severely breaks safety alignment and evades most mitigations.
nodes.problem: Benign fine-tuning data can degrade LLM safety; how to find the most harmful benign samples.
nodes.approach: Outlier detection via Self-Inf-N influence scoring to select samples for a fine-tuning attack.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-tuning safety attacks are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Improving Consistency Models with Generator-Augmented Flows
nodes.tldr: Introduces generator-augmented flows that transport noisy data toward consistency model outputs, reducing the consistency training/distillation discrepancy and improving convergence and quality.
nodes.problem: Consistency training uses a noisy single-sample velocity estimate, creating a discrepancy with consistency distillation.
nodes.approach: Define a flow transporting noisy data to consistency model outputs, proven to reduce the discrepancy and transport cost.
nodes.niche_reason: Consistency-model variants are a common diffusion subtopic.

nodes.title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.tldr: Defines automated failure attribution for LLM multi-agent systems, releasing the Who&When dataset and showing current methods find failing agents and steps poorly.
nodes.problem: Identifying which agent and step cause task failures in LLM multi-agent systems
nodes.approach: Curated failure logs with agent and step annotations; three attribution methods benchmarked against reasoning models.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: New research area of failure attribution in agent systems

nodes.title: Learning Parametric Distributions from Samples and Preferences
nodes.tldr: Shows preference feedback can accelerate parameter estimation from the 1/sqrt(n) rate to 1/n for parametric distributions, with a matching lower bound.
nodes.problem: Estimating parametric distribution parameters from samples alone is limited to a slow 1/sqrt(n) rate.
nodes.approach: Estimators that exploit deterministic preference constraints between sample pairs, plus a matching lower bound analysis.

secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization

nodes.title: TimeBase: The Power of Minimalism in Efficient Long-term Time Series Forecasting
nodes.tldr: TimeBase is an ultra-lightweight long-term forecasting network that extracts low-rank basis temporal components and forecasts at segment level, also reducing complexity of patch-based models.
nodes.problem: Long-term time series forecasting models are overly large and computationally inefficient.
nodes.approach: Extract core basis temporal components exploiting low-rank structure and do segment-level forecasting.

secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Time series forecasting is crowded, though minimalist angle is slightly different.

nodes.title: On the Power of Context-Enhanced Learning in LLMs
nodes.tldr: Proves gradient-based training with auxiliary in-context data can be exponentially more sample-efficient than standard learning for multi-step reasoning.
nodes.problem: Understanding how LLMs learn from context-supplied data beyond in-context learning is unclear.
nodes.approach: Gradient learning where context is enhanced with data excluded from autoregressive loss; theory plus experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Gradient analogue of in-context learning is a specialised theory direction

nodes.title: Policy Regularization on Globally Accessible States in Cross-Dynamics Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Improves cross-dynamics policy transfer by regularizing toward globally accessible states via F-distance constraints usable in offline and off-policy RL.
nodes.problem: Inaccessible expert states under changed dynamics make imitation-from-observation misleading
nodes.approach: F-distance regularized policy optimization over states visited under all dynamics
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-dynamics imitation is specialised but has prior work

nodes.title: Adaptive Multi-prompt Contrastive Network for Few-shot Out-of-distribution Detection
nodes.tldr: AMCN uses CLIP with learnable ID and OOD text prompts and class-wise adaptive thresholds to detect out-of-distribution images from only a few labeled in-distribution samples.
nodes.problem: Out-of-distribution detection when only a few labeled in-distribution samples are available.
nodes.approach: Adaptive multi-prompt contrastive learning on CLIP with class-wise thresholds and prompt-guided ID-OOD margin control.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot OOD detection with prompts is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Towards Robustness and Explainability of Automatic Algorithm Selection
nodes.tldr: Models algorithm selection with a causal DAG linking problem and algorithm features, improving robustness to distribution shift and providing counterfactual explanations.
nodes.problem: Algorithm selection models rely on correlations, hurting robustness and explainability.
nodes.approach: DAG over algorithm features conditioned on problem features, with counterfactual reconstruction of optimal algorithm features.

nodes.confidence_reason: Fits AutoML and causality equally; topic is a judgment call.

nodes.title: Position: Certified Robustness Does Not (Yet) Imply Model Security
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing certified robustness does not yet imply model security, identifying detection-without-distinction and unclear criteria, and calling for concrete research steps.
nodes.problem: Certified robustness is promoted as a fix for adversarial examples but has real-world deployment gaps.
nodes.approach: Critical analysis of gaps in current certification research, with concrete proposed steps for the community.
nodes.niche_reason: Common debate within adversarial robustness.

nodes.title: Position: Political Neutrality in AI Is Impossible — But Here Is How to Approximate It
nodes.tldr: Argues political neutrality in AI is infeasible and not always desirable, proposes eight approximation techniques, and evaluates LLM outputs.
nodes.problem: AI systems show political bias that can shape users' opinions and decisions.
nodes.approach: Eight techniques for approximating neutrality across three AI levels, with output-level LLM evaluation.
nodes.niche_reason: Normative AI ethics on political neutrality is specialised but growing.

nodes.title: Roll the dice & look before you leap: Going beyond the creative limits of next-token prediction
nodes.tldr: Uses minimal algorithmic tasks to show next-token training memorizes and is myopic, while multi-token and diffusion methods and input-noise seed-conditioning yield more creative outputs.

nodes.niche_reason: LLM creativity limits are an active but specialised topic

nodes.title: Reducing Variance of Stochastic Optimization for Approximating Nash Equilibria in Normal-Form Games
nodes.tldr: Proposes Nash Advantage Loss, an unbiased surrogate loss with far lower variance for stochastic optimization of Nash equilibria in normal-form games, converging faster empirically.

nodes.approach: Design a new unbiased surrogate loss (NAL) with provably reduced variance for sampled-play optimization.

nodes.niche_reason: Loss design for Nash equilibrium via ML optimization is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Towards a Mechanistic Explanation of Diffusion Model Generalization
nodes.tldr: Explains diffusion model generalization via localized denoising, showing trained denoisers share a local inductive bias replicable by aggregating local empirical denoisers without training.
nodes.problem: Why diffusion models generalize rather than memorize.
nodes.approach: Training-free local empirical denoiser algorithms compared against network denoisers to reveal local inductive bias.

nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion generalization theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Position: Formal Mathematical Reasoning—A New Frontier in AI
nodes.tldr: Position paper arguing that formal mathematical reasoning grounded in proof assistants is an essential complement to text-based AI for math, reviewing progress, challenges and milestones.

nodes.title: Log-Sum-Exponential Estimator for Off-Policy Evaluation and Learning
nodes.tldr: Proposes a log-sum-exponential estimator for off-policy evaluation and learning that reduces variance and handles heavy-tailed rewards better than inverse propensity scoring.
nodes.problem: Inverse propensity estimators have high variance with poor propensity scores and heavy-tailed rewards.
nodes.approach: LSE-operator estimator with bias and variance bounds for evaluation and regret bounds for learning.

nodes.title: Flowing Datasets with Wasserstein over Wasserstein Gradient Flows
nodes.tldr: Represents labeled datasets as distributions over distributions and defines Wasserstein-over-Wasserstein gradient flows to optimize them for transfer and distillation.
nodes.problem: Designing tractable gradient flows over labeled datasets viewed as probability distributions over distributions.

nodes.title: The Number of Trials Matters in Infinite-Horizon General-Utility Markov Decision Processes

nodes.approach: Bounds the mismatch between finite-trial and infinite-trial policy evaluation for discounted and average GUMDPs.

nodes.title: PCEvolve: Private Contrastive Evolution for Synthetic Dataset Generation via Few-Shot Private Data and Generative APIs

nodes.title: CACTI: Leveraging Copy Masking and Contextual Information to Improve Tabular Data Imputation
nodes.tldr: CACTI is a masked autoencoder for tabular imputation using copy masking from real missingness patterns plus column-name semantics, gaining 7.8% average R2 over baselines.
nodes.problem: Tabular data imputation ignores missingness structure and the semantic relationships between features.
nodes.approach: Masked autoencoding with copy masking drawn from empirical missingness patterns and text embeddings of column descriptions.
nodes.niche_reason: Tabular imputation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Catch Your Emotion: Sharpening Emotion Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: SEPM improves emotion recognition in multimodal LLMs at inference time via confidence-guided coarse-to-fine classification and visual augmentation that focuses on emotional cues.
nodes.problem: MLLMs confuse similar emotions and get distracted by redundant visual information.
nodes.approach: Training-free confidence-guided coarse-to-fine inference with focus-on-emotion visual augmentation.
nodes.niche_reason: Emotion perception in MLLMs is a specialised application.

nodes.title: DPO Meets PPO: Reinforced Token Optimization for RLHF
nodes.tldr: Reinforced Token Optimization models RLHF as a token-level MDP, learns token rewards from DPO, and uses them in PPO, outperforming PPO and direct preference methods.
nodes.problem: PPO in RLHF learns from sparse sentence-level rewards and performs sub-optimally.
nodes.approach: Token-wise MDP formulation; DPO-derived token rewards feed PPO policy optimization, with sample-efficiency guarantees.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Very crowded RLHF/DPO/PPO variant space.

nodes.title: Position: Language model developers should report train-test overlap
nodes.tldr: Argues LM developers should report train-test overlap, documenting that only 9 of 30 models do and urging transparency for interpretable evaluations.
nodes.problem: Evaluation results cannot be interpreted without train-test overlap information, which is rarely reported.
nodes.approach: Survey of 30 models' reporting practices and a case for disclosure.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Contamination reporting is established; position framing is specialised.

nodes.title: Adaptive Learn-then-Test: Statistically Valid and Efficient Hyperparameter Selection
nodes.tldr: aLTT is a hyperparameter selection method with finite-sample risk guarantees that uses e-processes for early-terminating sequential testing, matching LTT with far fewer tests.
nodes.problem: Learn-then-test needs many costly testing rounds to certify hyperparameter risk guarantees.
nodes.approach: Sequential data-dependent multiple hypothesis testing with e-processes and early termination.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Statistical guarantees fit both generalization and calibration; close call
nodes.niche_reason: Sequential e-process testing for risk-controlled model selection is rare

nodes.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
nodes.tldr: AxBench benchmarks LLM steering and concept detection, finding prompting and simple baselines beat sparse autoencoders; also proposes ReFT-r1, a competitive weakly-supervised representation method.
nodes.problem: No benchmark directly compares representation-based steering methods against prompting and finetuning.
nodes.approach: Large-scale benchmark on Gemma-2; introduce rank-1 representation finetuning with released feature dictionaries.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Active interpretability subfield, specialised benchmark comparing steering methods.

nodes.title: Learning dynamics in linear recurrent neural networks
nodes.tldr: Analytically derives learning dynamics of linear RNNs, showing singular values are learned in order of scale and temporal precedence, with implicit regularization and feature learning via an NTK derivation.
nodes.problem: Limited theoretical understanding of how temporal task structure shapes RNN learning dynamics.
nodes.approach: Analytic gradient-flow analysis of linear RNNs with a task-dynamics framework and finite-width NTK derivation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Exact learning dynamics of recurrent networks linked to neuroscience is rare.

nodes.title: Mastering Board Games by External and Internal Planning with Language Models
nodes.tldr: Combines language models with external MCTS or internally generated search trees to reach grandmaster-level chess and strong play in other board games.
nodes.problem: Improving LLM planning and reasoning strength in board games via search.
nodes.approach: LLM-guided MCTS (external) and in-context linearized search trees (internal), trained on domain data.
nodes.confidence_reason: Topic is a judgment call between close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: LLMs with search for board games is specialised.

nodes.title: DeFoG: Discrete Flow Matching for Graph Generation
nodes.tldr: DeFoG is a discrete flow-matching graph generator that decouples sampling from training, with theory linking loss and sampler, and achieves strong results using far fewer sampling steps.
nodes.problem: Graph diffusion models have inefficient sampling and tightly coupled training and sampling stages.
nodes.approach: Permutation-respecting discrete flow matching with disentangled training and flexible sampling design space.
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete flow matching for graphs is specialised.

nodes.title: Do We Really Need Message Passing in Brain Network Modeling?
nodes.tldr: Argues message passing underuses brain networks and proposes Brain Quadratic Network using Hadamard products instead of matrix-product message passing for better accuracy and efficiency.
nodes.problem: GNNs and Transformers' message passing is not fully exploited on correlation-based brain networks.
nodes.approach: Brain Quadratic Network replacing message passing with Hadamard-product quadratic neurons on connectivity matrices.
nodes.niche_reason: Questioning message passing for brain connectomes is unusual.

nodes.title: LipsNet++: Unifying Filter and Controller into a Policy Network
nodes.tldr: LipsNet++ is a policy network with a trainable Fourier filter and Jacobian-regularized Lipschitz layer that jointly suppresses observation noise and action fluctuation.
nodes.problem: RL policies fluctuate in actions due to observation noise and non-smooth policy functions.
nodes.approach: Trainable Fourier filter layer removes noise frequencies, plus Jacobian regularization for a low Lipschitz constant.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: smooth policy networks for control.

nodes.title: LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models, Provably and Efficiently
nodes.tldr: Proves LoRA adapters align with singular subspaces of the one-step full gradient, motivating LoRA-One, which initializes adapters from that gradient with preconditioning and gives linear convergence.
nodes.problem: Theoretically understanding and improving LoRA initialization and convergence for LLM fine-tuning.
nodes.approach: Initialize LoRA via singular subspaces of the one-step full gradient with preconditioners.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another LoRA variant in a very crowded area.

nodes.title: Expected Variational Inequalities
nodes.tldr: Introduces expected variational inequalities, a relaxation requiring a distribution satisfying the constraint in expectation, which is polynomial-time solvable even for nonmonotone operators.
nodes.problem: Variational inequalities are expressive but computationally intractable in general settings.
nodes.approach: Adapt game-theoretic techniques to solve for a distribution over solutions, generalizing correlated equilibria.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Could fit game theory or optimization; a judgment call between close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Expected variational inequalities are a rare relaxation in game theory.

nodes.title: Sundial: A Family of Highly Capable Time Series Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Sundial is a family of time series foundation models pretrained with a flow-matching loss on continuous values, delivering zero-shot probabilistic forecasts in milliseconds.
nodes.problem: Time series foundation models usually need discrete tokenization or restrictive parametric output densities.
nodes.approach: Flow-matching TimeFlow loss for next-patch distributions, trained on a trillion-point corpus with minimal Transformer changes.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Time series foundation models are an increasingly common direction.

nodes.title: A Unified Framework for Entropy Search and Expected Improvement in Bayesian Optimization
nodes.tldr: Variational Entropy Search unifies Expected Improvement and Max-value Entropy Search, interpreting EI as a variational approximation of MES, and proposes the VES-Gamma acquisition function.
nodes.problem: Expected Improvement and information-theoretic acquisition functions are viewed as unrelated in Bayesian optimization.
nodes.approach: Variational inference framework relating EI to MES, yielding the hybrid VES-Gamma acquisition function.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian optimization is an established specialised subfield.

nodes.title: Causal Attribution Analysis for Continuous Outcomes
nodes.tldr: Defines posterior causal estimands that attribute a continuous outcome to multiple correlated causes, with identification results and estimators.
nodes.problem: Attributing a continuous outcome to causes, where binarizing it loses information or biases conclusions.
nodes.approach: Posterior intervention, total and natural direct effects under sequential ignorability and monotonicity, with a simple estimator.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Causal attribution for continuous outcomes is specialised

nodes.title: When and How Does CLIP Enable Domain and Compositional Generalization?
nodes.tldr: Controlled training of CLIP on systematically constructed distributions shows domain diversity is key for domain and compositional generalization, with shared intermediate-layer circuits underlying success.
nodes.problem: When and how CLIP generalizes to unseen domains and unseen classes within partially seen domains is unclear.
nodes.approach: Train CLIP on controlled domain and class mixtures, with data-centric and mechanistic circuit analyses.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Controlled study of CLIP generalization is established but specialised.

nodes.title: G-Designer: Architecting Multi-agent Communication Topologies via Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Uses a variational graph autoencoder to generate task-specific communication topologies for LLM agent teams, cutting token use while keeping accuracy and robustness.
nodes.problem: Choosing an effective inter-agent communication topology for a task is hard and costs many tokens.
nodes.approach: Variational graph autoencoder encodes agents and a task node to decode a task-adaptive communication graph.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Learned communication topologies for LLM agents are emerging but specialised.

nodes.title: Fundamental Bias in Inverting Random Sampling Matrices with Application to Sub-sampled Newton
nodes.tldr: Corrects the inversion bias of random sampling and Hadamard sketches, yielding local convergence rates for sub-sampled Newton.
nodes.problem: Inverses of random sketches are biased even when the sketches are unbiased, hurting ML pipelines.
nodes.approach: Derive bias-correction factors for leverage-based and uniform sampling and structured random projections.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans randomized linear algebra, optimization and RMT; primary is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Inversion bias in randomized linear algebra is rarely studied

nodes.title: Navigating Semantic Drift in Task-Agnostic Class-Incremental Learning
nodes.tldr: Task-agnostic class-incremental learning method that compensates feature mean shifts and calibrates covariances with Mahalanobis constraints to reduce forgetting of earlier classes.
nodes.problem: Class-incremental learning without task IDs suffers from feature distribution drift on old classes.
nodes.approach: Mean shift compensation and Mahalanobis covariance calibration with feature self-distillation.
nodes.niche_reason: Class-incremental learning is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Federated Generalised Variational Inference: A Robust Probabilistic Federated Learning Framework
nodes.tldr: FedGVI is a probabilistic federated learning framework using generalised variational inference, robust to prior and likelihood misspecification, with convergence and robustness guarantees.
nodes.problem: Federated learning needs robust, calibrated predictions under prior and likelihood misspecification.
nodes.approach: Generalises partitioned variational inference with robust and conjugate client updates, with fixed-point and robustness analysis.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian federated learning with generalised VI is a rare combination.

nodes.title: Signed Laplacians for Constrained Graph Clustering
nodes.tldr: Constrained graph clustering via a Cheeger-type inequality and a signed Laplacian of the constraint graph, solved as a generalised eigenvalue problem.
nodes.problem: Clustering must cut one graph while avoiding cuts in a second, constraint graph.
nodes.approach: Signed Laplacian of the second graph with a generalised eigenvalue solve.
nodes.confidence_reason: Graph clustering has no clear topic; optimization fit is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Constrained spectral clustering with signed Laplacians is rare.

nodes.title: Towards Better-than-2 Approximation for Constrained Correlation Clustering
nodes.tldr: Shows solving the exponentially large Constrained Cluster LP gives a better-than-2 approximation for constrained correlation clustering; correction notes the earlier efficient LP claim was erroneous.
nodes.problem: Improving the factor-3 approximation for APX-hard constrained correlation clustering.
nodes.approach: Rounding analysis of the Constrained Cluster LP achieving better-than-2 approximation conditional on LP solvability.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Pure approximation-algorithms theory; closest vocab topic is a loose fit.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical approximation algorithms for clustering are very rare in ML venues.

nodes.title: Efficiently Vectorized MCMC on Modern Accelerators
nodes.tldr: Designs single-chain MCMC as finite state machines so vectorized multi-chain runs avoid synchronization overhead, giving up to order-of-magnitude speedups.
nodes.problem: Vectorizing MCMC with tools like vmap forces chains to wait for the slowest chain.
nodes.approach: Express MCMC samplers as finite state machines and derive theoretical speedups to guide design.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Accelerator-efficient MCMC design is a rare systems-statistics angle.

nodes.title: MGD$^3$ : Mode-Guided Dataset Distillation using Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Distills datasets by guiding a pretrained diffusion model to discover data modes and enhance diversity, without fine-tuning on distillation losses.
nodes.problem: Dataset distillation with generative models lacks sample diversity, and fine-tuning is expensive
nodes.approach: Mode discovery, mode-guided diffusion sampling for intra-class diversity, and stop guidance to remove artifacts.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based dataset distillation is a common, active area

nodes.title: Gridded Transformer Neural Processes for Spatio-Temporal Data
nodes.tldr: Gridded pseudo-token transformer neural processes with efficient attention and optional translation equivariance scale probabilistic modelling to large spatio-temporal data such as weather.
nodes.problem: Transformer neural processes do not scale to large, unstructured spatio-temporal datasets.
nodes.approach: Specialised encoders/decoders with gridded pseudo-token processor and equivariant variants using efficient attention.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Neural processes for spatio-temporal data are a rare niche.

nodes.title: Local Identifying Causal Relations in the Presence of Latent Variables
nodes.tldr: Gives local characterizations and fully localized algorithms that test whether one variable causes a target under latent confounding, avoiding global PAG learning.
nodes.problem: Identifying causes of a target with latent variables normally requires costly global structure learning.
nodes.approach: Necessary and sufficient local characterizations of causal relations between two variables, with sound and complete algorithms.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Local causal discovery with latent variables is a niche topic.

nodes.title: The dark side of the forces: assessing non-conservative force models for atomistic machine learning
nodes.tldr: Shows machine-learned forces not derived from energy cause instability in geometry optimisation and molecular dynamics, and suggests pairing them with conservative models.
nodes.problem: Whether directly predicted, non-conservative interatomic forces are reliable for microscopic simulation.
nodes.approach: Empirical analysis of geometry optimisation and molecular dynamics stability with direct versus energy-derived forces.
nodes.niche_reason: Non-conservative force fields in atomistic simulation; cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Direct Discriminative Optimization: Your Likelihood-Based Visual Generative Model is Secretly a GAN Discriminator
nodes.tldr: DDO fine-tunes likelihood-based visual generators using an implicit discriminator from the likelihood ratio to a reference model, achieving record FIDs for diffusion and autoregressive models.
nodes.problem: Maximum likelihood training is mode-covering and limits visual generation quality.
nodes.approach: Parameterize an implicit discriminator as likelihood ratio versus fixed reference, finetune with reverse-KL-like self-play.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion fine-tuning improvements are a crowded area.

nodes.title: AdaSplash: Adaptive Sparse Flash Attention
nodes.tldr: AdaSplash makes adaptive-sparsity alpha-entmax attention fast via a hybrid Halley-bisection solver and custom Triton kernels, approaching FlashAttention-2 efficiency.
nodes.problem: Adaptive sparse alpha-entmax attention is slow and memory-hungry, so it gives no runtime gains.
nodes.approach: Hybrid Halley-bisection root solver cutting iterations 7x, plus sparsity-aware Triton kernels.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: adaptive-sparsity attention kernels.

nodes.title: Auditing $f$-differential privacy in one run
nodes.tldr: Audits a mechanism's empirical privacy with a single run and f-DP-based analysis, giving tighter privacy estimates than prior auditing methods.
nodes.problem: Empirical privacy auditing is either computationally expensive with multiple runs or loose.
nodes.approach: Randomized example inclusion with a single run, using the hypothesized f-DP curve for tight estimates.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: privacy auditing is specialised; single-run variants are niche

nodes.title: Algorithms with Calibrated Machine Learning Predictions
nodes.tldr: Uses calibrated uncertainty from ML predictors as advice for online algorithms, achieving near-optimal ski rental performance and better job scheduling.
nodes.problem: Online algorithms with predictions need per-prediction trust levels, not one aggregate trust setting
nodes.approach: Calibrated prediction-level uncertainty used as advice in ski rental and job scheduling algorithms
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.confidence_reason: Online algorithms with ML advice; calibration sits between two topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare intersection of calibration and online algorithms with predictions

nodes.title: Revisiting Continuity of Image Tokens for Cross-domain Few-shot Learning
nodes.tldr: Finds that disrupting image-token continuity hurts source but barely hurts target domains, and proposes a token-disruption method for cross-domain few-shot learning.
nodes.problem: ViT transfers poorly to distant target domains with scarce labeled data.
nodes.approach: Deliberately disrupting token continuity so ViT relies on smaller, transferable patterns.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Established transfer-learning area; token-continuity angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Scalable Generation of Spatial Transcriptomics from Histology Images via Whole-Slide Flow Matching
nodes.tldr: STFlow predicts spatial transcriptomics from whole-slide histology images using flow matching over the joint slide-level gene expression with an efficient local spatial attention encoder.
nodes.problem: Existing methods predict spot expression independently and struggle with memory on large slides.
nodes.approach: Flow matching generative model of whole-slide expression with slide-level encoder and local spatial attention.
nodes.niche_reason: Generating spatial transcriptomics from histology is a rare application.

nodes.title: Conformal Prediction as Bayesian Quadrature
nodes.tldr: Recasts conformal prediction in Bayesian terms, offering interpretable guarantees and a richer picture of likely test losses.
nodes.problem: Frequentist conformal guarantees are limiting, since deployed model losses need a broader probabilistic account.
nodes.approach: Bayesian quadrature over the distribution of losses to produce distribution-free uncertainty guarantees.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian reinterpretation of conformal prediction is uncommon

nodes.title: Efficient First-Order Optimization on the Pareto Set for Multi-Objective Learning under Preference Guidance
nodes.tldr: First-order penalty-based algorithms optimize a preference function over the weakly Pareto-optimal set in multi-objective learning, using a merit function with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Optimizing a user preference function subject to Pareto optimality in multi-objective learning.
nodes.approach: Semivectorial bilevel reformulation with a merit-function constraint and penalty-based first-order solver.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised multi-objective bilevel optimization.

nodes.title: Adapter Naturally Serves as Decoupler for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
nodes.tldr: Finds adapters naturally decouple domain information, and proposes a structure-based Domain Feature Navigator fine-tuned alone on target domains for few-shot segmentation.
nodes.problem: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation suffers from domain gaps and fine-tuning with scarce target data.
nodes.approach: Adapter-based structural domain decoupler, with SAM-SVN constraining its source-domain overfitting.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: adapter-based domain adaptation vs segmentation is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: cross-domain few-shot segmentation is specialised

nodes.title: New Bounds for Sparse Variational Gaussian Processes
nodes.tldr: Relaxes the sparse variational GP assumption with a more general q(f|u) with N extra parameters, yielding a tighter collapsed ELBO that reduces hyperparameter bias.
nodes.problem: Standard sparse variational GP bounds fix the conditional prior in the variational posterior, loosening the bound.
nodes.approach: Generalized variational conditional with extra parameters optimized analytically for a tighter collapsed bound.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse GP bound refinements are a small niche.

nodes.title: A Generalization Result for Convergence in Learning-to-Optimize
nodes.tldr: Gives a probabilistic framework proving learned optimization algorithms converge to critical points with high probability, without safeguards.
nodes.problem: Learned optimizers lack convergence guarantees, since classical geometric proof arguments do not transfer.
nodes.approach: Probabilistic generalization of worst-case convergence analysis over parametric classes of non-smooth losses.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Convergence theory for learned optimizers is a rare direction

nodes.title: RLEF: Grounding Code LLMs in Execution Feedback with Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: RLEF trains code LLMs with end-to-end reinforcement learning to use execution feedback over multiple turns, outperforming prior work with fewer samples.
nodes.problem: Code LLMs struggle to improve code iteratively from execution feedback, unlike independent sampling.
nodes.approach: End-to-end RL on multi-turn code synthesis that learns to ground generations in execution feedback.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL for code LLMs is an active, fairly crowded area

nodes.title: SynEVO: A neuro-inspired spatiotemporal evolutional framework for cross-domain adaptation
nodes.tldr: SynEVO is a neuro-inspired spatiotemporal network sharing knowledge across domains via an elastic common container, task extractor, and adaptive coupler.
nodes.problem: Spatiotemporal learners trained per source transfer poorly across domains.
nodes.approach: Curriculum reordering, elastic common container with task extractor, and adaptive dynamic coupler for model growth.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans spatiotemporal learning, continual transfer, and neuro-inspired framing.
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual neuro-inspired evolutionary framing for spatiotemporal transfer.

nodes.title: Model Steering: Learning with a Reference Model Improves Generalization Bounds and Scaling Laws
nodes.tldr: Formalizes model steering, where a reference model guides data weighting for a target model, with generalization bounds and a CLIP variant showing better scaling.
nodes.problem: Heuristic reference-model data weighting is used widely but its generalization benefits are not understood.
nodes.approach: DRO-based DRRho risk minimization with generalization analysis, applied to a CLIP variant with a reference model.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory plus CLIP method; generalization vs data-curation topics overlap.
nodes.niche_reason: Reference-model steering is emerging but still specialised.

nodes.title: Position: General Intelligence Requires Reward-based Pretraining
nodes.tldr: Argues general intelligence requires pretraining to reason with RL on synthetic task curricula, disentangling reasoning from knowledge, with external retrieval-based memory.
nodes.problem: LLM reasoning overfits training data because reasoning and knowledge are entangled, limiting transfer.
nodes.approach: Proposes RL-from-scratch pretraining, synthetic curricula for reasoning priors, and small context windows plus external memory.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Position on RL-based pretraining is unusual but tied to a hot topic.

nodes.title: An Online Adaptive Sampling Algorithm for Stochastic Difference-of-convex Optimization with Time-varying Distributions
nodes.tldr: Adaptive sampling algorithm for stochastic nonsmooth difference-of-convex problems under time-varying distributions, with convergence guarantees to DC critical points.
nodes.problem: Stochastic nonsmooth DC optimization with distributions that shift over time.
nodes.approach: Distinct adaptive sampling rates for the convex and concave components of the objective.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Established optimization subfield with a specialised distribution-shift setting

nodes.title: Rapid Overfitting of Multi-Pass SGD in Stochastic Convex Optimization
nodes.tldr: Proves multi-pass SGD can overfit sharply in non-smooth stochastic convex optimization, with population loss jumping after a single extra pass.
nodes.problem: Multi-pass SGD is widely used, but its out-of-sample behavior beyond one pass is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Lower and upper bounds on population loss of multi-pass SGD in non-smooth convex optimization.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: SGD overfitting theory is established but specialised

nodes.title: How Do Large Language Monkeys Get Their Power (Laws)?
nodes.tldr: Shows aggregate power-law scaling of success with repeated attempts arises from heavy-tailed per-task success probabilities, despite exponential per-task scaling.
nodes.problem: Why repeated-sampling success scales as a power law when each task's failure rate falls exponentially.
nodes.approach: Distributional analysis of single-attempt success probabilities; heavy tails explain the aggregate power law and forecast its exponent.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.confidence_reason: Scaling-law explanation sits between scaling and evaluation topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Power-law inference scaling is an established but specialised topic.

nodes.title: Blink of an eye: a simple theory for feature localization in generative models
nodes.tldr: Stochastic localization theory explaining sudden critical windows where key output features are decided in both diffusion and autoregressive models, validated on LLM reasoning failures.
nodes.problem: Why generative models abruptly commit to features at narrow windows of generation.
nodes.approach: Stochastic localization formalism with few distributional assumptions giving bounds for diffusion and autoregressive models.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Unified theory of critical windows across model families is rare.

nodes.title: Learning Smooth and Expressive Interatomic Potentials for Physical Property Prediction
nodes.tldr: Proposes testing machine-learning interatomic potentials by energy conservation in molecular dynamics, and builds eSEN, a smooth expressive model with state-of-the-art physical property prediction.
nodes.problem: Low test error of interatomic potentials does not guarantee good downstream physical property predictions.
nodes.approach: Energy-conservation test in MD guides design of the smooth, expressive eSEN potential.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised ML for atomistic simulation.

nodes.title: Probabilistic Factorial Experimental Design for Combinatorial Interventions
nodes.tldr: Introduces probabilistic factorial experimental design for combinatorial interventions, proving dosage one half per treatment is near-optimal for k-way interaction models, plus multi-round acquisition.
nodes.problem: Efficiently designing experiments for combinatorial interventions with interacting treatments as the number of treatments grows.
nodes.approach: Product-Bernoulli dosage design with closed-form near-optimal passive solution and numerically optimizable active acquisition function.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical experimental design for combinatorial interventions is a rare niche.

nodes.title: ConceptAttention: Diffusion Transformers Learn Highly Interpretable Features
nodes.tldr: Training-free method that repurposes diffusion transformer attention layers into concept embeddings, giving sharp saliency maps and state-of-the-art zero-shot segmentation.
nodes.problem: Cross-attention saliency maps from diffusion transformers are blurry and poorly localized.
nodes.approach: Linear projections in the output space of DiT attention layers produce contextualized concept embeddings.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised interpretability of multimodal DiTs

nodes.title: Position: AI Competitions Provide the Gold Standard for Empirical Rigor in GenAI Evaluation
nodes.tldr: Argues GenAI evaluation is in crisis due to leakage and contamination, and that AI competitions' anti-cheating practices make them the gold standard for rigor.
nodes.problem: Traditional benchmarking fails for generative AI, especially due to test leakage and contamination.
nodes.approach: Position argument drawing on AI-competition practices for counteracting leakage and cheating.
nodes.niche_reason: Evaluation methodology is common; competition-based angle is less so.

nodes.title: Enhancing Certified Robustness via Block Reflector Orthogonal Layers and Logit Annealing Loss
nodes.tldr: Proposes a block reflector orthogonal layer and an annealed margin loss for Lipschitz networks, achieving state-of-the-art certified robustness on CIFAR and ImageNet.
nodes.problem: Lipschitz networks have limited expressivity and small margins, weakening certified robustness
nodes.approach: Block reflector orthogonal layers for expressive Lipschitz architectures, trained with a margin-annealing loss
nodes.niche_reason: Lipschitz certified robustness is known but still a crowded line

nodes.title: PokéChamp: an Expert-level Minimax Language Agent
nodes.tldr: LLMs replace action sampling, opponent modeling, and value estimation inside minimax tree search, yielding an expert-level Pokémon battle agent.
nodes.problem: Language agents struggle with large search spaces and partial observability in competitive games.

nodes.niche_reason: LLM-driven game-tree search for Pokémon is a rare unusual application.

nodes.title: LLM-SRBench: A New Benchmark for Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: LLM-SRBench is 239 scientific equation discovery problems designed to resist memorisation, where the best method reaches only 31.5% symbolic accuracy.
nodes.problem: Existing equation-discovery benchmarks use common equations that LLMs memorise, inflating apparent discovery ability.

nodes.niche_reason: LLM-driven equation discovery is a rare niche

nodes.title: Graph Diffusion for Robust Multi-Agent Coordination
nodes.tldr: Models multi-agent coordination with a sparse graph and graph diffusion to generate robust offline policies, improving coordination and robustness in dynamic environments.
nodes.problem: Offline MARL struggles with out-of-distribution states and actions, and per-agent diffusion ignores coordination.

nodes.title: Discrepancy Minimization in Input-Sparsity Time
nodes.tldr: Gives a combinatorial input-sparsity-time algorithm for discrepancy minimization, improving on Larsen's O(mn^2) runtime for sparse real-valued matrices.

nodes.title: One-Step Generalization Ratio Guided Optimization for Domain Generalization
nodes.tldr: GENIE, a gradient-preconditioning optimizer that equalizes per-parameter generalization ratios to reduce spurious correlations in domain generalization.

nodes.approach: Preconditioned optimizer equalizing the One-Step Generalization Ratio across parameters.

nodes.title: GL-LowPopArt: A Nearly Instance-Wise Minimax-Optimal Estimator for Generalized Low-Rank Trace Regression

nodes.title: Return of the Latent Space COWBOYS: Re-thinking the use of VAEs for Bayesian Optimisation of Structured Spaces
nodes.tldr: COWBOYS decouples the VAE generative model from the GP surrogate in latent-space Bayesian optimisation, combining them with a simple Bayesian update rule.

nodes.niche_reason: Evidential multi-view fusion with expert knowledge is rare.

nodes.title: Graph Adaptive Autoregressive Moving Average Models
nodes.tldr: GRAMA is a graph state-space model built on a learnable ARMA framework with selective attention, preserving permutation equivariance for long-range graph learning.

nodes.title: Achieving Linear Speedup and Near-Optimal Complexity for Decentralized Optimization over Row-stochastic Networks

nodes.title: Training a Generally Curious Agent
nodes.tldr: Paprika fine-tunes language models on synthetic multi-turn interaction data across tasks so they learn in-context exploration and adapt to unseen sequential decision tasks.

nodes.niche_reason: LLM agent fine-tuning is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Decision Theoretic Foundations for Conformal Prediction: Optimal Uncertainty Quantification for Risk-Averse Agents

nodes.title: Suitability Filter: A Statistical Framework for Classifier Evaluation in Real-World Deployment Settings

nodes.approach: Aggregate shift-sensitive model output signals and statistically test test-versus-user distributions.

nodes.title: Position: Probabilistic Modelling is Sufficient for Causal Inference

nodes.title: Aligning with Logic: Measuring, Evaluating and Improving Logical Preference Consistency in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Measures LLM logical preference consistency via transitivity, commutativity and negation invariance, and proposes REPAIR data refinement to improve it.

secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization

nodes.title: A Closer Look at Multimodal Representation Collapse

nodes.title: Feynman-Kac Correctors in Diffusion: Annealing, Guidance, and Product of Experts

nodes.title: Learning Dynamics in Continual Pre-Training for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Derives a continual pre-training scaling law that separates distribution shift and learning-rate annealing to predict loss at any step and schedule.

nodes.title: InfoSAM: Fine-Tuning the Segment Anything Model from An Information-Theoretic Perspective
nodes.tldr: InfoSAM fine-tunes Segment Anything with mutual-information objectives that distill and preserve pre-trained domain-invariant relational knowledge in a teacher-student framework.
nodes.problem: PEFT methods for SAM neglect domain-invariant relations encoded in the pre-trained model.

nodes.title: On Path to Multimodal Generalist: General-Level and General-Bench
nodes.tldr: Introduces General-Level, a five-level synergy-based framework, and General-Bench with 700+ tasks to rank multimodal generalist LLMs.
nodes.problem: Measuring true capability and generality of multimodal generalist models
nodes.approach: Synergy-based level framework plus massive multimodal benchmark evaluated on 100+ MLLMs
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Many MLLM benchmarks exist.

nodes.title: The Role of Randomness in Stability
nodes.tldr: Shows the randomness needed for replicable and differentially private learning is tightly controlled by global stability, and characterizes PAC learning randomness via Littlestone dimension.

nodes.title: Layer by Layer: Uncovering Hidden Representations in Language Models

nodes.title: PhySpec: Physically Consistent Spectral Reconstruction via Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition and Self-Supervised Meta-Auxiliary Learning
nodes.tldr: PhySpec reconstructs hyperspectral images from RGB with orthogonal subspace decomposition that estimates camera spectral sensitivity, plus test-time meta-auxiliary learning for physical consistency.
nodes.problem: Learned RGB-to-hyperspectral reconstruction fails to reproduce ground-truth RGB from predicted spectra.
nodes.approach: Orthogonal subspace decomposition estimating camera sensitivity and self-supervised meta-auxiliary test-time adaptation.
nodes.confidence_reason: Low-level restoration versus physical modeling; test-time adaptation component too.
nodes.niche_reason: Spectral reconstruction from RGB is a rare vision niche.

nodes.title: Improving Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness in Vision-Language Models by Closed-form Alignment of Adversarial Path Simplices

nodes.problem: Adversarial fine-tuning of VLMs ignores intermediate adversarial samples along the attack trajectory.
nodes.approach: Taylor-expansion upper bound on alignment loss using Jacobian/Hessian at clean samples, emulating infinite simplex sampling.
