nodes.approach: Augmented-state Bellman operator on bounded value functions, solved by discretized value iteration and Q-learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: CVaR risk-sensitive RL.

nodes.title: Required Spine Optional Limbs: Heterogeneous Federated Learning via Backbone-sharing and Activation-guided Selection
nodes.tldr: SpineFL shares a mandatory backbone across heterogeneous FL sub-models and selects neurons by activation frequency to reduce parameter conflicts under non-IID data.
nodes.problem: Heterogeneous devices and non-IID data make sub-model extraction in federated learning conflict-prone.
nodes.approach: Shared backbone plus activation-guided probabilistic neuron selection for sub-model extraction.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Federated sub-model pruning is a common research direction.

nodes.title: OmniFit: Bridging Modalities via Layer-Adaptive Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Training-free token compression for omni-modal LLMs that allocates retention budgets per layer by redundancy and modality preference, keeping 98% performance with 20% tokens.
nodes.problem: Prohibitive compute cost of omni-modal LLMs processing streaming video, audio, and text tokens.
nodes.approach: Layer-adaptive heterogeneity profiling plus alignment-rectified selection of cross-modally aligned tokens.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Token reduction is popular, but omni-modal audio-video setting is more specialised.

nodes.title: UniPercept: Towards Unified Perceptual-Level Image Understanding across Aesthetics, Quality, Structure, and Texture
nodes.tldr: UniPercept-Bench and UniPercept evaluate and improve MLLMs on perceptual-level image understanding of aesthetics, quality, structure and texture, trained with domain-adaptive pretraining and RL.
nodes.problem: MLLMs perceive perceptual-level image attributes such as aesthetics and quality poorly.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical benchmark plus a baseline trained with domain-adaptive pre-training and task-aligned RL, usable as reward.
nodes.niche_reason: Perceptual-level MLLM understanding is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Multimodal Nested Learning for Decoupled and Coordinated Optimization
nodes.tldr: MoNet reformulates multimodal learning as nested sub-processes with decoupled memory streams and multi-timescale coordinated fusion to address imbalanced multimodal optimization.
nodes.problem: Imbalanced multimodal optimization from entangled learning and uniform pace in monolithic frameworks.
nodes.approach: Nested learning with decoupled stable memory block and adaptive coordinated fusion across timescales.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Modality imbalance is established but specialised.

nodes.title: SAW-Bench: Learning Situated Awareness in the Real World
nodes.tldr: Introduces SAW-Bench, a benchmark of 786 smart-glasses videos and 2071 questions testing egocentric situated awareness in multimodal foundation models.
nodes.problem: Existing multimodal benchmarks focus on environment-centric spatial relations, not observer-centric awareness.
nodes.approach: Human-annotated egocentric video QA across six awareness tasks, evaluating frontier multimodal models.
nodes.niche_reason: Observer-centric spatial reasoning benchmark is less saturated than generic VQA

nodes.title: RoboMME: Benchmarking and Understanding Memory for Robotic Generalist Policies
nodes.tldr: Introduces RoboMME, a standardized benchmark of 16 memory-dependent manipulation tasks, and 14 memory-augmented VLA variants built on pi0.5.
nodes.problem: Memory-dependent robotic manipulation lacks standardized evaluation for VLA policies.
nodes.approach: Taxonomy of temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory tasks with memory-augmented VLA baselines.
nodes.niche_reason: Robot memory evaluation is a small but growing niche

nodes.title: Neural Thickets: Diverse Task Experts Are Dense Around Pretrained Weights
nodes.tldr: Argues well-pretrained large models have dense task experts near pretrained weights, so random sampling, top-K selection, and majority vote rivals PPO, GRPO, and ES post-training.
nodes.problem: Pretrained weights are treated only as starting points rather than a distribution already containing task-specific experts.
nodes.approach: Randomly sample N weight perturbations, select top K, and ensemble by majority vote as parallel post-training.
nodes.niche_reason: Random weight sampling as post-training is very unusual and few papers resemble it.

nodes.title: Scaling Real-World Robot Policy Evaluation via Discrete Diffusion World Model
nodes.tldr: dWorldEval is a discrete-diffusion world model treating actions as tokens, with keyframe memory and progress-as-text, for reliable robot policy evaluation.
nodes.problem: World-model-based robot policy evaluation produces false positives and poorly action-controllable predictions.
nodes.approach: Unified token space discrete diffusion with action tokens, sparse keyframe memory, and joint success-indicator generation.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: World-model policy evaluation is emerging and specialised.

nodes.title: Alignment Pretraining: AI Discourse Causes Self-Fulfilling (Mis)alignment
nodes.tldr: Controlled pretraining of 6.9B LLMs shows upsampling AI misalignment discourse increases misalignment, while aligned-behaviour discourse reduces it.
nodes.problem: Whether pretraining discourse about AI causally shapes downstream alignment of LLMs.
nodes.approach: Pretrain 6.9B models with varied synthetic alignment and misalignment document mixtures.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Causal study of AI discourse in pretraining data is rare

nodes.title: Learning to Discover at Test Time
nodes.tldr: TTT-Discover runs reinforcement learning at test time on one problem so an LLM keeps training and finds state-of-the-art solutions in math, kernels, algorithms and biology.
nodes.problem: Discovering new state-of-the-art solutions to individual scientific problems beyond frozen-LLM search.
nodes.approach: Test-time RL with objective and search subroutine prioritising the most promising solutions.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.niche_reason: Test-time RL for discovery is emerging and specialised.

nodes.title: DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research
nodes.tldr: DR Tulu uses Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics to train an open 8B deep research agent for long-form answers, rivaling proprietary systems cheaply.
nodes.problem: Open deep research agents trained on short-form verifiable QA do not extend to long-form research tasks.
nodes.approach: RL with rubrics that co-evolve with the policy using searched information and contrasting responses as on-policy feedback.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: LLM agents trained with RL are common, though evolving rubrics are novel.

nodes.title: On the Convergence Rate of LoRA Gradient Descent
nodes.tldr: Gives the first non-asymptotic convergence analysis of original LoRA gradient descent without boundedness assumptions, proving convergence to a stationary point at rate O(1/log T).
nodes.problem: LoRA lacks Lipschitz smoothness, so its convergence was only analyzed asymptotically or under artificial boundedness assumptions.
nodes.approach: Reformulate via the outer product of stacked adapters, use a modified descent lemma, and control step size.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of LoRA optimization is specialised among many LoRA papers.

nodes.title: Think in Cloud, Look at Edges: Semantic-Driven Query Decomposition for Efficient Video Reasoning
nodes.tldr: A cloud multimodal LLM decomposes video queries into a DAG plan that guides edge devices to fetch relevant frames, cutting transmission cost.
nodes.problem: Edge-cloud long video understanding trades off accuracy against bandwidth, and similarity filtering misses logical cues.
nodes.approach: Cloud LMM builds a query-decomposition DAG, and the edge retrieves evidence by logical necessity, not similarity.
nodes.confidence_reason: judgment call between video understanding, multimodal LLMs and systems
nodes.niche_reason: Edge-cloud video reasoning via DAG query decomposition is unusual

nodes.title: Thinking in Flow: A Dissipative Stabilization Operator for Robust Autoregressive Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Adds a dissipative Neural ODE thought state with gated steering to Transformers, stabilizing long chain-of-thought reasoning against distractions and drift.
nodes.problem: Long chain-of-thought generation is brittle; small deviations compound into inference drift.
nodes.approach: Dissipative Neural ODE controller with demand-supply and direction gates for selective representation steering.
nodes.confidence_reason: Steering method straddles reasoning and dynamical-systems design.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural ODE thought-state steering is a specialised reasoning angle.

nodes.title: PhenoBrain: Phenotype-Conditioned Long-Range Communication for Multi-Modal Brain Network Analysis
nodes.tldr: PhenoBrain conditions long-range connectome communication and attention on phenotype data to predict neuropsychiatric status from multi-modal brain networks.
nodes.problem: Existing methods fuse phenotypes late, ignoring that connectivity meaning depends on phenotype context.
nodes.approach: Phenotype-conditioned multi-hop routing kernel and phenotype-guided attention regulation.
nodes.niche_reason: Phenotype-conditioned connectome modeling is a rare niche.

nodes.title: S$^3$GNN: Efficient Global Mixing and Local Message Passing for Long-Range Graph Learning
nodes.tldr: Proposes S3GNN, combining efficient global spectral mixing with local message passing to fix oversquashing without restrictive theoretical assumptions.
nodes.problem: Message-passing GNNs suffer oversquashing, and spectral fixes rely on hard-to-attain guarantees.
nodes.approach: Lightweight reintroduction of omitted spectral components alongside message passing, with low compute cost.
nodes.niche_reason: Oversquashing is a well-studied GNN topic

nodes.title: Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents
nodes.tldr: LLM agents learn reusable procedural skills from their own experience without weight updates, verified by a non-parametric PPO gate and kept compact by score-based maintenance.
nodes.problem: LLM agents re-derive solutions to recurring scenarios, wasting computation and causing instability.
nodes.approach: Skill-MDP skill extraction with non-parametric PPO candidate generation and verification gate.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.confidence_reason: Agent skill memory versus RL-style optimization framing.
nodes.niche_reason: Non-parametric skill memory for LLM agents is emerging.

nodes.title: Towards Pareto-Optimal Tool-Integrated Agents with Pareto Ranking Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: ParetoPO aligns tool-using LLMs under competing objectives by combining hypervolume-guided scalarization with Pareto-ranking advantages for better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.
nodes.problem: Alignment for tool-using LLMs ignores efficiency, optimizing accuracy alone.
nodes.approach: Two-stage multi-objective RL with Pareto-ranking-based advantage computation.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-objective RL for tool-using LLMs is specialised.

nodes.title: CAT-Q: Cost-efficient and Accurate Ternary Quantization for LLMs
nodes.tldr: A post-training ternary quantization method for LLMs using learnable modulation and softened ternarization, matching BitNet with about 100,000x fewer training tokens.
nodes.problem: Ternary LLM quantization normally needs costly quantization-aware training.
nodes.approach: Learnable weight and threshold modulation with a differentiable softened ternarization, calibrated on 512 samples.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM quantization is a common, crowded area.

nodes.title: Divide-and-Denoise: A Game-Theoretic Method for Fairly Composing Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Divide-and-Denoise composes multiple pretrained diffusion models by solving a fair-division game each timestep to allocate image regions to models, fixing missing objects and attribute mismatches.
nodes.problem: Composing pretrained diffusion models risks one dominating or disagreeing, causing missing objects and mismatched attributes.
nodes.approach: At each step, solve a fair division game for region allocation, then guide each model to denoise its assigned region.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Game-theoretic fair division for model composition is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: SleepLM: Natural-Language Intelligence for Human Sleep
nodes.tldr: Sleep-language foundation models aligning polysomnography with natural language via a large sleep-text dataset and contrastive, captioning and reconstruction pretraining.
nodes.problem: Sleep analysis systems use closed label spaces and cannot describe or query novel sleep phenomena.
nodes.approach: Multilevel caption pipeline for 100K hours of data, unified contrastive, generative and reconstruction pretraining.
nodes.niche_reason: Language-aligned sleep physiology models are very rare.

nodes.title: The Axiomatic Value of Regularization in AI Alignment from Human Preferences
nodes.tldr: Shows reference-policy regularization makes the von Neumann winner RLHF rule satisfy social choice axioms, while the standard Borda-count objective still fails them.
nodes.problem: Standard RLHF aggregates diverse human preferences poorly, and its regularization's axiomatic effect is ignored.
nodes.approach: Analyze regularized RLHF objectives through social choice axioms, comparing Borda count and von Neumann winner rules.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Social-choice analysis of RLHF regularization is a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: MASPOB: Bandit-Based Prompt Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems with Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Optimizes prompts for multi-agent LLM systems with a UCB bandit, GNN-based topology-aware representations, and coordinate ascent to cut search space from exponential to linear.
nodes.problem: Multi-agent system prompts are costly to evaluate and coupled through the workflow topology.
nodes.approach: Sample-efficient UCB bandit over prompts, GNN structural priors, and univariate coordinate-ascent decomposition.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.confidence_reason: Prompt optimization spans prompting and bandit methods; the primary is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt optimization for multi-agent workflows is specialized

nodes.title: Compositional Generalization Requires Linear, Orthogonal Representations in Vision Embedding Models
nodes.tldr: Argues compositional generalization forces embeddings to decompose linearly into orthogonal per-concept factors, checked in CLIP, SigLIP and DINO.
nodes.problem: What geometry representations need in order to generalize to unseen combinations of known concepts.
nodes.approach: Formalize divisibility, transferability and stability, derive linear orthogonal constraints, then measure factorization in embeddings.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Linear representation hypothesis is established but specialised

nodes.title: Unifying Masked Diffusion Models with Various Generation Orders and Beyond
nodes.tldr: Unifies masked diffusion, autoregressive and block diffusion under one framework, then learns the generation order jointly with the model from scratch.
nodes.problem: Masked diffusion language models depend critically on a fixed, hand-chosen generation order.
nodes.approach: Order-expressive masked diffusion framework with a jointly learned ordering policy and backbone.
nodes.niche_reason: Learnable generation order for masked diffusion is specialised

nodes.title: EEmo-Logic: A Unified Dataset and Multi-Stage Framework for Comprehensive Image-Evoked Emotion Assessment
nodes.tldr: Introduces a 1.2M QA-pair image emotion dataset and an MLLM trained with instruction tuning and task-specific GRPO for emotion reasoning.
nodes.problem: Existing models perceive emotion coarsely or reason poorly about multi-dimensional image-evoked emotions.
nodes.approach: Automatically generated QA plus curated fine-grained assessment data, with instruction tuning and reward-designed GRPO.
nodes.confidence_reason: dataset and method contributions straddle two topics
nodes.niche_reason: Image-evoked emotion benchmark and MLLM are rare

nodes.title: Beyond ReLU: Bifurcation, Oversmoothing, and Topological Priors
nodes.tldr: Frames GNN oversmoothing via bifurcation theory and proves non-monotone activations create stable non-homogeneous patterns that resist it, with a scaling law and a bifurcation-aware initialization.
nodes.problem: Deep GNNs suffer oversmoothing, converging to a homogeneous non-informative node state.
nodes.approach: Bifurcation analysis via Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction showing non-monotone activations destabilize the homogeneous fixed point.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamical-systems bifurcation view of GNNs is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Reward and Guidance through Rubrics: Promoting Exploration to Improve Multi-Domain Reasoning
nodes.tldr: RGR-GRPO uses rubrics for dense rewards and offline guidance to improve multi-domain LLM reasoning under GRPO training.
nodes.problem: Purely online RLVR limits exploration and single-domain verifiable rewards restrict multi-domain reasoning.
nodes.approach: Rubric-based dense rewards plus offline guidance integrated into GRPO training.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another GRPO variant with rubric rewards; crowded area

nodes.title: SVL: Empowering Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient 3D Open-World Understanding
nodes.tldr: SVL is a spike-based vision-language pretraining framework giving spiking neural networks zero-shot 3D classification and open-world QA while remaining spike-efficient.
nodes.problem: Spiking neural networks lag ANNs in 3D understanding due to weak pretraining and heavy inference stacks.
nodes.approach: Label-free triplet contrastive alignment of 3D, image and text plus re-parameterizable spike-driven inference.
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking networks with vision-language 3D pretraining are very rare.

nodes.title: Geometric and Stochastic Analysis of Discontinuities in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
nodes.tldr: Rigorous geometric and stochastic analysis of Top-k routing discontinuities in sparse MoE, showing low-order discontinuities dominate, and proposing a cheap smoothing mechanism that improves performance.
nodes.problem: Top-k expert routing makes sparse MoE maps discontinuous, with unclear prevalence and effect.
nodes.approach: Measure-theoretic and diffusion-process analysis of discontinuity orders, plus soft expert inclusion near discontinuities.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Measure-theoretic study of MoE routing discontinuities is rare.

nodes.title: Nash Equilibria in Games with Playerwise Concave Coupling Constraints: Existence and Computation
nodes.tldr: Proves Nash equilibria exist in concave games with playerwise concave coupling constraints, and gives a log-barrier gradient method that converges for potential games.
nodes.problem: Equilibrium existence and convergent learning are unclear when players share coupling constraints.
nodes.approach: Topological fixed-point argument plus log-barrier regularized gradient ascent with adaptive stepsizes.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Specialized game-theoretic optimization with established foundations

nodes.title: Train for Truth, Keep the Skills: Binary Retrieval-Augmented Reward Mitigates Hallucinations
nodes.tldr: Reduces LLM hallucinations with online RL using a binary reward for responses free of contradictions with retrieved evidence, preserving general capabilities.
nodes.problem: Hallucination reduction methods degrade general capabilities, and continuous factuality rewards get reward-hacked.
nodes.approach: Binary reward for no factual contradictions against retrieved evidence, trained with online RL.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: LLM hallucination reduction via RL is a common direction

nodes.title: Concept Removal Guidance: Evidence-Calibrated Negative Guidance for Safe Diffusion Sampling
nodes.tldr: CRG estimates unwanted-concept presence at each diffusion step and adaptively calibrates negative guidance with a closed-form update, cutting attack success without fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Negative guidance for text-to-image safety trades off safety against fidelity and fails under attacks.
nodes.approach: Per-step concept presence estimate plus closed-form constrained update of negative guidance weight.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Negative-guidance safety for diffusion is a common direction.

nodes.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking
nodes.tldr: Jailbreak Foundry uses a multi-agent workflow to turn jailbreak papers into runnable modules in a unified harness, reproducing 30 attacks and enabling standardized benchmarking.
nodes.problem: Jailbreak benchmarks go stale and are inconsistent across papers
nodes.approach: Multi-agent paper-to-code translation with shared library and standardized evaluation harness
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Jailbreak work is crowded; automated paper-to-code reproduction is distinctive

nodes.title: Gradient Flow Through Diagram Expansions: Learning Regimes and Explicit Solutions
nodes.tldr: Uses Feynman-like diagram expansions of loss evolution to derive gradient flow learning regimes and explicit solutions for CP tensor decomposition learning.
nodes.problem: Understanding gradient flow dynamics in large-scale learning lacks analytic characterization across parameter scalings.
nodes.approach: Formal power series of loss evolution with a large-size limit, reduced to a PDE solvable by characteristics.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Dynamics theory placement between DL theory and training dynamics is a judgment.
nodes.niche_reason: Feynman-diagram expansion of gradient flow for CP tensor models is very rare.

nodes.title: The Value of Variance: Mitigating Debate Collapse in Multi-Agent Systems via Uncertainty-Driven Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: Defines hierarchical uncertainty metrics to detect debate collapse in multi-agent LLM debate and uses uncertainty-driven policy optimization to penalize contradiction and low confidence.
nodes.problem: Multi-agent debate systems suffer debate collapse, where final decisions rest on erroneous reasoning, with no principled detection or prevention.
nodes.approach: Three-level behavioral uncertainty metric, then policy optimization penalizing self-contradiction, peer conflict, and low-confidence outputs.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-agent debate failure modes are a specialised but growing area.

nodes.title: Time series saliency maps: Explaining models across multiple domains
nodes.tldr: Cross-domain Integrated Gradients generalizes attribution to any invertible differentiable transform of time series, such as frequency domain, via complex-valued path integrals.
nodes.problem: Time-domain saliency maps miss semantically meaningful features that live in other domains like frequency.
nodes.approach: Extend Integrated Gradients to complex-valued transformed domains while preserving path independence and completeness.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-domain attribution for time series models is an uncommon angle.

nodes.title: Efficient numeracy in language models through single-token number embeddings
nodes.tldr: BitTokens encodes any number as a single token via its IEEE 754 binary representation, letting small LMs learn arithmetic nearly perfectly with fewer reasoning tokens.
nodes.problem: Multi-token number tokenization makes LLM arithmetic inefficient
nodes.approach: Single-token number encoding using IEEE 754 floating-point bits
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Number encoding for LMs is a rare direction.

nodes.title: Benchmarking at the Edge of Comprehension
nodes.tldr: Critique-Resilient Benchmarking ranks LLMs with an adversarial generation-evaluation game where humans act as bounded verifiers, using a Bradley-Terry model.
nodes.problem: As frontier LLMs saturate benchmarks, humans may be unable to create, verify, or grade discriminative tasks.
nodes.approach: Itemized bipartite Bradley-Terry ranking of solvers and question generators under critique-resilient correctness.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Benchmarking beyond human comprehension is a rare evaluation framing.

nodes.title: CVE-Factory: Scaling Expert-Level Agentic Tasks for Code Security Vulnerability
nodes.tldr: Multi-agent framework that turns CVE metadata into executable vulnerability tasks, producing LiveCVEBench and 1000+ training environments for code security agents.
nodes.problem: Code-security agent evaluation relies on costly manual reproduction of vulnerabilities.
nodes.approach: Multi-agent pipeline that automatically builds executable CVE tasks and training environments.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Mixes benchmark, environment synthesis and training contributions.
nodes.niche_reason: Code-security environment synthesis for agents is specialised.

nodes.title: Safety Alignment of LMs via Non-cooperative Games
nodes.tldr: Frames LM safety as a non-zero-sum game where attacker and defender LMs co-train via online RL with pairwise preference rewards.
nodes.problem: Sequential adversarial training for LM safety is brittle and trades off helpfulness against robustness.
nodes.approach: Joint online RL of attacker and defender LMs with pairwise-comparison preference rewards.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.confidence_reason: Safety alignment straddles safety topic and multi-agent RL
nodes.niche_reason: Co-trained attacker-defender LMs for safety is a specialised framing

nodes.title: Shared Semantics, Divergent Mechanisms: Unsupervised Feature Discovery by Aligning Semantics and Mechanisms
nodes.tldr: Clusters LLM continuations using both semantic embeddings and mechanistic attribution signatures with a rate-distortion objective, giving unsupervised distribution-level circuit analysis.
nodes.problem: Circuit analysis explains a single prompt-completion pair and hides heterogeneity across a model's continuation distribution.
nodes.approach: Rate-distortion clustering of continuations by semantic embedding and prefix-to-continuation attribution signatures.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Distribution-level mechanistic clustering is an unusual interpretability angle.

nodes.title: SpatioLM: Towards General Physical Spatial Intelligence in Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Plug-and-play spatio-vision module that boosts spatial reasoning in VLMs without 3D inputs, using pseudo depth and camera supervision while preserving general capabilities.
nodes.problem: VLMs struggle with visual spatial reasoning, and existing fixes degrade general ability.
nodes.approach: Non-invasive spatio-vision module trained with pseudo depth and camera supervision.
nodes.niche_reason: Spatial reasoning adapters for VLMs are an active, specialised area.

nodes.title: OSM+: Billion-Level Open Street Map Dataset for City-wide Experiments
nodes.tldr: OSM+ is a worldwide billion-vertex road network graph dataset from OpenStreetMap with query tools, plus new traffic prediction and traffic control benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Lack of unified billion-scale road network benchmarks
nodes.approach: Distributed processing of OSM into structured graphs; build 31-city prediction and six-city control datasets
nodes.niche_reason: Large-scale road network data is an unusual niche.

nodes.title: Flex-Forcing: Towards a Unified Autoregressive and Bidirectional Video Diffusion Model
nodes.tldr: Flex-Forcing unifies bidirectional and autoregressive video diffusion via flexible chunking over time and denoising steps.
nodes.problem: Bidirectional video diffusion is slow, while autoregressive generation loses long-range consistency.
nodes.approach: Joint temporal-denoising chunking letting one model run under both inference regimes.
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive-bidirectional video diffusion is an active, crowded direction.

nodes.title: Optimal and Scalable MAPF via Multi-Marginal Optimal Transport and Schrödinger Bridges
nodes.tldr: Casts anonymous multi-agent path finding as multi-marginal optimal transport reducing to a polynomial LP, and scales it via Schrodinger bridges and multimarginal Sinkhorn.
nodes.problem: Optimal, scalable anonymous multi-agent path finding on graphs without agent collisions.
nodes.approach: Markovian multi-marginal OT formulated as totally unimodular LP, with Schrodinger bridge probabilistic scaling.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: MAPF via multi-marginal OT is very rare.

nodes.title: CIRBench: Evaluating Large Language Models as LLVM IR Optimizers
nodes.tldr: CIRBench is an 800-instance benchmark evaluating LLMs on LLVM IR analysis, repair, refactoring, and performance transformation with verification, equivalence checking, and speedup measurement.
nodes.problem: No rigorous IR-level benchmark tests whether LLMs can rewrite compiler IR under semantic constraints with performance impact.
nodes.approach: Four-track benchmark with layered verifier, equivalence-checking, and performance evaluation across six LLMs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLMs operating on compiler IR is an unusual, rare direction.

nodes.title: Detecting the Semantic Fixed Point: A Geometric Framework for Efficient Inference
nodes.tldr: Early-exits Transformer layers when hidden-state updates shrink in size and stabilize in direction, cutting FLOPs by 30-35% with minimal accuracy loss.
nodes.problem: Deciding when to stop iterating through Transformer layers without relying on output confidence.
nodes.approach: Monitor normalized update norm and cosine similarity between consecutive layer updates.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Geometric early exit is less common than confidence exits

nodes.title: FlexRank: Nested Low-Rank Knowledge Decomposition for Adaptive Model Deployment
nodes.tldr: FlexRank extracts nested, importance-ordered low-rank submodels from pretrained LLMs and ViTs so one trained model can be deployed at many compute budgets.
nodes.problem: Large models are fixed-cost monoliths, hindering deployment under varying compute budgets.
nodes.approach: Low-rank weight decomposition with nested importance-based consolidation to produce submodels of increasing capability.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Low-rank compression and elastic models are fairly common.

nodes.title: Reinforced Sequential Monte Carlo for Amortised Sampling
nodes.tldr: Connects sequential Monte Carlo with MaxEnt-RL-trained neural samplers, using SMC samples as off-policy behaviour data to train amortised samplers for unnormalised densities.
nodes.problem: Amortised neural samplers explore multi-modal unnormalised targets poorly and train unstably.
nodes.approach: Off-policy RL training with SMC using learned policy as proposal and value as twist, adaptive tempering, replay with AIS weights.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Neural samplers for unnormalised densities combined with SMC is a niche.

nodes.title: Activation Oracles: Training and Evaluating LLMs as General-Purpose Activation Explainers
nodes.tldr: Trains LLMs to answer natural-language questions about other LLMs' activations, and shows these Activation Oracles generalize far out of distribution, matching white-box baselines.
nodes.problem: Interpreting LLM activations with simple, general-purpose tools rather than specialized methods.
nodes.approach: Train LatentQA-style models on diverse activation-question datasets and evaluate on four downstream auditing tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Growing interpretability subarea; verbalizing activations is a distinctive angle.

nodes.title: Are VLMs Seeing or Just Saying? Uncovering the Illusion of Visual Re-examination
nodes.tldr: Image-swap probe shows VLMs claiming to recheck an image mostly miss a swap; thinking models are more vulnerable and self-reflection does not raise visual attention.
nodes.problem: Whether self-reflective statements in VLMs trigger genuine visual re-examination.
nodes.approach: VisualSwap probing with 800-pair VS-Bench and attention analysis across several VLMs.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Probing faithfulness of visual reflection in VLMs is a fairly specific angle.

nodes.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Bayesian Non-negative Reward Modeling
nodes.tldr: Bayesian non-negative reward model that disentangles reward factors and sparsely debiases spurious features, reducing reward hacking in RLHF.
nodes.problem: Learned reward models over-optimise and exploit biases like length, making RLHF unreliable.
nodes.approach: Non-negative factor analysis inside Bradley-Terry preferences with amortized variational inference over LLM features.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Reward modelling for RLHF is a crowded mainstream topic

nodes.title: Judging What We Cannot Solve: A Consequence-Based Approach for Oracle-Free Evaluation of Research-Level Math
nodes.tldr: Scores candidate math solutions by how well each works as an in-context example for solving related verifiable questions, outperforming reward models and LLM judges.
nodes.problem: Verifying research-level math solutions consumes scarce expert time.
nodes.approach: Consequence-Based Utility tests each candidate as an in-context exemplar on neighboring questions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Oracle-free verification of research-level math is specialised

nodes.title: Universal Redundancies in Time Series Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Finds leading time-series foundation models contain redundant layers; a stable-rank criterion locates heads causing motif parroting and seasonality bias.
nodes.problem: Time-series foundation models' internal components and degenerate behaviors are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Component ablations and direct logit attribution, plus a stable-rank criterion for head ablation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic analysis of time-series foundation models is rare

nodes.title: Control Consistency Losses for Diffusion Bridges
nodes.tldr: Learns diffusion bridges that simulate conditioned dynamics between initial and terminal states, using a self-consistency property of optimal control, without differentiating through trajectories.
nodes.problem: Conditioned dynamics for rare events are hard to simulate because unconditioned dynamics rarely reach the target state.
nodes.approach: Iterative online learning based on the self-consistency of the optimal control.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion bridges via stochastic control are specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Hamiltonian Flow Maps: Mean Flow Consistency for Large-Timestep Molecular Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Learns Hamiltonian flow maps that predict mean phase-space evolution over large timesteps, enabling stable molecular dynamics beyond classical integrator limits without trajectory data.
nodes.problem: Hamiltonian simulation needs tiny timesteps for stable integration, which is expensive.
nodes.approach: Mean Flow consistency for time-averaged Hamiltonian dynamics, trainable on independent trajectory-free samples.
nodes.confidence_reason: molecular dynamics sits between physics and flow-map topics
nodes.niche_reason: learned large-timestep flow maps for Hamiltonian systems are rare

nodes.title: Online Conformal Prediction via Universal Portfolio Algorithms
nodes.tldr: Gives parameter-free online conformal prediction with coverage guarantees by reducing interval learning to a two-asset portfolio problem solved by universal portfolios.
nodes.problem: Online conformal prediction needs manual learning-rate tuning for adversarial data streams
nodes.approach: Regret-to-coverage theory with a universal portfolio reduction for prediction intervals
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Universal-portfolio reduction for conformal prediction is unusual

nodes.title: Know More, Know Clearer: A Meta-Cognitive Framework for Knowledge Augmentation in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Partitions an LLM's knowledge into mastered, confused, and missing regions to target augmentation, and aligns confidence with accuracy for calibrated knowledge boundaries.
nodes.problem: Knowledge augmentation assumes performance equals knowledge, causing overconfident errors and uncertain truths.
nodes.approach: Uses internal cognitive signals to split knowledge into mastered, confused, and missing regions for targeted expansion.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.confidence_reason: Knowledge augmentation versus confidence calibration; both topics plausible
nodes.niche_reason: Meta-cognitive knowledge-boundary alignment is a specialised angle

nodes.title: Root Cause Analysis of Failures in Microservices via Bayesian Root Cause Discovery
nodes.tldr: Bayesian root cause discovery identifies root causes of microservice failures from a partial causal graph, with consistency guarantees and no full DAG enumeration.
nodes.problem: Root cause analysis needs many post-failure interventions or the full causal graph.
nodes.approach: Bayesian inference over a CPDAG using uniform DAG sampling, with consistency guarantees.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Causal RCA for cloud microservices is specialised but has some prior work.

nodes.title: Towards Optimal Robustness in Learning-Augmented Paging
nodes.tldr: Achieves the optimal randomized competitive ratio H_k + O(1) for learning-augmented paging, closing a gap in prediction-robustness bounds.
nodes.problem: Prior learning-augmented paging algorithms had robustness bounds of 2H_k + O(1), not optimal.
nodes.approach: A relative prediction budget analysis guides a new framework that neither over- nor under-uses predictions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: online paging algorithms with ML predictions and competitive analysis.

nodes.title: Listening Through the Noise: Cauchy-Driven Diffusion Bridges for Robust Gastrointestinal Auscultation and Clinical Benchmarking
nodes.tldr: Uses a Cauchy-driven diffusion bridge to separate bowel sounds from speech interference and heavy-tailed clinical noise, with a new 25-hour clinical dataset.
nodes.problem: Gaussian diffusion restorers fail on impulsive, heavy-tailed clinical noise that overlaps bowel sounds spectrally.
nodes.approach: Cauchy bridge driver with closed-form score and density, sampled efficiently via Gaussian scale-mixture reparameterization.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Cauchy-driven diffusion bridges for bowel sound restoration are very rare.

nodes.title: Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Argues RL with binary terminal rewards is a first-order approximation to maximum likelihood, and proposes MaxRL, a compute-indexed family of objectives interpolating between them.
nodes.problem: Expected-reward RL is only a first-order approximation of the likelihood over correct rollouts in sample-based training.
nodes.approach: Sample-based objectives indexed by sampling compute, a one-line change to standard RL implementations.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another RL objective variant for LLM training

nodes.title: ThreadWeaver: Adaptive Threading for Efficient Parallel Reasoning in Language Models
nodes.tldr: ThreadWeaver enables adaptive parallel chain-of-thought reasoning on standard inference engines via trie-based rollouts and parallelization-aware RL, matching sequential accuracy with up to 1.53x speedup.
nodes.problem: Sequential LLM reasoning decoding is slow and parallel reasoning methods lose accuracy.
nodes.approach: Parallel trajectory data generation, trie-based rollout, and parallelization-aware reinforcement learning.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM reasoning efficiency is a very active, common area.

nodes.title: Learning Unmasking Policies for Diffusion Language Models
nodes.tldr: Trains a small RL policy to choose which tokens to unmask at each diffusion step, matching strong heuristics and beating them in full-diffusion sampling.
nodes.problem: Heuristic unmasking rules need manual tuning and degrade with larger block sizes
nodes.approach: Masked-diffusion sampling as an MDP with a single-layer transformer policy over token confidences
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Learned sampling for diffusion LLMs is a small, emerging direction

nodes.title: OC-space: a Unifying Perspective on Verification of Tree Ensembles
nodes.tldr: Verifies properties like robustness and fairness of tree ensembles by searching the space of all combinations of tree predictions, faster than task-specific methods.
nodes.problem: Verifying robustness or fairness of tree ensembles is NP-hard and usually solved separately for each task.
nodes.approach: Frame verification as search over the OC-space of all ensemble output configurations, with spatial indexes.
nodes.confidence_reason: Verification framing spans robustness and fairness; tree ensembles are tabular.
nodes.niche_reason: Verifying tree ensembles against robustness and fairness is a niche verification topic.

nodes.title: HELIX: Hybrid Encoding with Learnable Identity and Cross-dimensional Synthesis for Time Series Imputation
nodes.tldr: HELIX gives each feature a learnable persistent identity embedding with hybrid temporal-feature attention for time series imputation, beating 16 baselines across 5 datasets.
nodes.problem: Attention-based imputation re-discovers feature relationships per layer without persistent anchors, and graph methods need fixed topology.
nodes.approach: Learnable feature identity embeddings plus hybrid temporal-feature attention learning dependencies end to end.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Imputation is an established but specialised time-series task.

nodes.title: PaperBanana: Automating Academic Illustration for AI Scientists
nodes.tldr: Agentic framework where specialized VLM agents retrieve references, plan, render and self-critique to automatically produce publication-ready academic diagrams, plus a 292-case benchmark.
nodes.problem: Automating labor-intensive creation of publication-ready academic illustrations.
nodes.approach: Multi-agent pipeline of retrieval, planning, rendering and iterative self-critique with VLMs and image generators.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual application: automated scientific figure generation for AI scientists.

nodes.title: DreamDojo: A Generalist Robot World Model from Large-Scale Human Videos
nodes.tldr: A robot world model pretrained on 44k hours of egocentric human video using continuous latent actions, running in real time at about 10.9 FPS.
nodes.problem: Robot world models lack action labels and data coverage for dexterous contact-rich tasks.
nodes.approach: Continuous latent actions as proxy labels for unlabeled video, plus distillation for real-time speed.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: World model could fit robotics simulation or video generation.
nodes.niche_reason: Robot world model pretrained on egocentric human video; emerging and specialised.

nodes.title: DGS-Net: Distillation-Guided Gradient Surgery for CLIP Fine-Tuning in AI-Generated Image Detection
nodes.tldr: DGS-Net fine-tunes CLIP for AI-generated image detection with gradient surgery, projecting away harmful directions and aligning with distilled beneficial ones to avoid forgetting.
nodes.problem: Catastrophic forgetting when fine-tuning CLIP for AI-generated image detection
nodes.approach: Gradient-space decomposition with projection plus distillation from a frozen CLIP encoder
nodes.niche_reason: Generated-image detection is active but common; gradient surgery angle specialised

nodes.title: Video-Based Optimal Transport for Feedback-Efficient Offline Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Learns reward functions from few preference labels by using optimal transport over video foundation model features to pseudo-label unlabeled trajectories.
nodes.problem: Preference-based RL needs too many costly human labels to learn reward functions.
nodes.approach: Semi-supervised optimal-transport alignment of video trajectories in video foundation model space.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Preference RL is established, video-OT pseudo-labelling is specialised

nodes.title: Securing Multimodal AI through Internal Information Decomposition
nodes.tldr: Detects harmful multimodal inputs at inference by checking whether fused and unimodal predictions agree, using Partial Information Decomposition flow vectors.
nodes.problem: Multimodal LLMs can be jailbroken by splitting malicious intent across modalities to evade unimodal safety checks.
nodes.approach: One-class detector trained on benign data using FlowVectors that measure cross-modal redundancy and synergy.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-modal consistency defense is specialised within MLLM safety

nodes.title: Unifying and Optimizing Data Values for Selection via Sequential Decision-Making
nodes.tldr: Reframes data selection as sequential decision-making solved by dynamic programming, unifying Data Shapley as a myopic approximation and proposing a graph-based greedy selector.
nodes.problem: Data values are used for selection without theory explaining when that is optimal.
nodes.approach: Approximate dynamic programming analysis plus a bipartite graph surrogate for scalable submodular greedy selection.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Valuation-based selection could fit curation or attribution.
nodes.niche_reason: Reframes data valuation as sequential selection via dynamic programming; specialised.

nodes.title: Less is Enough: Synthesizing Diverse Data in LLM Feature Space with Sparse Autoencoders
nodes.tldr: Introduces Feature Activation Coverage to measure data diversity in sparse-autoencoder feature space, and FAC Synthesis to generate samples covering missing features, improving downstream LLM tasks.
nodes.problem: Text-based diversity metrics poorly capture task-relevant features in LLM post-training data.
nodes.approach: Sparse autoencoder identifies missing features in seed data; generate synthetic samples targeting them.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Interpretability-driven data synthesis is somewhat unusual.

nodes.title: High-Accuracy Sampling for Diffusion Models and Log-Concave Distributions
nodes.tldr: Gives diffusion samplers polylogarithmic step complexity in accuracy, an exponential improvement, and extends the result to log-concave distributions.
nodes.problem: Diffusion sampling needs many steps for high accuracy, limiting theoretical efficiency
nodes.approach: Analysis of score-based sampling showing polylog(1/delta) steps given accurate score estimates in L2.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised sampling-complexity result within diffusion theory

nodes.title: Failure-Driven Workflow Refinement
nodes.tldr: CE-Graph refines tool-using LLM agent workflows by modelling failure distributions and editing workflow graphs against a pool of counterexamples, improving robustness at lower cost.
nodes.problem: Workflow search for tool-using agents collapses rich failure traces into binary scores, making refinement inefficient.
nodes.approach: Counterexample-guided distributional refinement with operator-constrained graph edits in a propose-and-verify loop.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: agent-workflow search vs robustness placement uncertain
nodes.niche_reason: failure-driven agent workflow search is specialised

nodes.title: The Signal is in the Steps: Local Scoring for Reasoning Data Selection
nodes.tldr: Scores each reasoning step using only a short window of preceding context to select better distillation traces from diverse teachers, outperforming full-trajectory likelihood selection.
nodes.problem: Selecting student-likely full solutions for distillation from many teachers fails, because students learn from reusable local steps.
nodes.approach: Local Average Log Probability: average log-probability of each step conditioned only on a small window of preceding context.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Step-level data selection for reasoning distillation is an emerging niche

nodes.title: Robust Filter Attention: Self-Attention as Precision-Weighted State Estimation
nodes.tldr: Robust Filter Attention treats tokens as noisy observations of an SDE-governed latent trajectory, weighting attention by consistency, improving perplexity over RoPE and length extrapolation.
nodes.problem: Self-attention lacks a principled uncertainty-aware treatment of position and noise.
nodes.approach: Attention as precision-weighted robust state estimation under a linear stochastic differential equation model.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Control-theoretic state estimation view of attention is unusual.

nodes.title: MuonSSM: Orthogonalizing State Space Models for Sequence Modeling
nodes.tldr: MuonSSM stabilizes state space models by conditioning update geometry with a momentum pathway and Newton-Schulz orthogonalization of low-rank input injections.
nodes.problem: SSMs suffer instability and memory degradation over long horizons due to poorly conditioned updates.
nodes.approach: Momentum pathway plus lightweight Newton-Schulz transform on low-rank input injections, preserving parallel scan.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Orthogonalized updates for SSMs are a specialised architecture niche.

nodes.title: Which Algorithms Can Graph Neural Networks Learn?
nodes.tldr: Gives sufficient conditions under which message-passing GNNs trained on small graphs provably generalize to arbitrary-size inputs for many algorithms, with impossibility results.
nodes.problem: Unclear when GNNs learn discrete algorithms and generalize beyond their training instance sizes.
nodes.approach: Theoretical framework for size generalization, plus impossibility proofs and expressive MPNN-like variants.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised theory within neural algorithmic reasoning

nodes.title: Teaching Models to Teach Themselves: Reasoning at the Edge of Learnability
nodes.tldr: A teacher LLM generates synthetic problems rewarded by student improvement on hard problems, enabling learning from sparse rewards on zero-success math tasks.
nodes.problem: RL for reasoning stalls on hard datasets with near-zero success and little training signal.
nodes.approach: Asymmetric teacher-student self-play with meta-RL, grounding curriculum rewards in real student progress.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: self-play curricula for LLM reasoning are specialised

nodes.title: When Attributes Disagree: Gradient Conflict in Image Aesthetic Assessment
nodes.tldr: Routes gradients into attribute-specific subspaces based on sensitivity, resolving gradient conflict in image aesthetic assessment trained only on overall scores.
nodes.problem: Blended attribute signals cause gradient conflict and systematic bias in aesthetic scoring.
nodes.approach: Attribute-guided gradient routing with semantic anchors and error-aware reweighting.
nodes.confidence_reason: Vision task, but contribution is training dynamics, not aesthetics
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised aesthetic task, gradient-conflict angle less common

nodes.title: Emergent Analogical Reasoning in Transformers
nodes.tldr: Formalizes analogy via category-theory functors; Transformers align relational geometry in embeddings then apply a functor, with the same trends in pretrained LLMs.
nodes.problem: Mechanisms of analogical reasoning in Transformers are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Functor-inspired synthetic tasks plus mechanistic analysis of embedding alignment and functor application.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Category-theoretic framing of analogy is unusual.

nodes.title: VGGT-Motion: Motion-Aware Calibration-Free Monocular SLAM for Long-Range Consistency
nodes.tldr: VGGT-Motion is a calibration-free monocular SLAM that uses optical-flow submaps and anchor-driven Sim(3) registration to stay consistent over kilometre-scale trajectories.
nodes.problem: Monocular SLAM with foundation-model geometry suffers scale drift on long, kilometre-scale sequences.
nodes.approach: Motion-aware submaps, direct dense Sim(3) alignment via context-balanced anchors, and submap pose-graph optimisation.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned monocular SLAM is an active, fairly common direction.

nodes.title: Real-World Unsupervised Models Generalize to Predict Brain Responses to Out-of-Distribution Stimuli
nodes.tldr: Unsupervised models trained on real-world data predict brain responses better than supervised ones, and generalise out-of-distribution across languages and viewpoints.
nodes.problem: Whether unsupervised, real-world-trained networks better model sensory cortex than supervised curated-data models.
nodes.approach: Compare unsupervised and supervised networks on natural data distributions against auditory and visual brain responses.
nodes.confidence_reason: neuroscience vs self-supervised learning placement is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: NeuroAI studies of training-data statistics are rare

nodes.title: Eigenvectors of Experts are Training-free Non-collapsing Routers
nodes.tldr: SSMoE uses eigenvectors of expert weight matrices as a training-free router, fixing expert collapse in pretrained sparse mixture-of-experts models.
nodes.problem: Expert collapse in sparse mixture-of-experts models persists after pretraining and degrades performance.
nodes.approach: Singular value decomposition of expert weights yields routing directions, requiring no retraining or fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Spectral routing for MoE is specialised but not unusual

nodes.title: FlatLand: Personalized Graph Federated Learning via Tailored Lorentz Space
nodes.tldr: FlatLand personalizes graph federated learning by embedding clients in tailored Lorentz hyperbolic space, separating time-like heterogeneous parameters from space-like shared ones for direct aggregation.
nodes.problem: Personalized federated learning ignores the geometry of structurally diverse client graphs under heterogeneous data.
nodes.approach: Client-specific Lorentz-space embeddings with parameter decoupling of time-like (personal) and space-like (common) components.
nodes.niche_reason: Hyperbolic personalized federated graph learning is a rare combination.

nodes.title: Posterior Behavioral Cloning: Pretraining BC Policies for Efficient RL Finetuning
nodes.tldr: Shows standard behavioral cloning can lack action coverage needed for RL finetuning, and proposes modeling the posterior over demonstrator behavior to give better initializations.
nodes.problem: Pretrained BC policies may be poor initializations for subsequent RL finetuning.
nodes.approach: Train generative policy to model posterior of demonstrator behavior given data, ensuring coverage.
nodes.niche_reason: Pretraining-for-finetuning theory in imitation learning is specialised.

nodes.title: On the Role of Computation in Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Formalizes compute-bounded RL policies, proves more compute can solve more problems, and proposes a minimal architecture whose performance improves with extra compute.
nodes.problem: Standard RL frameworks conflate compute with parameter count and cannot formally capture the role of compute.
nodes.approach: Compute-bounded policy formalization and a minimal variable-compute architecture evaluated on 31 RL tasks.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory and architecture contributions are both central.
nodes.niche_reason: Formal compute-bounded RL policies are rare.

nodes.title: Beyond First-order Asymptotics in Sequential Mean Testing
nodes.tldr: Proves a central limit theorem for the stopping time of an asymptotically optimal KL-inf sequential mean test, giving second-order characterization for bounded distributions.
nodes.problem: First-order analyses leave the fluctuations of sequential test stopping times uncharacterized.
nodes.approach: CLT for the KL-inf statistic, then scaled CLT for the stopping time with explicit variance.
nodes.confidence_reason: Sequential testing fits between information theory and bandit-style decisions
nodes.niche_reason: Second-order asymptotics of sequential tests is a rare theory topic

nodes.title: Geometry-Aware Decoding with Wasserstein-Regularized Truncation and Mass Penalties for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Top-W truncates LLM next-token distributions using Wasserstein distance over token-embedding geometry, balancing kept mass against entropy and improving accuracy and creativity.
nodes.problem: Heuristic truncation samplers ignore the semantic geometry of the token embedding space.
nodes.approach: Closed-form geometry-aware crop from a Wasserstein-regularized mass-entropy trade-off, found by linear scan.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.confidence_reason: Decoding fits sampling or LLM efficiency; a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: geometry-aware LLM decoding.

nodes.title: Don't Reinvent the Wheel, Just Realign the Spokes: Resource-Efficient Federated Fine-Tuning via Rank-Wise Expert Assembly
nodes.tldr: Reuses existing LoRA modules in federated fine-tuning by splitting them into rank-wise experts and adaptively allocating expert quotas to cut edge-device cost.
nodes.problem: Federated LLM fine-tuning is too costly in compute and communication for resource-constrained edge devices.
nodes.approach: Mixture of rank-wise LoRA experts activated by input and budget, with elastic per-matrix expert quota allocation.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.confidence_reason: federated LoRA reuse touches fine-tuning, federated systems, and MoE routing
nodes.niche_reason: Federated LoRA and MoE-style adapters are common, active directions.

nodes.title: Learning Coupled Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics from Irregular Events
nodes.tldr: Jointly models individual and population latent dynamics in continuous time, using a diffusion-based latent interpolator with neural ODEs for irregular event sequences.
nodes.problem: Irregular, sparse event sequences need individual and population dynamics modelled together in continuous time.
nodes.approach: Coupled neural ODE latent dynamics with a diffusion latent interpolator aligning states across arbitrary time points.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Coupled continuous-time event modelling with diffusion is unusual

nodes.title: 3ViewSense: Spatial and Mental Perspective Reasoning from Orthographic Views in Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Grounds VLM spatial reasoning in canonical orthographic projections, letting the model simulate views and reason about occluded 3D structure.
nodes.problem: Vision-language models fail at elementary spatial tasks like counting occluded blocks.
nodes.approach: Simulate-and-Reason: decompose scenes into orthographic projections and align egocentric views to them.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spatial reasoning in VLMs straddles vision-language and 3D geometry.
nodes.niche_reason: Orthographic-view spatial reasoning for VLMs is specialised.

nodes.title: CLEAR: Context-Aware Learning with End-to-End Mask-Free Inference for Adaptive Video Subtitle Removal
nodes.tldr: CLEAR is a lightweight adapter framework for video subtitle removal that learns occlusion priors self-supervised from video pairs and needs no explicit masks at inference.
nodes.problem: Mask-guided diffusion subtitle removal needs annotations, full fine-tuning, and mask sequences at inference.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised prior learning from pixel differences plus LoRA-based adaptive refinement for end-to-end mask-free removal.
nodes.niche_reason: Subtitle removal is a rare, narrow video editing task.

nodes.title: Neuro-evolutionary Continual Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Continual RL method that evolves masks over a fixed-capacity policy network, freezing neurons for old skills and reusing them for related tasks.
nodes.problem: Continual RL must retain old skills without forgetting while transferring knowledge to new tasks.
nodes.approach: Neuro-evolutionary mask population with importance-guided crossover and pruning of low-activity connections.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Neuro-evolutionary mask-based continual RL is unusual

nodes.title: Decoupling The "What" and "Where" With Polar Coordinate Positional Embedding
nodes.tldr: Replaces RoPE's entangled key-query matching with polar coordinate positional embeddings, improving sequence modeling and zero-shot length extrapolation.
nodes.problem: RoPE entangles content and position in attention, hurting matches that need them independent.
nodes.approach: Polar Coordinate Position Embedding (PoPE) removes the what-where confound in attention scoring.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: positional encoding variants are a crowded area

nodes.title: Characterizing, Evaluating, and Optimizing Complex Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Defines reasoning quality via the ME^2 principle, evaluates reasoning traces as DAGs, and trains a Thinking Reward Model whose signals improve test-time selection and RL training.
nodes.problem: No unified definition, reliable evaluation, or optimization use of complex reasoning trace quality.
nodes.approach: ME^2 principle, DAG-based pairwise trace evaluation, TRM-Preference dataset and a trained thinking reward model.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Reasoning reward models for LRMs are a crowded area.

nodes.title: Generative Modeling of Irregular Time Series via SDE-Induced Continuous-Discrete Variational Inference
nodes.tldr: SDEVI performs variational inference over discrete observations of irregular time series while staying consistent with an underlying neural SDE, avoiding costly path-based inference.
nodes.problem: Path-based variational inference for continuous-discrete state-space models is costly or restrictive.
nodes.approach: Variational inference on joint discrete-time distribution induced by a neural SDE.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Neural SDE variational inference for irregular series is niche.

nodes.title: Geometric Flow Grounding: A Unified Manifold Decoupling Framework for Dynamics Discovery and Verification
nodes.tldr: Enforces dynamics along the tangent space of a learned data manifold via a projection layer, improving dynamical-system forecasting and flagging deepfake videos by residual.
nodes.problem: Learned dynamics models drift off-manifold, violating geometric constraints over long horizons.
nodes.approach: Differentiable Neural Tangent Projection Layer separating static state from tangential motion.
nodes.primary_topic: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.confidence_reason: Vague method description spanning three unrelated applications
nodes.niche_reason: Manifold projection for both dynamics discovery and deepfake detection is unusual

nodes.title: Lookahead Sample Reward Guidance for Test-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Steers diffusion sampling toward high-reward regions via closed-form expected future reward and few-step lookahead, matching gradient guidance at 9.5x speed.
nodes.problem: Expected future reward for diffusion guidance is costly via rollouts or biased via Tweedie approximations
nodes.approach: Closed-form reward guidance from marginal samples plus few-step lookahead particle sampling with an accurate solver
nodes.niche_reason: Test-time guidance for diffusion is a specialised area

nodes.title: MemoryBench: A Benchmark for Memory and Continual Learning in LLM Systems
