nodes.approach: Decision-theoretic minimax policy against worst-case distributions consistent with coverage, yielding risk-optimal conformal sets.
nodes.niche_reason: Conformal prediction is established; decision-theoretic optimality is more specialised.

nodes.title: Orthogonal Concept Erasure for Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Erases unsafe concepts from diffusion models using multiplicative orthogonal weight transforms that preserve neuron magnitude and angular geometry, scaling to 100 concepts.
nodes.problem: Additive editing for concept erasure entangles direction and magnitude, hurting overall generation quality.
nodes.approach: Layer-wise closed-form orthogonal transformations with a subspace objective for multi-concept erasure.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: unlearning vs safety/generation framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: concept erasure is an active but specialised safety topic

nodes.title: From Pixels to Tokens: A Systematic Study of Latent Action Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models
nodes.tldr: Systematically compares four ways to supervise vision-language-action models with latent actions, finding image-based suits long-horizon tasks and action-based suits motor coordination.
nodes.problem: Latent action supervision for VLA models is fragmented and never compared systematically
nodes.approach: Unified VLA baseline comparing four image- and action-based latent integration strategies
nodes.niche_reason: Active VLA area; latent-action variants are increasingly common

nodes.title: World-Model Inspired Emotion-aware Token Refinement for Training-Free Multimodal Emotion Recognition
nodes.tldr: WETR is a training-free token refinement plug-in for MLLMs that suppresses noisy tokens and reweights emotion-relevant ones, improving multimodal emotion recognition.
nodes.problem: MLLMs lose sparse emotional cues among redundant context in multimodal emotion recognition.
nodes.approach: Noise-suppressed token selection and state-strengthened token reweighting under frozen parameters, inspired by world models.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Training-free token refinement for emotion recognition is niche.

nodes.title: Recurrent Structural Policy Gradient for Partially Observable Mean Field Games
nodes.tldr: RSPG is a history-aware hybrid structural policy gradient for partially observable mean field games, converging an order of magnitude faster than model-free RL.
nodes.problem: Model-free mean field game methods have high variance, and hybrid structural methods lack partial observability.
nodes.approach: Recurrent hybrid structural method computing exact expected returns over Monte Carlo common-noise rollouts, with JAX framework MFAX.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Partially observable mean field games with recurrent policies are rare.

nodes.title: FlashSinkhorn: IO-Aware Entropic Optimal Transport on GPU
nodes.tldr: FlashSinkhorn recasts log-domain Sinkhorn updates as attention-like LogSumExp reductions, enabling FlashAttention-style fused Triton GPU kernels with large speedups for entropic optimal transport.
nodes.problem: GPU entropic optimal transport solvers are inefficient and memory-bound at scale.
nodes.approach: IO-aware fused Triton kernels tiling Sinkhorn updates through SRAM like FlashAttention, with streaming transport application.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Systems-level optimal transport solver is specialised but part of an active line.

nodes.title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
nodes.tldr: Finds pretrained vision-language-action models resist catastrophic forgetting; simple experience replay often prevents forgetting entirely, with pretraining enabling recovery of seemingly lost skills.
nodes.problem: Continual learning causes robot policies to forget earlier skills; large pretrained VLAs are understudied.
nodes.approach: Empirical study of experience replay with varying replay buffer sizes across pretrained VLA and from-scratch policies.
nodes.niche_reason: Continual learning for VLAs is specialised but emerging.

nodes.title: TG-RAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Reasoning Guidance in Specialized Domains
nodes.tldr: Proposes TG-RAG, which interrupts reasoning to retrieve and inject step-specific directives from an expert procedure graph built from SOPs, keeping specialised-domain reasoning faithful.
nodes.problem: Reasoning models drift from standard operating procedures in specialised domains when given SOPs as context.
nodes.approach: Interrupt-Retrieve-Generate mechanism over an Expert Procedure Graph formalising unstructured SOPs.
nodes.confidence_reason: Abstract thin on evaluation; retrieval-versus-reasoning-guidance is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: RAG for domain reasoning is common; procedure-graph steering is less so.

nodes.title: Treatment Responder Classification with Abstention
nodes.tldr: Doubly robust method TRECA classifies treatment responders while abstaining on uncertain individuals, linking causal misclassification risk with abstention to CVaR.
nodes.problem: Classifying who benefits from treatment when abstaining on uncertain cases is allowed.
nodes.approach: Doubly robust learning via CVaR connection, extended to handle violations of monotonicity and unconfoundedness.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal classification with abstention is a rare combination.

nodes.title: UDM-GRPO: Stable and Efficient Group Relative Policy Optimization for Uniform Discrete Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: First framework combining GRPO with uniform discrete diffusion, using the clean sample as the action and forward-process trajectory reconstruction for stable text-to-image RL.
nodes.problem: Naively applying GRPO to uniform discrete diffusion causes instability and little gain.
nodes.approach: Treat final clean sample as action, reconstruct trajectories via forward process, add reduced-step and CFG-free training.
nodes.niche_reason: RL for discrete diffusion is newer and less crowded than continuous diffusion RL.

nodes.title: Linguistic Properties and Model Scale in Brain Encoding: From Small to Compressed Language Models
nodes.tldr: Finds 3B small language models match larger LLMs in predicting fMRI language responses, and quantization and pruning largely preserve brain alignment.
nodes.problem: Minimal model scale and precision needed to capture brain-relevant language representations is unknown.
nodes.approach: Compare full, small, quantized, and pruned LMs by predicting fMRI responses; probe linguistic properties.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LM-brain encoding studies are specialised cross-disciplinary work

nodes.title: CausalGame: Benchmarking Causal Thinking of LLM Agents in Games
nodes.tldr: A benchmark of interactive games testing whether LLM agents can design experiments and recover causal structure under confounders, selection bias and noise.
nodes.problem: Existing AI-scientist benchmarks ignore hidden confounders, selection bias, and noisy measurements.
nodes.approach: 14 interactive game settings where agents act, collect data, and explain a solution.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal reasoning evaluation for agents is specialised but growing.

nodes.title: FlashOptim: Optimizers for Memory-Efficient Training
nodes.tldr: Cuts per-parameter memory of mixed-precision optimizers by over half via better master-weight splitting and 8-bit companded optimizer states.
nodes.problem: Mixed-precision training needs many bytes of memory per parameter for weights, gradients, and optimizer state.
nodes.approach: Tight-bound master weight splitting, companding functions for 8-bit optimizer states, 16-bit gradients.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient optimizer memory is an active, fairly common area.

nodes.title: Information-Theoretic Disentangled Latent Modeling with Conditional Diffusion for Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
nodes.tldr: IDCD disentangles each view into semantic and view-specific latents, then uses a conditional diffusion model to generate missing views for clustering.
nodes.problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering suffers from view missingness and entangled shared and view-specific factors.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic disentanglement, Wasserstein mixture aggregation with Gaussian mixture prior, and conditional diffusion imputation.
nodes.confidence_reason: Multi-view clustering plus diffusion imputation; two topics plausibly fit.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based missing-view generation for clustering is specialised.

nodes.title: PhotoAgent: Exploratory Visual Aesthetic Planning with Large Vision Models
nodes.tldr: Agent system for autonomous photo editing that plans multi-step edits via tree search with memory and visual feedback, plus a 7,000-photo aesthetic benchmark.
nodes.problem: Instruction-based image editing burdens users with task decomposition; autonomous aesthetic editing needs planning and evaluation.
nodes.approach: Tree-search aesthetic planning in a closed loop with memory, using a learned aesthetic reward model.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Agentic aesthetic photo editing is a less common direction.

nodes.title: SceneSmith: Agentic Generation of Simulation-Ready Indoor Scenes
nodes.tldr: A hierarchical VLM-agent framework that generates dense, physically stable, simulation-ready indoor scenes with articulated objects from text, usable for robot policy evaluation.
nodes.problem: Existing scene synthesis yields sparse, physically simplistic rooms unsuitable for home robot simulation.
nodes.approach: Designer, critic and orchestrator VLM agents build layout, furniture and objects with text-to-3D, retrieval and physics estimation.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles 3D scene generation and robot simulation for robotics.
nodes.niche_reason: Agentic scene generation for robot simulation is specialised.

nodes.title: Improved Dimension Dependence for Bandit Convex Optimization with Gradient Variation
nodes.tldr: Improves dimension dependence of gradient-variation regret bounds for bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback, and extends them to dynamic and universal regret.
nodes.problem: Gradient-variation regret bounds are under-explored with bandit feedback, and existing ones have poor dimension dependence.
nodes.approach: Refined analysis of non-consecutive gradient variation under two-point bandit feedback.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Gradient-variation bandit regret theory is a specialised online learning niche

nodes.title: Diffract: Spectral View of LLM Domain Adaptation
nodes.tldr: SVD analysis of continual pre-training shows singular values stay invariant while singular vectors change; head-level importance enables rewinding heads, and checkpoints exhibit linear domain connectivity.
nodes.problem: How continual pre-training adapts LLM weights to specialized domains is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Spectral analysis of weights, head importance criterion with selective rewinding, and linear interpolation between domain checkpoints; open-source toolkit.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Spectral weight analysis of CPT is specialised but related work exists.

nodes.title: Procedural Pretraining: Warming Up Language Models with Abstract Data
nodes.tldr: Front-loading a small amount of procedurally generated abstract data, such as Dyck sequences, improves LLM pretraining and reduces the data needed.
nodes.problem: Standard web-corpus pretraining may not efficiently build algorithmic skills like context recall and structure.
nodes.approach: Warm up on procedural data from formal languages and simple algorithms before natural-language pretraining.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Procedural pretraining is emerging but still specialised

nodes.title: Symmetries in language statistics shape the geometry of model representations
nodes.tldr: Shows translation symmetry in word co-occurrence statistics explains why LLM representations encode circles and manifolds, robust to perturbation.
nodes.problem: Why LLM representations form simple geometric structures such as months on a circle is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Latent-variable model of co-occurrence statistics; proof for high-dimensional embeddings, validated on LLMs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: theory of embedding geometry is specialised but active

nodes.title: Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games
nodes.tldr: Studies learning in structured Stackelberg games with contextual follower types, introducing a new complexity measure that gives optimal online regret.
nodes.problem: A leader must learn a utility-maximizing policy against an unknown follower type from context.
nodes.approach: Stackelberg-Littlestone dimension characterizing instance-optimal regret, plus two dimensions for sample complexity.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: new game-theoretic learning complexity measure, few similar papers

nodes.title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
nodes.tldr: Proves conditional projective composition is equivalent to local conditional scores in diffusion models, explaining and causally enabling length generalization on CLEVR.
nodes.problem: Mechanisms behind compositional generalization in conditional diffusion models are unclear.
nodes.approach: Theory linking compositional structure to score locality, validated with CLEVR experiments and causal interventions.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic theory of diffusion compositionality is a rare angle.

nodes.title: Automated Formal Proofs of Combinatorial Identities via Wilf–Zeilberger Guidance and LLMs
nodes.tldr: Turns Wilf-Zeilberger proof plans into Lean 4 proof sketches that an LLM prover completes, reaching 34% on classical combinatorial identities.
nodes.problem: LLM provers struggle with long-horizon proof planning for combinatorial identities; unconstrained search explodes.
nodes.approach: Neuro-symbolic pipeline: symbolic WZ plans become Lean sketches, discharged by a dedicated, bootstrapped prover.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Formal proof of combinatorial identities with symbolic WZ guidance is rare.

nodes.title: TimeRewarder: Learning Dense Reward from Passive Videos via Frame-wise Temporal Distance
nodes.tldr: Learns dense progress-based rewards from passive robot and human videos by modeling frame-wise temporal distances, enabling near-perfect RL success on Meta-World tasks.
nodes.problem: Dense reward design for robotic RL is manual and does not scale.
nodes.approach: Train a temporal-distance model on frame pairs from passive videos and use progress estimates as proxy rewards.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Video-derived reward learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Mind Your Margin and Boundary: Are Your Distilled Datasets Truly Robust?
nodes.tldr: C^2R improves robustness of distilled datasets with a margin-based perturbation-score curriculum and class-balanced contrastive robustness loss.
nodes.problem: Robust dataset distillation has poor accuracy-robustness trade-off
nodes.approach: Attack-aware curriculum on small-margin adversaries plus contrastive loss widening class boundaries
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Robust dataset distillation is a specialised subarea.

nodes.title: BrokenMath: A Benchmark for Sycophancy in Theorem Proving with LLMs
nodes.tldr: BrokenMath is a benchmark of perturbed advanced theorems testing whether LLMs sycophantically produce convincing proofs for false statements.
nodes.problem: Existing benchmarks fail to measure LLM sycophancy in natural-language theorem proving.
nodes.approach: Build false-statement variants from advanced competition problems, expert-reviewed, and evaluate LLM sycophancy and mitigations.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Sycophancy in proof generation is a specialised evaluation niche.

nodes.title: High-accuracy and dimension-free sampling with diffusions
nodes.tldr: A diffusion sampler using low-degree approximation and collocation achieves polylogarithmic dependence on 1/epsilon and no explicit ambient-dimension dependence, the first high-accuracy guarantee with score access.
nodes.problem: Diffusion sampling iteration complexity scales polynomially in dimension and inverse accuracy.
nodes.approach: New diffusion ODE solver combining low-degree polynomial approximation with the collocation method, with provable complexity.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion convergence theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: From Distribution to Geometry: Stable Graph Generalization via Invariant Barycenters
nodes.tldr: DIGL improves GNN out-of-distribution generalization by modeling invariant graph prototypes as optimal-transport distribution barycenters and learning invariant representations with theoretical justification.
nodes.problem: GNNs generalize poorly under distribution shift and invariance lacks principled quantification.
nodes.approach: Optimal transport barycenter of environment graph representations as invariant prototype with a unified objective.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Graph OOD with OT barycenters is specialised.

nodes.title: Learning to Execute Graph Algorithms Exactly with Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proves GNNs with MLP-ensemble update functions can exactly learn to execute graph algorithms like BFS and Bellman-Ford from few local examples, via NTK theory.
nodes.problem: Whether GNNs can provably learn to execute graph algorithms exactly.
nodes.approach: Train MLPs on local node instructions, use as GNN update, and prove exactness using NTK theory.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Provable exact algorithm learning is a rare theory direction.

nodes.title: On the Optimization Trajectory of DeepWalk Embeddings
nodes.tldr: Analyzes the gradient descent optimization trajectory of DeepWalk skip-gram negative sampling embeddings, with guarantees on stochastic block model graphs.
nodes.problem: Optimization trajectory and guarantees of DeepWalk embeddings from random initialization are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of gradient descent dynamics on DeepWalk with negative sampling for stochastic block models.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of classical node embedding dynamics is rare.

nodes.title: Lottery Prior: Randomized Neural Compression for Zero-Shot Inverse Problems
nodes.tldr: Solves zero-shot image restoration by compressing a degraded observation with a lightweight random-network prior, achieving state-of-the-art with fewer effective parameters.
nodes.problem: Recovering clean signals from single degraded observations without any external training data.
nodes.approach: Compression-based maximum-likelihood solver using random-network architectural priors and randomness-induced ensembles of implicit priors.
nodes.niche_reason: Compression-based inverse solving is specialised; random-network priors less common

nodes.title: Neural Feature Geometry Evolves as Discrete Ricci Flow
nodes.tldr: Feature geometry in feedforward networks evolves like discrete Ricci flow on approximate data-manifold graphs, linking class separability to community structure.
nodes.problem: The geometric transformations of data manifolds in deep networks are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Geometric graphs approximate the unobserved manifold; theory and experiments on over 20,000 trained networks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete Ricci flow analogy for neural feature geometry is unusual.

nodes.title: Rethinking LLM Ensembling from the Perspective of Mixture Models
nodes.tldr: Reinterprets LLM ensembling as a mixture model so one stochastically chosen model generates each token, matching ensemble sampling but running 1.78-2.68x faster.
nodes.problem: Conventional LLM ensembling needs a forward pass from every model per token, which is computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Sample one model per step according to mixture weights, equivalent to sampling from the ensemble distribution.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: LLM ensembling is established but less crowded than other inference work.

nodes.title: Incentivizing Truthfulness and Collaborative Fairness in Bayesian Learning
nodes.tldr: Mechanism for collaborative Bayesian learning that provably gives both collaborative fairness and truthful data submission at equilibrium, combining semivalues with a truthful valuation function.
nodes.problem: Data valuation methods let sources manipulate submitted data to inflate rewards.
nodes.approach: Semivalues (Shapley) combined with a truthful validation-based data valuation function and an added equilibrium condition.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Incentive-compatible data valuation for Bayesian models is rare.

nodes.title: Flow Sampling : Learning to Sample from Unnormalized Densities via Denoising Conditional Processes
nodes.tldr: Learns a diffusion-style sampler for unnormalized densities from an energy function alone, with a closed-form drift for Riemannian manifolds such as hyperspheres.
nodes.problem: Sampling unnormalized densities needs costly energy evaluations when data samples are unavailable.
nodes.approach: Regress a noise-conditioned denoising drift built from the energy, using interpolants to limit energy calls.
nodes.confidence_reason: Sampler versus generative model placement is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Data-free diffusion samplers on manifolds are a rare angle.

nodes.title: Simple Algorithms for Bad Triangle Transversals with Applications to Correlation Clustering
nodes.tldr: Gives 2-approximations for bad triangle transversal, proves NP-hard to approximate better than 2137/2136, and on complete graphs bounds its optimum within 3/2 of correlation clustering.
nodes.problem: Finding the fewest edge deletions that remove all bad triangles from a signed graph is hard to approximate.
nodes.approach: Simple pivot-style 2-approximation procedures; a pivot transforms transversals into clusters.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Combinatorial approximation theory; no clean ML topic fits well.
nodes.niche_reason: Bad triangle transversals on signed graphs are a rare theoretical topic.

nodes.title: BFTS: Thompson Sampling with Bayesian Additive Regression Trees
nodes.tldr: Thompson sampling for contextual bandits with arm-wise Bayesian additive regression trees, with a Bayesian regret bound and strong OpenML and mobile health results.
nodes.problem: Contextual bandits need flexible nonlinear reward models with calibrated uncertainty for exploration.
nodes.approach: Arm-wise BART posterior draws via MCMC used for Thompson sampling, with information-theoretic regret bound.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Tree-based Bayesian bandits are specialised.

nodes.title: The Double-Edged Nature of the Rashomon Set for Trustworthy Machine Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows that diversity within Rashomon sets gives reactive robustness against attacks but also increases information leakage, creating a robustness-privacy trade-off.
nodes.problem: Real pipelines yield many near-optimal models, but their effect on trustworthiness is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Theoretical and empirical analysis of Rashomon sets, comparing sparse interpretable models with diverse near-optimal sets.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans robustness, privacy and interpretability; primary choice is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Rashomon-set trustworthiness is a rare, unusual angle

nodes.title: Deep Flow Networks
nodes.tldr: Introduces Deep Flow Networks, universal approximators of discrete functions that generalize minimum-cost flow value functions and optimize faster than baselines.
nodes.problem: Learning discrete functions with efficient optimization lacks expressive, structured approximators.
nodes.approach: Neural networks built on M-convex min-cost flow value functions, with a practical implementation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Discrete function approximator; theory and method span two topics
nodes.niche_reason: Flow-value-function approximators are an unusual architecture direction

nodes.title: Training Diffusion Language Models for Black-Box Optimization
nodes.tldr: Adapts diffusion language models to offline black-box design optimization using a unified prompt corpus, SFT, and RL on label improvements.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive LLMs struggle with bidirectional dependencies in offline black-box design problems.
nodes.approach: Delimiter-tagged prompt corpus, masked-response SFT, then RL with label-improvement rewards.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion-LLM and black-box optimization framing both central; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion LLMs applied to black-box design is rare.

nodes.title: FedPissa: Towards Federated Personalized Adaptation of Foundation Models via LoRA Subspace Mapping
nodes.tldr: Replaces dual-LoRA personalized federated fine-tuning with a single LoRA using selective aggregation and decorrelated subspace projection, cutting communication and computation cost.
nodes.problem: Federated LoRA personalisation suffers from data heterogeneity, and dual-LoRA designs add overhead and redundancy.
nodes.approach: Selectively aggregates LoRA components by aggregation dynamics and projects updates into a decorrelated subspace.
nodes.niche_reason: Personalised federated PEFT is established but specialised

nodes.title: NeuronCtrl: Geometry-Aware Safe Closed-Loop Generative Control for Neuronal Microenvironment Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Safe closed-loop generative control of 3D neuronal field dynamics, combining a latent-field observer, morphology-aware neural operator, flow-matching action proposals and barrier safety filters.
nodes.problem: Controlling neuronal field dynamics on irregular 3D shapes with unknown biophysics and hard safety constraints.
nodes.approach: Operator-level observer, neural-operator dynamics, flow-matching action generation and a distilled one-step policy.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans control, neural operators and neuroscience.
nodes.niche_reason: Closed-loop control of neuronal fields is very rare in ML.

nodes.title: Learning-to-Optimize via Deep Unfolded Flows
nodes.tldr: Learned flow-based optimizer that evolves a population of candidates with a velocity field, trained only on objective values and generalizing to higher dimensions.
nodes.problem: Non-convex optimization needs robust, fast solvers, while learned optimizers often require known solutions.
nodes.approach: Velocity-field iterations trained by flow matching to improved samples, then end-to-end fine-tuned on objective values.
nodes.confidence_reason: Learned optimizer built on flow models; straddles two areas
nodes.niche_reason: Flow-based learned optimizers are a rare direction

nodes.title: Do LLMs Signal When They’re Right? Evidence from Neuron Agreement
nodes.tldr: Neuron Agreement Decoding selects best-of-N LLM answers using activation sparsity and cross-sample neuron agreement, enabling early correctness prediction and large token savings.
nodes.problem: External output signals for ensembling LLM samples are poorly calibrated and need comparable text outputs.
nodes.approach: Unsupervised selection using internal neuron activation sparsity and agreement across samples; early stopping.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Internal-activation-based answer selection is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: Incremental BPE Tokenization
nodes.tldr: Proposes incremental BPE tokenization with worst-case O(log^2 t) per byte, a drop-in replacement up to 3x faster than Hugging Face.
nodes.problem: Streaming LLM pipelines need BPE tokenization that updates incrementally with latency guarantees.
nodes.approach: Maintains BPE results for every prefix incrementally, plus an eager algorithm that streams tokens early.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Incremental BPE with worst-case guarantees is a rare angle

nodes.title: Distributional Inverse Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Offline inverse RL that learns reward distributions by minimizing first-order stochastic dominance violations, yielding risk-aware policies for imitation of expert behavior.
nodes.problem: Conventional IRL recovers deterministic rewards or matches only expected returns.
nodes.approach: Distributional IRL with FSD-violation minimization and distortion risk measures in policy learning.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans inverse RL, distributional RL and imitation; primary is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Distributional IRL with stochastic dominance is rare.

nodes.title: daVinci-Dev: Agent-native Mid-training for Software Engineering
nodes.tldr: daVinci-Dev uses agent-native mid-training data of contextual and environmental trajectories to reach state-of-the-art open SWE-Bench Verified results with fewer mid-training tokens.
nodes.problem: Static pre-training mismatches dynamic agentic deployment, and post-training alone does not close the gap.
nodes.approach: Mid-train on contextually-native and environmentally-native agent trajectories from real tool calls and test executions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: SWE agents are crowded; mid-training angle is somewhat less common.

nodes.title: Agent0-VL: Exploring Self-Evolving Agent for Tool-Integrated Vision-Language Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Agent0-VL is a self-evolving vision-language model that acts as both solver and tool-grounded verifier, improving with no human labels or external reward models.
nodes.problem: Self-rewarding LVLMs with text-only self-evaluation hallucinate when verifying visual reasoning steps.
nodes.approach: Tool-integrated reasoning for solving and verification, aligned with reinforcement learning in a self-evolving cycle.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: self-rewarding multimodal reasoning is a crowded direction

nodes.title: T$^2$PO: Uncertainty-Guided Exploration Control for Stable Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: T2PO controls exploration in multi-turn agentic RL by monitoring token uncertainty to trigger thinking and resampling low-progress turns, stabilizing LLM agent training.
nodes.problem: Multi-turn agentic RL is unstable because policies waste exploration on low-information actions.
nodes.approach: Token-level uncertainty-triggered thinking intervention plus turn-level resampling of negligible-progress interactions.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Agentic RL for LLMs is a crowded, fast-moving area.

nodes.title: A Dirac-Frenkel-Onsager Principle: Instantaneous Residual Minimization with Gauge Momentum for Nonlinear Parametrizations of PDE Solutions
nodes.tldr: Adds a momentum-like gauge variable along nullspace directions of Dirac-Frenkel residual minimization, improving conditioning while keeping instantaneous residual minimization.
nodes.problem: Ill-conditioned nonlinear parametrizations of PDE solutions make parameter dynamics non-unique.
nodes.approach: Onsager minimum-dissipation momentum injected only into nullspace directions of the residual.
nodes.confidence_reason: PDE parametrization vs. optimizer design; close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Very rare: gauge momentum for Dirac-Frenkel PDE dynamics.

nodes.title: Is Your LLM Overcharging You? Tokenization, Transparency, and Incentives
nodes.tldr: Shows pay-per-token LLM pricing lets providers misreport token counts undetectably, gives an overcharging heuristic, and proves incentive-compatible pricing must be linear in character count.
nodes.problem: Pay-per-token pricing incentivizes providers to misreport token counts, and users cannot verify them.
nodes.approach: Game-theoretic analysis, a heuristic overcharging algorithm, and a character-linear incentive-compatible pricing scheme.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans mechanism design and LLM tokenization; topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Economics of LLM token billing is a very unusual topic.

nodes.title: Foundations of Equivariant Deep Learning: Unifying Graph and Sheaf Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Introduces order-equivariant and category-equivariant neural networks generalizing graph and sheaf networks, characterizing equivariant linear maps and proving universal approximation theorems.
nodes.problem: Geometric deep learning lacks a unified theory covering richer symmetry structures beyond graphs, including sheaf networks.
nodes.approach: Equivariant bundles over face posets and categories, with linear map characterization, layer construction, and universal approximation proofs.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Category-theoretic equivariant networks are a very rare niche.

nodes.title: ReQAT: Achieving Full-Precision Reasoning Accuracy with 4-bit Floating-Point Quantization-Aware Training
nodes.tldr: Quantization-aware training that lets fully 4-bit reasoning models match BF16 accuracy by focusing on low-entropy tokens.
nodes.problem: W4A4KV4 quantization severely degrades long chain-of-thought reasoning, which existing PTQ and QAT fail to recover.
nodes.approach: Trace-aligned QAT, selective entropy minimization, and quantization-friendly RoPE-consistent KV initialization.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.confidence_reason: Quantization vs reasoning focus overlap; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: low-bit reasoning-model quantization.

nodes.title: Chebyshev Policies and the Mountain Car Problem: Reinforcement Learning for Low-Dimensional Control Tasks
nodes.tldr: Analytically solves the Mountain Car problem, finds RL agents far from optimal, and introduces compact Chebyshev policies that beat neural nets with 277x fewer parameters.
nodes.problem: Understanding optimal control of a canonical RL benchmark and finding efficient policies for low-dimensional control.
nodes.approach: Derive the analytic optimal control, then use Chebyshev polynomial policies as drop-in replacements for neural networks.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Analytic solution and polynomial policies for classic control is very rare.

nodes.title: Prototype-guided Bilateral Alignment Multimodal Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: Federated multimodal learning that aligns heterogeneous client feature spaces with contrastive Gromov-Wasserstein alignment and aggregates entropy-weighted logit prototypes.
nodes.problem: Federated multimodal learning fails with heterogeneous client architectures and imbalanced modalities
nodes.approach: Feature-level Gromov-Wasserstein plus contrastive projection alignment and decision-level entropy-weighted prototype aggregation
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal federated learning is a specialised niche

nodes.title: GFD-EMVC: Evolutionary Multi-View Classification with Label Noise via Gradient and Feature Dual-Perception
nodes.tldr: Addresses label noise in evolutionary multi-view classification by detecting noisy samples via gradient outliers and correcting labels with feature prototypes.
nodes.problem: Label noise distorts fitness landscapes and causes fitness evaluation bias in evolutionary multi-view classification.
nodes.approach: Detect-then-calibrate purification: gradient-space outlier detection and prototype-based label correction.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Evolutionary multi-view classification is unusual; label-noise purification could also fit other topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Evolutionary multi-view learning with label noise is very rare.

nodes.title: A Constrained Optimization Perspective of Unrolled Transformers
nodes.tldr: Trains transformers to act like descent algorithms by enforcing layerwise loss-descent constraints via primal-dual training, improving robustness and out-of-distribution generalization.
nodes.problem: Standard ERM does not make transformer layers behave like monotone optimization descent steps.
nodes.approach: Layerwise descent constraints trained with a primal-dual scheme in place of empirical risk minimization.
nodes.niche_reason: Constrained training of unrolled transformers is specialised but emerging.

nodes.title: Equivalence of Context and Parameter Updates in Modern Transformer Blocks
nodes.tldr: Proves a context's effect on a Gemma-style LLM block equals rank-1 patches to MLP weights, generalizing to multi-layer and MoE models.
nodes.problem: Understanding how context changes transformer behavior is established only for vanilla transformers, not modern LLM architectures.
nodes.approach: Analytic construction of implicit rank-1 MLP weight patches, plus input and output controllability framework for general blocks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.confidence_reason: mechanistic theory of ICL spans transformer architecture and ICL topics
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit weight-patch theory of context for modern LLM blocks is rare

nodes.title: MACKO: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication for low sparsity
nodes.tldr: MACKO is a GPU sparse format and kernel that speeds up low-sparsity unstructured SpMV, making 50%-pruned LLM inference faster and smaller.
nodes.problem: Existing SpMV methods perform poorly at the low, unstructured sparsity typical of pruned LLMs.
nodes.approach: Storage-reduced GPU-friendly format co-designed with a kernel targeting memory bandwidth limits.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse LLM inference kernels are a common, active systems topic

nodes.title: Conservation Laws for Modern Neural Architectures
nodes.tldr: Characterises conservation laws in gradient flow for modern architectures including GELU/SwiGLU feedforward nets, rotary attention and mixture-of-experts, validated by experiments.
nodes.problem: Implicit bias via conservation laws is understood for linear and ReLU networks, but not modern architectures.
nodes.approach: Unified framework deriving gradient-flow invariants for activation, attention-encoding and gating designs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Conservation-law analysis of modern architectures is specialised

nodes.title: Fast Spectrally Sparse Signal Reconstruction via Jacobi-Preconditioned Gradient Descent
nodes.tldr: Preconditions gradient descent for spectrally sparse signal recovery via Hankel matrix completion, achieving condition-number-independent linear convergence.
nodes.problem: Spectrally sparse signal reconstruction is slow when the problem is ill-conditioned
nodes.approach: Jacobi-preconditioned factored gradient descent with a generator linking factor iterates to matrix-space manifold analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised signal reconstruction via Hankel low-rank completion

nodes.title: Monitoring Monitorability
nodes.tldr: Introduces evaluation archetypes, a metric and suite for chain-of-thought monitorability, showing CoT monitors beat action-only ones and studying scaling with model size and test-time compute.
nodes.problem: Whether chain-of-thought monitoring remains reliable for detecting agent misbehavior across training and scaling.
nodes.approach: Three evaluation archetypes, new monitorability metric, broad suite, and scaling studies of agent and monitor compute.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: CoT monitoring is a growing but specialised safety subtopic.

nodes.title: How much can language models memorize?
nodes.tldr: Separates unintended memorization from generalization to measure language model capacity at about 3.6 bits per parameter, with scaling laws for membership inference.
nodes.problem: Prior work cannot disentangle memorization from generalization when measuring LM capacity.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic memorization measure; train hundreds of transformers from 500K to 1.5B parameters.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Memorization capacity measurement is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Distribution Transformers: Fast Approximate Bayesian Inference With On-The-Fly Prior Adaptation
nodes.tldr: Distribution Transformer maps a Gaussian-mixture prior to a GMM posterior with self- and cross-attention, doing amortized Bayesian inference in milliseconds with on-the-fly prior changes.
nodes.problem: Approximate Bayesian inference is slow or needs retraining when priors change, hindering sequential inference.
nodes.approach: Transformer over GMM components attending to each other and to data, trained to map priors to posteriors.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Learning prior-to-posterior maps over GMMs is rare.

nodes.title: Accelerating Q-learning through Efficient Value-Sharing across Actions
nodes.tldr: Adds a parameter-free mean-expansion layer to Q-networks, sharing values across actions within a state to speed up learning and reduce overestimation.
nodes.problem: Action-value learning is slow and updates each state-action pair independently, ignoring shared structure.
nodes.approach: Reparameterizes action values as lower-norm representations that share value across actions in a state.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised architectural value-sharing for Q-network action values.

nodes.title: UniMapping: Unified SLAM Framework for Map-Centric Embodied Perception
nodes.tldr: UniMapping is a SLAM framework building a persistent neural-descriptor map from multimodal inputs, using a spatial-aware deformable transformer and spatial fusion to improve downstream perception.
nodes.problem: SLAM maps lack scale consistency and geometric fidelity needed for reliable downstream perception.
nodes.approach: Spatial-Aware Deformable Transformer for scale-invariant features plus Spatial Fusion decoupling aggregation from temporal sequences, building a neural descriptor map.
nodes.niche_reason: SLAM is established; neural descriptor maps for perception are specialised.

nodes.title: SurvDiff: A Diffusion Model for Generating Synthetic Data in Survival Analysis
nodes.tldr: SurvDiff is an end-to-end diffusion model generating synthetic survival data, jointly modeling mixed-type covariates, event times and censoring with a survival-tailored loss.
nodes.problem: Generating synthetic survival data requires faithfully reproducing event-time distributions and censoring mechanisms.
nodes.approach: Diffusion model jointly generating covariates, event times and censoring with a survival-structure loss.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Survival-analysis synthetic data with diffusion is a rare combination.

nodes.title: Effective Model Pruning : Measuring the Redundancy of Model Components
nodes.tldr: Derives an adaptive pruning ratio from the effective sample size of importance scores, with a provable bound on the loss change after pruning.
nodes.problem: How many scored model components can be discarded without sacrificing performance.
nodes.approach: Maps importance scores to an effective sample size N_eff and discards the N minus N_eff lowest-scoring components.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Pruning is crowded; effective-sample-size criterion is less common.

nodes.title: FlashSketch: Sketch-Kernel Co-Design for Fast Sparse Sketching on GPUs
nodes.tldr: Co-designs a block-permuted sparse sketch and a GPU CUDA kernel, achieving about 1.7x geomean speedup over prior GPU sketches.
nodes.problem: Random sparsity in sparse sketches causes irregular memory access that underuses GPU bandwidth.
nodes.approach: Structured block-permuted sparse sketch family with a tunable robustness-speed trade-off, plus an optimized kernel.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.niche_reason: sketch-kernel co-design for GPUs is rare

nodes.title: Certifying Capabilities from Finite Tests: When Is It Possible?
nodes.tldr: Formalizes capability evaluation as inference over task families: chi-squared radius governs sample complexity with matching lower bounds, with impossibility for worst-case capabilities.
nodes.problem: Unclear when finite test sets can certify broad model capabilities over a full task family.
nodes.approach: Minimax theory of evaluation: chi-squared radius sample complexity for stochastic settings, impossibility results for worst-case.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Rigorous theory of model evaluation is rare.

nodes.title: Learning Credal Ensembles via Distributionally Robust Optimization
nodes.tldr: Defines epistemic uncertainty by disagreement among models trained under relaxed i.i.d. assumptions via distributionally robust optimization, improving OOD detection and selective classification.
nodes.problem: Credal ensembles treat epistemic uncertainty as seed randomness, missing train-test distribution shift.
nodes.approach: Ensemble of DRO-trained models spanning plausible train-test distribution shifts.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Credal ensembles with DRO are a specialised uncertainty niche

nodes.title: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
nodes.tldr: Introduces a user-intent-driven online benchmark for mobile GUI agents with capability-level annotations, revealing large gaps and brittleness under environment variations.
nodes.problem: Existing mobile GUI agent benchmarks are app-centric and miss real-world usage diversity and instability.
nodes.approach: Realistic user-intent task design plus capability-oriented diagnostic annotation.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: GUI agent benchmarks are a busy area

nodes.title: Information dynamics and Memory in Neural Networks through Fisher Information Diffusion
nodes.tldr: Derives a Fisher information diffusion operator via mean-field theory explaining recurrent-network memory, yielding initialization rules that improve copy-task and sequential MNIST.
nodes.problem: How recurrent networks encode information about past inputs in dynamics and how to initialize them for memory.
nodes.approach: Dynamic mean-field theory with a Fisher information diffusion operator linking connectivity to information propagation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field information dynamics of RNNs is a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: A Kinetic Energy Perspective of Flow Matching
nodes.tldr: Defines Kinetic Path Energy, a per-sample trajectory effort measure for flow models, and a training-free inference schedule that reduces memorization and improves generation.
nodes.problem: Flow model samples vary in quality, and high-energy trajectories collapse into memorized training examples
nodes.approach: Physics-inspired action-like energy along ODE trajectories, with early boost and late soft-landing inference shaping
secondary_topics: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-inspired flow matching diagnostics are unusual

nodes.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo without Evaluating the Target: an Auxiliary Variable Approach
nodes.tldr: Unifies MCMC algorithms that avoid evaluating the target density under an auxiliary-variable framework, yielding new gradient-guided samplers for tall datasets and doubly-intractable distributions.
nodes.problem: Evaluating the unnormalized target is costly or infeasible for tall-data posteriors and doubly-intractable distributions.
nodes.approach: Auxiliary variables in both proposal and accept-reject steps, with estimated gradients guiding proposals.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Target-free MCMC for doubly-intractable settings is a specialised statistics niche.

nodes.title: Tilt Matching for Scalable Sampling and Fine-Tuning
nodes.tldr: Samples unnormalized densities and fine-tunes flow models by matching a reward-tilted velocity field, without reward gradients or backpropagation through trajectories.
nodes.problem: Existing methods for reward-tilted sampling and fine-tuning often need reward gradients or costly backpropagation.
nodes.approach: Velocity update from reward-interpolant covariance, a lower-variance objective than flow matching.
nodes.confidence_reason: Sampling and fine-tuning are both plausible primary contributions.
nodes.niche_reason: Reward-tilted flow sampling is specialised but emerging.

nodes.title: On the Power of Source Screening for Learning Shared Feature Extractors
nodes.tldr: Shows that training shared representations on a carefully screened subset of sources, with much data discarded, can achieve minimax-optimal subspace estimation.
nodes.problem: Including all data sources in shared representation learning can hinder subspace estimation.
nodes.approach: Linear subspace theory plus algorithms and heuristics that select an informative subpopulation of sources.
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory-heavy; representation versus transfer learning is ambiguous
nodes.niche_reason: Source selection for shared subspace learning is a specialised topic

nodes.title: BlitzRank: Principled Zero-shot Ranking Agents with Tournament Graphs
nodes.tldr: Selects top-m items from k-wise comparisons by aggregating induced pairwise preferences into a tournament graph, cutting LLM reranking tokens.
nodes.problem: Existing top-m methods discard comparison information or cost too much
nodes.approach: Tournament graph with transitive closure and greedy query scheduling, collapsing cycles into tiered rankings
nodes.confidence_reason: Ranking straddles LLM reranking and algorithmic theory; judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Top-m k-wise ranking with tournament graphs is uncommon

nodes.title: When to Trust the Cheap Check: Weak and Strong Verification for Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Decides when to accept LLM reasoning on cheap weak checks versus costly strong verification, with an online algorithm that controls error rates.
nodes.problem: Cheap self-consistency checks are noisy, while strong human verification is expensive.
nodes.approach: Two-threshold weak-strong verification policies with an assumption-free online error-controlling algorithm.
nodes.confidence_reason: Verification policy spans reasoning, calibration and sequential decisions.
nodes.niche_reason: Verification policies for reasoning are specialised.

nodes.title: Strategic Navigation or Stochastic Search? How Agents and Humans Reason Over Document Collections
nodes.tldr: MADQA benchmark of 2,250 questions over 800 PDFs tests whether multimodal agents navigate documents strategically; best agents match humans but rely on brute-force search.
nodes.problem: Do document agents reason strategically or just stochastically search, and how efficient are they versus humans?
nodes.approach: Human-authored benchmark designed with Classical Test Theory and an accuracy-effort evaluation protocol.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Document-agent benchmark with psychometric design is specialised.

nodes.title: Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking? Rewarding Perception for Multimodal Reasoning
nodes.tldr: MoCA trains a VLM with reinforcement learning, rewarding perception fidelity separately from reasoning so credit goes to bad seeing or bad thinking.
nodes.problem: VLM failures are ambiguous: perception errors and reasoning errors get the same credit.
nodes.approach: Interleaved perception and reasoning steps with blindfolded-reasoning verification and structured verbal rewards.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.confidence_reason: Multimodal RL sits between VLM and RL-for-reasoning topics.
nodes.niche_reason: RL for multimodal reasoning is a fast-growing, fairly common area.

nodes.title: PACT: Self-Evolving Physical Safety Alignment for Diffusion Policies in Embodied Manipulation
nodes.tldr: Post-training method that projects pretrained diffusion policies onto constraint-feasible regions without demonstrations or rewards, reducing safety violations.
nodes.problem: Diffusion policies often violate strict physical constraints required for safe robot deployment.
nodes.approach: Distills constraint gradients into the diffusion model via reverse-KL with a curriculum that progressively tightens constraints.
nodes.confidence_reason: Safety-constraint framing could fit robot control or safety topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Post-hoc physical safety alignment of diffusion policies is an emerging niche

nodes.title: Manifold-Optimal Guidance: A Unified Riemannian Control View of Diffusion Guidance
nodes.tldr: Manifold-Optimal Guidance reframes diffusion guidance as Riemannian optimal control, correcting off-manifold drift without retraining, with automatic guidance-scale scheduling.
nodes.problem: High classifier-free guidance scales cause oversaturation and artifacts because Euclidean extrapolation leaves the data manifold.
nodes.approach: Closed-form geometry-aware Riemannian update plus Auto-MOG energy-balancing schedule for guidance strength.
nodes.niche_reason: Geometric, control-theoretic guidance is a specialised reframing of CFG.

nodes.title: Real-Time Visual Attribution Streaming in Thinking Model
nodes.tldr: Learns to predict causal visual-region effects from attention features, giving faithful visual attribution streamed during multimodal reasoning.
nodes.problem: Verifying which image regions ground a thinking model's reasoning is costly or causally unreliable.
nodes.approach: Amortized estimator that predicts causal effects of semantic regions directly from attention features.
nodes.confidence_reason: Interpretability versus multimodal reasoning is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Interpretability is established; streaming attribution for reasoning traces is newer.

nodes.title: VideoKR: Towards Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Understanding
nodes.tldr: VideoKR is a 315K-example corpus over 145K expert-domain videos for knowledge- and reasoning-intensive video understanding, with an expert-annotated benchmark and SFT-then-GRPO training gains.
nodes.problem: Lack of training data for knowledge-intensive video reasoning.
nodes.approach: Human-in-the-loop skill-oriented pipeline to generate video reasoning examples with CoT rationales.
nodes.niche_reason: Video reasoning datasets for MLLMs are a crowded area.

nodes.title: POET-X: Memory-efficient LLM Training by Scaling Orthogonal Transformation
nodes.tldr: Makes orthogonal equivalence training of LLM weights cheaper in memory and compute, enabling billion-parameter pretraining on one H100 GPU.
nodes.problem: Original POET's orthogonal transformations consume too much memory and compute for LLM training.
nodes.approach: Scaled orthogonal equivalence transformations with reduced matrix-multiplication cost, preserving spectrum.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient LLM training is crowded; orthogonal reparameterization is specialised.

nodes.title: WaterSIC: Information-Theoretically (Near) Optimal \\Linear Layer Quantization
nodes.tldr: Proposes WaterSIC, a linear-layer quantizer that allocates per-column bit rates via waterfilling, within 0.255 bits of the information-theoretic limit and SOTA for LLMs.
nodes.problem: Converting dense linear layers to low precision; GPTQ can have arbitrarily large gap to the info-theoretic limit.
nodes.approach: Column-wise rate allocation mimicking classical waterfilling, applied to Llama and Qwen quantization.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Information-theoretic quantization is specialised but active

nodes.title: Symmetry Reveals Layerwise Dynamics: How Transformers Perform In-Context Classification
nodes.tldr: Makes in-context classification in transformers identifiable via permutation equivariance, revealing an explicit depth-indexed update rule that amplifies class separation.
nodes.problem: The inference-time algorithm behind transformer in-context classification remains opaque.
nodes.approach: Enforce feature and label permutation equivariance per layer to extract an interpretable recursion.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.confidence_reason: Synthetic linear classification, not language; interpretability vs ICL topic overlap.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic identification of in-context algorithms is rare

nodes.title: Minimax Optimal Strategy for Delayed Observations in Online Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Gives a UCB-with-augmentation algorithm for RL with randomly delayed state observations, proving a regret bound of H sqrt(D_max SAK) with a matching lower bound.
nodes.problem: Regret-optimal learning when the agent observes states after random delays.
nodes.approach: State augmentation combined with upper confidence bound exploration; general analysis for MDPs with known plus structured unknown dynamics.
nodes.niche_reason: Delayed-feedback RL theory is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Provable Bounds for the Learnability of Sample-Compressible Families from Noisy Samples
nodes.tldr: Shows sample-compressible distribution families stay PAC-learnable from noisy samples with additive independent noise, giving sample complexity bounds in l2 and total variation.
nodes.problem: Whether sample-compressible distribution families remain learnable when samples are perturbed by noise.
nodes.approach: Derive minimax-necessary and sufficient conditions and sample complexity bounds for noisy sample compression.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Distribution learning via sample compression is a narrow theory area.

nodes.title: End-to-End Autoregressive Image Generation with 1D Semantic Tokenizer
nodes.tldr: Jointly trains a visual tokenizer and autoregressive generator end-to-end so generation loss supervises tokenization, reaching FID 1.48 on ImageNet.
nodes.problem: Two-stage tokenizer and generator training leaves the tokenizer unaware of generation quality.
nodes.approach: End-to-end joint optimization of reconstruction and generation over a 1D semantic tokenizer using vision foundation models.
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive image generation with learned tokenizers is a common direction

nodes.title: Scaling Law for Quantization-Aware Training
nodes.tldr: Proposes a scaling law for 4-bit quantization-aware training, showing error rises with training tokens and coarser groups, and that FC2 activation outliers dominate.
nodes.problem: Quantization-aware training scaling at W4A4 precision is poorly understood; existing laws ignore tokens and granularity.
nodes.approach: Unified scaling law modeling quantization error by model size, tokens, and group size, split into weight and activation parts.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Scaling-law and quantization topics overlap; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Scaling laws are crowded; quantization-aware W4A4 scaling is more specific.

nodes.title: Correcting Split Selection in Online Decision Trees via Anytime-Valid Inference
nodes.tldr: Fixes invalid Hoeffding tree split decisions via anytime-valid inference, controlling false splits on non-stationary streams and giving smaller, better trees.
nodes.problem: Hoeffding tree split tests use fixed-sample bounds with data-dependent stopping, invalidating guarantees.
nodes.approach: Anytime-valid sequential testing by betting and confidence sequences for split selection.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Streaming decision trees with sequential testing is rare.

nodes.title: Weak Diffusion Priors Can Still Achieve Strong Inverse-Problem Performance
nodes.tldr: Shows mismatched, low-fidelity diffusion priors work nearly as well as in-domain ones for inverse problems when measurements are informative, explained by Bayesian theory.
nodes.problem: When and why do inverse-problem solvers stay robust to weak or mismatched diffusion priors?
nodes.approach: Extensive experiments plus Bayesian posterior-concentration theory and local spatial-correlation analysis of image priors.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles diffusion inverse solvers, theory, and image restoration topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Established area, but focus on prior mismatch and theory is specialised.

nodes.title: Hista and Numca: Estimate State Value Effectively for Large Language Model Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: PPO critics collapse to group averages on a new benchmark; Numca and Hista, using numerical spans and hidden states, give better LLM value estimates.
nodes.problem: Accurate state value estimation for LLM reinforcement learning is underexplored; critics collapse to coarse baselines.
nodes.approach: SVEB benchmark; Numca uses numerical spans as milestones; Hista weights rollouts by hidden-state representation similarity.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Value estimation for LLM RL is less crowded than critic-free methods.

nodes.title: Dissecting Multimodal In-Context Learning: Modality Asymmetries and Circuit Dynamics in modern Transformers
nodes.tldr: Controlled study on small transformers shows RoPE can delay ICL circuits and that multimodal ICL emerges with little secondary-modality diversity via induction-style label copying.
nodes.problem: How transformers learn to associate information across modalities from in-context examples.
nodes.approach: Mechanistic analysis of small transformers on synthetic classification tasks with controlled data statistics.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic ICL studies are established; multimodal angle is more specialised.

nodes.title: Privacy-Aware Video Anomaly Detection through Orthogonal Subspace Projection
nodes.tldr: Introduces an Orthogonal Projection Layer, with a guided variant that suppresses facial attributes via weak supervision, enabling video anomaly detection that preserves privacy, plus a joint evaluation framework.
nodes.problem: Video anomaly detection systems ignore privacy leakage of sensitive facial information.
nodes.approach: Orthogonal subspace projection removing task-irrelevant and face-related variation using cosine alignment, without identity labels.
nodes.niche_reason: Privacy-aware video anomaly detection is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Overcoming PINNs Failure Modes In High Dimension With Low-Rank Fourier Sum
nodes.tldr: Represents PDE solutions as low-rank sums of separable Fourier series, enabling closed-form physics losses without collocation sampling noise, so PINNs stay stable in high dimensions.
nodes.problem: PINNs fail on oscillatory, multiscale, high-dimensional PDEs due to sampling error and noisy gradients.
nodes.approach: Low-rank separable Fourier sum ansatz with analytic evaluation of residual and variational losses.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised PINN work but a well-established subfield.

nodes.title: ReViT: Rotational-equivariant Vision Transformers for Neural PDE Solvers
nodes.tldr: ReViT builds exact C4 and octahedral rotation equivariance into a Swin-style vision transformer for neural PDE solvers by mapping fields to locally invariant canonical-basis representations.
nodes.problem: Standard transformers in physics foundation models do not respect rotational symmetry of physical fields.
nodes.approach: Locally invariant representations from physics-based canonical bases enabling standard self-attention with exact discrete equivariance.
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariant transformers for PDE solvers are a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Asymmetric Perturbation in Solving Bilinear Saddle-Point Optimization
nodes.tldr: Introduces asymmetric perturbation, perturbing only one player's payoff, to speed convergence of bilinear saddle-point optimization to equilibria.
nodes.problem: Symmetric perturbation needs decaying strength, slowing convergence in bilinear saddle-point problems.
nodes.approach: Perturb one player's payoff with constant strength and analyze convergence rates.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-in-games perturbation theory is a rare niche.

nodes.title: One Intervention per Component is Enough: Towards Identifiability in Linear Stochastic Dynamics from Steady State
nodes.tldr: Proves one intervention per strongly connected component suffices to identify OU process parameters from steady-state data, and gives a regularized estimator.
nodes.problem: Recovering linear stochastic dynamics from snapshot data, where trajectory-based estimators do not apply.
nodes.approach: Recursive SCC-ordered learning plus regularized least squares on steady-state moment equations.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data

nodes.title: On the Accuracy of Newton Step and Influence Function Data Attributions
nodes.tldr: Gives local-condition analysis of influence functions and one Newton step for data attribution, with matching bounds for logistic regression.
nodes.problem: Existing guarantees for influence functions need global strong convexity and give pessimistic bounds.
nodes.approach: Replaces global assumptions with strong convexity and smoothness only near the first Newton step.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Local-convexity analysis of data attribution is a narrow theory niche.

nodes.title: Causal Modeling of Selection in Evolution
nodes.tldr: Separates static from evolutionary selection in causal discovery and introduces a graphical model for evolutionary selection with a sound and complete identification procedure.
nodes.problem: Existing causal discovery methods conflate static and evolutionary selection, causing false discoveries.
nodes.approach: New graphical selection model for repeated fitness-driven generations, with identification across environments.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal modeling of evolutionary selection is a rare cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Don't Force the Fit: Bounded Log-Likelihood Loss for Enhanced Reasoning in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Proposes a parameter-free SFT loss that bounds gradient contributions from low-probability tokens, improving reasoning generalization across model scales.
nodes.problem: Token-level SFT forces fitting stylistic low-probability tokens that do not affect reasoning correctness
nodes.approach: Bounded log-likelihood loss that caps gradients from low-probability tokens
nodes.niche_reason: SFT loss variants are a crowded direction

nodes.title: Measuring Agents in Production
nodes.tldr: Interviews and a survey of 86 practitioners show production LLM agents use simple prompting, short step chains, and human evaluation; reliability is the top challenge.
nodes.problem: We lack understanding of what technical methods make LLM agent deployments in production successful.
nodes.approach: Empirical study via 20 in-depth interviews and a survey of 86 deployed-agent practitioners across 26 domains.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Empirical interview-based study of deployed agents is unusual for ML venues.

nodes.title: ADEPT: RL-Aligned Agentic Decoding of Emotion via Evidence Probing Tools — From Consensus Learning to Ambiguity-Driven Emotion Reasoning
nodes.tldr: ADEPT turns a speech LLM into an agent that probes semantic and acoustic evidence with tools, trained via GRPO to reason about ambiguous emotions.
nodes.problem: Speech LLM emotion judgments are text-biased and ungrounded, and discard minority emotion annotations as noise.
nodes.approach: Multi-turn tool-probing agent with an evidence trust gate, using ambiguity-driven reasoning over minority annotations.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Speech emotion maps to audio area; agentic framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Agentic tool-use applied to speech emotion is an unusual pairing.

nodes.title: Excited Pfaffians: Generalized Neural Wave Functions Across Structure and State
nodes.tldr: Excited Pfaffians is a neural wave function architecture with multi-state importance sampling that represents many excited states and potential energy surfaces in one network.
nodes.problem: Computing excited states with variational Monte Carlo costs grow with the number of states due to overlap estimation.
nodes.approach: Multi-State Importance Sampling reusing samples across states plus a Hartree-Fock-inspired Pfaffian architecture covering many states.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural quantum chemistry for excited states is a very narrow niche.

nodes.title: AlgoVeri: An Aligned Benchmark for Verified Code Generation on Classical Algorithms
nodes.tldr: AlgoVeri aligns 77 classical algorithms across Dafny, Verus, and Lean with identical contracts to benchmark LLM verified code generation, showing large cross-language gaps.
nodes.problem: Verified code generation results across languages and tools are not directly comparable.
nodes.approach: Identical functional contracts for classical algorithms in three verification languages.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Verified code generation across Dafny, Verus, and Lean is rare.

nodes.title: On the Origin of Neural Scaling Laws: from Random Graphs to Natural Language
nodes.tldr: Shows scaling laws emerge for transformers trained on graph random walks without power-law data, and how exponents evolve from bigrams to richer language models.
nodes.problem: Understanding the origin of neural scaling laws without assuming power-law data correlations.
nodes.approach: Train transformers on random walks on tunable graphs and simplified generative language models, measuring exponents.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Scaling-law origin studies are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Revenue Guarantees of No-Swap-Regret Dynamics in First Price Auctions
nodes.tldr: Proves revenue lower bounds for approximate correlated equilibria of discrete first price auctions, giving polynomial convergence rates for no-swap-regret bidders.
nodes.problem: Revenue guarantees when bidders use no-swap-regret learning in first price auctions.
nodes.approach: Bound revenue of epsilon-approximate correlated equilibria as a function of bid grid and epsilon.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Algorithmic game theory of auctions is a rare niche.

nodes.title: WestWorld: A Knowledge-Encoded Scalable Trajectory World Model for Diverse Robotic Systems
nodes.tldr: Trains a trajectory world model with system-aware mixture-of-experts and structural embeddings, enabling zero-shot prediction and model-based control across diverse robot morphologies.
nodes.problem: Trajectory world models struggle to scale across many distinct robot dynamics and ignore physical structure knowledge.
nodes.approach: System-embedding-routed mixture of experts for scalability, plus a structural embedding aligning trajectories with robot morphology.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-morphology robot world models are specialised but growing

nodes.title: Post-Training with Policy Gradients: Optimality and the Base Model Barrier
nodes.tldr: Proves policy gradient post-training with outcome rewards is limited by the base model's support; process rewards avoid this barrier.
nodes.problem: Sample complexity of post-training autoregressive models beyond the base model's likelihood support.
nodes.approach: Analyses policy gradient with outcome versus process rewards under margin conditions, via a likelihood-quantile measure.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical limits of policy-gradient post-training; specialised but established.

nodes.title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
nodes.tldr: Predicts attention sparsity online with chunk-level routing propagated to tokens, letting a frozen long-context LLM run on limited memory.
nodes.problem: Dense attention quadratic cost blocks long-context LLM inference under tight memory budgets.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical chunk-to-token importance routing that dynamically sparsifies attention with a frozen backbone.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse attention for long-context LLMs is a common direction.

nodes.title: Exact Unlearning in Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Formulates exact unlearning for RL and gives a TV-stable algorithm whose unlearning costs a fraction of retraining, with near-minimax-optimal regret for tabular MDPs.
nodes.problem: Removing a user's data from an online RL learner without retraining from scratch.
nodes.approach: Rho-TV-stable tabular MDP algorithm with an exact unlearning procedure and matching lower bound.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Exact unlearning for reinforcement learning is a rare theoretical topic.

nodes.title: On the Limits of LLM Adaptability: Impact of Model-Internalized Priors on Annotation Task Performance
nodes.tldr: Shows zero-shot LLM annotation errors resist prompt correction, and that familiarity with task definitions, not memorization, predicts performance.
nodes.problem: Whether zero-shot LLM annotators can be corrected by prompting when internal priors conflict with definitions.
nodes.approach: Measure definition-specific familiarity and test prompt correction on toxicity detection across datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.confidence_reason: Prompting versus interpretability: memorization metrics blur the topic
nodes.niche_reason: LLM annotation reliability studies are increasingly common

nodes.title: Dynamic Programming for Epistemic Uncertainty in Markov Decision Processes
nodes.tldr: Proposes ambiguity-averse MDPs that apply a risk measure to random returns, and characterizes which risk measures allow dynamic programming.
