nodes.problem: MDPs with uncertain transition probabilities lack a unified framework that supports dynamic programming.
nodes.approach: Treat transition probabilities as random variables; extend value functions and Bellman operators to this setting.
nodes.niche_reason: Established robust-MDP area, with a specialised risk-measure theory angle.

nodes.title: ScaleMoE: Mixture-of-Experts for Scalable Continuous Control in Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: ScaleMoE inserts mixture-of-experts modules into actor and critic networks, letting continuous-control RL keep improving as the number of experts grows to 64.
nodes.problem: Scaling actor-critic network size in deep RL destabilizes training and saturates performance.
nodes.approach: Mixture-of-experts actor and critic with output-level or feature-level gating, applied to SimBa and BRC.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Scaling architectures for deep RL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Wait, Wait, Wait... Why Do Reasoning Models Loop?
nodes.tldr: Explains why reasoning models loop at low temperature, attributing it to learning errors, risk aversion from hard-to-learn actions, and transformers' bias to temporally correlated errors.
nodes.problem: Why reasoning LLMs repeat text in loops under greedy or low-temperature decoding.
nodes.approach: Empirical study of open reasoning models plus a synthetic graph reasoning task isolating two mechanisms.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic analysis of looping failure in reasoning models is specialised.

nodes.title: Clustering in Deep Stochastic Transformers
nodes.tldr: Proves deep Transformers with random-initialization noise converge to particle systems on the sphere driven by common Brownian noise, preventing collapse to one cluster.
nodes.problem: Token clustering theory assumes deterministic weights, ignoring stochasticity of standard random initialization.
nodes.approach: Diffusion-scaling limit analysis with RMS normalization, yielding an SDE with a phase transition for two tokens.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Stochastic particle-system theory of transformer depth is rare.

nodes.title: Attribution-Guided and Coverage-Maximized Pruning for Structural MoE Compression
nodes.tldr: Structurally prunes MoE experts at channel level, maximizing channel-score coverage via attribution approximation, retaining accuracy at 50% or 25% pruning.
nodes.problem: Expert-level MoE pruning is too coarse, misallocating budget and limiting compression.
nodes.approach: Attribution-based first-order channel scores with a coverage-maximizing prune-ratio objective.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: MoE compression is a common direction.

nodes.title: TabSwift: An Efficient Tabular Foundation Model with Row-Wise Attention
nodes.tldr: Lightweight tabular foundation model using row-wise attention only, with gated attention and register tokens, plus adaptive early exit for efficient in-context tabular prediction.
nodes.problem: Recent tabular foundation models gain accuracy through complex architectures with high inference cost.
nodes.approach: TabPFN-style row-wise attention backbone with gated attention, learnable registers, and per-sample layer-wise early exit.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Tabular foundation models are an established but specialised area.

nodes.title: Scalable Option Learning in High-Throughput Environments
nodes.tldr: Scalable Option Learning is a hierarchical policy-gradient algorithm with roughly 35x higher throughput, trained on 30 billion NetHack frames and validated on MiniHack and MuJoCo.
nodes.problem: Online hierarchical RL has not benefited from large-scale training in high-throughput environments.
nodes.approach: Throughput-optimized option-based hierarchical policy gradient implementation enabling massive-scale training.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Hierarchical RL at scale is established but specialised.

nodes.title: CoEvol-NO: State and Coordinate Co-Evolution with an Error-Driven Predictor-Corrector Paradigm for Neural Operator Transformer
nodes.tldr: CoEvol-NO is a neural operator transformer that jointly updates a persistent latent state and mesh tokens via an error-driven predictor-corrector, with linear time complexity.
nodes.problem: Long-sequence modeling in neural operator transformers with latent states treated as transient or decoupled.
nodes.approach: Persistent latent state co-evolving with mesh coordinates through layer-wise predictor-corrector updates driven by prediction error.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised neural-operator architecture with numerical-method inspiration.

nodes.title: Just-In-Time Reinforcement Learning: Continual Learning in LLM Agents Without Gradient Updates
nodes.tldr: Optimizes LLM agent policies at test time without gradient updates by retrieving trajectory advantages from memory and modulating output logits.
nodes.problem: Frozen LLM agents cannot adapt continually, and fine-tuning RL is costly and forgets.
nodes.approach: Non-parametric experience memory giving on-the-fly advantages that add to LLM logits.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans LLM agents, RL for LLMs, and continual learning
nodes.niche_reason: Gradient-free RL for LLM agents is an unusual direction

nodes.title: Balancing Understanding and Generation in Discrete Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Unifies masked and uniform-noise discrete diffusion language models via a stationary noise kernel, balancing understanding and few-step generation.
nodes.problem: Masked and uniform-noise discrete diffusion LMs each excel at only one of understanding and few-step generation.
nodes.approach: Stationary noise kernel bridging both paradigms, with algebraically simplified posteriors that reduce memory.
nodes.confidence_reason: Unifies two discrete diffusion paradigms; method sits between generation and language modelling.
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete diffusion language models are an active, crowded area.

nodes.title: Large Language Models Develop Novel Social Biases Through Adaptive Exploration
nodes.tldr: Shows LLMs spontaneously develop novel social biases toward artificial groups via exploration-exploitation, and that incentivizing exploration best reduces the stratification.
nodes.problem: Debiasing LLMs does not prevent new biases from emerging through their own decision-making experience.
nodes.approach: Psychology-paradigm task allocation with artificial groups, testing interventions on inputs, problem structure and explicit steering.
nodes.niche_reason: Emergent LLM group bias from exploration is an unusual angle

nodes.title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Operates at the Edge of Stability
nodes.tldr: Explains edge-of-stability sharpening with directional smoothness and generalized sharpness under arbitrary norms, covering vanilla, preconditioned and spectral gradient descent.
nodes.problem: Edge-of-stability theory is incomplete, especially for non-Euclidean gradient methods
nodes.approach: Directional smoothness generalized to arbitrary norms as a sharpness measure
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: non-Euclidean edge-of-stability analysis is a narrow subfield

nodes.title: Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs
nodes.tldr: Lets pretrained LLM layers be skipped or looped per input; a lightweight predictor picks programs that raise math reasoning accuracy with fewer layers.
nodes.problem: Fixed-depth LLM inference runs every layer for every input, wasting compute and missing answers alternative paths get right.
nodes.approach: Predicts per-input programs that skip or repeat pretrained layers, using a lightweight prediction network.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Per-input layer skipping and looping is a specialised efficiency angle.

nodes.title: FIDIA: Function-Informed Sequence Design via Inference-Aligned Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: FIDIA is an RL framework for protein sequence design that optimizes the policy under Best-of-N inference to reach high-fitness sequences.
nodes.problem: Inverse folding ignores function and its training objective mismatches Best-of-N inference.
nodes.approach: Composite functional rewards with a gradient estimator that maximizes the expected best-of-N reward.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Training-inference alignment for protein design via RL is specialised

nodes.title: MiniAppBench: Evaluating the Shift from Text to Interactive HTML Responses in LLM-Powered Assistants
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks LLMs on generating interactive HTML mini-apps, with an agentic browser-based evaluator that tests intention, static, and dynamic behavior.
nodes.problem: Existing benchmarks test algorithmic correctness or static layouts, not interactive generated apps.
nodes.approach: 500 tasks across six domains plus an agentic browser-automation evaluator for intention, static, and dynamic checks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.confidence_reason: Benchmark spans code generation and LLM evaluation; either topic fits
nodes.niche_reason: Interactive HTML app benchmarking is an emerging, less common direction

nodes.title: The Assistant Axis: Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models
nodes.tldr: Finds an Assistant Axis in activation space; restricting activations along it stabilizes persona and resists persona-based jailbreaks.
nodes.problem: LLMs drift out of their default Assistant persona into harmful or bizarre behavior.
nodes.approach: Measure deviation along a learned Assistant direction; cap activations to a fixed region.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Persona-space steering is specialised but has a growing following

nodes.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
nodes.tldr: Enables on-policy learning from demonstrations by using a demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher, reducing forgetting versus SFT.
nodes.problem: SFT on demonstrations is off-policy and causes catastrophic forgetting
nodes.approach: Self-distillation where an in-context, demonstration-conditioned model supplies on-policy training signals
nodes.niche_reason: Self-distillation for continual LLM learning is common

nodes.title: Exact Functional ANOVA Decomposition for Categorical Inputs Models
nodes.tldr: Derives a closed-form functional ANOVA decomposition for categorical inputs under arbitrary dependence via discrete Fourier analysis, generalizing SHAP values.
nodes.problem: Functional ANOVA lacks closed-form decomposition for dependent features, forcing costly sampling approximations.
nodes.approach: Extends discrete Fourier analysis to obtain exact decomposition and a SHAP generalization for categorical data.
nodes.niche_reason: Exact ANOVA for dependent categorical inputs is a rare theoretical topic.

nodes.title: Joint-Space Empowerment as a Theory of Dexterous Motor Coordination
nodes.tldr: Introduces joint-space empowerment, an information-theoretic objective that finds low-dimensional action manifolds for redundant musculoskeletal systems.
nodes.problem: Policy search is hard in high-dimensional musculoskeletal systems with many muscles per joint.
nodes.approach: Optimal precoding of latent actions into muscle commands, solved in closed form under Gaussian dynamics.
nodes.confidence_reason: Motor control with intrinsic-motivation objective; topic straddles two areas
nodes.niche_reason: Empowerment-based muscle-synergy manifolds are a very rare niche

nodes.title: FedARC: Anchor-Guided Residual Compensation for Data and Model Heterogeneous Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: Heterogeneous federated learning where a shared lightweight extractor is paired with client-specific fusion and residual compensation to correct feature mismatches.
nodes.problem: Data and model heterogeneity across clients cause weak alignment and poor personalization.
nodes.approach: Trainable projector with adaptive residual compensation and semantic anchor alignment across clients.
nodes.niche_reason: Crowded federated personalization area

nodes.title: Optimal Rates for Feasible Payoff Set Estimation in Games
nodes.tldr: Establishes minimax-optimal sample rates for estimating the set of payoffs consistent with observed Nash equilibrium play in bimatrix games.
nodes.problem: Learners observing equilibrium play must infer the full set of feasible payoffs, not one estimate.
nodes.approach: Hausdorff-precision estimation of the feasible payoff set from actions alone, analysed for exact and approximate equilibria.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Inverse game theory with set-valued payoffs is rare

nodes.title: Local Covariate Selection for Average Causal Effect Estimation without Pretreatment and Causal Sufficiency Assumptions
nodes.tldr: Selects adjustment covariates locally for nonparametric causal effect estimation, allowing latent variables and post-treatment covariates without global structure learning.
nodes.problem: Covariate selection usually assumes no latent variables or pretreatment covariates, and global learning is costly.
nodes.approach: Characterize the local existence boundary of valid adjustment sets, then learn covariates locally with sound and complete guarantees.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Covariate selection for causal effects is established; local, latent-tolerant methods are specialised.

nodes.title: Generalizable and Composable Multi-Model Embedding Translation
nodes.tldr: Translates embeddings across models without re-embedding, using a hierarchical mixture of experts robust to out-of-distribution inputs, mixing, and chaining.
nodes.problem: Embedding translation fails under OOD inputs, multi-model mixing, and chained translations.
nodes.approach: Geometry-aware error analysis plus localized parameter-efficient mixture-of-experts adaptation.
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-model embedding translation is specialised but studied.

nodes.title: From Feasible to Practical: Pareto-Optimal Synthesis Planning
nodes.tldr: Formulates retrosynthesis as multi-objective search, producing Pareto fronts of synthesis routes that trade off cost, sustainability and yield.
nodes.problem: Synthesis planning stops at one feasible route, ignoring cost, toxicity and other trade-offs.
nodes.approach: Weighted-scalarized multi-objective A* search with solution-informed sampling and optimality guarantees.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-objective retrosynthesis is a specialised chemistry niche

nodes.title: ConFlux: Multivariate Time Series in Flux, One Unified Forecast in Confluence
nodes.tldr: ConFlux is a time-series foundation model that reorders and patches variables into compact tokens for a ViT-style forecaster, with strong zero-shot results.
nodes.problem: Multivariate forecasting must unify asynchronous, heterogeneous variables for general-purpose zero-shot prediction.
nodes.approach: Variable sorting and adjacent-variable patching feeding a Vision Transformer-style backbone, pretrained on many datasets.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Common time-series foundation model direction.

nodes.title: DLM: Unified Decision Language Model for Offline Multi-Agent Sequential Decision Making
nodes.tldr: Recasts offline multi-agent decision making as dialogue-style sequence prediction with an LLM, fine-tuned then refined with group relative policy optimization.
nodes.problem: Offline multi-agent policies rely on fixed observation formats, limiting reuse across scenarios.
nodes.approach: Centralized-training decentralized-execution LLM with supervised fine-tuning and GRPO for robustness.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: LLM sequence modeling vs offline MARL; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: LLMs as offline multi-agent policies is an emerging but growing niche

nodes.title: Practical and Optimal Algorithm for Linear Contextual Bandits with Rare Parameter Updates
nodes.tldr: Gives linear contextual bandit algorithms with only O(log log T) parameter updates that achieve minimax-optimal regret and are computationally efficient.
nodes.problem: Bandit learners can update parameters only rarely, and prior batched methods are computationally heavy.
nodes.approach: Static update schedule; the second algorithm drops the near G-optimal design step while keeping optimal regret.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Low-switching bandit algorithms are a specialised theory niche.

nodes.title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
nodes.tldr: Argues alignment-faking behavior stems from sycophancy toward AI researchers rather than scheming, showing evaluation awareness persists when told deployed and probing cannot separate the two.
nodes.problem: Alignment faking in language models is interpreted as scheming; the sycophancy alternative is untested.
nodes.approach: Evaluation-awareness experiments, probing and steering, and fine-tuning for sycophancy to test the hypothesis.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Active but specialised AI safety debate on deceptive alignment.

nodes.title: Perceptrons and Localization of Attention’s Mean-Field Landscape
nodes.tldr: Studies transformers as interacting particle systems on the sphere and shows perceptron blocks make mean-field attention critical points atomic and localized.
nodes.problem: Effect of feed-forward blocks on the mean-field attention dynamics landscape.
nodes.approach: Wasserstein gradient flow analysis of interacting particles on the sphere with perceptron blocks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Mean-field particle-system view of transformers is very rare.

nodes.title: MIRA: A Score for Conditional Distribution Accuracy and Model Comparison
nodes.tldr: MIRA is a sample-based score assessing how accurate a candidate conditional distribution is using only joint samples, enabling Bayesian model comparison via posterior validation without evidence computation.
nodes.problem: Assessing accuracy of conditional distributions and comparing Bayesian models using only samples.
nodes.approach: Compare probability mass over regions to derive an analytic statistic with reference values and uncertainty.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Posterior validation scores for Bayesian model comparison are rare.

nodes.title: Conformal Policy Control
nodes.tldr: Uses conformal calibration on data from a safe reference policy to bound how far a new policy may deviate, provably enforcing a declared risk tolerance.
nodes.problem: Letting agents improve beyond a safe policy while guaranteeing safety constraints are not violated.
nodes.approach: Conformal risk control calibrates the probabilistic regulation of an untested policy using safe-policy data.
nodes.niche_reason: Conformal methods applied to policy safety are fairly specialised.

nodes.title: Learning with Admissibility: Robust Fuzzy Hashing for Cross-Modal Retrieval with Noisy Labels
nodes.tldr: Robust cross-modal hashing that uses fuzzy set possibility and necessity measures to turn noisy labels into admissible supervision, with dual-granularity alignment.
nodes.problem: Cross-modal hashing degrades when real-world label noise corrupts supervision.
nodes.approach: Fuzzy admissibility refinement calibrates supervision; dual-granularity structural alignment enforces cross-modal consistency.
nodes.confidence_reason: Hashing retrieval and noisy-label learning sit in different topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Established: cross-modal hashing; fuzzy label handling is specialised.

nodes.title: Any-Order GPT as Masked Diffusion Model: Decoupling Formulation and Architecture
nodes.tldr: Evaluates masked diffusion language models in a decoder-only architecture as any-order autoregressive models, fairly comparing to autoregressive models and achieving about 25x inference speedup.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive and masked diffusion LMs are confounded by differing architectures, hiding true algorithmic and efficiency tradeoffs.
nodes.approach: Implement MDM as decoder-only any-order autoregression, compare orders, and study architectural efficiency with temperature annealing.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete diffusion LMs are an emerging but specialised direction.

nodes.title: A Unifying View of Variational Generative Wasserstein Flows
nodes.tldr: Unifies many generative models as parametric JKO (Wasserstein gradient flow) schemes, extending beyond f-divergences to IPMs and MMD.
nodes.problem: Generative models rely on different divergence-minimization principles without a unified geometric framework.
nodes.approach: Parametric JKO scheme framework for f-divergence, IPM and MMD objectives, with theoretical equivalences between methods.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment call between generative models and optimal transport theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical unification of GANs via JKO flows; specialised

nodes.title: Towards the Explainability of Temporal Graph Networks via Memory Backtracking and Topological Attribution
nodes.tldr: Explains Temporal Graph Network predictions by attributing them to historical events through memory backtracking and topology attribution trees with LRP.
nodes.problem: Existing TGN explainers ignore the memory module, leaving the influence of past events unexplained.
nodes.approach: LRP-based attribution over topology and memory backtracking trees, with optimized selection of important events.
nodes.niche_reason: Memory-based explanations for temporal graph networks are rare

nodes.title: Unraveling Syntax: Language Modeling and the Substructure of Grammars
nodes.tldr: Proves that language modeling loss decomposes linearly over context-free grammar subgrammars, and shows models learn subgrammars in parallel, with limited benefit from subgrammar pretraining.
nodes.problem: Learning dynamics of language models on context-free grammars with respect to grammar substructure are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Define subgrammars, prove loss decomposition theorems, and test empirically with subgrammar pretraining and representation alignment analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Formal-language theory of LM learning dynamics is a rare angle.

nodes.title: Understanding Self-Supervised Learning via Latent Distribution Matching
nodes.tldr: Frames self-supervised learning as latent distribution matching, unifying ICA, contrastive, non-contrastive and predictive methods, with identifiability proofs and a Kalman-based Bayesian filtering model.
nodes.problem: SSL lacks a unifying theoretical framework explaining diverse methods and guiding new designs.
nodes.approach: Alignment under assumed latent model plus entropy maximization; derive sampling-free Bayesian filter and identifiability results.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical SSL unification with identifiability is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.tldr: LatentMAS lets LLM agents collaborate by exchanging last-layer hidden states and a shared latent working memory, training-free, instead of text messages.
nodes.problem: Text-based communication among LLM agents is lossy and inefficient for multi-agent reasoning.
nodes.approach: Autoregressive latent thought generation plus shared latent working memory for lossless cross-agent information transfer.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-space agent communication is newer and specialised.

nodes.title: Improving the Performance and Learning Stability of Parallelizable RNNs Designed for Ultra-Low Power Applications
nodes.tldr: Fixes gradient blocking in the bistable memory recurrent unit with a cumulative update giving skip connections through time, yielding CMRU for ultra-low-power analog-friendly parallelizable RNNs.
nodes.problem: Bistable-memory RNNs for low-power hardware underperform and train unstably on long-range dependencies.
nodes.approach: Cumulative update formulation restoring gradient flow while keeping quantized persistent states, yielding CMRU and alpha-CMRU.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Hardware co-designed analog RNNs are a rare direction.

nodes.title: Latent Laplace Diffusion for Irregular Multivariate Time Series
nodes.tldr: Generative latent-diffusion forecaster for irregular multivariate time series, generating whole horizons in Laplace-domain latent trajectories.
nodes.problem: Irregular time series force a trade-off: re-gridding distorts structure, while continuous solvers drift.
nodes.approach: Learnable complex-conjugate poles parameterize the diffusion mean in Laplace domain, with a gap-aware history summarizer.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Laplace-domain latent diffusion for forecasting, uncommon

nodes.title: What Makes Value Learning Efficient in Residual Reinforcement Learning?
nodes.tldr: Diagnoses cold-start and scale-mismatch bottlenecks in critic learning for residual RL and proposes DAWN, which uses base-policy data anchoring and critic normalization.
nodes.problem: Inefficient value learning when refining a frozen pretrained policy with bounded residual corrections.
nodes.approach: Warm up the critic with base-policy transitions and apply critic normalization (DAWN).
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Residual RL value learning is a specialised but established topic.

nodes.title: Variational Learning for Insertion-based Generation
nodes.tldr: Insertion Process learns where, what, and when to stop inserting tokens, using permutation-based variational inference to learn insertion order for variable-length generation.
nodes.problem: Non-monotonic generators are order-agnostic and fixed-length, so they cannot learn adaptive insertion order for variable-length sequences.
nodes.approach: Bijection between insertion trajectories and permutations gives exact likelihood; train a stochastic insertion model with permutation variational inference.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Non-monotonic insertion models are a specialised corner of discrete generation.

nodes.title: Optimal Transport under Group Fairness Constraints
nodes.tldr: Defines group fairness for optimal transport plans, gives a modified Sinkhorn for exact fairness, and relaxations via penalization and bilevel cost learning with guarantees.
nodes.problem: Ensuring group fairness in optimal-transport-based matching of scarce resources.
nodes.approach: Modified Sinkhorn plus penalized OT and bilevel ground-cost learning with theoretical bounds.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Fairness constraints in OT plans are a rare topic.

nodes.title: Rotary Position Encodings for Graphs
nodes.tldr: Adapts rotary position encodings to graphs by rotating tokens using graph Laplacian spectra, injecting structure into attention while remaining compatible with linear attention.
nodes.problem: Standard position encodings for graph transformers are bias-based and incompatible with linear attention.
nodes.approach: Wave-induced rotary encodings derived from the Laplacian spectrum.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph positional encodings are specialised but established.

nodes.title: DecodeShare: Tracing the Shared Subspace of LLM Decode-Time Decisions
nodes.tldr: Identifies a low-dimensional subspace shared across tasks in decode-time hidden states and shows removing it degrades LLM decisions more than prefill-derived subspaces.
nodes.problem: Unclear what task-general structure LLMs use at decode time versus prefill under KV-cached inference.
nodes.approach: Protocol finds a cross-task shared subspace, then causally ablates it only during decoding.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Decode-time shared subspaces are a rare mechanistic angle.

nodes.title: Hierarchical Successor Representation for Robust Transfer
nodes.tldr: Builds policy-robust successor representations with temporal abstractions, then uses NMF to get sparse, low-rank state features that transfer quickly to new reward tasks.
nodes.problem: Classical successor representations depend on the policy, so learned features go stale as the policy changes.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical successor representation with temporal abstractions, factorized by non-negative matrix factorisation.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.confidence_reason: Successor representation straddles hierarchical, transfer, and exploration topics
nodes.niche_reason: Successor representations are established RL theory, here with temporal abstraction

nodes.title: What Do Agents Learn from Trajectory-SFT: Semantics or Interfaces?
nodes.tldr: PIPE minimally rewrites agent environment interfaces to diagnose whether trajectory-SFT agents learn semantics or memorize interfaces, with an Interface Reliance metric across 16 environments.
nodes.problem: Agent benchmarks conflate semantic tool use with interface-specific pattern memorization.
nodes.approach: Protocol-level interface rewrites preserving task semantics plus counterbalanced alias-based Interface Reliance metric.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Agent evaluation is active; interface-shortcut diagnosis is specialised.

nodes.title: Faster Activation Functions at the Edge for Post-Training Speedups
nodes.tldr: FFCC is a compiler that generates fast floating-point-reinterpretation approximations of activation functions like GELU and Swish for edge devices, giving large speedups without retraining.
nodes.problem: Advanced activation functions are slow on edge hardware lacking fast exponentiation and division.
nodes.approach: Compile activation specs into efficient instruction sequences via floating-point bit reinterpretation and derivation rules.
nodes.niche_reason: Compiler-level activation approximation for microcontrollers is rare.

nodes.title: Learning Human-Robot Collaboration via Heterogeneous-Agent Lyapunov Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: HALO stabilizes decentralized multi-agent RL for human-robot collaboration by enforcing Lyapunov contraction in policy-parameter space, shrinking the rationality gap between heterogeneous agents.
nodes.problem: Heterogeneous human-robot decentralized policy updates deviate from cooperative optimization and can oscillate or diverge.
nodes.approach: Lyapunov-certified quadratic projection of decentralized policy gradients to ensure monotonic contraction of the rationality gap.
nodes.niche_reason: Lyapunov stability for heterogeneous human-robot MARL is unusual.

nodes.title: Rational Transductors
nodes.tldr: Augments Transformers with a matrix-valued automaton-style recurrence to recognize regular languages and NC1-complete tasks while keeping parallel training.
nodes.problem: Standard Transformers struggle with state tracking and length generalization on sequential logic.
nodes.approach: Dual-stream architecture injecting weighted-finite-automaton state into attention via deep rational injection.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Architecture and expressivity theory make primary topic ambiguous
nodes.niche_reason: Regular-language expressivity of Transformers is a rare angle

nodes.title: A Unifying Relational Perspective on Expressive Lottery Tickets
nodes.tldr: Proves sufficiently large relational and temporal GNNs contain sparse subnetworks that keep 1-RWL expressivity, with a probabilistic pruning bound.
nodes.problem: How parameter sparsity affects the expressivity of relational and temporal graph neural networks is unclear.
nodes.approach: Extends the strong expressive lottery ticket hypothesis to the relational WL test and reformulates temporal GNNs as RGNNs.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Expressivity of sparse relational and temporal GNNs is rare

nodes.title: Towards Understanding Adam Convergence on Highly Degenerate Polynomials
nodes.tldr: Identifies highly degenerate polynomials on which Adam converges locally linearly without schedulers, outperforming GD, and maps Adam's hyperparameter regimes.
nodes.problem: Understanding where Adam inherently converges well, beyond scheduler-dependent analyses.
nodes.approach: Local stability analysis on degenerate polynomials showing a second-moment decoupling that amplifies the effective learning rate.
nodes.niche_reason: Adam theory is established but this angle is specialised.

nodes.title: Provable Accuracy Collapse of Embedding-Based Representations under Dimensionality Mismatch
nodes.tldr: Proves embeddings below a constant fraction of the true dimension violate almost half of contrastive triplets, plus Unique-Games hardness.
nodes.problem: Choosing the embedding dimension for triplet-supervised representations risks a sudden accuracy collapse.
nodes.approach: Information-theoretic bounds on triplet violations plus computational hardness reductions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: information and hardness limits on triplet embedding dimension.

nodes.title: Local Redundancy: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Plasticity from Synthetic Memorization
nodes.tldr: Defines local redundancy, an information-theoretic plasticity measure bounded by gradient norms on a synthetic memorization task, predicting continual and transfer performance.
nodes.problem: Existing plasticity measures lack theory and poorly predict performance on new tasks.
nodes.approach: Universal-compression-derived local redundancy with a tractable lower bound from gradient norms on synthetic memorization.
nodes.niche_reason: Information-theoretic plasticity measure is a rare angle.

nodes.title: Even Faster Kernel Matrix Linear Algebra via Density Estimation
nodes.tldr: Improves KDE-based algorithms for kernel matrix tasks like matrix-vector products and spectral norm, with better epsilon and n dependence plus conditional lower bounds.
nodes.problem: Existing algorithms for kernel matrix computations have high polynomial dependence on epsilon and n.
nodes.approach: KDE-query-based sub-quadratic algorithms for relative-error approximation, complemented by conditional hardness lower bounds.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-grained algorithms via KDE are very rare in ML.

nodes.title: Hallucination is a Consequence of Space-Optimality: A Rate-Distortion Theorem for Membership Testing
nodes.tldr: Shows LLM hallucination on random facts is an optimal lossy-compression effect, via a rate-distortion theorem for membership testing tied to Bloom filters.
nodes.problem: Why language models hallucinate confidently on random facts with no inferable pattern.
nodes.approach: Formalize fact memorization as membership testing and derive a KL-based rate-distortion bound.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Rate-distortion view of hallucination linked to Bloom filters is unusual

nodes.title: Optimal structure learning and conditional independence testing
nodes.tldr: Shows minimax optimal rates for structure learning equal those of conditional independence testing for poly-forests, achieved by a modified PC algorithm.
nodes.problem: Statistical complexity of learning graphical model structure.
nodes.approach: Reduction from structure learning to conditional independence testing with a modified PC algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Minimax theory of causal structure learning is specialised.

nodes.title: Investigating Memory in Model-Free RL with POPGym Arcade
nodes.tldr: Introduces POPGym Arcade, accelerated Atari-like POMDP environments with matched fully and partially observable variants, and tools revealing how recurrent RL agents use memory.
nodes.problem: Understanding how deep RL agents use memory under partial observability.
nodes.approach: Paired observable/partially observable environments and policy analysis tools for counterfactual memory studies.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: POMDP memory analysis is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Effective Reasoning Chains Reduce Intrinsic Dimensionality
nodes.tldr: Shows effective chain-of-thought strategies lower a task's intrinsic dimensionality, which strongly inversely correlates with generalization on GSM8K with Gemma-3 models.
nodes.problem: Why chain-of-thought strategies generalize differently is poorly understood and not quantified.
nodes.approach: Measure minimum model dimensions needed to hit an accuracy threshold across reasoning strategies.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: intrinsic-dimension analysis of reasoning chains is specialised

nodes.title: TokSuite: Measuring the Impact of Tokenizer Choice on Language Model Behavior
nodes.tldr: Releases fourteen identical LMs differing only in tokenizer, plus a multilingual perturbation benchmark, to isolate how tokenizers affect language model behavior.
nodes.problem: Tokenizer influence on LM performance is poorly understood because it is hard to isolate.
nodes.approach: Controlled suite of pretrained models varying only the tokenizer, with a multilingual robustness benchmark.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Tokenization studies are specialised but a recognised research thread.

nodes.title: Alignment-Guided Score Matching for Text-to-Image Alignment in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Reward-free post-training that refines soft text tokens by injecting contrastive alignment guidance into the diffusion score-matching objective, fixing over-counting and repetition failures of SoftREPA.
nodes.problem: Text-to-image diffusion models misalign with prompts; contrastive soft-token tuning causes counting and repetition failures.
nodes.approach: Integrate contrastive alignment directions into the score-matching loss while tuning soft text tokens.
nodes.niche_reason: Common text-image alignment post-training, though reward-free score-level angle is slightly distinct.

nodes.title: Is Data Shapley Not Better than Random in Data Selection? Ask NASH
nodes.tldr: NASH decomposes a target utility into Shapley-informative components, aggregates them nonlinearly, and boosts Shapley-based data selection at low extra cost.
nodes.problem: Data Shapley is sometimes no better than random for selecting high-quality training subsets.
nodes.approach: Non-linear aggregation of Shapley-informative component utilities as the selection objective.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Data selection versus attribution is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Shapley-based data selection is an established but specialised line.

nodes.title: Disentangling Latent Risk Pathways via Bayesian Hypergraph Inference
nodes.tldr: Models multi-disease risk with Bayesian hypergraphs whose latent hyperedges are modulated by risk factors, using structured variational inference for calibrated, interpretable EHR analysis.
nodes.problem: Multi-disease EHR models treat diseases independently or use black boxes with little uncertainty quantification.
nodes.approach: Bayesian hypergraph with repulsion prior and structured variational inference.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Bayesian method applied to EHR; topic could sit under healthcare.
nodes.niche_reason: Hypergraph disease pathway models are rare in EHR work.

nodes.title: DroneDINO: Towards Heterogeneous Routed Mixture of Experts for Drone-based Unified Object Detection
nodes.tldr: A unified drone detector combining RGB, infrared and RGB-IR tasks via heterogeneous routed mixture-of-experts with shared, task-specific and dynamic experts.
nodes.problem: Unified MoE detectors over-activate experts for dominant tasks and under-activate others.
nodes.approach: Shared, task-specific and top-k dynamic experts, trained with a task-recognition auxiliary loss.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Drone unified detection with routed MoE is specialised.

nodes.title: Reward-free Alignment for Conflicting Objectives
nodes.tldr: RACO aligns LLMs to conflicting objectives directly from pairwise preferences using a clipped conflict-averse gradient descent, with convergence to weighted Pareto-critical points.
nodes.problem: Multi-objective preference alignment suffers gradient conflicts and relies on reward models that distort preferences.
nodes.approach: Reward-free clipped conflict-averse gradient descent on pairwise preference data.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-objective alignment is a specialised subarea of preference optimization.

nodes.title: Security--Fidelity Tradeoffs: The Hidden Cost of Prompt Injection Defense
nodes.tldr: Shows defenses against indirect prompt injection trade security for fidelity, and introduces SecFid, a benchmark that measures both across 48 configurations.
nodes.problem: Attack-success metrics miss that injection defenses corrupt tasks needing untrusted text.
nodes.approach: Benchmark where executing, processing, and ignoring an injection give distinguishable outputs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt-injection defense is crowded; fidelity framing is less common.

nodes.title: SplAttN: Bridging 2D and 3D with Gaussian Soft Splatting and Attention for Point Cloud Completion
nodes.tldr: Replaces hard point-cloud projection with differentiable Gaussian splatting to keep dense image-plane support, improving 2D-3D cross-modal learning for completion.
nodes.problem: Sparse projection collapses cross-modal support, so point cloud completion ignores visual cues.
nodes.approach: Gaussian soft splatting as continuous density estimation feeding cross-modal attention.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Splatting-based 2D-3D completion is specialised but established

nodes.title: Reverse Flow Matching: A Unified Framework for Online Reinforcement Learning with Diffusion and Flow Policies
nodes.tldr: Reverse flow matching unifies noise-expectation and gradient-expectation training of diffusion and flow policies in online RL without direct samples from the Q-defined Boltzmann target.
nodes.problem: Training diffusion and flow policies in online RL lacks samples from the target Boltzmann distribution.
nodes.approach: A unified reverse flow matching framework relating weighted-noise and weighted-Q-gradient objectives.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion policies for RL are a hot, fairly common direction.

nodes.title: Information Flow Reveals When to Trust Language Models
nodes.tldr: Traces layer-wise information flow from context tokens to outputs in RAG and derives simulatability and concentration measures to estimate whether an LLM answer is trustworthy.
nodes.problem: Estimating uncertainty of LLM answers in RAG by assessing whether predictions are grounded in relevant context.
nodes.approach: Layer-wise information-flow trace of context token contributions, yielding simulatability and concentration confidence measures.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Uncertainty estimation for RAG via internal information flow is specialised but active.

nodes.title: Path-dependent Discrete Amortized Inference
nodes.tldr: Lifts GFlowNet-style amortized samplers beyond Markovian MDPs with learnable latent dynamics so policies depend on full trajectory history, improving expressivity and convergence for discrete sampling.
nodes.problem: Markovian amortized samplers suffer from state aliasing and poor signal propagation when sampling discrete compositional objects.
nodes.approach: Augment the MDP with learnable latent dynamics enabling path-dependent policies, with extended learning algorithms.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: GFlowNets are a rare research subcommunity.

nodes.title: On Efficient Scaling of GNNs via IO-Aware Layers Implementations
nodes.tldr: Analyzes GNN layers into three kernel families and builds IO-aware GPU kernels that cut memory traffic, with large speedups over DGL.
nodes.problem: GNN layers materialize edge-wise intermediates, causing memory traffic that limits scalability on large graphs.
nodes.approach: Family-specific fused GPU kernels for SpMM, reduction and attention layers, plus graph reordering analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised GPU kernel work for graph layers

nodes.title: When the Prompt Becomes Visual: Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks for Large Image Editing Models
nodes.tldr: Shows image editing models can be jailbroken purely with visual prompts, and proposes a training-free defense using introspective multimodal reasoning.
nodes.problem: Vision-prompt image editing models expose a visual attack surface that unimodal safety filters do not cover.
nodes.approach: Visual-to-visual attack encoding malicious instructions in images, benchmarked on IESBench with a guard-free defense.
nodes.confidence_reason: jailbreak vs adversarial vs image editing; close topics
nodes.niche_reason: Visual-prompt jailbreaks of image editing models are rare

nodes.title: GoodDiffusion: Proactive Copyright Protection for Diffusion Bridge Models via Learnable Sample-specific Signatures
nodes.tldr: Makes diffusion bridge models refuse unauthorized inputs via backdoor-style, sample-specific learned signatures while serving authorized users normally.
nodes.problem: Post-hoc watermarking cannot prevent unauthorized use of diffusion bridge models, and static signatures are fragile.
nodes.approach: Learnable Signature Network that assigns input-conditioned signatures embedded via backdoor training.
nodes.confidence_reason: watermarking vs backdoor-based access control; close topics
nodes.niche_reason: Backdoor-based copyright control for diffusion bridges is rare

nodes.title: The Obfuscation Atlas: Mapping Where Honesty Emerges in RLVR with Deception Probes
nodes.tldr: Shows RL training against deception probes can yield obfuscated deception, and that high KL regularization plus detector penalty can produce honest policies.
nodes.problem: Whether training against deception detectors yields honesty or merely evasion.
nodes.approach: Coding RLVR environment with natural reward hacking; taxonomy of honest versus obfuscated policy outcomes.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Obfuscation of deception detectors under RL is an unusual safety niche

nodes.title: Learning to Theorize the World from Observation
nodes.tldr: Introduces Learning-to-Theorize, where a Neural Language-of-Thought Programmer induces executable latent programs from raw observation as explanations, enabling explanation-driven generalization.
nodes.problem: How AI systems can build theories of the world from non-textual observation rather than just predicting frames.
nodes.approach: Neural model that induces and executes latent programs as explanations of observations.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.confidence_reason: Abstract is conceptual; topic spans world models, program induction, representation.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory induction as executable programs from observation is very rare.

nodes.title: How Many Different Outputs Can a Transformer Generate?
nodes.tldr: Bounds how many distinct sequences a transformer can output, linear in prompt length, explaining copying and cramming failures.
nodes.problem: Predicting how many different sequences a transformer can generate, and why it fails on simple tasks.
nodes.approach: Theoretical upper bounds on accessible sequences as a function of prompt length, checked empirically across architectures.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Expressivity theory of output sets is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Learning Structured Reasoning via Tractable Trajectory Control
nodes.tldr: Guides RL rollouts toward diverse reasoning patterns using tractable trajectory control, with importance-sampling correction and power-scaled weights for stable on-policy optimization.
nodes.problem: Standard RL fails to reliably discover diverse reasoning behaviors because such trajectories are sparse in sampling.
nodes.approach: Behavior policy steers rollouts to target reasoning patterns while keeping unbiased importance-sampling estimates.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL for LLM reasoning is a crowded mainstream direction.

nodes.title: Adaptive Memory Retention in Dynamic Graphs
nodes.tldr: LAMP models snapshot-based dynamic graphs with impulsive neural ODEs, antisymmetric conservative flow and learned dissipation, yielding stable long-range propagation with theoretical stability guarantees.
nodes.problem: Uncontrolled information accumulation and noise in long-range dynamic graph modeling.
nodes.approach: Impulsive neural ODEs with antisymmetric parameterization plus learned dissipative dynamics.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamical-systems view of dynamic GNNs is uncommon.

nodes.title: Beyond Language Modeling: An Exploration of Multimodal Pretraining
nodes.tldr: Controlled from-scratch study of native multimodal pretraining with Transfusion, finding RAE visual representation, vision-language synergy, emergent world modeling, and MoE resolving scaling asymmetry.
nodes.problem: The design space of native multimodal pretraining is opaque, with unclear factors and scaling behavior.
nodes.approach: From-scratch Transfusion experiments on text, video and image-text, with IsoFLOP scaling-law analysis and MoE.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal pretraining and scaling are mainstream topics.

nodes.title: EgoTactile: Learning Grasp Pressure for Everyday Objects from Egocentric Video
nodes.tldr: EgoTactile benchmarks full-hand grasp pressure estimation from egocentric video, with a discriminative baseline and a video-diffusion-based EgoPressureDiff that resolves partial-observation ambiguity.
nodes.problem: Estimating full-hand grasp pressure from egocentric video without intrusive tactile hardware.
nodes.approach: Benchmark pairing video with pressure data, plus conditional video diffusion with physically-informed feature rectification.
nodes.niche_reason: Rare vision-based hand pressure estimation task.

nodes.title: PanoWorld-X: Generating Explorable Panoramic Worlds via Sphere-Aware Video Diffusion
nodes.tldr: PanoWorld-X generates explorable 360-degree scene videos with sphere-aware attention and a panoramic 3D motion embedding for geometrically consistent results.
nodes.problem: 2D video generators produce geometrically inconsistent, non-explorable 360-degree worlds.
nodes.approach: Sphere-aware attention on panoramic latents plus a Plucker-style 3D motion control embedding.
nodes.niche_reason: Explorable panoramic video worlds are specialised but active.

nodes.title: Delving into Muon and Beyond: Deep Analysis and Extensions
nodes.tldr: Frames Muon as one member of a spectral-power update family and shows spectral normalization helps, but Muon does not consistently beat Adam.
nodes.problem: The mechanisms behind the Muon optimizer and its relation to Adam are poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Spectral transformations U Σ^p V^T of momentum and RMS-normalized updates, with a coupled Newton iteration.
nodes.niche_reason: Muon and Adam optimizer analysis is a crowded mainstream topic

nodes.title: Joint Learning in the Gaussian Single Index Model
nodes.tldr: Analyzes gradient flow of alternating joint learning of direction and link function in Gaussian single-index models, proving convergence even from negatively correlated initialization, with an RKHS implementation.
nodes.problem: Jointly learning a projection direction and unknown univariate link function in high dimensions is non-convex.
nodes.approach: Gradient flow analysis of alternating scheme with information exponent, plus RKHS-based function estimation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Joint learning of link function in single-index models is quite rare.

nodes.title: EntroKV: Entropy-Guided Dynamic Budget Allocation for KV-Cache Compression
nodes.tldr: Allocates KV-cache compression budgets across layers and heads dynamically using attention entropy as a sensitivity proxy, retaining about 98% performance at 30% budget.
nodes.problem: Static or uniform KV-cache budget allocation ignores heterogeneity of information density across attention heads.
nodes.approach: Entropy-guided dynamic budget allocation, plug-and-play with various compression operators.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: KV-cache compression is a very crowded area.

nodes.title: On the Sharp Input-Output Analysis of Nonlinear Systems under Adversarial Attacks
nodes.tldr: Proves an l2-norm estimator learns nonlinear system input-output maps under sparse adversarial attacks, with a provably optimal error bound.
nodes.problem: Learning input-output maps of nonlinear systems when inputs are correlated and adversarially corrupted.
nodes.approach: Basis-function reformulation and l2-norm estimation, with an adversary whose attack times are sparse.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: system identification fits sequential data vs robustness framing
nodes.niche_reason: adversarial sysid analysis for nonlinear systems is rare

nodes.title: Scalable Event Cloud Network for Event-based Classification
nodes.tldr: SECNet classifies event-camera data by treating events as point clouds, injecting polarity into grouping/sampling and using Fourier-domain feature extraction to scale to many events.
nodes.problem: Event-based classification with scalable, efficient representations that preserve fine temporal information.
nodes.approach: Event cloud network with polarity-aware group/sampling modules and frequency-domain feature extraction via Fourier transform.
nodes.niche_reason: Event-camera classification is a specialised niche within vision.

nodes.title: MV-FGAD: Towards Efficient and Effective Federated Graph Anomaly Detection via Multi-view Learning
nodes.tldr: MV-FGAD detects graph anomalies in federated subgraphs through shared knowledge aggregation, multi-view learning, and Mahalanobis-distance scoring, targeting weak attribute or structural anomalies.
nodes.problem: Federated graph anomaly detection fails on partitioned subgraphs and weak anomalies.
nodes.approach: Federated knowledge module, multi-view anomaly pattern learning, and Mahalanobis-based scoring across views.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated graph anomaly detection is a narrow intersection.

nodes.title: Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control
nodes.tldr: GRAM adds gradient-routed modules during pretraining so ablating a module removes dual-use capabilities at inference, approximating data filtering at lower cost.
nodes.problem: Controlling access to dual-use capabilities without training many separate models.
nodes.approach: Gradient-routed auxiliary modules updated selectively in pretraining, ablated at inference to forget capabilities.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Between AI safety research and unlearning/privacy; judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Pretraining-time modular capability control is an unusual direction.

nodes.title: MetaphorVU: Towards Metaphorical Video Understanding
nodes.tldr: Introduces MetaphorVU-Bench, the first benchmark for metaphorical video understanding, shows MLLMs fail at cross-domain mapping, and proposes a metaphor-knowledge-graph inference-time booster.
nodes.problem: Multimodal LLMs poorly understand metaphorical videos requiring high-order cognition.
nodes.approach: Benchmark plus metaphor knowledge graph providing mapping augmentation at inference.
nodes.confidence_reason: Benchmark of MLLMs on video; split between video and multimodal LLM topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Metaphor comprehension in video is a rare cognitive-level direction.

nodes.title: VectorWorld: Efficient Streaming World Model via Diffusion Flow on Vector Graphs
nodes.tldr: Streams ego-centric vector-graph tiles to build a real-time driving world model, with a gated VAE, MeanFlow-based generator and physics-aligned NPC policy.
nodes.problem: Generative driving world models fail at history-compatible starts, real-time latency and kinematic feasibility
nodes.approach: Streaming vector-graph generation with interval-conditioned MeanFlow and differentiable kinematic shaping
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Driving world models are active; vector-graph streaming is specialised

nodes.title: PonderLM-2: Pretraining LLM with Latent Thoughts in Continuous Space
nodes.tldr: Pretrains LMs to emit a continuous latent thought (last hidden state) before each token, so a 1.4B model beats a 2.8B baseline at equal cost.
nodes.problem: Scaling per-token computation during pretraining to improve next-token prediction without more parameters.
nodes.approach: Feed the last hidden state back as an extra latent-thought input step before predicting each token.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-reasoning pretraining is an active but specialised direction.

nodes.title: DAVE: Distribution-Aware Attribution via ViT Gradient Decomposition
nodes.tldr: Gives stable, pixel-level attribution maps for Vision Transformers by decomposing the input gradient to suppress patch-embedding and attention-induced artifacts.
nodes.problem: ViT attribution maps show structured artifacts from patch embeddings and attention routing.
nodes.approach: Structured decomposition of the input gradient that isolates locally equivariant, stable components.
nodes.niche_reason: ViT attribution is specialised within interpretability.

nodes.title: Why Linear Recurrent Memory Works in Partially Observable Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Theoretically justifies linear recurrent memory in partially observable RL by constructing linear filters that reproduce HMM belief logits or decode states.
nodes.problem: Why linear recurrent memory units work well in partially observable RL remains theoretically unexplained.
nodes.approach: Constructs two linear filters: one matching HMM belief logits, one with vanishing state-decoding error.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.confidence_reason: Recurrent memory theory straddles RL theory and sequence architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Linear recurrent memory theory for partially observable RL is rare

nodes.title: Self-Soupervision: Cooking Model Soups without Labels
nodes.tldr: Generalizes model soups to self-supervised learning, mixing fine-tuned SSL ingredients trained on unlabeled shifted or corrupted data to boost robustness.
nodes.problem: Model soups require labeled data, limiting their use for robustness under unlabeled distribution shift.
nodes.approach: Self-Souping: fine-tune SSL ingredients with differing algorithms and hyperparameters on new data, then average their weights.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Model soups generalized to self-supervised learning is an unusual combination.

nodes.title: Do We Need Adam? Surprisingly Strong and Sparse Reinforcement Learning with SGD in LLMs
nodes.tldr: Finds plain SGD matches or beats AdamW for LLM RL fine-tuning, updating under 0.02% of weights, so RL needs little adaptive optimization.
nodes.problem: RL post-training of LLMs inherits AdamW from SFT, despite its high memory cost.
nodes.approach: Empirical and analytical comparison of SGD and AdamW in RLVR, with update-sparsity analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RLVR for LLMs is a very crowded area

nodes.title: Motion Attribution for Video Generation
nodes.tldr: Motive is a gradient-based data attribution framework isolating motion from appearance to find fine-tuning clips affecting temporal dynamics and curate data for better video generation.
nodes.problem: The influence of training data on motion in video generation models is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Gradient-based influence with motion-weighted loss masks to attribute motion, then curate fine-tuning data.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Data attribution for video generation motion is a rare combination.

nodes.title: Stop When Further Reasoning Won’t Help: Attention-State Adaptive Generation in Reasoning Models
nodes.tldr: Training-free method that infers reasoning state from attention distributions to stop overthinking early in large reasoning models, cutting tokens by nearly 40% on Qwen3-8B.
nodes.problem: Large reasoning models overthink, producing redundant tokens and lower accuracy; existing fixes need training or unreliable signals.
nodes.approach: An attention-distribution signal infers reasoning state and adaptively adjusts generation; plug-and-play, no training.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Early stopping for reasoning models is a common efficiency direction

nodes.title: What You Think is What You See: Driving Exploration in VLM Agents via Visual-Linguistic Curiosity
nodes.tldr: GLANCE drives exploration in VLM agents using the discrepancy between the agent's linguistic world-model prediction and visual representations from a target network as an intrinsic curiosity reward.
nodes.problem: VLM agents trained with RL on sparse-reward visual tasks lack an epistemic drive to explore.
nodes.approach: Ground linguistic predictions into target-network visual features; use the prediction discrepancy as curiosity reward in RL.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Curiosity for VLM agentic RL is a new but active niche.

nodes.title: Initialization is Half the Battle: Generating Diverse Images from a Guidance Potential Posterior
nodes.tldr: Improves diffusion and flow-matching diversity by optimizing the initial noise with Langevin dynamics toward guidance-potential regions, complementary to trajectory methods.
nodes.problem: Generative models suffer mode collapse because Gaussian initialization ignores the guidance potential landscape.
nodes.approach: Samples initial noise from a guidance potential posterior via Langevin dynamics (Diversity-inducing Initialization).
nodes.niche_reason: Diversity via initialization is an active but crowded sampling direction

nodes.title: Diffusion Flow Matching: Dimension-Improved KL Bounds and Wasserstein Guarantees
nodes.tldr: Proves tighter KL and 2-Wasserstein convergence bounds for Brownian-motion diffusion flow matching, with improved dimension dependence under minimal assumptions.
nodes.problem: Understanding discretization-error convergence guarantees of diffusion flow matching generative models.
nodes.approach: Refined theoretical analysis under KL and Wasserstein metrics with finite-moment and score integrability assumptions.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of diffusion sampling is active but specialised.

nodes.title: MSP: Probabilistically Consistent Multi-Scale Action Generation
nodes.tldr: Generates robot action sequences coarse-to-fine in a continuous latent space, with cross-scale probabilistic consistency via autoregressive semantic conditions and a MeanFlow decoder.
nodes.problem: Coarse-to-fine action generation loses cross-scale consistency, so local errors accumulate in long-horizon tasks
nodes.approach: Downsampled continuous latent multi-scale design; scale-wise autoregressive Transformer conditions a lightweight MeanFlow model
nodes.niche_reason: Coarse-to-fine action generation is becoming common in robotics

nodes.title: Martingale Posterior Neural Processes
nodes.tldr: Neural processes that use martingale posteriors, specifying a predictive distribution for future data, as the source of uncertainty instead of latent variables.
nodes.problem: Neural processes restrict uncertainty to finite-dimensional latent variables, limiting expressiveness.
nodes.approach: Equip a neural process with an implicit predictive distribution and use martingale posterior for uncertainty.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Martingale posteriors in neural processes are a rare Bayesian angle.

nodes.title: Formal Mathematics Statement Curriculum Learning
nodes.tldr: Expert iteration interleaving proof search with language-model training automatically builds a curriculum and surpasses prior state of the art on miniF2F.
nodes.problem: Training provers on formal statements needs ground-truth proofs and difficulty-matched curricula.
nodes.approach: Expert iteration: proof search interleaved with language-model learning over formal statement sets.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.confidence_reason: Expert iteration for theorem proving sits between reasoning and RL for LLMs.
nodes.niche_reason: Expert iteration for theorem proving is specialised.

nodes.title: Localized Randomized Smoothing for Collective Robustness Certification
nodes.tldr: Provides collective robustness certificates for structured outputs by scaling smoothing noise per input region by its importance to outputs.
nodes.problem: Certifying many joint predictions from one shared perturbed input is limited to local models.
nodes.approach: Localized randomized smoothing with region-dependent perturbation strength.
nodes.niche_reason: Collective certification for structured outputs is rare

nodes.title: Scaling Up Probabilistic Circuits by Latent Variable Distillation
nodes.tldr: Scales probabilistic circuits by distilling latent-variable assignments from Transformer generative models, boosting large PCs on ImageNet and WikiText-2.
nodes.problem: Large probabilistic circuits plateau in performance, suggesting existing optimizers fail to use their capacity.
nodes.approach: Transformer-based deep generative models supply extra supervision over PC latent variables during optimization.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Probabilistic circuits fit between Bayesian methods and generative models.
nodes.niche_reason: Scaling tractable probabilistic circuits via distillation is rare.

nodes.title: Corrupted Image Modeling for Self-Supervised Visual Pre-Training
nodes.tldr: CIM corrupts images by replacing patches with samples from a small BEiT generator and trains an enhancer to recover pixels or detect replacements, working for both ViT and CNN.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised visual pre-training that avoids artificial mask tokens and works across architectures.
nodes.approach: Jointly trained generator corrupting patches and enhancer performing pixel recovery or replaced-token detection.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Another masked-image-modeling-style pre-training variant.

nodes.title: Targeted Hyperparameter Optimization with Lexicographic Preferences Over Multiple Objectives
nodes.tldr: Formulates hyperparameter optimization with lexicographic preferences over multiple objectives and proposes LexiFlow, a randomized directed search that performs well empirically.
nodes.problem: Practitioners need to state multi-objective hyperparameter goals with a clear priority ordering.
nodes.approach: Lexicographic-preference formulation solved by LexiFlow, a randomized directed search.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised preference-based HPO

nodes.title: Capturing the Motion of Every Joint: 3D Human Pose and Shape Estimation with Independent Tokens
nodes.tldr: Estimates 3D human pose and shape from video with a transformer using independent joint-rotation, shape and camera tokens plus joint-level temporal modeling.
nodes.problem: Accurate monocular 3D human pose and shape estimation with local temporal consistency.
nodes.approach: Independent learnable tokens interacting with image features, then per-joint temporal modeling.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Human mesh recovery is a common vision topic.

nodes.title: MeshDiffusion: Score-based Generative 3D Mesh Modeling
nodes.tldr: MeshDiffusion trains a diffusion model on deformable tetrahedral grid parameterizations to generate 3D meshes with fine geometric detail.
nodes.problem: Scalable 3D mesh generation relies on sub-optimal post-processing, giving smooth or noisy surfaces.
nodes.approach: Represent meshes as deformable tetrahedral grids and train a score-based diffusion model directly on that parameterization.
nodes.niche_reason: Direct 3D mesh diffusion is established but specialised.

nodes.title: What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
nodes.tldr: Argues transformers in-context learn by implicitly running standard estimators like gradient descent and ridge regression, shown by construction and probing trained linear-regression models.
nodes.problem: Unclear what algorithm transformers implement when doing in-context learning.
nodes.approach: Constructive proofs plus probing of trained linear-regression in-context learners against closed-form estimators.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic analysis of in-context learning is specialised

nodes.title: View Synthesis with Sculpted Neural Points
nodes.tldr: Point-based view synthesis with sculpted neural points that beats NeRF visual quality while rendering about 100 times faster.
nodes.problem: Novel view synthesis from images is slow with implicit neural representations like NeRF.
nodes.approach: Differentiable point-based rendering with robust sculpted point features and spherical-harmonic view-dependence.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Point-based rendering is a known alternative to NeRF

nodes.title: STREET: A MULTI-TASK STRUCTURED REASONING AND EXPLANATION BENCHMARK
nodes.tldr: Introduces STREET, a multi-task, multi-domain benchmark where models answer questions and also produce step-by-step structured explanations; tested models lag human performance.
nodes.problem: QA benchmarks rarely check whether models produce valid, step-by-step reasoning explanations.
nodes.approach: Unified multi-task benchmark requiring structured premise-to-conclusion explanations, evaluated with few-shot and fine-tuned models.
nodes.niche_reason: Natural-language reasoning and explanation benchmarks are common.

nodes.title: DaxBench: Benchmarking Deformable Object Manipulation with Differentiable Physics
nodes.tldr: DaXBench is a JAX-based differentiable simulator and benchmark for deformable object manipulation covering fluids, ropes and cloth, usable with planning, imitation and RL methods.
nodes.problem: No general benchmark exists for evaluating diverse deformable object manipulation methods.
nodes.approach: Differentiable deformable-object simulation in JAX with Gym-style tasks across fluid, rope and cloth.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised differentiable-simulation benchmark for deformables.

nodes.title: Learning Fair Graph Representations via Automated Data Augmentations
nodes.tldr: Learns fairness-aware graph augmentations automatically from data, producing fair graph representations with a better fairness-accuracy trade-off on node classification.
nodes.problem: Hand-designed graph augmentations assume fairness properties that vary across datasets.
nodes.approach: Learned graph data augmentations that remove sensitive information while keeping useful signal.
nodes.niche_reason: Fair graph learning is specialised, with a learned-augmentation angle

nodes.title: Unsupervised Semantic Segmentation with Self-supervised Object-centric Representations
nodes.tldr: Shows self-supervised object-centric features plus saliency masks and clustering yield a strong unsupervised semantic segmentation baseline on VOC and COCO.
nodes.problem: Segmenting objects and scenes into semantic classes without any human labels.
nodes.approach: Saliency-based object discovery, self-supervised feature clustering, then pseudo-label training.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Active area of unsupervised segmentation with many similar papers

nodes.title: gDDIM: Generalized denoising diffusion implicit models
nodes.tldr: Extends DDIM's fast deterministic sampling from isotropic to general diffusion models, achieving strong FID with 27 to 50 score evaluations.
nodes.problem: DDIM's fast sampling only works for isotropic diffusion, and non-isotropic models lack it.
nodes.approach: Reinterprets DDIM as approximate score solving, then parameterizes the score network for non-isotropic diffusions.
nodes.niche_reason: Fast diffusion sampling is crowded; non-isotropic extension is a twist

nodes.title: STaSy: Score-based Tabular data Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Score-based generative model for tabular data synthesis with self-paced training and fine-tuning that improves sample quality and diversity.
nodes.problem: Tabular data synthesis struggles with the complexity of real-world tabular distributions.
nodes.approach: Score-based generative modeling with self-paced learning and a fine-tuning strategy for denoising score matching.
nodes.niche_reason: Score-based generation applied to tabular data is a fairly specialised direction.

nodes.title: Data Continuity Matters: Improving Sequence Modeling with Lipschitz Regularizer
nodes.tldr: Shows sequence models prefer different data continuity and adds a Lipschitz regularizer that adjusts input continuity to each model, improving many deep sequence models.
nodes.problem: Sequence models differ in the data continuity they prefer, and this property is rarely considered.
nodes.approach: Lipschitz regularizer that adjusts data continuity toward each model's preferred continuity at little extra cost.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Data-continuity regularization for sequence models is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: MocoSFL: enabling cross-client collaborative self-supervised learning
nodes.tldr: MocoSFL combines split federated learning with MoCo to enable cross-client self-supervised training on lightweight devices, with a privacy-resistance module.
nodes.problem: Collaborative self-supervised learning is too costly and data-hungry for many small-data clients.
nodes.approach: Split the backbone between client and server, with vector concatenation, feature sharing, and frequent synchronization.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated self-supervised learning on edge devices is specialised.

nodes.title: Exploring Active 3D Object Detection from a Generalization Perspective
nodes.tldr: CRB selects LiDAR point clouds for annotation using label conciseness, feature representativeness, and geometric balance, reaching full-supervision performance with 1% of boxes.
nodes.problem: Uncertainty and diversity active learning fail for 3D detection because they ignore annotation cost per box.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical filtering of redundant labels, latent features, and geometry, then greedy selection of informative clouds.
