secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.confidence_reason: Active learning is not in vocab; placed under LiDAR point-cloud detection
nodes.niche_reason: Active learning for 3D detection is established but specialised

nodes.title: HiViT: A Simpler and More Efficient Design of Hierarchical Vision Transformer
nodes.tldr: Simplifies Swin into HiViT, a hierarchical ViT using hierarchical patch embedding and no shifted windows, that is more efficient and accurate.
nodes.problem: Whether plain or hierarchical vision transformers are better, especially for masked image modeling.
nodes.approach: Ablates ViT versus Swin, keeping depth, relative position encoding, and hierarchical patch embedding.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: vision transformer architecture design is mainstream

nodes.title: Near-optimal Policy Identification in Active Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: AE-LSVI is a kernelized least-squares value iteration with optimism and pessimism for active exploration, provably identifying near-optimal policies uniformly over the state space with a generative model.
nodes.problem: Best policy identification uniformly over states when transitions can be queried at chosen states.
nodes.approach: Kernelized LSVI combining optimism and pessimism for active exploration with sample complexity guarantees.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Active RL with kernel value iteration and Bayesian optimization link is rare.

nodes.title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Selection-Inference alternates LLM-driven selection of facts and inference steps to produce interpretable multi-step logical reasoning traces, greatly improving few-shot performance.
nodes.problem: LLMs struggle to chain multiple reasoning steps in logical reasoning tasks.
nodes.approach: Alternate selection and inference modules built from a frozen pretrained LLM with few-shot prompting.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: LLM reasoning via prompting is very common.

nodes.title: Single-shot General Hyper-parameter Optimization for Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: FLoRA performs single-shot federated hyperparameter optimization by aggregating loss surfaces, so one good configuration can drive a single FL training run.
nodes.problem: Federated hyperparameter tuning normally needs many costly FL runs, and it is hard to do for arbitrary models.
nodes.approach: Federated loss-surface aggregation with a single hyperparameter choice, plus an optimality-gap analysis under heterogeneous data.
nodes.niche_reason: Single-shot federated HPO is a specialised tuning niche.

nodes.title: Differentially Private $L_2$-Heavy Hitters in the Sliding Window Model
nodes.tldr: First differentially private algorithm for L2-heavy hitters in the sliding window streaming model, handling sub-additive norm and high-sensitivity smooth histograms.
nodes.problem: Privately releasing L2-heavy hitters over only the most recent W stream items.
nodes.approach: Run many L2-heavy hitter instances with low thresholds plus frequency tracking, adding noise via smooth sensitivity.
nodes.niche_reason: Private streaming algorithms are a rare theory subarea.

nodes.title: Seeing Differently, Acting Similarly: Heterogeneously Observable Imitation Learning
nodes.tldr: Enables imitation when expert demonstrations use different observations than the learner, reweighting demonstrations via importance weighting and rejection learning.
nodes.problem: Imitation with limited coexistence of expert and learner observation spaces, causing dynamics and support mismatch
nodes.approach: Importance weighting with learning-with-rejection (IWRE) to handle dynamics and support mismatch
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Imitation topic fits robotics area, but experiments are Atari
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised imitation setting with heterogeneous observations

nodes.title: No Reason for No Supervision: Improved Generalization in Supervised Models
nodes.tldr: Supervised training with multi-scale crops, an expendable projector, and class prototypes from a memory bank improves transfer learning while matching ImageNet accuracy.
nodes.problem: Supervised ImageNet models trade off training-task accuracy against transferability to future tasks.
nodes.approach: Multi-scale crop augmentation, expendable projector head controlling the trade-off, and class prototypes computed with a memory bank.
nodes.niche_reason: Improving supervised pretraining transfer is a common topic.

nodes.title: Benchmarking Offline Reinforcement Learning on Real-Robot Hardware
nodes.tldr: Proposes a benchmark with large datasets from the TriFinger dexterous platform and real-robot execution to evaluate offline RL algorithms on real hardware.
nodes.problem: Offline RL lacks benchmarks for real-world dexterous manipulation with real-robot evaluation.
nodes.approach: Collect large datasets from simulation-trained agents on two tasks, offer real-robot and simulator evaluation, benchmark open-source offline RL methods.
nodes.niche_reason: Real-robot offline RL benchmarks are specialised and uncommon.

nodes.title: DiffEdit: Diffusion-based semantic image editing with mask guidance
nodes.tldr: DiffEdit infers an edit mask by contrasting diffusion predictions under different text prompts, then edits with latent inference to preserve the rest of the image.
nodes.problem: Text-driven semantic image editing without requiring user-supplied masks.
nodes.approach: Mask from differing noise predictions of two prompts, combined with DDIM latent inversion and mask-guided denoising.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based image editing is a very crowded area.

nodes.title: Offline Q-learning on Diverse Multi-Task Data Both Scales And Generalizes
nodes.tldr: Shows offline Q-learning with ResNets, distributional backups, and feature normalization scales with model capacity, training one policy on 40 Atari games.
nodes.problem: Offline RL was thought to struggle to scale model capacity on large, heterogeneous datasets.
nodes.approach: Re-examined design choices: ResNets, cross-entropy distributional backups, feature normalization.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL scaling studies are specialised.

nodes.title: Few-Shot Domain Adaptation For End-to-End Communication
nodes.tldr: Adapts a trained communication autoencoder to a shifted wireless channel using few labeled samples, via affine transforms on a Gaussian mixture density network.
nodes.problem: Retraining end-to-end autoencoders for changing wireless channels is slow and data-hungry.
nodes.approach: Regularized affine adaptation of the MDN channel model plus decoder-input compensation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot adaptation of wireless autoencoders is rare.

nodes.title: Dirichlet-based Uncertainty Calibration for Active Domain Adaptation
nodes.tldr: Selects informative target-domain samples for annotation using Dirichlet-based predictive distributions that calibrate uncertainty under distribution shift.
nodes.problem: Active domain adaptation relies on deterministic models whose uncertainty is miscalibrated under shift.
nodes.approach: Dirichlet prior over predictions with two-round selection by uncertainty origin, balancing representativeness and discriminability.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: active domain adaptation is specialised but established

nodes.title: SketchKnitter: Vectorized Sketch Generation with Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Generates vector sketches by diffusion-based denoising of stroke points, with an RNN recognizability score guiding sampling and shortcut steps.
nodes.problem: Generating recognizable vector sketches from stroke points lacks a recognizability signal during diffusion sampling.
nodes.approach: Diffusion over stroke-point positions and pen states, with recognizability scores from an auxiliary RNN classifier.
nodes.niche_reason: Stroke-level diffusion for vector sketches is an unusual formulation

nodes.title: ACMP: Allen-Cahn Message Passing with Attractive and Repulsive Forces for Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Allen-Cahn message passing treats node features as interacting particles with attractive, repulsive and Allen-Cahn forces, enabling GNNs over one hundred layers deep.
nodes.problem: Deep GNNs suffer oversmoothing, collapsing node features as depth grows.
nodes.approach: Reaction-diffusion particle dynamics solved numerically as message passing, with a provable Dirichlet energy lower bound.
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-inspired reaction-diffusion GNN is established but specialised.

nodes.title: The Role of ImageNet Classes in Fréchet Inception Distance
nodes.tldr: Shows FID's feature space is so close to ImageNet classes that matching class histograms can lower FID without improving image quality.
nodes.problem: FID is the main generative metric but sometimes disagrees with human judgement.
nodes.approach: Analysis of ImageNet classifier histograms and FID manipulation experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Metric analysis for generative models is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Inequality phenomenon in $l_{\infty}$-adversarial training, and its unrealized threats
nodes.tldr: Finds that l-infinity adversarial training makes predictions depend on few features, so perturbing them breaks the model; simple attacks exploit this.
nodes.problem: Adversarially trained models may rely on a few dominant features, a hidden reliability risk
nodes.approach: Empirical analysis of feature inequality, plus perturbation and occlusion attacks on important features
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial training is crowded; feature-inequality angle is less common

nodes.title: Embedding Fourier for Ultra-High-Definition Low-Light Image Enhancement
nodes.tldr: Embeds Fourier transforms in a cascaded network to enhance amplitude and phase of UHD low-light images separately, avoiding noise amplification.
nodes.problem: Joint luminance enhancement and noise removal for ultra-high-definition low-light images is hard and costly.
nodes.approach: Fourier-domain amplitude and phase processed separately at low resolution, then scaled to high resolution cheaply.
nodes.niche_reason: Common low-light enhancement area with a Fourier-domain twist

nodes.title: LMC: Fast Training of GNNs via Subgraph Sampling with Provable Convergence
nodes.tldr: LMC compensates messages discarded in subgraph-sampling GNN training in forward and backward passes, giving accurate gradients and the first provable convergence guarantee.
nodes.problem: Subgraph-wise sampling for GNN training loses messages, harming gradient accuracy and lacking convergence guarantees.
nodes.approach: Local Message Compensation retrieves discarded messages in forward and backward passes via message-passing formulation of backprop.
nodes.niche_reason: Scalable GNN training is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning to Estimate Shapley Values with Vision Transformers
nodes.tldr: Trains a separate explainer model to amortize Shapley value estimation for vision transformers, using attention masking, giving more accurate explanations than rollout, GradCAM or LRP.
nodes.problem: Shapley value explanations for vision transformers are too computationally expensive to be practical.
nodes.approach: Evaluate ViTs on masked patches with attention masking, and train an amortized explainer network to output Shapley values.
nodes.niche_reason: Shapley explanation for ViTs is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning a Data-Driven Policy Network for Pre-Training Automated Feature Engineering
nodes.tldr: FETCH pretrains a feature-engineering policy network on a dataset-conditioned MDP, so it transfers to unseen tabular datasets without new exploration.
nodes.problem: NAS-style automated feature engineering does not generalize across datasets and is computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Data-driven MDP using the tabular dataset as state, with feature generation and selection policy pretraining.
nodes.confidence_reason: Tabular AutoML: feature engineering vs AutoML topic is close
nodes.niche_reason: Pretrained feature-engineering policies are a specialised AutoML niche.

nodes.title: Neuroevolution is a Competitive Alternative to Reinforcement Learning for Skill Discovery
nodes.tldr: Shows quality-diversity neuroevolution matches or beats information-theoretic RL for skill discovery, and is less hyperparameter-sensitive.
nodes.problem: RL-trained skill diversity needs careful hyperparameter tuning, and skills overfit to their training tasks.
nodes.approach: Compares eight state-of-the-art skill-discovery algorithms on skill diversity, adaptation, and hierarchical planning performance.
nodes.niche_reason: neuroevolution for skill discovery, less common than RL

nodes.title: A Kernel Perspective of Skip Connections in Convolutional Networks
nodes.tldr: Derives Gaussian process and neural tangent kernels of residual convolutional networks, showing similar spectral decay with skip connections but stronger locality and better condition numbers.
nodes.problem: Theoretical effects of skip connections in over-parameterized convolutional ResNets are not well understood.
nodes.approach: Explicit kernel formulas, spectral analysis, and condition number bounds for residual versus non-residual convolutional kernels.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: NTK analysis of architectures is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Multifactor Sequential Disentanglement via Structured Koopman Autoencoders
nodes.tldr: Disentangles sequential data into more than two factors by assuming linear latent dynamics and a spectral loss for structured Koopman matrices.
nodes.problem: Sequential disentanglement usually yields only two factors, static and dynamic, not multiple semantic components.
nodes.approach: Koopman autoencoder with a spectral loss that structures the Koopman matrix, enabling unsupervised multifactor disentanglement.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Sequence modality and data type unclear from abstract.
nodes.niche_reason: multifactor Koopman disentanglement is uncommon

nodes.title: Implicit Bias of Large Depth Networks: a Notion of Rank for Nonlinear Functions
nodes.tldr: Shows deep homogeneous networks' implicit bias converges to a notion of rank for nonlinear functions, and when global minima recover the true data rank.
nodes.problem: Which notion of rank deep networks implicitly use, and whether training recovers the data's true rank.
nodes.approach: Analyzes the representation cost of fully connected homogeneous networks as depth grows to infinity.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Nonlinear rank via representation cost is an unusual theory angle

nodes.title: Planning Goals for Exploration
nodes.tldr: PEG plans exploratory goal commands with learned world models so an exploration policy starts from high-potential states during goal-conditioned training.
nodes.problem: Goal-conditioned agents in unknown environments explore inefficiently when training goals are chosen naively.
nodes.approach: Optimise an intrinsic exploration reward by sampling-based planning over goal commands in learned world models.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Planning exploratory goals with world models is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: Neural Networks Efficiently Learn Low-Dimensional Representations with SGD
nodes.tldr: Proves SGD-trained two-layer networks learn the principal subspace of multiple-index targets, yielding width-independent generalization and low-rank weights.
nodes.problem: Explaining why gradient-trained networks beat kernel methods on low-dimensional targets.
nodes.approach: Analyzes online SGD with weight decay to show first-layer weights converge to the target subspace.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Feature learning theory for two-layer networks is established but specialised

nodes.title: MEDFAIR: Benchmarking Fairness for Medical Imaging
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks fairness of medical imaging models across eleven bias mitigation methods, ten datasets, and three model selection criteria.
nodes.problem: Fairness methods in medical imaging are hard to compare due to inconsistent settings.
nodes.approach: Unified reproducible framework evaluating methods across datasets, metrics and ID/OOD settings.
nodes.niche_reason: Medical-imaging fairness benchmarking is established but specialised

nodes.title: Subquadratic Algorithms for Kernel Matrices via Kernel Density Estimation
nodes.tldr: Gives subquadratic algorithms for kernel-matrix primitives like top eigenvector, sparsification, and linear solves, using kernel density estimation as a black box.
nodes.problem: Kernel methods need the full n x n kernel matrix, costing quadratic time.
nodes.approach: Reductions from weighted vertex and edge sampling, random walks and importance sampling to KDE queries.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Sublinear sampling via KDE for kernel graphs is a rare algorithmic niche.

nodes.title: Learning Group Importance using the Differentiable Hypergeometric Distribution
nodes.tldr: Introduces a differentiable hypergeometric distribution with reparameterized gradients, letting models learn subset sizes for clustering and weakly supervised learning.
nodes.problem: Learning unknown subset sizes is non-differentiable because hard constraints block gradient-based optimization.
nodes.approach: Hypergeometric distribution over group sizes parameterized by relative group importance, with reparameterizable gradients.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.confidence_reason: judgment call between probabilistic modelling and differentiable layers
nodes.niche_reason: Learning explicit group sizes via a hypergeometric is unusual

nodes.title: Sequential Latent Variable Models for Few-Shot High-Dimensional Time-Series Forecasting
nodes.tldr: Bayesian meta-learning framework for few-shot forecasting of high-dimensional time series, adapting latent dynamics functions from a small support set of series.
nodes.problem: Long-term forecasting of latent dynamics in high-dimensional time series across diverse dynamics with few examples.
nodes.approach: Sequential latent variable models with Bayesian meta-learning conditioning latent dynamics on embedded few-shot support series.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot forecasting with latent-variable meta-learning is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Fast and Precise: Adjusting Planning Horizon with Adaptive Subgoal Search
nodes.tldr: Searches over subgoals at varying distances, verifying reachability cheaply, to adapt the planning horizon to each state's difficulty.
nodes.problem: Hierarchical planners use fixed subgoal horizons, which are inefficient across states of varying difficulty.
nodes.approach: Generates diverse subgoals at multiple distances and filters unreachable ones with a verification mechanism.
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment between hierarchical RL and search-based reasoning.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised: adaptive subgoal horizons for search-based planning.

nodes.title: Encoding Recurrence into Transformers
nodes.tldr: Rewrites an RNN layer as a positional encoding matrix inside self-attention, yielding a gated recurrence-augmented attention module with better sample efficiency than transformers.
nodes.problem: Transformers lack recurrent inductive bias, hurting sample efficiency on sequential tasks.
nodes.approach: Decompose RNNs into recurrence encoding matrices added to attention positional encodings, with a gate mixing recurrent and attention signals.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Hybrid RNN-transformer design is a specialised but known direction.

nodes.title: Certified Training: Small Boxes are All You Need
nodes.tldr: SABR is a certified training method propagating interval bounds over a small, carefully chosen subset of the adversarial region, improving both standard and certified accuracy.
nodes.problem: Certified training suffers from approximation error and a robustness-accuracy trade-off.
nodes.approach: Propagate interval bounds only through small boxes selected around adversarial examples to approximate worst-case loss.
nodes.niche_reason: Certified training is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Universal Few-shot Learning of Dense Prediction Tasks with Visual Token Matching
nodes.tldr: Visual Token Matching is a universal few-shot learner for arbitrary dense prediction tasks, using non-parametric patch-token matching with tiny task-specific adapters.
nodes.problem: Few-shot learning of arbitrary dense prediction tasks beyond semantic segmentation.
nodes.approach: Non-parametric matching of embedded image and label tokens across ViT feature hierarchies.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Universal few-shot dense prediction is a specialised setting

nodes.title: Is Reinforcement Learning (Not) for Natural Language Processing: Benchmarks, Baselines, and Building Blocks for Natural Language Policy Optimization
nodes.tldr: Introduces the RL4LMs library, the GRUE benchmark of reward-supervised generation tasks, and NLPO, an RL algorithm that reduces action space for stable language model alignment.
nodes.problem: RL for aligning language models lacks open libraries and benchmarks and suffers from instability due to combinatorial action spaces.
nodes.approach: Modular RL library, six-task reward-based benchmark, and NLPO with action-space masking compared against PPO.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: RL-based LM alignment is a very active area.

nodes.title: Hebbian Deep Learning Without Feedback
nodes.tldr: Trains deep networks without backpropagation using a multilayer Hebbian soft winner-take-all rule, matching bio-plausible baselines on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.
nodes.problem: Backprop approximations are inefficient and biologically implausible while losing accuracy
nodes.approach: Feedback-free Hebbian learning in soft winner-take-all layers with a linear classifier head
nodes.confidence_reason: Training-rule paper; could also fit neuroscience or representation learning
nodes.niche_reason: Biologically plausible deep learning without feedback is an unusual direction

nodes.title: Combinatorial-Probabilistic Trade-Off: P-Values of Community Properties Test in the Stochastic Block Models
nodes.tldr: Develops a shadowing bootstrap test giving p-values for combinatorial community properties in stochastic block models, with a combinatorial-probabilistic trade-off and matching lower bound.
nodes.problem: Testing combinatorial community properties of stochastic block models with uncertainty quantification is hard because of the combinatorial nature.
nodes.approach: Shadowing bootstrap exploiting symmetry, with theory on a combinatorial distance and minimax lower bound.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Hypothesis testing for combinatorial SBM properties is a very rare statistical niche.

nodes.title: Learning Soft Constraints From Constrained Expert Demonstrations
nodes.tldr: Recovers cumulative soft constraints from expert demonstrations when the reward is known, by iteratively adjusting constraints until behaviour matches the expert.
nodes.problem: Expert behaviour driven by unknown constraints is hard to explain with reward alone
nodes.approach: Iterative constrained-optimization constraint learning inside an IRL loop with cumulative soft constraints
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Soft-constraint IRL is specialised

nodes.title: Self-supervised learning with rotation-invariant kernels
nodes.tldr: Regularizes SSL embeddings toward uniformity on the hypersphere using MMD with rotation-invariant kernels, matching state of the art with lower time and memory cost.
nodes.problem: Collapse-avoiding regularizers in self-supervised learning are costly for large embedding dimensions
nodes.approach: Kernel mean embedding loss family with rotation-invariant kernels, minimizing MMD to uniform hypersphere distribution
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Kernel-based uniformity regularizers are a specialised SSL niche

nodes.title: Distilling Model Failures as Directions in Latent Space
nodes.tldr: Automatically distills model failure modes as directions in a latent space via linear classifiers, enabling captioning of hard subpopulations, dataset debugging, and targeted fixes.
nodes.problem: Finding hard subpopulations and spurious correlations usually needs human effort and dataset-specific analysis.
nodes.approach: Train linear classifiers on features to find consistent errors; treat their directions as failure modes and caption them.
nodes.confidence_reason: Between interpretability, evaluation methodology and spurious-correlation debugging.
nodes.niche_reason: Automated failure-mode discovery is specialised.

nodes.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
nodes.tldr: Fully reverse-engineers small transformers on modular addition, discovering a Fourier-based algorithm, and uses it to define continuous progress measures that precede grokking.
nodes.problem: Understanding emergent behaviors like grokking requires continuous progress measures underlying seemingly discontinuous changes.
nodes.approach: Mechanistic reverse engineering of learned circuits, ablation validation, and progress measures derived from the circuit components.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic interpretability of grokking is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Disentanglement with Biological Constraints: A Theory of Functional Cell Types
nodes.tldr: Proves nonnegativity and energy-efficiency constraints on neuron activity and weights produce disentangled, single-factor selective neurons, explaining functional cell types like grid and object-vector cells.
nodes.problem: Why biological neurons become selective for single task factors, and when representations entangle.
nodes.approach: Mathematical proofs of disentanglement under nonnegativity and energy constraints, validated across tasks and VAEs.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory linking biological constraints to disentanglement is uncommon.

nodes.title: NeRN: Learning Neural Representations for Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Represents a pretrained CNN's weights with a coordinate-based neural network, using smoothness and distillation to reconstruct them accurately.
nodes.problem: Compactly representing trained neural network weights while preserving accuracy.
nodes.approach: Coordinate-indexed predictor network regularized by smoothness and knowledge distillation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.confidence_reason: Compression vs neural-field framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Neural-representation of network weights is a rare direction

nodes.title: SMART: Self-supervised Multi-task pretrAining with contRol Transformers
nodes.tldr: SMART pretrains a Control Transformer with a control-centric self-supervised objective for multi-task sequential decision making, transferring to unseen tasks via imitation and RL.
nodes.problem: Pretraining representations for sequential decision making across many tasks with high-dimensional perception is difficult.
nodes.approach: Control Transformer with control-centric self-supervised pretraining, then finetuning for IL and RL.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Pretraining for control is a fairly common direction.

nodes.title: Hidden Markov Transformer for Simultaneous Machine Translation
nodes.tldr: HMT treats translation start moments as hidden states of a hidden Markov model and trains by maximizing marginal likelihood over them, improving simultaneous translation.
nodes.problem: Simultaneous translation must learn when to start each target token, and those moments are unobserved.
nodes.approach: Hidden Markov Transformer marginalizes over candidate starting moments during training.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: No clean NLP topic for simultaneous MT; latent-variable fit is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-moment SiMT modelling is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Powderworld: A Platform for Understanding Generalization via Rich Task Distributions
nodes.tldr: Presents Powderworld, a lightweight GPU simulator with diverse task distributions for studying generalization in world models and reinforcement learning.
nodes.problem: Generalization research lacks a fast, expressive environment with rich task distributions
nodes.approach: GPU-native simulation environment with hand-designed world-model and RL task distributions
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: GPU-native simulation platform for task generalization is unusual

nodes.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling
nodes.tldr: S5 replaces S4's many single-input SSMs with one multi-input multi-output state space layer using parallel scans, matching efficiency and reaching 87.4% on Long Range Arena.
nodes.problem: S4 layers use many independent SISO state space models and complex machinery for long-range sequence modeling.
nodes.approach: One MIMO linear SSM with parallel scan, with initialization and parameterization derived from its connection to S4.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: State space sequence models are a popular, active area.

nodes.title: NTFields: Neural Time Fields for Physics-Informed Robot Motion Planning
nodes.tldr: Neural field solving the Eikonal PDE gives arrival-time fields for robot motion planning in cluttered 3D scenes, without expert data.
nodes.problem: Neural motion planners need expert data, while grid-based Eikonal planners suffer the curse of dimensionality.
nodes.approach: Physics-informed neural field trained on the Eikonal equation, outputting continuous arrival times for path solutions.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural Eikonal planners are a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Continuous PDE Dynamics Forecasting with Implicit Neural Representations
nodes.tldr: DINo forecasts PDE dynamics with implicit neural representations and a learned latent ODE, extrapolating to arbitrary space-time locations and grids.
nodes.problem: Neural PDE forecasters depend on fixed spatial and temporal discretizations and cannot generalize across grids.
nodes.approach: Encode spatial observations as implicit neural representations in a small latent space whose dynamics follow a learned ODE.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: continuous-discretization PDE forecasting.

nodes.title: GRACE-C: Generalized Rate Agnostic Causal Estimation via Constraints
nodes.tldr: GRACE-C uses constraint programming and structural insights to learn causal graphs from time series with unknown causal-versus-measurement timescale mismatch, scaling beyond 100 variables.
nodes.problem: Causal structure learning from time series is misleading when causal and measurement timescales differ unknown.
nodes.approach: Constraint programming with problem-structure theory and prior knowledge for rate-agnostic causal estimation.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Rate-agnostic causal discovery is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Multi-lingual Evaluation of Code Generation Models
nodes.tldr: MBXP and Multilingual HumanEval benchmarks translate MBPP and HumanEval into over 10 programming languages to evaluate multilingual code generation models.
nodes.problem: Code generation evaluation covers mostly Python, leaving multilingual and out-of-domain language ability unmeasured.
nodes.approach: Automatic transpilation of prompts and tests into target languages, plus bootstrapped synthetic solutions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: code benchmarks are a common evaluation direction

nodes.title: DEP-RL: Embodied Exploration for Reinforcement Learning in Overactuated and Musculoskeletal Systems
nodes.tldr: Uses differential extrinsic plasticity to drive state-covering exploration, enabling fast RL for overactuated musculoskeletal reaching and locomotion.
nodes.problem: Ineffective exploration in large overactuated action spaces hampers RL on musculoskeletal models.
nodes.approach: Integrates differential extrinsic plasticity, a self-organization method, into RL as an exploration strategy.
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual bridge of self-organization and musculoskeletal RL

nodes.title: Neural Episodic Control with State Abstraction
nodes.tldr: Improves episodic control in deep RL using state abstraction, richer episodic memory and multi-step analysis, gaining sample efficiency on MuJoCo and Atari.
nodes.problem: Episodic control methods underuse historical state transitions and scale poorly during DRL training.
nodes.approach: State abstraction builds comprehensive episodic memory with a novel state evaluation and multi-step state analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Episodic control for sample efficiency is a common approach

nodes.title: Hungry Hungry Hippos: Towards Language Modeling with State Space Models
nodes.tldr: Designs H3, a state-space layer that matches attention on recall and comparison tasks, plus FlashConv for faster SSM training and inference.
nodes.problem: State space models underperform attention on language modeling and run slowly on hardware.
nodes.approach: Recall and comparison-oriented SSM layer, hybrid SSM-attention models, and fused block FFT convolution.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: SSMs for language are a popular, crowded direction.

nodes.title: Win: Weight-Decay-Integrated Nesterov Acceleration for Adaptive Gradient Algorithms
nodes.tldr: Win integrates weight decay with Nesterov-style two-step updates to accelerate AdamW, Adam, LAMB and SGD, with proven convergence advantages.
nodes.problem: Adaptive optimizers converge slowly when training deep networks on large-scale datasets.
nodes.approach: Conservative and reckless Taylor-based steps on a proximal-regularized loss, linearly combined.
nodes.niche_reason: Optimizer acceleration is a crowded mainstream direction.

nodes.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
nodes.tldr: Aligns hidden units across independently trained networks by permutation symmetry, showing merged models lie in a near-convex basin with zero-barrier linear connectivity.
nodes.problem: Whether independently trained neural networks can be merged in weight space despite permutation symmetry of hidden units.
nodes.approach: Three algorithms permute one model's units to match a reference, producing functionally equivalent weights that can be averaged.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Model merging via permutation symmetry straddles loss-landscape theory and training.
nodes.niche_reason: Model merging and linear mode connectivity are active, well-studied topics.

nodes.title: MPCFORMER: FAST, PERFORMANT AND PRIVATE TRANSFORMER INFERENCE WITH MPC
nodes.tldr: Uses knowledge distillation to make transformers fast and accurate under secure multi-party computation, cutting private-inference latency with similar accuracy.
nodes.problem: Private transformer inference with MPC increases latency by over 60x or hurts quality.
nodes.approach: Knowledge distillation of transformers into MPC-friendly architectures.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised cryptographic inference, distinct from mainstream LLM efficiency

nodes.title: Guiding Energy-based Models via Contrastive Latent Variables
nodes.tldr: Uses contrastive representation learning as a latent variable to guide and stabilize energy-based model training, lowering FID with faster training.
nodes.problem: Energy-based models are hard to train and lag GANs and diffusion in generation quality
nodes.approach: Joint training of an EBM with a contrastive latent variable via a latent-variable EBM formulation.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.confidence_reason: EBMs lack a dedicated topic; closest is latent-variable generative models
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-variable EBM training is specialised within generative modelling

nodes.title: FluidLab: A Differentiable Environment for Benchmarking Complex Fluid Manipulation
nodes.tldr: FluidLab is a differentiable simulation benchmark for complex fluid manipulation tasks, with GPU physics engine, RL and trajectory optimization baselines, and sim-to-real tests.
nodes.problem: Robot fluid manipulation lacks platforms covering complex materials and multi-fluid interactions.
nodes.approach: Differentiable GPU fluid simulator FluidEngine with tasks and domain-specific optimization schemes.
nodes.niche_reason: Complex fluid manipulation in differentiable simulation is very rare.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Reconstruction for Operator Learning of PDEs with Discontinuities
nodes.tldr: Proves linear-reconstruction operator learning methods like DeepONet fail on PDEs with discontinuous solutions, while nonlinear reconstruction methods such as FNO and shift-DeepONet overcome these bounds.
nodes.problem: Operator learning for PDEs with discontinuous solutions is poorly understood, particularly approximation limits.
nodes.approach: Lower approximation bounds for linear reconstruction, plus shift-DeepONet and empirical tests on hyperbolic PDEs.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of operator learning for discontinuities is rare.

nodes.title: Learning MLPs on Graphs: A Unified View of Effectiveness, Robustness, and Efficiency
nodes.tldr: NOSMOG distills GNNs into noise-robust, structure-aware MLPs using position features, representational similarity distillation and adversarial feature augmentation, improving effectiveness, robustness and inference efficiency.
nodes.problem: GNN-distilled MLPs are neither effective nor robust: feature-label misalignment, hard matching, and noise sensitivity.
nodes.approach: Add structural position features, similarity-based distillation, and adversarial feature augmentation to MLP students.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: GNN-to-MLP distillation is an established but specialised line.

nodes.title: Visual Recognition with Deep Nearest Centroids
nodes.tldr: Replaces parametric classifier heads with nonparametric nearest-sub-centroid classification on deep embeddings, giving explainable predictions and transfer to pixel recognition.
nodes.problem: Parametric classifiers lack simplicity and explainability for visual recognition.
nodes.approach: Deep nearest sub-centroids classification with learned embeddings and case-based reasoning.
nodes.niche_reason: Nonparametric prototype classifiers are a niche revival.

nodes.title: Neural ePDOs: Spatially Adaptive Equivariant Partial Differential Operator Based Networks
nodes.tldr: Introduces spatially adaptive, translation-equivariant partial differential operator networks whose coefficients come from an equivariant MLP, reaching state of the art on MNIST-rot.
nodes.problem: Linear, spatially shared PDO coefficients limit per-position feature learning in equivariant networks.
nodes.approach: Coefficient matrices generated from local features by an equivariant MLP, with theory for rotation equivariance.
nodes.confidence_reason: Equivariant architecture with no clean topic; classification is the benchmark
nodes.niche_reason: Spatially adaptive equivariant PDO networks are a rare physics-inspired architecture

nodes.title: Dichotomy of Control: Separating What You Can Control from What You Cannot
nodes.tldr: Future-conditioned policy learning that separates controllable actions from environment randomness, so return-conditioning stays consistent in stochastic settings.
nodes.problem: Return-conditioned supervised policies like decision transformer fail in highly stochastic environments.
nodes.approach: Latent future representation with a mutual-information constraint removing environment-only randomness.
nodes.niche_reason: Return-conditioned RL is established but specialised

nodes.title: RLx2: Training a Sparse Deep Reinforcement Learning Model from Scratch
nodes.tldr: Trains a sparse deep RL model from scratch via gradient-based topology evolution and a multi-step TD target with a dynamic-capacity replay buffer.
nodes.problem: Deep RL models are costly to train, and sparse training from scratch is unstable under bootstrapping.
nodes.approach: Rigged-lottery-style sparse training with multi-step TD targets and dynamic-capacity replay.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse training in deep RL is specialised but established

nodes.title: Voxurf: Voxel-based Efficient and Accurate Neural Surface Reconstruction
nodes.tldr: Voxel-grid neural surface reconstruction that uses a two-stage training schedule and dual color network to recover fine geometry efficiently from multi-view images.
nodes.problem: Voxel-based reconstruction methods struggle with fine geometry and local minima.
nodes.approach: Two-stage voxel training with dual color network and hierarchical geometry features.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Voxel-based SDF surface reconstruction is a common research direction.

nodes.title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
nodes.tldr: Shows shallow transformers can exactly simulate automata with few layers via algebraic semigroup structure, with depth O(log T) generally and O(1) for solvable groups.
nodes.problem: Why shallow non-recurrent transformers solve multi-step algorithmic tasks with few layers.
nodes.approach: Transformation-semigroup decomposition yielding shortcut simulators, validated by training on synthetic automata.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Algebraic-automata view of shallow transformer shortcuts is a rare theory angle.

nodes.title: Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task
nodes.tldr: Shows a GPT model trained only on Othello move sequences learns an internal nonlinear board-state representation that can be intervened on.
nodes.problem: Whether sequence models learn real world representations or only surface statistics.
nodes.approach: Train a GPT variant on legal Othello moves and run interventional experiments on activations.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Established interpretability subfield with a specific synthetic-game setup

nodes.title: Spectral Augmentation for Self-Supervised Learning on Graphs
nodes.tldr: Spectral augmentation guides graph topology perturbations for contrastive learning by maximizing spectral change, improving self-supervised representations, transfer, and robustness to adversarial attacks.
nodes.problem: Random spatial graph augmentations ignore spectral structure, leaving unclear what invariance graph contrastive learning should capture.
nodes.approach: Topology augmentation chosen to maximize change in the graph spectrum.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph self-supervised learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Sparse Group Models Through Boolean Relaxation
nodes.tldr: Convex relaxation of a cardinality-constrained Boolean program for sparse group models, with conditions for exact integral solutions and a rounding procedure.
nodes.problem: Cardinality-constrained sparse group selection is combinatorial and hard to solve with few samples.
nodes.approach: Boolean-variable convex relaxation with a rounding algorithm for fractional solutions, plus an exactness condition.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › High-dimensional & Random Matrix Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Sparse recovery spans optimization and high-dimensional statistics.
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse group selection is established but specialised.

nodes.title: UNIFIED-IO: A Unified Model for Vision, Language, and Multi-modal Tasks
nodes.tldr: Single transformer for many vision and language tasks, mapping all inputs and outputs to shared discrete tokens and training jointly on 90+ datasets.
nodes.problem: Unifying heterogeneous vision and language tasks with different input and output formats.
nodes.approach: Homogenize all inputs and outputs into discrete tokens for one sequence-to-sequence transformer.
nodes.niche_reason: Generalist multimodal models are an established direction.

nodes.title: SimPer: Simple Self-Supervised Learning of Periodic Targets
nodes.tldr: SimPer is a contrastive self-supervised method that learns periodic and frequency structure in data using periodicity-specific augmentations and a generalized contrastive loss.
nodes.problem: Standard self-supervised methods ignore intrinsic periodicity and fail to capture periodic attributes.
nodes.approach: Periodicity-aware augmentations, feature similarity measures and a generalized contrastive loss.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Periodic SSL is a specialised but established niche

nodes.title: Mastering the Game of No-Press Diplomacy via Human-Regularized Reinforcement Learning and Planning
nodes.tldr: Trains Diplodocus for no-press Diplomacy using human-regularized planning and RL (DiL-piKL), outperforming human participants in a tournament.
nodes.problem: Self-play RL alone fails to cooperate well with humans in mixed cooperative-competitive games.
nodes.approach: Planning regularized toward human imitation policy (DiL-piKL) extended to self-play RL with human model.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Human-compatible agents for Diplomacy is a rare setting.

nodes.title: LightGCL: Simple Yet Effective Graph Contrastive Learning for Recommendation
nodes.tldr: Graph contrastive learning for recommendation that uses SVD-based graph augmentation to preserve global collaborative structure and resist noise and sparsity.
nodes.problem: Stochastic or heuristic augmentations in graph contrastive recommendation distort semantic structure.
nodes.approach: Singular value decomposition of the interaction graph gives contrastive views without perturbation.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph contrastive recommendation is a crowded, mainstream research line.

nodes.title: CROM: Continuous Reduced-Order Modeling of PDEs Using Implicit Neural Representations
nodes.tldr: Builds a low-dimensional neural-field embedding of continuous PDE solution fields, trained on any discretisation, giving much faster and more accurate reduced-order simulation.
nodes.problem: High-fidelity PDE solvers are too slow for time-critical use, and prior reduced models depend on discretisation.
nodes.approach: Continuously differentiable neural fields represent the reduced manifold of vector fields rather than their discretisation.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural-field reduced-order modelling of PDEs is a rare cross-disciplinary niche.

nodes.title: Is the Performance of My Deep Network Too Good to Be True? A Direct Approach to Estimating the Bayes Error in Binary Classification
nodes.tldr: Estimates the Bayes error of binary classifiers by averaging labels that show class-assignment uncertainty, a model-free estimator usable to detect test-set overfitting.
nodes.problem: Knowing the irreducible Bayes error limit to judge whether deep classifiers are near optimal.
nodes.approach: Mean of uncertain labels as a hyperparameter-free, model-free Bayes error estimate, also for weak supervision.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: irreducible-error theory versus evaluation methodology is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Bayes error estimation is a specialised theory-evaluation topic

nodes.title: Parametrizing Product Shape Manifolds by Composite Networks
nodes.tldr: Learns efficient neural approximations of Riemannian shape-space parametrizations by exploiting product-of-low-dimensional-manifold structure, applied to triangular surface shape spaces.
nodes.problem: Riemannian parametrizations of shape manifolds are computationally costly to compute.
nodes.approach: Composite network learning low-dimensional factors separately then combining, using sparse principal geodesic analysis factorization.
nodes.niche_reason: Riemannian shape space neural parametrization is very rare.

nodes.title: Learnable Behavior Control: Breaking Atari Human World Records via Sample-Efficient Behavior Selection
nodes.tldr: Learnable Behavioral Control enlarges the exploration behavior space with hybrid behavior mappings and bandit meta-controllers, breaking human world records on Atari.
nodes.problem: Population-based exploration is limited because behavior selection is bounded by a fixed policy population.
nodes.approach: Hybrid behavior mapping over all policies, with bandit-based meta-controllers in distributed off-policy actor-critic.
nodes.niche_reason: population-based exploration is established; the hybrid behavior space is distinctive

nodes.title: DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion
nodes.tldr: DreamFusion optimizes a NeRF from text using score distillation from a pretrained 2D diffusion model as a prior, needing no 3D training data.
nodes.problem: Text-to-3D synthesis without large 3D datasets.
nodes.approach: Probability density distillation loss using a frozen text-to-image diffusion model to optimize a NeRF from random views.
nodes.niche_reason: Seminal but very widely followed text-to-3D direction.

nodes.title: Language Modelling with Pixels
nodes.tldr: PIXEL is a language model that renders text as images and is pretrained by reconstructing masked pixel patches, avoiding vocabulary bottlenecks and aiding cross-script transfer.
nodes.problem: Fixed vocabularies limit scaling language models to many languages and scripts.
nodes.approach: Render text as images and train a masked autoencoder to reconstruct pixels of masked patches.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles pretraining, multilingual modeling and representation learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Modelling language purely from rendered pixels is rare.

nodes.title: Efficient Attention via Control Variates
nodes.tldr: Recasts random-feature attention as a sum of control variate estimators, enabling a more flexible efficient attention that narrows the gap to softmax attention.
nodes.problem: Random-feature attention has a poorly understood approximation gap to softmax attention.
nodes.approach: Control variate decomposition of random-feature attention, yielding a new linear-complexity attention with better approximation.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Random-feature attention theory is specialised.

nodes.title: Socratic Models: Composing Zero-Shot Multimodal Reasoning with Language
nodes.tldr: Composes multiple pretrained multimodal models zero-shot through language prompts, enabling captioning, video QA, and robot planning without finetuning.
nodes.problem: Joint multimodal training is costly; combining existing models lacks systematic zero-shot methods.
nodes.approach: Modular systems where pretrained models exchange language intermediate representations via multimodal-informed prompting.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.confidence_reason: Broad application scope; core contribution is prompting-based model composition
nodes.niche_reason: Zero-shot composition of pretrained multimodal models is a specialised framing

nodes.title: ISS: Image as Stepping Stone for Text-Guided 3D Shape Generation
nodes.tldr: Generates 3D shapes from text without paired text-shape data by mapping CLIP features into a reconstruction model's shape space, with images as a bridge.
nodes.problem: Text-to-3D shape generation lacks large paired text-shape datasets and faces a large cross-modal gap.
nodes.approach: Two-stage feature-space alignment of CLIP features into a pretrained single-view reconstruction shape space, plus shape stylization.
nodes.niche_reason: Established 3D generation direction; the image-bridge, unpaired approach is less common.

nodes.title: AutoGT: Automated Graph Transformer Architecture Search
nodes.tldr: AutoGT is a neural architecture search framework jointly optimizing graph Transformer architectures and graph encoding strategies with an encoding-aware supernet splitting strategy.
nodes.problem: Graph Transformer design relies on manual choices of architecture and graph encodings.
nodes.approach: Unified graph Transformer search space with encoding-aware performance estimation by gradually splitting supernets.
nodes.niche_reason: NAS for graph Transformers is a specialised intersection.

nodes.title: Time Will Tell: New Outlooks and A Baseline for Temporal Multi-View 3D Object Detection
nodes.tldr: Treats temporal multi-view fusion as stereo matching, combining a long-history cost volume with short-term fine matching for state-of-the-art camera-only 3D detection.
nodes.problem: Camera-only 3D detection uses too little temporal history, limiting temporal stereo matching quality.
nodes.approach: Long-history coarse cost volume combined with short-term fine-grained matching and monocular depth predictions.
nodes.confidence_reason: Could equally be filed under depth/geometry or autonomous driving.
nodes.niche_reason: Common camera-based 3D detection setting for driving.

nodes.title: Revisiting adapters with adversarial training
nodes.tldr: Shows co-training on clean and adversarial inputs needs only small adapters, such as separate ViT class tokens, instead of dual batch norm.
nodes.problem: Adversarial co-training for clean accuracy needs costly separate batch statistics.
nodes.approach: Use light domain-specific adapters, e.g. ViT class tokens, for clean and adversarial inputs.
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial training variants are common.

nodes.title: ImageNet-X: Understanding Model Mistakes with Factor of Variation Annotations
nodes.tldr: ImageNet-X adds sixteen human-annotated factors (pose, background, lighting) to ImageNet and uses it to analyze failure modes of 2,200 recognition models.
nodes.problem: Benchmarks reveal model mistakes but do not explain why they occur.
nodes.approach: Annotate ImageNet images with factors of variation and analyze models by architecture, paradigm, and augmentation.
nodes.niche_reason: Image classification robustness analysis is common.

nodes.title: A System for Morphology-Task Generalization via Unified Representation and Behavior Distillation
nodes.tldr: Trains one transformer policy across many agent morphologies and tasks by distilling behavior data through a unified morphology-task graph representation.
nodes.problem: Single control policies fail to generalize across diverse agent morphologies and tasks.
nodes.approach: Unified morphology-task graph IO representation with a Transformer policy trained on distilled behavior.
nodes.confidence_reason: Imitation, representation and benchmark contributions overlap
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-morphology control policies are a specialised robotics niche

nodes.title: The Asymmetric Maximum Margin Bias of Quasi-Homogeneous Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Extends maximum-margin implicit bias results to quasi-homogeneous networks with residuals and normalization, showing gradient flow favors an asymmetric subset of parameters.
nodes.problem: Implicit bias of gradient descent on exponential loss beyond homogeneous networks is unknown.
nodes.approach: Geometric analysis of gradient flow dynamics on a quasi-homogeneous model class past separability.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit bias theory is established but specialised; quasi-homogeneous class is new

nodes.title: FedExP: Speeding Up Federated Averaging via Extrapolation
nodes.tldr: FedExP adaptively sets the federated server step size via extrapolation, motivated by FedAvg's link to projection onto convex sets, for faster convergence.
nodes.problem: Server step sizes in federated averaging have not shown practical benefits.
nodes.approach: Adaptively extrapolate pseudo-gradients, motivated by POCS extrapolation in the overparameterized regime.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated optimization is common but the POCS angle is less so.

nodes.title: Accurate Image Restoration with Attention Retractable Transformer
nodes.tldr: Transformer for image restoration that alternates dense window attention with sparse attention, enlarging the receptive field for super-resolution, denoising and JPEG artifact removal.
nodes.problem: Window-based self-attention in restoration transformers only attends within dense regions, restricting receptive fields.
nodes.approach: Alternating dense and sparse attention modules so tokens from sparse image areas can interact.
nodes.niche_reason: Transformer image restoration is a common, crowded direction

nodes.title: GPViT: A High Resolution Non-Hierarchical Vision Transformer with Group Propagation
nodes.tldr: Proposes GPViT, a non-hierarchical vision transformer that exchanges global information via learnable group tokens, enabling efficient high-resolution features for dense prediction.
nodes.problem: Global information exchange between high-resolution tokens is too expensive with self-attention.
nodes.approach: Group Propagation Block groups features with learnable tokens, propagates globally, and returns updates.
nodes.niche_reason: vision transformer backbones are a mainstream area

nodes.title: A framework for benchmarking Class-out-of-distribution detection and its application to ImageNet
nodes.tldr: A framework to benchmark class-out-of-distribution detection at varying difficulty levels, applied to 525 pretrained ImageNet-1k classifiers.
nodes.problem: Evaluating how well image classifiers detect instances from classes unseen in training.
nodes.approach: Difficulty-graded class-OOD benchmark generation for any ImageNet classifier, applied to 525 models.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: OOD detection benchmarking is a common topic.

nodes.title: Toeplitz Neural Network for Sequence Modeling
nodes.tldr: Replaces quadratic attention with a relative-position Toeplitz matrix product, reducing sequence modeling cost to log-linear and extrapolating from 512 to 14K tokens.
nodes.problem: Transformer attention has quadratic cost, limiting scaling to long input sequences
nodes.approach: Toeplitz matrix-vector product with a lightweight relative position encoder generating coefficients for any length
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient sequence models are a crowded direction

nodes.title: Sparsity May Cry: Let Us Fail (Current) Sparse Neural Networks Together!
nodes.tldr: Introduces SMC-Bench, 10 datasets across 4 diverse tasks, showing state-of-the-art sparse training methods often fail when applied out-of-the-box.
nodes.problem: Sparse neural network algorithms are evaluated on simple tasks, which may hide their real failures.
nodes.approach: Curated benchmark of 4 diverse tasks and 10 datasets to stress-test magnitude and gradient-based sparse methods.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Sparse-network benchmarking is an established research area

nodes.title: Learning rigid dynamics with face interaction graph networks
nodes.tldr: FIGNet is a graph network operating on mesh faces rather than nodes to learn rigid-body collisions, more accurate and efficient than node- and particle-based simulators.
nodes.problem: Learned simulators struggle with rigid collisions among complex shapes; node-based interactions are inaccurate or particle ones too costly.
nodes.approach: Face interaction graph network computing face-face interactions on meshes, trained on simulated and real friction data.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned rigid-body simulators are a rare direction.

nodes.title: Mosaic Representation Learning for Self-supervised Visual Pre-training
nodes.tldr: MosRep composes small crops from different images into mosaic views to enrich backgrounds in multi-crop self-supervised learning, improving downstream and low-label ImageNet results.
nodes.problem: Multi-crop self-supervised learning lacks diverse contextual backgrounds, limiting view variance and representation quality.
nodes.approach: Mosaic augmentation: tile crops from different images into one view and jitter positions.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Yet another contrastive SSL augmentation variant in a crowded area.

nodes.title: LAVA: Data Valuation without Pre-Specified Learning Algorithms
nodes.tldr: LAVA values training data using a class-wise Wasserstein distance between training and validation sets, independent of any learning algorithm, obtained cheaply from optimal transport dual solutions.
nodes.problem: Data valuation depends on the chosen learning algorithm and is expensive to compute.
nodes.approach: Class-wise Wasserstein distance proxy with sensitivity analysis of the optimal transport solution to score points.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Data valuation is a specialised but established subfield.

nodes.title: The Lie Derivative for Measuring Learned Equivariance
nodes.tldr: Measures learned equivariance of hundreds of pretrained vision models with the Lie derivative, finding violations stem from aliasing and larger models are more equivariant.
nodes.problem: Understanding how much equivariance modern vision models actually learn, and what drives it.
nodes.approach: Apply the Lie derivative as an equivariance metric to hundreds of pretrained CNNs, transformers and Mixers.
nodes.niche_reason: Symmetry-focused large-scale empirical study; specialised but established.

nodes.title: Rarity Score : A New Metric to Evaluate the Uncommonness of Synthesized Images
nodes.tldr: Proposes rarity score, a nearest-neighbor metric in feature space that measures how uncommon each generated image is and compares models on rare-image generation.
nodes.problem: Diversity metrics compare distributions and cannot score how rare an individual generated image is.
nodes.approach: Nearest-neighbor distances in VGG16-style feature space for per-image rarity.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Per-image rarity metrics for generative models are specialised

nodes.title: Implicit Bias in Leaky ReLU Networks Trained on High-Dimensional Data
nodes.tldr: Shows gradient flow on leaky ReLU networks with nearly orthogonal data yields a rank-two max-margin solution; small-init gradient descent stays low-rank.
nodes.problem: Why gradient training shows strong implicit bias in neural networks is unclear.
nodes.approach: Analyze gradient flow and gradient descent in two-layer networks with near-orthogonal high-dimensional data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit bias theory for leaky ReLU networks is specialised

nodes.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
nodes.tldr: Off-the-shelf Token Merging gradually combines similar tokens in ViTs, doubling throughput with small accuracy loss and speeding training across image, video, and audio.
nodes.problem: Speeding up existing ViTs without retraining, while keeping accuracy better than token pruning.
nodes.approach: Lightweight matching that merges similar tokens layer by layer, as fast as pruning but more accurate.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Popular efficient-ViT theme with a simple merging twist

nodes.title: Agree to Disagree: Diversity through Disagreement for Better Transferability
nodes.tldr: Trains an ensemble that agrees on training data but disagrees on OOD data, capturing diverse predictive features to reduce shortcut learning.
nodes.problem: Gradient-based learning's simplicity bias favors spurious features and limits out-of-distribution transferability.
nodes.approach: Diversity-By-disAgreement Training enforces training agreement and OOD disagreement, derived from generalized discrepancy.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Ensemble diversity for OOD generalization is a common mainstream direction

nodes.title: Symmetric Pruning in Quantum Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Explains why symmetric ansatze train better in quantum neural networks via an effective quantum NTK, and proposes symmetric pruning to derive symmetric ansatze automatically.
nodes.problem: Theoretical reason why symmetric quantum circuit ansatze have better trainability for ground state preparation.
nodes.approach: Effective quantum neural tangent kernel analysis linking over-parameterization to symmetry, then a pruning scheme.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum NN trainability theory with symmetric pruning is very rare.

nodes.title: Faster Gradient-Free Methods for Escaping Saddle Points
nodes.tldr: Accelerated zeroth-order methods that use Nesterov-style acceleration to escape saddle points without gradients, reaching second-order stationarity with fewer oracle calls.
nodes.problem: Escaping saddle points without explicit gradients lacks accelerated methods.
nodes.approach: Accelerated variants of perturbation-based and negative-curvature zeroth-order methods.
nodes.niche_reason: Established optimization line; gradient-free acceleration is specialised.

nodes.title: Not All Tasks Are Born Equal: Understanding Zero-Shot Generalization
nodes.tldr: Finds a few key training tasks (mostly QA) beat using all tasks for zero-shot generalization, and proposes automatically identifying and resampling them.
nodes.problem: Understanding which training tasks drive zero-shot generalization in multitask prompted pretraining.
nodes.approach: Pairwise task generalization analysis to identify key tasks and resample the training task distribution.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Topic fits both pretraining data selection and transfer learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Task-mixture analysis for prompted multitask models is specialised.

nodes.title: When and Why Vision-Language Models Behave like Bags-Of-Words, and What to Do About It?
nodes.tldr: Introduces the ARO benchmark showing vision-language models act like bags-of-words, and fixes it with composition-aware hard-negative mining in contrastive training.
nodes.problem: Vision-language models poorly encode relations, attributes and word order, undetected by standard retrieval tests.
nodes.approach: ARO benchmark plus contrastive fine-tuning with composition-aware hard negatives.
nodes.niche_reason: CLIP-style VLM evaluation and contrastive fixes are widely studied.

nodes.title: PEER: A Collaborative Language Model
nodes.tldr: PEER is a language model trained to imitate the whole collaborative writing process: drafting, suggesting, editing and explaining, using multiple instances for self-training data.
nodes.problem: LMs generate only final text and cannot update drafts, take edit instructions or explain actions.
nodes.approach: Train infilling instances of PEER on edit histories and self-train to synthesize more data.
nodes.niche_reason: Collaborative editing LMs are an unusual focus.

nodes.title: Equiformer: Equivariant Graph Attention Transformer for 3D Atomistic Graphs
nodes.tldr: Equiformer is an SE(3)-equivariant graph attention transformer for 3D molecular graphs, using irreducible-representation features and MLP attention.
nodes.problem: Transformers underperform on 3D atomistic graphs even with symmetry-related inductive biases.
nodes.approach: Equivariant transformer with irreps features and MLP-based equivariant graph attention.
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariant transformers for molecules are specialised

nodes.title: Training language models to summarize narratives improves brain alignment
nodes.tldr: Language models trained to summarize narratives have representations that align better with human fMRI brain activity, especially for character names.
nodes.problem: Whether training on narrative understanding yields deeper language understanding, measured by brain alignment.
nodes.approach: Fine-tune LMs on narrative summarization and compare representations to fMRI recordings.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles NLP training and neuroscience brain-alignment analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Brain-NLP alignment is a rare cross-disciplinary direction.

nodes.title: Conditional Antibody Design as 3D Equivariant Graph Translation
nodes.tldr: Co-designs antibody CDR sequences and 3D structures as conditional equivariant graph translation with antigen context, avoiding slow autoregressive decoding.
nodes.problem: Existing antibody design methods use incomplete context and slow autoregressive CDR generation.
nodes.approach: Multi-channel E(3)-equivariant attention with progressive full-shot co-design of sequence and structure.
nodes.niche_reason: Antibody CDR co-design is a specialised biology direction.

nodes.title: The Role of Coverage in Online Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows existence of a data distribution with good coverage (coverability) enables sample-efficient online RL, and introduces the self-normalized coefficient complexity measure.
nodes.problem: Understanding whether offline-style coverage conditions govern sample complexity of online RL.
nodes.approach: Define coverability as an MDP structural property, prove upper bounds and separations, compare with Bellman rank.
nodes.niche_reason: RL theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Betty: An Automatic Differentiation Library for Multilevel Optimization
nodes.tldr: Betty is a software library for gradient-based multilevel optimization with a dataflow graph enabling efficient automatic differentiation and scalable systems support.
nodes.problem: Implementing and scaling multilevel optimization gradients is difficult and compute and memory intensive.
nodes.approach: Dataflow-graph abstraction for efficient automatic differentiation plus mixed-precision and data-parallel support.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.confidence_reason: Software library; closest topic is structured differentiable optimization.
nodes.niche_reason: Multilevel optimization tooling is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Adversarial Training of Self-supervised Monocular Depth Estimation against Physical-World Attacks
nodes.tldr: Adversarial training for self-supervised monocular depth models using view synthesis and L0-bounded physical-world perturbations, without depth ground truth.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised depth networks lack labels for traditional adversarial training and are vulnerable to physical attacks.
nodes.approach: View-synthesis-based adversarial training with L0-norm-bounded perturbations used during training.
nodes.niche_reason: Robustness of self-supervised depth to physical attacks is specialised

nodes.title: Learning with Logical Constraints but without Shortcut Satisfaction
nodes.tldr: Learning with logical constraints without shortcut satisfaction, using dual variables for logical connectives and a variational distributional loss compatible with standard training.
nodes.problem: Logical-constraint losses are vacuously satisfied via shortcuts, failing to exploit the knowledge.
nodes.approach: Dual variables encode how constraints are satisfied; variational framework solved with stochastic gradient descent ascent.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Neuro-symbolic constraint learning is a rare direction.

nodes.title: Addressing Parameter Choice Issues in Unsupervised Domain Adaptation by Aggregation
nodes.tldr: Proposes weighted least squares aggregation of hyper-parameter-varied models for unsupervised domain adaptation, with target error within twice the optimal.
nodes.problem: Choosing hyper-parameters in unsupervised domain adaptation lacks theoretically grounded error bounds.
nodes.approach: Extends weighted least squares to vector-valued functions such as deep networks, then aggregates trained models linearly.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Aggregation-based model selection for domain adaptation is specialised.

nodes.title: Does Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning Exist?
nodes.tldr: Systematically tests zero-shot RL via successor features and forward-backward representations in offline reward-free settings, finding forward-backward representations perform best and most consistently.
nodes.problem: Whether agents can solve any task instantly after reward-free pretraining remains untested systematically.
nodes.approach: Introduce improved losses and SF models, compare SF and FB schemes on offline replay buffers in Unsupervised RL benchmark.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Zero-shot RL with FB representations is a rare direction.

nodes.title: Real-time variational method for learning neural trajectory and its dynamics
nodes.tldr: Introduces an exponential-family variational Kalman filter for online inference of latent neural trajectories while learning the underlying dynamical system, with a tighter ELBO.
nodes.problem: Real-time online latent trajectory inference for neural recordings is under-studied versus offline methods.
nodes.approach: Recursive Bayesian variational filter with closed-form variational predict step for exponential-family latent states.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Online latent dynamics inference for neuroscience is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Optimal Transport for Offline Imitation Learning
nodes.tldr: Relabels unlabeled offline data with rewards from optimal-transport alignment to a few expert demonstrations, enabling offline RL without true rewards.
nodes.problem: Offline RL needs reward labels, which are hard to engineer or costly to annotate.
nodes.approach: Optimal transport alignment between dataset trajectories and one expert demonstration as reward.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: OT-based reward relabeling is a specialised offline-RL angle.

nodes.title: UNICORN: A Unified Backdoor Trigger Inversion Framework
nodes.tldr: UNICORN formally defines backdoor triggers and the trigger-inversion problem, then proposes one framework to recover triggers across many trigger types in DNNs.
nodes.problem: Existing backdoor trigger inversion methods make attack-specific assumptions and fail to generalize across trigger types.
nodes.approach: Formal trigger definition plus a unified inversion framework based on identified inner behaviors of backdoor models.
nodes.confidence_reason: Backdoor defense has no exact topic; adversarial robustness is nearest
nodes.niche_reason: Unified backdoor trigger inversion is a specialised security niche.

nodes.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
nodes.tldr: MEMIT edits a language model's weights to insert thousands of factual memories at once, scaling to GPT-J and GPT-NeoX far beyond single-edit methods.
nodes.problem: Existing model editing updates only single associations, not many at once.
nodes.approach: Direct batched parameter updates across multiple MLP layers to write many factual associations.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Model editing is a recognized common subarea.

nodes.title: Where to Begin? On the Impact of Pre-Training and Initialization in Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: Empirically shows that starting federated learning from pre-trained models speeds convergence, improves accuracy up to 40 percent, and reduces the effect of data and system heterogeneity.
nodes.problem: Federated optimization is usually evaluated from random initialization despite available proxy pre-training data.
