nodes.approach: Empirical study of pre-trained versus random initialization across four federated benchmarks.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated learning heterogeneity is a common topic.

nodes.title: A Laplace-inspired Distribution on SO(3) for Probabilistic Rotation Estimation
nodes.tldr: Proposes a Laplace-inspired distribution on SO(3) for probabilistic rotation regression that resists outliers and converges better than Bingham or matrix Fisher.
nodes.problem: Gaussian-like rotation noise models such as Bingham and matrix Fisher are sensitive to outliers.
nodes.approach: Rotation Laplace distribution on SO(3) with heavier-tailed likelihood giving stronger gradients near low error.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Outlier-robust SO(3) distributions are a rare niche

nodes.title: Towards Open Temporal Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Propagates only class-agnostic information between nodes of different classes in temporal graphs, with triad sampling to avoid forgetting old classes.
nodes.problem: Open temporal graphs add new node classes over time, causing conflicting propagation and forgetting.
nodes.approach: Information-bottleneck message passing that propagates class-agnostic knowledge, plus diverse triad selection.
nodes.niche_reason: Open temporal graph class-incremental learning is specialised

nodes.title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion
nodes.tldr: Learns a new pseudo-word embedding from 3-5 images of a concept, enabling personalized text-to-image generation with a frozen model.
nodes.problem: Text-to-image models cannot easily generate or edit specific user-provided concepts.
nodes.approach: Optimize a single new word embedding in a frozen text-to-image model's vocabulary.
nodes.niche_reason: Personalization of text-to-image is a crowded direction

nodes.title: Designing BERT for Convolutional Networks: Sparse and Hierarchical Masked Modeling
nodes.tldr: Adapts BERT-style masked image pretraining to convnets using sparse convolution on unmasked pixels and a hierarchical decoder for multi-scale features.
nodes.problem: Masked image pretraining is hard to apply to convnets, which cannot handle irregular masked inputs.
nodes.approach: Sparse convolution over unmasked pixels treated as voxels, with a hierarchical multi-scale decoder.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Masked image modeling is crowded; convnet sparse variant is less common

nodes.title: Human-Guided Fair Classification for Natural Language Processing
nodes.tldr: Generates candidate sentence pairs differing in sensitive attributes via style transfer and GPT-3, validates by crowdsourcing, and learns human-aligned individual fairness specifications.
nodes.problem: Formal similarity specifications for individual fairness in text poorly match human intuition.
nodes.approach: Generate counterfactual pairs with style transfer and GPT-3, crowdsource validation, learn similarity from human feedback.
nodes.niche_reason: Individual fairness for text with human-guided specs is specialised.

nodes.title: Near-optimal Coresets for Robust Clustering
nodes.tldr: Constructs near-optimal epsilon-coresets of size O(m + poly(k/epsilon)) for robust k-clustering with m outliers in near-linear time, with a nearly matching lower bound.
nodes.problem: Compressing data for robust k-median/k-means clustering with outliers while preserving cost.
nodes.approach: Adapt a capacity-constrained clustering coreset framework to handle center-dependent excluded outliers.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: No exact seed topic for clustering and coresets; closest is lower bounds and complexity.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical computer science coresets for robust clustering are very rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: Guarded Policy Optimization with Imperfect Online Demonstrations
nodes.tldr: Guarded Policy Optimization lets a student RL agent learn with interventions from imperfect teacher policies, using an off-policy actor-critic with shared control.
nodes.problem: Teacher-student RL assumes a near-optimal teacher, which is rarely available in practice.
nodes.approach: Off-policy RL integrating arbitrary teacher interventions as online demonstrations with guarded exploration.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles online RL, safe RL and learning from demonstrations.
nodes.niche_reason: Intervention-based RL with imperfect teachers is specialised.

nodes.title: Multi-Rate VAE: Train Once, Get the Full Rate-Distortion Curve
nodes.tldr: Trains one VAE with a hypernetwork that maps the beta trade-off to optimal parameters, yielding the full rate-distortion curve without retraining.
nodes.problem: VAEs need many training runs to pick the distortion-rate trade-off beta.
nodes.approach: Hypernetwork with beta-conditioned gating of pre-activations, analyzed exactly for linear VAEs.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Hypernetwork rate-distortion VAEs are specialised.

nodes.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems
nodes.tldr: Extends diffusion posterior sampling to general noisy nonlinear inverse problems via a Laplace approximation, handling Gaussian and Poisson noise.
nodes.problem: Diffusion inverse solvers mostly handle noiseless linear problems.
nodes.approach: Laplace-approximated posterior sampling blending diffusion with manifold-constrained gradient.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion solvers for noisy nonlinear inverse problems are specialised.

nodes.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning by Breaking the Replay Ratio Barrier
nodes.tldr: Shows that periodically resetting deep RL agent parameters enables strong replay-ratio scaling, boosting sample efficiency on Atari and DMC.
nodes.problem: Improving sample efficiency by raising the replay ratio, which usually destabilises deep RL training.
nodes.approach: Full or partial parameter resets combined with an order-of-magnitude higher update count.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Sample-efficiency tricks for deep RL are a common direction

nodes.title: BC-IRL: Learning Generalizable Reward Functions from Demonstrations
nodes.tldr: Introduces BC-IRL, which updates reward parameters so the policy trained on them matches expert demonstrations, yielding rewards that generalize better than MaxEnt IRL.
nodes.problem: Reward functions learned by maximum-entropy IRL overfit demonstrations and generalize poorly to unseen states.
nodes.approach: Reward update that tunes parameters so the policy trained on the reward imitates demonstrations.

nodes.title: Effects of Graph Convolutions in Multi-layer Networks

nodes.title: Learning with Stochastic Orders

nodes.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Equivariant Models in Domains with Latent Symmetry
nodes.tldr: Shows that equivariance constraints only approximating a latent domain symmetry help learning, improving supervised and robotic RL performance.

nodes.title: The Symmetric Generalized Eigenvalue Problem as a Nash Equilibrium
nodes.tldr: Recasts top-k generalized eigenvalue problems as a game with eigenvectors as Nash equilibrium, giving a parallel O(dk)-per-iteration minibatch algorithm.

nodes.title: Learning Controllable Adaptive Simulation for Multi-resolution Physics
nodes.tldr: LAMP jointly learns a GNN PDE surrogate and a GNN actor-critic that refines or coarsens the mesh, trading error against compute controllably at inference time.

nodes.title: Choreographer: Learning and Adapting Skills in Imagination
nodes.tldr: Choreographer learns skills in a world model's latent imagination, decoupling exploration from skill learning, then adapts them to downstream tasks in parallel.

nodes.tldr: Flow Matching trains continuous normalizing flows by regressing conditional vector fields, simulation-free, subsuming diffusion paths and enabling optimal-transport paths with faster training and sampling.

nodes.title: Metadata Archaeology: Unearthing Data Subsets by Leveraging Training Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Infers hidden metadata like mislabeled or atypical examples by comparing learning dynamics on transformed probe subsets of a dataset.

nodes.title: Sign and Basis Invariant Networks for Spectral Graph Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: SignNet and BasisNet are universal architectures invariant to eigenvector sign flips and basis changes, more expressive than existing spectral graph methods and positional encodings.

nodes.title: Contrastive Audio-Visual Masked Autoencoder
nodes.tldr: Extends masked autoencoders to audio-visual data and combines contrastive correspondence learning with masked modeling to learn joint audio-visual representations.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised audio-visual representations lack a joint, coordinated objective.

nodes.tldr: Jointly learns the geometry of metamaterial elastic solids and a neural controller by gradient descent, so the body performs morphological computation.

nodes.title: Efficient Discrete Multi Marginal Optimal Transport Regularization
nodes.tldr: Efficient discrete multi-marginal optimal transport regularizer using a generalized earth mover's distance subroutine, with efficiently computed gradients, applied to fairness constraints.

nodes.title: Simplicial Embeddings in Self-Supervised Learning and Downstream Classification
nodes.tldr: Projects SSL representations into softmax simplices, adding group sparsity and formally better generalization for downstream classification.

nodes.title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts are Domain Generalizable Learners
nodes.tldr: Proposes a sparse mixture-of-experts vision transformer whose architecture aligns with dataset correlations, improving ERM-trained domain generalization on DomainBed.

nodes.title: A Model or 603 Exemplars: Towards Memory-Efficient Class-Incremental Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows that when stored models count toward the memory budget, model-saving class-incremental learning methods often lose to exemplar storage, and proposes a memory-efficient approach.

nodes.title: Meta-prediction Model for Distillation-Aware NAS on Unseen Datasets

nodes.title: Extreme Q-Learning: MaxEnt RL without Entropy

nodes.title: Draft, Sketch, and Prove: Guiding Formal Theorem Provers with Informal Proofs

nodes.title: Serving Graph Compression for Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Compresses the training graph used at GNN inference time into a smaller graph, reducing storage while keeping the trained model and forward pass unchanged.

nodes.title: Statistical Efficiency of Score Matching: The View from Isoperimetry

nodes.title: Hyperbolic Deep Reinforcement Learning

nodes.title: Flow Annealed Importance Sampling Bootstrap
nodes.tldr: FAB trains normalizing flows with annealed importance sampling and alpha=2 divergence, learning Boltzmann distributions like alanine dipeptide without MD samples using 100x fewer target evaluations.
nodes.problem: Training flows on unnormalized targets suffers from mode-seeking, costly MCMC samples, or high-variance losses.
nodes.approach: Augment flows with annealed importance sampling and minimize the mass-covering alpha=2 divergence.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Normalizing flow training versus Bayesian sampling; physical-system application also fits.
nodes.niche_reason: Sample-free Boltzmann distribution learning with flows is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
nodes.tldr: Rectified flow learns ODEs that transport between two distributions along straight paths via simple least-squares, unifying generative modeling and domain transfer.
nodes.problem: Transporting between two distributions for generation and domain transfer with fast, simple training.
nodes.approach: Learn an ODE following straight paths between paired samples via nonlinear least squares, with iterative reflow.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Flow matching is a very crowded mainstream area.

nodes.title: Packed Ensembles for efficient uncertainty estimation
nodes.tldr: Packed-Ensembles build lightweight ensembles with grouped convolutions in a single backbone, matching deep ensembles on accuracy, calibration, and OOD detection at lower cost.
nodes.problem: Deep ensembles are too memory- and compute-heavy for hardware-limited real-world systems.
nodes.approach: Parallelize structured sub-networks via grouped convolutions with modulated encoding dimension in one forward pass.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Ensemble uncertainty estimation is a common topic.

nodes.title: Code Translation with Compiler Representations
nodes.tldr: Improves unsupervised code translation by feeding LLVM intermediate representations as a pivot, boosting correct translations across C++, Java, Rust, Go.
nodes.problem: Neural code translation treats code as text tokens and confuses semantically different snippets.
nodes.approach: Augments neural machine translation with LLVM IR pivots, and trains IR decompilation models.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: compiler-IR pivots for translation, uncommon angle

nodes.title: Compressing multidimensional weather and climate data into neural networks
nodes.tldr: Compresses petabyte-scale weather and climate grids by overfitting a coordinate-based neural network, reaching 300x to 3000x compression with small forecasting loss.
nodes.problem: High-resolution climate simulation outputs are too large to store and share
nodes.approach: Coordinate-based neural network overfit to gridded data, with its weights serving as the compressed representation
nodes.niche_reason: Neural compression of climate grids is an unusual cross-disciplinary use

nodes.title: VIP: Towards Universal Visual Reward and Representation via Value-Implicit Pre-Training
nodes.tldr: Pretrains a visual representation on unlabeled human videos whose embedding distance yields dense goal-conditioned rewards for unseen robot tasks.
nodes.problem: Learning general visual reward and representations for robot manipulation from scarce task-specific robot data.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised dual goal-conditioned value objective, action-free, pretrained on Ego4D with implicit time-contrastive embedding.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.confidence_reason: Reward and representation learning overlap; primary topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Visual reward from human videos is established but specialised.

nodes.title: A Call to Reflect on Evaluation Practices for Failure Detection in Image Classification
nodes.tldr: Shows failure-detection research uses inconsistent protocols, and benchmarks confidence scores, finding a simple softmax baseline performs best overall.
nodes.problem: Failure detection methods are evaluated under inconsistent protocols that ignore many failure sources
nodes.approach: Unified requirements plus a large-scale empirical benchmark of confidence scoring functions across all failure sources.
nodes.niche_reason: Confidence-scoring evaluation is a common research topic

nodes.title: Multi-skill Mobile Manipulation for Object Rearrangement
nodes.tldr: Makes manipulation skills mobile and trains navigation to end at regions rather than points, reducing compounding errors in long-horizon mobile rearrangement.
nodes.problem: Chaining stationary manipulation skills with point-goal navigation compounds errors on long-horizon tasks.
nodes.approach: Mobile manipulation skills plus region-goal navigation trained with reinforcement learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Modular mobile manipulation is a common robotics pattern

nodes.title: Evolve Smoothly, Fit Consistently: Learning Smooth Latent Dynamics For Advection-Dominated Systems
nodes.tldr: Learns smooth, low-dimensional latent dynamics with hypernetworks, giving fast accurate rollouts for advection-dominated PDE surrogate models.
nodes.problem: Slow-decaying Kolmogorov n-width makes reduced models inaccurate for advection-dominated physical systems.
nodes.approach: Hypernetwork latent dynamics on a compact representation network's parameter space, with consistency regularization.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised surrogate modelling for PDEs

nodes.title: Associative Memory Augmented Asynchronous Spatiotemporal Representation Learning for Event-based Perception
nodes.tldr: Learns asynchronous event-camera representations by self-attention over sparse events plus an associative memory that updates only where and when events occur.
nodes.problem: Dense models and existing event-based methods are computationally costly on asynchronous event streams
nodes.approach: Set-based self-attention over events with a memory addressed by location and time, updating latent states per event.
nodes.confidence_reason: Event-camera data fits both video and set-processing topics
nodes.niche_reason: Asynchronous event-camera representation learning is a rare niche

nodes.title: Energy-Inspired Self-Supervised Pretraining for Vision Models
nodes.tldr: Self-supervised vision pretraining that treats a network's forward pass as energy estimation and its backward pass as gradient-based data restoration, folding encoder-decoder into one model.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised vision pretraining beyond masked image modeling without an auxiliary decoder.
nodes.approach: Energy-based model: forward pass fits an energy function; backward pass restores corrupted data via energy-minimizing gradients.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Energy-based self-supervision is a less common alternative to MIM.

nodes.title: DocPrompting: Generating Code by Retrieving the Docs
nodes.tldr: DocPrompting generates code by first retrieving relevant documentation for a natural-language intent, enabling use of unseen libraries and improving CodeT5 on CoNaLa and Bash.
nodes.problem: Code models cannot use new or unseen APIs absent from training data.
nodes.approach: Retrieve relevant documentation pieces from the intent, then condition code generation on intent plus retrieved docs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Retrieval-augmented code generation is fairly common.

nodes.title: Symbolic Physics Learner: Discovering governing equations via Monte Carlo tree search
nodes.tldr: Symbolic Physics Learner discovers governing equations of nonlinear dynamics by searching expression trees with Monte Carlo tree search, enforcing parsimony.
nodes.problem: Distilling analytical governing equations of nonlinear dynamics from limited data.
nodes.approach: Represent formulas as expression trees and explore them with an MCTS agent guided by data fit.
nodes.primary_topic: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.niche_reason: MCTS-based equation discovery is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Active Learning in Bayesian Neural Networks with Balanced Entropy Learning Principle
nodes.tldr: Proposes Balanced Entropy Acquisition, a standalone closed-form uncertainty measure for Bayesian active learning using Beta approximations, avoiding redundant selection and batch cost.
nodes.problem: Info-max active learning like BALD selects redundant points and has high batch selection cost.
nodes.approach: Approximate softmax and label marginals by Beta distributions to form closed-form ratio of entropies.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Active learning acquisition functions are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Last Layer Re-Training is Sufficient for Robustness to Spurious Correlations
nodes.tldr: Shows simple last-layer retraining on models with spurious features matches state-of-the-art spurious-correlation robustness at far lower cost, including on ImageNet models.
nodes.problem: Neural classifiers rely on spurious background and texture features, hurting robustness.
nodes.approach: Retraining only the last layer of a pretrained network.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Spurious-correlation robustness is a crowded benchmark area.

nodes.title: Confidence-Conditioned Value Functions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Learns Q-functions conditioned on a confidence level so offline RL policies can adapt their conservatism at evaluation time instead of using one fixed setting.
nodes.problem: Conservative offline RL fixes one degree of conservatism, often suboptimal at deployment.
nodes.approach: Confidence-conditioned Bellman backup learning lower-bound Q-values for any confidence, selected adaptively online.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL conservatism is a common theme.

nodes.title: Optimal Conservative Offline RL with General Function Approximation via Augmented Lagrangian
nodes.tldr: First practical, statistically optimal offline RL under general function approximation and single-policy concentrability, using a marginalized importance sampling formulation with augmented Lagrangian enforcing occupancy validity.
nodes.problem: Provable conservative offline RL is intractable or suboptimal under nonlinear function approximation.
nodes.approach: Marginalized importance sampling with augmented Lagrangian to enforce occupancy validity constraints.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Continual evaluation for lifelong learning: Identifying the stability gap
nodes.tldr: Reveals the stability gap: continual learning methods show temporary sharp forgetting right after new tasks begin, found via per-iteration evaluation and new worst-case metrics.
nodes.problem: Standard task-end evaluation hides transient forgetting in continual learning.
nodes.approach: Continual evaluation framework with per-iteration testing, new worst-case metrics, and gradient plasticity/stability analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Continual learning evaluation insight; established area with specialised angle.

nodes.title: Implicit regularization in Heavy-ball momentum accelerated stochastic gradient descent
nodes.tldr: Shows heavy-ball momentum SGD implicitly regularizes more strongly than plain GD by a factor (1+β)/(1-β), via a modified-loss continuous trajectory analysis.
nodes.problem: Understanding whether momentum contributes to implicit regularization in gradient descent and why it generalizes better.
nodes.approach: Backward error analysis deriving modified loss with implicit regularizer for GD+M and SGD+M, validated experimentally.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Established theory topic, specialised backward error analysis of momentum.

nodes.title: Image to Sphere: Learning Equivariant Features for Efficient Pose Prediction
nodes.tldr: Maps image features onto the SO(3) rotation manifold and uses equivariant layers to predict object orientation distributions that handle symmetric objects.
nodes.problem: Single-image object pose prediction handles symmetric objects and uncertainty poorly, and distribution models are sample-inefficient.
nodes.approach: Lifts image features to SO(3) and applies equivariant layers to output a rotation distribution sampleable at any resolution.
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariant rotation distributions for pose are specialised

nodes.title: Prompt-to-Prompt Image Editing with Cross-Attention Control
nodes.tldr: Edits images using only text by manipulating cross-attention maps during diffusion, preserving layout while changing words, adding specifications, or reweighting concepts.
nodes.problem: Text-driven image editing without masks is hard because small prompt changes drastically alter generated images.
nodes.approach: Inject and control cross-attention maps from the original prompt during the diffusion process.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion image editing is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Stochastic Multi-Person 3D Motion Forecasting
nodes.tldr: Introduces stochastic multi-person 3D motion forecasting with a dual-level generative framework modeling individual motion locally and social interaction globally through shared latent intent codes.
nodes.problem: Prior motion forecasting ignores social interaction, motion diversity, and articulated complexity for multiple people.
nodes.approach: Dual-level generative model with learnable intent latent codes switching between local individual and global social modes.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Motion forecasting is established; multi-person stochastic setting is specialised.

nodes.title: STUNT: Few-shot Tabular Learning with Self-generated Tasks from Unlabeled Tables
nodes.tldr: Few-shot semi-supervised tabular learning by self-generating meta-learning tasks from random columns of unlabeled tables.
nodes.problem: Tabular data needs few-shot learning but existing methods transfer poorly.
nodes.approach: Random columns as pseudo-targets for meta-learning, plus unsupervised validation.
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot tabular learning is under-explored

nodes.title: Knowledge-in-Context: Towards Knowledgeable Semi-Parametric Language Models
nodes.tldr: A semi-parametric LM that retrieves typed knowledge from an external memory per input, letting a 770M model beat LLMs 4-39x larger zero-shot.
nodes.problem: Fully parametric LMs need huge parameter counts to store knowledge and adapt slowly
nodes.approach: Knowledge selector acting as an MoE router that retrieves knowledge types to augment text-to-text input
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Semi-parametric LM with a learned knowledge selector

nodes.title: D4FT: A Deep Learning Approach to Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory
nodes.tldr: D4FT directly minimizes Kohn-Sham total energy with reparameterized orthogonality and minibatch SGD over quadrature grids, cutting complexity from O(N^4) to O(N^3).
nodes.problem: Slow, unstable self-consistent-field solvers for Kohn-Sham density functional theory
nodes.approach: Direct energy minimization with feed-forward orthogonality and amortized stochastic quadrature
nodes.confidence_reason: Quantum chemistry fits Materials & Physics or Chemistry equally
nodes.niche_reason: Deep learning for DFT is a rare AI-for-science niche

nodes.title: A Holistic View of Label Noise Transition Matrix in Deep Learning and Beyond
nodes.tldr: Unifies label-noise transition matrix estimators under a minimum geometric envelope framework, shows their inconsistency under imperfect posteriors, and proposes a bilevel optimization estimator ROBOT with guarantees.
nodes.problem: Existing noise transition matrix estimators fail when noisy posterior estimates are imperfect.
nodes.approach: Bilevel optimization framework (ROBOT) with identifiability, consistency, and generalization guarantees.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Learning with noisy labels theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: GEASS: Neural causal feature selection for high-dimensional biological data
nodes.tldr: GEASS identifies sparse nonlinear Granger-causal features in high-dimensional spatiotemporal biological data with a single neural network maximizing sparsity-regularized transfer entropy with recovery guarantees.
nodes.problem: Neural causality detection for high-dimensional biological data is uninterpretable and does not scale.
nodes.approach: Single network maximizing sparsity-regularized modified transfer entropy for Granger feature selection.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.confidence_reason: Topic split between biology application and causal feature selection method.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural Granger feature selection for spatial transcriptomics is rare.

nodes.title: A Higher Precision Algorithm for Computing the $1$-Wasserstein Distance
nodes.tldr: Proposes a wrapper that boosts any additive-error 1-Wasserstein approximation, giving much tighter estimates when the true distance is small.
nodes.problem: Additive-error Wasserstein estimators are noisy when the true distance is small.
nodes.approach: Runs the base algorithm at error epsilon/d with a logarithmic overhead, plus a faster variant for bipartite matching.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Wasserstein estimation accuracy is a specialised algorithmic topic.

nodes.title: Image as Set of Points
nodes.tldr: Treats an image as an unordered point set and extracts features with a simple clustering algorithm, with no convolution or attention.
nodes.problem: Vision backbones rely on grids or patch sequences; a point-set view of images is unexplored.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical clustering over points with raw features and coordinates, forming context clusters.
nodes.confidence_reason: Backbone architecture; several vision topics fit equally well.
nodes.niche_reason: Clustering-only vision backbone is an unusual alternative to ConvNets and ViTs.

nodes.title: Do We Really Need Complicated Model Architectures For Temporal Networks?
nodes.tldr: GraphMixer shows a simple MLP-based link encoder and mean-pooling node encoder matches or beats RNN and attention models on temporal link prediction.
nodes.problem: Temporal graph models use complicated RNN or attention architectures that may be unnecessary.
nodes.approach: MLP-Mixer-style link encoder, neighbor mean-pooling node encoder, and MLP link classifier.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Temporal graph learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Canary in a Coalmine: Better Membership Inference with Ensembled Adversarial Queries
nodes.tldr: Improves membership inference by optimizing ensembles of adversarial queries that are discriminative and diverse, notably better at low false-positive rates.
nodes.problem: Membership inference using only unaltered samples extracts little information about model behavior.
nodes.approach: Adversarially optimized, ensembled queries per target sample for stronger statistical tests.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Membership inference attacks are an established specialised area.

nodes.title: Adversarial Attacks on Adversarial Bandits
nodes.tldr: Shows an attacker perturbing rewards can force any no-regret adversarial bandit learner onto a target action at sublinear cost.
nodes.problem: Security of adversarial bandit algorithms against an attacker who manipulates rewards.
nodes.approach: Victim-agnostic reward-perturbation attack needing only the regret rate, with a matching cost lower bound.
nodes.niche_reason: attacks on adversarial bandits are a rare angle

nodes.title: Ask Me Anything: A simple strategy for prompting language models
nodes.tldr: Ask Me Anything aggregates several imperfect question-style prompts, reformatted by the LLM itself, with weak supervision to beat few-shot prompting.
nodes.problem: Prompt design is brittle and requires painstaking effort to find a single perfect prompt.
nodes.approach: Generate question-answering prompts per input, collect noisy votes, and combine them via weak supervision.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Prompting strategies for LLMs are a very crowded area.

nodes.title: On the Usefulness of Embeddings, Clusters and Strings for Text Generation Evaluation
nodes.tldr: Shows Mauve works for the wrong reasons: cluster-based approximation with classical divergences can evaluate text generators better than its proposed divergence.
nodes.problem: Unclear why the Mauve metric correlates well with human judgements of generated text.
nodes.approach: Theoretical and empirical analysis plus probing of cluster-based string-distribution divergences using LM embeddings.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Evaluation-metric analysis for text generation is specialised but established.

nodes.title: From Play to Policy: Conditional Behavior Generation from Uncurated Robot Data
nodes.tldr: Conditional Behavior Transformer learns task behaviors from noisy uncurated play data by combining multimodal action generation with future-goal conditioning.
nodes.problem: Uncurated play data is noisy and multimodal, making task behaviors hard to extract.
nodes.approach: Behavior Transformer with future-conditioned goal specification, trained on play data.
nodes.niche_reason: Learning from uncurated play data is relatively uncommon.

nodes.title: Fisher-Legendre (FishLeg) optimization of deep neural networks
nodes.tldr: Learns a direct online model of the inverse Fisher-vector product, enabling natural-gradient steps that beat first-order and match or beat second-order optimizers.
nodes.problem: Natural gradient needs inverting the Fisher, which is intractable for large networks.
nodes.approach: Legendre-Fenchel duality to learn an inverse-Fisher model online from noisy gradients.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned inverse-Fisher natural gradient is specialised

nodes.title: Learning to Grow Pretrained Models for Efficient Transformer Training
nodes.tldr: LiGO learns Kronecker-factorized linear width and depth growth operators mapping a small pretrained transformer to initialize a larger one, saving up to 50% compute.
nodes.problem: Larger transformers are trained from scratch despite existing smaller pretrained counterparts.
nodes.approach: Learn linear width- and depth-growth operators with Kronecker factorization to initialize the larger model.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Model growth for training efficiency is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Relational Attention: Generalizing Transformers for Graph-Structured Tasks
nodes.tldr: Generalizes transformer attention to update edge vectors in each layer, creating a relational transformer that beats GNNs on graph-structured tasks like CLRS.
nodes.problem: Transformers treat inputs as sets and struggle with graph-structured reasoning involving relations.
nodes.approach: Relational attention that attends over and updates node and edge vectors in every layer.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph transformers are established; algorithmic reasoning focus is specialised.

nodes.title: DINO as a von Mises-Fisher mixture model
nodes.tldr: Interprets DINO and iBOT as von Mises-Fisher mixture models and adds proper normalization constants, yielding DINO-vMF with better stability and downstream representations.
nodes.problem: DINO's cluster assignment lacks a probabilistic interpretation and is unstable for larger ViTs with unnormalized prototypes.
nodes.approach: Cast DINO as a vMF mixture and include vMF normalization constants in assignment probabilities.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Self-supervised ViT pre-training is common; probabilistic angle is mildly distinct.

nodes.title: On Representing Linear Programs by Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proves GNNs can represent linear programs, predicting feasibility, boundedness and optimal solutions, via links to the Weisfeiler-Lehman test.
nodes.problem: Theoretical foundations for applying GNNs to solve linear programs are missing.
nodes.approach: Construct GNNs separating LPs and prove expressiveness using Weisfeiler-Lehman connections.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: GNN expressiveness for linear programs is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Learning Probabilistic Topological Representations Using Discrete Morse Theory
nodes.tldr: Learns a probabilistic model over discrete Morse theory structure representations, producing true structures rather than pixel maps for topologically correct segmentation and interactive proofreading.
nodes.problem: Pixel-wise segmentation of fine-scale structures lacks topological integrity, even with topological losses.
nodes.approach: Build a one-parameter family of structures via discrete Morse theory and persistent homology, then learn a probabilistic model over it.
nodes.confidence_reason: Segmentation application versus topological representation learning is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete Morse theory in deep segmentation is very rare.

nodes.title: TabPFN: A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
nodes.tldr: TabPFN is a transformer pretrained on synthetic causal-prior datasets to approximate Bayesian inference, classifying small tabular datasets in one forward pass without tuning.
nodes.problem: Classifying small tabular datasets typically needs slow hyperparameter tuning and AutoML systems.
nodes.approach: Prior-data fitted network trained offline on structural causal model-generated datasets, taking train and test sets as input.
nodes.niche_reason: Tabular foundation models are established but not mainstream.

nodes.title: Neural Lagrangian Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge: Diffusion Modeling for Population Dynamics
nodes.tldr: Models population dynamics as a Lagrangian Schrodinger bridge with a regularized neural SDE, recovering stochastic sample trajectories from coarse snapshots.
nodes.problem: Fixed-point population observations are coarse in time, leaving sample trajectories underdetermined.
nodes.approach: Least-action Lagrangian Schrodinger bridge solved via advection-diffusion neural SDE.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.confidence_reason: Trajectory inference for populations; no direct topic, closest is OT
nodes.niche_reason: Lagrangian Schrodinger bridges for population ecology is rare

nodes.title: Neural Optimal Transport
nodes.tldr: Neural-network algorithm for optimal transport maps and plans under strong and weak costs, with a proof that networks approximate transport plans.
nodes.problem: Computing transport maps and plans for strong and weak costs needs a scalable method.
nodes.approach: Neural networks parameterize transport maps and plans for strong and weak costs, evaluated on toy and image translation tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Neural optimal transport is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Efficient Conditionally Invariant Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: CIRCE is a kernel conditional independence regularizer needing one precomputed ridge regression to learn features independent of a distractor given the target.
nodes.problem: Learning features conditionally independent of a distractor given the label without costly, biased multi-regression penalties.
nodes.approach: Regress kernel features of Z on Y once, then penalize dependence of features on the residuals.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Kernel conditional independence regularization is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Multi-Objective Online Learning
nodes.tldr: Formulates multi-objective online convex optimization with a Pareto-based regret and proposes Doubly Regularized Online Mirror Multiple Descent, matching optimal single-objective regret bounds.
nodes.problem: Single-objective online learning guarantees fail to extend to vector-valued, multi-objective losses.
nodes.approach: Min-regularized-norm gradient composition combined with online mirror descent, with regret analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-objective regret in online convex optimization is a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: Mitigating Gradient Bias in Multi-objective Learning: A Provably Convergent Approach
nodes.tldr: Proposes a stochastic multi-objective gradient correction that removes gradient bias and converges without increasing batch size, even nonconvex.
nodes.problem: Existing stochastic multi-objective gradient methods use biased, noisy update directions
nodes.approach: Gradient correction term for multi-objective stochastic updates with convergence guarantees
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-objective gradient methods are established but specialised

nodes.title: A General Framework for Sample-Efficient Function Approximation in Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Presents OPERA, a sample-efficient RL algorithm under a unified model-based and model-free framework, with regret bounds matching or beating prior results.
nodes.problem: Tractable RL with general function approximation lacks a unifying framework and sample-efficient guarantees.
nodes.approach: Optimization-based exploration with a decomposable estimation function, analysed via functional Eluder dimension.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical RL framework, established but specialised

nodes.title: Can We Find Nash Equilibria at a Linear Rate in Markov Games?
nodes.tldr: A decentralized policy optimization meta-algorithm that interleaves local-fast and global-slow methods to reach Nash equilibria in zero-sum Markov games at a linear rate.
nodes.problem: Independent policy learners in zero-sum Markov games converge only slowly to Nash equilibria.
nodes.approach: Homotopy switching between a globally convergent slow method and a locally fast OGDA method.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Established theoretical line on game-theoretic policy optimization.

nodes.title: Using Language to Extend to Unseen Domains
nodes.tldr: LADS uses text descriptions of source and target domains to learn a CLIP-embedding transformation, extending a classifier to unseen domains without any target images.
nodes.problem: Making vision models robust to unseen domains without collecting training data for each domain.
nodes.approach: Learn image-embedding transformations in a joint vision-language space guided by domain text descriptions, preserving task information.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Common CLIP-based domain adaptation theme with a text-only twist.

nodes.title: Learning where and when to reason in neuro-symbolic inference
nodes.tldr: Pairs a neural predictor with a symbolic reasoning module and an attention module that learns where to reason, outperforming prior methods on visual Sudoku.
nodes.problem: Enforcing hard constraints on network outputs at inference without exhaustive reasoning cost.
nodes.approach: Neural attention directs a symbolic reasoning module toward likely prediction errors.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Neuro-symbolic inference-time reasoning is rare.

nodes.title: Indiscriminate Poisoning Attacks on Unsupervised Contrastive Learning
nodes.tldr: Contrastive Poisoning is an indiscriminate data-poisoning attack that degrades unsupervised contrastive learning and transfers to supervised models, with a matrix-completion defense.
nodes.problem: Indiscriminate poisoning is well studied for supervised learning but unknown for unsupervised contrastive learning.
nodes.approach: Poisoning samples crafted against contrastive objectives; momentum encoders resist, and matrix completion defends.
nodes.niche_reason: poisoning of contrastive learning is a specialised security topic

nodes.title: Domain Generalization via Heckman-type Selection Models
nodes.tldr: Frames domain generalization as sample selection and proposes Selection-Guided DG with Heckman-type estimators that provably achieve lower risk than ERM under nonrandom domain sampling.
nodes.problem: ERM's iid assumption fails when domains are nonrandomly sampled from a common population.
nodes.approach: Learn per-domain selection probabilities and joint outcome-selection distribution via Heckman-type parametric estimators.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Econometric Heckman selection for domain generalization is unusual.

nodes.title: Exploring Temporally Dynamic Data Augmentation for Video Recognition
nodes.tldr: DynaAugment varies augmentation magnitude over time per frame using Fourier Sampling to produce smooth, diverse temporal variation for video recognition training.
nodes.problem: Video augmentation applies the same operations to all frames, ignoring temporal variation of real videos.
nodes.approach: Fourier Sampling parameterizes time-varying augmentation magnitudes, with an extended augmentation search space.
nodes.niche_reason: Video-specific augmentation is less crowded than image augmentation.

nodes.title: Towards Stable Test-time Adaptation in Dynamic Wild World
nodes.tldr: Makes test-time adaptation stable under mixed shifts, small batches, and imbalanced labels by avoiding batch-norm problems, using sharpness-aware and reliable-sample entropy minimization (SAR).
nodes.problem: Online test-time adaptation is unstable under mixed shifts, small batches, and label imbalance.
nodes.approach: Batch-independent normalization plus sharpness-aware reliable entropy minimization filtering noisy samples.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Test-time adaptation is a common topic.

nodes.title: EVA3D: Compositional 3D Human Generation from 2D Image Collections
nodes.tldr: Learns an unconditional 3D human generator from 2D image collections using a compositional body-part NeRF with pose-guided sampling, producing detailed geometry and renders.
nodes.problem: Articulated human bodies are hard to generate in 3D from sparse 2D collections with imbalanced poses.
nodes.approach: Human NeRF divided into local part volumes, trained adversarially with a pose-guided sampling strategy.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Specialized 3D human generation with a compositional prior

nodes.title: Deterministic training of generative autoencoders using invertible layers
nodes.tldr: Trains generative autoencoders deterministically using invertible flow layers instead of stochastic variational inference, yielding sharper samples than VAEs.
nodes.problem: Stochastic variational training of generative autoencoders is noisy and limits sample quality.
nodes.approach: Encoder and decoder as affine layers of an invertible flow, trained by exact maximum likelihood.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Flow-based autoencoder variant; established direction.

nodes.title: Unsupervised Model Selection for Time Series Anomaly Detection
nodes.tldr: Selects the most accurate time-series anomaly detector without labels by aggregating unsupervised surrogate metrics via robust rank aggregation.
nodes.problem: Choosing the best anomaly detector for a dataset is hard without labels.
nodes.approach: Robust rank aggregation of prediction error, model centrality, and synthetic-anomaly performance.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Label-free anomaly detector selection is specialised.

nodes.title: TEMPERA: Test-Time Prompt Editing via Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses reinforcement learning to edit initial prompts per query at test time, covering instructions, exemplars, and verbalizers.
nodes.problem: Zero- and few-shot LLM performance depends heavily on prompt design, which is hard to automate per query.
nodes.approach: RL agent with an action space of prompt edits that adapts an interpretable prompt to each query.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Common prompt optimization direction; RL-based editing is crowded.

nodes.title: Proposal-Contrastive Pretraining for Object Detection from Fewer Data
nodes.tldr: Pretrains object detectors with contrastive learning on the many object proposals a transformer detector produces, enabling small batches and less data.
nodes.problem: Contrastive pretraining needs large batches, yet dense detection benefits from local object-level information.
nodes.approach: Contrastive loss over detector object proposals, with positives chosen by object location, and backbone-head consistency.
nodes.niche_reason: Contrastive detection pretraining is a moderately common niche

nodes.title: Self-Guided Noise-Free Data Generation for Efficient Zero-Shot Learning
nodes.tldr: Improves data-generation-based zero-shot learning by guiding pretrained language models to synthesize cleaner, noise-free training data for small task-specific models.
nodes.problem: PLM-synthesized data for zero-shot learning contains many low-quality, noisy samples.
nodes.approach: Self-guided generation of noise-free synthetic data to train small task models efficiently.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Data-generation zero-shot learning is a specialised paradigm.

nodes.title: On the Sensitivity of Reward Inference to Misspecified Human Models
nodes.tldr: Shows reward inference error can blow up under small adversarial human-model errors, but is bounded linearly under reasonable assumptions.
nodes.problem: How accurate human behavior models must be for reward inference to be reliable.
nodes.approach: Theoretical bounds on reward error versus human-model error, validated on control tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Reward inference under human-model error is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Pink Noise Is All You Need: Colored Noise Exploration in Deep Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows pink (1/f) action noise outperforms white, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and other colored noise for exploration in off-policy continuous-control RL.
nodes.problem: White Gaussian action noise gives insufficient exploration in continuous control.
nodes.approach: Empirical comparison of colored noise families as action noise in SAC and MPO.
nodes.niche_reason: Exploration noise tuning is a common RL direction.

nodes.title: InCoder: A Generative Model for Code Infilling and Synthesis
nodes.tldr: InCoder is a generative code model trained with causal masking so it can both synthesize code left to right and infill arbitrary regions using bidirectional context.
nodes.problem: Code is edited iteratively, but left-to-right models cannot infill regions conditioned on surrounding code.
nodes.approach: Train on code with random spans masked and moved to file end, enabling infilling with bidirectional context.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Code LLMs are common, infilling is a recognised sub-direction.

nodes.title: Divide to Adapt: Mitigating Confirmation Bias for Domain Adaptation of Black-Box Predictors
nodes.tldr: Divide-to-adapt splits the unlabeled target domain into easy and hard samples so cross-domain distillation from a black-box predictor carries less noise.
nodes.problem: Black-box domain adaptation suffers confirmation bias from noisy predictor labels.
nodes.approach: Easy/hard target division with semi-supervised learning and weak-strong augmentation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Black-box domain adaptation is a common, active direction.

nodes.title: Towards Interpretable Deep Reinforcement Learning with Human-Friendly Prototypes
nodes.tldr: Prototype-Wrapper Network wraps any RL agent backbone so decisions rely on human-friendly prototypes, matching black-box performance and improving user trust calibration in a study.
nodes.problem: Black-box deep RL agents are hard to trust in sensitive domains.
nodes.approach: Interpretable-by-design wrapper forcing decisions through learned prototype similarities.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Prototype-based interpretable RL is specialised.

nodes.title: Dual Algorithmic Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Dual Algorithmic Reasoning trains neural algorithmic reasoners jointly on a primal algorithm and its dual, exploiting duality, e.g. max-flow and min-cut.
nodes.problem: Finding similar algorithms to co-train neural reasoners becomes hard for complex problems.
nodes.approach: Joint training on primal and dual algorithm pairs via graph neural networks.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural algorithmic reasoning is a rare subfield.

nodes.title: In-context Reinforcement Learning with Algorithm Distillation
nodes.tldr: Algorithm Distillation trains a causal transformer on RL learning histories so it improves its policy in-context, without parameter updates, more data-efficiently than the source algorithm.
nodes.problem: Making a model perform reinforcement learning in-context rather than via weight updates.
nodes.approach: Autoregressively predict actions from across-episode learning histories generated by a source RL algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: In-context RL is an established but specialised area.

nodes.title: SmartFRZ: An Efficient Training Framework using Attention-Based Layer Freezing
nodes.tldr: Training framework that automatically freezes layers during training using attention-guided criteria, cutting computation and accelerating training without accuracy loss across networks.
nodes.problem: Manual or heuristic layer freezing does not generalize across networks and can hurt accuracy.
nodes.approach: Attention-guided automatic selection of layers to freeze during training.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Attention-guided layer freezing is specialised.

nodes.title: Near-Optimal Adversarial Reinforcement Learning with Switching Costs
nodes.tldr: First provably efficient algorithms for adversarial RL with switching costs, with a regret lower bound and switching-reduced methods that nearly match it.
nodes.problem: Switching costs in adversarial, non-stationary RL had no provably efficient algorithm.
nodes.approach: Regret lower bound plus switching-reduced algorithms matching it, with and without known transitions.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Adversarial RL with switching costs is a rare theory niche.

nodes.title: Confidential-PROFITT: Confidential PROof of FaIr Training of Trees
nodes.tldr: Certifies fair decision-tree training with zero-knowledge proofs so an auditor can verify fairness without seeing the model or training data.
nodes.problem: Post hoc fairness audits are sensitive to test samples and require sharing confidential models.
nodes.approach: Fair tree-learning algorithms with customized zero-knowledge proofs of training fairness.
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual cross-over of cryptographic proofs with fairness auditing

nodes.title: Neuro-Symbolic Procedural Planning with Commonsense Prompting
nodes.tldr: PLAN elicits procedural planning from LLMs with commonsense-infused prompts and symbolic executors framed as causal intervention, reducing spurious goal-step correlations without training.
nodes.problem: LLM procedural planning suffers spurious goal-step correlations and needs manual exemplars.
nodes.approach: Neuro-symbolic prompting using commonsense knowledge bases as causal intervention on a structural causal model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Neuro-symbolic procedural planning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: CLIP-Dissect: Automatic Description of Neuron Representations in Deep Vision Networks
nodes.tldr: Presents CLIP-Dissect, which labels hidden neurons in vision networks with open-ended concepts using a multimodal model, without labeled data, faster than prior methods.
nodes.problem: Describing what individual hidden neurons in vision networks compute usually needs labeled data or human examples.
nodes.approach: Scores neuron activations against CLIP concept similarities to pick the best description.
nodes.niche_reason: Neuron description via CLIP is specialised interpretability work

nodes.title: Learning the Positions in CountSketch
nodes.tldr: Learns both values and nonzero locations of a CountSketch matrix, improving low-rank approximation and Hessian sketching for second-order optimization.
nodes.problem: Prior learned sketches only learn entry values, not where non-zeros sit.
nodes.approach: Greedy and fast gradient-based algorithms that optimize sketch non-zero locations alongside values.
nodes.confidence_reason: Learned sketching straddles algorithms and optimization; a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned sketch positions are a rare learning-augmented algorithms niche.

nodes.title: Rhino: Deep Causal Temporal Relationship Learning with History-dependent Noise
nodes.tldr: Rhino is a deep structural equation model for causal discovery in time series with nonlinear and instantaneous effects and history-dependent noise, with proven identifiability.
nodes.problem: Causal discovery from time series with nonlinear relations, instantaneous effects, and history-dependent noise.
nodes.approach: Combine vector autoregression, deep learning, and variational inference with identifiability proof.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Temporal causal discovery with history-dependent noise is rare.

nodes.title: CodeGen: An Open Large Language Model for Code with Multi-Turn Program Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Releases CodeGen open LLMs up to 16.1B for program synthesis and the Multi-Turn Programming Benchmark, showing multi-turn prompts improve synthesis over single-turn.
nodes.problem: Open large code language models and multi-step program synthesis lacked access and benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Train CodeGen on natural and programming language data; build MTPB with multi-turn factorized prompts.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Code LLMs are a common area.

nodes.title: Continual Unsupervised Disentangling of Self-Organizing Representations
nodes.tldr: A continual generative model with a topologically connected spike-and-slab mixture latent space discovers and accumulates semantic factors across data environments, enabling replay and continual disentanglement.
nodes.problem: Continual unsupervised learning of disentangled representations that reuse and expand semantic factors across environments.
nodes.approach: Self-organizing spike-and-slab mixture latent prior trained with variational inference, with generative replay.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Continual disentangling with SOM-like latent structure is rare.

nodes.title: QuAnt: Quantum Annealing with Learnt Couplings
nodes.tldr: QuAnt learns QUBO couplings from data via backpropagation for quantum annealers, solving graph matching, point alignment and rotation estimation with far fewer qubits.
nodes.problem: Deriving QUBO formulations for vision problems is manual and constrains solution encodings.
nodes.approach: Learn QUBO forms end-to-end with gradient backpropagation through the annealing objective.
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum annealing for vision is extremely rare.

nodes.title: DIFFormer: Scalable (Graph) Transformers Induced by Energy Constrained Diffusion
nodes.tldr: DIFFormer derives scalable transformer encoders from energy-constrained diffusion over instances, with closed-form pairwise diffusion strengths and a linear-complexity variant, for graph and general tasks.
nodes.problem: Instance inter-dependencies violate IID assumptions and complicate learning structured instance representations at scale.
nodes.approach: Energy-constrained diffusion across instances yielding closed-form attention-like diffusion strengths, with linear and advanced instantiations.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans transformers and graph learning; general-purpose encoder claim.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph transformers are established; the diffusion-energy derivation is specialised.

nodes.title: Task-customized Masked Autoencoder via Mixture of Cluster-conditional Experts
nodes.tldr: MoCE trains cluster-conditional experts in a masked autoencoder so each downstream task gets a customized pre-trained model from semantically similar data, reducing negative transfer.
nodes.problem: MAE pre-training suffers negative transfer when downstream data distributions differ from pre-training data.
nodes.approach: Mixture of experts with cluster-conditional gates, each expert trained only on semantically relevant images; tasks routed to best expert.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: MoE applied to MAE pre-training with task customization is specialised.

nodes.title: MIMT: Masked Image Modeling Transformer for Video Compression
nodes.tldr: MIMT replaces raster-order autoregressive entropy models in learned video codecs with a masked transformer that decodes tokens in confidence-driven order, beating VVC.
nodes.problem: Unidirectional autoregressive entropy models are inefficient for learned video compression.
nodes.approach: Masked-token transformer entropy model with spatial-temporal priors, iterative confidence-based parallel decoding, shifted-window attention.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned compression is an established specialised niche.

nodes.title: Visual Classification via Description from Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Classifies images by checking LLM-generated visual descriptors with CLIP-style vision-language models, giving more interpretable zero-shot decisions that can be edited to reduce bias.
nodes.problem: Zero-shot VLM classification by category name gives no explanation and little control over the criteria.
nodes.approach: Query an LLM for class-specific visual descriptors and classify by similarity to those descriptors with a VLM.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-augmented zero-shot CLIP classification is a common direction.

nodes.title: SAM as an Optimal Relaxation of Bayes
nodes.tldr: Shows sharpness-aware minimization is a relaxation of the Bayes objective, yielding an Adam-like variant that gives reasonable uncertainty estimates.
nodes.problem: SAM improves generalization, but its underlying mechanism is not well understood
nodes.approach: Replaces expected negative loss in the Bayes objective with a convex biconjugate bound; derives Adam-like SAM.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised theoretical link between SAM and variational Bayes

nodes.title: Learning Label Encodings for Deep Regression
nodes.tldr: Learns real-valued label encodings end-to-end for regression-by-binary-classification, with a regularizer balancing per-bit error against error correction, beating direct regression by about 11%.
nodes.problem: Good label encodings for binary-coded regression are hard to find and usually hand-designed.
nodes.approach: Continuous relaxation of label encodings trained jointly with the network under a regularization function.
nodes.confidence_reason: Generic regression; no exact topic fits well.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned label encodings for regression are an unusual angle.

nodes.title: A Unified Algebraic Perspective on Lipschitz Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Unifies 1-Lipschitz network layers under a common semidefinite programming condition, deriving SDP-based Lipschitz Layers that improve certified robust accuracy on image classification.
nodes.problem: Existing 1-Lipschitz network designs lack a common theoretical framework for better layer design.
nodes.approach: Algebraic SDP condition generalizing convex potential and AOL layers; Gershgorin-based new parameterizations.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Lipschitz-constrained network design for certification is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: MapTR: Structured Modeling and Learning for Online Vectorized HD Map Construction
nodes.tldr: Camera-only online vectorized HD map construction with a structured Transformer that models map elements as permutation-equivalent point sets.
nodes.problem: Online HD map construction needs accurate, efficient, real-time vectorized map elements from cameras.
nodes.approach: Permutation-equivalent point-set modeling with hierarchical query embeddings and hierarchical bipartite matching.
nodes.niche_reason: Autonomous-driving map construction is a crowded mainstream area

nodes.title: On the duality between contrastive and non-contrastive self-supervised learning
nodes.tldr: Shows contrastive and covariance-based non-contrastive self-supervised criteria are algebraically equivalent under limited assumptions, and that SimCLR can match VICReg with careful tuning.
nodes.problem: Understanding theoretical similarities between contrastive and non-contrastive self-supervised learning.
nodes.approach: Design algebraically related criteria, prove equivalence, and validate by tuning SimCLR and output dimensions.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Self-supervised learning is common, though duality theory is somewhat specialised.

nodes.title: A Minimalist Dataset for Systematic Generalization of Perception, Syntax, and Semantics
nodes.tldr: HINT is a minimalist arithmetic-like dataset testing systematic generalization of perception, syntax, and semantics from weakly supervised raw images.
nodes.problem: Measuring whether models learn generalizable concepts across perception, syntax and semantics.
nodes.approach: Dataset of handwritten-symbol expressions with multi-level generalization splits and baselines.
nodes.niche_reason: Systematic generalization of concepts is a rare cognitive-inspired angle.

nodes.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection and Selective Generation for Conditional Language Models
nodes.tldr: A lightweight OOD detector for conditional language models, enabling selective generation that abstains on low-quality outputs in summarization and translation under distribution shift.
nodes.problem: Conditional language models degrade on OOD inputs and it is unclear when to trust generated outputs.
nodes.approach: Accurate lightweight OOD detection scores used to selectively generate or abstain.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: OOD detection for generation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Warping the Space: Weight Space Rotation for Class-Incremental Few-Shot Learning
nodes.tldr: WaRP rotates weight space so new-class finetuning minimally disrupts old knowledge, reducing forgetting in class-incremental few-shot learning.
nodes.problem: Catastrophic forgetting and overfitting in class-incremental few-shot learning.
nodes.approach: Weight space rotation process that isolates parameters important for previous classes.
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot continual learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: A probabilistic framework for task-aligned intra- and inter-area neural manifold estimation
nodes.tldr: TAME-GP is a probabilistic latent model partitioning neural population variability into private and shared, task-relevant and irrelevant parts, with Poisson noise and GP temporal smoothing.
nodes.problem: Existing neural manifold tools lack task-aligned interpretability and struggle without trial repeats across brain areas.
nodes.approach: Graphical model with Poisson observations, private and shared latents split by task relevance, and Gaussian Process priors.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Neural population latent modeling is a specialised cross-disciplinary niche.

nodes.title: Modeling content creator incentives on algorithm-curated platforms
nodes.tldr: The exposure game models content creators competing for user attention under recommender algorithms, showing that design choices change equilibria, and proposes pre-deployment audits.
nodes.problem: Recommender algorithms induce strategic content creator behavior that can misalign incentives.
nodes.approach: Formalization of Nash equilibrium creator competition for factorization and two-tower models, with numerical audits on MovieLens and LastFM.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Creator strategic incentives in recommenders is an unusual game-theoretic angle.

nodes.title: Binding Language Models in Symbolic Languages
nodes.tldr: Binder is a training-free neural-symbolic framework where Codex generates programs with embedded LM API calls, achieving state-of-the-art table question answering with few exemplars.
nodes.problem: End-to-end neural QA lacks interpretability, and symbolic languages lack coverage for diverse questions.
nodes.approach: Few-shot prompted Codex parses to SQL/Python with LM API calls, executed by the same LM.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Neural-symbolic table QA is specialised though active.

nodes.title: Efficient recurrent architectures through activity sparsity and sparse back-propagation through time
nodes.tldr: Extends GRUs with threshold-triggered discrete events so communication and backpropagation through time scale with event count, giving efficient, neuromorphic-friendly recurrent models.
nodes.problem: RNN training and inference are inefficient because all activations propagate at every time step.
nodes.approach: Event-emitting GRU units with activity sparsity and sparse backpropagation through time.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.confidence_reason: Recurrent efficiency paper spans compression, sparsity, and sequence-model topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Event-based sparse RNNs for neuromorphic hardware are uncommon.

nodes.title: Decompositional Generation Process for Instance-Dependent Partial Label Learning
nodes.tldr: Partial label learning method that explicitly models how candidate label sets are generated per instance in two steps, then performs MAP inference.
nodes.problem: Partial-label methods assume random candidate generation, ignoring instance-dependent annotation noise.
nodes.approach: Decomposed probabilistic model of candidate label generation with MAP inference.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: No weak-supervision topic; probabilistic fit is closest.
nodes.niche_reason: Instance-dependent partial label learning is niche.

nodes.title: Emergence of Maps in the Memories of Blind Navigation Agents
nodes.tldr: Shows blind RL navigation agents, sensing only egomotion, build implicit maps and collision neurons, with no mapping bias built in.
nodes.problem: Whether navigation agents without mapping inductive bias still build internal maps.
nodes.approach: Train blind PointGoal agents with recurrent networks via RL and probe their memory representations.
nodes.niche_reason: Emergent maps in blind agents is a rare angle.

nodes.title: Graph Neural Networks for Link Prediction with Subgraph Sketching
nodes.tldr: ELPH passes subgraph sketches as messages to approximate subgraph GNNs for link prediction efficiently, and BUDDY scales it via feature precomputation.
nodes.problem: GNNs underperform at link prediction; subgraph methods are expressive but slow.
nodes.approach: Hashing-based subgraph sketches as message passing, with precomputed features for scalability.
nodes.niche_reason: Link prediction GNN expressivity is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Turning the Curse of Heterogeneity in Federated Learning into a Blessing for Out-of-Distribution Detection
nodes.tldr: FOSTER uses other clients' heterogeneous classes as outliers, training a class-conditional generator to synthesize virtual OOD samples for federated OOD detection.
nodes.problem: OOD detection needs real outlier data, which is costly or infeasible on resource-limited federated clients.
nodes.approach: Learns a class-conditional generator that synthesizes virtual external-class samples, preserving data confidentiality and communication efficiency.
nodes.confidence_reason: Federated setting and OOD detection both fit; judgment call on primary.
nodes.niche_reason: Turning federated data heterogeneity into OOD supervision is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Zero-Shot Image Restoration Using Denoising Diffusion Null-Space Model
nodes.tldr: Zero-shot framework for arbitrary linear image restoration that refines only null-space content of a pretrained diffusion model, enforcing data consistency.
nodes.problem: Image restoration models are task-specific and do not generalize across degradation operators.
nodes.approach: Null-space refinement during reverse diffusion with an off-the-shelf generative prior.
nodes.niche_reason: Zero-shot restoration with diffusion priors is established but specialised

nodes.title: PaLI: A Jointly-Scaled Multilingual Language-Image Model
nodes.tldr: PaLI is a jointly scaled multilingual language-image model combining large encoder-decoder LMs and a 4B-parameter ViT, trained on a 10B-image multilingual dataset for captioning, VQA, and scene-text tasks.
nodes.problem: Building a scalable multilingual model jointly handling vision, language and multimodal tasks.
nodes.approach: Jointly scale ViT-e and encoder-decoder language model on a multilingual image-text pretraining mix.
nodes.niche_reason: Large-scale VLM pretraining is common, though multilingual angle is slightly distinct.

nodes.title: A CMDP-within-online framework for Meta-Safe Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: A meta-algorithm for safe RL that learns across tasks in a CMDP-within-online framework, giving task-averaged regret and constraint-violation guarantees that improve with task similarity.
nodes.problem: Meta-RL ignores constraint violations, limiting use in safety-critical settings.
nodes.approach: Online gradient-based meta-learning over CMDPs with off-policy stationary distribution corrections and adaptive learning rates.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: Rare combination of meta-learning, constrained MDPs and online regret theory.

nodes.title: Efficiently Computing Nash Equilibria in Adversarial Team Markov Games
nodes.tldr: First polynomial-time algorithm for approximate Nash equilibria in adversarial team Markov games, using independent team policy gradients plus adversary best responses via linear programming.
nodes.problem: Computing Nash equilibria efficiently in team-versus-adversary Markov games, where general-sum intractability blocks guarantees.
nodes.approach: Independent policy gradient for team players combined with adversary best response obtained by solving a constructed linear program.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised game-theoretic RL theory, established subcommunity.

nodes.title: EA-HAS-Bench: Energy-aware Hyperparameter and Architecture Search Benchmark
nodes.tldr: Benchmark for energy-aware joint hyperparameter and architecture search, with a surrogate predicting learning curves via Bezier curves.
nodes.problem: AutoML search consumes large energy, and energy-aware NAS lacks reproducible benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Large joint search space with energy-related configurations, a Bezier-curve surrogate, and an energy-aware AutoML wrapper.
nodes.niche_reason: Energy-aware NAS benchmarks are a rare, sustainability-driven niche.

nodes.title: Partially Observable RL with B-Stability: Unified Structural Condition and Sharp Sample-Efficient Algorithms
nodes.tldr: Introduces B-stability, a unified structural condition for predictive state representations, showing polynomial sample-efficient learning of partially observable RL via three algorithms.
nodes.problem: Lack of unified conditions and sharp sample complexities for learnable partially observable RL.
nodes.approach: B-stability for PSRs analyzed with optimistic MLE, Estimation-to-Decisions, and model-based optimistic posterior sampling.
nodes.niche_reason: PSR/POMDP learnability theory is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Post-hoc Concept Bottleneck Models
nodes.tldr: Post-hoc concept bottleneck models turn an existing network into an interpretable concept model, and allow concept-level edits to fix spurious correlations.
nodes.problem: Concept bottleneck models need dense concept labels and often lose accuracy relative to unrestricted networks.
nodes.approach: Learn a concept layer on an existing network, transferring concepts from other datasets or language via multimodal models.
nodes.niche_reason: Post-hoc concept bottlenecks are a specialised interpretability niche.

nodes.title: Minimalistic Unsupervised Representation Learning with the Sparse Manifold Transform
nodes.tldr: A minimalist white-box unsupervised representation method combining sparse coding, manifold learning and slow feature analysis that nearly matches self-supervised baselines without augmentation.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised representation learning usually needs heavy augmentation and engineering; simple white-box methods lag.
nodes.approach: One-layer sparse manifold transform trained in a single epoch; shown to be a simple form of VICReg.
nodes.confidence_reason: White-box sparse method sits close to self-supervised learning
nodes.niche_reason: White-box sparse-manifold alternative to mainstream SSL is unusual

nodes.title: IS SYNTHETIC DATA FROM GENERATIVE MODELS READY FOR IMAGE RECOGNITION?
