nodes.tldr: Empirically studies whether text-to-image synthetic images can train recognition models, showing gains in zero/few-shot and pretraining but noting shortcomings, and proposing strategies.
nodes.problem: Unclear whether images from state-of-the-art text-to-image models are useful for recognition tasks.
nodes.approach: Evaluates generated images in zero-shot, few-shot, and large-scale pretraining settings and proposes strategies for using them.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Synthetic data for vision is an active, crowded area.

nodes.title: The Influence of Learning Rule on Representation Dynamics in Wide Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Uses dynamical mean field theory on infinite-width networks to compare representation dynamics under gradient descent and biologically plausible rules like feedback alignment and Hebbian learning.
nodes.problem: How the learning rule changes feature learning and representation dynamics in wide networks.
nodes.approach: Derive time-varying effective NTK and DMFT for GD, feedback alignment, direct feedback alignment, Hebb and gated linear networks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: DMFT analysis of bio-plausible learning rules is rare.

nodes.title: PiFold: Toward effective and efficient protein inverse folding
nodes.tldr: One-shot protein sequence design for a target structure using a residue featurizer and graph layers, 70x faster than autoregressive methods with better recovery.
nodes.problem: Structure-based protein design is slow and inaccurate due to weak features and autoregressive decoders.
nodes.approach: Novel residue featurizer with PiGNN graph layers that decode the whole sequence in one pass.
nodes.niche_reason: Protein inverse folding is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Concept-level Debugging of Part-Prototype Networks
nodes.tldr: Lets a human supervisor give concept-level feedback on which part-prototypes to keep or forget, fine-tuning ProtoPNets to drop confounders at low annotation cost.
nodes.problem: Part-prototype networks learn confounders and shortcuts, hurting accuracy and generalization.
nodes.approach: Human feedback on learned part-prototypes used to fine-tune the model toward confounder-free concepts.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Concept-level debugging of prototype networks is specialised

nodes.title: One-Pixel Shortcut: On the Learning Preference of Deep Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Perturbing a single pixel per image, at a class-wise fixed position and value, makes unlearnable examples that survive adversarial training and augmentation.
nodes.problem: Unlearnable examples protecting data are easily removed by adversarial training and augmentations.
nodes.approach: Class-wise one-pixel perturbation chosen to deviate from original images, creating shortcut features and the CIFAR-10-S dataset.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Unlearnable examples form an established but specialised data-protection niche.

nodes.title: Transfer NAS with Meta-learned Bayesian Surrogates
nodes.tldr: Meta-learns a Bayesian optimization surrogate (deep-kernel GP with graph and dataset encoders) across prior evaluations to transfer NAS knowledge, matching one-shot NAS speed.
nodes.problem: NAS is costly or non-robust and starts from scratch, ignoring prior knowledge from related datasets.
nodes.approach: Deep-kernel Gaussian process surrogate with GNN architecture embeddings and transformer set encoder, meta-learned across datasets.
nodes.niche_reason: Meta-learned Bayesian NAS is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Diffusion Models Already Have A Semantic Latent Space
nodes.tldr: Finds a semantic latent space, h-space, inside frozen pretrained diffusion models via an asymmetric reverse process, enabling controllable image editing.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models lack a semantic latent space needed to control the generative process.
nodes.approach: Asymmetric reverse process discovers a semantic h-space in frozen pretrained diffusion models.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion editing is common; h-space analysis is somewhat specialized.

nodes.title: Vision Transformer Adapter for Dense Predictions
nodes.tldr: ViT-Adapter adds a pre-training-free adapter injecting vision-specific inductive biases into plain ViT, matching specialised backbones on detection and segmentation.
nodes.problem: Plain ViT underperforms on dense prediction due to weak image priors.
nodes.approach: Spatial prior module and cross-attention injectors/extractors adapting a plain ViT without changing its pretraining.
nodes.niche_reason: Common vision backbone adaptation topic.

nodes.title: Domain-Indexing Variational Bayes: Interpretable Domain Index for Domain Adaptation
nodes.tldr: Defines domain index probabilistically and infers interpretable domain indices from multi-domain data with an adversarial variational Bayes framework, improving domain adaptation.
nodes.problem: Domain adaptation gains need domain indices, which are often unavailable
nodes.approach: Adversarial variational Bayesian inference of latent domain indices
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Latent domain-index inference is specialised within domain adaptation

nodes.title: Learning on Large-scale Text-attributed Graphs via Variational Inference
nodes.tldr: GLEM fuses LLMs and GNNs on large text-attributed graphs via variational EM, alternately updating each module so they train separately yet reinforce each other.
nodes.problem: Jointly training LLMs and GNNs on large text-attributed graphs is computationally prohibitive
nodes.approach: Variational EM alternating between language model and GNN updates
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Text-attributed graph learning is established but specialised

nodes.title: Towards Effective and Interpretable Human-Agent Collaboration in MOBA Games: A Communication Perspective
nodes.tldr: MCC enables human-agent collaboration in MOBA games via an interpretable Meta-Command communication protocol and a selector estimating the most valuable command per agent.
nodes.problem: Game AI focuses on competing with humans rather than collaborating with them in MOBA games.
nodes.approach: Meta-Command communication protocol plus a value-based Meta-Command Selector trained with deep RL.
nodes.niche_reason: Human-AI collaboration in MOBA games is a rare topic.

nodes.title: Disparate Impact in Differential Privacy from Gradient Misalignment
nodes.tldr: Finds gradient misalignment from unequal clipping drives DPSGD's disparate impact on groups, and proposes a method that prevents it to reduce unfairness.
nodes.problem: Differentially private SGD worsens disparate impact across groups in the data.
nodes.approach: Identify inequitable gradient clipping as the cause and prevent gradient misalignment.
nodes.niche_reason: Fairness costs of DP-SGD is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Rethinking the Expressive Power of GNNs via Graph Biconnectivity
nodes.tldr: Introduces biconnectivity-based expressivity metrics for GNNs, finds most architectures fail them, and proposes GD-WL, a provably expressive Transformer-like model.
nodes.problem: Beyond-WL expressive power of GNNs is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Biconnectivity metrics and Generalized Distance Weisfeiler-Lehman (GD-WL) with a Transformer-like implementation.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Beyond-WL GNN expressivity is a specialised theory niche.

nodes.title: Clean-image Backdoor: Attacking Multi-label Models with Poisoned Labels Only
nodes.tldr: First clean-image backdoor attack: poisons only training labels of multi-label models, using searched triggers and target-label strategies, reaching 98% attack success while evading defenses.
nodes.problem: Backdoor attacks on multi-label models require modifying training images, which is impractical in many real settings.
nodes.approach: Manipulate annotations of samples with specific class sets as triggers, with trigger exploration and target label selection strategies.
nodes.niche_reason: Backdoor attacks are established; label-only multi-label variant is specialised.

nodes.title: Denoising Diffusion Error Correction Codes
nodes.tldr: Uses denoising diffusion models for soft decoding of linear error-correcting codes, conditioned on parity-error counts with a syndrome-based reverse step size.
nodes.problem: Neural ECC decoders are complex and lack the iterative structure of classical decoders.
nodes.approach: Diffusion process over channel corruption, parity-error conditioning, and syndrome line search for step size.
nodes.confidence_reason: Communications application not in taxonomy; diffusion vs systems
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based channel decoding is a rare cross-disciplinary application.

nodes.title: Programmatically Grounded, Compositionally Generalizable Robotic Manipulation
nodes.tldr: Modular manipulation policy that parses instructions into an executable program of grounded vision-action modules, disentangling perception from action for zero-shot compositional generalization.
nodes.problem: Standard VL-pretraining entangles action and visual learning, hurting generalization to new objects and tasks.
nodes.approach: Semantic parser produces a program of neural and deterministic modules driving manipulation primitives.
nodes.confidence_reason: Modular program grounding could also be task planning.
nodes.niche_reason: Modular program-grounded manipulation is specialised.

nodes.title: The Trade-off between Universality and Label Efficiency of Representations from Contrastive Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves a trade-off between universality and label efficiency in contrastively pretrained representations with linear probing, and proposes a contrastive regularization to improve it.
nodes.problem: Pretrained representations cannot simultaneously be universal across tasks and label-efficient for downstream tasks.
nodes.approach: Theoretical data-model analysis of contrastive learning with linear probing, plus contrastive regularizer.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of contrastive representation trade-offs is established but specialised.

nodes.title: ZiCo: Zero-shot NAS via inverse Coefficient of Variation on Gradients
nodes.tldr: Proposes ZiCo, a training-free zero-shot NAS proxy based on gradient statistics, shown to beat parameter count and prior proxies.
nodes.problem: Zero-shot NAS proxies often fail to beat simply counting network parameters.
nodes.approach: Inverse coefficient of variation of per-sample gradients used as a training-free architecture score.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Zero-shot NAS proxies are a specialised but established subfield.

nodes.title: Few-shot Cross-domain Image Generation via Inference-time Latent-code Learning
nodes.tldr: Adapts a frozen pretrained GAN to new domains from few samples by training a small latent-generation network at inference time.
nodes.problem: Pretrained GANs struggle to generate out-of-distribution target domains with scarce data
nodes.approach: Embed target samples into the source GAN latent space with a per-batch latent-generation network.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Frozen-GAN few-shot domain generation is specialised

nodes.title: Learning About Progress From Experts
nodes.tldr: Learns a monotonically increasing progress function from expert observation-only gameplay to guide exploration in sparse-reward NetHack tasks.
nodes.problem: Long-horizon sparse-reward tasks are too hard for exploration without progress signals.
nodes.approach: Expert observation-only demonstrations used to learn a progress estimator that shapes exploration.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Progress learning for NetHack is a specialised setting.

nodes.title: Is Conditional Generative Modeling all you need for Decision Making?
nodes.tldr: Recasts decision-making as return-conditioned generative modeling, avoiding dynamic programming, and shows the policy can also be conditioned on constraints or skills to compose behaviors.
nodes.problem: Offline RL relies on dynamic programming, which brings many complexities for sequential decision-making.
nodes.approach: Return-conditioned generative policy trained by supervised conditional modeling, conditioned on constraints or skills.
nodes.confidence_reason: Offline RL or conditional generative policy; topic straddles both areas.
nodes.niche_reason: Generative modeling as decision-making is an unusual RL framing

nodes.title: Temporal Domain Generalization with Drift-Aware Dynamic Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Temporal domain generalization framework that models drift in data and model dynamics with a Bayesian recurrent graph generator, predicting future models without future data.
nodes.problem: Models trained on temporally drifting data fail to generalize to unseen future distributions.
nodes.approach: Joint Bayesian modeling of data and model dynamics, with recurrent generation of dynamic graph-structured networks.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Temporal drift spans domain generalization and dynamic networks.
nodes.niche_reason: Temporal domain generalization with drift-aware networks is rare.

nodes.title: Semi-Implicit Variational Inference via Score Matching
nodes.tldr: SIVI-SM trains semi-implicit variational families with a score matching minimax objective, avoiding surrogate ELBOs and inner MCMC, and matches MCMC accuracy on Bayesian inference tasks.
nodes.problem: Semi-implicit variational inference has intractable densities, forcing surrogate ELBOs or costly inner-loop MCMC.
nodes.approach: Denoising score matching minimax objective exploiting hierarchical structure of semi-implicit distributions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Semi-implicit VI is a rare specialised niche.

nodes.title: PAC-NeRF: Physics Augmented Continuum Neural Radiance Fields for Geometry-Agnostic System Identification
nodes.tldr: PAC-NeRF estimates unknown geometry and physical parameters of dynamic objects from multi-view videos by constraining a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian NeRF with continuum mechanics.
nodes.problem: System identification from video assumes known object geometry, which is rarely available.
nodes.approach: Hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian radiance field coupled with differentiable material point method physics.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-grounded NeRF for parameter identification is a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Pre-training via Denoising for Molecular Property Prediction
nodes.tldr: Pretrains molecular encoders by denoising 3D equilibrium structures, which learns a force field, to set new QM9 property prediction results.
nodes.problem: Molecular property prediction from 3D structures has limited labeled data, hurting generalization.
nodes.approach: Denoising pre-training on equilibrium conformations, linked to score matching and a Gaussian-mixture Boltzmann approximation.
nodes.niche_reason: denoising pretraining for molecules, specialised

nodes.title: The In-Sample Softmax for Offline Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses an in-sample softmax over dataset actions to avoid out-of-distribution maximization in offline RL, giving a convergent In-Sample Actor-Critic that also suits fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Bootstrapping with the max operator in offline RL selects unseen actions, causing overestimation.
nodes.approach: Policy iteration with in-sample softmax approximating in-sample max; derive In-Sample Actor-Critic.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL value-regularization methods are common.

nodes.title: When Source-Free Domain Adaptation Meets Learning with Noisy Labels
nodes.tldr: Analyzes source-free domain adaptation as learning with noisy labels, showing SFDA noise differs from conventional noise and exploiting early-time training phenomenon to improve SFDA methods.
nodes.problem: Pseudo-label noise in source-free domain adaptation breaks standard noisy-label methods
nodes.approach: Theoretical noise analysis and early-time training phenomenon based regularization
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Source-free adaptation is established but specialised

nodes.title: Adversarial Diversity in Hanabi
nodes.tldr: ADVERSITY generates diverse yet reasonable Hanabi agents using off-belief learning for skill and repulsive fictitious transitions for diversity, releasing agents for ad-hoc coordination research.
nodes.problem: Producing diverse Dec-POMDP policies that are also high-performing and reasonable.
nodes.approach: Off-belief learning combined with repulsive fictitious transitions to encourage diverse playstyles.
nodes.niche_reason: Cooperative game diversity is specialised but established in MARL.

nodes.title: REVISITING PRUNING AT INITIALIZATION THROUGH THE LENS OF RAMANUJAN GRAPH
nodes.tldr: Analyzes pruning-at-initialization through Ramanujan graph properties, shows the property does not predict performance, and proposes IMDB and NaRC metrics that track performance.
nodes.problem: Pruning at initialization lags post-training pruning, and Ramanujan-graph properties do not explain its performance.
nodes.approach: Analyzes sparse networks via the Ramanujan property, introducing IMDB and NaRC metrics that relax and bound the eigenvalue assumption.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Graph-theoretic analysis of pruning at initialization is an unusual lens.

nodes.title: Offline RL with No OOD Actions: In-Sample Learning via Implicit Value Regularization
nodes.tldr: Shows in-sample offline RL methods implicitly regularize values, and proposes SQL and EQL, which are sparser and more robust to noisy data than IQL.
nodes.problem: Offline RL must avoid out-of-distribution actions when learning value functions.
nodes.approach: Implicit value regularization framework yielding fully in-sample Q-learning variants (SQL, EQL).
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL value regularization is a crowded area; in-sample variants are common.

nodes.title: On the complexity of nonsmooth automatic differentiation
nodes.tldr: Bounds the computational cost of backward-mode automatic differentiation for nonsmooth programs, showing dimension-independent overhead via conservative gradients.
nodes.problem: Backward-mode autodiff cost for nonsmooth programs is unclear, especially versus forward-mode overhead.
nodes.approach: Conservative-gradient complexity model showing dimension-independent backward overhead for semi-algebraic programs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.confidence_reason: Complexity theory of autodiff; could also fit optimization or differentiable programming
nodes.niche_reason: Complexity of nonsmooth autodiff is a rare theoretical niche

nodes.title: Generative Augmented Flow Networks
nodes.tldr: GAFlowNets augment Generative Flow Networks with intermediate intrinsic rewards, enabling learning in sparse-reward settings beyond terminal rewards and improving exploration.
nodes.problem: GFlowNets only learn from terminal rewards, limiting use in sparse-reward tasks.
nodes.approach: Edge-based intrinsic rewards integrated into flow-matching objectives for GFlowNets.
nodes.niche_reason: GFlowNets are a small research community.

nodes.title: Modeling the Data-Generating Process is Necessary for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
nodes.tldr: Shows no single fixed invariance constraint works across all distribution shifts, and proposes adaptive constraint minimization guided by the data-generating process.
nodes.problem: Domain generalization methods fail inconsistently across multi-attribute distribution shifts.
nodes.approach: Causal graph analysis selects which independence constraints to regularize per shift type.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal approaches to domain generalization are specialised

nodes.title: Depth Separation with Multilayer Mean-Field Networks
nodes.tldr: Shows the depth-separating function of Safran et al. is efficiently learnable by an overparametrised multilayer mean-field network, making depth separation algorithmic.
nodes.problem: Why deeper networks beat shallow ones, and whether such separation holds for learning rather than representation.
nodes.approach: Extend mean-field limit to multilayer networks and decompose loss to control discretisation error.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: established deep learning theory question

nodes.title: Outcome-directed Reinforcement Learning by Uncertainty \& Temporal Distance-Aware Curriculum Goal Generation
nodes.tldr: Outcome-directed RL generates curriculum goals through bipartite matching using uncertainty and temporal-distance awareness to guide exploration toward desired outcomes.
nodes.problem: Exploration in RL when desired outcomes are rarely observed and curricula lack calibrated guidance.
nodes.approach: Curriculum goal generation by bipartite matching with uncertainty and temporal-distance estimates.
nodes.niche_reason: Curriculum goal-conditioned RL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Retrieval-based Controllable Molecule Generation
nodes.tldr: Steers a pre-trained molecule generator toward design criteria by retrieving and fusing a small set of exemplar molecules, with no task-specific fine-tuning and iterative database refinement.
nodes.problem: Controllable molecule generation needs large datasets and fine-tuning that real design tasks lack.
nodes.approach: Retrieval mechanism fusing exemplars with input molecule, trained by nearest-neighbor self-supervision, with iterative refinement.
nodes.niche_reason: Retrieval-augmented molecular generation is specialised.

nodes.title: Crossformer: Transformer Utilizing Cross-Dimension Dependency for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
nodes.tldr: Crossformer is a Transformer for multivariate time series forecasting that uses two-stage attention to model both cross-time and cross-variable dependencies in a hierarchical encoder-decoder.
nodes.problem: Transformer forecasters ignore dependencies among different variables in multivariate time series.
nodes.approach: Dimension-segment-wise embedding, two-stage attention over time and dimension, hierarchical encoder-decoder.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Time series transformers are a common, active subarea.

nodes.title: WikiWhy: Answering and Explaining Cause-and-Effect Questions
nodes.tldr: Introduces WikiWhy, a benchmark of 9,000+ why-questions requiring answers plus natural-language rationales, showing GPT-3 struggles.
nodes.problem: Existing QA benchmarks poorly test LLM reasoning, since they cover narrow situations and subjects.
nodes.approach: Cause-and-effect QA dataset built on Wikipedia facts, requiring explicit supporting-statement rationales.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Explanation-based QA benchmarks are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Transformers are Sample-Efficient World Models
nodes.tldr: Sample-efficient agent that learns in imagination inside a world model of a discrete autoencoder and autoregressive Transformer, reaching above-human mean score on Atari 100k.
nodes.problem: Model-free agents need huge samples; learned world models must stay accurate over time.
nodes.approach: Discrete autoencoder tokenizes frames; autoregressive Transformer models dynamics for imagined rollouts.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: World-model agents on Atari 100k are a crowded benchmark area.

nodes.title: Moving Forward by Moving Backward: Embedding Action Impact over Action Semantics
nodes.tldr: Action Adaptive Policy models action impact via latent embeddings and a transformer policy head, letting embodied navigation agents handle unseen or perturbed action spaces.
nodes.problem: Embodied agents assume actions have stable effects, failing when action impact changes, such as broken wheels.
nodes.approach: Latent action impact embeddings combined with a transformer-based policy head, evaluated in AI2-THOR and Habitat.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Adapting to altered action semantics at inference is unusual.

nodes.title: AANG : Automating Auxiliary Learning
nodes.tldr: Automatically generates and searches auxiliary learning objectives via a unified taxonomy, with theory on generalization, showing gains on NLP end-tasks.
nodes.problem: Auxiliary objectives are hand-designed slowly, and their benefit lacks theoretical grounding.
nodes.approach: Unified objective taxonomy, generated auxiliary objectives, and an efficient search guided by stability theory.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Auxiliary objective search straddles AutoML and transfer learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Auxiliary objective search is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Minimum Variance Unbiased N:M Sparsity for the Neural Gradients
nodes.tldr: Shows MSE-optimal N:M pruning fails for neural gradients and designs unbiased minimum-variance masks, enabling 1:2 or 2:4 sparse gradient computation for faster training.
nodes.problem: N:M sparsity was used for weights but not for neural gradients, where MSE pruning fails.
nodes.approach: Derive tensor-level optimality criteria and design unbiased minimum-variance pruning masks.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Structured sparsity for training gradients is specialised.

nodes.title: The Modality Focusing Hypothesis: Towards Understanding Crossmodal Knowledge Distillation
nodes.tldr: Analyzes why crossmodal knowledge distillation works or fails, introducing the modality Venn diagram and the modality focusing hypothesis as the decisive factor for efficacy.
nodes.problem: The working mechanism of crossmodal knowledge distillation is unexplained, and it sometimes fails.
nodes.approach: Failure cases, a modality Venn diagram framework, and the modality focusing hypothesis tested on multimodal datasets.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: Split between representation learning and cross-modal learning.
nodes.niche_reason: Theoretical understanding of crossmodal distillation is a rare analysis topic.

nodes.title: Sparse MoE as the New Dropout: Scaling Dense and Self-Slimmable Transformers
nodes.tldr: SMoE-Dropout trains dense transformers with a fixed random router that gradually activates more experts, yielding better accuracy and self-slimmable inference.
nodes.problem: Sparse MoE suffers redundant experts and poor expert-count scalability at inference and fine-tuning.
nodes.approach: Randomly initialized fixed router with progressively increasing number of activated experts during training.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: MoE training variants are established but specialised.

nodes.title: A Closer Look at Model Adaptation using Feature Distortion and Simplicity Bias
nodes.tldr: Analyzes linear probing, fine-tuning and LP+FT through feature distortion and simplicity bias, proposing modified linear probes that improve OOD generalization and safety metrics.
nodes.problem: Adaptation protocols behave differently on safety objectives, and feature distortion alone does not explain this.
nodes.approach: Study simplicity bias in LP/FT/LP+FT on synthetic data, then propose modified linear probes for better initialization.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Adaptation protocol analysis is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Unmasking the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: What's Encoded in a Winning Ticket's Mask?
nodes.tldr: Explains lottery tickets via error landscape geometry: IMP masks identify linearly connected modes, SGD tolerates early perturbation, and flatness limits per-iteration pruning.
nodes.problem: Why and when iterative magnitude pruning finds sparse matching subnetworks remains unclear.
nodes.approach: Linear mode connectivity and Hessian eigenspectrum analysis of IMP masks and retraining.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Lottery ticket analysis is an established, specialised subarea.

nodes.title: ROSCOE: A Suite of Metrics for Scoring Step-by-Step Reasoning
nodes.tldr: ROSCOE is a suite of unsupervised metrics scoring step-by-step reasoning chains on consistency, logicality, informativeness and factuality, validated against a typology of reasoning errors.
nodes.problem: No reliable automatic way to evaluate reasoning step correctness independent of final answers.
nodes.approach: Interpretable unsupervised scores plus error typology and human and synthetic diagnostic datasets for validation.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Common reasoning-evaluation topic.

nodes.title: VA-DepthNet: A Variational Approach to Single Image Depth Prediction
nodes.tldr: VA-DepthNet imposes classical first-order variational constraints on depth gradients within an encoder-decoder network, improving supervised single-image depth prediction.
nodes.problem: Supervised single-image depth networks overlook scene regularity priors like depth gradient smoothness.
nodes.approach: First-order variational constraints in scene space integrated into an encoder-decoder depth network.
nodes.niche_reason: Monocular depth is established; variational priors give a specialised angle.

nodes.title: ExpressivE: A Spatio-Functional Embedding For Knowledge Graph Completion
nodes.tldr: ExpressivE embeds relations as spatio-functional regions to jointly model composition, hierarchy and other patterns for KG completion, with geometric interpretability.
nodes.problem: KG embeddings cannot jointly capture inference patterns like composition and hierarchy interpretably.
nodes.approach: Embed entity pairs as points and relations as hyper-parallelograms in virtual triple space.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Knowledge Graphs & Relational Learning
nodes.niche_reason: KG embedding is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Neural Collapse Inspired Feature-Classifier Alignment for Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
nodes.tldr: Pre-assigns a fixed simplex equiangular tight frame of classifier prototypes so features align with classifiers across incremental sessions, reducing forgetting.
nodes.problem: Few-shot class-incremental learning suffers feature-classifier misalignment, causing catastrophic forgetting of old classes.
nodes.approach: Neural-collapse-inspired fixed classifier prototypes with a loss driving features toward them.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised continual-learning niche built on neural collapse theory

nodes.title: Sparsity-Constrained Optimal Transport
nodes.tldr: Optimal transport with explicit cardinality constraints on the plan, solvable by first-order methods, motivated by matching tokens to experts in sparse mixture of experts.
nodes.problem: Regularized OT lacks direct control over sparsity of the transportation plan.
nodes.approach: Cardinality-constrained OT with tractable (semi) dual problems solved by gradient methods.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised OT regularization with explicit cardinality control.

nodes.title: Continuized Acceleration for Quasar Convex Functions in Non-Convex Optimization
nodes.tldr: Applies continuized Nesterov acceleration to quasar-convex functions, reaching the optimal gradient-evaluation bound with high probability, and shows GLM training is quasar-convex.
nodes.problem: Accelerated methods for quasar-convex functions need binary search, missing the lower bound.
nodes.approach: Continuized Nesterov acceleration without binary-search subroutines.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Accelerated methods for quasar-convex nonconvex objectives are a rare optimization niche.

nodes.title: Phase2vec: dynamical systems embedding with a physics-informed convolutional network
nodes.tldr: Phase2vec learns physically meaningful embeddings of low-dimensional dynamical systems from flow data with a convolutional network and vector-field reconstruction loss, encoding stability and conservation properties.
nodes.problem: Predicting physical equivalence classes of dynamical systems from data, where time-series classifiers struggle.
nodes.approach: Convolutional backbone with physics-informed vector field reconstruction loss learns unsupervised embeddings.
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles dynamical-systems physics and representation learning topics; no exact seed topic.
nodes.niche_reason: Embedding dynamical systems by phase portraits is very rare.

nodes.title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
nodes.tldr: Explains grokking via an L-U mismatch between training and test losses along weight norm, and induces it on images, language, and molecules.
nodes.problem: Grokking, delayed generalization long after overfitting, lacked a clear mechanism.
nodes.approach: Analyzes loss landscapes versus weight norm to find a train-test loss mismatch, then tests it on new tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Grokking theory is a specialised but actively studied topic.

nodes.title: Minimax Optimal Kernel Operator Learning via Multilevel Training
nodes.tldr: Establishes the minimax rate for learning Hilbert-Schmidt operators between Sobolev RKHSs and proposes a multilevel kernel algorithm that attains it for linear operators.
nodes.problem: What is the statistical limit for learning operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces?
nodes.approach: Regularization that learns spectral components between bias and variance contours, implemented via multilevel training.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Minimax operator learning in Sobolev RKHSs is a rare theory niche.

nodes.title: Is Adversarial Training Really a Silver Bullet for Mitigating Data Poisoning?
nodes.tldr: Shows adversarial training does not defend against a new entangled-features data poisoning attack that induces large accuracy drops even at equal poison and adversarial budgets.
nodes.problem: Indiscriminate data poisoning was believed ineffective against adversarially trained models when the adversarial budget matches the poison budget.
nodes.approach: Craft poisons that induce entangled features, evaluated across budgets, architectures, and adaptive defenses.
nodes.niche_reason: Poisoning of adversarially trained models is specialised within robustness.

nodes.title: PLOT: Prompt Learning with Optimal Transport for Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Learns multiple prompts for CLIP-style vision-language models by matching them to image features with optimal transport and Sinkhorn optimization.
nodes.problem: Multiple learned prompts collapse to one point when directly matched to the same visual feature
nodes.approach: Bi-level prompt learning with optimal transport distance solved via Sinkhorn
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt learning for CLIP is a common direction

nodes.title: MICN: Multi-scale Local and Global Context Modeling for Long-term Series Forecasting
nodes.tldr: Proposes MICN, a multi-scale forecasting network combining down-sampled convolution for local features with isometric convolution for global context at linear complexity.
nodes.problem: Transformers capture global correlations at quadratic cost and miss targeted local features.
nodes.approach: Multi-branch design with down-sampled convolution for local patterns and isometric convolution for global correlations.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Long-term forecasting architectures are a crowded benchmark area

nodes.title: Sampling is as easy as learning the score: theory for diffusion models with minimal data assumptions
nodes.tldr: Proves score-based diffusion models can sample nearly any realistic distribution given accurate scores, and finds critically damped Langevin does not reduce complexity.
nodes.problem: Prior sampling guarantees require uniform score accuracy and restrictive log-concavity-type assumptions.
nodes.approach: Analyses discretised Langevin-based sampling under L2 score error, with polynomial scaling and no functional inequality conditions.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of diffusion sampling is established but specialised

nodes.title: Dropout Enhanced Bilevel Training
nodes.tldr: Proposes a dropout-based bilevel optimization model and method to reduce overfitting, analyzing hypergradients and giving convergence complexity to a stationary point.
nodes.problem: Bilevel training on limited data overfits and dropout in bilevel methods lacks convergence guarantees.
nodes.approach: Bilevel model over distribution of dropout masks, dropout bilevel algorithm with stationary-point complexity analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Dropout in bilevel optimization is a rare combination.

nodes.title: One-shot Empirical Privacy Estimation for Federated Learning
nodes.tldr: Estimates a model's differential privacy loss during a single training run, without retraining or knowing the architecture, task, or DP algorithm.
nodes.problem: Empirical privacy auditing usually needs strong assumptions or thousands of retraining runs.
nodes.approach: One-shot auditing during a single training run, with provably correct Gaussian-mechanism estimates.
nodes.niche_reason: Empirical DP auditing is specialised within privacy

nodes.title: Q-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Foundation Models on Low-level Vision
nodes.tldr: A benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs perceive, describe, and assess low-level visual attributes, finding these skills unstable and imprecise.
nodes.problem: MLLM evaluations overlook low-level visual perception, description, and quality assessment.
nodes.approach: Three datasets: LLVisionQA questions, LLDescribe golden descriptions, and softmax-based quality scoring.
nodes.niche_reason: Established: MLLM benchmarks; low-level vision focus is specialised.

nodes.title: Bespoke Solvers for Generative Flow Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces Bespoke solvers, tiny learned ODE solvers tailored to a pretrained flow model that produce high-quality samples with far fewer function evaluations.
nodes.problem: Flow and diffusion sampling needs many function evaluations, while distillation is costly and can degrade quality.
nodes.approach: Optimizes an order-consistent solver with about 80 learnable parameters, trained for roughly 1% of model training cost.
nodes.niche_reason: Fast sampling for flows is a common active direction

nodes.title: Self-Alignment with Instruction Backtranslation
nodes.tldr: Builds an instruction-following LLM by generating instructions for web text with a seed model, self-curating examples, and finetuning on them.
nodes.problem: Instruction-following models need costly human-written instruction data.
nodes.approach: Self-augmentation and self-curation of web-derived instruction data, iterated finetuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Instruction data synthesis is a crowded LLM direction

nodes.title: Unified Human-Scene Interaction via Prompted Chain-of-Contacts
nodes.tldr: Language-driven framework where an LLM planner converts prompts into chains of human-object contacts, and a unified controller executes them for diverse human-scene interactions.
nodes.problem: Human-scene interaction lacks versatile language-based control and user-friendly interfaces.
nodes.approach: Chain-of-Contacts representation with LLM planning and a unified task controller.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.confidence_reason: Simulated human-scene control straddles animation and embodied agents.
nodes.niche_reason: Language-controlled human-scene interaction is a specialised niche

nodes.title: Mastering Memory Tasks with World Models
nodes.tldr: Adds state-space-model memory to DreamerV3-style world models so agents recall distant observations and assign credit over long horizons.
nodes.problem: Model-based RL agents struggle with long-term dependencies and distant credit assignment.
nodes.approach: Recall to Imagine integrates a new family of state space models into the world model.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Memory-augmented world models are an active, crowded area.

nodes.title: What does the Knowledge Neuron Thesis Have to do with Knowledge?
nodes.tldr: Argues the knowledge neuron thesis is an oversimplification: MLP edits also change non-factual linguistic behavior.
nodes.problem: Whether factual recall in LLMs is stored in MLP weights as knowledge.
nodes.approach: Comprehensive evaluation of knowledge-neuron editing across factual and linguistic phenomena.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Critical analysis of a specific interpretability thesis, moderately specialised.

nodes.title: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Detects whether LLMs have memorised benchmark data by prompting with dataset-guided partial instances and comparing completions, flagging contaminated instances and partitions.
nodes.problem: Test data leaking into LLM training corpora inflates benchmark scores, and contamination is hard to verify.
nodes.approach: Guided-instruction completion matched against references at instance level, then statistical and GPT-4 partition-level tests.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Contamination detection is an active, fairly common evaluation topic.

nodes.title: Beyond Reverse KL: Generalizing Direct Preference Optimization with Diverse Divergence Constraints
nodes.tldr: f-DPO generalizes direct preference optimization from reverse KL to arbitrary f-divergence constraints such as Jensen-Shannon and alpha-divergences, trading alignment and diversity.
nodes.problem: DPO is tied to reverse KL regularization, limiting divergence choices for aligning language models.
nodes.approach: Derive reward-policy mapping under general f-divergences and obtain f-DPO objectives without a separate reward model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: DPO variants are extremely crowded.

nodes.title: Vision Transformers Need Registers
nodes.tldr: Identifies high-norm artifact tokens in ViT feature maps and fixes them by adding extra register tokens, yielding smoother attention maps and better dense prediction.
nodes.problem: Vision Transformers produce high-norm artifact tokens in background regions that harm feature and attention maps.
nodes.approach: Append extra learnable register tokens to the input sequence so the model uses them for internal computation.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: ViT improvements are common, though the artifact analysis is specific.

nodes.title: Ferret: Refer and Ground Anything Anywhere at Any Granularity
nodes.tldr: Ferret is a multimodal LLM that refers to and grounds image regions of any shape using hybrid discrete-continuous region representations and a 1.1M-sample GRIT dataset.
nodes.problem: MLLMs struggle with flexible spatial referring and grounding at any granularity.
nodes.approach: Hybrid region representation with spatial-aware visual sampler and refer-and-ground instruction tuning.
nodes.niche_reason: Grounded MLLMs are a crowded, popular direction.

nodes.title: Conformal Risk Control
nodes.tldr: Extends conformal prediction to control the expected value of any monotone loss, with distribution-free guarantees and tight bounds.
nodes.problem: Conformal prediction only guarantees coverage, not control of general expected losses such as false negatives.
nodes.approach: Generalizes split conformal calibration to monotone losses, plus extensions to distribution shift and quantile risk.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Established conformal prediction area; extends guarantees to general losses.

nodes.title: CrIBo: Self-Supervised Learning via Cross-Image Object-Level Bootstrapping
nodes.tldr: Self-supervised dense representation learning that bootstraps object-level nearest neighbors across images, strong for in-context learning and segmentation.
nodes.problem: Global image-level bootstrapping entangles objects in scene-centric images.
nodes.approach: Cross-image object-level nearest-neighbor bootstrapping throughout training, enabling test-time retrieval.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Self-supervised dense representation learning is a crowded area.

nodes.title: GIO: Gradient Information Optimization for Training Dataset Selection
nodes.tldr: Introduces GIO, a scalable information-theoretic method that selects training subsets matching a small unlabeled target set, applicable across tasks without task-specific design.
nodes.problem: Selecting a training subset that matches a target distribution is intractable in practice.
nodes.approach: Relaxes an information-theoretic gradient objective into a scalable, efficient selection algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Data selection is a common data-centric AI direction

nodes.title: Generalization error of spectral algorithms
nodes.tldr: Derives asymptotic generalization error of spectral algorithms, including kernel ridge regression and gradient descent as special cases, under power-law spectra for two data models.
nodes.problem: Generalization estimates exist for kernel ridge regression but not for gradient-descent-like spectral algorithms.
nodes.approach: Compute loss as a functional of the learning profile for Gaussian and translation-invariant models.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Asymptotic kernel regression theory is a specialised theoretical niche.

nodes.title: BTR: Binary Token Representations for Efficient Retrieval Augmented Language Models
nodes.tldr: Precomputes passage tokens as 1-bit binary vectors to speed up retrieval-augmented language models and cut storage by over 100x.
nodes.problem: Retrieval-augmented LMs are slow and storage-heavy because retrieved passages must be processed at inference.
nodes.approach: Binary token representations with calibration and training objectives to recover accuracy after compression.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Efficient retrieval-augmented LM inference is a common direction

nodes.title: LEGO-Prover: Neural Theorem Proving with Growing Libraries
nodes.tldr: LEGO-Prover lets LLMs build proofs modularly with a growing library of verified lemmas, retrieving and creating skills, raising miniF2F pass rates and generating 20,000+ lemmas.
nodes.problem: LLM theorem provers assume a fixed theorem library and cannot create reusable new lemmas.
nodes.approach: Growing skill library of verified lemmas retrieved, created and evolved by LLM prompting during proving.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Formal theorem proving with LLMs is a rare, specialised area.

nodes.title: Towards Principled Representation Learning from Videos for Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Theoretical analysis of video-based representation learning for RL: autoencoding, temporal contrast and forward modeling succeed with iid noise but can fail under exogenous noise.
nodes.problem: Why pretraining representations from video for RL works in theory is unknown, especially with exogenous noise.
nodes.approach: Upper bounds for contrastive and forward-model methods under iid noise; lower bound for exogenous noise.
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of video pretraining for RL is a rare, cross-cutting direction.

nodes.title: SEGNO: Generalizing Equivariant Graph Neural Networks with Physical Inductive Biases
nodes.tldr: SEGNO is a second-order equivariant graph neural ODE that builds continuity and second-order motion into equivariant GNNs, with trajectory uniqueness and error bounds.
nodes.problem: Equivariant GNNs for physical dynamics generalize poorly, ignoring state continuity and second-order motion laws.
nodes.approach: Equivariant graph neural ODE parameterizing second-order dynamics, with theoretical trajectory error bound.
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariant physical-dynamics GNNs are established but specialised.

nodes.title: OPTIMAL ROBUST MEMORIZATION WITH RELU NEURAL NETWORKS
nodes.tldr: Proves NP-hardness of certain robust memorization networks and constructs ReLU networks achieving optimal robust memorization with O(Nn) parameters.
nodes.problem: Robust memorization of finite datasets by neural networks is understudied
nodes.approach: Explicit ReLU network constructions and width lower bounds, plus Lipschitz control for binary classification sets.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Robust memorization theory is a specialised niche

nodes.title: Mixed-Type Tabular Data Synthesis with Score-based Diffusion in Latent Space
nodes.tldr: Synthesizes mixed-type tabular data by running a fast latent diffusion model inside a VAE-learned unified embedding space.
nodes.problem: Extending diffusion to mixed-type tabular data with varied distributions is challenging.
nodes.approach: Diffusion in a VAE latent space that unifies data types, needing fewer reverse steps.
nodes.niche_reason: Tabular diffusion is a common generative direction

nodes.title: One For All: Towards Training One Graph Model For All Classification Tasks
nodes.tldr: Unifies graphs from many domains as text-attributed graphs, enabling few- and zero-shot classification via graph prompting.
nodes.problem: Different graph domains have distinct attributes, and tasks span node, link, and graph levels.
nodes.approach: Encode node and edge text with a language model into one space, plus graph prompting substructures for in-context learning.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-domain graph foundation models are a specialised direction

nodes.title: Coordinate-Aware Modulation for Neural Fields
nodes.tldr: Injects grid-derived scale and shift modulation into MLP intermediate features, combining MLP expressiveness with grids' bias-free fast learning for neural fields.
nodes.problem: MLP neural fields suffer spectral bias and slow convergence, while grids cost high memory.
nodes.approach: Coordinate-aware modulation of MLP features using scale and shift from grid representations.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.confidence_reason: Neural-field architecture spans NeRF and compression tasks.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural-field modulation is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Stable Neural Stochastic Differential Equations in Analyzing Irregular Time Series Data
nodes.tldr: Proposes three stable classes of neural SDEs (Langevin, linear noise, geometric) for irregular time series, with robustness guarantees and strong interpolation, forecasting and classification results.
nodes.problem: Neural SDEs on irregularly sampled, missing-value time series suffer instability from poor drift and diffusion design.
nodes.approach: Design stable Langevin-type, linear noise and geometric SDE classes with robustness analysis under distribution shift.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Continuous-time neural SDEs are specialised but established.

nodes.title: Space and time continuous physics simulation from partial observations
nodes.tldr: Predicts fluid dynamics in continuous space and time from sparse observations using two coupled dynamical systems with recurrent GNNs and spatio-temporal attention.
nodes.problem: Learned fluid simulators are tied to fixed grids and cannot predict at arbitrary locations and times.
nodes.approach: Coupled sparse-node and continuous-domain dynamical systems with a spatio-temporal attention observer.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised neural PDE setup with continuous space-time prediction

nodes.title: Demystifying CLIP Data
nodes.tldr: Reverse-engineers CLIP's data curation into MetaCLIP, a metadata-balanced curation algorithm over raw web data that outperforms CLIP's data.
nodes.problem: CLIP's data collection is undisclosed, hindering reproduction and understanding.
nodes.approach: Metadata-based substring matching and balancing to curate image-text pairs from CommonCrawl.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: CLIP data work is well covered but curation transparency is valued.

nodes.title: Image2Sentence based Asymmetrical Zero-shot Composed Image Retrieval
nodes.tldr: Trains a lightweight query-side model with an adaptive token learner that maps images to pseudo-sentences, enabling zero-shot composed image retrieval from unlabeled images.
nodes.problem: Composed image retrieval needs labeled triplets, and large vision-language models are hard to deploy on edge devices.
nodes.approach: Asymmetric dual model distilled from a large VL model, with a token learner and text modifier fusion.
nodes.niche_reason: Composed image retrieval is established but specialised

nodes.title: Interpreting CLIP's Image Representation via Text-Based Decomposition
nodes.tldr: Decomposes CLIP's image representation into patches, layers, and attention heads, interpreting each with text embeddings to find spurious features and enable zero-shot segmentation.
nodes.problem: CLIP's image representations are opaque, so it is unclear which components drive them.
nodes.approach: Additive decomposition of the image embedding, with heads and patches explained via text.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic interpretability of CLIP is specialised but increasingly studied.

nodes.title: Physics-Regulated Deep Reinforcement Learning: Invariant Embeddings
nodes.tldr: Phy-DRL embeds physics knowledge into deep RL via residual policies, safety-embedded rewards, and physics-guided network editing, giving provable safety guarantees on cart-pole and quadruped tasks.
nodes.problem: Safety-critical autonomous systems need DRL with guaranteed safety and physics compliance.
nodes.approach: Residual physics-plus-data policy, automatically constructed safety reward, and physics-guided neural network editing.
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-model-guided network editing for RL safety is uncommon.

nodes.title: The Effective Horizon Explains Deep RL Performance in Stochastic Environments
nodes.tldr: Shows many stochastic MDPs are solved by few value-iteration steps on the random policy Q function, explaining deep RL with instance-dependent bounds.
nodes.problem: Why do deep RL algorithms with random exploration succeed despite worst-case theory suggesting otherwise?
nodes.approach: Define effective horizon; prove bounds and empirically validate on stochastic MDPs.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Instance-dependent RL theory explaining practice is specialised.

nodes.title: Multiscale Positive-Unlabeled Detection of AI-Generated Texts
nodes.tldr: Detects AI-generated text, including short texts, by treating short machine texts as partially unlabeled in a multiscale positive-unlabeled loss.
nodes.problem: Detectors of LLM-written text fail on short texts like tweets, SMS, and reviews.
nodes.approach: Length-sensitive multiscale PU loss with text multiscaling augmentation to enrich training corpora.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.confidence_reason: Detection and PU-learning topics both fit; primary is judgment.
nodes.niche_reason: Short-text AI detection via PU learning is a fairly specialised angle.

nodes.title: Towards Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning under Diverse Data Corruption
nodes.tldr: Analyzes offline RL under data corruption and proposes Robust IQL, adding Huber loss and quantile estimators to IQL for heavy-tailed corrupted targets.
nodes.problem: Offline RL degrades badly when states, actions, rewards, or dynamics are corrupted.
nodes.approach: Huber loss for heavy-tailed Q targets plus quantile estimators balancing corrupted-data penalties.
nodes.niche_reason: Offline RL robustness is an active but common direction

nodes.title: Learning to Relax: Setting Solver Parameters Across a Sequence of Linear System Instances
nodes.tldr: Uses a bandit learner to tune SOR relaxation parameters across a sequence of linear systems, approaching the best fixed parameter using only iteration counts.
nodes.problem: Choosing solver parameters like SOR's omega per linear system is costly, and heuristics are suboptimal.
nodes.approach: Sequential bandit and contextual bandit parameter selection, with regret guarantees toward instance-optimal parameters.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Learning-based numerical solver tuning is an unusual cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: SaProt: Protein Language Modeling with Structure-aware Vocabulary
nodes.tldr: SaProt is a protein language model with a structure-aware vocabulary combining residue tokens and Foldseek structural tokens, trained on 40M proteins.
nodes.problem: Protein language models ignore explicit protein structure information.
nodes.approach: Structure-aware vocabulary from residue plus 3D structure tokens for masked pretraining.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Protein LMs are established but a specialised domain.

nodes.title: Graphical Multioutput Gaussian Process with Attention
nodes.tldr: GMOGP builds multi-output Gaussian processes with attention-based graphical dependencies and distributed Pareto-optimal kernel learning, improving accuracy, speed and memory over prior MOGPs.
nodes.problem: Multi-output Gaussian processes are computationally costly and mismatch non-Gaussian data.
nodes.approach: Graphical GP priors from parent processes with attention-based representations and distributed Pareto-optimal hyperparameter learning.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-output GPs with attention graphs are a rare niche.

nodes.title: NoiseDiffusion: Correcting Noise for Image Interpolation with Diffusion Models beyond Spherical Linear Interpolation
nodes.tldr: NoiseDiffusion corrects invalid encoded noise for diffusion-based interpolation of natural images, adding subtle noise, constraints and raw-image injection to avoid artifacts.
nodes.problem: Spherical interpolation fails for natural images because inverted noise is off-distribution.
nodes.approach: Noise correction with Gaussian noise and extreme-value constraint, plus raw image injection in noisy space.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based image interpolation is a specialised editing task.

nodes.title: Dynamic Discounted Counterfactual Regret Minimization
nodes.tldr: DDCFR learns a dynamic discounting scheme for counterfactual regret minimization as a Markov decision process, speeding convergence in imperfect-information games over fixed schedules.
nodes.problem: Fixed manual iteration-weighting schemes in CFR variants limit convergence speed in imperfect-information games.
nodes.approach: Policy optimization over learned iteration discounts, formalized as an MDP that weights iterations at runtime.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Game-solving via learned regret discounting is established but specialised

nodes.title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Extends pre-trained LLM context lengths cheaply by combining sparse shifted local attention in training with an improved LoRA that trains embeddings and norms.
nodes.problem: Training long-context LLMs with dense attention is computationally expensive.
nodes.approach: Shifted sparse local attention during fine-tuning plus LoRA with trainable embedding and normalization layers.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Long-context LoRA extension is a common direction

nodes.title: Local Search GFlowNets
nodes.tldr: Trains GFlowNets with local search by backtracking via backward policy and reconstructing via forward policy, biasing samples toward high reward in molecular tasks.
nodes.problem: GFlowNets over-explore and struggle to consistently generate high-reward samples.
nodes.approach: Local neighborhood exploration through backward-policy backtracking and forward-policy reconstruction during training.
nodes.niche_reason: GFlowNets are a rare, small subfield.

nodes.title: Towards Optimal Regret in Adversarial Linear MDPs with Bandit Feedback
nodes.tldr: Gives an optimal-rate sqrt(K) regret algorithm and an efficient K^(3/4) one for adversarial linear MDPs with bandit feedback.
nodes.problem: Regret bounds for adversarial linear MDPs with bandit feedback were suboptimal.
nodes.approach: Two algorithms improving regret: one computationally inefficient but simulator-free, one efficient.
nodes.niche_reason: Regret bounds for adversarial linear MDPs are specialised theory

nodes.title: RetroBridge: Modeling Retrosynthesis with Markov Bridges
nodes.tldr: Introduces the Markov Bridge Model for discrete data and RetroBridge, a template-free single-step retrosynthesis method that avoids a tractable noise prior.
nodes.problem: Single-step retrosynthesis requires modeling dependence between two intractable discrete molecule distributions.
nodes.approach: Markov bridge process pinned at endpoints, directly mapping product molecules to precursors.
nodes.niche_reason: Markov bridge for retrosynthesis is a rare approach.

nodes.title: Exploring the Common Appearance-Boundary Adaptation for Nighttime Optical Flow
nodes.tldr: Nighttime optical flow framework adapting from daytime and event domains through common appearance (reflectance) and boundary (spatiotemporal gradient) latent spaces.
nodes.problem: Nighttime optical flow degrades from weak texture and noise, and direct domain adaptation has large gaps.
nodes.approach: Common-space appearance adaptation via intrinsic decomposition and boundary adaptation via event-image motion correlation.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Nighttime event-assisted optical flow adaptation is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Real3D-Portrait: One-shot Realistic 3D Talking Portrait Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Real3D-Portrait generates one-shot realistic 3D talking portraits from an image via an image-to-plane model, motion adapter, torso/background synthesis and audio-to-motion model.
nodes.problem: One-shot talking portraits lack accurate 3D reconstruction, stable animation and natural torso and background.
nodes.approach: Large image-to-plane model distilled from a 3D face GAN, motion adapter, and head-torso-background super-resolution.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Talking head synthesis is established but specialised.

nodes.title: BooookScore: A systematic exploration of book-length summarization in the era of LLMs
nodes.tldr: Studies coherence of LLM book-length summarization via human annotation of error types and introduces BooookScore, an automatic metric for evaluating summaries of 100K+ token books.
nodes.problem: Evaluating coherence of LLM summaries for book-length documents exceeding context windows.
nodes.approach: Human annotation taxonomy of coherence errors and an LLM-based automatic metric validated against humans.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised long-document summarization evaluation.

nodes.title: Provable Compositional Generalization for Object-Centric Learning
nodes.tldr: Proves autoencoders with structural decoder assumptions and encoder-decoder consistency learn object-centric representations that generalize compositionally, validated on synthetic images.
nodes.problem: No principled understanding of when object-centric representations enable compositional generalization.
nodes.approach: Identifiability theory giving conditions on decoder structure and encoder-decoder consistency.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Identifiability theory for object-centric learning is specialised

nodes.title: Can Sensitive Information Be Deleted From LLMs? Objectives for Defending Against Extraction Attacks
nodes.tldr: Shows model editing methods like ROME leave sensitive facts recoverable from LLMs via whitebox and blackbox extraction attacks, and proposes partial defenses.
nodes.problem: Deleting sensitive or harmful knowledge directly from LLM weights so that prompt attacks cannot extract it.
nodes.approach: Attack-and-defense framework evaluating model editing and new defence methods against whitebox and blackbox extraction.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM unlearning and extraction attacks are a crowded, active area.

nodes.title: SpikePoint: An Efficient Point-based Spiking Neural Network for Event Cameras Action Recognition
nodes.tldr: SpikePoint is a point-based spiking neural network that processes sparse event-camera data directly as point clouds for ultra-low-power action recognition.
nodes.problem: Converting asynchronous events into frames loses sparsity and conflicts with SNN and event-camera efficiency goals.
nodes.approach: End-to-end single-stage point-based SNN extracting global and local features from event clouds with surrogate gradient training.
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking networks on event-camera point clouds are very rare.

nodes.title: EQA-MX: Embodied Question Answering using Multimodal Expression
nodes.tldr: Introduces 8 embodied QA tasks combining verbal utterances and gestures such as pointing, an 8M-sample dataset, and VQ-Fusion, a vector-quantized multimodal representation model.
nodes.problem: Embodied question answering lacks tasks involving multimodal expressions like gestures plus language from multiple perspectives.
nodes.approach: New large dataset EQA-MX and VQ-based multimodal fusion model for verbal and multiview visual representations.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Gesture-grounded embodied QA is a rare setting.

nodes.title: Detecting, Explaining, and Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Detects memorized prompts in text-to-image diffusion models via text-conditional prediction magnitude, explains token contributions, and mitigates memorization at inference or training.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models replicate training data, raising legal and privacy concerns.
nodes.approach: Magnitude of text-conditional noise predictions for detection, token attribution, and inference/training-time mitigation.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: Could be privacy/memorization or diffusion guidance; judged by contribution.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion memorization is an established but specialised topic.

nodes.title: CLAP: Collaborative Adaptation for Patchwork Learning
nodes.tldr: Imputes missing modalities across privacy-preserving clients with heterogeneous modality sets by learning cross-client transformations via an ELBO and Pareto min-max optimization.
nodes.problem: Clients hold different modality combinations with non-i.i.d. data, and raw data cannot be shared
nodes.approach: Learns transformations between shared modality intersections and other modalities, optimized with a Pareto min-max framework
nodes.confidence_reason: Federated and multimodal framings both fit; primary choice is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Uncommon federated multimodal patchwork imputation setting

nodes.title: OmniQuant: Omnidirectionally Calibrated Quantization for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: OmniQuant learns weight clipping and equivalent transformations for post-training LLM quantization, achieving strong results at low-bit settings like W4A4 and W2A16.
nodes.problem: Hand-crafted quantization parameters degrade LLM performance in extremely low-bit post-training quantization.
nodes.approach: Learnable Weight Clipping and Learnable Equivalent Transformation optimized block-wise differentiably.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: LLM quantization is very crowded.

nodes.title: Poisoned Forgery Face: Towards Backdoor Attacks on Face Forgery Detection
nodes.tldr: Clean-label backdoor attack on face forgery detectors using a scalable trigger generator and landmark-based relative embedding for stealthy translation-sensitive triggers.
nodes.problem: Backdoor vulnerability of face forgery detection models is unrecognized.
nodes.approach: Trigger generator with convolving process producing translation-sensitive triggers, embedded relative to landmark regions.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Backdoors targeting deepfake detectors are specialised.

nodes.title: What does automatic differentiation compute for neural networks?
nodes.tldr: Proves that automatic differentiation returns a Clarke subderivative for ReLU and maxpool networks under stated conditions, and checks those conditions empirically.
nodes.problem: What autodiff outputs for nondifferentiable neural networks is unclear
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of AD on pointwise-activation and maxpool networks via Clarke subdifferentials
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Correctness of autodiff for nonsmooth networks is a rare angle

nodes.title: MUSTARD: Mastering Uniform Synthesis of Theorem and Proof Data
nodes.tldr: Presents MUSTARD, a pipeline that synthesizes math problems with step-wise formal proofs, checked by Lean, yielding 5,866 validated theorem-proof examples.
nodes.problem: Theorem proving and math reasoning need step-wise formal data, which is labour-intensive to annotate.
nodes.approach: Samples concept seeds, prompts an LLM for informal and formal solutions, then filters with a proof assistant.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Formal theorem-proof data synthesis is specialised but active

nodes.title: Multi-granularity Correspondence Learning from Long-term Noisy Videos
nodes.tldr: Norton uses optimal transport to handle clip-caption and frame-word misalignment in long noisy videos, with an alignable prompt bucket and soft-maximum operator for video-language pretraining.
nodes.problem: Long-video language learning suffers multi-granularity noisy correspondence between clips, captions, frames and words.
nodes.approach: Noise-robust temporal optimal transport with video-paragraph and clip-caption contrastive losses.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Noisy correspondence with optimal transport is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis
nodes.tldr: WebAgent plans with decomposed instructions, summarises long HTML, and acts via generated Python programs, improving real-website success by over 50%.
nodes.problem: LLM web agents struggle on real websites with open domains, limited context, and poor HTML inductive bias.
nodes.approach: Plan-and-summarise pipeline with HTML-T5 long-document model and Flan-U-PaLM program synthesis.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM web agents are a common direction

nodes.title: Towards Understanding Factual Knowledge of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces Pinocchio, a 20K-question benchmark probing LLM factual knowledge, composition, temporal updating, multi-fact reasoning, and adversarial robustness across languages and domains.
nodes.problem: The extent and scope of factual knowledge in LLMs is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Build diverse factual question benchmark and evaluate LLMs on composition, temporal, and adversarial tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Factuality benchmarks for LLMs are common.

nodes.title: De novo Protein Design Using Geometric Vector Field Networks
nodes.tldr: Introduces Vector Field Network, an encoder doing learnable vector computations on frame-anchored virtual atoms, improving protein diffusion design and inverse folding over IPA.
nodes.problem: Protein structure encoders for residue frames are weak because atom-wise features are unavailable in backbone frame modeling.
nodes.approach: Learnable vector-valued linear layers over virtual atom coordinates with attention aggregation to update residue representations.
nodes.niche_reason: Established protein design area with a specialised encoder angle.

nodes.title: Zipformer: A faster and better encoder for automatic speech recognition
nodes.tldr: Zipformer is a faster, more memory-efficient ASR encoder with a U-Net-like structure, BiasNorm and new activations, trained with the ScaledAdam optimizer.
nodes.problem: Improving speed, memory use and accuracy of Conformer-style ASR encoders.
nodes.approach: U-Net-like multi-rate encoder, attention weight reuse, BiasNorm, Swoosh activations, and ScaledAdam optimizer.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised ASR architecture work.

nodes.title: Entropy is not Enough for Test-Time Adaptation: From the Perspective of Disentangled Factors
nodes.tldr: Shows entropy is unreliable for test-time adaptation under bias, and proposes DeYO, using a shape-destruction confidence metric (PLPD) with entropy for sample selection.
nodes.problem: Entropy is an unreliable confidence metric for test-time adaptation under biased scenarios, causing error accumulation.
nodes.approach: Pseudo-Label Probability Difference measures prediction change after object-destructive transformation; combine with entropy for sample selection and weighting.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Test-time adaptation is a common research topic.

nodes.title: Coeditor: Leveraging Repo-level Diffs for Code Auto-editing
nodes.tldr: Coeditor is a fine-tuned code LM that predicts edits to a code region from recent repo-level diffs, trained on commit histories of 1650 Python projects.
nodes.problem: Code models mostly generate new code, not edit existing code from recent changes.
nodes.approach: Line-diff representation of changes plus static analysis to build repo-aware contexts for a fine-tuned model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Code editing is established but more specialised than generation.

nodes.title: Generalization in diffusion models arises from geometry-adaptive harmonic representations
nodes.tldr: Shows denoisers trained on disjoint subsets learn the same score, and their inductive bias is a geometry-adaptive harmonic shrinkage.
nodes.problem: Whether diffusion models truly learn the data density or merely memorize the training set.
nodes.approach: Compare denoisers trained on non-overlapping data and analyze the learned shrinkage bases.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Harmonic-basis analysis of denoisers is specialised theory

nodes.title: On the hardness of learning under symmetries
