nodes.title: H2O-SDF: Two-phase Learning for 3D Indoor Reconstruction using Object Surface Fields
nodes.tldr: H2O-SDF uses a two-phase learning scheme with an Object Surface Field to reconstruct indoor scenes, preserving room layout while capturing fine object surface detail.
nodes.problem: Indoor 3D reconstruction struggles to keep both room layout geometry and high-frequency object details.
nodes.approach: Two-phase implicit surface learning separating object and non-object regions via an Object Surface Field.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Neural surface reconstruction is a common topic.

nodes.title: Implicit bias of SGD in $L_2$-regularized linear DNNs: One-way jumps from high to low rank
nodes.tldr: Proves SGD in L2-regularized deep linear networks can jump from higher-rank to lower-rank minima with positive probability but never back, defining nested absorbing sets.
nodes.problem: Understanding implicit bias of SGD among local minima of different ranks in regularized deep linear networks.
nodes.approach: Define nested absorbing sets of rank-bounded minima and prove one-way SGD transition probabilities.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Implicit bias theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Confidential-DPproof: Confidential Proof of Differentially Private Training
nodes.tldr: Confidential-DPproof generates a zero-knowledge cryptographic certificate of (epsilon, delta)-DP guarantee during training, without revealing data or model.
nodes.problem: Post hoc privacy auditing gives only lower bounds and requires sharing model updates and data with an auditor.
nodes.approach: Custom zero-knowledge proof protocol covering noise addition and subsampling amplification in DP training.
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Cryptographic proofs of DP training are a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: CrossQ: Batch Normalization in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Greater Sample Efficiency and Simplicity
nodes.tldr: Uses careful batch normalization and no target networks in SAC-style critics, matching state-of-the-art sample efficiency at UTD 1.
nodes.problem: Sample-efficient deep RL usually requires costly high update-to-data ratios.
nodes.approach: Batch normalization in critics with target networks removed, built on SAC at low UTD.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Sample-efficient SAC variants are a crowded mainstream

nodes.title: Never Train from Scratch: Fair Comparison of Long-Sequence Models Requires Data-Driven Priors
nodes.tldr: Shows pretraining on downstream data with denoising objectives closes the Transformer versus state-space-model gap on Long Range Arena, so random-init comparisons mislead.
nodes.problem: Architecture comparisons on long-sequence benchmarks with random initialization overestimate differences between models.
nodes.approach: Self-supervised denoising pretraining using only downstream data, then compare Transformers and SSMs and ablate structured parameterizations.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Long-sequence benchmark methodology is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Deep Geodesic Canonical Correlation Analysis for Covariance-Based Neuroimaging Data
nodes.tldr: DeepGeoCCA introduces geodesic correlation and a geometric deep learning framework for multi-view self-supervised learning on SPD covariance matrices from EEG and fMRI neuroimaging.
nodes.problem: Learning shared representations across neuroimaging modalities whose covariance data lie on the SPD manifold.
nodes.approach: Geodesic correlation extending CCA to SPD manifolds, optimized by a geometric deep network.
nodes.niche_reason: Riemannian multi-view learning on SPD neuroimaging data is very rare.

nodes.title: Geographic Location Encoding with Spherical Harmonics and Sinusoidal Representation Networks
nodes.tldr: Location encoder combining spherical harmonics with sinusoidal representation networks, avoiding polar artifacts of planar Fourier embeddings for global geographic data.
nodes.problem: Planar Fourier coordinate embeddings create artifacts at poles for globally distributed geographic data.
nodes.approach: Spherical harmonic basis functions fed into SIREN networks as learned Double Fourier Sphere features.
nodes.niche_reason: Spherical location encoders are a specialised geospatial niche

nodes.title: MovingParts: Motion-based 3D Part Discovery in Dynamic Radiance Field
nodes.tldr: MovingParts reconstructs dynamic scenes with NeRF and discovers rigid parts by combining Eulerian and Lagrangian motion views with cycle consistency, enabling part tracking and editing.
nodes.problem: Discovering object parts from motion in dynamic radiance fields, which Eulerian deformation fields make intractable.
nodes.approach: Dual Lagrangian particle-trajectory and Eulerian representations with cycle consistency, factorizing motion into part-level rigid motions.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Fluid-inspired motion-based part discovery in dynamic NeRF is unusual.

nodes.title: TorchRL: A data-driven decision-making library for PyTorch
nodes.tldr: Open-source PyTorch library for decision and control, built around the TensorDict primitive with modular, standalone RL components and benchmarks.
nodes.problem: PyTorch lacks a comprehensive native library for decision and control tasks.
nodes.approach: TensorDict data primitive with well-integrated, standalone RL building blocks.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: RL libraries are a common systems contribution.

nodes.title: Large Brain Model for Learning Generic Representations with Tremendous EEG Data in BCI
nodes.tldr: Pretrains a large EEG Transformer on masked channel patches predicting neural codes, transferring across many BCI datasets and tasks.
nodes.problem: EEG datasets are small and heterogeneous, so models do not generalize across electrodes, lengths and tasks.
nodes.approach: Channel-patch segmentation with a vector-quantized neural tokenizer and masked code-prediction pretraining.
nodes.niche_reason: Large-scale EEG foundation models are still rare.

nodes.title: NaturalSpeech 2: Latent Diffusion Models are Natural and Zero-Shot Speech and Singing Synthesizers
nodes.tldr: Zero-shot speech and singing synthesis that uses a latent diffusion model over neural codec latents, conditioned on text and a speech prompt.
nodes.problem: Autoregressive TTS suffers unstable prosody, word skipping and weak voice quality
nodes.approach: Residual-VQ neural codec with diffusion-generated latents and speech-prompt in-context learning
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: TTS with diffusion is a crowded, mainstream direction

nodes.title: MT-Ranker: Reference-free machine translation evaluation by inter-system ranking
nodes.tldr: Reframes reference-free machine translation evaluation as pairwise ranking of two translations, trained with NLI indirect supervision and synthetic data, achieving state-of-the-art on WMT benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Reference-free MT evaluation with interpretable, consistent judgments instead of absolute quality scores.
nodes.approach: Train a pairwise ranker using NLI supervision and weakly labeled synthetic translation pairs, no human annotations.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.confidence_reason: Evaluation-metric paper; NLP topic choice between evaluation and linguistics is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: MT metric research is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Realistic Evaluation of Semi-supervised Learning Algorithms in Open Environments
nodes.tldr: Proposes robustness metrics, theory and an open benchmark evaluating semi-supervised learning algorithms under open environments where label, feature or distribution mismatch exists.
nodes.problem: SSL algorithms assume matched labeled/unlabeled distributions, unlike real open environments.
nodes.approach: Robustness analysis curve metrics, generalization theory, and unified toolkit benchmark across image, text, tabular data.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Topic is a judgment call between close topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Semi-supervised learning benchmarking under open environments is specialised.

nodes.title: What's In My Big Data?
nodes.tldr: WIMBD is a platform of sixteen scalable analyses revealing duplicates, low-quality content, PII, toxicity, and benchmark contamination in large text corpora like C4, The Pile, and RedPajama.
nodes.problem: Little is known about the contents and quality of the large corpora used to train language models.
nodes.approach: Scalable count and search primitives enabling analysis of over 35 terabytes of text on a single node.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Corpus auditing is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Guiding Instruction-based Image Editing via Multimodal Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Uses a multimodal LLM to rewrite brief edit instructions into expressive guidance, trained end-to-end with an image editing model for better instruction-based edits.
nodes.problem: Brief human editing instructions are often too vague for current instruction-based editors.
nodes.approach: MLLM derives expressive instructions as explicit guidance that the editing model consumes end-to-end.
nodes.niche_reason: Instruction-based image editing via MLLMs is a common direction

nodes.title: Complex priors and flexible inference in recurrent circuits with dendritic nonlinearities
nodes.tldr: A recurrent circuit model with dendritic nonlinearities optimized for denoising samples from complex priors, linking diffusion-style priors to how the brain does probabilistic inference.
nodes.problem: How the brain represents and uses structured natural-image priors in probabilistic inference.
nodes.approach: Recurrent stochastic circuit with denoising dendritic nonlinearities and an oscillating global noise signal sampling from the prior.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Biophysical circuit model tying diffusion priors to dendrites is very rare.

nodes.title: Prediction without Preclusion: Recourse Verification with Reachable Sets
nodes.tldr: Recourse verification uses reachable sets to test whether a model assigns fixed predictions that preclude people from changing outcomes, studied on consumer finance data.
nodes.problem: Models ignoring feature actionability can assign fixed predictions, denying access to credit or jobs.
nodes.approach: Model-agnostic reachable-set construction for discrete features, using integer programming to certify responsiveness.
nodes.niche_reason: Algorithmic recourse verification is a rare topic.

nodes.title: Mask-Based Modeling for Neural Radiance Fields
nodes.tldr: MRVM-NeRF is a self-supervised pretraining target predicting complete scene representations from masked ray and view features, improving generalizable NeRF across scenes.
nodes.problem: Generalizable NeRFs lack mechanisms for interaction across points and views, limiting cross-scene generalization.
nodes.approach: Masked ray and view modeling pretraining that predicts full scene features from partially masked features.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Generalizable NeRF pretraining is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Controlled Text Generation via Language Model Arithmetic
nodes.tldr: Model arithmetic composes and biases multiple LLMs at inference time via formulas over their distributions, enabling controlled generation without retraining and with speculative sampling.
nodes.problem: Controlled text generation without retraining or specialised datasets.
nodes.approach: Linear combinations of model token distributions as formulas, extended with speculative sampling for efficiency.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Inference-time LM composition is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Neuron Activation Coverage: Rethinking Out-of-distribution Detection and Generalization
nodes.tldr: Neuron activation coverage measures neuron behavior on in-distribution data, enabling strong OOD detection across benchmarks and a criterion correlating with OOD generalization for model selection.
nodes.problem: Understanding and detecting out-of-distribution inputs and predicting model robustness.
nodes.approach: Define neuron activation states and a coverage measure over in-distribution data for detection and validation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: OOD detection is a common topic.

nodes.title: CABINET: Content Relevance-based Noise Reduction for Table Question Answering
nodes.tldr: CABINET trains an unsupervised relevance scorer with the QA LLM to suppress irrelevant table cells, setting state of the art on table question answering.
nodes.problem: Irrelevant table content distracts LLMs in table question answering.
nodes.approach: Unsupervised relevance scorer trained jointly with the QA LLM plus weakly supervised parsing-statement cell highlighting.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised table QA subarea.

nodes.title: R-EDL: Relaxing Nonessential Settings of Evidential Deep Learning
nodes.tldr: Relaxes two non-essential design choices in evidential deep learning, a prior weight and a variance regularizer, to reduce overconfident uncertainty estimates.
nodes.problem: Evidential deep learning produces overconfident uncertainty estimates due to nonessential settings.
nodes.approach: Treat prior weight as a tunable hyperparameter; optimize Dirichlet expectation instead of variance regularizer.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Classifier uncertainty estimation is established and fairly crowded.

nodes.title: Variational Bayesian Last Layers
nodes.tldr: A deterministic variational formulation for Bayesian last layer networks gives a sampling-free single-pass model with quadratic cost, improving accuracy, calibration, and OOD detection.
nodes.problem: Cheap and effective uncertainty estimation in neural networks via Bayesian last layers.
nodes.approach: Deterministic variational lower bound for Bayesian last layers, optionally with variational feature learning.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian deep learning method; established but specialised.

nodes.title: Neural Fine-Tuning Search for Few-Shot Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses neural architecture search to find the best arrangement of adapters and which layers to freeze or fine-tune for few-shot recognition, for ResNets and ViTs.
nodes.problem: Designing the optimal fine-tuning adaptation strategy for few-shot classification.
nodes.approach: Stochastic NAS over adapter placement and frozen versus fine-tuned layers on pre-trained networks.
nodes.niche_reason: NAS for adaptation in few-shot learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Proximal Policy Gradient Arborescence for Quality Diversity Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Adapts on-policy PPO to the differentiable quality-diversity framework, yielding PPGA, which discovers diverse high-performing skills on stochastic humanoid tasks with 4x best-reward gains.
nodes.problem: Quality-diversity RL is limited to off-policy or evolution methods and struggles in stochastic environments.
nodes.approach: Combine PPO with differentiable quality diversity (CMA-based arborescence) plus modifications for efficient optimization.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Quality-diversity RL is a small, distinct community.

nodes.title: Harnessing Density Ratios for Online Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: GLOW brings density ratio modeling to online RL under coverability for sample-efficient exploration, with HyGLOW giving an efficient hybrid RL reduction to offline RL.
nodes.problem: Density ratio methods from offline RL seem inapplicable to online RL where no exploratory dataset exists.
nodes.approach: Truncated density ratio plus value function realizability with optimism; hybrid RL black-box reduction to offline RL.
nodes.niche_reason: Statistical RL theory with density ratios is rare.

nodes.title: Feature-aligned N-BEATS with Sinkhorn divergence
nodes.tldr: Feature-aligned N-BEATS adds stack-wise Sinkhorn divergence feature alignment across source domains to achieve domain-generalized time series forecasting.
nodes.problem: Time series forecasting models generalize poorly across domains.
nodes.approach: Align marginal feature distributions per N-BEATS stack using Sinkhorn divergence alongside forecasting loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Domain-generalized forecasting with optimal transport alignment is specialised.

nodes.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization with Bias and Variance Reduction
nodes.tldr: Prospect is a single-learning-rate stochastic gradient method for distributionally robust optimization, with linear convergence and 2-3x speedups over baselines.
nodes.problem: Existing DRO algorithms need multiple hyperparameters or yield biased gradients that may fail to converge.
nodes.approach: Stochastic gradient reweighting of training examples with a single tuned learning rate and regularized losses.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: DRO optimization is established; single-hyperparameter convergence is specialised

nodes.title: Overthinking the Truth: Understanding how Language Models Process False Demonstrations
nodes.tldr: Shows false demonstrations make intermediate predictions diverge at a critical layer, driven by late false induction heads copying misinformation.
nodes.problem: Few-shot imitation reproduces inaccurate or harmful content from the context.
nodes.approach: Intermediate-layer decoding plus head ablation to locate false induction heads.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic study of false in-context demonstrations is specialised.

nodes.title: On the Foundations of Shortcut Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows that adding one hidden ReLU or Tanh layer induces shortcut bias, explained by neural tangent kernels, while linear models stay unbiased.
nodes.problem: Models favor features that are easy to extract over more predictive ones, but the reasons are unclear.
nodes.approach: Synthetic datasets with controlled predictivity and availability, measuring each model's shortcut bias.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.confidence_reason: Shortcut bias straddles theory and OOD; judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Feature availability and shortcut bias is a specialised analysis

nodes.title: Learning Hierarchical World Models with Adaptive Temporal Abstractions from Discrete Latent Dynamics
nodes.tldr: THICK learns hierarchical world models with discrete latents: the low level updates sparse invariant contexts, the high level predicts context changes, aiding MBRL and planning.
nodes.problem: Most model-based RL uses flat world models without temporal abstraction for multi-timescale reasoning.
nodes.approach: Two-level latent dynamics with sparse low-level context updates and high-level prediction of context changes.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Hierarchical world models are an established but specialised direction.

nodes.title: Understanding and Mitigating the Label Noise in Pre-training on Downstream Tasks
nodes.tldr: Studies how label noise in pre-training data affects downstream ID and OOD performance and proposes NMTune, a lightweight feature-space tuning method to mitigate it.
nodes.problem: Label noise in pre-training data harms downstream generalization, especially out-of-domain.
nodes.approach: Black-box affine tuning of the feature space (NMTune) with extensive noisy pre-training analysis.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Noise in pre-training data is a specialised transfer learning angle.

nodes.title: Meta Continual Learning Revisited: Implicitly Enhancing Online Hessian Approximation via Variance Reduction
nodes.tldr: Combines regularization-based continual learning with meta-continual learning, using variance reduction so the online Hessian approximation is both timely and accurate.
nodes.problem: Regularization continual learners use fixed Hessians, and meta-CL has high variance
nodes.approach: Variance-reduced online Hessian estimation within meta-continual learning
nodes.niche_reason: Continual learning is crowded, but Hessian-based meta-CL is specialised

nodes.title: Sample-Efficient Linear Representation Learning from Non-IID Non-Isotropic Data
nodes.tldr: Proposes a debiased, feature-whitened alternating descent for linear representation learning, with rates matching an oracle under non-isotropic data.
nodes.problem: Multi-task representation learning with non-isotropic, non-iid covariates loses favorable sample complexity.
nodes.approach: Modified alternating minimization-descent with bias correction and feature whitening, with linear convergence analysis.
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory of representation learning; meta and representation topics overlap
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of linear multi-task representation learning is specialised

nodes.title: Large Content And Behavior Models To Understand, Simulate, And Optimize Content And Behavior
nodes.tldr: Adds receiver behavior tokens such as likes and clicks to LLM training so models can simulate, predict and optimize how audiences respond to content.
nodes.problem: LLMs do not model or optimize how receivers will behave in response to messages.
nodes.approach: Behavior tokens added to LLM training corpora, plus a released Content Behavior Corpus.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Behavior-token LLM; fits several LLM topics, judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Behavior tokens in LLMs are a rare cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: Spatially-Aware Transformers for Embodied Agents
nodes.tldr: Spatially-Aware Transformers add spatial context to episodic memory for embodied agents, building place-centric memory, with an RL-trained Adaptive Memory Allocator improving efficiency.
nodes.problem: Transformer episodic memory for agents ignores the spatial dimension, only storing temporally ordered experiences.
nodes.approach: Place-centric spatially-aware transformer memory plus an RL-trained adaptive memory allocator.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.confidence_reason: Straddles memory architectures, embodied agents, and RL; no single clear topic.
nodes.niche_reason: Place-centric episodic memory inspired by cognitive science is uncommon.

nodes.title: Towards Reliable and Efficient Backdoor Trigger Inversion via Decoupling Benign Features
nodes.tldr: Defends against backdoored models by decoupling benign features and inverting triggers that minimize benign-feature differences, without scanning all target classes.
nodes.problem: Backdoor trigger inversion generates triggers that poorly match the adversary's real triggers
nodes.approach: Decouple benign features, then invert triggers by minimizing benign differences
nodes.confidence_reason: No dedicated backdoor topic; closest is adversarial robustness
nodes.niche_reason: Backdoor defense is an established security topic

nodes.title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
nodes.tldr: Decouples helpfulness and harmlessness preferences into separate reward and cost models, then fine-tunes LLMs with Lagrangian constrained RL.
nodes.problem: Helpfulness and harmlessness objectives conflict and confuse crowd preference labels during LLM alignment.
nodes.approach: Separate reward and cost models with Lagrangian constrained RL, adjusting the balance during fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Safe RLHF is a common alignment direction

nodes.title: Scaling Laws for Associative Memories
nodes.tldr: Derives precise scaling laws for associative memories built from outer products of embeddings, with respect to sample and parameter size.
nodes.problem: How transformer-like associative memories store and scale abstract rules is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: High-dimensional outer-product memory model analyzed for statistical efficiency of estimators, validated numerically.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Theory of memory scaling; transformer link is indirect.
nodes.niche_reason: Scaling laws for outer-product associative memories are a rare theoretical niche.

nodes.title: ODEFormer: Symbolic Regression of Dynamical Systems with Transformers
nodes.tldr: A transformer that infers multidimensional ODE systems in symbolic form from a single observed solution trajectory, robust to noise and irregular sampling.
nodes.problem: Recovering governing differential equations from noisy, irregularly sampled trajectories.
nodes.approach: Sequence-to-symbol transformer trained to output ODE expressions from trajectory observations.
nodes.primary_topic: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.niche_reason: Symbolic ODE discovery is rare relative to mainstream ML

nodes.title: CivRealm: A Learning and Reasoning Odyssey in Civilization for Decision-Making Agents
nodes.tldr: Civilization-inspired environment with imperfect-information general-sum play and changing player counts, with interfaces for RL agents and language agents.
nodes.problem: Decision-making benchmarks emphasize learning while neglecting complex reasoning in open-ended games.
nodes.approach: Benchmark environment offering tensor-based and language-based agent interfaces, with baseline results.
nodes.niche_reason: Game environment with mixed LLM and RL agent interfaces is fairly unusual.

nodes.title: EfficientDM: Efficient Quantization-Aware Fine-Tuning of Low-Bit Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: EfficientDM fine-tunes low-bit diffusion models with a data-free, quantization-aware low-rank adapter, reaching QAT-level quality at PTQ-like cost.
nodes.problem: Diffusion model deployment is costly, and post-training quantization degrades quality at low bit-widths.
nodes.approach: Quantization-aware LoRA with scale-aware optimization and temporal learned step-size quantization, distilled without data.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion quantization is a crowded efficiency direction.

nodes.title: Query-Policy Misalignment in Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows preference-based RL query selection misaligns with the agent's policy, and fixes it with policy-aligned queries and hybrid experience replay.
nodes.problem: Queries chosen to improve the reward model may not help policy learning, which wastes human feedback.
nodes.approach: Policy-aligned query selection plus hybrid experience replay that enforces bidirectional query-policy alignment.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Query-policy alignment in preference-based RL is an under-studied issue

nodes.title: Accelerating Data Generation for Neural Operators via Krylov Subspace Recycling
nodes.tldr: Accelerates PDE solver data generation for neural operators by sorting linear systems for similarity and recycling Krylov subspaces, up to 13.9x.
nodes.problem: Generating labeled PDE data requires solving many linear systems independently, which is redundant and slow.
nodes.approach: Sort systems by similarity, then solve sequentially with Krylov subspace recycling.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Krylov recycling for neural-operator data generation is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: DreamGaussian: Generative Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Content Creation
nodes.tldr: Fast image-to-3D and text-to-3D generation using Gaussian Splatting with progressive densification, then mesh extraction and UV texture refinement, producing textured meshes in two minutes.
nodes.problem: Slow per-sample optimization in score-distillation-based 3D content generation.
nodes.approach: Generative Gaussian splatting with progressive densification, mesh extraction, and UV-space texture fine-tuning.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Crowded 3D generation area, though splatting angle is newer.

nodes.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-world Github Issues?
nodes.tldr: Introduces SWE-bench, 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repositories, where models must edit codebases to resolve issues, with early models solving very few.
nodes.problem: Language model evaluation lacks realistic, challenging software engineering tasks spanning multiple files.
nodes.approach: Benchmark built from real GitHub issues and their pull requests; models edit whole codebases to resolve each issue.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Coding benchmarks are common; repository-level issue resolution is a growing subarea.

nodes.title: Influencer Backdoor Attack on Semantic Segmentation
nodes.tldr: Poisoning attack on semantic segmentation that flips all victim-class pixels via a trigger placed on non-victim pixels at inference.
nodes.problem: Backdoor attacks on segmentation models are largely unstudied compared to classification.
nodes.approach: Nearest-neighbor trigger injection with pixel random labeling during poisoning.
nodes.niche_reason: Backdoor attacks on segmentation are rare relative to classification.

nodes.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
nodes.tldr: Multi-agent LLM framework encoding human standardized operating procedures into prompts so agents follow an assembly-line workflow for software tasks.
nodes.problem: Chaining LLM agents causes logic inconsistencies and cascading hallucinations on complex tasks.
nodes.approach: Assigns SOP-driven roles in an assembly-line workflow so agents verify each other's intermediate results.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-agent LLM collaboration is a crowded area

nodes.title: On the Role of Discrete Tokenization in Visual Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: Theoretically analyzes how discrete tokens in masked image modeling affect generalization, proposes the TCAS metric, and designs ClusterMIM with a better tokenizer.
nodes.problem: The theoretical role of discrete tokens as reconstruction targets in masked image modeling is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Link MIM to contrastive learning for a generalization analysis, define TCAS, and build a clustering-based tokenizer.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Tokenization theory for MIM is specialised within self-supervision.

nodes.title: Lipschitz Singularities in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Shows diffusion models often have infinite Lipschitz constants near timestep zero, hurting training and sampling stability, and proposes E-TSDM to alleviate the singularity.
nodes.problem: Diffusion sampling near timestep zero has infinite Lipschitz constants, which threatens stability and accuracy.
nodes.approach: Theoretical proofs and empirical checks, then E-TSDM, a timestep-singularity fix that also lowers FID of DDIM and DPM-Solver.
nodes.niche_reason: Lipschitz singularities in diffusion timesteps is a specialised theory-practice niche.

nodes.title: Improved Techniques for Training Consistency Models
nodes.tldr: Improves consistency training without distillation by removing EMA from the teacher, using Pseudo-Huber losses, a lognormal noise schedule and curriculum, reaching one-step FID 2.51 on CIFAR-10.
nodes.problem: Consistency models rely on diffusion distillation and biased learned metrics like LPIPS.
nodes.approach: Remove teacher EMA, Pseudo-Huber loss, lognormal noise schedule, and progressively doubled discretization steps.
nodes.niche_reason: Consistency models and few-step diffusion are a popular direction.

nodes.title: Knowledge Card: Filling LLMs' Knowledge Gaps with Plug-in Specialized Language Models
nodes.tldr: Knowledge Card plugs domain-specialized small language models into a general LLM as knowledge sources, with selectors for relevance, brevity and factuality, to fill knowledge gaps modularly.
nodes.problem: Static LLMs are costly to update and fail to provide up-to-date or domain knowledge.
nodes.approach: Specialized LMs generate background knowledge, filtered by content selectors and integrated into a base LLM.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Modular LM-as-knowledge-source is an established but less common alternative to RAG.

nodes.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo for 3D Sliced Wasserstein
nodes.tldr: Replaces Monte Carlo with quasi-Monte Carlo point sets on the 3D sphere for sliced Wasserstein approximation, with randomized unbiased variants tested on point-cloud tasks.
nodes.problem: Monte Carlo approximation of Sliced Wasserstein distance is suboptimal in approximation error.
nodes.approach: QMC point sets on the 3D hypersphere and randomized QSW with convergence and unbiasedness proofs.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: QMC for sliced Wasserstein is a rare numerical niche.

nodes.title: Stack Attention: Improving the Ability of Transformers to Model Hierarchical Patterns
nodes.tldr: Stack attention adds differentiable stacks to transformer attention so models can learn hierarchical, context-free patterns, improving formal language recognition and small-budget language modeling.
nodes.problem: Standard attention cannot handle arbitrarily nested hierarchical patterns such as context-free languages.
nodes.approach: Attention operator with latent stack models inspired by deterministic and nondeterministic pushdown automata.
nodes.niche_reason: Formal-language-inspired attention is a rare direction.

nodes.title: Stabilizing Contrastive RL: Techniques for Robotic Goal Reaching from Offline Data
nodes.tldr: Makes contrastive goal-conditioned RL work on image-based real robot manipulation, where tasks are specified by a single goal image after training.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised goal-reaching RL has rarely been shown to work on real robots from images
nodes.approach: Architecture and hyperparameter fixes found in simulation, then contrastive RL trained on real image data
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Real-robot contrastive goal-reaching is a rare application

nodes.title: Generating Images with 3D Annotations Using Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Generates images with explicit 3D control by conditioning ControlNet on edge maps of rendered 3D shapes, giving free 3D annotations that improve vision tasks.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models lack 3D structure control, so generated images lack 3D annotations for training vision models.
nodes.approach: Render 3D shapes, extract edge maps, and use them as ControlNet visual prompts to generate annotated images.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-generated training data with 3D annotations is specialised.

nodes.title: Leveraging augmented-Lagrangian techniques for differentiating over infeasible quadratic programs in machine learning
nodes.tldr: Uses augmented-Lagrangian techniques to differentiate through feasible and infeasible quadratic programs, enabling QP layers that tolerate infeasibility, with an open-source C++ package QPLayer.
nodes.problem: Optimization layers break when underlying QPs are infeasible during training.
nodes.approach: Primal-dual augmented Lagrangian differentiation of closest-feasible QP solutions, with a fast C++ implementation.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.niche_reason: Differentiable QP layers are a rare niche.

nodes.title: Symmetric Mean-field Langevin Dynamics for Distributional Minimax Problems
nodes.tldr: Extends mean-field Langevin dynamics to distributional minimax problems with symmetric algorithms (MFL-AG, MFL-ABR) that converge to mixed Nash equilibria, with propagation-of-chaos results.
nodes.problem: Provably convergent minimax optimization over probability distributions with symmetric updates.
nodes.approach: Single-loop weighted-averaged gradient descent ascent and double-loop anchored best response, analyzed with particle discretization.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Very rare mean-field minimax optimization theory.

nodes.title: Tuning LayerNorm in Attention: Towards Efficient Multi-Modal LLM Finetuning
nodes.tldr: Tuning only the LayerNorm in each attention block turns an LLM into a competitive multimodal LLM, with fewer trainable parameters and less memory than LoRA.
nodes.problem: Adapting LLMs to multimodal inputs is costly with full finetuning or LoRA.
nodes.approach: Finetune only LayerNorm parameters within attention blocks, optionally on conversational data.
nodes.niche_reason: Parameter-efficient multimodal LLM tuning is a crowded direction

nodes.title: Is ImageNet worth 1 video? Learning strong image encoders from 1 long unlabelled video
nodes.tldr: Learns strong image encoders from one long unlabeled walking-tour video using DoRA, a tracking-based self-supervised method with transformer cross-attention.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised pretraining uses billions of images; can far less data suffice?
nodes.approach: Track objects over time with cross-attention and use track-derived views in self-distillation.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Single-video pretraining is an unusual data-efficiency angle.

nodes.title: Addressing Signal Delay in Deep Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Formalizes delayed-observation MDPs and proposes strategies that let deep RL handle large signal delays, matching non-delayed performance on continuous control.
nodes.problem: Lag between perception and action makes standard deep RL fail under signal delay.
nodes.approach: Delayed-observation MDP formulation with strategies for handling delayed observations.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Delay-robust RL is a specialised but recognised problem.

nodes.title: A Lightweight Method for Tackling Unknown Participation Statistics in Federated Averaging
nodes.tldr: FedAU adapts FedAvg aggregation weights from clients' participation history to handle unknown heterogeneous participation without heavy memory, with convergence guarantees and linear speedup.
nodes.problem: Unknown, heterogeneous client participation biases federated averaging, and existing fixes need heavy memory.
nodes.approach: Online estimates of optimal aggregation weights in FedAvg from participation history, with convergence analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated optimization is established but specialised.

nodes.title: CO2: Efficient Distributed Training with Full Communication-Computation Overlap
nodes.tldr: Enables large-model data-parallel training on low-bandwidth clusters by overlapping communication with computation via local updates and asynchronous communication.
nodes.problem: Large-scale data-parallel training needs costly high-bandwidth clusters, limiting access.
nodes.approach: Local updating with asynchronous communication, staleness gap penalty, and outer momentum clipping.
nodes.niche_reason: Low-bandwidth distributed LLM training is an established systems direction

nodes.title: Retrieval-based Disentangled Representation Learning with Natural Language Supervision
nodes.tldr: VDR is a bi-encoder retrieval framework mapping data and text into a vocabulary space, using natural language as proxies of variation for interpretable disentangled representations.
nodes.problem: Disentangled representation learning lacks natural factors of variation in real data.
nodes.approach: Bi-encoder projecting data and language into a vocabulary space with sparse, retrieval-based training.
nodes.niche_reason: Interpretable sparse retrieval framed as disentanglement is specialised.

nodes.title: Diffusion Model for Dense Matching
nodes.tldr: DiffMatch uses a conditional diffusion model with matching cost to explicitly learn both data and prior terms for dense correspondence, in a cascaded pipeline.
nodes.problem: Dense matching struggles with ambiguities like textureless regions, repetition and large displacements.
nodes.approach: Conditional denoising diffusion on matching cost with cascaded super-resolution of the matching field.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion for correspondence is a specialised application.

nodes.title: LLMCarbon: Modeling the End-to-End Carbon Footprint of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: LLMCarbon projects the end-to-end carbon footprint of dense and mixture-of-experts LLMs before training, including embodied and operational emissions.
nodes.problem: Existing tools cannot predict pre-training carbon for MoE LLMs or embodied emissions.
nodes.approach: Architecture-aware end-to-end carbon projection model covering GPUs and embodied carbon.
nodes.niche_reason: Carbon modeling of LLMs is an emerging, specialised topic.

nodes.title: The mechanistic basis of data dependence and abrupt learning in an in-context classification task
nodes.tldr: Explains abrupt in-context learning as induction-head formation, via nested logit learning, and how data burstiness trades off against in-weights learning.
nodes.problem: Why transformers switch abruptly to in-context learning, and how data distribution controls that trade-off.
nodes.approach: Two-parameter phenomenological model of induction head formation, validated with progress measures and targeted experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Induction-head mechanistic studies are a popular, growing area.

nodes.title: Decision ConvFormer: Local Filtering in MetaFormer is Sufficient for Decision Making
nodes.tldr: Decision ConvFormer replaces attention in Decision Transformer with local convolution token mixing in a MetaFormer, matching or beating it on offline RL with fewer resources.
nodes.problem: Decision Transformer's attention poorly captures the local dependence structure of MDP trajectories.
nodes.approach: MetaFormer action predictor using local convolution filtering as the token mixer for offline RL.
nodes.niche_reason: Sequence-model offline RL is a common direction.

nodes.title: Predictive auxiliary objectives in deep RL mimic learning in the brain
nodes.tldr: Analyses predictive auxiliary objectives in deep RL, finding they stabilise learning and mirror hippocampal and cortical representational changes in the brain.
nodes.problem: Unclear how predictive auxiliary objectives shape RL representations and whether they resemble brain learning.
nodes.approach: Controlled RL experiments comparing module representations with known hippocampal, cortical and striatal activity patterns.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Cross-disciplinary RL-neuroscience comparison, unusual angle

nodes.title: Making Pre-trained Language Models Great on Tabular Prediction
nodes.tldr: TP-BERTa is a language model pre-trained for tabular prediction using relative magnitude tokenization of numeric values and intra-feature attention, competitive with gradient-boosted trees.
nodes.problem: Language models' discrete text space is incompatible with numerical feature values across heterogeneous tables.
nodes.approach: Relative magnitude tokenization of numbers plus intra-feature attention linking values to feature names.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Tabular foundation models are an established but specialised area.

nodes.title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
nodes.tldr: Finds LLMs can be swayed by coherent external evidence that conflicts with memory, yet show confirmation bias when evidence partly matches their parametric knowledge.
nodes.problem: How LLMs behave when retrieved or tool-provided evidence conflicts with their parametric memory.
nodes.approach: Controlled framework that elicits parametric memory and builds counter-memory for systematic experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Knowledge conflicts in RAG are an active, fairly common topic

nodes.title: Phenomenal Yet Puzzling: Testing Inductive Reasoning Capabilities of Language Models with Hypothesis Refinement
nodes.tldr: Studies LM inductive reasoning via iterative hypothesis refinement with symbolic interpreters, finding LMs propose good rules but struggle to apply them, unlike humans.
nodes.problem: Understanding the inductive reasoning capabilities and limits of language models.
nodes.approach: Propose-select-refine hypothesis loop with task-specific symbolic interpreters and human comparison analyses.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Inductive reasoning analysis is specialised within LLM reasoning.

nodes.title: Latent Trajectory Learning for Limited Timestamps under Distribution Shift over Time
nodes.tldr: Infers continuous data-distribution trajectories between sparse timestamps using stochastic differential equations, improving generalization to unseen future domains.
nodes.problem: Evolving domain generalization has too few timestamps to capture distribution shift dynamics.
nodes.approach: SDE-modeled trajectories aligned with interpolated continuous-time samples across domains.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Could be time-series or domain generalization; modality not stated.
nodes.niche_reason: Continuous-time evolving domain generalization is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: FITS: Modeling Time Series with $10k$ Parameters
nodes.tldr: Lightweight time-series model with about 10k parameters that interpolates in the complex frequency domain, competitive for forecasting and anomaly detection.
nodes.problem: Time-series models process raw time-domain data and are large, which limits deployment on edge devices.
nodes.approach: Complex-frequency-domain interpolation implemented with a tiny complex-valued network.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Frequency-domain tiny time-series models are a less common design choice

nodes.title: Sharpness-Aware Data Poisoning Attack
nodes.tldr: Poisons training data by optimizing the attack against the sharpest worst-case retrained model, so it survives retraining uncertainty in initialization and architecture.
nodes.problem: Data poisoning attacks are unreliable because retraining randomness weakens the injected effect.
nodes.approach: Loss-landscape sharpness objective approximating the worst-case re-trained network.
nodes.confidence_reason: Attack framing is clear; sharpness-to-training link is thin in abstract
nodes.niche_reason: Poisoning attacks are a common security topic

nodes.title: METRA: Scalable Unsupervised RL with Metric-Aware Abstraction
nodes.tldr: METRA learns diverse skills by covering a compact latent space metrically tied to states via temporal distances, scaling unsupervised RL to pixel-based locomotion.
nodes.problem: Unsupervised RL fails to scale to high-dimensional environments via pure exploration or mutual information skills.
nodes.approach: Temporal-distance-aware latent abstraction objective that learns to move in every latent direction.
nodes.niche_reason: Unsupervised skill discovery is an established but specialised subfield.

nodes.title: Deep Orthogonal Hypersphere Compression for Anomaly Detection
nodes.tldr: Deep anomaly detection with an orthogonal projection layer and bi-hypersphere compression giving a compact hyperspherical shell boundary, extended to graph-level anomaly detection.
nodes.problem: Hypersphere decision boundaries for anomaly detection are hard to obtain and not compact in high dimensions.
nodes.approach: Orthogonal projection layer enforcing hypersphere hypothesis, bi-hypersphere shell compression, graph mutual-information representation.
nodes.niche_reason: Deep one-class anomaly detection is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Approximating Nash Equilibria in Normal-Form Games via Stochastic Optimization
nodes.tldr: Gives the first loss for approximate Nash equilibria of normal-form games that admits unbiased Monte Carlo estimates, so standard stochastic gradient methods apply.
nodes.problem: Approximating Nash equilibria lacks losses suited to stochastic optimization
nodes.approach: Unbiased Monte Carlo-estimable loss enabling non-convex stochastic gradient optimization with guarantees
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Stochastic-optimization view of Nash equilibria is unusual

nodes.title: Large Language Models are Efficient Learners of Noise-Robust Speech Recognition
nodes.tldr: Uses an LLM to correct noisy ASR n-best hypotheses, with a language-space noise embedding distilled from audio; up to 53.9% WER correction.
nodes.problem: LLM error correction for ASR lacks explicit awareness of acoustic noise conditions
nodes.approach: Language-space noise embedding from N-best lists, with mutual-information knowledge distillation from audio
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: LLM error correction for ASR is an active, specialised niche

nodes.title: Learning the greatest common divisor: explaining transformer predictions
nodes.tldr: Shows small transformers learning GCD are explained by their inputs and outputs, learning a divisor list shaped by training distributions.
nodes.problem: Why small transformers learn GCD and how training distributions affect what they learn.
nodes.approach: Characterizes the learned divisor list by analyzing model inputs and outputs across training distributions.
nodes.confidence_reason: interpretability of a toy arithmetic task; topic placement is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: mechanistic explanation of arithmetic in toy transformers is rare

nodes.title: Generalized Policy Iteration using Tensor Approximation for Hybrid Control
nodes.tldr: TTPI uses Tensor Train low-rank approximation of state-value and advantage functions in generalized policy iteration, handling hybrid discrete-continuous actions for robot control.
nodes.problem: Control with hybrid action spaces is hard for standard approximate dynamic programming methods.
nodes.approach: Tensor Train approximation of value and advantage functions within generalized policy iteration.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Approximate DP for control vs policy-iteration RL; topic straddles two areas
nodes.niche_reason: Tensor-train value approximation for hybrid action control is uncommon

nodes.title: Procedural Fairness Through Decoupling Objectionable Data Generating Components
nodes.tldr: Introduces disguised procedural unfairness and a Rawls-inspired framework decoupling objectionable from neutral data-generating components using reference points, so only problematic aspects are altered.
nodes.problem: Fairness interventions may inadvertently alter neutral aspects of the data generating process, a disguised procedural unfairness.
nodes.approach: Decouple objectionable data generating components from neutral ones via reference points and value instantiation rules.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.confidence_reason: Abstract is conceptual and framework details are thin.
nodes.niche_reason: Philosophy-driven procedural fairness framing is unusual.

nodes.title: Bounds on Representation-Induced Confounding Bias for Treatment Effect Estimation
nodes.tldr: Provides a representation-agnostic neural refutation framework that bounds confounding bias induced by low-dimensional representations in CATE estimation, via partial identification.
nodes.problem: Representation learning for CATE can lose confounder information, causing unquantified bias.
nodes.approach: Theory of non-identifiability plus neural partial identification estimating bias bounds.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Established causal inference subfield, specialised topic.

nodes.title: Small-scale proxies for large-scale Transformer training instabilities
nodes.tldr: Reproduces transformer training instabilities such as logit growth at small scale, showing which optimizer and model interventions reduce learning-rate sensitivity.
nodes.problem: Large-scale transformer training instabilities are costly to reproduce and study.
nodes.approach: Small-model learning-rate sweeps with warm-up, weight decay, and MuParam, plus scaling of activation and gradient norms.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: Transformer training stability is a common, active research area

nodes.title: Tool-Augmented Reward Modeling
nodes.tldr: Themis gives reward models access to calculators and search engines, producing tool-use reasoning traces that improve preference ranking and RLHF win rates.
nodes.problem: Conventional reward models fail at arithmetic, code execution and factual lookup.
nodes.approach: Tool-augmented preference modeling with autoregressive tool calls and reasoning traces; tool-related RM datasets released.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Reward modeling for RLHF is a crowded mainstream area.

nodes.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
nodes.tldr: ToolLLM builds a tool-use instruction dataset over 16k real APIs, trains LLaMA with a depth-first decision-tree search, and evaluates it with an automatic judge.
nodes.problem: Open-source LLMs lag closed models at using external APIs because instruction tuning ignores tool use.
nodes.approach: ChatGPT-generated instructions and solution paths for real APIs, a depth-first search for reasoning traces, and ToolEval.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: LLM tool use is a fast-growing mainstream area.

nodes.title: Topological data analysis on noisy quantum computers
nodes.tldr: Presents NISQ-TDA, a short-depth quantum algorithm for topological data analysis that avoids data loading and runs on noisy devices.
nodes.problem: Classical topological data analysis is computationally prohibitive, and prior quantum TDA needs fault tolerance.
nodes.approach: Short-depth circuit with provable asymptotic speedup, run on quantum hardware and noisy simulators.
nodes.confidence_reason: Quantum ML for TDA; no exact topic, so nearest areas are used.
nodes.niche_reason: Quantum TDA on near-term hardware is extremely rare

nodes.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
nodes.tldr: SDXL scales latent diffusion with a 3x larger UNet, dual text encoders, new conditioning schemes, multi-aspect training and a refinement model for high-resolution text-to-image synthesis.
nodes.problem: Improving quality and resolution of open latent diffusion text-to-image models.
nodes.approach: Larger UNet backbone, second text encoder, size/crop conditioning, multi-aspect training and a refiner.
nodes.niche_reason: Mainstream text-to-image diffusion model.

nodes.title: Initializing Models with Larger Ones
nodes.tldr: Weight selection initializes small models by taking a subset of weights from a larger pretrained model, improving accuracy and training time and complementing distillation.
nodes.problem: Small models lack good initialization even though large pretrained models are widely available.
nodes.approach: Select a subset of pretrained larger-model weights to initialize a smaller model of the same family.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Initialization from larger models is established but less crowded.

nodes.title: Lion Secretly Solves a Constrained Optimization: As Lyapunov Predicts
nodes.tldr: Shows Lion is theoretically grounded: it minimizes a loss under an infinity-norm bound via decoupled weight decay, using a new Lyapunov function.
nodes.problem: Lion works well empirically but lacks a theoretical basis explaining its behavior.
nodes.approach: Continuous- and discrete-time analysis with a new Lyapunov function for constrained composite optimization.
nodes.niche_reason: Lion optimizer analysis is active but a common optimization topic

nodes.title: PixArt-$\alpha$: Fast Training of Diffusion Transformer for Photorealistic Text-to-Image Synthesis
nodes.tldr: PixArt-alpha is a cheap-to-train diffusion transformer for text-to-image synthesis, using decomposed training, an efficient cross-attention DiT and auto-labeled data.
nodes.problem: State-of-the-art text-to-image models need huge training cost and emissions.
nodes.approach: Three-stage training decomposition, efficient T2I transformer with cross-attention, and dense auto-labeled data.
nodes.niche_reason: Text-to-image diffusion transformers are very crowded mainstream.

nodes.title: Merge, Then Compress: Demystify Efficient SMoE with Hints from Its Routing Policy
nodes.tldr: MC-SMoE merges mixture-of-experts experts guided by routing statistics after neuron alignment, then compresses them low-rank and sparse, cutting memory up to 80%.
nodes.problem: Sparse MoE models use heavy memory and have redundant experts, hindering resource-constrained deployment.
nodes.approach: Align expert neurons, group by routing policy, merge weighted by activation frequency, then low-rank and sparse decomposition.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: MoE compression is established but more specialised than mainstream.

nodes.title: Blending Imitation and Reinforcement Learning for Robust Policy Improvement
nodes.tldr: Robust Policy Improvement interleaves imitation and reinforcement learning based on online performance estimates, learning from black-box oracles.
nodes.problem: RL is sample-hungry and IL is capped by oracle quality, and sparse-reward exploration is especially hard.
nodes.approach: Robust Active Policy Selection and Robust Policy Gradient choose per state between imitating oracles and learning from RL.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.confidence_reason: Imitation-RL mix could fit either RL or imitation topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Mixing imitation and RL with oracles is a common hybrid approach

nodes.title: SaNN: Simple Yet Powerful Simplicial-aware Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Scalable simplicial network that pre-aggregates simplex features so cost is independent of complex size, with provable Weisfeiler-Lehman-style expressivity.
nodes.problem: Simplicial neural networks are too costly in memory and training time for large complexes
nodes.approach: Pre-aggregated simplicial-aware features fed to a standard neural network
nodes.niche_reason: Simplicial complex learning is rare relative to mainstream GNNs

nodes.title: Understanding In-Context Learning in Transformers and LLMs by Learning to Learn Discrete Functions
nodes.tldr: Shows Transformers nearly match optimal learners on simple Boolean function classes, learn two algorithms for one task, and LLMs compete with nearest-neighbor baselines.
nodes.problem: Unclear how far Transformer in-context learning extends beyond real-valued functions, and whether it transfers to pretrained LLMs.
nodes.approach: Controlled experiments on Boolean function classes with teaching sequences, plus tests of LLaMA-2 and GPT-4 on held-out tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: ICL theory on Boolean functions is a specialised analysis niche.

nodes.title: Consistency Training with Learnable Data Augmentation for Graph Anomaly Detection with Limited Supervision
nodes.tldr: ConsisGAD uses consistency training with learnable data augmentation and a homophily-aware simple GNN backbone to detect anomalous nodes under limited labels and class imbalance.
nodes.problem: Graph node anomaly detection under limited supervision and class imbalance.
nodes.approach: Consistency training with learned augmentation on unlabeled nodes plus homophily-based GNN backbone.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph anomaly detection is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Towards Energy Efficient Spiking Neural Networks: An Unstructured Pruning Framework
nodes.tldr: Proposes unstructured weight and neuron pruning for deep spiking neural networks to maximize sparsity and energy efficiency, achieving 91x efficiency gain on CIFAR-10.
nodes.problem: Deep SNNs lose energy efficiency advantage; existing pruning does not target energy or neuron sparsity.
nodes.approach: Combined unstructured weight pruning and unstructured neuron pruning targeting energy consumption.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Spiking network pruning is a rare niche.

nodes.title: AnyText: Multilingual Visual Text Generation and Editing
nodes.tldr: AnyText is a diffusion model that renders and edits accurate multilingual text in images using glyph/position latents and OCR-based text embeddings, with a 3M-image dataset.
nodes.problem: Text-to-image models produce blurred or wrong characters in generated visual text.
nodes.approach: Auxiliary latent module and OCR-based text embedding in diffusion with text-control and perceptual losses.
nodes.niche_reason: Visual text rendering is specialised within image generation.

nodes.title: LiDAR: Sensing Linear Probing Performance in Joint Embedding SSL Architectures
nodes.tldr: LiDAR is a label-free metric, the rank of the LDA matrix of the SSL surrogate task, predicting linear probing performance and good hyperparameters.
nodes.problem: Evaluating joint-embedding SSL representations without downstream labels or tasks to iterate on design choices.
nodes.approach: Compute rank of the linear discriminant analysis matrix over surrogate-task classes as a representation quality metric.
nodes.niche_reason: Unsupervised SSL evaluation metrics are a specialised subtopic.

nodes.title: Project and Probe: Sample-Efficient Adaptation by Interpolating Orthogonal Features
nodes.tldr: Learns diverse orthogonal linear feature projections from pretrained embeddings, then linearly probes their interpolation for sample-efficient adaptation under distribution shift.
nodes.problem: Adapting pretrained models to distribution shift needs labels that are scarce in the target domain.
nodes.approach: Orthogonal projection learning on source data, then linear probe over interpolated projected features.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Linear probing and feature adaptation are common research directions

nodes.title: Convergence of Bayesian Bilevel Optimization
nodes.tldr: Proves sublinear regret for Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters with inner SGD training, showing joint convergence of model parameters and hyperparameters.
nodes.problem: No convergence guarantee exists for Bayesian bilevel optimization of hyperparameters with SGD training.
nodes.approach: Models SGD excess risk as evaluation noise inside Bayesian optimization regret analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.confidence_reason: Regret analysis spans bilevel optimization and Bayesian optimization.
nodes.niche_reason: Regret theory for Bayesian bilevel hyperparameter tuning is rare.

nodes.title: $\mathcal{B}$-Coder: Value-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Program Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Proposes value-based deep RL for program synthesis, using pretrained LM initialisation and a conservative Bellman operator, and using value functions to post-process generated programs.
nodes.problem: Policy-gradient methods dominate RL for code generation, leaving value-based approaches unexplored.
nodes.approach: Pretrained-LM initialisation and conservative Bellman updates for off-policy program data, with unit-test rewards.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.confidence_reason: Value-based RL versus RL-for-LLM framing is a judgement call
nodes.niche_reason: Value-based code RL is less common than policy methods

nodes.title: Consistent Multi-Class Classification from Multiple Unlabeled Datasets
nodes.tldr: Learns a multi-class classifier from several unlabeled sets given only class priors, with a consistent risk-based importance-weighting method.
nodes.problem: Training multi-class classifiers from multiple unlabeled datasets given only class priors.
nodes.approach: Classifier-consistent transition-matrix method, then risk-consistent importance-weighted purification of supervision.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.confidence_reason: No weak-supervision topic exists; theory-versus-method call.
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-unlabeled-set weak supervision is a specialised setting

nodes.title: Circuit Component Reuse Across Tasks in Transformer Language Models
nodes.tldr: The IOI circuit in GPT-2 is largely reused (78% head overlap) for Colored Objects; intervening on four heads lifts accuracy from 49.6% to 93.7%.
nodes.problem: Whether mechanistic circuits generalize across tasks rather than being task-specific.
nodes.approach: Circuit analysis of IOI versus Colored Objects, with attention-head interventions to repair behavior.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic interpretability is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Tensor Trust: Interpretable Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game
nodes.tldr: Releases a 563k-attack dataset from an online game and a benchmark showing many LLMs are vulnerable to prompt extraction and hijacking.
nodes.problem: Prompt injection attacks on instruction-following LLMs lack large human-generated attack and defense data
nodes.approach: Crowdsourced attacks and defenses from players of an online game, turned into a two-type robustness benchmark.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt injection security is an active mainstream LLM topic

nodes.title: Improving Generalization of Alignment with Human Preferences through Group Invariant Learning
nodes.tldr: Improves RLHF generalization across domains by learning a consistent policy via group invariant learning that discovers data groups without annotations.
nodes.problem: RLHF exploits shortcuts and generalizes poorly across domains and challenging samples.
nodes.approach: Invariant learning that infers latent data groups and enforces consistent policy across them.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: RLHF variants are very common; invariance angle is mildly distinct.

nodes.title: Flow Matching on General Geometries
nodes.tldr: Riemannian Flow Matching trains continuous normalizing flows on manifolds without simulation on simple geometries, using closed-form target vector fields and spectral premetrics for general geometries.
nodes.problem: Scalable, unbiased generative modeling on manifolds without costly simulation or divergence computation.
nodes.approach: Simulation-free flow matching with premetric-based closed-form target vector fields; spectral decompositions for general meshes.
nodes.niche_reason: Flow matching is crowded, but manifold geometry is specialised.

nodes.title: Adaptive Rational Activations to Boost Deep Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Introduces joint-rational activation functions that are closed under residual connections, improving deep RL plasticity and Atari performance with regularised parameters.
nodes.problem: Static activation functions limit neural plasticity in deep RL agents facing changing environments.
nodes.approach: Adaptable rational activation units shared across layers, derived to be closed under residual connections.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Learnable rational activations for RL plasticity is a specialised angle

nodes.title: Evaluating the Zero-shot Robustness of Instruction-tuned Language Models
nodes.tldr: Shows instruction-tuned LLMs are sensitive to instruction rephrasings, and proposes soft-prompt embeddings trained to make representations of equivalent instructions similar.
nodes.problem: Instruction-tuned models may be brittle to unseen but semantically equivalent phrasings.
nodes.approach: Learned soft-prompt embeddings optimized to align representations of paraphrased instructions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Prompt and instruction robustness is a common, well-studied theme.

nodes.title: Gene Regulatory Network Inference in the Presence of Dropouts: a Causal View
nodes.tldr: Introduces a causal dropout model showing that deleting zero-valued samples for conditioned variables preserves conditional independence tests for gene regulatory network inference.
nodes.problem: Dropout zeros in single-cell RNA-seq distort joint distributions, biasing network inference.
nodes.approach: Test-wise deletion of zero samples for conditioned variables, plugged into existing structure-learning methods.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Causal dropout modelling for gene networks is a niche angle

nodes.title: Würstchen: An Efficient Architecture for Large-Scale Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Würstchen is a cost-efficient text-to-image diffusion architecture that guides latent diffusion with a highly compressed learned semantic image representation, greatly cutting training and inference compute.
nodes.problem: Large-scale text-to-image diffusion models are computationally expensive to train and run.
nodes.approach: Multi-stage latent diffusion where a text-conditional prior generates an extremely compact image latent for decoding.
nodes.niche_reason: Text-to-image diffusion is crowded, though efficiency angle is distinct.

nodes.title: DyVal: Dynamic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Reasoning Tasks
nodes.tldr: DyVal is a protocol for dynamically generating LLM reasoning evaluation samples from DAGs with controllable complexity, mitigating data contamination and fixed-difficulty benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Static benchmarks risk contamination and cannot scale difficulty with LLM capabilities.
nodes.approach: Generate evaluation samples on the fly using directed acyclic graphs for math, logic and algorithm tasks.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM benchmark creation is crowded.

nodes.title: Confronting Reward Model Overoptimization with Constrained RLHF
nodes.tldr: Uses constrained RL so each component reward model stays within its useful range, learning dynamic weights via Lagrange multipliers to avoid overoptimization.
nodes.problem: Composite reward models are hard to weight and vulnerable to overoptimization in RLHF.
nodes.approach: Constrained RL with per-reward-model thresholds, Lagrange multipliers as dynamic weights, and gradient-free adaptive search.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: RLHF overoptimization is a common, active alignment topic.

nodes.title: Can LLMs Keep a Secret? Testing Privacy Implications of Language Models via Contextual Integrity Theory
nodes.tldr: CONFAIDE benchmark uses contextual integrity to test whether LLMs keep information private in context; GPT-4 and ChatGPT leak 39% and 57% of the time.
nodes.problem: Existing LLM privacy evaluation ignores contextual disclosure judgments in interactive multi-source settings.
nodes.approach: Four-tier benchmark grounded in contextual integrity, up to theory-of-mind privacy reasoning.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Contextual privacy reasoning in LLMs is a specialised angle.

nodes.title: SalUn: Empowering Machine Unlearning via Gradient-based Weight Saliency in Both Image Classification and Generation
nodes.tldr: Erases the influence of forgotten data, classes, or concepts by updating only salient weights, closing the gap to exact unlearning.
nodes.problem: Existing unlearning methods lack accuracy, stability, and cross-domain applicability.
nodes.approach: Gradient-based weight saliency directs unlearning to specific weights rather than the full model.

nodes.niche_reason: Unlearning and weight saliency is a moderately crowded area

nodes.title: Multi-Source Diffusion Models for Simultaneous Music Generation and Separation
nodes.tldr: A single diffusion model learns the joint score of musical sources, enabling mixture generation, source separation, and source imputation using a Dirac-likelihood-based separation inference.
nodes.problem: Music generation and source separation are handled by separate models.
nodes.approach: Score-based diffusion over jointly modeled sources trained on Slakh2100, with Dirac likelihood inference.

secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Music generation and separation unified is specialised.

nodes.title: Solving Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Cooperative Tasks with Greedy Sequential Execution
nodes.tldr: Cooperative multi-agent method using greedy sequential execution with an individual utility function, handling both homogeneous and heterogeneous tasks via credit from marginal contributions.
nodes.problem: Value decomposition fails to handle homogeneous and heterogeneous cooperative tasks together.
nodes.approach: Sequential execution policies with individual utility and greedy marginal-contribution credit.

nodes.niche_reason: Common value-decomposition MARL variant.

nodes.title: Lemur: Harmonizing Natural Language and Code for Language Agents
nodes.tldr: Lemur and Lemur-Chat are open models pretrained on code-heavy corpora to balance natural language and coding for language agents.
nodes.problem: Open models specialise in either language or code, which limits their use as versatile agent backbones.
nodes.approach: Code-intensive pretraining followed by instruction fine-tuning on mixed text and code data.

secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use

nodes.niche_reason: Open code-and-language LLMs for agents are a common direction.

nodes.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
nodes.tldr: Self-RAG trains one LM with reflection tokens to retrieve adaptively and critique retrieved context and its own generations, improving factuality and citation accuracy.
nodes.problem: Fixed, indiscriminate retrieval hurts LM versatility and can yield unhelpful or unfactual responses.
nodes.approach: Train an LM to emit reflection tokens deciding when to retrieve and assessing relevance and its own outputs.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: RAG is a crowded area.

nodes.title: Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!
nodes.tldr: Red-teaming shows a handful of adversarial or even benign fine-tuning examples can strip safety alignment from aligned LLMs, exposing risks in customized fine-tuning APIs.
nodes.problem: Safety alignment of aligned LLMs may not survive user fine-tuning, which is now offered by APIs.
nodes.approach: Red-teaming with small adversarial and benign fine-tuning datasets, measuring jailbreak rates after tuning.

secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-tuning safety erosion is a mainstream LLM safety concern

nodes.title: A path-norm toolkit for modern networks: consequences, promises and challenges
nodes.tldr: Develops path-norm tools for general DAG ReLU networks incl. skip connections and max pooling, giving sharp generalization bounds and testing their practical promise.
nodes.problem: Existing path-norm generalization bounds do not cover modern architectures with biases, skip connections and pooling.
nodes.approach: Extended path-norm toolkit with contraction lemma and peeling to derive bounds, tested numerically on real networks.
