nodes.title: Finetuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Fairness
nodes.tldr: Debiases text-to-image diffusion models via a distributional alignment loss and adjusted direct finetuning, reducing gender and race bias and supporting user-defined target distributions.
nodes.problem: Text-to-image diffusion models propagate social biases such as gender and racial bias in occupations.

nodes.title: On Bias-Variance Alignment in Deep Models
nodes.tldr: Shows that for deep ensembles, squared bias and variance align per sample on correctly classified points, explained via calibration and neural collapse theory.
nodes.problem: Classical bias-variance tradeoff may not hold for deep ensemble classifiers.
nodes.approach: Empirical study across deep models, plus theory under calibration and neural collapse assumptions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Established analysis area, but bias-variance alignment is specialised

nodes.title: Scaling Laws for Sparsely-Connected Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Derives the first scaling law relating weight sparsity, non-zero parameter count and data, finding optimal sparsity rises with training data across ViT and T5 models.
nodes.problem: How weight sparsity affects scaling behavior of Transformers trained on massive datasets.
nodes.approach: Empirical scaling-law fitting across sparsity levels, structures (n:m) and strategies on ViT/JFT-4B and T5/C4.

secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data

nodes.title: Asymptotically Free Sketched Ridge Ensembles: Risks, Cross-Validation, and Tuning
nodes.tldr: Proves generalized cross-validation consistently estimates prediction risk for sketched ridge ensembles, enabling tuning and valid prediction intervals.
nodes.problem: Estimating prediction risk and tuning regularization and sketch size for sketched ridge ensembles.
nodes.approach: Random matrix theory consistency proof for generalized cross-validation, extended to subquadratic risks.

secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning

nodes.title: Feature emergence via margin maximization: case studies in algebraic tasks
nodes.tldr: Proves that margin maximization alone determines features learned on algebraic tasks, yielding Fourier features for modular addition and group-representation features for group composition.

nodes.niche_reason: Theory of feature emergence on algebraic tasks is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Neural Contractive Dynamical Systems

nodes.title: Gradual Domain Adaptation via Gradient Flow
nodes.tldr: Generates labeled intermediate domains by transporting source samples toward the target via Wasserstein gradient flow and Langevin dynamics, enabling gradual adaptation.

nodes.title: Graph Metanetworks for Processing Diverse Neural Architectures

nodes.problem: Metanetworks built for MLPs and CNNs don't extend easily to attention, normalization and residual layers.

nodes.title: MAPE-PPI: Towards Effective and Efficient Protein-Protein Interaction Prediction via Microenvironment-Aware Protein Embedding

nodes.title: Learning Performance-Improving Code Edits

nodes.title: Solving Inverse Problems with Latent Diffusion Models via Hard Data Consistency
nodes.tldr: ReSample solves general inverse problems with pretrained latent diffusion models by enforcing hard data consistency and resampling back onto the noisy manifold.

nodes.title: Less is More: Fewer Interpretable Region via Submodular Subset Selection
nodes.tldr: Frames image attribution as submodular subset selection over small regions, using confidence, effectiveness, consistency and collaboration constraints.
nodes.problem: Attribution methods produce inaccurate small regions and fail on wrongly predicted samples.
nodes.approach: Novel submodular objective with four subset-selection constraints for region importance.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised submodular attribution, less common than gradient methods

nodes.title: ASID: Active Exploration for System Identification in Robotic Manipulation
nodes.tldr: ASID uses an initial simulator to design exploration policies that gather real-world data for refining simulation parameters, enabling sim-to-real transfer for manipulation.
nodes.problem: Accurate simulators need costly manual tuning of assets and physical parameters for each environment.
nodes.approach: Active exploration policies from a simulator collect informative real data to identify physical parameters, then plan control.
nodes.niche_reason: Active system identification for manipulation is specialised.

nodes.title: MuSR: Testing the Limits of Chain-of-thought with Multistep Soft Reasoning
nodes.tldr: Benchmark of free-text narratives requiring multistep soft reasoning, generated with a neurosymbolic synthetic-to-natural algorithm, exposing gaps in chain-of-thought reasoning.
nodes.problem: Static reasoning benchmarks no longer challenge capable LLMs, and realistic narrative tests are scarce.
nodes.approach: Neurosymbolic synthetic-to-natural generation of long narrative reasoning instances.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Narrative soft-reasoning benchmark is specialised.

nodes.title: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning with Communication Compression
nodes.tldr: Simplifies stochastic controlled averaging and proposes SCALLION and SCAFCOM, compressed federated learning methods that converge under arbitrary heterogeneity and partial participation.
nodes.problem: Communication compression in federated learning clashes with partial participation and data heterogeneity.
nodes.approach: Halved-uplink controlled averaging formulation with unbiased and biased compression variants.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Compressed federated learning is a common, active area.

nodes.title: Unprocessing Seven Years of Algorithmic Fairness
nodes.tldr: Re-evaluates seven years of fairness methods; postprocessing's fairness-accuracy frontier contains all other methods tested, after controlling confounds.
nodes.problem: Claimed improvements over the fairness postprocessing baseline may stem from methodological confounds.
nodes.approach: Thousands of tabular evaluations plus an unprocessing inverse-postprocessing comparison device.
nodes.niche_reason: Fairness evaluation of postprocessing; a well-trodden area.

nodes.title: From Sparse to Soft Mixtures of Experts
nodes.tldr: Soft MoE replaces sparse token routing with differentiable soft assignment of weighted token combinations to experts, scaling capacity cheaply and outperforming ViTs and standard MoEs.
nodes.problem: Sparse MoEs suffer instability, token dropping, and poor scaling in number of experts.
nodes.approach: Fully differentiable soft assignment passing weighted mixtures of all tokens to each expert.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: MoE architectures are a common research direction.

nodes.title: BECLR: Batch Enhanced Contrastive Few-Shot Learning
nodes.tldr: BECLR improves unsupervised few-shot learning with a dynamic clustered memory for contrastive pretraining and an optimal transport step at inference.
nodes.problem: Contrastive unsupervised few-shot methods suffer in pretraining sampling and inference-time distribution shift.
nodes.approach: Dynamic clustered memory module plus optimal-transport-based cluster alignment.
nodes.niche_reason: Unsupervised few-shot learning is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Selective Visual Representations Improve Convergence and Generalization for Embodied AI
nodes.tldr: Adds a small task-conditioned learnable codebook that filters frozen visual features for embodied agents, improving convergence and generalization across navigation and manipulation benchmarks.
nodes.problem: General-purpose visual backbones feed task-irrelevant information to embodied agents, adding noise to learning.
nodes.approach: Jointly trained task-conditioned codebook bottleneck acting as selective filter over visual observations.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.niche_reason: Task-conditioned visual filtering for embodied agents is specialised.

nodes.title: SE(3)-Stochastic Flow Matching for Protein Backbone Generation
nodes.tldr: FoldFlow is a family of SE(3) flow-matching generative models, including Riemannian OT and stochastic variants, for faster and more stable protein backbone generation than diffusion.
nodes.problem: Generating designable, diverse, novel protein backbones with stable and fast training.
nodes.approach: Simulation-free flow matching on SE(3) with Riemannian optimal transport and stochastic dynamics.
nodes.niche_reason: Protein generation with flow matching is specialised but active.

nodes.title: Leveraging Unpaired Data for Vision-Language Generative Models via Cycle Consistency
nodes.tldr: Uses cycle consistency to train image-text generators on unpaired images and texts, supplemented by a small paired set.
nodes.problem: Vision-language generative models need costly, scarce paired image-text data.
nodes.approach: Cycle-consistent image-to-text-to-image training on unpaired data with a joint encoder and disjoint decoders.
nodes.niche_reason: Unpaired cycle-consistent vision-language training is less common

nodes.title: Multi-resolution HuBERT: Multi-resolution Speech Self-Supervised Learning with Masked Unit Prediction
nodes.tldr: Multi-resolution hierarchical transformer with HuBERT-style masked prediction, matching or beating HuBERT with faster inference.
nodes.problem: Speech SSL models use a fixed 20ms resolution, ignoring the varying information content across resolutions.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical Transformer processing speech at several resolutions with masked unit prediction objectives.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Speech Recognition & Synthesis
nodes.niche_reason: Speech SSL is a well-established area

nodes.title: Beyond Memorization: Violating Privacy via Inference with Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Shows pretrained LLMs infer personal attributes like location and income from text at high accuracy and low cost, and that mitigations fail.
nodes.problem: LLMs may violate individual privacy by inferring personal attributes from inference-time text.
nodes.approach: Dataset of real Reddit profiles to benchmark LLM attribute inference, plus chatbot extraction and mitigation tests.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM privacy inference is an emerging but specialized topic.

nodes.title: TRAM: Bridging Trust Regions and Sharpness Aware Minimization
nodes.tldr: Combines sharpness-aware minimization with a trust-region bound so fine-tuning finds flat, representation-preserving minima that generalize out-of-domain.
nodes.problem: Fine-tuned models lose pre-trained representations and transfer poorly between anticorrelated domains.
nodes.approach: Trust-region bound defines the SAM adversarial neighborhood, adding function-space curvature awareness to parameter flatness.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: SAM variants are a common, crowded optimization direction.

nodes.title: A Poincaré Inequality and Consistency Results for Signal Sampling on Large Graphs
nodes.tldr: A Poincaré inequality for graphon signals identifies unique sampling sets, giving a consistent, scalable signal sampling algorithm for large graphs.
nodes.problem: Subsampling large graphs needs spectral computations that must be redone as graphs grow.
nodes.approach: Graphon signal sampling theory linking Paley-Wiener sampling sets to spectral clustering and Gaussian elimination.
nodes.confidence_reason: No signal-processing topic; graph-learning placement is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Graphon signal sampling theory is rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: Vision-Language Foundation Models as Effective Robot Imitators
nodes.tldr: Adapts open-source vision-language models to robot control by light imitation-learning fine-tuning with an explicit sequential policy head for language-conditioned manipulation.
nodes.problem: Making existing vision-language models usable for robot manipulation without heavy training costs.
nodes.approach: Single-step VLM comprehension plus a history-modeling policy head, fine-tuned only on manipulation data.
nodes.niche_reason: VLM-based robot policies are a growing, fairly crowded direction.

nodes.title: Efficient ConvBN Blocks for Transfer Learning and Beyond
nodes.tldr: Introduces a Tune mode for Conv-BatchNorm blocks that matches Eval-mode stability in transfer learning while approaching Deploy-mode efficiency, cutting memory and training time.
nodes.problem: ConvBN blocks trade off training stability (Eval) against efficiency (Deploy) in transfer learning.
nodes.approach: Theoretical analysis of Deploy-mode instability and a Tune mode that fuses Conv and BN in training.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Low-level ConvBN mode engineering is a rare topic.

nodes.title: Improved Efficiency Based on Learned Saccade and Continuous Scene Reconstruction From Foveated Visual Sampling
nodes.tldr: Uses RL-learned saccades to sample a few foveal glances and reconstruct the full scene, cutting input pixels by over 90% with similar recognition accuracy.
nodes.problem: High-accuracy, low-latency, energy-efficient vision needs fewer pixels per frame without losing recognition.
nodes.approach: Foveal-peripheral glimpses stitched into a scene reconstruction, guided by an RL saccade policy.
nodes.confidence_reason: active sensing spans efficiency, RL saccade policy, and recognition
nodes.niche_reason: Biologically inspired foveated saccade sampling is a rare, unusual vision direction.

nodes.title: On Diffusion Modeling for Anomaly Detection
nodes.tldr: Studies diffusion models for tabular anomaly detection and proposes Diffusion Time Estimation, scoring anomalies by estimated diffusion time, far faster than DDPM.
nodes.problem: Using diffusion models for unsupervised and semi-supervised anomaly detection efficiently.
nodes.approach: Estimate diffusion time of an input with a network and use it as the anomaly score.
nodes.confidence_reason: Primary could be generative or anomaly detection; no anomaly topic exists.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion for anomaly detection is a moderately specialised application.

nodes.title: Bounding Box Stability against Feature Dropout Reflects Detector Generalization across Environments
nodes.tldr: Predicts a detector's test accuracy without ground truth using a bounding-box stability score under feature-map dropout, which correlates strongly with mAP.
nodes.problem: Assessing detector generalization on real-world test sets without test ground truths.
nodes.approach: Compare boxes before and after feature dropout via bipartite matching and average IoU.
nodes.confidence_reason: Venue hint (representation learning) mismatches detection-evaluation focus
nodes.niche_reason: Label-free detector evaluation is specialised but active

nodes.title: Submodular Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Introduces submodular RL for history-dependent diminishing-returns rewards, with hardness results and a greedy policy-gradient algorithm applied to coverage and informative path planning.
nodes.problem: Standard additive Markov rewards cannot model diminishing returns in coverage, experiment design, and path planning.
nodes.approach: Model rewards as submodular set functions; subPO policy gradient greedily maximizing marginal gains.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Submodular, non-additive rewards in RL are unusual.

nodes.title: Bandits Meet Mechanism Design to Combat Clickbait in Online Recommendation
nodes.tldr: Studies bandits where arms strategically choose click-rates to get clicked, and proposes UCB-S, an incentive-aware algorithm with O(sqrt(KT)) regret across equilibria.
nodes.problem: Incentive-unaware bandit algorithms fail when arms strategically inflate click-rates.
nodes.approach: Incentive-aware UCB variant (UCB-S) that makes arm behaviour desirable while learning unknown rewards.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: Bandit algorithm vs. mechanism design framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Strategic arms that game clicks are a rare bandit setting

nodes.title: Sentence-level Prompts Benefit Composed Image Retrieval
nodes.tldr: Composed image retrieval method using sentence-level prompts instead of pseudo-word tokens to capture complex reference-to-target changes.
nodes.problem: Pseudo-word prompting fails on complex edits like object removal in composed image retrieval.
nodes.approach: Generate sentence-level prompts from the reference image and fuse with relative caption.
nodes.niche_reason: Composed image retrieval is an established specialised task.

nodes.title: Fantastic Gains and Where to Find Them: On the Existence and Prospect of General Knowledge Transfer between Any Pretrained Model
nodes.tldr: Shows pretrained models learn complementary features and proposes a data-partitioning extension of knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge between arbitrary pretrained models, even weaker ones.
nodes.problem: Transferring complementary knowledge between arbitrary pretrained models without performance degradation.
nodes.approach: Data-partitioned distillation extension enabling model-agnostic transfer, including unsupervised settings.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans knowledge distillation, transfer learning, and model-zoo analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Model-agnostic transfer between pretrained models is somewhat uncommon.

nodes.title: An Analytical Solution to Gauss-Newton Loss for Direct Image Alignment
nodes.tldr: Derives a closed-form expected optimum of the Gauss-Newton loss, letting direct image alignment control its convergence basin for more robust pose initialization.
nodes.problem: Learned direct image alignment is biased toward specific motions and pose initializations.
nodes.approach: Closed-form analytical solution to the expected Gauss-Newton optimum, tuned by assumed uncertainty.
nodes.niche_reason: Closed-form analysis of direct image alignment is unusual today

nodes.title: SOTOPIA: Interactive Evaluation for Social Intelligence in Language Agents
nodes.tldr: Introduces an interactive role-play environment and evaluation framework for measuring social intelligence in LLM-based agents.
nodes.problem: AI social intelligence is hard to measure, with no open-ended way to test social goals.
nodes.approach: Simulated role-play between LLM agents and humans across scenarios, scored by the SOTOPIA-Eval framework.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Social intelligence evaluation of LLM agents is an unusual angle

nodes.title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Model for Few-Shot Meta Learning
nodes.tldr: Proposes a hierarchical Bayesian model where episode-specific variables are governed by a global variable, using Normal-Inverse-Wishart closed forms to avoid MAML's costly unrolled gradients.
nodes.problem: Few-shot meta-learning needs principled per-episode adaptation without costly MAML gradient chains.
nodes.approach: Global Normal-Inverse-Wishart prior with approximate closed-form local posteriors per episode.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Bayesian few-shot meta-learning is a common-ish direction.

nodes.title: Analyzing Feed-Forward Blocks in Transformers through the Lens of Attention Maps
nodes.tldr: Analyzes Transformer feed-forward blocks by rendering their effect in attention maps, showing they reshape input contextualization toward linguistic compositions and often cancel surrounding components.
nodes.problem: Feed-forward blocks in Transformers are understudied relative to attention for interpretability.
nodes.approach: Render feed-forward block effects as attention maps for masked and causal language models.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Transformer interpretability is active; feed-forward focus is more specialised.

nodes.title: Enabling Efficient Equivariant Operations in the Fourier Basis via Gaunt Tensor Products
nodes.tldr: Gaunt Tensor Products link Clebsch-Gordan to Gaunt coefficients and use 2D Fourier bases with FFT to cut E(3)-equivariant tensor product cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3).
nodes.problem: Tensor products of irreps in E(3)-equivariant networks become computationally expensive at high degree.
nodes.approach: Express irrep tensor products as spherical function multiplication in a 2D Fourier basis accelerated by FFT.
nodes.confidence_reason: Equivariant architecture efficiency with applications in molecular/materials modeling.
nodes.niche_reason: E(3)-equivariant tensor product acceleration is a specialised niche.

nodes.title: Views Can Be Deceiving: Improved SSL Through Feature Space Augmentation
nodes.tldr: Shows standard SSL augmentations induce invariances that leave spurious features, and proposes feature-space augmentation (LateTVG) to reduce reliance on spurious features and improve minority-group performance.
nodes.problem: Self-supervised representations rely on spurious features because image augmentations create unwanted invariances.
nodes.approach: Augment in feature space by perturbing learned representations to remove spurious-feature reliance.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: Spurious features in SSL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: OctoPack: Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: OctoPack instruction-tunes code LLMs on CommitPack, 4TB of Git commits, and introduces HumanEvalPack covering repair, explanation, and synthesis across six languages.
nodes.problem: Improving instruction-following of code LLMs without relying on proprietary model outputs.
nodes.approach: Use Git commit messages as natural instructions; build CommitPack dataset and HumanEvalPack benchmark.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Code LLM instruction tuning is a common direction.

nodes.title: Mayfly: a Neural Data Structure for Graph Stream Summarization
nodes.tldr: Mayfly is the first neural data structure for graph stream summarization, meta-trained then adapted to streams, beating handcrafted sketches on edge, node and connectivity queries.
nodes.problem: Summarizing massive dynamic graph streams with sub-linear space and accurate queries.
nodes.approach: Memory-augmented network meta-trained in larval and metamorphosis phases on synthetic and real-stream meta-tasks.
nodes.confidence_reason: Neural data-structure paper; fits meta-learning and graph topics about equally.
nodes.niche_reason: Learned replacement for streaming sketch data structures is very rare.

nodes.title: The Consensus Game: Language Model Generation via Equilibrium Search
nodes.tldr: Reconciles generative and discriminative LM scoring by training-free equilibrium search in a signaling game between generator and discriminator.
nodes.problem: Generative and discriminative LM predictions often disagree, so answers lack coherence.
nodes.approach: Regularized imperfect-information signaling game solved for approximate equilibria, giving equilibrium-ranking decoding.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.confidence_reason: decoding method sits between generation and game-theoretic equilibrium
nodes.niche_reason: game-theoretic LM decoding is a rare cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Monte Carlo guided Denoising Diffusion models for Bayesian linear inverse problems.
nodes.tldr: Uses sequential Monte Carlo over a sequence of intermediate linear inverse problems defined by a diffusion prior to sample posteriors of ill-posed Bayesian inverse problems.
nodes.problem: Sampling accurate posteriors for linear inverse problems with score-based generative priors.
nodes.approach: Define intermediate noise-level inverse problems and sample the sequence of posteriors with sequential Monte Carlo.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: SMC-based diffusion inverse problem solvers are specialised.

nodes.title: Input-gradient space particle inference for neural network ensembles
nodes.tldr: Repels ensemble members in input-gradient space, making them functionally diverse and more robust under covariate shift.
nodes.problem: Ensemble diversity is limited; weight-space and function-space repulsion both underperform.
nodes.approach: Particle variational inference with a repulsion term over first-order input gradients (FoRDE).
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Diversity-driven ensembles with particle inference are specialised

nodes.title: An Image Is Worth 1000 Lies: Transferability of Adversarial Images across Prompts on Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Proposes cross-prompt adversarial transferability for VLMs and CroPA, which updates image perturbations against learnable adversarial-countering prompts so one image fools many prompts.
nodes.problem: Whether a single adversarial image can mislead VLM predictions across many different prompts.
nodes.approach: Optimize visual perturbation jointly with learnable textual prompts that counteract the attack.
nodes.niche_reason: Established VLM adversarial attack area with new angle.

nodes.title: PF-LRM: Pose-Free Large Reconstruction Model for Joint Pose and Shape Prediction
nodes.tldr: PF-LRM reconstructs a 3D object from a few unposed images and estimates camera poses in about 1.3 seconds via a transformer and differentiable PnP.
nodes.problem: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction from unposed sparse views requires jointly estimating camera poses.
nodes.approach: Transformer predicts per-view coarse point clouds; a differentiable PnP solver recovers camera poses.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Large feed-forward reconstruction models are a crowded direction.

nodes.title: Pre-Training Goal-based Models for Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Pre-trains a goal-conditioned low-level policy and clusters dataset goals into a discrete high-level action space, with a goal prior regularizing RL for sample efficiency.
nodes.problem: RL is sample-inefficient on complex tasks, and goal spaces are high-dimensional.
nodes.approach: Pre-trained goal-conditioned skills, clustered goal space for the high-level policy, and a goal prior regularizer.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.niche_reason: goal-conditioned hierarchical RL is a common direction

nodes.title: Information Retention via Learning Supplemental Features
nodes.tldr: Keeps supplemental relevant features alongside a mainline representation, via a three-stage supervised framework, to improve out-of-domain generalization in low-resource settings.
nodes.problem: Information bottleneck compression can discard features useful under distribution shift in low-resource settings.
nodes.approach: Three-stage supervised learning that jointly learns mainline and supplemental features without suppression.
nodes.confidence_reason: Representation learning vs information theory is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Retention-over-compression view is a specialised contrarian angle

nodes.title: Adversarial AutoMixup
nodes.tldr: AdAutomixup trains an adversarial mixup sample generator against the classifier to produce hard, diverse mixed images that improve image classification generalization.
nodes.problem: Automatic mixup generates consistent rather than diverse samples, causing overfitting.
nodes.approach: Alternately optimize a mixed-sample generator and classifier adversarially, with EMA teacher and cosine similarity.
nodes.confidence_reason: Augmentation method; closest topic is image classification but could be training/generalization.
nodes.niche_reason: Mixup variants are a crowded augmentation area.

nodes.title: Graph Neural Networks for Learning Equivariant Representations of Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Represents neural networks as parameter computational graphs processed by permutation-equivariant graph neural networks and transformers, applied to diverse architectures.
nodes.problem: Neural networks processing other networks ignore permutation symmetry or architecture details.
nodes.approach: Neural computational graphs of parameters encoded by GNNs and transformers.
nodes.confidence_reason: Weight-space learning topic fit is ambiguous.
nodes.niche_reason: Networks-as-graphs for weight-space learning is unusual.

nodes.title: ExeDec: Execution Decomposition for Compositional Generalization in Neural Program Synthesis
nodes.tldr: Decomposes neural program synthesis into step-by-step execution subgoals and introduces a meta-benchmark for compositional generalization, improving Transformers and LLM prompting.
nodes.problem: Neural program synthesis models often fail to compositionally generalize to complex unseen tasks.
nodes.approach: Predicts execution subgoals at each step, conditioned on program execution results.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: Compositional generalization in program synthesis is specialised

nodes.title: ReLU Strikes Back: Exploiting Activation Sparsity in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Argues for ReLU over GELU/SiLU in LLMs: it barely hurts quality, cuts inference compute and weight transfer, and reuses activated neurons across tokens.
nodes.problem: LLM inference is memory-bound and expensive, hindering deployment on constrained devices.
nodes.approach: ReLU activations with sparsity exploitation via reuse of activated neurons during decoding.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: ReLU sparsity for LLM inference is specialised but active

nodes.title: Prototypical Information Bottlenecking and Disentangling for Multimodal Cancer Survival Prediction
nodes.tldr: Predicts cancer survival from pathology slides and genomics by using prototypical information bottlenecks to filter redundant patches and disentangle shared versus modality-specific features.
nodes.problem: Multimodal survival prediction suffers from intra-modal and inter-modal redundancy in pathology and genomics.
nodes.approach: Prototypical information bottleneck selects discriminative instances; disentanglement splits common and specific knowledge.
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Pathology-genomics survival modelling is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Soft Contrastive Learning for Time Series
nodes.tldr: Replaces hard positive and negative pairs in time-series contrastive learning with soft assignments based on data-space distance and timestamp differences.
nodes.problem: Contrastive time-series learning ignores inherent correlations between similar instances and adjacent timestamps.
nodes.approach: Instance-wise and temporal contrastive losses with soft assignments ranging from zero to one.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Contrastive time-series learning is a common direction

nodes.title: Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning via Bounded Rationality Curricula
nodes.tldr: Trains robust adversarial RL with a curriculum over the adversary's bounded rationality, avoiding hard Nash saddle-point computation via entropy regularization.
nodes.problem: Robust adversarial RL needs Nash equilibria, which are hard to compute in high-dimensional control.
nodes.approach: Entropy-regularized adversary with annealed rationality curriculum for protagonist-adversary training.
nodes.niche_reason: Robust adversarial RL with bounded rationality is specialised.

nodes.title: Robust agents learn causal world models
nodes.tldr: Proves that any agent satisfying a regret bound across many distributional shifts must have learned an approximate causal model of the data-generating process.
nodes.problem: Whether robust, generalizing agents must learn causal models of their environment.
nodes.approach: Formal theorem linking regret bounds under distribution shifts to approximate causal model identification.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Theory connecting agent robustness to causal models is rare.

nodes.title: Kernel Metric Learning for In-Sample Off-Policy Evaluation of Deterministic RL Policies
nodes.tldr: Relaxes deterministic target policies with a kernel and learns the kernel metric to make in-sample off-policy evaluation work in continuous actions.
nodes.problem: Importance sampling OPE has high variance, and in-sample methods fail for deterministic continuous policies.
nodes.approach: Learns a kernel metric minimizing the TD update error of an in-sample importance-resampling estimator.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: OPE for deterministic continuous policies is a specialised sub-area

nodes.title: Jailbreak in pieces: Compositional Adversarial Attacks on Multi-Modal Language Models
nodes.tldr: Cross-modality jailbreaks pair adversarial images, crafted in embedding space to mimic toxic content, with benign text prompts to break alignment of vision-language models.
nodes.problem: Vision-language models built on aligned LLMs remain vulnerable to compositional cross-modal jailbreaks.
nodes.approach: Embedding-space adversarial image generation needing only vision encoder access, composed with generic text prompts.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Jailbreak attacks are common though multimodal angle is newer.

nodes.title: ODE Discovery for Longitudinal Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Inference
nodes.tldr: Learns closed-form ODEs instead of neural networks for longitudinal heterogeneous treatment effects, a framework turning any ODE discovery method into a treatment-effect method.
nodes.problem: Longitudinal treatment effect inference relies solely on neural networks, lacking interpretability and irregular-sampling handling.
nodes.approach: Frame treatment effects estimation as ODE discovery with a framework wrapping any ODE discovery method.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
secondary_topics: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
nodes.niche_reason: Replacing neural nets with discovered ODEs for treatment effects is unusual.

nodes.title: How I Warped Your Noise: a Temporally-Correlated Noise Prior for Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Introduces integral noise, a temporally correlated noise representation with a transport method to advect noise across frames, reducing flicker in video diffusion editing and generation.
nodes.problem: Independent per-frame noise in diffusion causes flickering and texture sticking in video tasks.
nodes.approach: Continuous integrated noise field with noise transport that preserves noise statistics while maximizing frame correlation.
nodes.niche_reason: Noise-prior design for temporal coherence is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Masks, Signs, And Learning Rate Rewinding
nodes.tldr: Studies why learning rate rewinding beats iterative magnitude pruning, showing its ability to flip parameter signs aids mask learning, with proof in a single-neuron setting.
nodes.problem: Understanding why learning rate rewinding excels at finding and training sparse lottery-ticket masks.
nodes.approach: Experiments disentangling mask and parameter learning plus theory on sign flipping for one hidden neuron.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Pruning dynamics analysis is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Relay Diffusion: Unifying diffusion process across resolutions for image synthesis
nodes.tldr: Relay Diffusion transfers low-resolution images or noise to high resolution so diffusion continues across resolutions without restarting from pure noise.
nodes.problem: High-resolution diffusion synthesis suffers from mismatched SNR across resolutions.
nodes.approach: Blurring diffusion with block noise relays the process to a higher resolution.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion image synthesis is a crowded mainstream topic

nodes.title: Fast Imitation via Behavior Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: Uses RL foundation models based on successor measures to imitate expert behavior from a few demonstrations within seconds, with no RL training or fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Imitation methods need many demonstrations and a new RL run for every imitation task.
nodes.approach: Successor-measure foundation model yields imitation policies from demonstrations via behavioral cloning, feature matching, or goal reductions.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
nodes.confidence_reason: Imitation task versus RL foundation-model method; topic falls between two areas.
nodes.niche_reason: Successor-measure foundation models for imitation are a niche direction

nodes.title: Grounding Language Plans in Demonstrations Through Counterfactual Perturbations
nodes.tldr: Uses LLMs and counterfactual perturbed demonstrations to learn mode-family groundings, turning language plans into interpretable reactive robot policies.
nodes.problem: Grounding LLM common-sense plans in physical task structure and constraints from demonstrations.
nodes.approach: Replay perturbed demos for counterfactual successes and failures; learn differentiable mode classifiers.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Mode-family grounding combining LLMs and manipulation planning is rare.

nodes.title: Catastrophic Jailbreak of Open-source LLMs via Exploiting Generation
nodes.tldr: Shows alignment of open-source LLMs breaks by only varying decoding hyperparameters and sampling, raising jailbreak success from 0% to over 95%, and proposes a mitigation.
nodes.problem: Safety alignment of open-source LLMs is evaluated only under default decoding.
nodes.approach: Generation exploitation attack varying decoding strategies, plus alignment training with diverse generation strategies.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Jailbreak attacks are a crowded area.

nodes.title: Nearly $d$-Linear Convergence Bounds for Diffusion Models via Stochastic Localization
nodes.tldr: Convergence bounds for denoising diffusion models that are linear in data dimension, assuming only finite second moments of the data distribution.
nodes.problem: Prior diffusion convergence bounds were superlinear in dimension or required strong smoothness assumptions.
nodes.approach: Girsanov-based analysis plus a stochastic-localization-inspired treatment of reverse SDE discretization error.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion convergence theory is an active but crowded theory area

nodes.title: Image Inpainting via Iteratively Decoupled Probabilistic Modeling
nodes.tldr: Inpaints images by iteratively spreading informative pixels with decoupled probabilistic modeling, combining GAN-like efficiency with probabilistic prediction at low cost.
nodes.problem: GAN inpainting struggles with large holes, while diffusion and autoregressive inpainting are costly.
nodes.approach: Iterative pixel spread model that selectively propagates informative pixels in a few decoupled probabilistic steps.
nodes.niche_reason: Hybrid GAN-probabilistic inpainting is an established but specialised niche

nodes.title: On the Provable Advantage of Unsupervised Pretraining
nodes.tldr: Proves that unsupervised pretraining via MLE on latent-variable models reduces downstream excess risk when unlabeled data is plentiful, covering factor models and contrastive learning.
nodes.problem: Why unsupervised pretraining helps downstream tasks lacks rigorous general theory.
nodes.approach: MLE pretraining on an abstract latent-variable class and ERM for downstream tasks, with complexity-based excess risk bounds.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: General theory of pretraining benefit is specialised but established

nodes.title: Intriguing Properties of Generative Classifiers
nodes.tldr: Shows zero-shot text-to-image diffusion classifiers exhibit strong human-like shape bias, out-of-distribution accuracy, and error patterns that match human recognition.
nodes.problem: Whether discriminative or generative inference better models human object recognition.
nodes.approach: Turns text-to-image diffusion models into zero-shot classifiers and compares them with humans and discriminative models.
nodes.confidence_reason: Studies diffusion classifiers' behavior, overlapping classification and generative topics.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion classifiers compared with human psychophysics is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Variational Inference for SDEs Driven by Fractional Noise
nodes.tldr: Variational inference framework for neural SDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion, learning the Hurst index and drift/diffusion via ELBO.
nodes.problem: Brownian-driven SDEs miss long-term dependencies; fBM inference is costly or statistically inefficient.
nodes.approach: Markov approximation of fBM, closed-form approximation coefficients, and neural-network variational posterior trained by ELBO.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment call between probabilistic inference and time-series modeling.
nodes.niche_reason: Unusual combination of fractional noise SDEs with variational video prediction.

nodes.title: SILO Language Models: Isolating Legal Risk In a Nonparametric Datastore
nodes.tldr: Trains an LM on permissively licensed text and adds a swappable nonparametric datastore at inference, so high-risk data is never trained on.
nodes.problem: Training on copyrighted text raises legal risk, but low-risk-only data hurts performance.
nodes.approach: Parametric LM on an open license corpus plus inference-time retrieval from a removable datastore.
nodes.niche_reason: Legally motivated datastore LMs are a specialised niche

nodes.title: Learning to Act without Actions
nodes.tldr: LAPO recovers latent action spaces, latent-action policies and world models from action-free videos, enabling pretraining that fine-tunes quickly into expert policies.
nodes.problem: Web videos lack action labels needed for imitation, blocking large-scale pre-training for RL.
nodes.approach: Learn inverse and forward dynamics models with latent action bottleneck from observed transitions, then fine-tune policy.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Latent action learning from video is emerging but specialised.

nodes.title: Selective Mixup Fine-Tuning for Optimizing Non-Decomposable Objectives
nodes.tldr: Fine-tunes pre-trained models with a selective mixup sampling distribution to optimize non-decomposable objectives like worst-case recall or fairness.
nodes.problem: Current methods handle non-decomposable objectives poorly, and theoretical fixes need training from scratch.
nodes.approach: Mixup features between classes using a sampling distribution chosen to optimize the given objective.
nodes.confidence_reason: Spans fine-tuning, long-tail imbalance, and fairness objectives.
nodes.niche_reason: Optimizing non-decomposable objectives via mixup fine-tuning is specialised.

nodes.title: CAMIL: Context-Aware Multiple Instance Learning for Cancer Detection and Subtyping in Whole Slide Images
nodes.tldr: CAMIL adds neighbor-constrained attention and contextual priors to multiple instance learning for whole slide images, improving cancer subtyping and metastasis detection.
nodes.problem: Attention-based MIL ignores contextual dependencies among neighboring tiles in whole slide images, causing misclassification.
nodes.approach: Neighbor-constrained attention with contextual constraints as priors in a multiple instance learning architecture.
nodes.niche_reason: Computational pathology MIL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: SocioDojo: Building Lifelong Analytical Agents with Real-world Text and Time Series
nodes.tldr: SocioDojo is a lifelong learning environment with news, knowledge bases, and 30K time series for a hyperportfolio task evaluating LLM agents' societal analysis, plus an Analyst-Assistant-Actuator agent.
nodes.problem: Evaluating autonomous agents on human-like societal analysis and decision-making lacks scalable benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Open-ended environment with time-series hyperportfolio task and Analyst-Assistant-Actuator agent with Hypothesis and Proof prompting.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Environment, benchmark, and agent method combined; topic judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Societal analysis agents evaluated via time-series portfolios are unusual.

nodes.title: Learning Interactive Real-World Simulators
nodes.tldr: Trains a universal generative video simulator of real-world interaction from diverse datasets, enabling zero-shot real-world transfer of planners and RL policies trained inside it.
nodes.problem: Learning a realistic simulator of visual outcomes for human, robot and agent actions.
nodes.approach: Generative video model orchestrated over complementary datasets, conditioned on high-level text and low-level controls.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Video world models are an active, crowded research direction.

nodes.title: NuwaDynamics: Discovering and Updating in Causal Spatio-Temporal Modeling
nodes.tldr: NuwaDynamics identifies causal spatial patches via self-supervision and applies interventions, improving spatio-temporal prediction under data imbalance.
nodes.problem: Sparse, imbalanced spatio-temporal data makes models overfit and generalize poorly.
nodes.approach: Two-stage causal discovery with self-supervised patch interventions, then downstream targeted fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.confidence_reason: Causal and earth-science spatio-temporal topics overlap
nodes.niche_reason: Causal intervention for spatio-temporal forecasting is specialised

nodes.title: Towards Meta-Pruning via Optimal Transport
nodes.tldr: Intra-Fusion merges neurons via optimal transport after structural pruning, recovering accuracy without fine-tuning and cutting pruning training time.
nodes.problem: Discarding neurons during structural pruning causes large accuracy loss that needs costly fine-tuning.
nodes.approach: Model fusion with optimal transport aligns and merges neurons given any importance metric.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Pruning and compression is a crowded mainstream area.

nodes.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines
nodes.tldr: DSPy is a programming model and compiler that turns declarative LM modules into pipelines, automatically optimizing prompts and demonstrations to maximize a metric.
nodes.problem: LM pipelines rely on hand-written prompt templates found by trial and error.
nodes.approach: Declarative parameterized modules in text transformation graphs, with a compiler bootstrapping demonstrations to optimize metrics.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
nodes.niche_reason: Programming-model view of prompting is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
nodes.tldr: Shows LLMs favor certain option IDs in multiple-choice questions, and proposes PriDe, a label-free inference-time method that removes this prior bias.
nodes.problem: LLMs' answers to multiple-choice questions shift when option positions change, due to selection bias.
nodes.approach: Estimate the prior over option-ID tokens by permuting option contents, then remove it from predictions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.confidence_reason: evaluation versus fairness/bias framing is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: LLM evaluation bias is a common, active research theme

nodes.title: LRM: Large Reconstruction Model for Single Image to 3D
nodes.tldr: Feed-forward 500M-parameter transformer that predicts a NeRF from one image in about five seconds, trained on a million multi-view objects.
nodes.problem: Single-image 3D reconstruction methods are category-specific and trained on small datasets.
nodes.approach: Scalable transformer regressing NeRF from image tokens, trained end-to-end on Objaverse and MVImgNet.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Feed-forward single-image 3D is a crowded direction.

nodes.title: Whole-Song Hierarchical Generation of Symbolic Music Using Cascaded Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Generates whole pop songs symbolically with a cascaded diffusion model over a hierarchical musical language from form and phrase down to notes.
nodes.problem: Existing music generation lacks high-quality, well-structured whole-song output.
nodes.approach: Cascaded diffusion over a hierarchical symbolic language, each level conditioned on upper levels.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Audio, Speech & Music Generation
nodes.niche_reason: Symbolic whole-song music generation is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Likelihood Training of Cascaded Diffusion Models via Hierarchical Volume-preserving Maps
nodes.tldr: Makes multi-scale cascaded diffusion a strong likelihood model by diffusing in Laplacian-pyramid or wavelet latent spaces.
nodes.problem: Cascaded multi-scale models have intractable likelihoods because intermediate scales add extraneous variables.
nodes.approach: Hierarchical volume-preserving maps (Laplacian pyramid, wavelets) make the likelihood a joint over scales.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.confidence_reason: Diffusion method versus likelihood-evaluation theory is close
nodes.niche_reason: Likelihood-tractable cascaded diffusion is a specialised variant

nodes.title: BatteryML: An Open-source Platform for Machine Learning on Battery Degradation
nodes.tldr: Open-source platform unifying battery data preprocessing, feature extraction, and traditional and state-of-the-art degradation models for ML.
nodes.problem: Battery degradation ML lacks shared data formats, standards, and benchmarks, and is hard for both sides to adopt.
nodes.approach: Unified software pipeline with standardized data format and benchmark-ready model implementations.
nodes.confidence_reason: No battery or energy topic in vocab; placed under materials and physics
nodes.niche_reason: Battery degradation ML is a rare application niche

nodes.title: Frozen Transformers in Language Models Are Effective Visual Encoder Layers
nodes.tldr: Frozen pretrained LLM transformer blocks used as visual encoder layers improve many vision tasks without any language input.
nodes.problem: Whether text-only LLMs can help purely visual tasks is unclear.
nodes.approach: Insert frozen LLM blocks into vision encoders, testing on 2D, 3D, video, and multimodal tasks.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.confidence_reason: Transformer reuse vs vision foundation models is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Text-only LLM blocks as visual encoders is an unusual cross-modal angle

nodes.title: Generalization of Scaled Deep ResNets in the Mean-Field Regime
nodes.tldr: Proves generalization bounds for infinitely deep and wide scaled ResNets in the mean-field regime beyond lazy training, using time-varying Gram matrix and Rademacher complexity.
nodes.problem: Generalization of deep ResNets beyond the lazy training regime is unexplored.
nodes.approach: Mean-field PDE analysis, Gram matrix eigenvalue bounds, KL control, uniform convergence via Rademacher complexity.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised but established deep learning theory.

nodes.title: Towards Robust Out-of-Distribution Generalization Bounds via Sharpness
nodes.tldr: Proves a connection between sharpness and robustness to derive tighter out-of-distribution generalization bounds, supporting the flat-minima-help-OOD hypothesis.
nodes.problem: OOD generalization bounds ignore the optimization property of the learned minimum, such as sharpness.
nodes.approach: Theoretically link sharpness to algorithmic robustness and derive a sharpness-based OOD bound.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Established theory topic with specialised sharpness-robustness angle.

nodes.title: Text2Reward: Reward Shaping with Language Models for Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Uses LLMs to write executable dense reward code from a natural-language goal, grounded in environment summaries, matching expert rewards on many robot tasks.
nodes.problem: Designing dense reward functions for RL requires specialised knowledge and is costly.
nodes.approach: LLM generates shaped reward programs from a compact environment representation, refined with human feedback.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-written dense reward code is an emerging but fairly common direction.

nodes.title: Generative Modeling with Phase Stochastic Bridge
nodes.tldr: Generative model that builds a stochastic path in an augmented position-velocity phase space, producing realistic samples earlier, which helps few-step generation.
nodes.problem: Diffusion models need many function evaluations, and sample quality emerges only late in sampling.
nodes.approach: Stochastic optimal control defines a phase-space path measure that uses velocity information for sampling.
nodes.confidence_reason: New framework sitting between diffusion and sampling topics
nodes.niche_reason: Phase-space generative framing is unusual

nodes.title: Provable Offline Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: Gives a provable offline preference-based RL algorithm, with polynomial sample guarantees under general function approximation whenever the target policy is covered by data.
nodes.problem: Learning from trajectory preferences offline, without explicit rewards, lacks guarantees under general function approximation.
nodes.approach: MLE reward estimate, then distributionally robust planning over a confidence set; single-policy concentrability.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Offline preference RL theory with general function approximation is specialised.

nodes.title: Learning to Reject Meets Long-tail Learning
nodes.tldr: Shows standard learning-to-reject is suboptimal for balanced or worst-group error, derives the Bayes-optimal classifier and rejector, and proposes a plug-in method.
nodes.problem: Learning to reject methods target standard error and fail under label imbalance metrics.
nodes.approach: Derive Bayes-optimal classifier and rejector for balanced error, then a plug-in approximation extended to general metrics.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Selective classification under imbalance is specialised.

nodes.title: A Benchmark for Learning to Translate a New Language from One Grammar Book
nodes.tldr: MTOB benchmarks translating English and Kalamang from one grammar book, testing whether LLMs can learn a genuinely unseen language from reference text.
nodes.problem: Evaluating LLM adaptation to truly unseen tasks and low-resource languages absent from web data.
nodes.approach: Benchmark with grammar book, wordlist and parallel examples for Kalamang translation, with LLM baselines and human comparison.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: Learning an endangered language from one book is unusual.

nodes.title: Social Reward: Evaluating and Enhancing Generative AI through Million-User Feedback from an Online Creative Community
nodes.tldr: Learns a reward model from implicit million-user feedback on a creative platform to score text-to-image outputs by community appreciation and fine-tune generators.
nodes.problem: Existing text-to-image metrics miss community creative preference; small user studies poorly reflect social appreciation.
nodes.approach: Predictive reward model trained on implicit social-network feedback from editing generated images, then used for fine-tuning.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Social-popularity reward from creative community feedback is unusual.

nodes.title: Maximum Entropy Heterogeneous-Agent Reinforcement Learning
nodes.tldr: HASAC is a maximum-entropy soft actor-critic for heterogeneous cooperative multi-agent RL, with monotonic improvement and convergence to quantal response equilibrium proofs.
nodes.problem: Cooperative MARL suffers sample inefficiency, training instability and convergence to suboptimal Nash equilibria.
nodes.approach: Maximum-entropy objective from probabilistic graphical models, plus a unified mirror-learning template for MaxEnt algorithms.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Maximum-entropy cooperative MARL is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Quick-Tune: Quickly Learning Which Pretrained Model to Finetune and How
nodes.tldr: Meta-learns a gray-box performance predictor from learning curves over many pretrained models and datasets to jointly choose a model and its hyperparameters.
nodes.problem: Practitioners must pick which pretrained model to finetune and with which hyperparameters for a new dataset.
nodes.approach: Gray-box learning-curve predictor meta-trained on a large meta-dataset of 20k finetuning runs; used for fast HPO.
nodes.confidence_reason: AutoML versus transfer-learning placement is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Model-selection and HPO are established AutoML topics.

nodes.title: SWAP-NAS: Sample-Wise Activation Patterns for Ultra-fast NAS
nodes.tldr: Proposes SWAP-Score, a training-free metric from sample-wise activation patterns that correlates strongly with network accuracy, enabling NAS in minutes of GPU time.
nodes.problem: Zero-cost NAS proxies have limited correlation and generalise poorly across search spaces.
nodes.approach: Measure network expressivity via activation patterns over a batch, regularise it, and plug into evolutionary search.
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised zero-cost NAS subfield.

nodes.title: ScaleCrafter: Tuning-free Higher-Resolution Visual Generation with Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Generates ultra-high-resolution images from a low-resolution pretrained diffusion model without tuning, by dynamically re-dilating convolutions during inference.
nodes.problem: Pretrained diffusion models at higher resolution repeat objects and produce unreasonable structures.
nodes.approach: Re-dilation adjusting U-Net conv perception fields at inference, plus dispersed convolution and noise-damped guidance.
nodes.niche_reason: Tuning-free high-resolution diffusion is an active, common topic.

nodes.title: Entity-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Object Manipulation from Pixels
nodes.tldr: Proposes an entity-centric visual RL architecture for goal-conditioned multi-object manipulation from pixels that generalizes from 3 to over 10 objects.
nodes.problem: Visual RL struggles with many objects and goal dependencies due to dimensionality.
nodes.approach: Object-centric structured architecture representing entities and interactions, with a compositional generalization argument.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Object-centric RL for manipulation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Enhanced Face Recognition using Intra-class Incoherence Constraint
nodes.tldr: Improves face recognition by recombining orthogonal feature components from two models, and by an intra-class incoherence constraint when only one model exists.
nodes.problem: Face recognition accuracy is near saturation, and feature representation space has received little attention.
nodes.approach: Orthogonal decomposition of superior-model features against inferior-model features, rescaled and summed; IIC distillation.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.confidence_reason: Feature-space method on face recognition; topic choice is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: Face recognition gains are a mature, crowded area.

nodes.title: Model Tells You What to Discard: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for LLMs
nodes.tldr: Cuts LLM KV cache memory without fine-tuning by profiling attention heads and keeping only the cache each head needs.
nodes.problem: Generative inference with LLMs stores key-value vectors for all context tokens, using too much GPU memory.
nodes.approach: Lightweight attention profiling chooses per-head eviction policies: local, special-token, or full cache.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: KV cache compression is a crowded area

nodes.title: Unbiased Watermark for Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Proposes unbiased LLM watermarks that preserve the output distribution while remaining detectable, removing the assumed quality-vs-strength trade-off.
nodes.problem: Watermarking LLM outputs without degrading generation quality.
nodes.approach: Distribution-preserving reweighting watermark with a detection test and theory.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM watermarking is active but specialised.

nodes.title: GROOT: Learning to Follow Instructions by Watching Gameplay Videos
nodes.tldr: Instruction-following agent for open-world Minecraft that takes reference gameplay videos as goals, learned from videos without text annotations.
nodes.problem: Open-ended instruction following needs goal specs without costly text-gameplay annotations.
nodes.approach: Video instruction encoder and causal-transformer encoder-decoder policy with structured goal space.
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Embodied Multimodal Agents
nodes.confidence_reason: Minecraft agent; embodied multimodal vs imitation framing.
nodes.niche_reason: Video-goal Minecraft agents are a specialised niche.

nodes.title: How to Capture Higher-order Correlations? Generalizing Matrix Softmax Attention to Kronecker Computation
nodes.tldr: Generalizes attention to triple-wise token correlations via Kronecker products; shows near-linear algorithms exist for bounded entries but n^3 lower bounds otherwise.
nodes.problem: Attention captures only pairwise token interactions; higher-order correlations are missed and naively costly.
nodes.approach: Kronecker-product tensor attention analyzed with polynomial-method and fine-grained complexity tools.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Higher-order tensor attention with complexity bounds is rare.

nodes.title: Statistically Optimal $K$-means Clustering via Nonnegative Low-rank Semidefinite Programming
nodes.tldr: Solves a nonnegative low-rank restriction of the SDP-relaxed K-means via Burer-Monteiro factorization, keeping NMF-like scalability with SDP-level statistical optimality.
nodes.problem: SDP K-means has strong guarantees but is too costly; NMF is scalable but lacks guarantees.
nodes.approach: Nonconvex Burer-Monteiro nonnegative low-rank SDP solver achieving statistically optimal mis-clustering rates.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
nodes.niche_reason: SDP-based clustering with low-rank factorization is a rare niche.

nodes.title: How Many Pretraining Tasks Are Needed for In-Context Learning of Linear Regression?
nodes.tldr: Proves that pretraining a one-layer linear attention model for in-context linear regression needs only few tasks, and that it approaches Bayes-optimal ridge regression.
nodes.problem: How many pretraining tasks are needed for transformers to learn in-context linear regression.
nodes.approach: Statistical task-complexity bound for single-layer linear attention under Gaussian prior, with near Bayes-optimal risk proof.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › In-context Learning & Prompting
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of ICL on linear regression is a known specialised thread.

nodes.title: From Bricks to Bridges: Product of Invariances to Enhance Latent Space Communication
nodes.tldr: Builds a product space of invariant components on top of latent representations, improving zero-shot stitching across vision, text and graph models.
nodes.problem: Estimating the right transformation between independently trained latent spaces is hard
nodes.approach: Product space of invariant components added to latent representations without prior invariance knowledge
nodes.confidence_reason: Representation vs transfer learning is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Latent communication via invariance products is uncommon

nodes.title: ModernTCN: A Modern Pure Convolution Structure for General Time Series Analysis
nodes.tldr: Pure convolution architecture that modernizes TCN for time series, achieving state-of-the-art on five tasks with larger effective receptive fields.
nodes.problem: Convolution has fallen behind Transformer and MLP models for time series analysis.
nodes.approach: Modernized temporal convolution with time-series-specific modifications that enlarge effective receptive fields.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Modernized convolutional time-series models are a common response to Transformers

nodes.title: Towards LLM4QPE: Unsupervised Pretraining of Quantum Property Estimation and A Benchmark
nodes.tldr: Proposes LLM4QPE, an LLM-style pretrain-then-finetune paradigm for quantum property estimation that learns from unlabeled quantum data and needs little labeled data.
nodes.problem: Quantum property estimation models are task-specific; no universal pretrained model exists for quantum systems.
nodes.approach: Unsupervised pretraining across diverse quantum systems, then supervised finetuning on downstream tasks.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.confidence_reason: LLM-style pretraining applied to physics; topic is a judgment call
nodes.niche_reason: Foundation-style pretraining for quantum many-body data is rare

nodes.title: Batched Low-Rank Adaptation of Foundation Models
nodes.tldr: FLoRA lets each example in a minibatch use its own low-rank adapter weights, enabling efficient batched serving of heterogeneous task-specific LoRA requests.
nodes.problem: Serving many task-specific LoRA adapters efficiently in real-time for personalized requests.
nodes.approach: Per-example low-rank adapter weights batched within a minibatch.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-LoRA serving is a common efficiency topic

nodes.title: Linearity of Relation Decoding in Transformer Language Models
nodes.tldr: For many relations, a transformer LM computes relations as a single linear transformation of the subject representation, though some relations are not linearly encoded.
nodes.problem: How transformer language models internally represent and decode relational knowledge is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: First-order approximation of the LM from a single prompt yields linear relation operators, tested across relation types.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Established interpretability subfield with a specific linearity angle.

nodes.title: BarLeRIa: An Efficient Tuning Framework for Referring Image Segmentation
nodes.tldr: Parameter-efficient tuning framework that adds bidirectional vision-language adapters to frozen models for referring image segmentation.
nodes.problem: Existing PET methods ignore dense prediction and vision-language interaction
nodes.approach: Bidirectional intertwined vision-language adapters with global and local attention tuning modules
nodes.niche_reason: PEFT for segmentation is established with a vision-language twist

nodes.title: Learning No-Regret Sparse Generalized Linear Models with Varying Observation(s)
nodes.tldr: First exact online algorithm for sparse generalized linear models handling simultaneous addition and deletion of observations, via bilevel gradient flow with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Efficiently updating sparse GLMs as observations are added or removed, instead of retraining from scratch.
nodes.approach: Recast as bilevel optimization with explicit gradient flow and transition rules at non-smooth points.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Online Learning & Regret
nodes.niche_reason: Data-varying sparse GLM path algorithms are rare.

nodes.title: Uni3D: Exploring Unified 3D Representation at Scale
nodes.tldr: Scales a 2D-initialized ViT to one billion parameters, aligning 3D point cloud features with image-text embeddings to set records on zero-shot 3D tasks.
nodes.problem: 3D representations lack the scale and pretrained ecosystem that 2D vision enjoys.
nodes.approach: Align point cloud ViT features to image-text aligned targets, initialized from a 2D pretrained ViT.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Scaled 3D foundation models are specialised relative to 2D

nodes.title: Unleashing the Potential of Fractional Calculus in Graph Neural Networks with FROND
nodes.tldr: Replaces integer-order differential equations in continuous GNNs with Caputo fractional derivatives, capturing long-range dependencies and mitigating oversmoothing.
nodes.problem: Continuous GNNs use Markovian integer-order dynamics that struggle with long-term dependencies and oversmoothing.
nodes.approach: Fractional-order graph dynamical network using the Caputo derivative, applied to existing integer-order continuous GNNs.
nodes.niche_reason: Fractional-order continuous GNNs are a rare, unusual dynamical-systems angle.

nodes.title: $\texttt{NAISR}$: A 3D Neural Additive Model for Interpretable Shape Representation
nodes.tldr: NAISR models 3D shape populations by deforming an atlas with a neural additive model over disentangled covariates, enabling interpretable shape evolution, transfer and patient-specific prediction.
nodes.problem: No shape representation captures individual dependencies on covariates for scientific shape discovery.
nodes.approach: Deep implicit atlas deformed by additive covariate-specific effects.
nodes.niche_reason: Covariate-aware interpretable implicit shape atlases are rare.

nodes.title: Compositional Generative Inverse Design
nodes.tldr: Optimizes designs over energy functions of composed diffusion models, avoiding adversarial modes and enabling inverse design of more complex systems like multi-airfoil layouts than seen in training.
nodes.problem: Inverse design via learned dynamics models falls into adversarial modes and cannot generalize to larger systems.
nodes.approach: Optimize over a diffusion-learned energy and compose multiple diffusion models of subcomponents at test time.
nodes.niche_reason: Compositional diffusion for engineering inverse design is uncommon.

nodes.title: Benchmarking Algorithms for Federated Domain Generalization
nodes.tldr: Federated domain generalization benchmark with a partitioning method that controls client heterogeneity; 14 methods tested show large remaining gaps.
nodes.problem: Existing federated DG evaluations are limited in client scale and dataset diversity.
nodes.approach: Data partition method distributing any domain dataset across few or many clients with tunable heterogeneity.
nodes.niche_reason: Federated domain generalization is a smaller, specialised subfield

nodes.title: Synaptic Weight Distributions Depend on the Geometry of Plasticity
nodes.tldr: Shows synaptic weight distributions depend on plasticity geometry, and log-normal weights fit non-Euclidean mirror descent better than gradient descent.
nodes.problem: Computational neuroscience models of synaptic plasticity assume Euclidean geometry without justification.
nodes.approach: Use mirror descent theory to derive weight distributions under different update geometries and compare with data.
nodes.niche_reason: Very few papers link mirror descent geometry to synaptic weights

nodes.title: How Over-Parameterization Slows Down Gradient Descent in Matrix Sensing: The Curses of Symmetry and Initialization
nodes.tldr: Proves over-parameterization slows gradient descent in matrix sensing to sublinear rates, shows asymmetric parameterization restores linear convergence, and proposes a one-step modification removing initialization dependence.
nodes.problem: How over-parameterization and initialization affect gradient descent convergence in low-rank matrix sensing.
nodes.approach: Rigorous convergence analysis with lower bounds, asymmetric parameterization, and a modified GD step.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Non-convex matrix recovery theory is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Subtractive Mixture Models via Squaring: Representation and Learning
nodes.tldr: Learns subtractive mixture models by squaring probabilistic circuits, proving squared circuits can be exponentially more expressive than additive mixtures.
nodes.problem: Learning mixtures that subtract density while remaining non-negative, to model distributions with fewer components.
nodes.approach: Square tensorized probabilistic circuits to guarantee non-negativity, with expressiveness proofs and density estimation experiments.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Probabilistic circuits with squared subtractive mixtures are very rare.

nodes.title: Constrained Bi-Level Optimization: Proximal Lagrangian Value Function Approach and Hessian-free Algorithm
nodes.tldr: Introduces a smooth proximal Lagrangian value function enabling a single-loop, Hessian-free algorithm for constrained bi-level optimization with coupled lower-level constraints, with convergence guarantees.
nodes.problem: Constrained bilevel optimization with coupled lower-level constraints needs costly Hessian computations.
nodes.approach: Smooth proximal Lagrangian value function yielding a single-loop Hessian-free first-order algorithm.
nodes.niche_reason: Bilevel optimization theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Impact of Computation in Integral Reinforcement Learning for Continuous-Time Control
nodes.tldr: Shows that quadrature error in integral RL policy evaluation degrades policy iteration, and that Bayesian quadrature with a Matérn kernel improves convergence.
nodes.problem: Integral RL needs accurate utility integrals in policy evaluation; quadrature error effects on control are unstudied.
nodes.approach: Newton-method analogy for policy evaluation error plus Bayesian quadrature with an RKHS-inducing kernel; convergence proofs.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Quadrature choice in continuous-time integral RL is a rare theory topic.

nodes.title: Negative Label Guided OOD Detection with Pretrained Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Post hoc OOD detection for vision-language models that uses a large corpus of negative labels to score unknown-class samples, robust under domain shift.
nodes.problem: Vision-language OOD detection rarely exploits text-side information about unknown classes.
nodes.approach: Harvests many negative labels from corpus databases and designs an OOD score built on them.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Domain Adaptation & OOD Generalization
nodes.niche_reason: VLM-based OOD detection is an active, common direction.

nodes.title: Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms
nodes.tldr: Analyzes privacy amplification by sampling for correlated-noise matrix mechanisms (DP-FTRL), giving tighter guarantees that can asymptotically match DP-SGD's noise level.
nodes.problem: Privacy amplification via sampling does not directly apply to correlated-noise DP-FTRL algorithms.
nodes.approach: Conditional composition: correlated outputs are analyzed as independent by conditioning on prior outputs (MMCC).
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised matrix-mechanism privacy analysis within an established DP area.

nodes.title: Inherently Interpretable Time Series Classification via Multiple Instance Learning
nodes.tldr: MILLET applies multiple instance learning to existing deep time-series classifiers, making them inherently interpretable with sparse local explanations and no loss in accuracy.
nodes.problem: Deep time-series classifiers are black boxes whose decisions are hard to explain.
nodes.approach: Multiple instance learning over time segments yields sparse, quickly computed local explanations built into the model.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
nodes.niche_reason: Inherently interpretable MIL for time series is specialised but established.
