nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot 3D segmentation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: GeSubNet: Gene Interaction Inference for Disease Subtype Network Generation
nodes.tldr: GeSubNet learns a representation that predicts gene interactions while separating disease subtypes, so generated graphs give subtype-specific gene networks for cancers.
nodes.problem: Gene networks from knowledge databases do not match subtype-specific disease variation, and current methods miss it.
nodes.approach: Deep generative subtype model, a GNN over prior gene networks, and an inference loss fusing both representations for subtype-specific interactions.
nodes.niche_reason: Subtype-specific gene network generation is a rare biology-ML niche.

nodes.title: Instant Policy: In-Context Imitation Learning via Graph Diffusion
nodes.tldr: Instant Policy learns new robot tasks from one or two demonstrations by graph diffusion, trained on simulated pseudo-demonstrations.
nodes.problem: Robots usually need many demonstrations to learn each new task, with no instant in-context adaptation.
nodes.approach: Model in-context imitation as graph generation with a learned diffusion process over demonstrations, observations and actions.
nodes.niche_reason: In-context imitation via graph diffusion is a rare, unusual formulation.

nodes.title: Preference Optimization for Reasoning with Pseudo Feedback
nodes.tldr: Generates pseudo preference labels for reasoning by scoring solutions against test cases, then applies preference optimization to improve math and coding reasoning.
nodes.problem: Preference optimization for reasoning needs verified labels that are scarce.
nodes.approach: Pseudo feedback from test-case pass rates, including self-generated tests, used to build DPO preference pairs.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
nodes.niche_reason: Crowded DPO-for-reasoning space.

nodes.title: Identifiable Exchangeable Mechanisms for Causal Structure and Representation Learning
nodes.tldr: Unifies causal discovery, ICA, and causal representation learning under exchangeable data, giving new identifiability results via a duality condition.
nodes.problem: Identifiability methods rely on exchangeable non-i.i.d. data, but this shared assumption has been left unexplored.
nodes.approach: Probabilistic graphical model (IEM) generalising the causal de Finetti theorem with cause and mechanism variability conditions.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Unified identifiability framework linking causal discovery and ICA; specialised.

nodes.title: Root Cause Analysis of Anomalies in Multivariate Time Series through Granger Causal Discovery
nodes.tldr: AERCA jointly learns Granger causality and models normal exogenous variable distributions, treating anomalies as interventions to identify root causes in multivariate time series.
nodes.problem: Identifying root causes of anomalies amid complex dependencies in multivariate time series.
nodes.approach: Granger causal discovery with explicit modeling of exogenous variable distributions to flag deviating variables.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Time Series & Sequential Data
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Root cause analysis in time series is a rare combination.

nodes.title: INCLUDE: Evaluating Multilingual Language Understanding with Regional Knowledge
nodes.tldr: INCLUDE is a benchmark of 197k QA pairs from local exams across 44 languages to evaluate multilingual LLMs on regional knowledge and reasoning.
nodes.problem: Multilingual evaluation resources are scarce and translated English benchmarks ignore regional and cultural knowledge.
nodes.approach: Collect local exam questions in 44 written languages to build knowledge- and reasoning-centric benchmark.
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Multilingual LLM benchmarks are common.

nodes.title: Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching
nodes.tldr: Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching uses few pre-aligned pairs as state feedback in an entropic OT objective to speed up and improve semi-supervised bridge matching.
nodes.problem: Bridge matching trades off scalability against access to optimal pairings.
nodes.approach: Entropic OT objective with semi-supervised guidance from few aligned pairs, recast dynamically for matching training.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Schrödinger bridge matching is a niche diffusion subarea.

nodes.title: MetaUrban: An Embodied AI Simulation Platform for Urban Micromobility
nodes.tldr: MetaUrban is a compositional simulator generating infinite interactive urban scenes for micromobility research, with point and social navigation benchmarks and RL and imitation baselines.
nodes.problem: No simulation platform supports generalizable, safe embodied AI for urban micromobility.
nodes.approach: Compositional procedural scene generation with pedestrians and agents, plus navigation tasks and baselines.
nodes.niche_reason: Urban micromobility simulation is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Toward Guidance-Free AR Visual Generation via Condition Contrastive Alignment
nodes.tldr: Condition Contrastive Alignment fine-tunes autoregressive visual generators to remove the need for classifier-free guidance, halving sampling cost with one epoch of fine-tuning.
nodes.problem: Classifier-free guidance is inconsistent with unified language-vision autoregressive generation and costly at sampling.
nodes.approach: Alignment-inspired contrastive fine-tuning that directly fits the guided target distribution.
nodes.niche_reason: Links language alignment to visual guidance, somewhat unusual.

nodes.title: Copyright-Protected Language Generation via Adaptive Model Fusion
nodes.tldr: CP-Fuse combines models trained on disjoint copyrighted data at inference, adaptively aggregating outputs with a balancing property to reduce regurgitation of copyrighted content.
nodes.problem: Language models reproduce copyrighted training material; existing inference-time protections are costly or hurt performance.
nodes.approach: Adaptively fuse outputs of models trained on disjoint copyrighted sets, balancing their likelihoods during decoding.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Copyright mitigation is an established but specialised LLM safety area.

nodes.title: Standard Gaussian Process is All You Need for High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization
nodes.tldr: Shows standard Gaussian process Bayesian optimization works well in high dimensions when using Matérn kernels and proper length-scale initialization, rebutting the belief it fails.
nodes.problem: Whether standard GP-based Bayesian optimization really underperforms in high-dimensional optimization.
nodes.approach: Benchmark across twelve problems and theory showing SE kernel failure stems from length-scale initialization and vanishing gradients.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised Bayesian optimization subfield.

nodes.title: LayerDAG: A Layerwise Autoregressive Diffusion Model for Directed Acyclic Graph Generation
nodes.tldr: Generates directed acyclic graphs layer by layer by combining autoregressive ordering with diffusion over bipartite layers, scaling to 400-node DAGs.
nodes.problem: Generating realistic DAGs is hard due to directional and logical dependencies between nodes.
nodes.approach: Autoregressive generation across partial-order layers, each layer a bipartite graph modeled by discrete diffusion.
nodes.niche_reason: Autoregressive-diffusion DAG generation is a rare topic.

nodes.title: Learning and aligning single-neuron invariance manifolds in visual cortex
nodes.tldr: Learns continuous invariance manifolds of stimuli that drive visual neurons and aligns them with affine transforms, revealing functional clusters in macaque V1.
nodes.problem: Existing methods probe isolated stimuli, so comparing neuronal invariances across receptive fields is hard.
nodes.approach: Learn invariance manifolds with a neural response model, then fit a pixel-coordinate affine map aligning neurons.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural invariance manifolds in macaque V1 are a very rare niche.

nodes.title: Learning local equivariant representations for quantum operators
nodes.tldr: SLEM predicts DFT Hamiltonian, overlap, and density matrices with strictly local equivariant message passing, improving efficiency and scalability to large materials.
nodes.problem: Predicting quantum operator matrices for large systems is costly and struggles with scalability.
nodes.approach: Strictly local SO(2)-convolution equivariant network with invariant overlap parameterization.
nodes.niche_reason: Equivariant quantum operator prediction is a rare cross-disciplinary niche.

nodes.title: Diffusion Attribution Score: Evaluating Training Data Influence in Diffusion Models
nodes.tldr: Diffusion Attribution Score measures training sample influence in diffusion models by directly comparing predicted distributions, with speedups, outperforming prior data attribution on linear datamodeling score.
nodes.problem: Existing diffusion data attribution uses diffusion loss changes, which only indirectly captures model behavior differences.
nodes.approach: Direct comparison of predicted distributions with theoretical analysis and computational speedups for large diffusion models.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Data attribution for diffusion models is specialised.

nodes.title: OmniCorpus: A Unified Multimodal Corpus of 10 Billion-Level Images Interleaved with Text
nodes.tldr: Releases OmniCorpus, a 10-billion-scale image-text interleaved web corpus with 8.6B images and 1.7T text tokens, filtered by an efficient data engine.
nodes.problem: Current image-text interleaved datasets are too small and narrow for training multimodal LLMs.
nodes.approach: Data engine filters and extracts high-quality documents from English, non-English, and video-centric websites.
nodes.niche_reason: Image-text interleaved corpora are a common multimodal data direction.

nodes.title: Reti-Diff: Illumination Degradation Image Restoration with Retinex-based Latent Diffusion Model
nodes.tldr: Reti-Diff uses a Retinex-based latent diffusion model to produce compact reflectance and illumination priors that guide a transformer to restore images degraded by poor illumination.
nodes.problem: Diffusion-based illumination restoration is computationally heavy and suffers pixel misalignment.
nodes.approach: Latent diffusion generating Retinex priors that guide a Retinex-guided transformer for decomposition and refinement.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-based image restoration is common.

nodes.title: Navigating the Digital World as Humans Do: Universal Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
nodes.tldr: Trains UGround, a universal visual grounding model that maps GUI element descriptions to screen coordinates, enabling purely visual GUI agents.
nodes.problem: Text-based GUI agent inputs are noisy and incomplete, hurting grounding robustness.
nodes.approach: Visual grounding trained on 10M GUI elements from web synthetic data with a LLaVA-style model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment call between GUI agents and visual grounding.
nodes.niche_reason: GUI agents are a fast-growing, crowded area.

nodes.title: Controlling Language and Diffusion Models by Transporting Activations
nodes.tldr: Steers LLM and text-to-image activations with optimal-transport maps, controlling toxicity, concepts, truthfulness and image style with little overhead.
nodes.problem: Controlling reliability, safety and style of large generative models after training
nodes.approach: Optimal-transport-guided activation steering applied to LLMs and diffusion models
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.confidence_reason: Steering spans controllability, safety and interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Optimal-transport activation steering is specialised

nodes.title: ADIFF: Explaining audio difference using natural language
nodes.tldr: ADIFF explains differences between two audio recordings in natural language, with new datasets from AudioCaps/Clotho and a model using cross-projection and staged training.
nodes.problem: Describing differences between audio recordings in language
nodes.approach: Prefix-tuned audio-language model with cross-projection, position captioning, three-stage training
nodes.primary_topic: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio & Music Understanding
nodes.niche_reason: Audio difference explanation is a novel, very rare task.

nodes.title: Online Reinforcement Learning in Non-Stationary Context-Driven Environments
nodes.tldr: LCPO mitigates catastrophic forgetting in online RL under non-stationary context-driven environments by locally constraining policy updates to anchor outputs on out-of-context past experiences.
nodes.problem: Online RL forgets prior knowledge in non-stationary environments without task labels.
nodes.approach: Locally Constrained Policy Optimization anchoring policy outputs on old samples outside current context distribution.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Transfer, Meta & Continual RL
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Continual online RL with exogenous context is specialised.

nodes.title: MonST3R: A Simple Approach for Estimating Geometry in the Presence of Motion
nodes.tldr: Adapts DUSt3R's pointmap representation to dynamic scenes by fine-tuning on scarce posed dynamic video data, estimating per-frame geometry directly.
nodes.problem: Estimating geometry from dynamic scenes relies on complex multi-stage pipelines prone to error.
nodes.approach: Predicts a pointmap per timestep with a static-scene 3D model fine-tuned on dynamic data, without explicit motion modelling.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamic 3D geometry from video is a popular area

nodes.title: Token Statistics Transformer: Linear-Time Attention via Variational Rate Reduction
nodes.tldr: Derives a linear-time attention operator, token statistics self-attention, from a variational rate reduction objective, giving the efficient and interpretable ToST transformer.
nodes.problem: Quadratic attention cost and lack of principled, interpretable transformer design.
nodes.approach: Unroll gradient descent on a variational maximal coding rate reduction objective to obtain token statistics attention.
nodes.niche_reason: White-box architecture derivation is a specialised angle on efficient attention.

nodes.title: NV-Embed: Improved Techniques for Training LLMs as Generalist Embedding Models
nodes.tldr: NV-Embed trains decoder-only LLMs as generalist text embedding models using latent attention pooling, bidirectional contrastive training, and two-stage instruction tuning, topping MTEB.
nodes.problem: Making decoder-only LLMs strong general-purpose text embedding and retrieval models.
nodes.approach: Latent attention pooling, removing causal mask during contrastive training, two-stage contrastive instruction tuning with hard negatives.
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-based embedding models are a busy area.

nodes.title: RESuM: A Rare Event Surrogate Model for Physics Detector Design
nodes.tldr: RESuM combines a conditional neural process with a multi-fidelity Gaussian process to optimize rare-event physics detector designs, cutting neutron background 66.5% with 3.3% of compute.
nodes.problem: Optimizing detector designs when the background metric is rare and simulations are costly.
nodes.approach: Surrogate model using pre-trained conditional neural process prior within multi-fidelity Gaussian process.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Kernels, GPs & Nonparametrics
nodes.niche_reason: Rare-event surrogate for neutrinoless double-beta decay detectors is very niche.

nodes.title: gRNAde: Geometric Deep Learning for 3D RNA inverse design
nodes.tldr: Uses a multi-state graph neural network with autoregressive decoding to design RNA sequences conditioned on given 3D backbone structures.
nodes.problem: RNA design usually targets one secondary structure and ignores 3D conformational diversity.
nodes.approach: Multi-state GNN encoder with autoregressive sequence decoding conditioned on one or more 3D backbones.
nodes.niche_reason: 3D RNA inverse design with geometric GNNs is a rare niche

nodes.title: Boltzmann-Aligned Inverse Folding Model as a Predictor of Mutational Effects on Protein-Protein Interactions
nodes.tldr: Boltzmann Alignment transfers inverse-folding model log-likelihoods to predict protein binding free energy changes, with an explicit unbound-state term, reaching state-of-the-art SKEMPI v2 correlations.
nodes.problem: Predicting mutational binding free energy (ddG) changes is limited by scarce experimental ddG data.
nodes.approach: Bayes-based Boltzmann alignment of pretrained inverse-folding likelihoods, modeling the thermodynamic cycle.
nodes.niche_reason: Protein binding affinity prediction is established but specialised.

nodes.title: LLM-SR: Scientific Equation Discovery via Programming with Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: LLM-SR uses LLMs' scientific priors to propose equation skeletons, refined by evolutionary search over equation programs fitted to data.
nodes.problem: Discovering scientific equations from data needs navigating huge hypothesis spaces while ignoring domain priors.
nodes.approach: LLM proposes equation program skeletons, refined by evolutionary search and data-based parameter fitting.
nodes.primary_topic: Science & Applications › Scientific Discovery & Symbolic Regression
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Code Generation & Software
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-driven symbolic regression is a rare cross-disciplinary angle

nodes.title: Overcoming False Illusions in Real-World Face Restoration with Multi-Modal Guided Diffusion Model
nodes.tldr: MGFR restores low-quality faces with diffusion guided by text attributes, reference images and identity information to avoid false attributes, plus a 21K-image Reface-HQ dataset.
nodes.problem: Generative face restoration hallucinates false facial attributes and identities.
nodes.approach: Multi-modal guided diffusion with dual-control adapter and two-stage training using text, reference and identity priors.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Face restoration is established but specialised.

nodes.title: MQuAKE-Remastered: Multi-Hop Knowledge Editing Can Only Be Advanced with Reliable Evaluations
nodes.tldr: Audits the MQuAKE multi-hop knowledge-editing dataset, finds widespread corrupted labels, and releases a repaired MQuAKE-Remastered benchmark with a simple baseline.
nodes.problem: Many knowledge-editing methods are evaluated on MQuAKE, whose questions and labels contain many errors.
nodes.approach: Systematic error audit and fix, then benchmarking editing methods on the repaired dataset, with GWalk as a minimal baseline.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: Multi-hop knowledge editing evaluation is a specialised subfield.

nodes.title: WizardMath: Empowering Mathematical Reasoning for Large Language Models via Reinforced Evol-Instruct
nodes.tldr: WizardMath boosts open LLM math reasoning by applying reinforcement learning from Evol-Instruct feedback with process supervision.
nodes.problem: Open LLMs lack math-specific optimization and struggle on competition-level math benchmarks.
nodes.approach: Reinforcement learning from Evol-Instruct feedback, using instruction evolution and process supervision.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › RL for LLMs & Reasoning
nodes.niche_reason: Crowded: RL for math reasoning in open LLMs

nodes.title: CBGBench: Fill in the Blank of Protein-Molecule Complex Binding Graph
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks structure-based drug design by framing it as graph completion of protein-molecule binding graphs across de novo, linker, fragment, scaffold and sidechain tasks.
nodes.problem: Structure-based drug design methods lack standardized, fair comparison across diverse tasks.
nodes.approach: Unified modular framework with fairness-focused evaluation of graph-completion models and a shared codebase.
nodes.niche_reason: Structure-based drug design benchmarks are specialised but established

nodes.title: Predictive Inverse Dynamics Models are Scalable Learners for Robotic Manipulation
nodes.tldr: Seer predicts robot actions with inverse dynamics conditioned on forecasted future visual states, pre-trained on DROID and fine-tuned for scalable manipulation.
nodes.problem: Robot policies must exploit both action data and visual pre-training, which are usually handled separately.
nodes.approach: Transformer inverse dynamics model conditioned on predicted future visual states, trained end-to-end at scale.
nodes.confidence_reason: Robot foundation model vs imitation learning; both fit
nodes.niche_reason: Predictive inverse dynamics for robots is a common foundation-model line

nodes.title: Probabilistic Geometric Principal Component Analysis with application to neural data
nodes.tldr: PGPCA generalizes probabilistic PCA to data distributed around a given nonlinear manifold using a geometric coordinate system and EM learning, with neural data applications.
nodes.problem: Linear PPCA cannot describe data distributed around nonlinear manifolds, common in neural recordings.
nodes.approach: Fit a manifold, derive geometric coordinates for deviations, and learn parameters with a data-driven EM algorithm.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Classical latent-variable modeling with a manifold geometry twist for neuroscience.

nodes.title: Correlated Proxies: A New Definition and Improved Mitigation for Reward Hacking
nodes.tldr: Defines reward hacking via proxy-true reward correlation under a reference policy and shows chi-squared occupancy measure regularization mitigates it better than KL, including in RLHF.
nodes.problem: Optimizing proxy rewards causes reward hacking, and there is no principled definition to mitigate it.
nodes.approach: Correlation-based definition of reward hacking and chi-squared divergence regularization of occupancy measures to the reference policy.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Reward hacking theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Mind the Gap: Examining the Self-Improvement Capabilities of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Formalizes LLM self-improvement via a generation-verification gap, showing it scales with pre-training compute, and studies when and how iterative self-improvement works.
nodes.problem: Lack of fundamental understanding of when LLM self-improvement through self-verification and distillation works.
nodes.approach: Mathematical formulation around generation-verification gap plus controlled scaling experiments across model families.
secondary_topics: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: LLM self-improvement is a common, active topic.

nodes.title: Judge Decoding: Faster Speculative Sampling Requires Going Beyond Model Alignment
nodes.tldr: Speeds up speculative decoding by training a compact judge on target-model embeddings to accept high-quality draft tokens that differ from the target.
nodes.problem: Standard speculative verification rejects many valid draft tokens, limiting LLM decoding speedup
nodes.approach: Learned judge module on target embeddings that accepts non-aligned but correct continuations
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: Speculative decoding is a crowded direction

nodes.title: ThinK: Thinner Key Cache by Query-Driven Pruning
nodes.tldr: ThinK prunes the least important KV cache channels using query-dependent scoring, cutting KV memory over 20% while preserving accuracy and composing with quantization.
nodes.problem: KV cache memory grows with long sequences, and channel-dimension redundancy is unexploited.
nodes.approach: Query-driven pruning of KV cache channels to minimize attention weight loss.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Long Context & Memory
nodes.niche_reason: KV cache compression is a common topic; channel-wise pruning is a mild variant.

nodes.title: Transformers Provably Solve Parity Efficiently with Chain of Thought
nodes.tldr: Proves one-layer transformers learn k-parity efficiently with chain-of-thought supervision, teacher forcing or verification augmentation.
nodes.problem: Why chain-of-thought helps transformers learn hard tasks like k-parity is theoretically unclear.
nodes.approach: Gradient-based training analysis of a one-layer transformer with intermediate parity supervision and augmented data.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Theory of chain-of-thought learning dynamics on parity is rare

nodes.title: OS-ATLAS: Foundation Action Model for Generalist GUI Agents
nodes.tldr: OS-Atlas is an open foundation GUI action model trained on the largest open cross-platform GUI grounding corpus (13M elements), strong at grounding and out-of-distribution agent tasks.
nodes.problem: Open-source VLMs lag closed models in GUI grounding and OOD GUI agentic tasks.
nodes.approach: Toolkit to synthesize cross-platform GUI grounding data and train a foundational GUI action model.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: GUI agents are a crowded, fast-growing topic.

nodes.title: Vision-RWKV: Efficient and Scalable Visual Perception with RWKV-Like Architectures
nodes.tldr: Adapts the RWKV linear-attention architecture to vision, offering global context and high-resolution processing without windowing, beating ViT on classification with lower cost.
nodes.problem: Transformer self-attention is too costly for high-resolution vision, and window-based fixes complicate design.
nodes.approach: Vision-tailored RWKV blocks with reduced spatial aggregation complexity, handling sparse inputs such as masked images.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Vision Foundation Models & Self-Supervision
nodes.niche_reason: Linear-attention vision backbones are an active, common direction.

nodes.title: Large-scale and Fine-grained Vision-language Pre-training for Enhanced CT Image Understanding
nodes.tldr: Aligns CT anatomical regions with report sentences for anatomy-level contrastive pretraining, correcting false negatives for zero-shot diagnosis.
nodes.problem: Global image-report contrastive learning misses local region-sentence links and creates false negatives.
nodes.approach: Per-anatomy contrastive pretraining with false-negative identification that calibrates patient-level to disease-aware pairing.
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised: anatomy-level contrastive pretraining on CT reports.

nodes.title: Artificial Kuramoto Oscillatory Neurons
nodes.tldr: Replaces threshold neurons with Kuramoto oscillators whose synchronization binds features, improving object discovery, robustness and uncertainty.
nodes.problem: Standard threshold neurons lack the binding and spatiotemporal dynamics that neuroscience suggests matter.
nodes.approach: Generalized Kuramoto update layer that binds neurons through synchronization, combinable with fully connected, convolutional, or attentive designs.
nodes.confidence_reason: novel neuron dynamics with no clear topic match
nodes.niche_reason: oscillator-based neurons, very few comparable architectures

nodes.title: Ctrl-Adapter: An Efficient and Versatile Framework for Adapting Diverse Controls to Any Diffusion Model
nodes.tldr: Ctrl-Adapter adapts pretrained ControlNets to new image and video diffusion backbones, supporting multi-condition and sparse-frame control with under 10 GPU hours of training.
nodes.problem: ControlNets cannot be reused across diffusion backbones, and per-frame application breaks temporal consistency in video.
nodes.approach: Lightweight adapter mapping pretrained ControlNet features to new backbones, with patch-level multi-condition and sparse-frame control.
nodes.niche_reason: Controllable diffusion with ControlNet-style adapters is crowded.

nodes.title: Internet of Agents: Weaving a Web of Heterogeneous Agents for Collaborative Intelligence
nodes.tldr: Internet of Agents is an LLM multi-agent framework with an agent integration protocol, messaging-like architecture, and dynamic teaming for heterogeneous third-party agents.
nodes.problem: Existing multi-agent frameworks poorly integrate heterogeneous agents and use rigid communication
nodes.approach: Integration protocol, instant-messaging architecture, dynamic team formation and conversation flow control
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: LLM multi-agent frameworks are very common

nodes.title: CAX: Cellular Automata Accelerated in JAX
nodes.tldr: Open-source JAX library for hardware-accelerated cellular automata, up to 2,000x faster, demonstrated on classic, neural and novel automata including outperforming GPT-4 on 1D-ARC.
nodes.problem: Lack of a fast, flexible cellular automata library hinders research and reproducibility.
nodes.approach: Modular JAX library supporting discrete and continuous cellular automata in arbitrary dimensions.
nodes.confidence_reason: Library paper with no clean topic in the vocabulary.
nodes.niche_reason: Cellular automata tooling is a very rare niche in ML venues.

nodes.title: ChartMoE: Mixture of Diversely Aligned Expert Connector for Chart Understanding
nodes.tldr: Replaces the linear connector of a multimodal LLM with a mixture of aligned experts, trained on a chart-table-JSON-code dataset, for better chart understanding.
nodes.problem: Multimodal LLMs give unfaithful data and unreliable analysis when reading charts.
nodes.approach: Mixture-of-experts connector with experts initialized from distinct alignment tasks.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal LLM connector variants are fairly crowded.

nodes.title: On the Benefits of Memory for Modeling Time-Dependent PDEs
nodes.tldr: Shows theoretically and empirically that memory of past states helps model time-dependent PDEs, introducing MemNO that combines S4 state-space models with Fourier Neural Operators.
nodes.problem: Markovian neural PDE solvers underperform when data is low-resolution or noisy.
nodes.approach: Mori-Zwanzig-motivated analysis plus Memory Neural Operator combining S4 with FNO over past states.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
nodes.niche_reason: Neural operators are established; memory-based variants are specialised.

nodes.title: ZAPBench: A Benchmark for Whole-Brain Activity Prediction in Zebrafish
nodes.tldr: Benchmark for predicting cellular-resolution neural activity across a whole zebrafish brain, from a dataset of 4D light-sheet recordings of over 70,000 neurons.
nodes.problem: No standard benchmark exists for forecasting whole-brain neural activity at cellular resolution.
nodes.approach: Motion-stabilized voxel-level segmented light-sheet data with time-series and volumetric-video baselines.
nodes.niche_reason: Whole-brain vertebrate activity forecasting benchmarks are very rare.

nodes.title: Not All LLM-Generated Data Are Equal: Rethinking Data Weighting in Text Classification
nodes.tldr: Proposes weighted-loss methods that emphasize high-quality, diverse LLM-generated samples using a tiny real dataset, improving BERT-level text classification over standard cross-entropy.
nodes.problem: LLM-generated training data deviates from real-world distributions, harming downstream classifiers.
nodes.approach: Weighted loss that upweights high-quality, diverse synthetic examples using a small real anchor set.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Weighting LLM synthetic data is a common, active direction.

nodes.title: TokenFormer: Rethinking Transformer Scaling with Tokenized Model Parameters
nodes.tldr: Replaces transformer linear projections with token-parameter attention, so model parameters act as keys and values and models scale incrementally without retraining from scratch.
nodes.problem: Transformer scaling requires retraining from scratch whenever architecture dimensions change, which is costly.
nodes.approach: Input tokens query learnable key-value parameter tokens, replacing all linear projections with attention.
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Parameter-as-token scaling is a distinctive architecture idea

nodes.title: LLaVA-Interleave: Tackling Multi-image, Video, and 3D in Large Multimodal Models
nodes.tldr: LLaVA-Interleave is one large multimodal model handling multi-image, video, and 3D inputs via an interleaved data format and M4-Instruct.
nodes.problem: Open large multimodal models focus on single images and do not generalize across multi-image, video, and 3D.
nodes.approach: Unified interleaved-format instruction tuning on a 1.18M-sample M4-Instruct dataset.
nodes.niche_reason: Multimodal LLM instruction tuning is a common direction

nodes.title: DarkBench: Benchmarking Dark Patterns in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: A 660-prompt benchmark that probes LLMs for dark design patterns such as sycophancy, brand bias, and sneaking, finding manipulative behavior across major developers.
nodes.problem: Dark design patterns that manipulate users in LLM interactions lack systematic measurement.
nodes.approach: Six-category prompt benchmark evaluated across five leading LLM developers' models.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Specialised: manipulative design patterns in LLMs, few papers.

nodes.title: Provably Reliable Conformal Prediction Sets in the Presence of Data Poisoning
nodes.tldr: Builds conformal prediction sets with provable reliability under training and calibration data poisoning by aggregating classifiers on data partitions.
nodes.problem: Conformal prediction sets break under poisoning of training and calibration data.
nodes.approach: Smoothed score aggregation over training partitions plus majority voting across calibration subsets.
nodes.niche_reason: Poisoning-robust conformal prediction is specialised.

nodes.title: MaestroMotif: Skill Design from Artificial Intelligence Feedback
nodes.tldr: Uses LLM feedback to write per-skill reward functions from natural-language descriptions, then trains and composes skills with RL to solve NetHack tasks.
nodes.problem: Specifying complex decision-making skills in natural language and reusing them in RL agents is hard.
nodes.approach: LLM-designed rewards and LLM-generated code for skill training, combined via language-specified behaviors.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: LLM-designed rewards for NetHack skills is a specialised niche

nodes.title: Exploring Local Memorization in Diffusion Models via Bright Ending Attention
nodes.tldr: Identifies a cross-attention anomaly in text-to-image diffusion models where memorized patches attend strongly to the final text token, enabling localization of memorized regions.
nodes.problem: Existing memorization methods miss local memorization and cannot locate the memorized image regions.
nodes.approach: Bright ending attention score localizes memorized patches and integrates into existing mitigation frameworks.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.confidence_reason: Memorization is a privacy and copyright issue, but the analysis targets generative attention.
nodes.niche_reason: Localizing memorization in diffusion models is a rare direction.

nodes.title: No Need to Talk: Asynchronous Mixture of Language Models
nodes.tldr: SMALLTALK LM trains a mixture of language models near-asynchronously with a prefix-based router that picks one expert at inference, beating dense baselines at equal FLOPs.
nodes.problem: Training mixtures of LMs without high-bandwidth communication or corpus clustering.
nodes.approach: Independently trained specialist LMs with a lightweight router selecting a single expert from a short prefix.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
nodes.niche_reason: Asynchronous mixture training is an established but specialised direction.

nodes.title: Data Scaling Laws in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation
nodes.tldr: Shows manipulation policies generalize roughly power-law in environments and objects, with diversity mattering far more than demonstration count.
nodes.problem: Whether data scaling yields zero-shot policies for new objects and environments is unknown.
nodes.approach: Large real-world study of 40,000+ demonstrations and 15,000+ rollouts, plus a fast collection strategy.
nodes.niche_reason: Imitation learning scaling studies are increasingly common.

nodes.title: Control-oriented Clustering of Visual Latent Representation
nodes.tldr: Finds neural-collapse-like clustering in visual representations of image-based control policies and uses NC pretraining of the vision encoder to boost test performance 10-35%.
nodes.problem: Little is known about the geometry of visual representations in image-based behavior-cloning control.
nodes.approach: Neural-collapse-style regularization pretrains the vision encoder to cluster features by control-oriented relative pose classes.
nodes.niche_reason: Neural collapse in visual control representations is an unusual angle.

nodes.title: Scalable and Certifiable Graph Unlearning: Overcoming the Approximation Error Barrier
nodes.tldr: Scales certified graph unlearning to billion-edge graphs by integrating approximate graph propagation while keeping certified guarantees on exact embeddings.
nodes.problem: Certified graph unlearning requires costly re-propagation, impractical on large graphs.
nodes.approach: Approximate graph propagation with certified error bounds for node feature, edge, and node unlearning.
nodes.primary_topic: Trustworthy ML › Machine Unlearning & Privacy Attacks
nodes.niche_reason: Established but specialised: certified unlearning on GNNs.

nodes.title: On Scaling Up 3D Gaussian Splatting Training
nodes.tldr: Grendel partitions 3D Gaussian Splatting parameters across GPUs with sparse communication and load balancing, enabling larger high-resolution scenes and batched multi-view training.
nodes.problem: 3DGS training on one GPU is memory-limited for high-resolution, large-scale reconstruction
nodes.approach: Distributed parameter partitioning with sparse all-to-all Gaussian transfer, dynamic load balancing, and sqrt batch-size LR scaling
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.niche_reason: Distributed 3DGS systems work is fairly specialised

nodes.title: Scalable Decision-Making in Stochastic Environments through Learned Temporal Abstraction
nodes.tldr: L-MAP learns discrete macro-actions with a state-conditional VQ-VAE and plans over them with MCTS, handling stochastic environments in offline RL with low latency.
nodes.problem: Planning in high-dimensional continuous action spaces under stochastic dynamics in offline RL is computationally costly.
nodes.approach: State-conditional VQ-VAE macro-actions, learned latent prior, and Monte Carlo tree search over discrete latent actions.
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
nodes.niche_reason: Latent-action MCTS planning for offline RL is specialised but established.

nodes.title: CLoSD: Closing the Loop between Simulation and Diffusion for multi-task character control
nodes.tldr: CLoSD closes the loop between a text-driven autoregressive motion diffusion planner and an RL tracking controller, enabling physics-based multi-task humanoid character control.
nodes.problem: Motion diffusion lacks physical plausibility and environment interaction, while RL controllers lack intuitive text control.
nodes.approach: Fast autoregressive diffusion planner feeds motion plans to an RL motion-imitation controller that returns environment feedback in a closed loop.
secondary_topics: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
nodes.niche_reason: Physics-based character animation with diffusion planning is specialised.

nodes.title: Towards a Complete Logical Framework for GNN Expressiveness
nodes.tldr: Builds a framework mapping arbitrary GNN architectures to equivalent logical formulas, unifying prominent GNN classes and determining homomorphism expressivity of general GNN models.
nodes.problem: Lack of a systematic, interpretable characterization of GNN expressiveness beyond Weisfeiler-Lehman tests.
nodes.approach: Identify equivalent logic formulas for GNN architectures and derive homomorphism expressivity from a logical perspective.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Logic-based GNN expressivity theory is a small theoretical subcommunity.

nodes.title: Retri3D: 3D Neural Graphics Representation Retrieval
nodes.tldr: Retrieves stored neural 3D scenes by text query by selecting clean viewpoints from pretrained neural graphics representations.
nodes.problem: Existing frameworks cannot accurately retrieve stored NeRF and 3DGS scenes from text queries.
nodes.approach: Neural field artifact analysis plus a smart camera movement module to pick informative views for embeddings.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › 3D Reconstruction, NeRF & Gaussian Splatting
nodes.confidence_reason: Retrieval task straddles 3D representation and vision-language topics
nodes.niche_reason: Retrieval over stored neural 3D representations is an unusual direction

nodes.title: Iterative Label Refinement Matters More than Preference Optimization under Weak Supervision
nodes.tldr: Under unreliable supervision, iterative label refinement of SFT data using comparison feedback outperforms DPO-based preference optimization on math, coding and safe instruction-following.
nodes.problem: Post-training effectiveness when human demonstrations and preference comparisons are unreliable.
nodes.approach: Use comparison feedback to replace demonstrations with model-generated alternatives, then retrain via SFT.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Trustworthy ML › AI Safety & Alignment Research
nodes.niche_reason: Scalable-oversight-motivated alternative to RLHF is a somewhat specialised angle.

nodes.title: Both Ears Wide Open: Towards Language-Driven Spatial Audio Generation
nodes.tldr: Generates stereo spatial audio from text with a latent diffusion model guided by spatial-aware encoders and azimuth state matrices.
nodes.problem: Stereo audio generators struggle with multiple moving sources and controllable spatial direction.
nodes.approach: Large simulated, GPT-assisted stereo dataset (BEWO-1M) plus spatial guidance for latent diffusion.
nodes.primary_topic: Generative Models › Audio, Speech & Music Generation
nodes.niche_reason: Stereo spatial audio generation from text is specialised.

nodes.title: GETS: Ensemble Temperature Scaling for Calibration in Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Calibrates graph neural networks by combining input and model ensembles inside a graph mixture-of-experts that selects experts per node.
nodes.problem: Post-hoc temperature scaling ignores graph structure, leaving GNNs overconfident or underconfident.
nodes.approach: Graph MoE over logits, node features and degree embeddings that adaptively weights experts for each node's calibration.
nodes.niche_reason: Calibration is established; GNN-specific ensembling is somewhat specialised.

nodes.title: Mitigating Information Loss in Tree-Based Reinforcement Learning via Direct Optimization
nodes.tldr: SYMPOL trains axis-aligned decision-tree policies end-to-end with policy gradients inside standard on-policy RL, giving interpretable policies that outperform prior tree-based RL.
nodes.problem: Neural RL policies are black boxes, and learning tree policies on-policy is hard.
nodes.approach: Differentiable axis-aligned tree model trained with a policy gradient method.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Online & Deep RL Algorithms
nodes.niche_reason: Gradient-trained tree policies are an unusual RL direction.

nodes.title: Demystifying the Token Dynamics of Deep Selective State Space Models
nodes.tldr: Analyzes the continuous-time dynamics of tokens in deep selective SSMs like Mamba, proving tokens converge to zero or diverge, and proposes refinements to improve performance.
nodes.problem: Deep selective state space models lack theoretical understanding of token dynamics.
nodes.approach: Derive continuous-time limit dynamical system, characterize asymptotics, and propose exclusion of convergent regime and token reordering.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › State-Space Models & Linear Attention
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Dynamical-systems analysis of Mamba tokens is a rare theoretical angle.

nodes.title: DEEM: Diffusion models serve as the eyes of large language models for image perception
nodes.tldr: Uses diffusion models' generative feedback to align an MLLM's image encoder, reducing hallucinations and improving robustness to out-of-distribution visual inputs.
nodes.problem: Multimodal LLM image encoders like CLIP miss fine visual details and hallucinate on OOD images.
nodes.approach: Aligning encoder semantic distributions with generative feedback from a diffusion model.
nodes.niche_reason: Diffusion-for-perception in MLLMs is a fast-growing area

nodes.title: 4K4DGen: Panoramic 4D Generation at 4K Resolution
nodes.tldr: Generates immersive 4K panoramic 4D scenes from a single panorama by adapting 2D diffusion priors and lifting to animated 3D Gaussians.
nodes.problem: Creating free-viewpoint 360-degree dynamic scenes from one panorama for VR and AR.
nodes.approach: Panoramic denoiser adapts 2D diffusion for video, then dynamic panoramic lifting to 3D Gaussians.
nodes.niche_reason: Panoramic 4D generation is a rare combination of topics

nodes.title: Improving Unsupervised Constituency Parsing via Maximizing Semantic Information
nodes.tldr: Trains unsupervised constituency parsers by maximizing semantic information in constituent structures rather than sentence likelihood, improving PCFG parsing accuracy by about 7.85 F1 across languages.
nodes.problem: Likelihood objective correlates weakly with parsing accuracy in unsupervised constituency parsing.
nodes.approach: Maximize SemInfo from a bag-of-substrings model with a TreeCRF-based model for PCFG training.
nodes.niche_reason: Unsupervised grammar induction is very rare in current ML.

nodes.title: Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent with Chain of Thought
nodes.tldr: Proves transformers trained with a chain-of-thought objective learn multi-step gradient descent autoregressively, recovering the true weights that one-layer models without CoT cannot.
nodes.problem: The training mechanism behind chain-of-thought gains in transformers is largely unexplored.
nodes.approach: Analyzes training dynamics of linear transformers on in-context weight prediction with a CoT objective.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Training dynamics of CoT transformers on linear regression is a specialised theory niche.

nodes.title: Consistency Checks for Language Model Forecasters
nodes.tldr: Evaluates LLM forecasters by checking consistency across logically related questions using arbitrage, which correlates with future Brier scores.
nodes.problem: Forecasting ground truth is only known in the future, so LLM forecasters cannot be evaluated instantly.
nodes.approach: Automated arbitrage-based consistency checks on generated question sets, plus a proper-scoring-rule benchmark that resolves in 2028.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Arbitrage-based consistency evaluation for forecasting is unusual

nodes.title: Interleaved Scene Graphs for Interleaved Text-and-Image Generation Assessment
nodes.tldr: ISG is a scene-graph-based multi-granularity evaluation framework and 1,150-sample benchmark for interleaved text-and-image generation, plus a plan-execute-refine baseline agent.
nodes.problem: No principled way to evaluate consistency and coherence of interleaved text-and-image outputs.
nodes.approach: Scene graph evaluation at holistic, structural, block and image levels, with ISG-Bench and ISG-Agent.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › Generative Model Evaluation & Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Interleaved generation evaluation is emerging and specialised.

nodes.title: PathGen-1.6M: 1.6 Million Pathology Image-text Pairs Generation through Multi-agent Collaboration
nodes.tldr: Multi-agent pipeline extracts WSI patches and generates refined captions, producing 1.6M pathology image-text pairs that improve pathology CLIP.
nodes.problem: Pathology vision-language training data from PubMed and social media is limited, unscalable, and low quality.
nodes.approach: Large multimodal model captioning of patches mined from TCGA whole-slide images, refined by collaborating agents.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Synthetic Data & Data Curation
nodes.niche_reason: Pathology vision-language data is specialised, with several peers

nodes.title: Joint Gradient Balancing for Data Ordering in Finite-Sum Multi-Objective Optimization
nodes.tldr: Orders training samples by jointly balancing gradients of all objectives online, accelerating MGDA convergence over random ordering.
nodes.problem: Sample order affects convergence in finite-sum multi-objective optimization, which is largely unexplored.
nodes.approach: Online vector balancing over per-objective gradients to choose sample orders jointly across objectives.
nodes.niche_reason: Sample ordering for multi-objective optimization is rarely studied.

nodes.title: Homomorphism Expressivity of Spectral Invariant Graph Neural Networks
nodes.tldr: Proves spectral invariant GNNs homomorphism-count exactly parallel trees, giving an expressiveness hierarchy and settling open questions on depth, subgraph counting, and higher-order GNNs.
nodes.problem: Theoretical power of spectral invariants in GNNs is poorly understood.
nodes.approach: Homomorphism expressivity analysis characterizing which patterns spectral invariant GNNs can count.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: Homomorphism-expressivity GNN theory is a small specialised community.

nodes.title: Rethinking Reward Modeling in Preference-based Large Language Model Alignment
nodes.tldr: Shows Bradley-Terry reward models are order-consistent and proposes an alternative upper-bound objective using off-the-shelf binary classifiers, tested across 12,000 setups.
nodes.problem: Why Bradley-Terry reward models work for sparsely compared LLM responses is theoretically unclear.
nodes.approach: Order-consistency analysis plus an upper-bound binary classification objective compatible with off-the-shelf classifiers.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Alignment & Preference Optimization
secondary_topics: Reinforcement Learning › Reward Learning, Inverse RL & Preferences
nodes.niche_reason: Reward-model variant in the crowded RLHF space

nodes.title: UniCBE: An Uniformity-driven Comparing Based Evaluation Framework with Unified Multi-Objective Optimization
nodes.tldr: Uniformity-driven sampling framework for comparison-based LLM evaluation that cuts evaluation budget while keeping high correlation with ground truth.
nodes.problem: Comparison-based LLM evaluation wastes scarce preference signals by optimizing a single objective.
nodes.approach: Three decoupled sampling probability matrices enforcing uniformity, with unified multi-objective optimization.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Established evaluation topic with a specialised sampling angle

nodes.title: Linear Representations of Political Perspective Emerge in Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Probes attention heads show LLMs encode American political ideology linearly, predicting lawmaker DW-NOMINATE scores, generalizing to news slant, and enabling steering via interventions.
nodes.problem: How LLMs represent and reflect political perspectives internally.
nodes.approach: Linear probing of attention head activations plus linear interventions to steer ideological stance.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
nodes.niche_reason: Political-science-flavored interpretability is an unusual cross-disciplinary angle.

nodes.title: PianoMotion10M: Dataset and Benchmark for Hand Motion Generation in Piano Performance
nodes.tldr: Introduces PianoMotion10M, a dataset of 116 hours of piano video with 10M annotated hand poses, plus a baseline generating hand motions from piano audio.
nodes.problem: Music instruction systems lack guidance for hand movements and fingering between key presses in piano playing.
nodes.approach: Collect annotated bird's-eye piano videos, build an audio-to-hand-motion baseline with position predictor and gesture generator, define metrics.
nodes.primary_topic: Computer Vision › Human Pose, Avatars & Faces
secondary_topics: Audio, Speech & Multimodal › Audio-Visual & Cross-modal Learning
nodes.niche_reason: Piano hand-motion generation from audio is a very rare application.

nodes.title: Emergent Orientation Maps —— Mechanisms, Coding Efficiency and Robustness
nodes.tldr: A spiking neural network with Hebbian plasticity reproduces salt-and-pepper versus pinwheel orientation maps across species and analyzes their coding efficiency and robustness.
nodes.problem: Mechanisms and functional roles of orientation map emergence in visual cortex.
nodes.approach: Self-evolving spiking network with Hebbian plasticity using species-specific physiological parameters.
nodes.niche_reason: Computational neuroscience of cortical orientation maps is very rare at ML venues.

nodes.title: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Limited LLM Benchmark
nodes.tldr: Introduces LiveBench, a contamination-limited LLM benchmark with frequently updated questions, automatic ground-truth scoring, and harder task versions over time.
nodes.problem: Test-set contamination and biased LLM or human judging make benchmark results unreliable.
nodes.approach: Monthly-refreshed questions from recent sources, scored automatically against objective ground truth.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: LLM benchmarks are a crowded area; this one is well-known but common in kind.

nodes.title: Graph Neural Networks Can (Often) Count Substructures
nodes.tldr: Shows message-passing GNNs often can count subgraphs on real data, giving sufficient conditions for counting and sample-efficient learning, plus dynamic programs GNNs can simulate.
nodes.problem: Explaining why GNNs count substructures in practice despite worst-case expressivity limits.
nodes.approach: Derive sufficient conditions and dynamic programming algorithms that message-passing GNNs can simulate; validate empirically.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
nodes.niche_reason: GNN expressivity theory is established but specialised.

nodes.title: Benchmarking Predictive Coding Networks -- Made Simple
nodes.tldr: A fast open-source library and standard benchmark suite for predictive coding networks, with new results and an honest view of scalability limits.
nodes.problem: Predictive coding networks lack scalable, comparable benchmarks, and most prior work uses small, inconsistent tasks.
nodes.approach: Implements a performance-focused library with standard benchmarks and tests adapted bio-plausible methods at larger scale.
nodes.niche_reason: Predictive coding networks are a rare, bio-plausible training paradigm.

nodes.title: Improved Finite-Particle Convergence Rates for Stein Variational Gradient Descent
nodes.tldr: Proves finite-particle convergence rates for Stein variational gradient descent in KSD and Wasserstein-2, improving the known rate to near i.i.d. order.
nodes.problem: Finite-particle convergence rates for SVGD were weak, lacking near-optimal dependence on particle count.
nodes.approach: Relative-entropy analysis splitting its time derivative into a dominant KSD-based negative part and a smaller positive part.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Optimal Transport & Divergences
nodes.niche_reason: Particle-based variational inference theory is specialised but established.

nodes.title: Bundle Neural Network for message diffusion on graphs
nodes.tldr: Bundle Neural Networks perform message diffusion on flat vector bundles, alleviating over-smoothing and over-squashing with provable expressivity for graph learning.
nodes.problem: Message passing GNNs suffer over-smoothing, over-squashing, and limited expressivity.
nodes.approach: Continuous diffusion PDE on flat vector bundles, a special case of sheaf neural networks.
nodes.niche_reason: Vector-bundle message diffusion is an unusual geometric angle on graphs.

nodes.title: Do as We Do, Not as You Think: the Conformity of Large Language Models
nodes.tldr: Studies conformity in LLM multi-agent systems with the BenchForm benchmark, analyzing influencing factors and mitigation via enhanced personas and reflection.
nodes.problem: Whether and why LLM agents conform to group opinions, undermining collaborative problem solving.
nodes.approach: BenchForm benchmark with five interaction protocols, conformity metrics, factor analysis, and mitigation strategies.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Social psychology-style conformity of LLM agents is unusual.

nodes.title: Tractable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning through Behavioral Economics
nodes.tldr: Adding risk aversion and bounded rationality yields risk-averse quantal response equilibria, which are tractable in all n-player matrix and finite-horizon Markov games.
nodes.problem: Nash equilibria are intractable to compute in general multi-agent RL.
nodes.approach: Behavioral-economics solution concept (RQE) reached by no-regret learning, with sample complexity analysis.
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Behavioral economics angle on MARL equilibria is unusual.

nodes.title: Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks: Null Models Achieve High Win Rates
nodes.tldr: Shows a null model outputting a constant, instruction-irrelevant response can reach top win rates on AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena-Hard-Auto, and MT-Bench, exposing gameability of LLM-judge benchmarks.
nodes.problem: Automatic LLM benchmarks may be gamed to achieve high win rates.
nodes.approach: Craft transferable constant adversarial responses that fool LLM judges without access to instructions.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Benchmark gameability is a notable but focused topic.

nodes.title: Effective post-training embedding compression via temperature control in contrastive training
nodes.tldr: Shows contrastive training temperature controls embedding intrinsic dimensionality, and proposes temperature aggregation to compress text embeddings by an order of magnitude.
nodes.problem: Large dense text embeddings are costly to store, and compression often hurts retrieval quality.
nodes.approach: Analyse temperature effects on intrinsic dimension, then aggregate embeddings across temperatures to shrink size.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Efficient Training, Compression & Pruning
nodes.niche_reason: Embedding compression is a common, practical research direction.

nodes.title: MoE++: Accelerating Mixture-of-Experts Methods with Zero-Computation Experts
nodes.tldr: MoE++ adds zero, copy and constant experts alongside FFN experts so tokens use a dynamic number of FFNs, cutting compute while improving performance.
nodes.problem: Mixture-of-Experts models spend uniform compute on all tokens, limiting efficiency and effectiveness.
nodes.approach: Heterogeneous MoE mixing FFN experts with zero-computation experts (discard, skip, replace) and routing with gating residuals.
nodes.primary_topic: Architectures & Training › Mixture of Experts & Sparsity
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Efficient LLM Inference & Architectures
nodes.niche_reason: MoE efficiency is common; zero-computation experts are a modest twist.

nodes.title: Classic but Everlasting: Traditional Gradient-Based Algorithms Converge Fast Even in Time-Varying Multi-Player Games
nodes.tldr: Proves last-iterate convergence rates of extra-gradient and optimistic gradient methods in perturbed multi-player games, including constrained time-varying settings.
nodes.problem: Last-iterate behavior of gradient methods in time-varying multi-player games is poorly understood
nodes.approach: Tangent-residual potential analysis showing O(1/sqrt T) rates when perturbations vanish fast enough.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Game Theory & Mechanism Design
nodes.niche_reason: Time-varying multi-player game convergence is a rare niche

nodes.title: Uncovering Overfitting in Large Language Model Editing
nodes.tldr: The paper identifies Editing Overfit in LLM knowledge editing, introduces the EVOKE benchmark, and proposes Learn the Inference to improve multi-hop generalization.
nodes.problem: Edited LLMs overweight direct edit prompts and fail to generalize new knowledge to multi-hop reasoning.
nodes.approach: Multi-stage Inference Constraint module guides edited models to recall knowledge as in-context learning does.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
nodes.niche_reason: Knowledge editing is an active but well-populated area.

nodes.title: Boosting Ray Search Procedure of Hard-label Attacks with Transfer-based Priors
nodes.tldr: Improves query efficiency of hard-label black-box attacks by integrating transfer-based surrogate priors into ray-search gradient estimation, with theoretical cosine similarity analysis.
nodes.problem: Hard-label black-box attacks need many queries for ray direction search.
nodes.approach: Prior-guided gradient estimators projecting onto surrogate-gradient and random subspaces.
nodes.niche_reason: Black-box attacks are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning Dynamics of LLM Finetuning
nodes.tldr: Decomposes how training examples influence LLM predictions during finetuning, explaining hallucination strengthening and the DPO squeezing effect, plus a simple alignment improvement.
nodes.problem: Finetuning's side effects, like strengthened hallucinations and DPO lowering desired-output likelihood, lack a unified explanation.
nodes.approach: Step-wise decomposition of how influence accumulates among candidate responses, extended with a squeezing-effect analysis.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.confidence_reason: Influence analysis of finetuning spans attribution, alignment and fine-tuning.
nodes.niche_reason: Training-dynamics analysis of LLM finetuning is less crowded than method work.

nodes.title: Booster: Tackling Harmful Fine-tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Perturbation
nodes.tldr: Defends LLM fine-tuning-as-a-service against harmful fine-tuning with an alignment-stage regularizer that attenuates harmful loss reduction under simulated harmful perturbation.
nodes.problem: Harmful fine-tuning attacks break LLM safety alignment and existing defenses fall short.
nodes.approach: Alignment-stage loss regularizer penalizing harmful-loss reduction after simulated harmful weight perturbation.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Safety & Jailbreaks
nodes.niche_reason: Fine-tuning safety defenses are a common LLM safety topic.

nodes.title: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models
nodes.tldr: Cybench offers 40 professional CTF tasks with subtasks to measure how autonomously LM agents find and exploit vulnerabilities across eight models.
nodes.problem: Policymakers need to quantify how capable LM agents are at cyber offense
nodes.approach: Framework of CTF tasks with subtask decomposition and multiple agent scaffolds
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › LLM Evaluation & Benchmarks
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Agents & Tool Use
nodes.niche_reason: Cyber-offense agent evaluation is a specialised and growing niche

nodes.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
nodes.tldr: Scales k-sparse autoencoders to 16M latents on GPT-4 activations, finds clean scaling laws, and introduces new feature-quality metrics.
nodes.problem: Studying sparse autoencoder scaling is hard due to reconstruction-sparsity tradeoffs and dead latents.
nodes.approach: Use k-sparse autoencoders with dead-latent fixes, fit scaling laws, and propose evaluation metrics.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Pretraining, Scaling & Data
nodes.niche_reason: SAE interpretability is currently very popular.

nodes.title: Flow Matching with General Discrete Paths: A Kinetic-Optimal Perspective
nodes.tldr: Framework for discrete flow and diffusion generative models with arbitrary corruption paths, using kinetic-optimal velocity formulas and mixture paths that beat masked constructions.
nodes.problem: Discrete generative models are restricted mostly to simple masked corruption paths.
nodes.approach: Velocity formulas for arbitrary discrete probability paths with kinetic-optimal mixture paths.
nodes.niche_reason: Discrete flow matching is specialised but active.

nodes.title: Knowledge Localization: Mission Not Accomplished? Enter Query Localization!
nodes.tldr: Shows the knowledge localization assumption behind knowledge neurons is too rigid and proposes query localization, which also accounts for attention, improving knowledge modification.
nodes.problem: Whether facts localize to a few knowledge neurons, ignoring attention's role in expression.
nodes.approach: Empirically tests localization assumption, then proposes Query Localization and a consistency-aware knowledge neuron edit.
nodes.primary_topic: Language Models & NLP › Language Model Interpretability
secondary_topics: Language Models & NLP › Knowledge Editing & Factuality
nodes.niche_reason: knowledge neuron localization is established but specialised

nodes.title: Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Generation with Privacy, Utility, and Efficiency
nodes.tldr: THePUff generates temporal heterogeneous graphs by perturbing input with differential privacy then training a GAN, balancing privacy, utility, and efficiency, with six new metrics.
nodes.problem: Temporal heterogeneous graphs expose sensitive node information and need privacy-preserving synthetic graph generation.
nodes.approach: Differentially private graph perturbation followed by adversarial generation using perturbed and original graphs; new temporal utility and privacy metrics.
secondary_topics: Generative Models › GANs, VAEs & Normalizing Flows
nodes.niche_reason: Private generation of temporal heterogeneous graphs is a rare niche.

nodes.title: Robustness Inspired Graph Backdoor Defense
nodes.tldr: Detects poisoned nodes in graph backdoor attacks via prediction variance under random edge dropping, then applies robust training to neutralize triggers across attack types.
nodes.problem: Defending GNNs against diverse graph backdoor attacks with differently-behaved triggers.
nodes.approach: Random edge dropping to identify poisoned nodes by prediction variance, plus a robust training strategy.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph backdoor defense is a rare sub-area of robustness.

nodes.title: Improving Convergence Guarantees of Random Subspace Second-order Algorithm for Nonconvex Optimization
nodes.tldr: Proposes Random Subspace Homogenized Trust Region, a second-order random-subspace method with best known iteration complexity and local linear or quadratic convergence for nonconvex optimization.
nodes.problem: Random subspace methods for large-dimensional nonconvex problems need stronger convergence guarantees at low computational cost.
nodes.approach: Homogenized trust region steps in randomly projected low-dimensional subspaces with first and second-order stationarity analysis.
nodes.niche_reason: Random subspace second-order methods are a rare specialised topic.

nodes.title: Enhancing the Scalability and Applicability of Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for Molecular Systems
nodes.tldr: Predicts Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for large molecules using a larger dataset and a physics-based wavefunction alignment loss that cuts total-energy error and speeds SCF.
nodes.problem: DFT Hamiltonian prediction models lose physical accuracy and scalability on large molecules.
nodes.approach: Scalable network trained on a larger PubChemQH set with a basis-aligned Hamiltonian loss (WALoss).
nodes.confidence_reason: Physics versus chemistry domain; GNN and loss overlap
nodes.niche_reason: Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians are a specialised DFT-learning niche

nodes.title: Block Diffusion: Interpolating Between Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
nodes.tldr: Block diffusion language models interpolate between discrete diffusion and autoregressive generation, enabling flexible-length output with KV caching and parallel sampling.
nodes.problem: Diffusion language models lag in likelihood and are limited to fixed-length generation.
nodes.approach: Block-wise interpolation between discrete diffusion and autoregression, with KV caching and a training recipe.
nodes.niche_reason: Hybrid diffusion-AR language modeling is an active but specialised niche

nodes.title: Scaling In-the-Wild Training for Diffusion-based Illumination Harmonization and Editing by Imposing Consistent Light Transport
nodes.tldr: IC-Light trains diffusion illumination editors at scale by imposing consistent light transport, where blended illuminations match mixed-light appearance, preserving albedo and details.
nodes.problem: Scaling diffusion-based illumination editing is hard because details and intrinsic properties like albedo drift.
nodes.approach: Light-transport consistency constraint enabling training on over 10M mixed data with SDXL and Flux backbones.
nodes.niche_reason: Illumination editing is specialised within image editing.

nodes.title: Two Effects, One Trigger: On the Modality Gap, Object Bias, and Information Imbalance in Contrastive Vision-Language Models
nodes.tldr: Analyzes the modality gap and object bias in CLIP-like models, showing both stem from information imbalance between images and captions and linking the gap to logit entropy.
nodes.problem: Why contrastive VLMs show a modality gap and object bias, and whether these hurt performance.
nodes.approach: Empirical analysis of off-the-shelf VLMs and controlled experiments varying shared information between modalities.
nodes.niche_reason: Mechanistic analysis of CLIP embedding geometry is specialised.

nodes.title: Capturing the Temporal Dependence of Training Data Influence
nodes.tldr: Defines trajectory-specific leave-one-out influence and approximates it cheaply with data value embeddings, revealing that early and late training data matter most.
nodes.problem: Influence functions assume permutation-invariant training, which fails for order-sensitive modern training.
nodes.approach: Data value embedding capturing cumulative data-model interactions, so LOO influence reduces to a dot product with test gradients.
nodes.primary_topic: Data, Benchmarks & Evaluation › Data Attribution & Influence
nodes.niche_reason: Trajectory-aware data influence is a specialised attribution angle

nodes.title: Learning Distributions of Complex Fluid Simulations with Diffusion Graph Networks
nodes.tldr: Samples turbulent fluid states from their equilibrium distribution using a graph-based latent diffusion model on meshes, avoiding long simulations.
nodes.problem: Long, expensive simulations are needed to estimate full distributions of unsteady physical flows.
nodes.approach: Latent diffusion with a multi-scale GNN on unstructured meshes, trainable from short, incomplete simulations.
nodes.niche_reason: Graph latent diffusion for fluid statistics is specialised.

nodes.title: On the Expressiveness of Rational ReLU Neural Networks With Bounded Depth
nodes.tldr: Proves depth lower bounds for exactly representing max(0,x1..xn) with ReLU networks having rational weights, partially confirming a conjecture of logarithmic depth.
nodes.problem: Whether ReLU network expressive power grows with depth for exact representation of max functions.
nodes.approach: Number-theoretic and mixed-volume arguments on lattice polytopes for decimal and N-ary fraction weights.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Deep Learning Theory
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Learning Theory Lower Bounds & Complexity
nodes.niche_reason: Polyhedral/number-theoretic ReLU depth bounds are very rare.

nodes.title: Weighted Point Set Embedding for Multimodal Contrastive Learning Toward Optimal Similarity Metric
nodes.tldr: Represents instances as weighted point sets for multimodal contrastive learning and proves this reaches the optimal similarity under symmetric InfoNCE.
nodes.problem: A single latent point per instance cannot capture rich similarity structure in multimodal data.
nodes.approach: Weighted point set embeddings with a theoretical analysis of symmetric InfoNCE.
nodes.confidence_reason: Method and theory both central; topic is a judgment call.
nodes.niche_reason: CLIP-style contrastive learning is mainstream; theory is specific.

nodes.title: IGL-Bench: Establishing the Comprehensive Benchmark for Imbalanced Graph Learning
nodes.tldr: Benchmarks 24 imbalanced graph learning algorithms on 17 datasets with uniform protocols, assessing effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency.
nodes.problem: Imbalanced graph learning lacks consistent protocols, so algorithm comparisons are unfair.
nodes.approach: Unified data processing and splitting, plus an open-source package covering class and topology imbalance.
nodes.niche_reason: Imbalanced graph learning benchmarks are specialised.

nodes.title: Can Watermarked LLMs be Identified by Users via Crafted Prompts?
nodes.tldr: Water-Probe detects whether an LLM is watermarked using crafted prompts exploiting consistent key biases, and Water-Bag merges multiple keys to make watermarks harder to identify.
nodes.problem: Imperceptibility of LLM text watermarks: can users tell a service is watermarked?
nodes.approach: Prompt-based identification exploiting key-specific biases; defend by merging multiple watermark keys.
nodes.niche_reason: Watermark imperceptibility attacks are a specialised subtopic.

nodes.title: How Much is Unseen Depends Chiefly on Information About the Seen
nodes.tldr: Shows expected missing mass depends on counts of classes seen k times, then searches for lower-MSE estimators than Good-Turing.
nodes.problem: Estimating the missing mass of classes absent from training data, without distributional assumptions.
nodes.approach: Optimization over nearly unbiased estimators to minimize MSE given only the sample.
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Generalization & Statistical Learning
secondary_topics: Learning Theory & Optimization › Probabilistic & Bayesian Methods
nodes.niche_reason: Rare: missing-mass estimation with searched estimators.

nodes.title: Counterfactual Realizability
nodes.tldr: Formally defines realizability and gives a complete algorithm to decide which counterfactual distributions can be sampled directly by physical experiments.
nodes.problem: Counterfactual distributions are assumed inaccessible, so it is unclear which can be estimated experimentally
nodes.approach: Complete decision algorithm for realizability under physical constraints such as no time travel
nodes.primary_topic: Learning Theory & Optimization › Causality & Causal Inference
nodes.niche_reason: Very rare: counterfactual realizability is a narrow theoretical question

nodes.title: SynFlowNet: Design of Diverse and Novel Molecules with Synthesis Constraints
nodes.tldr: SynFlowNet is a GFlowNet that builds molecules via chemical reactions and buyable reactants, so generated molecules are synthesizable and diverse.
nodes.problem: Generative drug design models often output molecules that cannot be synthesized.
nodes.approach: GFlowNet with a reaction-based action space and learned backward policies to enforce forward synthesis.
nodes.niche_reason: GFlowNets for chemistry are established but specialised.

nodes.title: Learning to Search from Demonstration Sequences
nodes.tldr: Learns to build best-first search trees from demonstration sequences via gradient descent, jointly learning encoder, value function, and world model.
nodes.problem: Supervised learning on demonstration sequences fails in the vast unseen search space.
nodes.approach: Differentiable best-first tree construction with a stochastic expansion policy trained by REINFORCE.
nodes.primary_topic: Reinforcement Learning › Model-Based RL & World Models
secondary_topics: Architectures & Training › Differentiable Optimization & Structured Layers
nodes.confidence_reason: Judgment between planning, model-based RL, and differentiable search.
nodes.niche_reason: Learning search from demonstrations is less common than standard planning.

nodes.title: UniMatch: Universal Matching from Atom to Task for Few-Shot Drug Discovery
nodes.tldr: UniMatch combines hierarchical atom-to-molecule matching with meta-learned task-level matching to improve few-shot molecular property prediction on MoleculeNet and FS-Mol.
nodes.problem: Few-shot drug discovery lacks annotations and existing methods ignore hierarchical molecular structure.
nodes.approach: Dual matching network: hierarchical pooling across atoms, substructures, molecules plus meta-learning for task-level matching.
nodes.niche_reason: Few-shot molecular learning is an established but specialised subarea.
